Added separate `headless/game_liveness.h` pure C++ `Probe`, sampled **only on the existing once-per-second watchdog thread**, never instrumenting JIT blocks/GPU frame hotpaths. Starts after `system.Run()`, stops at game completion/teardown via explicit DisarmGame and scope guard.
- Watch uses existing developer `Performance::gpu_dispatch.calls` and `rasterizer_draw.calls` counters. It needs evidence of a counter **change during this session** before reporting; if counters are absent/unavailable, records nothing, avoiding false claims. After **30 seconds** without *new counted GPU work*, emits `EDEN_GAME_GPU_STALL_SUSPECT` including dispatch/draw counts, GPU queue-full, guest sync wait and each guest CPU phase; repeat every ~30 sec with **max four reports total per game**, resetting delay after resumed progress. Does **not** exit/restart the game; menu pause or suspended presentation may also look idle, so these are suspects, not proof of bug cause.
- Only exists inside `EDEN_DEV_PROFILE && PS5_NATIVE` guarded header, with no additional per-frame work or shipping change. `tools/check-game-liveness.py` compiles actual portable policy on Linux and checks 30-second threshold, no GPU counters => no suspect, per-incident recovery, monotonic clock anomaly, cap four per session and source-side arming/disarming. Added lightweight and native release source preflights; **no firmware build/test yet**.
- Existing rasterizer/GPU counters must be confirmed to advance on the selected Vulkan/OpenGL backend before trusting negative diagnosis; no GPU activity report ≠ confirmed freeze. Source-only test awaiting next `[core-ready]` CI. No PS5 native build authorized and Issue #8 stays OPEN.

### 2026-10-08 — Third-pass correctness: bounded glyph config, zero-overhead unsupported titles, watchdog session epochs (CI PENDING)

- Inspected the actual HEAD in `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`, including `headless/main.cpp`, `glyph_overrides_runtime.h`, `metadata_bridge.cpp`, `stall_watchdog.h` and JIT memory policy. Found **three real source-level correctness/efficiency problems** overlooked by earlier green CI:
  1. `GlyphOverrides::ReadBounded` checked JSON `file_size` then performed an **unbounded** `std::istreambuf_iterator` read. Under concurrent JSON growth/replacement it could allocate arbitrarily beyond the 128KiB input cap. Replaced with a 4KiB chunked read that refuses any bytes beyond the limit, rejects I/O error, and rechecks final size. New C++ fixture tests exact boundary, oversized, symlink, empty file.
  2. `main.cpp` always read the game's NACP/control RomFS for glyphs **even when no title rules or files existed** (currently the shared catalogue has ZERO qualified games). Added `GlyphOverrides::NeedsGameVersion`: require an eligible installed graphics mod and curated title rule, with PlayStation visual mode requested, game mods enabled, not Safe Launch nor already manually disabled. Only then call the expensive NACP metadata bridge; source and actual C++ tests protect the absent-rule, absent-mod, disabled-style path. The catalogue remains install-only; no per-frame work or mapping changes.
  3. In rapid back-to-back launches, the developer in-game GPU watcher could miss the `game_armed=false` window between its 1Hz samples and carry stale previous-title counters into the next title. Added `game_session_epoch`, incremented on every `ArmGame`, so Loop resets `GameLiveness::Probe` for every new title regardless of missed disarm edge; upgraded host fixture to compile/link/execute real developer watchdog header using tiny upstream CPU clock stub.
- Also fixed `LoadCatalogue` equal-revision ambiguity: local JSON now requires strictly **higher** revision than compiled snapshot, not `>=`, with a host regression for conflicting same-revision rules.
- Docs/PS5_INGAME_GLYPHS.md updated. New source-only `[core-ready]` CI must run before claiming PASS; no PS5 full native app build, UI re-render, release merge or real game artwork/FPS proof. Issues #7 and #8 both remain OPEN.

### 2026-10-09 — User demands no *eager physical* JIT reservation; unresolved GPU and glyphs audit

- User correctly objected that reducing the dense JIT upfront budget from **4376 to 2188 MiB** is NOT the promised no-upfront-physical-commit memory architecture. The current shipping path is still dense and eagerly allocates. Quarter-pool is an **interim OOM reduction only**.

### 2026-10-09 — Critical sparse JIT fallback defect removed; allocator/physical-demand host gate

- During actual `headless/jit-allocator.h` review, developer-only sparse branch silently fell back to `Common::AllocateMemoryPages(size)` (FULL dense direct-memory allocation) whenever `ReserveSparseJitCode(size)` failed to reserve VA or its 4-MiB bootstrap. ### 2026-10-09 — Physical topology failure source root clarified

### 2026-10-09 — First real Fermi2D base-layer compatibility candidate; NO BUILD

- The upstream software blitter in `eden-emulator/mirror` `src/video_core/engines/sw_blitter/blitter.cpp` already calls `UnswizzleSubrect` with the original `src.depth` and block-depth, and `SwizzleSubrect` for destination. `textures/decoders.cpp` explicitly hardcodes `origin_z = 0`; the subrectangle decoder processes the first z slice only when given one plane's worth of lines.
- A PS5-native-only CMake-derived Fermi implementation in `headless/gpu_native_observability.cmake` now handles `regs.src.depth > 1` **only** for `src.layer=0`, `dst.layer=0`, `dst.depth>=1`, `Operation::SrcCopy`, and `clip_enable=0`. It bypasses the unverified accelerated 3D path and calls the pinned software blitter using **temporary** source/destination surface descriptors with `depth=1` (while preserving original `block_depth`/layout), so unrelated 3D slices are not read into temporary buffers. Original guest descriptors and addresses are never modified. The first eight successful base-layer copies emit bounded `EDEN_GPU_FERMI2D_Z0_SOFTWARE` evidence.
- All other source-depth anomalies continue the bounded `EDEN_GPU_FERMI2D_UNSUPPORTED` trace and original `AssertFailSoftImpl()` contract. Nonzero z/layer copies are **not implemented**; no fake normalized depth or silently ignored operation. Maxwell `PRMT_imm` remains unimplemented with bounded raw traces.
- CMake now fails closed if pinned software `src.depth`, `dst.depth` and `origin_z=0` anchors change. `tools/check-gpu-native-diagnostics.py` verifies source contract. Source commits `043ac5a858bb` and `c50b2fa6f365`, `[skip ci]`; a read-only connector comparison against current public Eden mirror found all 6 expected source anchors. **Not an SDK build, not proof pinned source matches, and not a console validation.**
- Native qualification gates: proper 3D-to-2D slice pixels and no GPU regression, worst frame latency from software fallback, clipping/format/stride constraints, leak/teardown and FW13.60 crash resilience. If pinned blitter/decoder semantics differ, build must fail rather than introduce wrong pixels. All Fermi layers beyond z=0 and PRMT remain open.

### 2026-10-09 — Maxwell PRMT Index compatibility code (source candidate; NOT BUILD-QUALIFIED)

- Replaced the prior diagnostic-only `PRMT_imm(u64)` wrapper in `headless/gpu_native_observability.cmake` with genuine Eden IR translation for NVIDIA Maxwell **PRMT Index mode 0**. Decoder uses SM50 immediate opcode `0x36c0` register A bits 8..15, B bits 39..46, immediate 16-bit selector bits 20..35, destination bits 0..7, mode bits 48..50. Each 4-bit selector nibble chooses A/B, byte number 0..3 and sign-bit replication (0xff if selected byte MSB is 1, 0 otherwise). Implemented via `BitFieldExtract`, logical shifts, bitwise masks/OR; no fake zero result. Mode 1..6/7 still `ThrowNotImplemented` with bounded `EDEN_GPU_PRMT_IMM` log. Supported mode emits at most eight `EDEN_GPU_PRMT_IMM_INDEX` lines. Commit `81d83e3a50cd`.
- Also replaced `PRMT_reg(u64)` diagnostic-only stub with genuine **dynamic register-selector Index mode 0** translation, using selector register bits 20..27, A/B registers and runtime IR shift/select/mask/sign-replication. Other modes throw with bounded `EDEN_GPU_PRMT_REG_UNSUPPORTED` log; supported variant emits bounded `EDEN_GPU_PRMT_REG_INDEX`. Commit `57583029970e`.
- Source encoding cross-checked against Nouveau Mesa `sm50.rs` `impl SM50Op for OpPrmt` (reg opcode `0x5bc0`, imm `0x36c0`, selector and mode bit ranges), and `ir.rs` `PrmtSelByte` nibble sign-bit semantics; Eden mirror `bitfield_extract.cpp`, `integer_shift_right.cpp`, `common_funcs.cpp` confirm intended IR emitter ops exist. **Read-only reference check, not proof the pinned local dependency builds.**
- Source contract `tools/check-gpu-native-diagnostics.py` extended with exact decoder predicates and pure-model representative byte permutation/sign-replication cases, plus explicit unsupported-mode throw retention. Commits `2e3e44b19d2f`, `c7dbb95a030d` and header docs `f99ef28925ed`. `[skip ci]`, **no CI, SDK build or PS5 run**; do not claim PRMT compatibility confirmed in games yet.
- Still unsupported: `PRMT_rc`, `PRMT_cr` and non-Index modes, plus multi-layer Fermi2D beyond z=0. The user demanded all actual implementations; this is an incremental functional subset, not a final signoff. Continue implementation/compatibility work and preserve no-GitHub-run gate.

### 2026-10-09 — Additional guarded Fermi2D pitch-linear layer compatibility (SOURCE ONLY)

- Fermi2D GPU compatibility derived from the pinned source now **also** accepts nonzero source/destination layer IDs for pitch-linear images when: `source.linear==Pitch`, `destination.linear==Pitch`, both `layer<depth`, formats identical, `Operation::SrcCopy`, clipping disabled, dimensions nonzero, pitch nonzero and >= width*bytes/block. It computes the appropriate plane address `original_GPU_address + pitch * height * layer` in u64, rejects overflow and invalid geometry, creates temporary one-plane descriptors with `depth=1` and `layer=0`, and runs the original software copy. Original GPU register state remains untouched. Block-linear **z>0 is not implemented**; non-Index PRMT modes not implemented. Absent preflight conditions retain the original `UNIMPLEMENTED_IF_MSG` soft asserts.
- The original Fermi `src.layer`/`dst.layer` exceptions are replaced only under that narrow predicate, and the `src.depth!=1` check likewise exempts only the already-guarded z0 and pitch cases. CMake aborts at configure time if pinned layer/source-depth/copy anchors have drifted. `tools/check-gpu-native-diagnostics.py` includes conditions, overflow model and layer-index examples. Source commits `b6f6f591ed52`, `43407cb873bd`, `8a5f1c846af6`, `fc751ec36440`, `7b57294c3e9f`, all `[skip ci]`.
- Important qualification: **Not compiled or tested on PS5**, no empirical validation of texture colors, Fermi layout semantics or speed, no new release or build. Software pitch copies could be expensive; remain an experimental source candidate until a source-gated native build and instrumented real-game output test are explicitly authorized. Do NOT claim the entire Fermi2D 3D-layer problem is solved; block-linear nonzero z, incompatible formats and clipping remain unsupported.

### 2026-10-09 — Frame-loop artwork cache CPU cleanup + robust uneven sparse JIT reservation (NO BUILDS)

Source-only commits on `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`, with `[skip ci]`; approved UI/branding and `fix/0.40-zbic-13.60` untouched.

1. **UI texture-frame CPU cost:** `headless/prosperoeden/pe/ui/textures.cpp` previously allocated and sorted a `std::vector<pair<last_used, key>>` **on every frame** while the cover cache exceeded 160 entries. Its pending decode queue was a `vector` with front erasure O(n), another scroll-sensitive hot-path cost. Now the cache scans for the oldest eligible completed cover with no temporary sort/vector and deletes **at most two textures per frame**, keeping the protection for covers used within the last two frames. The decode queue is a `std::deque` with O(1) `pop_front`; no media decoding/upload is moved onto the UI thread. `tools/check-nlib-ui-recovery.py` has source-contract guards for this. Commits `7926a7273501`, `4242c78257c5`, `e4ff60c28021`.
2. **Sparse JIT uneven arena sizes:** `headless/jit-allocator.h` requested `Common::ReserveSparseJitCode(size)` with the raw Xbyak size, but the native reserve API deliberately **rejects sizes not divisible by 2 MiB**. It now rounds up the **virtual reservation only** to 2 MiB, with overflow guard and correct ownership/logged capacity. The current 4 MiB constant-pool bootstrap still commits only two 2 MiB chunks; backing remains demand-driven rather than dense. A new `tools/check-jit-sparse-host.py` regression case requests 5 MiB + 4096 bytes, asserts 6 MiB virtual vs 4 MiB physical initially, grows to 6 MiB, verifies RW/RX alias and full cleanup. Commits `c830d38d9214`, `99d4544323d6`.
3. These are **real source edits but not yet compiled or executed**. The native PS5 sparse JIT remains developer-only behind `EDEN_SPARSE_JIT_DEV`, real firmware RW/RX mapping/pinning not qualified. This fix does not change the current dense FC27 memory admission (2188 MiB) or claim an FPS uplift. Need a separately approved, instrumented native qualification before enabling globally.
4. Still OPEN: guest CPU/HLE freeze and frame pacing, block-linear Fermi layers >0, PRMT other modes, JIT runtime growth/OOM, controller glyph texture integration. Do not close project or launch Github Actions prematurely.

### 2026-10-09 — Last source pass: diagnostics render I/O removed, cancellable scans, GL invalidation amortized (NO BUILD)

### 2026-10-09 — AMD Zen-family 17h physical topology fallback for PS5 (NO BUILD)

- Real firmware FC27 log: `EDEN_WORKER_TOPOLOGY ready=0 distinct_cores=1 cpus=0,0,0,0,0`. Original `headless/performance.cpp::CheckWorkerTopology` used only x2APIC CPUID leaf `0xB` and returned immediately if absent, even if the PS5's AMD family 17h+ CPU advertises `TopologyExtensions`. That log is a FAILED topology probe, not proof game code executes on only one physical CPU.
- Added AMD-vendor and family >=0x17 detection with extended-leaf availability `0x8000001E` and feature flag `CPUID 0x80000001 ECX[22]`. When available, read physical `CoreId` from `0x8000001E EBX[7:0]`, threads per core from `EBX[15:8]+1` (reject >8), node from `ECX[7:0]`, key node+CoreId; prioritize this documented AMD path before falling back to valid x2APIC leaf `0xB` SMT shift. Only accept each pinned CPU after `cpuset_getaffinity` reads back exactly its one-CPU mask; no assumption that logical CPU numbering uniquely identifies physical cores. If insufficient distinct reported cores, `worker_topology_ready` remains false; the existing user-selected logical-only trial still logs `physical_verified=0`. The new topology log includes `amd_ext` / `x2apic` capability flags. Could allow automatic physical worker pinning when evidence becomes available, but has NOT been PS5-qualified.
- Important multi-title safety: reset `worker_topology_ready`, `secondary_cpus`, `worker_cpus`, `cpu_core`, `topology_allowed_valid` **before** any affinity/cpuid early failure. Never keep physical placement from previous title after a later probe fails.
- Architectural source reference: Linux kernel AMD topology specification for family >=0x17: https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/arch/x86/topology.html and Linux `arch/x86/kernel/cpu/topology_amd.c`. This is reference for bit encoding, **not firmware verification**. Regenerated source-contract in `tools/check-experimental-performance.py` checks AMD detection, SMT-vs-physical key, OS affinity readback, fallback and early reset; host model verifies two logical siblings share a physical CoreId and separate nodes do not.

### 2026-10-09 — JIT memory telemetry: correct lifecycle instead of misleading early zeros (NO BUILD)

- Real 2026-10-08 FC27 `EDEN_JIT_SPARSE_MEMORY phase=core_initialized reserved=0 committed=0` and `EDEN_JIT_DENSE_MEMORY phase=core_initialized physically_owned=0` were logged at `passed("core_initialized")` directly after `system.Initialize()`, **before** the title `system.Load`, `system.GetCpuManager().OnGpuReady`, or guest JIT startup. The zero is therefore **not evidence that Dynarmic was using no RAM**, nor proof that 2188 MiB JIT physical memory allocation failed; the separate `EDEN_JIT_ALIAS` records show successful allocator creation later. No increase to physical JIT budget is justified by that misleading stage.
- Added `Eden::Performance::ReportJitCodeState(phase)`, which reads exact `Common::SparseJitUsage` (reserved VA vs committed direct physical) and `Common::DenseJitDirectBytes` (actual owning direct-memory allocation), prints one short `EDEN_JIT_MEMORY phase=... sparse_reserved=... sparse_committed=... dense_direct=...` receipt. Unlike `ReportDirectMemoryState`, it performs **no 8192-region kernel memory walk and is never called in the GPU frame loop**. `headless/main.cpp` invokes it at `game_loaded` / `nro_loaded`, `cpu_manager_ready`, `core_shutdown` lifecycle marks. This will let next authorized hardware build prove whether JIT memory exists when CPU workers are ready.

### 2026-10-09 — Native PS5 log rotation ownership and recovery hardening (NO BUILDS)

- `headless/log_pipe.h` already implements two 8 MiB log segments per stream (`stderr.log`/`stderr.first.log` and `heap.log`/`heap.first.log`), with a background pipe drain rather than ~25ms synchronous SSD writes. No new rotation design needed. Fixed an actual failure path in `LogPipe::Attach`: after redirecting `stdout`/`stderr` into a pipe, failure to start the draining `std::thread` would otherwise leave the stream writing into a pipe without a consumer, eventually blocking game/launcher logging. New `try/catch` restores the stream's file descriptor via `dup2`, closes pipe/old duplicate, clears ownership, and returns false.
- Second log segment recycling no longer relies on `ftruncate` + `lseek` (inconsistently available on native FW runtimes) or risk continuing at an old file offset. It reopens the existing tail with `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC` before closing the former descriptor, resetting offset and staying within limit. Original first segment remains preserved; rotation failure continues draining the pipe without growing SSD data. Rotation marker updated from obsolete `Eden 0.40 Improved` to `Eden Encore`.
- Added `tools/check-log-pipe-rotation-source.py` requiring the 8MiB dual segment policy, thread failure descriptor restoration, fail-closed recycle and background drain behavior. Code `7c487917491b`; source gate `1d3ac8fc3aa1` both `[skip ci]`. Read-only cross-file inspection reports 9/9 guards; script not executed, no fault injection/native tests. **This is a defensive source change, NOT a confirmed runtime crash fix**.

### 2026-10-09 — Source audit: software Fermi blitter overflow, high-FPS frame-skip atomics, shader workers (NO BUILD)

- **Shared GPU software blitter arithmetic, real defect.** Inspected the upstream Eden `video_core/engines/sw_blitter/blitter.cpp` implementation used by the native pinned source. Its pitch-linear plane length, `static_cast<size_t>(surface.pitch * surface.height)`, and its `src_copy_size = src_extent_x * src_extent_y * src_bytes_per_pixel` / equivalent destination expression multiply as 32-bit integers BEFORE promotion to `size_t`, risking truncated GPU guest-memory reads/writes and incorrectly sized buffers. The fork does not version the pinned `src/video_core` subtree directly. `headless/gpu_native_observability.cmake` therefore now fail-closed verifies three exact upstream arithmetic anchors and generates `sw_blitter_sized.cpp` replacing the original video_core compilation unit with versions which promote the **FIRST** factor to `size_t`. This affects all PS5 native software-blit fallback calls, not only FC27 or z0. Added strict source admission for new Fermi2D software routes: nonzero src/dst bytes-per-pixel, pitch*height products within u32 so no old staging assumption, and source/destination rectangle byte counts within u32, plus existing bounds checks. Unsupported candidates soft-assert and return with bounded `EDEN_GPU_FERMI2D_SOFTWARE_BOUNDS_INVALID` evidence rather than passing malformed sizes to the blitter. `tools/check-gpu-native-diagnostics.py` updated with source contracts and pure mathematical boundary examples. Commits `3e2d90b81d8c`, `8bb5324d744f`, `b733e26ac1ff`, `c95291ca1cf4`, `0cc33cd0a750`, all `[skip ci]`. No hardware-render evidence or speed claim.
- **Global high-FPS presentation correctness.** `headless/display_refresh.h::SkipFrame()` used a static non-atomic `long long last_shown_ns` across ALL game sessions, resulting in a stale first-frame decision and potential cross-renderer data race. New `inline std::atomic<long long> last_shown_frame_ns` uses a CAS loop: discard too-soon frames, do not roll back a newer timestamp, preserve real gameplay frames when game rate <= output. New `ResetSkipFrameTracking()` clears both last-show timestamp and skipped-frame count, called by `headless/main.cpp` between sessions. `tools/check-runtime-frame-budget.py` guards it. Commits `9030c826d347`, `b456582399cd`, `9f6e1a74a871`, `[skip ci]`. This only affects source rendering faster than screen refresh; it DOES NOT synthesize 60 FPS for a 30 FPS game or resolve FC27's 18-24 FPS drops.
- **Physical CPU topology source-regression gate.** New AMD-family-17h `__cpuid` probe had made existing host `tools/check-worker-affinity.py` mock uncompilable: mock lacked `__cpuid` and extended CPUID feature detection. Fixture now implements both Intel x2APIC and AMD extended `0x8000001E` vendor/family/topology leaves and adds Zen SMT sibling + missing-extension fallback cases while retaining affinity restoration tests. Commit `25b16b4adac4`, `[skip ci]`. Not executed.
- **Shader build concurrency was double-conservative.** Found the actual `EDEN_PS5_SHADER_WORKERS reported=16 available=13 workers=3` policy inside `tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py`. It reserved six logical slots for guest/GPU, then divided the remaining seven *logical* slots by two as an SMT heuristic. One pipeline compilation worker actually occupies one OS-logical scheduler slot; doubling the reserve can leave parallel shader backlog unnecessarily serialized. New general PS5 Vulkan policy reserves six slots for guest cores/GPU plus one slot for audio/services, then uses up to SIX workers across actual allowed logical slots, with a six-worker hard cap; the observed 13 available produces six workers (6+1+6=13). Missing affinity information retains one worker. `tools/check-vulkan-shader-workers.py` checks policy and representative 13/16/10/8/unknown CPU counts. Commits `302b2e4dabe7`, `6dc3dfb5721e`, `[skip ci]`. **This is a potentially useful but UNQUALIFIED scheduling experiment**: sustained compilation can compete with game cores and might reduce FPS; do not claim improvement without 13.60 gameplay timing on PS5.
- This entire checkpoint contains SOURCE EDITS and read-only source confirmations only. No source checker executed, no CMake configure, no SDK compilation, no GitHub Actions, no PS5 runtime. Release branch `fix/0.40-zbic-13.60` and user-approved purple Eden Encore design left untouched. Open: non-Index Maxwell PRMT, multi-layer 3D Fermi swizzle, sparse Dynarmic long-session mapping, FC27 guest freeze/root cause, real FPS/frame pacing, PlayStation glyph packs (zero embedded verified rules), log/cleanup native fault qualification.

### 2026-10-09 — JIT capacity recovery / sparse hot-path mutex / Fermi overflow closeout (SOURCE ONLY, NO BUILD)

- **Native A64/A32 JIT memory admission improvement:** `headless/jit-startup-retry.h::NextCapacity` previously cut any rejected contiguous code arena by **50%** immediately. That often discards hundreds of MiB of usable code capacity when the native reservation barely misses its requested size; replace with geometric **25% reduction** (rounded down to 2 MiB) and strict baseline floor. Example A64 failed 1024 MiB request now retries 768→576→432→324→256 MiB rather than 512→256, retaining larger caches whenever they fit. Fully successful allocations unchanged; only catches `Xbyak::ERR_CANT_ALLOC` / `std::bad_alloc`, never non-memory/JIT correctness exceptions. No infinite retry: next capacity must be strictly smaller. Host fixture `tools/check-jit-startup-retry.py` updated for exact A64/A32 retry sequences and near-floor behavior, **not run**.
- **Actionable per-core telemetry:** Retry logs now identify `reason=xbyak_alloc` vs `reason=host_alloc` and `attempt`; on recovered allocation they emit `EDEN_JIT_STARTUP_RECOVERED bits=... core=... bytes=... retries=...`. Emitted only on startup failures/recovery, not per-frame or per compiled block. Source commit `837832f395e5`, `9a95b7c8fb1e`, `c83011673cbb`.
- **Sparse compile hot path:** In the generated Dynarmic `BlockOfCode::EnsureMemoryCommitted` injection, a selected `sparse_jit_cache` used to call `IsSparseJitCode(getCode())` under global mutex, then `CommitSparseJitCode` which takes the **same mutex and revalidates owner/capacity**, for each JIT emission. The native allocator in explicit sparse mode is *strictly sparse-or-fail* (never falls back to dense), so remove the redundant first lookup/mutex. The single `CommitSparseJitCode` call still checks that the actual code pointer is an owned registered sparse region and that growth is inside reserved capacity; otherwise reports failure. Keep one mutex for actual chunk growth and accounting. `tools/check-experimental-performance.py` source contract protects this and strict sparse selection. Commits `9cfbbe602ae9`, `9a595833c48a`.
- **Dense alias uniqueness:** `headless/jit-allocator.h` previously ignored `unordered_map::emplace` duplicate result in the dense path while the sparse path already aborted on a duplicate live RX VA. Both now fail closed: a duplicate live RX pointer can never silently overwrite/lose the second mapping's ownership. Commit `bf6c21d2db2f`.
- **Fermi2D overflow check on extreme guest dimensions:** Initial native overlay `copy_sizes_valid` multiplied 64-bit width × height × BPP before comparing to 32-bit allocation bound; in malformed 2^31-scale guest rectangles this u64 multiplication can wrap. New `valid_byte_count` validates positive coordinates and BPP, then checks width ≤ `UINT32_MAX/bpp` and height ≤ `UINT32_MAX/(width*bpp)`. Thus neither the checker itself nor the pinned software blitter can process a wrapped size along newly enabled 3D/pitch-layer paths. Regression model `tools/check-gpu-native-diagnostics.py` covers valid 1080p and malicious dimensions, zero/huge pixel width. Commits `c8e34c85bbea`, `01d6056d44ae`.
- Read-only cross-file source inspection found 11/11 new predicates; NOT executed test scripts, not a compiled ABI check, no native firmware results. All commits `[skip ci]`, `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` only. `fix/0.40-zbic-13.60` preserved; approved purple Home UI preserved; no workflow/CI invoked.
- Still open: verify sparse fixed RX/RW alias behavior and memory pressure in long-session FW13.60, actual allocation-retry effects, Vulkan six-worker scheduling impact, guest HLE deadlock and FC27 frame pacing, PRMT non-Index / Fermi block-linear z>0, PlayStation glyph pack compatibility. Do not claim performance uplift or freezes solved until real hardware qualification.

### 2026-10-09 — DualSense rumble mutex avoided on unchanged HID output (SOURCE ONLY)

- The PS5 input loop calls `PadEngine::TakeRumble` on every poll for each connected player, previously acquiring a shared `rumble_mutex` even when the guest has not changed its vibration request. The guest's `SetVibration` uses the same mutex to write separate virtual Joy-Con amplitudes, so repeat lock contention is unnecessary.
- Added per-player `rumble_pending` `std::atomic<bool>` hints. The guest writer sets the hint with release semantics **inside** its existing mutex after updating rumble payload and `sides.changed`; the PS5 poller first acquire-loads and returns immediately if false. If true, it locks and consumes the payload as before, clearing the hint **inside the same mutex**, so a concurrent writer cannot be accidentally erased. Normal vibration amplitude calculation, motor output and disconnected shutdown remain unchanged.
- The `tools/check-dualsense-input-hotpath.py` source gate now protects hint memory order, mutex serialization and button/axis transition dedup. Commits `d603771a3556`, `a2ee52267b21`, `d1cd159e4f02`, all `[skip ci]` on `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. Read-only cross-file inspection found 10/10 expected source predicates. Optional `--spec-out` outputs a schema-1 renderer draft with `button:null` for every candidate; `ps-glyph-atlas.py render` refuses unresolved icons. Prevents draft/report same-path collision and validates both destinations and title/version before writing either. Fonts, opaque sprite sheets, compressed layouts may yield no candidates and must remain unsupported. This is an aid to human/AI-assisted title mapping, NOT a magic auto-replacement.
- **New `tools/ps-glyph-bntx-inspect.py`**: offline, bounded **READ-ONLY** BNTX/NX texture-container inspection grounded in public 3DSkit BNTX header/BRTI documentation and BNTX-Injector source. Validates BNTX magic/BOM/reported size, 256-max texture pointer table, each BRTI offset/size, width/height/depth, mip count, format, tile mode and length-bounded texture name; presents candidate internal texture names. `ps-glyph-scan.py` includes up to 32 BNTX inventory records and at most 32 named likely controller/UI textures per container. Does NOT unswizzle/decompress/repack ASTC/BC/linear block memory or change the game. Real proprietary BNTX and BFRES in-game glyph replacement remains OPEN. Docs: https://github.com/Tyulis/3DSkit/blob/master/doc/BNTX.md and https://github.com/aboood40091/BNTX-Injector/blob/master/bntx.py ; documented layouts must still be console-verified.
- **`tools/ps-glyph-atlas.py::discover` ranking**: replaced first-200-filesystem-entries stop with a deterministic full RomFS name enumeration, scoring button/controller/prompt/UI/atlas/textures, then opening/hash-checking up to 200 highest-ranked candidates. No per-title import of irrelevant first 200 generic textures; image SHA/dimensions only if viable. This is offline code (NOT in PS5 frame/game hotpath).
- **New `tools/ps-glyph-reuse.py`**: finds original game PNG/TGA atlases with byte-identical SHA-256 in target titles/versions, copies pixel coordinates into a new per-title spec; by default clears all symbol labels to `null` for manual semantic verification. Only explicit `--approve-same-semantics` reuses previously verified icon names after user checks that menu/gameplay mappings agree. Duplicate/ambiguous atlas matches, edited bytes, unsafe paths, malformed types fail closed. Supports repeated art layouts without promising same behavioral mapping across Nintendo title contexts.
- **Safer `render`**: old acceptance only required *one* transparent pixel in an arbitrary chosen sprite rectangle, potentially clearing neighbors/solid artwork. Now requires nonempty original alpha and at least one fully transparent pixel perimeter between the actual glyph alpha bounding box and EVERY boundary of its chosen rectangle. Also validates explicit string type before icon variant/button membership, refusing unknown/unassigned values.
- **Source fixture updates** `tools/check-ps-glyph-atlas.py`: synthetic Nx/BNTX table with one BRTI for a named RGBA8 icon, rejected out-of-file BRTI pointer, RGBA projection candidates with null mappings, identical-hash cross-title reuse with/without approval, original source immutability, newly required sprite perimeter and deliberately unresolved draft. **Fixture created/updated only; NOT RUN.** Initial fake BNTX fixture byte-escape error corrected in source before any test execution.
- **Guide refreshed** `docs/IN_GAME_PLAYSTATION_GLYPHS.md`: runnable CLI examples for scanner/spec draft, direct BNTX inspect and safe atlas reuse, transparent border requirements, explicit limits and why PlayStation Auto menu mapping differs from game physical-button mapping. Licence still Zacksly CC BY 3.0 with mandatory acknowledgement.
- Commits `b9aa0d31955d` scanner, `d24705eddfc4` scanner host fixtures, `357f2c310739` BNTX inspector, `faaa338fcfda` BNTX scanner integration, `82a8b6bf41cb` synthetic NX fixture, `6905c9847c32` binary fixture escape correction, `634354adc24a` ranked discovery, `2af2b7d361b9` unapproved spec draft, `a008de981116` SHA-only reuse, `c6d77b450a00` sprite alpha bounds, `112040092abf` new fixtures, `3518d80daeeb` reuse type check, `f52c305d7f88` guide, `4840b5471303` safe output paths, `561fac58ecd` unresolved/opaque image fixtures. ALL `[skip ci]` on `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.
- Source inspection only. NO Python fixture executed, NO Python-based model benchmark, NO C++/PS5 build, NO Actions/CI, NO PS5 gameplay verification; preserve approved UI and release `fix/0.40-zbic-13.60`. Remaining real blockers to **all games**: actual title ROMFS/media fingerprints, BNTX/BFRES/ASTC/BC decoder/repacker with roundtrip/mips/swizzle preservation, reliable Nintendo glyph identity classification per scene, scene-dependent mapping vs PlayStation Auto, per-title regression/screenshots and reversible rollback. ### 2026-10-09 — PS5 firmware 13.60 field failure from all-on #232: deterministic 16 MiB sparse precommit overflow

- User tested *installable folder* created from [all-on #232](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/37926886141), artifacts from source SHA `e5d39849`, on real firmware `0x13600007`. The JIT sparse probe and RX/RW reservations SUCCEEDED. Critical interpretation: the 16 MiB failure is the **static over-capacity precommit request**, BEFORE PS5 direct physical mapping was attempted (no associated EDEN_JIT_SPARSE_OOM/MAP_FAILED). Earlier speculation that 12 GiB physical RAM was exhausted was wrong. Four A64 worker arenas were reserved (three large, final core 16 MiB); the final 16 MiB core necessarily fails when Dynarmic's 16 MiB PRELUDE_COMMIT_SIZE hint is added to ~2 MiB already written by its constant pool. Host CI mocks missed this edge despite all-on #232 going green.
- Fixed all-title sparse JIT precommit via `headless/jit-sparse-commit.h` and derived Dynarmic `BlockOfCode::EnsureMemoryCommitted` in `headless/CMakeLists.txt`: request up to the available **virtual** bytes without overflow; do not alter Xbyak's actual code-emission bounds, do not silently fall back to dense, and never treat virtual bytes as physically committed until native mapping succeeds. Emits `EDEN_JIT_SPARSE_PRECOMMIT_CLAMPED` only on a clipped hint. No FC27-specific branch, no experimental profile toggle, no approved UI changes, no protected shipping-branch change.
- Strengthened executable `tools/check-jit-sparse-host.py` to replay exact `2113536 + 16777216 > 16777216` values with a real host-mocked `Common::ReserveSparseJitCode` 16 MiB arena, commit to full boundary, byte alias and full cleanup; also checks invalid written positions, no unsigned overflow, and ordinary non-clamped growth. Updated architecture source gate.
- Separately reported symptom **FC27 not present in Library** cannot be proven from these three logs; no ROM filename inventory, directory listing or FC27 scan failure is captured. Existing `EdenServices::games()` did silently skip non-regular/stat-failed NSP/XCI and could publish an empty list on a native directory I/O error. Added single worker-thread `EDEN_ROM_SCAN` inventory diagnostics and first three failing stat filenames; on an enumeration error throw `std::system_error` so `Launcher::finish_scan` retains its prior list instead of emptying the UI. No files deleted or migrated. `tools/check-home-media.py` asserts these contracts.

### 2026-10-09 — Clarification du partage PS5 16 SMT / 8 shader slots [skip ci]

- Sony PS5: 8 Zen 2 physical cores, 16 SMT threads. R237 `reported=16 available=8` in `EDEN_PS5_SHADER_WORKERS` describes 16 reported hardware threads versus the shader thread's narrowed *secondary* affinity 0x1fe0. It is false to infer that Sony blocked 8 hardware threads. The 5 primary worker CPUs are scheduled separately; the hot guest 0–2 SMT siblings are deliberately protected from background contention. Previous trace does not establish actual OS-accessible thread count for main/probe thread.

### 2026-10-09 — Bounded private PS5 heap caches, source-only [skip ci]

- In `headless/heap_arenas.inc`, each thread previously retained up to 64 blocks in each of 127 size bins (up to around 8 MiB total per thread), making freed objects unavailable to other mspaces until that thread exits. This can promote unnecessary 128 MiB backing-piece growth across long-running games; it does NOT itself prove a leak of the ~1.375 GiB process-lifetime committed heap.
- Staged **1 MiB tcache cap per thread**; keep per-bin 64 cap and the 2 KiB cutoff. Free over cap returns directly to owning mspace, preserving ownership and malloc/free semantics. Track per-thread cached bytes with owner-write relaxed atomics (no shared counter on allocation hotpath) and expose approximate `EDEN_PERF_HEAP tcache_bytes` in existing snapshot. TLS destructor drains/free-lists and zeros held bytes. Host 8-thread heap harness includes multi-bin pressure, post-free and post-worker-join upper bounds; test script edited **not executed**.
- Physical 128 MiB backing pieces cannot safely be unmapped without firmware-verified mspace emptiness + child arena/TLS teardown + direct-memory PA metadata and proper virtual-range preservation. Not implemented. No Mac/FTP/build/test/Actions, no protected shipping branch change, no unqualified FPS improvement claim. User explicitly approves a run before qualification; FC27/BOTW performance/glyph issues still OPEN.

### 2026-10-09 — Direct-memory graphics GC transient-query failure suppression [skip ci]

### 2026-10-09 — Stop repeat heap piece leaks on growth mspace failure [skip ci]

- Found a real OOM escalation in `headless/heap_arenas.inc`: when a new physical 128 MiB backing commit succeeded but Sony `sceLibcMspaceCreate` failed, the piece became an orphan. - `Game::docked` is now calculated on the existing **async ROM/mod scan worker**. `refresh_selected_game()` reads the immutable in-memory effective flag, never storage. Same-file rescan now refreshes selected mode instead of waiting for a changed ROM list.
- After a saved per-title setting, Home or Library updates the cached effective mode. Global preferences saves schedule an asynchronous refresh; if a scan is in flight a one-time repeat is scheduled after completion so old values cannot silently persist. Existing immediate Home hero cache invalidation remains.
- Added source-only `check-runtime-frame-budget.py` regression contracts. No SDK build, tests, GitHub Actions, PS5 playback or claimed frame-time gain; confirm under held D-pad and compare `EDEN_UI_HOTSPOT`/`EDEN_UI_FRAMES` at authorized hardware test.

### 2026-10-09 — Complete mapped-VA extent check before PS5 JIT and CPU direct backing [skip ci]

- `src/memory_pages.cpp` already declared a checked CPU mapping window `cpu_mapping_range(base, size)`, but `AllocateMemoryPages` and the dense JIT's `MapExecutableAlias` validated only the **first address** with `cpu_mapping_address()`. A positive kernel mapping that starts inside the allowed region yet extends into the high GPU/device VA range was accepted. Now validate the **whole span**, unmap any successful out-of-window alias before releasing owned physical direct RAM, and return allocation failure cleanly. The sparse page-table zero-block scratch alias also validates the complete 2 MiB extent before zeroing, with explicit ordered cleanup on rejected success.

### 2026-10-09 — Protect sparse page-table remaps from unexpected fixed-map aliases [skip ci]

- `MapSlot()` formerly returned false if `sceKernelMapDirectMemory(..., MAP_FIXED)` returned a **different** virtual address, but did not unmap that successful foreign alias before the caller released or reused its backing physical page. This could leave an orphan physical alias under unusual kernel behavior. Now a successful unexpected alias is explicitly unmapped before the caller receives failure; an error with a mutated address aborts rather than guessing mapping ownership. Ordinary successful fixed maps and regular failures (unchanged address) retain prior behavior. Source preflight contract added; native firmware semantics still unqualified.

### 2026-10-09 — Remove global dev HLE profiler mutex/map from every guest IPC request [skip ci]

- The all-on PS5 test build instruments every guest `InvokeRequest`/`InvokeRequestTipc`. The prior `RecordHle` acquired a **single mutex** and performed `std::map` lookup on **every service command** across guest cores, injecting profiler contention and allocator pressure directly into FC27's workload. Its map also retained non-owned service-name pointers across title lifetimes.
- Introduced `headless/hle_counters.h`: 4,096 bounded preallocated service-name/command slots; stable text-content FNV-1a hash instead of pointer identity; owned 80-byte diagnostic name per slot; lock only while first registering a new pair, then atomic call/ns totals with no lock or map allocation for normal requests. Snapshots iterate atomics without contending with guest HLE dispatch. An overflow aggregate preserves total accounting when all slots are occupied. No change to game HLE behavior or IPC sequencing, only diagnostic aggregation.
- Integrated a dedicated C++20 eight-thread host stress/recycled-service-name/fixed-table-overflow fixture `tools/check-hle-counter-contention.py` into the explicit GitHub all-on preflight. This reduces expected diagnostic overhead but **does not establish actual FC27 FPS improvement** until a compiled native build and paired console logs. No CI/build/test launched in this edit.

### 2026-10-09 — HLE first-registration race closed before native compile [skip ci]

- Review identified a publication race in the new fixed HLE profiler: if two workers first saw the same empty hash slot, the second waited for the registration mutex; after the first published the same service/command, the second could skip that slot and insert a duplicate farther in the table. Corrected the under-lock recheck to merge into the newly published **same** entry, not skip it. Host eight-thread fixture now explicitly requires all 35 unique service/command identities, each reported once, with unchanged exact aggregate counts and no overflow for the normal stress case. ### 2026-10-09 — Hard bound per-command HLE diagnostic probe depth [skip ci]

- Prevented a diagnostic self-inflicted worst-case: with 4,096 hash slots, a game with thousands of distinct service/command pairs could make **every subsequent hot HLE call scan thousands of slots** before incrementing its overflow counter. Each call now probes at most 64 consecutive slots; collisions/near-full clusters spill into atomic aggregate overflow. The source host fixture explicitly accepts overflow before complete table occupancy but requires `attributed_calls + overflow_calls == total_calls` and matching nanoseconds, and retains exact 35-key multithread attribution at normal occupancy. Bounded runtime overhead takes priority over per-command detail when saturated. No test run.

### 2026-10-09 — Fail-closed on mutated output pointer from failed PS5 direct map syscall [skip ci]

A failed `sceKernelMapDirectMemory` returning a **different output pointer** was previously treated like an ordinary failure: the caller released physical backing despite uncertain VA alias ownership. Now each of these paths **aborts on an error-mutated output** rather than risk releasing a still-mapped physical page. Ordinary errors with unchanged pointer still return gracefully, and successful but out-of-window aliases still unmap before direct-memory release. ### 2026-10-09 — Fast negative ownership filter for direct large malloc/free [skip ci]

- Audited the heap's per-call ownership dispatch: when **any** >=32 MiB direct-owned allocation was alive, `eden_heap_large_find()` previously scanned up to **256 atomic address slots** for every foreign `free`, `realloc`, or `malloc_usable_size`, even though almost all libc pointers have never belonged to an owned direct block. This is avoidable guest CPU cache/memory contention.
- Added a **4 KiB monotonic two-hash Bloom filter** in `headless/heap_arenas.inc`, populated **before** publishing each successfully allocated large block. The lookup skips all 256 slots when either membership bit is absent; positive pointers still use the exact original address comparison, and past bits never clear (so stale positives may cost work but may NEVER wrongly route an owned block to libc). No new dynamic allocation, mutex, physical backing or change to direct ownership/free semantics.
- Host growth fixture now keeps a real large block live while it exercises foreign libc allocation → wrap realloc → wrap free 1000 times, asserting the owned block remains Bloom-positive and at least one foreign pointer is filtered. **Not run**, not native-qualified, no claimed FC27 FPS boost.

### 2026-10-09 — Remove thousands of snprintf and reallocations from live GPU PC block dumps [skip ci]

### 2026-10-09 — Isolate heavy development PC snapshot from guest CPU workers [skip ci]

- `Performance::Snapshot()` runs every five seconds from the PS5 render thread and from optional host captures. Its original single `std::lock_guard(workers_mutex)` covered **all** host-PC histogram maps, native/guest block hex dumps, sorting, scheduler/clock syscalls and `std::fflush`, so guest cores calling `SampleCpu()` and the frontend `PollGpuPc()` could be blocked by the profiler itself during a potentially very expensive GPU-thread report.
- Split synchronization: new `snapshot_mutex` serializes only independent snapshot/report consumers and their PC cursors, while `workers_mutex` now protects exclusively an immutable copy of `workers` and `cpu_samples`. The snapshot's syscalls, print loops and block dumps use those local copies after unlocking. Added `EDEN_DEV_SNAPSHOT_COST mono_ns=… elapsed_ns=…` in development to expose the report's own wall-time disturbance. The GPU render thread can still stall running the report, but guest worker publication and PC polling do not wait for its heavy formatting.

### 2026-10-09 — Rolling PC profiler samples and bounded guest sampler thread lifetime [skip ci]

- In development `pc_fast=on`, a detached 500 Hz guest-core signal thread previously ran until the fixed **65,536-sample** array filled, then profiling silently stopped (~131 s after fast sampling began); the native GPU sample buffer similarly stopped at 8192 samples (~16 s at 500 Hz). That breaks FC27 profiling later in the same match or after an in-process relaunch, and a detached sampler can outlive the guest thread.
- For normal PC-only mode, sample slots now use **lock-free atomic uintptr_t circular buffers** (8192 GPU, 65536 guest). The single-owner signal handler stores its PC before release-publishing the monotonically increasing sequence number; Snapshot reads with acquire, clamps to the last capacity entries, and explicitly logs `EDEN_PERF_PC_SAMPLES_LOST source=gpu|guest count=N` when consumer lag drops older PCs. Concurrent wrap accesses use atomic slots. Special `EDEN_DEV_WAIT_CALLERS` remains GPU-bounded because its eight-word caller chains are not atomic.
- Replaced the detached 500 Hz generator with a **thread-local `std::jthread`** on the owner guest CPU thread. Its 45-second boot delay is chunked into 200ms stop-aware sleeps; teardown requests stop and joins instead of leaking sampler workers across games. Guest sampler TLS registration clears `core_sample_ready` on exit. The sampler is placed on verified secondary slots where available. Source guards staged; no native compile, signal ABI validation, or firmware timing test yet.

### 2026-10-09 — Keep sampling pthread_kill out of guest CPU publication mutex [skip ci]

### 2026-10-09 — Clear stale GPU/CPU thread registrations at owner exit [skip ci]

- An in-process return to Library followed by another title destroys/recreates native GPU and guest CPU workers. Previous `RegisterWorker()` wrote `workers[i].registered=true` but never cleared it on thread exit; `PollGpuPc()` could target an exited/recycled GPU `pthread_t`, and periodic worker snapshots could report stale CPU clocks/affinity as current.
- Added a tiny `thread_local WorkerRegistration` owner hook that locks `workers_mutex` only **on thread exit**, verifies the recorded `pthread_t` still matches the slot and marks the slot unregistered. TLS hook is touched before the PC sampler objects so C++ reverse destruction joins the fast `std::jthread` first, then clears core readiness, then unregisters the worker. No new GPU/guest hotpath lock and no false claim that a kill begun before teardown can be canceled retroactively.
- Existing `PollGpuPc()` now copies the registered GPU target under the mutex and sends only after unlock. Source contract checks identity, registration and construction order. No native execution, thread lifecycle test or GitHub Actions triggered.

### 2026-10-09 — Prove stale worker-slot teardown with extracted C++ host test [skip ci]

### 2026-10-09 — Unify PS5 virtual reservation VA ownership for heap, sparse tables and JIT [skip ci]

- Five native paths independently called `sceKernelReserveVirtualRange` with a mutable output pointer: sparse-JIT alias probe RW+RX, long-lived RW+RX JIT reservations, sparse zero-table reservation and growing 3 GiB heap. Several returned after syscall failure without checking **a changed output VA**, and sparse/heap out-of-window cleanup ignored `munmap` errors, potentially losing ownership and hiding a VA leak across title relaunches.
- Added `ReserveCpuVirtualRange(bytes,alignment)` with one exact contract: zero-size fails; unsuccessful unmodified hint returns null; error **mutating the hint aborts** rather than silently abandon an uncertain reservation; success must fit the full CPU VA window or be fully unmapped (abort if cleanup cannot be proven). Wired all five reservation families to the same helper. Existing caller rollback still owns already successful RW reservations when RX fails, and sparse-table partial alias failure now checks `munmap` return. This is a hardening of exceptional paths, not proof the firmware uses this ABI or the memory OOM is fixed.
- Source contracts staged in `tools/check-ps5-sparse-jit-va-lifetime.py`; no C++ compile, CI, test or console run.

It also avoids accessing host pointer 0 when PageType::Memory but pointer missing: reports guest unmapped, uses zero-fill on reads and skips writes. - 2026-10-10 source-only compile guard discovery: `PS5_NATIVE=1` is PRIVATE only on `common` and `eden-headless` (and Dynarmic's one block_of_code.cpp); not automatically inherited by pinned `core/memory.cpp` or `video_core/host1x/gpu_device_memory_manager.cpp`. Without targeted definitions new GPU/guest mapping fixes compile out! Scoped `set_property(SOURCE ... TARGET_DIRECTORY ... COMPILE_DEFINITIONS "PS5_NATIVE=1")` to exact core original/derived memory.cpp and host1x GPU manager translation units, avoiding whole-engine #ifdef changes. Pinned PS5 source-check now asserts both flags. No build or runtime confirmation.

- 2026-10-10 potential legitimate pointer-delta-zero recovery: pinned Eden `PageEntryData::Pointer()` treats zero as "missing"; MapPages stores host-minus-guest page base, so coincident host and guest VAs produce a ZERO delta across a contiguous mapping. In source, `GetPointerImpl` incorrectly rejects this, preventing GPU DeviceMemoryManager Map from seeing a valid backing page and producing missing-texture/unmapped-read symptoms. New pinned `eden-ps5-guest-zero-alias.patch` detects it ONLY if entire read/write address lies within real DeviceMemory backing (base + KSystemControl::Init::GetIntendedMemorySize), restores direct host pointer in CPU GetPointerImpl and WalkBlock, and records guest_alias_mapped/guest_alias_access counts. All other invalid pages still fail closed. Strong source-level candidate for FC27 black backgrounds/5120 map asserts, not verified on hardware. No build/CI/native tests run.

- 2026-10-10 guest CPU direct-span correctness source-only: pinned Eden `Memory::Impl::GetSpan` checks `(addr+size)>>12` even though the final touched byte is `addr+size-1`, so page-aligned spans check a spurious next page (and can index outside max AS). Same initial/final block number does not guarantee intermediate pages are still mapped. Added `eden-ps5-guest-span.patch`: PS5-only range bounds, correct final page, O(1) single-page fast path, validate intervening page pointer deltas/types/blocks for multi-page spans, const/nonconst share one algorithm. This may prevent malformed texture/CPU buffer direct access; uncompiled and untested on PS5. Source test and backport validator included.

- 2026-10-10 PS5 per-title mapping counters: the six inline atomic GPU + guest fault counters were process-cumulative, making FC27/BOTW and repeated title sessions ambiguous after a launcher return. Added `Eden::GpuFault::ResetTitleCounters()` for all 6 once per new title, before `system.Load` and only after prior owners' full teardown. Next `EDEN_GPU_UNMAPPED_COUNTERS` snapshots refer to the current title, not previous title’s error storm; no heavy per-frame cost. Source-only guard added; no native test/compile.

- 2026-10-10 PS5 GPU reverse-map replacement lifecycle: pinned Eden `DeviceMemoryManager::Map` overwrote `tracked_entries[gpu_page].compressed_physical_ptr` without unregistering an existing reverse `compressed_device_addr[old_phys]`; remapping the same backing registered an additional MultiAddressContainer member, retaining stale aliases and making later invalidation unreliable. New pinned incremental backport `eden-ps5-gpu-remap-reverse.patch` (after `eden-ps5-gpu-memory-mapping.patch`) detects old/replacement physical pages under existing `mapping_guard`, skips duplicate reverse re-registration for same physical mapping while refreshing CPU page backing, and removes previous reverse page from single/multi associations before installing new; on a mismatched single-reverse value it records sampled warning and leaves unrelated reverse entry untouched. Two counters `remap_replaced` and `remap_mismatch` added to per-title GPU snapshot and reset. Source-only, no native build, shader rendering or heap-reclamation validation. Distinct from direct physical heap issue; unsafe wholesale mspace free remains explicitly prohibited.

- 2026-10-10 GPU Unmap inverse-map correction: pinned device memory manager clears `compressed_device_addr[old_phys]` even when its direct reverse mapping refers to a DIFFERENT GPU page. A repeated/overwritten guest mapping can therefore erase a valid texture cache alias. New minimal incremental `eden-ps5-gpu-unmap-reverse-guard.patch` after remap cleanup checks `base_dev == retiring_page` before clearing direct inverse reference, logs sampled `EDEN_GPU_UNMAP_REVERSE_MISMATCH` otherwise and preserves the unrelated reverse entry. `Map` and `Unmap` reverse ownership now consistent for single direct mapping without corrupting other pages. Source-only, not native-compiled or hardware-verified.

- 2026-10-10 PS5 reverse multi-mapping defensive fix: pinned `MultiAddressContainer::Unregister` iterates storage by next_entry without missing-value / cycle bounds. A stale multi-reverse mapping from remaps (or corrupted guest mapping metadata) can dereference `storage[-1]` and crash. New incremental pinned `eden-ps5-gpu-multi-missing-guard.patch` adds PS5-only bounded `Contains(value,head)` (checks invalid index and cycle) and calls it ONLY before multi-list unlink in Map/Unmap, not on the hot one-page GPU read path; invalid link logs sampled `EDEN_GPU_REMAP_MULTI_MISSING` or `EDEN_GPU_UNMAP_MULTI_MISSING` and retains unrelated reverse state rather than dereferencing invalid storage. No compiler/console run; strict source replay and validators pending.

- 2026-10-10 GPU Map/Unmap bounds preflight `cdafa83b` and counters `f6914578`: pinned upstream GPU DeviceMemoryManager called sparse-table CommitRegion/driver InvalidateRegion without validating device virtual range; Map also lacked guest virtual span bound. Added PS5-only incremental `eden-ps5-gpu-map-bounds.patch` after other reverse fixes; size0 is silent no-op, malformed nonzero range rejected via subtraction-safe `address>=device_as_size || size > device_as_size-address` and guest-as-size guards BEFORE allocation/invalidation. Counters `bad_map_range`, `bad_unmap_range` exact per title; power-of-two sampled logs. Source check and pinned receipt integrated. No PS5 build/CI/hardware validation; no claims FC27 black textures or 0 FPS solved.

- 2026-10-10 sparse table physical-slot commit vs decommit interleaving: `ZeroRegion` clears host-page bitmap entries and decommits a 2 MiB private slot when the bitmap looks empty. `CommitPage` previously raced the final scan so a new writer could publish a page then have the entire slot remapped read-only/shared zero (lost data and potential fault). Native generated sparse header now uses **per SparseLargeVector** `std::mutex` held by `ZeroRegion` across bitmap + decommit and by `CommitPage` across CommitSparsePage + bitmap publication; double-check `IsCommittedPage` after locking. `GetOrDefault` and already committed accesses retain lock-free fast paths. The test `tools/check-sparse-index-boundary.py` checks CMake injected locking alongside prior one-past-end fix. This is source-only, not compiled on PS5; externally concurrent logical remap vs an actual write still requires caller sync.

- 2026-10-10 native SparseRange lifetime hardening: `src/memory_pages.cpp::CommitSparsePage` previously read `SparseRangeOf(page)` and dereferenced `range->owned[slot]` **before** `sparse_mutex`. Concurrent `FreeSparsePages` under the mutex can deallocate that bitmap or reuse the range record -> use-after-free/wrong physical slot mapping. Moved the sparse mutex acquisition to the beginning of `CommitSparsePage` and performed range lookup, bitmap check and `OwnSlot` all under the same lock. Only a first-commit slow path takes this lock; ordinary sparse-table hot reads stay lock-free. Added a strict order check to `tools/check-sparse-index-boundary.py`. Works together with per-vector ZeroRegion/CommitPage synchronization, but cannot legalize accessing a SparseLargeVector object after its destructor. No PS5 build/hardware validation.

- 2026-10-10 PS5 sparse table stale-page contents: generated `SparseLargeVector::DecommitPage` previously cleared the HostPageSize commit bitmap and, when any OTHER page in the same 2 MiB physical slot remained committed, simply returned without zeroing the retired host page. Re-committing that host page called `CommitSparsePage`, which found slot already owned and did not remap/zero; old guest/GPU page translations could silently resurrect. Dense-fallback ZeroRegion was broken similarly because DecommitSparsePage is a no-op for dense allocation. Fixed in derived `sparse_private_replacement`: memset the retiring known-committed host page to zero *before* clearing its bitmap/deciding whether to return or reclaim entire slot. Uses existing per-vector ZeroRegion/CommitPage mutation lock, no extra per-frame work. New source order/model regression in `tools/check-sparse-index-boundary.py`. No host compiler or PS5 binary test yet.

- 2026-10-10 CPU→GPU reverse-map inline callback hardening: pinned `src/core/device_memory_manager.h::ApplyOpOnPAddr` read `compressed_device_addr[physical_page]` without validating `physical_page`, and treated reverse value 0 (no GPU mapping) as GPU VA 0, causing unrelated invalidation. `ApplyOpOnPointer` subtracted `physical_base` without checking p was inside actual backing, and `GetPhysicalRawAddressFromDAddr` indexed the GPU table without checking virtual page range. Added pinned header backport `eden-ps5-gpu-reverse-inline-bounds.patch` (three hunks), zero-mapping fast return, DRAM and GPU VA bounds. No global mapping lock added on per-texture hot reads. Header implementation works on both host/PS5 for consistent inline definitions across translation units. Source validator wired; no host compiler/native PS5 FPS validation.

- 2026-10-10 further GPU multi-reverse safety: pinned `MultiAddressContainer::Unregister` can return zero new head when it removed a last remaining node from a corrupted/degenerate "multi" reverse list, but Map and Unmap previously called `ReleaseEntry(0)` and dereferenced `storage[-1]`. Added `eden-ps5-gpu-empty-multi-head.patch` as pinned post-remap source backport to return reverse sentinel zero on empty head, leaving ordinary two-node transitions unchanged. Applied in both remap and unmap, source validator guards both. This is fail-closed defense for malformed reverse state, not a claim of renderer/FPS repair; no PS5 compile/test.

- **2026-10-10 R254 — avoid unsigned overflow in Vulkan texture residency/GC budgets:** The pinned Eden `RunGarbageCollector` PS5 Vulkan prefetch used `u64 usage = total_used_memory; usage -= ReclaimedBytes(image);` with no underflow protection. - **2026-10-10 R258 / Vulkan GC staging ownership correction (host gate requested):** The prefetch path in `headless/vulkan_gc_downloads.inc` stored staging map descriptors by **copy**, before calling `image.DownloadMemory(map, copies)`, unlike the already validated normal Vulkan readback path that moves its descriptor into the deferred batch. - **2026-10-10 R259 — pinned Vulkan staging audit corrects R258 premise, and fixes actual early-frame GC overflow:** Inspection of the EXACT upstream Eden mirror at pinned commit `5f142c7926d0c7fcbbd0ce30794d72f638a43b2a` shows `vk_staging_buffer_pool.h::StagingBufferRef` is a trivially copyable, non-owning value descriptor (VkBuffer, span, offset, usage, level, index); the pool, **not the descriptor destructor**, owns its lifetime. Hence R258's claim that copying this handle caused a RAII double-release/UAF was **incorrect**, and its move-only host mock was not representative of production. Restored the original staging reference copy-before-recording ordering and removed the misleading mock from both CI gates. R258's prior host green result proves only that synthetic model, NOT a real Vulkan lifecycle fix. Independently verified `texture_cache_base.h` initializes unsigned `u64 frame_tick = 0`, while the pinned `RunGarbageCollector` passes `frame_tick - ticks_to_destroy` to `lru_cache.ForEachItemBelow` **twice**, with ages 10/25/50. When immediate texture pressure enters GC during the first frames, unsigned subtraction wraps. The pinned LRU's signed comparison actually treats the wrapped number as a negative sentinel and normally **skips**, rather than evicts, new textures; the earlier claim that this alone explained startup texture loss was incorrect. We make that grace period explicit so it cannot regress when removing the wrap. Added nonallocating `::Eden::VulkanMemory::OldestEvictionTick(frame_tick, min_age)` to `headless/vulkan_gc_budget.h` (clamps to 0). The pinned generator now fail-closed checks/replaces **all three** LRU cutoff expressions (one Vulkan lookahead and two common cleanup loops), and guards the lookahead and BOTH cleanup passes so an inclusive LRU cutoff of zero cannot accidentally evict textures touched at frame zero. The policy after age threshold is unchanged. Extended the existing `tools/check-vulkan-gc-budget-host.py` with source transformation/age-guard checks and C++20 ASan/UBSan tests for 0..109 frames, all three GC age thresholds, boundary/UINT64_MAX and 200,000 randomized cases. **HOST CI NOT YET DISPATCHED** as of this note; request only `[core-ready]` preflight, no native build. This is a bounded correctness fix, not observed PS5 FPS/texture proof or CPU/GPU/GDDR6 saturation. Issue #8 remains open.

- **R259 follow-up correction / host-only validation request:** The pinned `common/lru_cache.h::ForEachItemBelow` includes its cutoff; replacing wrapped u64 with zero without an age gate would turn safe no-eviction at frame 0 into an early eviction. Added `frame_tick >= ticks_to_destroy` guards for both generated GC cleanup loops and `frame_tick < ticks_to_destroy` early return inside Vulkan prefetch. - **2026-10-10 R280 — Vulkan present worker in-flight completion / error propagation (HOST CI REQUESTED):** Compared exact pinned Eden mirror `5f142c79` present manager with current PS5 generated patch. `WaitPresent()` could return when present queue became empty merely because worker popped its final frame, even though `CopyToSwapchain()` was still in progress, and earlier `present_failure || queue.empty()` patch could silently return after exception. - **2026-10-10 R281 — release free-frame mutex before blocking on a Vulkan present fence (HOST CI REQUESTED):** In the exact pinned `vk_present_manager.cpp`, `PresentManager::GetRenderFrame()` held `free_mutex` during `frame->present_done.Wait()` and `.Reset()` even after popping that frame from the queue. Since `PresentThread()` needs the same mutex to return *other* completed frames into `free_queue`, a long GPU fence wait could serially block the producer's completion handoff and amplify frame backlog. New host concurrent stand-in creates a blocked per-frame fence and uses `try_lock` to assert the unrelated frame producer can acquire the free-queue mutex/recycle another frame during it; covered by existing R280 host ASan/UBSan/TSan test and the `[core-ready]` suite. ### 2026-10-12 R335 — prevent permanent Vulkan surface-loss retries

- Source-level liveness bug: pinned `vk_present_manager.cpp` `PresentManager::CopyToSwapchain` catches `VK_ERROR_SURFACE_LOST_KHR` inside `while(true)` and can recreate repeatedly forever on a permanently unavailable surface, monopolizing the present thread and withholding frame handoff. This is distinct from the FC27 30-FPS live-render menu freeze, whose cause remains unresolved.
- Upstream Eden 2026-10-08 commit `3cdd2ce141224079ce1dc8bfb4be7edc113aca02` (#4509) fixes retries. R335 source generator backports only `MAX_PRESENT_ATTEMPTS=3`, bounded retry, `DiscardFrame` (empty graphics submit consumes frame render_ready semaphore and signals present_done under submit mutex), and the associated method declaration. Other Android renderer default changes are deliberately excluded.
- New source-sha-pinned replay + host compiled actual body `tools/check-ps5-vulkan-present-retry-liveness.py`: original FAIL after 4 surface loss events (exceeds desired bound); R335 PASS 3 attempts/1 frame discard, 2 losses then success, 0 losses success; checks real semaphore/fence abandon. See docs `PS5_R335_2026-10-12_VULKAN_SURFACE_LOST_BOUNDED_RETRY.md`.

### 2026-10-12 R336 candidate — PS5 Vulkan swapchain metadata race between GPU and presenter

- R335 confirms the upstream October 8 `#4509` native Vulkan present bounded retries. ### 2026-10-12 R337 candidate — secondary Vulkan present infinite acquisition-recreation loop

- After R335 capped outer surface-loss recovery, found **another** unbounded `while(swapchain.AcquireNextImage()) { RecreateSwapchain(frame); }` inside `PresentManager::CopyToSwapchainImpl`. `Swapchain::AcquireNextImage()` returns true on every VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR / VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_KHR, and `Swapchain::Create()` resets status flags. ### 2026-10-12 R363 — guaranteed-only native descriptor ring pre-drain

- Audit of exact compiled sources found that DescriptorBufferRing::Allocate can exhaust the last frame chunk and call scheduler.Finish() inside RasterizerVulkan::PrepareDraw paired buffer/texture mutexes. R323 only moved frame-reuse Wait; R360 only counted the late Finish. Old October 11 cached logs show no explicit exhaustion message, so rate of the older test binary incidence is UNKNOWN (DEBUG logging may omit it). Not a proven FC27 root cause.
- R363 moves that existing full-ring Finish to BEFORE both cache locks only when a GraphicsPipeline has descriptor-buffer enabled, cached allocation generation or payload count differs (thus new allocation is guaranteed if Configure reaches it), descriptor size is valid and the final ring chunk is insufficient. No preflight when payload may be reused; Allocate retains its original guarded Finish fallback. After preflight, flush guest caching and reselect pipeline.
- PreflightCapacity performs the original scheduler.Finish before reusing the ring, resets cursor/chunk and increments generation. Maintained native sources and pinned-source generator must remain byte-equal. Host source-extracted C++ regression checks no extra Finish on normal frames, exact fit, another chunk, reusable payload, disabled extension, pending frame recycle or oversized request; verifies one outside-lock completion and generation invalidation.
- DescriptorRingPreflight versus DescriptorRingFinish sample counters distinguish the moved wait from under-lock fallback; only detailed diagnostics on actual rare waits pay timer cost. Quiet normal draw paths are unchanged.
- Source-only qualification pending native CI and PS5 game validation. Do not claim fixed FC27 stutter, texture/HUD issues or input/menu freeze; other buffer/texture cache waits still exist, and no fences were removed.

### 2026-10-12 R382 — pre-dispatch command chunks BEFORE GPU cache locks

- SHA-proven R370 live frozen match: ~809645 sampled GPU Configure draws (1/16 sample), mean pair-held 9.478us, Configure 8.331us, MAX pair-held 1024us, Configure 1014us.
