`SETTINGS.md`:

```md
# Prospero.Eden Encore — Settings guide

> **Exactly the 31 official PS5 system language/region choices; 31 launcher translation catalogs (including en-US and en-GB):** [Language directory](LANGUAGES.md). No extra launcher languages are exposed. This strict policy follows [Sony's official console-language list](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/); translation/font quality still requires validation.


This guide explains the settings exposed by Encore on PS5, their defaults, and practical starting profiles.

> **Important:** TV output and Game resolution are different. TV output is the final image sent to the display. Game resolution is the internal Switch render scale before scaling.

## Factory defaults

A clean Encore configuration starts with:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Renderer | **Vulkan** |
| Video preset | **Recommended** |
| TV output | **1440p** |
| Game resolution | **1.25x** |
| Upscaling filter | **FSR 1 (spatial)** |
| FSR sharpness | **50%** |
| Texture filtering (anisotropy) | **4x** |
| Frame Generation | **Off (extra)** |
| Neural Rendering | **Off (extra)** |
| DLSS-NR intensity | **100% stored, inactive when NR is Off** |
| Anti-aliasing | **FXAA** (Recommended) |
| Refresh rate | **60 Hz** |
| FPS overlay | **Off** |
| Console mode | **Docked** |
| Stick deadzone | **8%** |
| Vibration | **100%** |
| Detailed logging | **Off** |
| Language | Seeded from the PS5 system language on first setup |

A clean configuration starts on the authored **Recommended** tier. Selecting another Video preset rewrites the video settings owned by that tier; manual edits become Custom when they no longer match an authored profile.

## Video presets

| Preset | Renderer | TV output | Game resolution | Filter | FSR sharpness | AA | Refresh |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| **Minimum** | Vulkan | 1080p | 1x | Bilinear | 50% | None | 60 Hz |
| **Recommended** | Vulkan | 1440p | 1.25x | **FSR 1** | 50% | **FXAA** | 60 Hz |
| **High** | Vulkan | 2160p | 1.5x | Bicubic | 50% | **FXAA** | 60 Hz |
| **Ultra** | Vulkan | 2160p | 2x | Bilinear | 50% | None | 60 Hz |

Presets are real starting points, not labels. They are generated from `encore-overrides`, and a title-specific profile can refine a tier without changing the global choice. After applying one, every advanced row can still be changed manually. If the resulting combination no longer matches an authored tier, Encore shows **Custom** (`Personnalisé` in French); matching a tier again restores its label automatically. The same behavior applies to per-game overrides.

## Video settings

### Renderer

- **Vulkan — default/recommended.** Main PS5 renderer.
- **OpenGL.** Compatibility fallback for a title with a Vulkan-specific problem.

Do not use OpenGL only because a title is slow unless Vulkan is known to be the cause.

### TV output

Available: **1080p, 1440p, 2160p**.

This is the final output surface. It is not the internal game resolution. A 2160p output can look cleaner on a 4K TV, but it also increases presentation and bandwidth work.

For demanding titles, 1080p or 1440p is the safer starting point even on a 4K television.

### Game resolution

Available:

**0.25x · 0.5x · 0.75x · 1x · 1.25x · 1.5x · 2x · 3x · 4x**

- **1x.** Native Switch render scale and a useful lighter manual choice.
- **0.75x.** Useful performance compromise, especially with FSR.
- **0.5x / 0.25x.** Emergency performance or diagnostic values; visibly softer.
- **1.25x — Recommended tier.** Moderate supersampling while keeping sensible PS5 headroom.
- **1.5x.** Higher-quality supersampling for titles with spare GPU headroom.
- **2x and above.** Expensive in GPU time and graphics memory; not normal PS5 defaults.

Docked and Handheld modes can also change what the game itself chooses to render.

### Upscaling filter

- **Bilinear.** Lightest general-purpose scaler, useful as a manual fallback or when using a Neural Rendering mode.
- **AMD FSR 1 — Recommended default (spatial only).** Particularly useful when Game resolution is below TV output; this is not temporal FSR 3.1.
- **Bicubic.** Sharper conventional scaling.
- **Nearest.** Mainly useful for pixel-art or diagnostics.

### FSR sharpness

Range: **0–100%**, changed in 5% steps. Factory value: **50%**.

Higher is not automatically better. Too much sharpening can make grass, hair, crowds and thin lines look noisy or grainy.

Useful starting points:

- **40–55%** for 0.75x with FSR;
- **25–45%** if the image looks grainy;
- increase only when the image is clearly too soft.

### Anti-aliasing

In the regular UI: **None, FXAA, SMAA Ultra, FXAA+** (the last mode is Vulkan-only). MSAA 2x/4x/8x/16x values exist in the settings schema, but the native forced-sample path is not qualified as a selectable GPU option; a stored setting is not proof of working MSAA.

- **None — fastest manual choice.**
- **FXAA — Recommended preset.** Light smoothing with a small clarity trade-off.
- **SMAA.** Better edge quality, but use it only when performance headroom remains.

### Refresh rate

- **60 Hz — default/recommended.**
- **120 Hz.** Requests a 120 Hz output mode when the display supports it.

120 Hz does not turn a 30 FPS game into a 120 FPS game. Encore exposes optional frame-generation choices (MihawkGen, FSR 3 optical flow and LSFG with a user-supplied DLL), all **Off by default**. Selection does not mean a generated frame has been validated on PS5. For the separate research paths to improve *real* game FPS and investigate 30→60 **display** FPS via interpolation, see [Performance roadmap](docs/PERFORMANCE_ROADMAP.md). Synthetic FPS must never be presented as native game FPS.

### FPS overlay

**Off by default.** Useful while tuning or diagnosing a title.

### In-game Encore quick overlay (Vulkan)

**Short-click the DualSense touchpad**, not the PS button, to open the purple
translucent in-game quick menu. Use L1/R1 to switch between Game, Graphics,
Controller Mapping and Diagnostics. FPS visibility and bounded detailed logs
can be toggled there instead of using the retired touchpad + R1 FPS shortcut.
Per-game graphics and controller mapping changes are saved for the next launch.
The existing touchpad long hold remains guest Minus when the overlay is closed;
OpenGL games keep their previous guest tap behavior.

Full controls, limits and validation status:
[PS5 touchpad quick overlay](docs/PS5_TOUCHPAD_QUICK_OVERLAY.md).

## Console mode

- **Docked — default.** Usually asks the game for its higher graphics targets.
- **Handheld.** Can reduce the game's own workload and is worth testing on demanding titles.

This is a game-side mode change, not merely a TV-output setting.

## Neural Rendering and Frame Generation — optional extras

Both features default to **Off**. Standard Minimum, Recommended, High and Ultra presets change the spatial/AA/resolution settings without silently enabling neural effects or synthetic frames.

- **Neural Rendering choices:** Off, A4K Détails améliorés, A4K Image adoucie, A4K Image nettoyée, DLSS-NR Original, and DLSS-NR Compact. The A4K family belongs to Neural Rendering, not Upscaling.
- **DLSS-NR intensity:** 0–100% (stored default 100%). Editable only with Original or Compact. It remains saved when selecting A4K or Off; the source catalog does not yet contain measured per-title intensity recommendations.
- **Composition guardrails:** Vulkan only; the currently supported policy requires Bilinear spatial scaling, no concurrent Frame Generation, and no forced MSAA. These conservative limitations must not be mistaken for permanent renderer capabilities.
- **DLSS-NR runtime:** The two models can be selected and persisted, but the full native image graph is not yet proven to render a complete frame on PS5.

The classic Encore and Switch-style visual themes must expose the same extras, including their per-game inherited values. No change to a video preset should turn either extra on without an explicit user action.

## Per-game video settings

Library → Game settings can override the global configuration for one title:

- Renderer
- Video preset
- TV output
- Game resolution
- Upscaling filter
- FSR sharpness
- Anti-aliasing
- Texture filtering (anisotropy)
- Frame Generation (Off/explicit method)
- Neural Rendering (Off/A4K/DLSS-NR)
- DLSS-NR intensity (stored independently)
- Refresh rate
- Console mode

A per-game value of **Default** means “follow the global setting”. Resetting the game overrides returns those rows to the global configuration.

## Controls

Encore exposes four controller profiles globally and per game:

| Profile | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| **PlayStation** — default | PS-style Cross/Circle menu semantics. In the stock profile, Encore can switch to physical Switch face-button positions during sustained gameplay input and return to menu context with hysteresis. |
| **Switch** | Fixed Nintendo-position face-button layout. No automatic context switching. |
| **Custom PS5** | User-defined mapping derived from the PlayStation layout. Fixed exactly as configured. |
| **Custom Switch** | User-defined mapping derived from the Switch layout. Fixed exactly as configured. |

Settings → Controls → Button mapping can assign the emulated A/B/X/Y, L/R/ZL/ZR, Plus/Minus and stick-click actions to DualSense buttons. A title can use its own mapping without changing the global one.

The adaptive behavior applies **only** to the untouched PlayStation profile. Switch and both Custom profiles are never rewritten automatically. The profile's thresholds are generated from `encore-overrides/general/controls.json` with the video-profile snapshot.

Defaults:

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Button profile | **PlayStation** |
| Stick deadzone | **8%** |
| Vibration | **On** |
| Vibration strength | **100%** |

Encore controls the emulated input mapping and its own PlayStation-style UI glyphs. A game's own rendered button textures/prompts are game assets and cannot be universally replaced by the emulator; per-title patches may still be needed for titles that hard-code Nintendo glyph artwork.

## Language

The launcher exposes **exactly 31 official PS5 system language/region choices** and **31 translation catalogs** (including distinct English US/UK spelling variants). This is a deliberate compatibility policy: **no extra launcher languages** beyond the [Sony PS5 system language list](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/). All 31 are selectable; the historical first 18 keep their saved indices. See [LANGUAGES.md](LANGUAGES.md) for the full matrix and the [strict PS5 language policy](docs/PS5_SYSTEM_LANGUAGE_POLICY.md) for the authoritative 31-entry allowlist.

Settings → Language primarily selects the launcher interface. Only the original 18 selections map directly to a supported guest language.

On first setup, Encore seeds the preference from the PS5 system language. Changing it rebuilds the launcher immediately with the selected catalog/fonts. The original 18 selections preserve their guest language/region mappings; the 13 newly selectable PS5 system-language entries use an English guest-language fallback because these locales are not supported by the emulator's existing game-language enum. A game can still ignore the requested language when unsupported.

## Audio

- Game volume: **100%**
- Mute: **Off**
- Launcher/menu volume: **70%**

## Accessibility

Launcher-only options:

- Larger text
- High contrast
- Reduce motion

All are **Off by default**.

For verified launcher behavior, limitations (including unverified screen-reader integration), controller guidance and a reporting checklist, see [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md). These options do not modify game graphics or animation.

## Diagnostics

Detailed logging is **Off by default**. In the **unreleased local release-profile candidate**,
turning the setting on will **not** force the whole game to `*:Debug`: that previously generated
excessive output during FC27. Detailed guest tracing requires an explicitly diagnostic build.
The preference may remain visible for compatibility, but normal shipping builds use a bounded
log policy instead of unlimited debug output.

Logs are stored under the Encore storage root, normally `/data/prosperoeden/logs/`.
The local candidate keeps up to **8 MiB of earliest plus 8 MiB of recent content per active
log stream**, with previous-session rotation/cleanup. This is a storage policy, not a guarantee
that a crash or frozen guest can always be diagnosed from the available records.

## Practical profiles

These are starting points, not compatibility guarantees.

### 4K TV — balanced

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Renderer | Vulkan |
| TV output | **1440p** |
| Game resolution | **1x** |
| Filter | Bilinear |
| Anti-aliasing | **FXAA** |
| Refresh | 60 Hz |
| Console mode | Docked |

A modern 4K TV can upscale 1440p well while Encore keeps more GPU and presentation headroom.

### 4K TV — image quality

Use only after the title is already stable.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Renderer | Vulkan |
| TV output | **2160p** |
| Game resolution | **1x to 1.25x** |
| Filter | Bilinear or Bicubic |
| Anti-aliasing | None first, then SMAA if headroom remains |
| Refresh | 60 Hz |

Increase one setting at a time. If frame pacing worsens, return TV output to 1440p first.

### 4K TV — demanding game / unstable frame pacing

For a heavy title, start by separating **stability** from **image reconstruction**.

**Preferred first test when the picture already looked grainy/pixelated:**

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Renderer | Vulkan |
| TV output | **1080p** |
| Game resolution | **1x** |
| Filter | **Bilinear** |
| FSR sharpness | Not used |
| Anti-aliasing | None first; test FXAA only if edge shimmer remains |
| Refresh | 60 Hz |
| Console mode | Docked |

This avoids adding FSR sharpening while diagnosing grain, shimmer or pixel crawl. If 1x is still too
heavy after runtime/stability fixes, then try **0.75x + AMD FSR**, but begin around **25–35% FSR
sharpness**, not an aggressive value. Raise sharpness only if the image is too soft.

Anti-aliasing can reduce jagged edges or shimmer, but it does not fix every kind of grain. FXAA may
hide some high-frequency shimmer at the cost of softness; SMAA preserves more detail but is a little
heavier. Encore R1 does not add a separate debanding pass: Eden has no reusable deband stage today,
and an extra fullscreen shader is not enabled without PS5 performance evidence. A game's own temporal
AA/reconstruction may also interact with Encore's post-process AA, so
there is no universally best AA choice.

Once stable and visually clean at 1080p/1x, try 1440p output. Treat 2160p and internal scales above
1x as later image-quality experiments, not starting values.

### 1080p TV

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| TV output | **1080p** |
| Game resolution | **1x** |
| Filter | Bilinear |
| Anti-aliasing | None |
| Refresh | 60 Hz |

There is normally little benefit in forcing a 2160p Encore output on a 1080p display.

### Troubleshooting / compatibility

When a game crashes, freezes or renders incorrectly:

1. Use **Safe Launch** once.
2. Keep **60 Hz, 1080p, 1x, Bilinear, AA None**.
3. If the issue is graphical, test OpenGL.
4. If it is performance-related, return to Vulkan and try 0.75x + FSR.
5. Change one major setting at a time and compare logs/FPS.

Safe Launch is temporary and does not overwrite saved global or per-game settings.

## Compared with Eden desktop/Windows

Encore now exposes most of the settings that are useful for normal PS5 tuning, but it intentionally does **not** mirror every Eden desktop debug/advanced switch.

Still internal or not exposed include examples such as:

- anisotropic-filter overrides;
- aspect-ratio overrides;
- advanced GPU-accuracy toggles;
- ASTC decode/recompression modes;
- low-level VSync/frame-pacing controls;
- VRAM/memory-layout modes;
- shader-backend and shader-cache internals;
- advanced CPU timing/accuracy controls;
- platform-specific options that do not make sense on fixed PS5 hardware.

The goal is **complete practical PS5 tuning**, not a one-for-one copy of every Windows engineering switch. Additional Eden controls should be exposed only when they have a real PS5 use case and a safe default.


## Neural Rendering and image composition

Neural Rendering is a **separate image-processing engine**, not another spatial upscaling filter. The six directly selectable modes are:
`off`, `a4k_detail`, `a4k_soft`, `a4k_denoise`,
`dlss_nr_original`, and `dlss_nr_compact`.

The three A4K modes use their existing Vulkan shaders (formerly identified internally as 7/8/9), but no longer appear in the upscaling-filter list. Original and Compact neural modes have separate RDNA2 model-processing paths. Their 0–100% intensity setting is visible, but cannot be edited unless one of those two modes is selected.

- **Neural Rendering:** `off` by default, including on a new installation.
- **Frame Generation:** independently `off` by default.
- **Upscaling:** a separate spatial filter; it does not include the A4K modes.
- **Anti-aliasing:** None/FXAA/SMAA are distinct; forced MSAA composition is not enabled for Neural Rendering without physical-console proof.
- **Neural Rendering + Frame Generation:** the combined mode is not validated and is therefore rejected.
- **Renderer:** selecting an A4K or learned-model mode requires Vulkan.
- **Evidence boundary:** selecting a model or intensity is not a performance preset and does not demonstrate that an authentic neural image has already been rendered on PS5.

The real preference keys are `video.neural_rendering` (one of the six modes) and `video.neural_strength` (0–100). Per-game overrides use the same keys under `games.<TITLE_ID>`; missing per-game keys inherit the global settings.

Legacy filters `anime4k_3d`, `anime4k_soft`, and `anime4k_denoise` migrate to the corresponding Neural Rendering modes. The older `neural_rendering:rdna2` value is migrated according to the previous `neural_model` field.

See [Neural Rendering UI and override behavior](docs/ENCORE_R09_NEURAL_RENDERING_UI_OVERRIDES.md).
```

```md
# Support

## Supported target

Prospero.Eden Encore currently treats **PS5 firmware 13.60** as its tested release target.

## Before asking for help

Please check:

1. [README.md](README.md) for installation, compatibility and recommended defaults, or [choose a launcher language](LANGUAGES.md).
2. [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for quick fixes by symptom (install, language, storage, freezes and controllers).

5. The launcher's **Diagnostics** screen for filesystem mode, free space, cache and logs.
6. **Safe Launch** if one title no longer starts after changing settings.
7. [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) if the PS5/Encore language is French but the launcher still appears in English; a complete install must include all 31 official PS5 `ui/lang/*.po` catalogs. Language-menu choices must match exactly the 31 Sony system selections.

Useful reports include the Encore version/commit, PS5 firmware, renderer, relevant settings, exact
steps, and sanitized logs.

## What this project can help with

- Encore build or packaging failures;
- launcher/runtime crashes;
- regressions introduced by Encore;
- ZBIC/NSO loader behavior;
- renderer, controller, save-transfer or settings bugs in Encore;
- reproducible performance or compatibility regressions;
- documentation and translation problems;
- accessibility barriers in the Encore interface or controls, as described in [ACCESSIBILITY.md](ACCESSIBILITY.md).

## Out of scope

This repository does not provide:

- console keys or firmware;
- game downloads or copyrighted content;
- help finding ROM/NSP/XCI sources;
- PS5 FPKG entitlement/PPR fixes;
- general kstuff/jailbreak support;
- support for unofficial modified Encore builds.

Security vulnerabilities should not be filed as normal support requests. Follow
```

```md
  GPL-3.0. Encore is derived from its PS5 port/fork and retains portions of its
  native integration and 1.000.040-era filesystem-access path.

  core is built from the commit pinned in `UPSTREAM.json`.
- **[Citron Neo emulator](https://github.com/citron-neo/emulator)** — GPL-family

  and lazy audio backport refers to Citron commits `f07609c52033` and `21813e8cb3ea`.
  Its source is retained for isolated review; it is not active in the shipping baseline.
  Original copyright and license notices remain applicable.
- Eden's pinned dependencies include **Dynarmic (0BSD), Boost, fmt, Xbyak, zstd,
  LZ4, Opus, SDL3, simpleini, sirit, SPIRV-Headers, Vulkan-Headers,
  Vulkan-Utility-Libraries, Vulkan Memory Allocator, ENet, frozen,
  cpp-httplib, nlohmann/json** and time-zone data. Each component retains its
  upstream license and copyright notices; the available full texts are bundled
  under `LICENSES/`.
- **[FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org)** — LGPL-2.1-or-later. Encore builds the
  pinned source with the H.264, VP8 and VP9 decoder subset used by the PS5
  media path.
- **[OpenSSL](https://www.openssl.org)** — Apache-2.0, and **zlib** — zlib
  license. The PS5 libraries come from the pinned
  [pacbrew](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/pacbrew-repo) package.
- **LLVM compiler-rt** pieces used by the PS5 cross-build are covered by the
  LLVM project's Apache-2.0 license with LLVM exception.

### ZBIC license selection

Encore pins **[kinnay/zbic](https://github.com/kinnay/zbic)** at commit
`11b08f2712264bbed731545085cbd9702096ceb7` for Nintendo Switch 22.0+ ZBIC
NSO decompression.

The kinnay/zbic repository itself contains a GPLv2 root license, but Encore
does **not** compile or redistribute its Python extension/module as a separate
dependency. The PS5 build includes only the snapshot's Zstandard implementation
files used by `headless/zbic_compression.cpp`. Those files state in their own
headers that they are dual-licensed under a BSD-style license or GPLv2 and that
the recipient may select either. **Encore selects the BSD-style terms for those
files.** The selected license text is preserved as
`LICENSES/ZBIC-zstd-BSD.txt`.
## Graphics

  the RADV/Vulkan PS5 path. Mesa source files retain their upstream permissive
  file-level notices; Mihawk's PS5 platform/tooling repository is GPL-3.0.

  experimental native PS5 Vulkan work used by the graphics stack.
- **[ps5-opengl](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-opengl)** — GPL-3.0,
  with Mesa components retaining their own licenses. Encore pins source commit
  `ad2807d41cef2681882a9ee0d20808779f74b7cd`; `third_party/app_heap.c`
  originates from that project.

## Native frame generation source and upstream licences

The vendor repository contains complete, byte-exact sources for MihawkGen
(`c57232a9f16bcb6df5fe07c9bb631518f2b1cc0e`) and FSR3 Optical Flow
(`64362101757cdd6f7df9eeb984cb53f03f1fbfca`). MihawkGen's pinned
1,757,240-byte model retains upstream GPL/MIT notices and the author's model
training/distillation credits. Optical Flow preserves the Swordpdf GPL and
AMD shader licence material. Each notice is copied into the installed PS5
title's legal directory. Sources being bundled does not establish successful
PS5 interpolation, third-party endorsement or independent copyright ownership.

## Runtime metadata and media

- **[LaunchBox](https://www.launchbox-app.com/)** — third-party public game catalogue and optional front/back case-art lookup. The build creates a compact local index, but does not embed the full external catalogue or commercial cover scans. Downloaded images remain subject to their original ownership and applicable terms.

- **[ghost-land/Nlib-API](https://github.com/ghost-land/Nlib-API)** — GPL-3.0.
  Encore queries its public NX endpoints at runtime for title metadata and
  launcher media such as icons, banners and screenshots. Nlib source code and
  a pre-seeded Nlib media library are **not** embedded in the Encore release;
  returned responses/media may be cached locally by the user.
- Copyright, trademark and other rights in metadata, cover art, banners,
  screenshots or other media returned by a remote service remain with their
  respective rightsholders. Encore does **not** represent Nlib-served media as
  public-domain, royalty-free, or licensed for independent redistribution.
  Remote-service availability and terms can change independently of Encore.

## Project-authored sound effects

The launcher UI sound files under `headless/prosperoeden/ui/sounds/` are
generated deterministically by `tools/launcher/generate-sfx.py` from
mathematical oscillators and deterministic noise. They contain no third-party
audio samples, recordings, model-generated clips, or external audio-service
output. The generation script and generated assets are distributed as part of
Encore under the project's applicable GPL-3.0-or-later terms.
## Compressed-container reader (NSZ/XCZ)

regression fixtures under `headless/ncz.h`, `headless/ncz.cpp`,

and `tools/check-ncz.py` originate from the community contribution
[`ProsperoEden` PR #285](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ProsperoEden/pull/285)
by Oliv3rmoon (Copyright 2026), licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**.

Encore retains the original source copyright and license notices and adds
native C++ source-owner adaptations, symlink-safe cache access, tests and
project-specific integrations. These formats do not bundle games, proprietary
keys, firmware or proprietary compression algorithms.
```

`TROUBLESHOOTING.md`:

```md
# Troubleshooting — Prospero.Eden Encore

> **Exactly the 31 official PS5 system language/region choices; 31 launcher translation catalogs (including en-US and en-GB):** [Language directory](LANGUAGES.md). No extra launcher languages are exposed. This strict policy follows [Sony's official console-language list](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/); translation/font quality still requires validation.


[← Main README](README.md) · [Installation / upgrading](INSTALL.md) · [Languages](LANGUAGES.md) · [Support](SUPPORT.md)

This is a practical guide to common problems, not a compatibility guarantee. Encore has been tested on a PS5 running **firmware 13.60 only**. Earlier firmware might work but is not qualified; no minimum firmware is established.

## Before changing anything: protect your data

**Never delete `/data/prosperoeden/` to “fix” an install.** It can contain your settings, saved games, keys and other important files. Back up both the complete application `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/` and persistent `/data/prosperoeden/` data, plus any selected external-storage root.

Encore and the original native ProsperoEden **share application ID `PPSA99008`**. They do not normally install as separate applications. Use [Encore Releases](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/releases) to update Encore—not an arbitrary upstream release.

## Find your problem

| Symptom | What to check first |
| --- | --- |
| **App won't open, black screen or crash** | Correct package, complete file layout, homebrew environment and Diagnostics/logs |
| **“Setup incomplete”** | Current Storage root and your `keys/prod.keys` and firmware files |
| **Games missing from Library** | Correct `roms/` under the *selected* storage root; supported file extension |
| **Launcher stuck in English** | Settings → Language and complete `PPSA99008/ui/lang/` catalogs |
| **A title fails after changing its settings** | One-session **Safe Launch**, without deleting saved data |
| **Artwork or screenshots missing** | Artwork fetching/metadata and network; sample art is fictional, not a compatibility list |
| **Stutter, stale HUD, pause/half-time freeze** | Known outstanding gameplay issues; collect a reproducible example |
| **Wrong buttons or glyphs in games** | Per-game Controls profile; a game's own button images may remain Nintendo-style |
| **NSZ/XCZ extremely slow** | Solid compression may need decompression and free space |
| **ZIP vs FFPFSC conflicting installs** | Identify which `PPSA99008` is being launched/mounted before updating |

## Application doesn't start

1. Get the package from [Encore Releases](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/releases) and verify any published checksum. A passing CI artifact does not automatically equal a console-tested release.
2. In a regular ZIP/FTP install, you need a **single complete** `PPSA99008/` directory containing `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/param.json` and `ui/lang/`. Avoid the accidental `PPSA99008/PPSA99008/` nesting.
3. With **FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus**, use the image-specific mount/update steps. Do not unpack the image into the ordinary app folder.
4. Verify the required PS5 homebrew environment is working. General jailbreak, FPKG/PPR entitlement and kstuff issues are outside Encore's support scope.
5. Check the app Diagnostics screen and `/data/prosperoeden/logs/` without publishing sensitive information.

[Full ZIP/FTP and FFPFSC instructions](INSTALL.md).

## Launcher stays in English

The **language menu must offer exactly 31 official PS5 system language/region choices**, backed by **31** `ui/lang/*.po` translation catalogs. All official choices are selectable. If a new build exposes more or fewer choices, this is a regression against the [Sony console-language reference](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/).

Select **Settings → Language**. If the selected language is ignored after a manual FTP upgrade, reinstall the **entire application directory including `ui/lang/`**, and follow [the old-development-language-override checks](INSTALL.md#if-encore-is-set-to-french-but-the-launcher-stays-in-english). Do not remove unknown files blindly.

## Library, storage, keys or firmware

The selected Storage root normally has `keys/`, `firmware/`, `roms/`, `updates/` and other subdirectories. An external drive must use the **same structure beneath the selected root**.

Check the root actually selected in Settings → Storage. Direct NRO/NSO/NCA/NAX/KIP files might not contain a complete bootable title. A compressed NSZ/XCZ title can also need extra free storage and decompression work.

Encore never bundles keys, proprietary firmware or commercial games. Use only files and content you are entitled to use.

## Performance, gameplay and controller issues

A successful build or host regression test **does not prove stable PS5 frame times**. The active investigations include first-use shader compilation, pipeline waiting, texture freshness, game-input mapping and freezes during pause or half-time. Start with the **Recommended** video profile and change one setting at a time; see [Settings](SETTINGS.md).

The emulator's controller profile cannot universally replace **button graphics drawn inside a game**. Try the PlayStation, Switch or per-title Custom profiles before reporting a mapping bug.

**Switch 2:** common NS1/NS2 source work has moved onto `main`, with finite host exit gates, but these later changes are **not** in the published October 2026 R1 PS5 FTP binary. No guest-rendered NS2 PS5 frame is confirmed. Frame generation and automatic updates are not verified as shipped features. See [release and workflow evidence](docs/RELEASE_BASELINE_WORKFLOW_AUDIT_2026-11-09.md).

## Reporting an issue

Please include the Encore release or **commit SHA**, console firmware, installation method (ZIP or FFPFSC), renderer, selected storage, language, controller profile, steps to reproduce, expected/actual behavior and whether the test used a **real PS5**. Redact logs from `/data/prosperoeden/logs/`.

**Never upload console keys, identifying information, account data, save files or commercial game files.** File regular bugs via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/issues/new/choose); report security issues privately using [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
```

`data/glyph-research/README.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore · Recherche de glyphes PlayStation par jeu Switch 1

**Stockage persistant : dépôt GitHub `niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore`, branche
`dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.** Ce dossier contient uniquement des métadonnées,
liens et preuves de correspondance. Ne pas y ajouter de ROM, clés, textures
Nintendo ni archives de mods redistribuables sans licence.

## Organisation

| Emplacement | Contenu | Persistance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `games/01007EF00011E000.json` | BOTW : mods Switch/Wii U, scènes, mapping A=Cross et preuves manquantes | Commit Git |
| `games/<TITLE_ID>.json` | Futurs dossiers par jeu, lorsque les données sont qualifiées | Commit Git |
| `discovery/leads.json` | Liens GameBanana/ModDB/Nexus/GitHub repérés, provenance, requêtes Switch/PC | Régénéré puis commité sur cette branche par GitHub Actions |
| `discovery/progress.json` | Curseurs de recherche par Title ID, moteur et variante | Régénéré puis commité sur cette branche par GitHub Actions |
| `catalog/switch1-titles.json.gz` | Catalogue régional Switch 1 consolidé | Export gzip GitHub Actions et commit Git |
| `catalog/source-queries.json.gz` | Requêtes publiques préconstruites (Switch/PC/GameBanana/ru) | Export gzip GitHub Actions et commit Git |
| `catalog/scope-audit.json` | Contrôle du périmètre Switch 1, volume d'IDs candidats, doublons de noms et démos/cloud suspectées | Rapport indépendant, commité sur la branche |

Les fichiers `discovery` et `catalog` apparaissent au **premier run dont le
commit a été autorisé**. Si le jeton Actions n'a pas le droit d'écrire, si la
branche a bougé, ou si le serveur refuse les requêtes, un avertissement est
émis et les résultats restent en artefacts GitHub Actions, qui ne sont
**pas** un stockage définitif. Ne jamais annoncer un commit sans le vérifier.

## Différence entre candidat et jeu fonctionnel

Un lien de mod et les positions d'interface d'une édition PC/Wii U ne
constituent pas un atlas Switch activable. Les données de ressources vérifiées
incluent `original SHA-256`, `game update`, `romfs_path`,
`texture_name`, `slot rect_xywh`, `guest action vs spatial button`.
Les champs `null` du fichier BOTW indiquent exactement les preuves non
encore produites.

Les scripts `tools/ps-glyph-*` exécutent les adaptations techniques ;
`docs/PS_GLYPH_SOURCE_INDEX.json` et
`docs/PS_GLYPH_CROSS_PLATFORM_INDEX.json` restent les indices de sources
historiques. L'approbation des données n'active aucun pack dans l'émulateur.

## Recherches publiques HTTP vs vrai navigateur

`curl` avec User-Agent Firefox est le chemin léger par défaut, mais ne
devient pas pour autant un navigateur Firefox. Playwright Firefox peut être
choisi explicitement lorsqu'une page exige un rendu JavaScript. Aucun de ces
clients ne contourne CAPTCHA, authentification, 403 ou limitation de débit.
Yandex via ses pages de recherche publiques ne nécessite pas une API payante ;
l'API Search officielle est une voie **distincte** et uniquement sur
activation avec ses clés et sa facturation éventuelle.

## Périmètre matériel vérifié

Seuls les **jeux et logiciels ayant réellement une version Nintendo Switch 1**
entrent dans le catalogue. Les versions qui existent **sur Switch 1 et Switch 2**
restent présentes via leurs IDs Switch 1 `0100…` (par exemple Zelda BOTW).
Les exclusivités Switch 2 `0400…` (par exemple Mario Kart World) sont
exclues. La compatibilité rétroactive sur Switch 2 ne convertit pas un jeu
Switch 2 exclusif en jeu Switch 1.

Le total `24 205` initial représente **des IDs d'applications candidates**
collectés dans plusieurs régions, pas 24 205 jeux commerciaux uniques.
L'audit `scope-audit.json` explique les doublons de noms et les indices
de démos/versions cloud, sans exclure à tort des jeux Switch 1.


## Switch 1 uniquement : vérification du catalogue (10 octobre 2026)

**Ne pas interpréter le catalogue TitleDB comme une liste vérifiée de jeux
officiels.** L'audit indépendant GitHub Actions
[`#38008270773`](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38008270773)
a traité 24 205 identifiants au format application Switch 1 et retenu
**23 997 candidats non officiellement confirmés** après exclusion de
153 démos clairement nommées, 17 versions cloud et 38 titres à sortie
future. Les 95 occurrences de Title IDs Switch 2 seuls `0400…` ont
également été rejetées au moment de la lecture des sources régionales.

Cette correction est un **premier filtre de métadonnées**, pas la preuve
que 23 997 jeux Switch 1 existent : un second recoupement avec des
sources indépendantes reste nécessaire. Les estimations d'inventaires
diffèrent selon les critères de comptage (édition, régions, jeux
numériques/physiques, périodes). **Aucune limite arbitraire** n'est
utilisée.

Règle constante : un jeu ayant une édition réellement jouable sur
**Switch 1** reste inclus même s'il possède aussi une édition Switch 2 ;
les jeux **exclusivement Switch 2** ne font jamais partie du catalogue
destiné à l'émulation Switch 1. Un ancien catalogue non filtré ne
doit pas déclencher un nouveau long balayage.
```

```md
# 2026-10-15 — Field log analysis and stop-test checkpoint

Branch: **dev/ps5-sparse-jit**. Evidence from October 15 console logs, current code and an offline parser. **No runtime defect is claimed fixed. No new native package, release or console test is requested.**

## Tested binary identity

- Source SHA in the console trace: 5629395324ff65c98b50c44f35f2142a4a92654a.
- Firmware: 0x13600007; installed native title folder: PPSA99008.
- The newer branch HEAD and passing CI cannot retroactively change the tested binary.
- In-game configuration says title_override=1, own_mapping=0, profile map {}. The reported custom gameplay mapping is not shown as loaded.

## Controller/guest-input distinction

The raw PS5 sample is usable only when Data.connected is nonzero and its buttons do not carry kButtonIntercepted (third_party/ps5_pad.hpp). But the heartbeat 'connected=1' is an **open slot bitmap**, not Data.connected (headless/pad.cpp).

Across polls **273750–281250**, 7,500 more samples arrive in **30,914 ms**, without any rise in usable, intercepted, or read-error counters. With the sampled counter semantics, this is consistent with raw samples reporting disconnected. It is not proof of a guest CPU deadlock: system UI focus takeover near the end of the session is not ruled out.

After the plateau: options_edges=2, virtual published_plus_edges=2 and Npad LIFO reports two Plus edges. This shows input delivery through more than one layer, but **does not prove the title consumed those actions**. It also argues against a permanently missing physical Options-to-Npad route.

## GPU and memory

Replay of heap(20261015-161206).log and stderr(20261015-161213).log:

| Marker / observation | Result |
|---|---|
| Detailed pad heartbeats | 227 |
| Vulkan five-second windows | 232 |
| Windows below 20 FPS | 5 |
| Windows with worst individual frame >400 ms | 12 |
| Windows at 29.95–30.05 FPS | 190 |
| Mean of reported GPU idle milliseconds, final five windows | 3881.8 ms per window |
| Sparse JIT at core_destroyed | reserved=0 committed=0 |
| Heap pieces retained at core_destroyed | 1,744,830,464 bytes |
| Heap retention | 939,524,096 pinned + 805,306,368 unpinned, reclaim disabled because quiescence unproven |
| CPU topology | 13 claimed physical IDs, rejected; optimization skipped |
| Process CPU clock | valid=0 |

Important qualifiers:
- **Frames presented are not proof of changing guest game content.** Do not label a 30 FPS plateau as stable gameplay.
- GPU-idle values are instrumentation counters; no definitive hardware utilization or CPU bottleneck follows automatically.
- The retained heap is **not** a proven leak. Do not reclaim native pages without per-owner emptiness and quiescence proofs.
- GPU unmapping counters are zero within their measurement scope; this neither explains nor rules out all texture/HUD coherency faults.
- CPU topology and process-clock instrumentation are not verified on this firmware.

## Reproduce without touching the console

Run in a host terminal, with copies of the original logs stored outside the repo:

    python3 tools/analyze-ps5-session-log.py --self-test
    python3 tools/analyze-ps5-session-log.py --stderr 'stderr(20261015-161213).log' --heap 'heap(20261015-161206).log'

The synthetic self-test and replay of the user's supplied captures both ran locally. Raw user logs must not be committed to this public repository.

1. Freeze console testing and do not publish another speculative experimental binary.
2. Only make risky runtime corrections after identifying an exact faulty path with source and reproducible evidence.
3. For a future source-only audit, prioritize guest-thread wait ownership/content progression and GPU buffer/texture freshness; treat heap lifetime independently.
4. Do not fix gameplay input by injecting synthetic HOME or Pause events; this trace does not warrant it.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_CLEAR_SCISSOR_OVERFLOW.md`:

```md
# Clear scissor signed underflow at INT32_MIN

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

In the native rasterizer's clear-path `clamp_rect_to_render_area`,
a negative scissor offset was negated directly as an `s32` to compute the
amount of a rectangle lying outside the render area. For `INT32_MIN`,
`-offset` overflows signed 32-bit arithmetic and causes undefined behavior.
The result may be incorrect scissor clipping or a build-dependent fault.

The native code and pinned source generator now widen the signed offset to
`s64` **before** negating it. The value then fits safely in `u32`,
including the magnitude of `INT32_MIN`. No Vulkan synchronization,
framebuffer state, pipeline selection or valid rectangle calculation changes.

The source-extracted host test compiles the production clipping lambda with
Clang C++20, AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. It evaluates
230,400 rectangle/area combinations, including `INT32_MIN`, `INT32_MAX`,
zero extents and oversized rectangles, and compares with an independent
64-bit intersection oracle. The full pinned/active generator parity preflight
also runs in CI.

No console build, release or hardware test is requested. This fixes a
reproducible integer arithmetic defect; it is **not** evidence that
a particular title's HUD, stutters or freezes are resolved.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_COMPUTE_DESCRIPTOR_QUEUE_PREFLIGHT.md`:

```md
# Compute guest descriptor queue preflight (native-only)

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

## Source defect

`RasterizerVulkan::DispatchCompute` held both guest cache mutexes while
`ComputePipeline::Configure` called `GuestDescriptorQueue::Acquire`. The
latter retains an overflow fallback that waits for the GPU command worker.
Unlike the draw path, compute had no ordinary descriptor queue preflight before
the mutex pair. This is a source-reachable wait-under-lock risk, not an
observed FC27 event.

## Bounded fix

The native dispatch path now runs the already-existing
`PreflightGuestDraw` before choosing the compute pipeline and before locking
the guest caches. When the queue needs a worker drain, it consumes guest memory
invalidations with `gpu_memory->FlushCaching()` before selecting the compute
pipeline, mirroring the graphics path.

The original `Acquire` fallback remains for atypical reservations greater
than 0x400 entries and other configurations. The descriptor buffer ring's
`Allocate` fallback may also still wait under the caches: this patch does
**not** solve that separate issue.

## Proof and limits

`tools/check-ps5-compute-guest-descriptor-preflight-host.py` extracts the
production `PreflightGuestDraw` method verbatim for Clang ASan/UBSan host
testing. Static guards require the new call and invalidation refresh to
precede pipeline selection and both mutexes. The existing generator preserves
the insertion on fresh source preparation. No console build, release, hardware
test or performance improvement is claimed.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_COMPUTE_DESCRIPTOR_RING_PREFLIGHT.md`:

```md
# Compute descriptor ring waits outside the guest cache mutex pair

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

The native compute rasterizer previously entered `ComputePipeline::Configure`
under the texture and buffer cache mutexes before allocating descriptor-buffer
memory. Unlike graphics, compute always allocates a new descriptor-buffer payload
on every dispatch. An eight-frame reuse fence or exhausted last chunk may
therefore trigger `Wait` or `Finish` while both locks are held.

The compute pipeline's immutable descriptor-buffer capability and layout size
are now exposed via native-only getters in the pinned source-generator adapter.
Before acquiring either cache lock, `DispatchCompute` preflights the exact
ring frame-reuse fence and the guaranteed capacity overflow. After any GPU
worker/fence drain it flushes guest memory invalidations, reselects the compute
pipeline and checks large guest descriptor reservations again. The existing
`Allocate` waits remain the fallback for uncommon situations.

A source-extracted Clang ASan/UBSan fixture checks the production ring
`PreflightFrameReuse`, `PreflightCapacity` and `Allocate` methods together,
including no-wait, frame reuse, last-chunk exhaustion, disabled extension and
pipeline layout changes. It asserts no ring waits occur under simulated cache
locks once the preflight is applied. CI also tests source/generator parity.

No console build, release or hardware tests were performed. The graphics
descriptor-buffer conditional-reuse case remains unresolved. Host evidence
does not establish actual game performance, timing or resolution of freezes.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_DESCRIPTOR_CONDITIONAL_REUSE_LOCK_WAIT.md`:

```md
# Conditional descriptor-ring reuse: remaining locked GPU wait

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.
Status: source-level hazard reproduced; **not** an observed FC27 event.

## Why the guaranteed-only preflight is incomplete

`GraphicsPipeline::DescriptorRingPreflightSize()` returns zero when the
pipeline's previous descriptor-buffer generation and entry count match the
current values. This is intentionally conservative: the actual guest
descriptor payload cannot be compared until the caches are locked.

Inside `GraphicsPipeline::ConfigureDraw()`, the payload can differ while
its count remains identical. The existing `std::memcmp` then rejects the
old allocation and calls `DescriptorBufferRing::Allocate()`. If the
current ring chunk is exhausted and there are no additional chunks,
`Allocate()` calls `scheduler.Finish()` while `PrepareDraw()` still
holds the guest buffer-cache and texture-cache mutexes.

The source-extracted Clang ASan/UBSan host witness at
`tools/check-ps5-descriptor-conditional-reuse-host.py` constructs:
- equal generation and descriptor count, but different descriptor bytes;
- a full last ring chunk;
- a zero-size preflight and a later allocation under both locks.

It confirms that the original fallback calls `Finish` while locked, and
also verifies the successful pre-drain path when generation mismatch
makes a new allocation certain.

## Native capability and release build gate

The release recipe in `tools/build-package.sh` selects
`EDEN_PS5_VULKAN=ON EDEN_VULKAN_DRIVER=RADV`. The active vendored RADV source
(`vendor/encore-active/ps5-mesa/src/amd/vulkan/radv_physical_device.c`)
advertises `EXT_descriptor_buffer = true` and `descriptorBuffer = true`.
The native application's `headless/dev_vulkan.h` defaults
`disable_descriptor_buffer` to `false`, including the title reset.
The Vulkan device adapter retains the feature when supported by the
selected physical device, and ring initialization also requires buffer
device address support and usable host-visible/coherent memory.

The host witness now pins this production source path. Thus the unsafe
fallback is *source-reachable* on the configured driver, not merely a
desktop-only code path. It is **not** proof that the feature was enabled
on a particular boot or that a game's descriptors exhausted the ring.
Runtime extension negotiation, ring allocation and per-game use remain
unmeasured. No new console execution is requested.

## Engineering trade-off

The host fixture now proves the *two-outcome, same-observation* case with
production source-extracted `PreflightCapacity` and `Allocate`:

1. An exhausted ring, matching generation and matching entry count,
   with a byte-identical guest payload: `ConfigureDraw` reuses the old
   allocation and requires **no GPU wait**.
2. Exactly the same pre-lock ring and pipeline metadata, but one changed
   guest descriptor: `ConfigureDraw` allocates and can reach
   `scheduler.Finish()` **under the cache locks**.

Passing the full layout to preflight to cover the second case necessarily
causes an unnecessary `Finish` in the first case; it also changes the ring
generation and invalidates the previously reusable allocation. Therefore,
changing a getter or making `PreflightCapacity` unconditional does **not**
provide a no-regression fix.

Finishing the GPU unconditionally whenever the ring is full would avoid
this particular locked wait, but would force submission/completion on
otherwise reusable descriptor payloads. That is a potentially severe
frame-pacing regression, and a pre-drain changes ring generation, which
can itself prevent descriptor reuse.

A safe redesign would need to decide whether a new allocation is required
without violating guest-memory/descriptor-lock ownership, or provide a
retry mechanism that releases the cache mutexes, drains the exact GPU
fence and then **revalidates** every guest descriptor binding before
committing the draw. Both require a separate integration review.

## Future redesign acceptance conditions

A real fix must preserve all three properties in the same draw:
- Cache-dependent descriptor identities and buffer/image lifetimes remain
  valid from descriptor collection through the GPU command submission.
- An identical payload still reuses its previous allocation without an
  unnecessary GPU drain or extra descriptor allocation.
- A changed payload can reclaim full-ring capacity without holding the
  guest texture/buffer mutex pair during `scheduler.Finish()` and without
  dropping or duplicating commands, draws, upload barriers or query updates.

A two-phase staging/retry mechanism would also need to detect invalidations
between lock release and reacquisition and restart descriptor capture safely.
`ConfigureImpl` already updates buffer bindings, texture views, render
targets and scheduler work **before** reaching `ConfigureDraw`: simply
re-running it is not a proven idempotent retry. Snapshotting raw cache-owned
image-view pointers without lifetime pinning is likewise unsafe.

The current contract test is deliberately a *negative* safety gate, not an
emulator performance improvement. No console test is required to establish
these source-level trade-offs, but host tests cannot establish FC27 behavior.

## Scope and limits

This commit adds a host-only executable regression and CI hook. It does
not change Vulkan runtime, scheduling, descriptor layout, cache locking,
render order, or artifact packaging. Descriptor-buffer availability on
the actual console depends on the runtime device's advertised extension
and features. The witness does not prove that a particular game ever
took this path, and does not resolve FPS stalls, freezes or missing HUD.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_DESCRIPTOR_ENTRY_CANONICALIZATION.md`:

```md
# Descriptor payload byte canonicalization (native-only)

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

## Source defect

The Vulkan descriptor ring uses a bytewise `std::memcmp` over
`DescriptorUpdateEntry` to decide whether an existing allocation can be reused.
This union stores multiple Vulkan structures, including 24-byte image descriptors
and address descriptors with a four-byte padding tail.

Assigning only the active Vulkan fields does not promise initialization of the
inactive union storage or structure padding. Optimized Clang builds can leave
different bytes there despite identical semantic descriptor fields. Such a false
difference triggers needless ring allocations and can increase pressure on
the already-documented conditional reuse / in-lock `scheduler.Finish()` path.

## Scoped change

For native descriptor-buffer writes only, `AddSampledImage`, `AddImage`,
`AddBuffer` (device address variant), and `AddTexelBuffer` (address variant)
zero the entire slot before assigning the active descriptor fields individually.
The regular Vulkan update-template path remains unchanged, as do the union size,
descriptor queue ABI, fences, scheduler, cache locks, and draw order.

The pinned source generator and the active header carry identical logic.
`tools/check-ps5-descriptor-entry-canonical-host.py` compiles the exact
methods extracted from the active header under Clang -O2 with ASan/UBSan,
poisons otherwise inactive bytes, and proves equal semantic descriptors produce
equal full-entry bytes and survive vector copying.

## Limits

This addresses false misses only; genuine descriptor changes can still trigger
the known in-lock GPU `Finish` fallback when the ring is exhausted. The isolated
host test proves deterministic entry bytes, not performance, game correctness,
GPU execution, or resolution of FC27 freezes, frame stalls or missing HUD.
No console build, release or hardware test is authorized.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_DESCRIPTOR_RING_SIZE_OVERFLOW.md`:

```md
# Descriptor ring allocation-size overflow guard

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

The upstream `DescriptorBufferRing::CanAllocate` aligned an untrusted `VkDeviceSize` before comparing it with its fixed chunk capacity. Pinned `Common::AlignUp` uses unsigned arithmetic; for `UINT64_MAX` and 16-byte alignment the result wraps to zero. An impossibly large descriptor size can thus be misclassified as fitting a few-megabyte descriptor ring.

The native-only generated header rejects `size > chunk_capacity` before calling `AlignUp`. All requests of at most the finite ring capacity still follow the original aligned-capacity test. The immutable pinned upstream file is unchanged. The generator explicitly reproduces the guard.

`tools/check-ps5-descriptor-ring-overflow-host.py` compiles the verbatim guarded method alongside the pinned predicate and real pinned alignment function under C++20 ASan/UBSan. It reproduces original UINT64_MAX misclassification and checks ordinary, edge, disabled and oversized cases.

This protects invalid metadata. It does not move `scheduler.Finish`, alter descriptor reuse, cache locks, frame timing, Vulkan allocation behavior for valid requests or the console build/release. No claim is made that FC27 emits such a size or that its freezes, HUD or stutters improve.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_DRAW_TEXTURE_INVALIDATION.md`:

```md
# Drain guest memory invalidations before DrawTexture cache lookup

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

The native Vulkan `DrawTexture()` used `FlushWork()` followed immediately
by acquiring `texture_cache.mutex`, `SynchronizeDescriptors(false)` and
`UpdateRenderTargets(false)`. Unlike the ordinary draw, clear and compute
paths, it did not call `gpu_memory->FlushCaching()` before resolving textures
and framebuffers.

`MemoryManager::FlushCaching()` consumes queued page-map invalidations,
then invokes `RasterizerVulkan::InnerInvalidation()`. The latter takes
`texture_cache.mutex` and invalidates texture pages and cached pipeline
bindings. It must run **before** `DrawTexture` locks the texture cache:
calling it inside the existing critical section would deadlock.

The pinned Vulkan adapter and active renderer now place the existing
invalidation drain immediately after `FlushWork()`, before the texture
lock and all sampled-image/render-target lookups. No draw order, cache
locking, GPU fence, descriptor buffer, sampling or blit parameters change.

A source-backed Clang ASan/UBSan test extracts the exact pre-lock sequence,
verifies the native/pinned generator parity and production invalidation
lock ownership, then exercises pending and empty invalidation queues
without recursive locking.

This is a source-level cache coherency correction. It does not establish
that a particular game uses the DrawTexture path, that stale texture
lookups occurred on the console, or that the HUD/freeze symptoms are fixed.
No console build, release or hardware tests are requested.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_GPU_SYNC_ENQUEUE_FENCE.md`:

```md
# GPU sync fence publication — 16 October 2026

The pinned native GPU implementation increments `last_sync_fence` before
`sync_requests.emplace_back`. If the callback insertion throws, a fence
number is consumed without creating an executable callback. A subsequent
CPU waiter could therefore wait for a fence the worker cannot acknowledge.

The native-only CMake source derivation now inserts the callback **before**
incrementing the fence counter, under the same mutex. A deterministic Clang
ASan/UBSan regression compiles the generated request and tick methods,
injects a callback copy throwing `std::bad_alloc`, and verifies that the
next successful callback receives and completes fence 1.

This is source-level correctness, **not evidence** that FC27 freezes were
caused by callback allocation failure. No console build, release or device
test is requested.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_GPU_SYNC_TICK_SNAPSHOT.md`:

```md
# Native GPU TickWork snapshot fairness — 16 October 2026

Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. This is a source-level liveness correction, **not** a demonstrated fix for FC27 freezes, HUD disappearance, or frame pacing. No console build or test requested.

## Identified defect

Pinned `video_core/gpu.cpp` drains `sync_requests` via `while (!sync_requests.empty())`, temporarily releasing the mutex while executing each callback. CPU threads can append more requests while that callback executes. Therefore a continuously replenished queue can keep one `GPUTick` command executing indefinitely and delay other work on the same native GPU owner, even if each callback succeeds. This is a provable unbounded-batch risk, not evidence that it occurred in the observed FC27 sessions.

## Corrective contract

Native CMake derives a **single bounded entry snapshot count** under the same `sync_request_mutex`. The worker consumes exactly that many original FIFO requests and then returns to its GPU command queue. Requests appended during processing remain pending for their own `TickGPU` commands. Call sites in the pinned GPU implementation that enqueue `RequestSyncOperation` directly also schedule `TickGPU`; the public `RequestFlush` path is paired with `TickGPU` in native `ThreadManager::FlushAndInvalidateRegion`.

Each successful callback still increments `current_sync_fence` once and notifies waiting CPU threads. An exception continues propagating with **no invented fence acknowledgement**. The `unique_lock`-owned unlock/lock pair remains exception-safe. The non-native source and experimental guest-write deferral are unchanged.

## Host validation and limits

`tools/check-gpu-sync-failure-host.py` derives the **actual native CMake source fragment**, extracts `TickWork`, and compiles it under Clang ASan/UBSan. The added cases verify 16 successive reentrant appends terminate one per tick, original FIFO requests precede a callback-enqueued request, and completion fences advance only for executed callbacks; earlier normal, throwing and fatal-waiter tests remain.

No evidence yet establishes real shader, cache, draw, guest-thread or native device progress under FC27. The historical frozen-game traces include runs where presented frames and draw counts continued, so this fix must not be credited with ending those stalls. Do not publish a console candidate or request new tests based on this host regression alone.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_LATE_DESCRIPTOR_PREFLIGHT.md`:

```md
# Descriptor queue: final preflight after pipeline reselection

## Source-level hazard

The native Vulkan draw path preflights the guest descriptor queue before taking
the buffer and texture cache mutexes. An independent descriptor-buffer ring
capacity preflight may still call Scheduler::Finish, consume pending guest
invalidations, and reselect a different graphics pipeline. That pipeline can
reserve more descriptor entries than the pipeline checked earlier.

UpdateDescriptorQueue::Acquire contains a WaitWorker fallback. Without a final
check, the fallback can run inside GraphicsPipeline::Configure while both
cache mutexes are held. The retained native-only change repeats
PreflightLargeGuestDraw after the ring-triggered pipeline reselection, before
the cache mutex pair. If a drain is required, it flushes guest invalidations
and reselects the pipeline again. No descriptor guest state is read ahead
of the cache locks and no actual GPU fence or queue order is changed.

The host test compiles the exact active C++ header preflights under Clang
ASan/UBSan and reproduces a changed reservation that was too large for the
earlier check. The model proves the late drain occurs outside both locks.
Source ordering guards pin the new call after the ring refresh and before
the paired lock. This is a bounded safety/preflight correction, not a
replacement for the full #187 guest CPU write deferral protocol.

**Limits:** no console build, shader workload tracing, or evidence that
FC27 encountered this exact late pipeline change. No FPS/HUD/freeze
improvement is claimed.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_QUAD_INDEX_INITIAL_FENCE.md`:

```md
# Avoid a first-use full GPU fence for quad-index LUTs

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

The active Vulkan `QuadIndexBuffer::UpdateBuffer` used to call
`scheduler.Finish()` on its *first ever* allocation as well as on each
subsequent capacity growth. The first allocation starts with default-initialized
`vk::Buffer buffer{}` (a null Vulkan handle). There is no previous LUT buffer
to protect from in-flight work, so completing all queued GPU commands is
unnecessary on that first call.

The native Vulkan source now conditions the *existing* Finish on `if (buffer)`.
Every resize with an existing buffer still uses the exact original fence before
replacing it. No draw, index generation, copy barrier, later lifetime guard,
cache mutex or scheduler ordering is changed. Both quad and quad-strip index
LUTs use this same class.

`tools/check-ps5-quad-index-initial-fence-host.py` asserts the actual source
placement and pinned generator adapter, the Vulkan wrapper's null-handle
semantics, and executes the exact extracted condition in a Clang ASan/UBSan
fixture. The fixture distinguishes first allocation, identical/lower count
and subsequent growth. Full native-generator parity is enforced by the existing
CI preflight.

This is narrow: the source still has GPU waits under guest cache locks for
**later quad-index buffer resizes** and conditional graphics descriptor-buffer
ring reuse. No claim is made about FC27, which may never use quad topologies.
No console build, release or hardware test is requested.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_QUAD_STRIP_DRAW_COUNT.md`:

```md
# Native quad-strip draw count: prevent unsigned underflow

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

`MakeDrawParams` converted quad strips with
`(num_vertices - 2) / 2 * 6` using `u32` arithmetic. For zero or one
vertex, subtraction wraps to a very large number, creating a giant
`vkCmdDrawIndexed` request rather than an empty primitive.

The native renderer and pinned generator now use
`num_vertices >= 2 ? (num_vertices - 2) / 2 * 6 : 0`.
`BindQuadIndexBuffer` additionally reuses its existing null-buffer
binding for all draws with fewer than four vertices; those cannot form
a complete quad and must not trigger a zero-byte LUT allocation.
Normal strips, quad arrays, triangle paths, base-vertex handling,
render-pass state, descriptor queues and Vulkan synchronization are unchanged.

`tools/check-ps5-quad-strip-draw-count-host.py` extracts the production
function into a C++20 Clang ASan/UBSan witness. It checks 256 consecutive
counts including 0, 1, 2 and 3, both direct/indexed inputs, and verifies
the existing non-strip topology counts are unchanged. Source and generator
guards verify incomplete quad draws never reach LUT allocation.

No console build or release is requested. This is a demonstrated arithmetic
defect, not an established cause of any particular title's freeze or HUD issue.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_RADV_GS_COMPUTE_SINK.md`:

```md
# Guard dropped GS-as-compute draw pointers — 16 October 2026

The maintained RADV path could leave vertex-output, index, count and
output-index pointers equal to zero when GPU-side geometry setup rejected
an oversized draw. Later passes risked dereferencing null GPU addresses.

Now the CPU-side parameters default to a dedicated 256-byte sink, and the
rejected GPU-side setup assigns its three outputs to the draw's read-only
sink. Both source units are versioned, with pinned Mesa left immutable.

Native build input lists, source-equivalence oracle and cached-driver
fingerprint include the maintained OpenCL source, now 12 files. Clang
ASan/UBSan host test extracts the actual rejected-draw code and compares
old null pointers to the guarded branch. No native driver was compiled.

This does not establish that the known game freezes/HUD issues reached
this specific geometry-shader path, or that console performance improved.
Reference: https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/80bfd2b67f81
```

`docs/2026-10-16_SHADER_LOCAL_SCRATCH_BOUNDS.md`:

```md
# Shader local scratch bounds — 16 October 2026

The pinned shader translator selects zero for an out-of-bounds local read,
but emits `ir.LoadLocal(word_offset)` before selecting the result. In shader
IR this is an actual read operation, not a conditional expression; the
invalid scratch index can reach the GPU. Local writes from dynamic offsets
are unguarded, including the tail of multiword stores.

The maintained, native-only shader source first selects a valid local address
then performs reads, returns zero for out-of-bounds reads, and preserves the
previous contents of word zero when an invalid dynamic store is emitted.
Immediate out-of-bounds tail words are dropped, and zero-sized scratch
allocation never emits a read or write. The original pinned source remains
unchanged. The shader_recompiler target uses the maintained single TU.

The CI host regression compiles the real pinned and maintained helper code
with Clang ASan/UBSan and a bounded scratch-memory mock. The pinned helper
must reproduce the unsafe load; the maintained helper must handle dynamic
and immediate OOB access without touching invalid scratch. Source guards
ensure 8/16/32/64/128 bit stores route through the checked helper.

This is a source-level correctness improvement, not evidence that past FC27
crashes or HUD defects had this cause; it does not qualify a console build.
Reference: https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/a302cde87a03158bfeab2a37aaf27e772d184b9d

## Multiword tail overflow follow-up

The original maintained multiword LDL/STL translation added `i*4` to a
32-bit byte offset before testing its bound. For an offset `0xFFFFFFFC`, the
next word's byte offset wraps to zero, making an invalid access appear valid
and potentially aliasing scratch word zero. The same issue applies to an
in-range base whose later word exceeds the allocation.

Both LDL and STL now pass the **original** byte offset together with the
compile-time word advance to their helpers. The guards compare the original
offset against `local_size - byte_advance` (or reject when the advance does
not fit). No overflowing address addition participates in the bounds check.
ASan/UBSan tests cover wrapped tails, boundary crossings, valid tails and
empty scratch, and source checks reject reintroducing the unsafe expression.

```

`docs/2026-10-16_TITLE_CACHE_STORAGE_ISOLATION.md`:

```md
# Guest cache ownership by title — 16 October 2026

Original pinned SaveDataFactory::GetFullPath substitutes the current process
ID for guest Account/Device storage requests with title ID zero, but not Cache.
Consequently two titles requesting Cache(0) can share the same save/cache/0
folder, even when their cached binary data is not compatible.

This port keeps the pinned sources untouched and builds a versioned maintained
core file whose sole difference resolves Cache(0) to the running program ID.
Explicit Cache IDs and System/Temporary/Account/Device paths are unchanged.

The CI Clang ASan/UBSan host test compiles the actual GetFullPath method from
both pinned and maintained source, checks that the original reproduces the
shared zero-ID path and the maintained source separates two games, and checks
unchanged explicit IDs and other save types. No native package is built.

Existing old shared cache files are not migrated or deleted. A new per-title
cache may need regeneration. This does not establish FC27 gameplay improvement,
nor does it prove FC27 uses zero-ID cache on the console.

Reference: https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/a302cde87a03158bfeab2a37aaf27e772d184b9d
```

`docs/2026-10-16_VERTEX_BINDING_RANGE.md`:

```md
# Protect Vulkan vertex-binding counts from reversed ranges

Date: 2026-10-16. Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

The native Vulkan `BufferCacheRuntime::BindVertexBuffers` clamps each
`HostBindings` endpoint to `device.GetMaxVertexInputBindings()`, then
previously subtracted two unsigned `u32` endpoints and rejected only an
**exactly zero** result. An inverted range could therefore underflow to
a giant `binding_count`, passed to Vulkan with much smaller backing vectors.

The caller normally constructs ordered ranges. This is a defensive backend
boundary check for corrupted or unexpected binding metadata, not evidence
that a particular game currently reaches it.

The source and pinned generator now reject `max_binding <= min_binding`
**before** the subtraction. Valid ranges, clipping and both Vulkan
binding modes are unchanged. The source-extracted C++20 ASan/UBSan fixture
verifies ordinary, clipped, empty, reversed and max-u32 inputs. CI also checks
41-file Vulkan generator parity.

No descriptor-buffer lifetime, GPU fence, draw order, console build or
release is modified. This does not establish that FC27's HUD, freezes or
stutters are fixed.
```

`docs/2026-10-16_VERTEX_IDENTITY_AND_TITLE_RESET.md`:

```md
# Vertex input identity correction — 16 October 2026

Historical shader-classification code used only the vertex-B hash when choosing
whether the current graphics pipeline may use static input with no vertex
attributes. Merged vertex programs depend on both vertex-A and vertex-B.
Two distinct vertex-A programs with the same vertex-B could otherwise inherit
the wrong classification. The maintained fork now uses the exact A/B identity
array, as corrected in reference upstream change #184.

The GPU pipeline cache destructor also resets its process-global last-bound
vertex-input hint, preventing a previous game's state from skipping new
vertex buffer dirty rebinding. The per-title development reset restores
static_vertex_input=true before the next title's per-session switches.

Both source-generator and active versioned Vulkan files are updated together.
The host regression compiles the extracted actual classification helper with
Clang address/UB sanitizers to check colliding B hashes, cache invalidation
and two independent title resets. It is not a rendering-on-console test.

No console build, release or hardware test. Existing FC27 image/HUD errors
might have other causes; do not label them fixed from host checks.

Reference: https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/1b6ffb88727d3ea079666d53b4d8cdf3c069dba3
```

`docs/AUDIT_INDEPENDANT_NXNATIVE_EDEN_ENCORE_NS1_NS2_2026-11-06.md`:

# Audit indépendant — `seedds/nxnative` face à Eden Encore (NS1 / NS2)

**Date :** 6 novembre 2026

## 1. Verdict synthétique

**Intérêt : très élevé comme corpus de diagnostics et d'oracles ; faible comme backend directement transplantable.** `nxnative` n'est pas un émulateur Switch complet : le code ARM du jeu est réécrit pour exécution native Apple Silicon, les services Horizon sont substitués, NVN/NVN2 est traduit en opérations Metal. Eden Encore émule les chemins invité CPU/HLE/GPU et produit du **Vulkan sur PS5/RDNA2**. On ne copie ni son scheduling Apple, ni MetalFX, ni son GPU Metal comme s'ils étaient un moteur Vulkan.

Les enseignements les plus utiles pour Eden Encore sont, dans l'ordre :

1. **La chaîne causale « image absente » de Bananza.** Elle est documentée bien plus finement qu'un simple « écran noir » : initialisation du SDK/NVN2, shaders compute, conditions de clear, textures block-linear, géométrie, écritures mémoire globales et indirect draws.
2. **La séparation des vrais mécanismes de la logique par titre.** `game.tsv` contient des faits mesurés sur une version et un hôte ; le bon portage Eden consiste à comprendre NPDM, commandes GPU, attributs de shader, tables de textures et synchronisation, pas à forcer un mode spécial par TitleID.
3. **Des lacunes source vérifiables chez nous existent encore**, par exemple `ISBEWR 0x927`, `CSMTEST 0x80d`, les stages Task/Mesh, certaines formes de texture-buffer arrays et de sorties physiques, et le timeout d'acquisition de sémaphore. Mais il serait **faux** de prétendre que QMD3, le bridge Ampere, les atomiques, la mémoire NS2 ou NUP sont absents : ils ont déjà des propriétaires dans le code.
4. **Le catalogue des 148 répertoires de jeux** et les multiples documents par symptôme offrent un excellent modèle de couverture : comparer des preuves multi-titres et multi-versions plutôt que conduire le portage au rythme des écrans noirs d'un seul jeu.
5. **L'atteinte du premier framebuffer NS2 sur PS5 ne peut pas être déduite de ces preuves.** Dans notre dernier test console documenté, `guest_frame_handoff=0` sur Bananza/Mario Kart World, alors que l'initialisation Vulkan et le CPU invité démarraient. La qualification console reste **P5** ; le travail code/ABI/test hôte pour P0–P4 ne doit pas l'attendre.

### Priorités actionnables après comparaison

| Priorité technique | Cible précise | Pourquoi / qualification attendue | Etat au snapshot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Critique P2.4** | `ISBEWR 0x927`, `CSMTEST 0x80d`, instructions Task/Mesh et géométrie | `ISBEWR` est nommé en table ISA sans voie correspondante repérée dans `lower_to_maxwell.h`; `CSMTEST` sans abaissement repéré ; MKW prouve l'intérêt des shaders Task/Mesh | **Manque à traiter, ABI exact encore à établir** |
| **Haute P2.3/P2.4** | écritures GPU via pointeurs chargés, `GlobalMemoryToStorageBuffer`, mémoire de sortie physique | Bananza avait des comptes indirects incorrects lorsque les stores étaient supprimés ; notre SPIR-V contient un refus de certaines sorties physiques | **Partiel ; risque réel mais non rattaché à une capture PS5 actuelle** |
| **Haute P2.2c/P2.3** | TIC/TSC, SSBO/CBUF QMD3, texture-buffer arrays, lifetime image | Notre chemin existe mais le shader SPIR-V refuse explicitement les tableaux de texture buffers | **Chemin existant, formes restantes à qualifier** |
| **Haute P2.7** | `Puller::ProcessSemaphoreAcquire` | Un `TODO` sur `acquire_timeout` subsiste ; les attentes sont sensibles à la cohérence GPU/CPU | **Manque source confirmé** |
| **Haute P1.3** | réponses `GetInfo` NS2, Graphical Supervisor/VI2, nvdrv, vidéo | Bananza répertorie les valeurs attendues par SDK20 ; plusieurs IPC Eden sont encore conditionnels | **À vérifier commande par commande, sans inventer de succès** |
| **Moyenne P2.4** | texture GOB NS2, BC7/ASTC, niveaux mip et barrières | Défauts amont causant trous, texels NaN, cible noire | **À confronter au vrai cache de textures partagé NS1/NS2** |
| **Moyenne P4** | fixtures de shaders/opcodes et couverture par versions | Les TSV peuvent fournir clés, couples et formes contrôlées sans embarquer de données de jeu | **Outillage de qualification à construire, pas port de backend** |

---

## 2. Pourquoi l'architecture de `nxnative` est différente

| Sujet | `nxnative` | Eden Encore sur PS5 | Conséquence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exécution CPU | NSO transformé ; ARM invité exécuté directement sur puce Apple, substitutions spécifiques | CPU/JIT émulation, gestion du processus invité et ABI Horizon | Les patchs du réécrivain NSO ne sont pas des correctifs génériques Dynarmic |
| Système | HLE native liée aux fonctions de jeu/SDK ; `dm/host/hle_*` | Kernel/HLE + services IPC/TIPC, NVDRV, KProcess, VI2 | Réutiliser les **contrats** et les séquences, pas les stubs Apple |
| GPU | NVN/NVN2 vers Metal ; composants du jeu prétransformés en SPIR-V/MSL et bibliothèques Apple | Méthodes GPU NVIDIA → pipeline Ampere/Maxwell → SPIR-V → Vulkan/RADV | Les métadonnées NVN2 et les sémantiques shaders sont transférables, pas les PSO Metal compilés |
| Mémoire | Pools Apple Silicon, texture Metal, allocations propre à l'app créée | GMMU/NVMap, mémoire et textures partagées du moteur PS5 | Respecter adresses/aliases/tuilage du **matériel invité**, pas l'allocateur Apple |
| Upscaling | NDSR de jeu, converti ou remplacé par MetalFX | NDSR/DLSS invités à interpréter, puis options graphiques PS5 Vulkan | Ne pas assimiler NDSR à DLSS Neural Rendering natif PS5 ou à FSR3.1 |
| Distribution | Une app Mac/iOS dérivée du jeu à partir d'un dump/NSP/NUP | Une app PS5 unique, bibliothèque multi-jeux NS1/NS2 | `game.tsv` doit rester une base de diagnostics, pas devenir une configuration obligatoire par titre |

**Convergence réelle :** les deux projets rencontrent les mêmes instructions Ampere, les mêmes sorties de culling, les mêmes registres de GPU, les mêmes formats de textures et les mêmes interactions de SDK. C'est à cette couche qu'il faut comparer.

### Organisation documentaire de `nxnative`

À la révision consultée, `dm/games` affiche **148 répertoires par TitleID**, dont **11 commençant par `040`** ; la présence d'un répertoire ne constitue pas une preuve que le jeu fonctionne intégralement. Cinq fichiers de contrôle complètent ce dossier : `README.md`, `game.py`, `profile_guess.py`, `settings.py`, `settings.tsv`.

- `dm/games/<titleid>/README.md` : version testée, symptôme, cause, correctif, validation et limites.
- `dm/games/<titleid>/game.tsv` : identité, modules, ressources, formats, paramètres observés, clés de shader.
- `shader_map.tsv`, `shader_facts.tsv`, `shader_pairs.tsv`, `pso_*` : *données d'évidence* produites/consommées par outils.
- `docs/reference/{shaders,rendering,nvn-objects,services,memory,movies,frame-rate,packing}.md` : index transversal **symptôme → cause → correction → jeux touchés**.
- `dm/gfx/tools/shader_split.py`, `dmsh_ampere.py`, `dmsh_xlate`, `dmsh_mesh.py` : extraction, décodage, conversion, sélection de shaders ; références **algorithmiques**, pas modules PS5 prêts à compiler.
- `dm/gfx/nvn/hle_nvn.c`, `nvn_mtl.m`, `dm/host/hle_svc.c`, `hle_codec_video.c`, `hle_oe.c`, `dm/gfx/hle_vi.c` : sources pour recouper la sémantique réelle.
- `dm/games/game.py` : matérialisation et validation du profil ; `dm/tools/impact_map.tsv` et les outils d'analyse peuvent inspirer des matrices de régression.

Un point fort est la **provenance multi-jeux** : la même cause peut être observée dans Bananza, MKW, Splatoon ou BOTW, ce qui évite de prendre une coïncidence de profil pour une exigence de l'architecture.

## 3. Audit détaillé des neuf fichiers de Donkey Kong Bananza

Dossier : [`dm/games/040074A01BF12000/`](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative/tree/b4318c7a4d0bcbd16e7873ce63f33d344d1acbfb/dm/games/040074A01BF12000) ; environ **5 406 181 octets** de documents et d'index.

| Fichier | Taille du blob GitHub | Contenu et apport | Transfert recommandé vers Eden |
