`docs/CONTENT_FORMAT_MATRIX_2026-10-23.md`:

```md
# Encore — game containers, internal compression and validation

**Branch:** `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. **Source of NSZ/XCZ reader:** [community contribution #285](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ProsperoEden/pull/285), adapted to Encore's complete-source architecture.

## Format support matrix

| Input | Type | Recognized by current Library? | Internal loader |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.nsp` | Game/update/DLC container | Yes | NSP |
| `.xci` | Cartridge game container | Yes | XCI |
| `.nsz` | NSP with compressed NCAs | Experimental | NSP + NCZ VFS |
| `.xcz` | XCI with compressed NCAs | Experimental | XCI + NCZ VFS |
| `.ncz` | Compressed NCA inside NSZ/XCZ | No | Translated to `.nca` by NCZ adapter |
| `.nro` | Homebrew program | **Selectable**, may not be a full game | Upstream NRO |
| `.nso` | Executable module | **Selectable**, may require other program contents | Upstream NSO, retaining LZ4 and ZBIC/zstd |
| `.nca` | Content archive | **Selectable**, only bootable when complete/valid | Upstream NCA |
| `.nax`, `.kip` | Program/archive types | **Selectable**, not always bootable alone | Upstream NAX and KIP loaders |
| Deconstructed ExeFS title directory | `roms/<name>/main` plus `main.npdm` | **Yes**; displayed as EXEFS, symlinks rejected | Upstream deconstructed-directory loader |
| `.zst`, `.zstd`, `.zbic` | Compression-oriented extensions | **No** | **Not** independent game containers |

**Do not conflate file formats:** zstd is used by the NCZ decompressor and the separately retained ZBIC path. LZ4 remains supported for NSO segments. This does **not** mean a raw `.zst` or `.zbic` is a playable title.

## Native source ownership

The reader and front-end adapter are `headless/ncz.h`, `headless/ncz.cpp`, `headless/ncz_vfs.h`. Five complete adapted translation units live under `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/`:

- `file_sys/submission_package.cpp` — resolve embedded `.ncz` when `.nca` is absent
- `file_sys/card_image.cpp` — open NCZ members as NCA views
- `loader/loader.cpp` — route NSZ to NSP and XCZ to XCI
- `loader/nsp.cpp` — accept NCZ member names during container identification
- `file_sys/registered_cache.cpp` — include compressed update/DLC containers

`headless/CMakeLists.txt` selects those five maintained source owners and compiles the NCZ adapter; it does not generate C++ by textual substitutions. Pinned Eden sources remain unchanged. Library filename checks are case-insensitive for all **nine** picker extensions.

## Storage, memory and access model

- NCZ **block** compression: bounded decompressed blocks kept in memory; no full copy required.
- NCZ **solid** compression: during play, a decompressed copy can be written under `/data/prosperoeden/user/cache/nsz/`. Outside a game, limited, checksummed reading windows are kept instead.
- Temporary `.part` files are created exclusively and cache opens refuse symlinks. The launcher refuses symlinked cache directory components. Unsafe archive entry names are rejected.
- Touchpad + L1 during loading stops permitting further solid unpack; the runtime closes its session-wide permission on exit.
- Insufficient storage may cause a slow sequential-read fallback; there is no promise of interactive performance from that path.

## Evidence and remaining acceptance

- **Source comparison:** the five maintained owners have been compared with their pinned baselines; each contains its reviewed NCZ adaptation, plus `ncz_vfs.h` inclusion where used. The maintained `loader.cpp` additionally includes the explicitly reviewed NAX extension fallback.
- **Committed host checks:** `tools/check-ncz.py` runs synthetic block/solid NCZ reconstruction under ASan/UBSan; `tools/check-encore-ncz-sources.py` verifies native-owner selection, all nine picker extensions in upper/lowercase, storage counts, and safe direct-loader metadata routing.
- **Security regression:** `headless/ncz_check.cpp` exercises symlinked cache paths and verifies they cannot overwrite a protected file.
- **Unverified:** full host CI and native PS5 package at the current HEAD; no console gameplay test of NSZ/XCZ.
- **FC27:** engine exits F01–F06 remain open; this feature does not constitute a fix for stutter, missing textures or the in-game HUD. Console qualification F07 remains postponed until the engine is ready.

This document is an implementation/validation ledger, not a compatibility claim for released binaries.


## October 23 integration checkpoint

- Selected maintained code is byte-for-byte equal to the five pinned Eden
  sources after the five reviewed NCZ transformations, with only the required
  VFS include on the two affected source owners.
- The launcher now enables solid unpack **before content/update registration**,
  avoids enabling it for ordinary Library discovery, and turns it off during
  game cancellation/teardown.
- NCZ cache protection rejects path separators, embedded NULs, symlinked
  cache directories, symlinked cache files and pre-existing partial files.
- A locally compiled **isolated reproduction** of the actual
  `headless/game_files.h` code passes the initial four-container extension cases and
  nine rejected examples; the maintained CI oracle now covers all nine loader extensions under `-O0` and `-O2` with UBSan.
- An isolated source-extracted NCZ cache open guard rejects symlinked
  `.unpacked`, `.part` and `.pieces` files under `-O0`/`-O2` with
  UBSan. The full `headless/ncz_check.cpp` suite is checked into the host CI.

## All-format Library routing — 23 October

The Encore game picker and its storage counter now accept these **nine**
case-insensitive extensions: `.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz`, `.xcz`, `.nro`,
`.nso`, `.nca`, `.nax`, `.kip`. Each is passed to the matching native
Eden loader; for raw executable/archive types the Library uses filename or
ID fallback rather than incorrectly opening them as NSP/XCI Control RomFS.
`.nax` now also has an explicit filename-type fallback, while signature
identification still takes precedence.

The underlying loader additionally identifies an extracted-game `main`
with its associated directory content and special NAX-style `00`
inputs. Encore now discovers the former when a direct child of `roms/`
contains regular non-symlink `main` and `main.npdm`, and persists
only a `<folder>/main` selection. These are **directory layouts**, not
ordinary file extensions. NAX-style `00` remains an internal layout,
not a standard top-level Library file format. There is no independent game loader for
raw `.ncz`, `.zst`, `.zbic` or `.lz4` files.

**Compression remains separate:** the original LZ4 NSO segment path and
Encore's ZBIC/zstd segment path are retained, alongside the NCZ zstd
block/solid reader for NSZ/XCZ. An executable/archive may be recognized
but fail to boot when it lacks its companion files or required metadata.
No blanket compatibility claim is made before native CI and hardware tests.


## Final all-extension source checkpoint

The TV Library's **actual scanning loop**, not just `ValidRomFilename`,
now checks `Eden::IsGameFile(file)` from `headless/game_files.h` rather
than the historical NSP/XCI-only conditional. This unifies discovery,
saved/recents selection, development-ROM filtering and storage counts
for the nine file extensions.

The generic Metadata Bridge recognizes the distinction between full
NSP/XCI-style containers and direct NRO/NSO/NCA/NAX/KIP files. Direct
modules are never misparsed as submission packages for icon/language
extraction. The native core makes the final decision about bootability.

A recheck of **all five** NCZ-aware maintained source owners against the
pinned Eden files confirmed byte-for-byte expected transformations,
including the explicit NAX filename fallback. `check-encore-ncz-sources.py`
contains a negative assertion that the legacy
`format != "NSP" && format != "XCI"` scan condition cannot return.
The source and host-test gate is committed, but the native build status
for the latest HEAD remains unknown; these are **development** features,
not a hardware-tested compatibility statement.

The pre-existing FC27 performance and memory-correctness work remains
separate. F01-F06 cannot be closed merely because more loading formats
are visible in the front-end. A complete native compilation is requested
with `[full-build]`, and F07 still requires the planned final PS5
qualification, not an immediate test.

## ExeFS host regression — 23 October

Maintained title discovery now supports **nine file extensions plus
deconstructed ExeFS directories** under `roms/<folder>/`. Each candidate
must contain regular non-symlink `main` and `main.npdm` files.
Only `<folder>/main` is an admissible persisted selection: arbitrary
nested paths, `../`, backslashes, symlinked directories and symlinked
required files are excluded. The frontend revalidates this structure
immediately before native title loading. Saved/recent titles, dev
autoboot, launcher file counts, and the displayed folder title are
covered by dedicated code paths.

`tools/check-exefs-directory-host.py` compiles the maintained ExeFS
selector and the real saved-ROM validator with C++20/UBSan on available
host compilers, covering valid layouts, symlink attacks, invalid selection
paths and ordinary game containers. Its host CI registration is included
in `.github/workflows/encore-core-preflight.yml`.

**Status:** source changes and regression test are committed.
Neither a full host prevalidation success nor a native PS5 build or
hardware qualification is claimed. ExeFS is a loader capability,
not evidence that the FC27 rendering/performance exits F01–F06 are closed.


### ExeFS validation checkpoint

- ExeFS discovery in the TV Library is **source-integrated**; the display
  title is the containing folder and the canonical saved selection is
  `<folder>/main`, never an arbitrary nested path.
- Both files (`main` and `main.npdm`) must be regular, not symlinks;
  the containing directory must also be non-symlink. The launcher repeats
  these checks at game start.
- The storage summary includes directory-mode enumeration
  (`ListEntries(directory, true, ok)`), not the file-only enumeration
  used by the nine extensions. The test contracts explicitly reject
  accidental regression to file-only counts.
- **Isolated native-C++-style host witness**: Clang and GCC, `-O0`
  and `-O2`, UBSan — all four combinations passed on 23 October.
  This replayed the maintained validation logic but does **not** substitute
  for executing the repository's source-extracted
  `tools/check-exefs-directory-host.py` in CI.
- **Outstanding**: full GitHub host prevalidation, actual PS5 native build
  and final hardware qualification; do not classify the path as released
  or declare engine gate F01–F06 complete.

`docs/DEFERRED_DMA_RESUME_BOUNDARIES_2026-10-17.md`:

```md
# DMA command resume and side effects: actual-method host witness

Branch: dev/ps5-sparse-jit. Baseline: 06f004b. Native post-store bridge remains OFF.

## Exact source boundaries

- DmaPusher::DispatchCalls resets dma_pushbuffer_subindex to zero every
  time it is entered, calls Step() in a loop, then unconditionally calls
  GPU::FlushCommands() and GPU::OnCommandListEnd().
- DmaPusher::Step advances dma_pushbuffer_subindex only after the entire
  command header is processed, and pops the front CommandList when its
  final segment completes.
- DmaPusher::ProcessCommands uses a local command-word index. That index
  is not exposed as a resumable cursor, and method effects occur before
  the corresponding index/count update in some branches.
- The prefetch_command_list branch also processes its entire command
  span before popping its CommandList. A mid-span suspension lacks a
  native restart checkpoint.
- Step can wait in sync_cv for a rasterizer fence. A worker-deferred
  transition must preserve that fence's signaling dependencies.

## Host witness

tools/check-native-dma-resume-boundary-host.py extracts and compiles
the **unchanged pinned bodies** of DispatchCalls(), Step(),
ProcessCommands() and SetState() with narrow fake RAM, GPU and method
side effects. For both safe and unsafe guest command read variants:

1. An uninterrupted two-segment submission applies each command once,
   then flushes and signals command-list end once.
2. An artificially bounded DispatchCalls execution stops after its first
   fully completed Step; on re-entering DispatchCalls, the source resets
   the segment index, repeats the first effect, then executes the second.
   The command-list finalization also occurs twice.
3. Injecting an exception after the first method's observable effect
   exits Step before committing the segment index; calling Step again
   repeats that effect. This exception is an artificial pause witness,
   **not** a claim that native runtime currently throws at this point.
4. Calling Step twice without restarting DispatchCalls preserves the
   between-segment cursor in the fixture, but skips the DispatchCalls
   final FlushCommands / OnCommandListEnd behavior. It is not a complete
   replacement dispatcher.

These behaviors are demonstrated for the real method bodies but with
fake GPU and method effects, not real engine execution or Vulkan fences.

## Consequence

Do not add arbitrary pause points inside ProcessCommands, and do not
resume a pending pushbuffer by calling DispatchCalls again unchanged.
A safe resumable decoder would need an explicit durable checkpoint for
the current CommandList, header/segment, command-word position, method
count, non-incrementing mode, DMA offset, channel state, side-effect
commit status, and fence/end-of-list completion. It must establish
at-most-once externally visible effects even if a blocked operation is
canceled or the worker fails.

A safer alternative to research first is a true nonblocking deferral
*before* command decoding and side effects. But an early command list
envelope does not fully enumerate indirect memory dependencies and
command RAM can change before execution. A barrier before decode is
therefore not by itself a complete first-use GPU coherence solution.

No native execution change, no game fix, no console build/release and
no approval to enable bridge #187 follows from this test.

`docs/DEFERRED_GPU_INDIRECT_DEPENDENCY_2026-10-17.md`:

```md
# GPU submission cannot seal indirect-memory dependencies (host evidence)

Source branch: dev/ps5-sparse-jit. Parent candidate: 9c7f0db.
This note supplements DEFERRED_JIT_QUIESCENCE_ARCHITECTURE_2026-10-17.md.
**NO-GO: native post-store publication remains disabled.**

## Verified native call path

1. GPU::PushGPUEntries forwards a CommandList to GPUThread::SubmitList.
2. GPUThread::StartThread pops SubmitListCommand and invokes Scheduler::Push.
3. Scheduler::Push calls dma_pusher.Push and then DispatchCalls.
4. DmaPusher::Step takes the next CommandListHeader (addr, size, sync)
   and only there instantiates GpuGuestMemory<CommandHeader, SafeRead or
   UnsafeRead> to read guest-backed command words. ProcessCommands then
   decodes method values and dispatches them to engine code.

At the SubmitList boundary the envelope does NOT enumerate all guest-memory
ranges subsequently referenced by decoded methods. Two submissions with
identical headers can result in different decoded method arguments when
the backing command RAM differs at Step execution.

tools/check-native-dma-indirect-dependencies-host.py compiles the
**unchanged pinned DmaPusher::Step() C++ method body** with narrow fake
MemoryManager, GpuGuestMemory and rasterizer dependencies. It tests both
safe/unsafe reads, identical envelope/different RAM content, and a change
to command RAM between enqueue and Step. The fake ProcessCommands only
records method words; this test does NOT execute actual GPU engine methods
or establish device-side use, writes, or Vulkan barriers.

## Impact on the quiescence design

The previous idea, "prepare all page transitions before queuing a
SubmitList", cannot in general derive a complete page dependency set
from the current submitted CommandList headers. A source-compatible
pre-classification that reads the indirect payload earlier also needs
an explicit RAM snapshot, source lifetime and coherency protocol:
the guest may change command RAM between pre-scan and GPU execution.
A blind pre-scan without snapshots is not proof.

A first-use hook at the actual guest-memory read or GPU cache operation
can observe the concrete address, but the GPU worker must NOT synchronously
wait there for quiescence: in the current queue, GPU::TickWork only runs
on a later GPUTickCommand, and GPU::OnCPURead can enqueue such a tick then
wait on it. A synchronous wait risks cyclic head-of-line blocking.

Permissible avenues for future research, not implementation approval:

- A producer-side sealed/snapshotted command plan with proven guest
  memory lifetime, indirect decode, alias and GPU fence ordering.
- A resumable GPU command interpreter that defers only the dependent
  operation, without losing its DMA decode state, silently reordering
  rasterizer work, or starving CPU-read synchronization.
- A bounded transition protocol whose confirmed quiescence occurs
  outside JIT and GPU-thread blocking call stacks.

A new GPU dispatcher must preserve SubmitList ordering, command list
fences, syncpoint callbacks, channel state, and the current shutdown
semantics. The existing DmaPusher::Step also waits for sync_cv when
signal_sync && !synced; this is another suspension point to audit.

## Explicit missing proof

No real Dynarmic + GPU DmaPusher integration test, no native device
memory visibility proof, no CAS/store postpublication, no mutable
GuestMemory alias coverage, and no quantitative performance outcome.
Keep #187 OFF. This host experiment does not justify console or FC27 tests.


## Additional host evidence: safe command reads are not always snapshots

The pinned \`core/guest_memory.h\` \`GuestMemory::Read()\` tries
\`GetSpan()\` first. When that succeeds, \`SafeRead\` calls \`FlushRegion()\`
but exposes a mutable, backing-RAM \`std::span\` rather than copying command
bytes. This is an important distinction: safe cache synchronization does not
freeze an immutable command payload for pre-decode analysis.

The existing \`tools/check-native-guest-memory-coherence-host.py\` now executes
two additional actual-template C++ checks with aligned 32-bit words:

- A contiguous \`SafeRead\` invokes \`FlushRegion\`, holds a live pointer
  into guest backing memory, and observes a subsequent backing-store update.
- A noncontiguous \`SafeRead\` copies via \`ReadBlock\` and retains the
  original word despite the same subsequent RAM update.

These controlled single-thread updates demonstrate alias-vs-copy *semantics*,
not a specific racy runtime write, cache stale-read occurrence, or Vulkan
device-coherence failure. Real GPU command dependencies cannot be considered
sealed just because \`SafeRead\` ran at pre-scan time. A future snapshot
design must guarantee ownership/lifetime and coverage of every indirect
command word, map/unmap generation, and dependent resource before authorizing
any reordered first-use GPU operation. The bridge remains disabled.

`docs/DEFERRED_JIT_QUIESCENCE_ARCHITECTURE_2026-10-17.md`:

```md
# JIT tracked-page quiescence architecture — host model only

Branch: dev/ps5-sparse-jit. Baseline: 1c970b0.

**NO-GO: native deferred bridge #187 stays disabled.** This is not a
gameplay fix. The new host-only model never changes runtime code.

## Facts from native source

1. PhysicalCore::Interrupt() sets an interrupt flag then calls the
   active ArmInterface::SignalInterrupt(). Dynarmic A32/A64 request
   HaltExecution(BreakLoop). This requests an exit, not proof of one.
2. PhysicalCore::RunThread() has an EnterContext/ExitContext boundary
   enclosing actual JIT execution. ExitContext unlocks the thread and
   clears the active interface; there is no per-title handoff epoch.
3. CpuManager::MultiCoreRunGuestThread() can enter RunThread again.
   A new admission therefore must be blocked while a transition is pending.
4. KernelCore::SuspendEmulation() waits for scheduler threads to stop.
   It must not be called synchronously by an active JIT callback or by the
   GPU worker when a CPU core may be waiting for that GPU worker.
5. RasterizerMarkRegionCached() changes the checked fastmem access
   permissions and page-table mark. A pre-checked direct JIT store can
   nevertheless still be in flight at the GPU's first dependent use.

## Candidate two-phase handoff

REQUEST:
- Under a short coordinator lock, declare a generation/epoch pending.
  Reject new JIT run admission, protect tracked-page fastmem access and
  mark the affected page table entries, and request interrupts on active
  cores. Return immediately to guest callbacks, including the requester
  itself. Do not wait under any memory, scheduler or GPU cache lock.
- The GPU owner must be able to defer only dependent commands, and keep
  servicing unrelated commands and CPU-to-GPU/GPU-to-CPU requests.

QUIESCE:
- A core acknowledges only after its actual old-generation JIT run
  has stopped and all its direct writes have completed.
- A signal, interrupt flag, scheduler suspend request, or partial callback
  return is not itself such an acknowledgment. The restart path must
  check the pending epoch before entering another JIT run.
- Account for idle cores, concurrent processes, guest span writers,
  error shutdown and asynchronous renderer callbacks independently.

CONFIRM:
- Permit first GPU use of the page only after all relevant JIT runs have
  acknowledged AND page mappings, host memory, and device-visible writes
  are synchronized. Finalization must not race another transition.
- Release run admission with acquire/release ordering, and keep the
  marked-page callback path active for new guest accesses.
- If interrupted workers cannot exit or a fence fails, fail closed
  instead of releasing an unqualified page.

## Deterministic host witness

tools/check-native-jit-quiescence-model-host.py compiles a C++20 model
with three controlled schedules: a stale pre-checked writer while another
core waits for GPU work, a request issued from inside an active JIT run,
and terminal failure. The gate is modeled at RUN entry/exit only; the
GPU owner continues to service work while the transition is pending.

PASS proves only the synthetic scheduling protocol. It does not execute
Dynarmic, PhysicalCore, or a Vulkan device fence, and it gives no
performance measurements. It does not prove absence of real lock cycles.

## Unmet enablement gates

- Prove actual interrupt-to-ExitContext acknowledgments and restart
  admission with a real host Dynarmic integration test.
- Prove the GPU dispatcher can defer dependent use without deadlocking
  GPU-read/download requests triggered by guest callbacks.
- Close mutable CPU-side GuestMemory span producer and lifetime gaps.
- Join CAS read/device fence, reserve/store/publish, GPU invalidate/dirty
  replay and cancellation/fatal paths with a concrete lock ordering proof.
- Quantify normal-run and contested-run overhead, transition latency
  p50/p95/p99 and worst-case tails before considering native activation.

No console build, release or FC27 test is requested.

## Newly verified FIFO head-of-line hazard

The pinned GPU worker (`video_core/gpu_thread.cpp`) pops ONE
`CommandDataContainer` and completes its SubmitList branch before
dispatching the next entry. GPU read synchronization uses
`RequestSyncOperation` + `gpu_thread.TickGPU` to enqueue a later
`GPUTickCommand`, which invokes `GPU::TickWork`.

If an earlier dependent SubmitList blocks the GPU worker awaiting JIT
quiescence, while a JIT core waits for its GPU read fence via the later
GPUTick, the GPU queue cannot advance. This produces a precise wait cycle:
SubmitList → JIT exit → CPU read fence → GPUTick → SubmitList completion.

`tools/check-native-gpu-fifo-quiescence-host.py` reproduces this bounded
head-of-line stall from a FIFO model tied to actual source anchors.
It also demonstrates a hypothetical *independently qualified* GPU control
path which services the read synchronization but leaves later graphics
submits ordered. The model does NOT prove it is safe to process such a
control request ahead of the blocked SubmitList in real Vulkan or DMA.
If independence or fence ordering is unknown, it explicitly fails closed.

**Design impact:** before adding any quiescence wait to `DispatchCalls`,
`FlushCaching`, a rasterizer operation or a queued SubmitList, either
(i) resolve the transition before the dependent command enters the FIFO,
or (ii) introduce a separately proven non-blocking command suspension
and control-plane progress mechanism. Do not pump arbitrary GPU commands,
call `TickWork` out of order, or bypass graphics FIFO merely to avoid
the deadlock. Both approaches still require real hardware/device-fence
qualification. The native deferred bridge gate remains false.


## Real PhysicalCore method boundary: interrupt request versus exit acknowledgment

The added host fixture \`tools/check-native-physical-core-interrupt-ack-host.py\`
compiles the **unchanged source method bodies** of
\`PhysicalCore::RunThread()\`, \`PhysicalCore::Interrupt()\`, and
\`PhysicalCore::ClearInterrupt()\` from the pinned native core.
A narrow fake \`ArmInterface\` blocks inside its JIT \`RunThread()\` method
and reports entry, interrupt calls and final guest-thread unlocks.
This is a real *core control flow* test but not a real Dynarmic JIT build.

Expected finite scenarios:

- With one RUN deliberately blocked, \`Interrupt()\` returns and calls
  \`SignalInterrupt()\` while \`ExitContext()\` has not yet unlocked the
  guest thread. Interrupt REQUEST is therefore not the quiescence ACK.
- Once the mocked JIT returns \`BreakLoop\`, the original
  \`ExitContext()\` unlocks the guest thread and clears active members.
- Calling \`RunThread()\` while its interrupt flag remains set returns
  without another JIT RUN admission.
- Calling \`ClearInterrupt()\` and then \`RunThread()\` permits a second
  execution. The current source does not hold a separate page-transition
  epoch or conditional admission barrier across that restart.

This is the precise native insertion opportunity for future design:
ACK must be recorded only after the actual \`ExitContext\` work completes;
RESUME must consult an independently controlled transition generation
before clearing the interrupt or allowing another JIT admission.
A naive ACK inside \`Interrupt()\` or unconditional \`ClearInterrupt()\`
would reintroduce a stale direct-write/first-GPU-use window.

Strict limits: mock \`SignalInterrupt()\` simply records a request; it
does not execute Dynarmic, guarantee interrupt latency, exercise code
patching, handle multi-core migration, prove any memory or GPU fence,
or implement the barrier. Existing Source/JIT native gate remains OFF,
and no gameplay improvement is claimed.


## IsInterrupted: eliminate a real host data race without ABI changes

Core::PhysicalCore was storing m_is_interrupted under m_guard and
reading it without a lock in IsInterrupted(), including the guest CPU
scheduler's MultiCoreRunGuestThread loop. Under the C++ memory model
that is a conflicting concurrent plain read/write, even though the
writers take a mutex. This is independent of the disabled #187 bridge.

The native-only CMake source derivation now includes
headless/physical_core_interrupt_atomic.cmake immediately before the
existing physical_core.cpp output. The helper requires exactly five
pinned accesses (six in the diagnostic profile variant), replacing
ALL reads and writes with std::atomic_ref<bool> / atomic_ref<const bool>
relaxed load/store. The original bool field and its layout remain
unchanged; no vendored file is modified. The existing m_guard mutex
continues to protect active ArmInterface/thread pointers and
the Idle condition-variable predicate. Relaxed atomic operations are
sufficient for this flag's standalone visibility; they do not provide
a JIT-exit acknowledgment, release a page epoch or synchronize GPU
memory. If the pinned source grows new accesses, CMake aborts rather
than allowing new unsynchronized mixed atomic/plain accesses.

The host-only test tools/check-native-physical-core-atomic-host.py
actually runs CMake -P against the pinned native source for both
shipping and diagnostic profile variants, checks every transformed
access, and compiles/runs the unchanged derived RunThread, Interrupt,
ClearInterrupt and IsInterrupted C++ method bodies. It injects a
bounded two-thread flag reader/toggler, while retaining the existing
mocked JIT interrupt/exit/reentry witness. It does not execute
the native console binary or prove Dynarmic/GPU handoff safety.

This is a concrete fix for a C++ data race in the native-derived code,
NOT a claim that the freezes/HUD stalls are fixed. #187 stays disabled.

```

`docs/DEFERRED_SELECTIVE_GUEST_WRITE_DESIGN_2026-10-16.md`:

```md
# Selective tracked-page guest writes — design, not an activation approval

Source branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. Baseline: `3cf279f`; selective-source checks added in `0f96500` and `0e732a3`.

**Decision:** Keep `kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false`. Nothing in this
document changes native execution, GPU scheduling, releases, or gameplay.
The #187 deferred bridge remains an unqualified candidate.

## What the current source actually provides

1. `common/page_table.h`: `MarkRasterizerCached()` atomically sets
   `marked` and the `RasterizerCachedMemory` type. `ExtractPointer()`
   returns zero for marked entries unless `ignore_marked=true`.
2. `core/memory.cpp::RasterizerMarkRegionCached()`: when a region becomes
   GPU-cached, `host_buffer->Protect(...)` removes direct fastmem **write access**.
   In this x86-64 native port, `EDEN_A32_FASTMEM=ON` changes
   `HostMemory::Protect()` into updates to a **per-guest-page checked access
   byte map**, not an OS `mprotect()` call. The JIT checks the blocked-write bit
   before accessing the A32 fastmem window. The read permission depends on
   reactive flushing. Ordinary pages retain their direct path. A64 native
   application processes are excluded from the A32 fastmem arena in the
   CMake-derived `memory.cpp` (`!process.Is64Bit()` condition).
3. `core/memory.cpp::GetPointerImpl()`: marked regions take the
   `RasterizerCachedMemory` branch and invoke `on_rasterizer`. Scalar
   `Write<T>()` and conditional writes pass `HandleRasterizerWrite()`
   as that callback.
4. `core/arm/dynarmic/arm_dynarmic_{32,64}.cpp` installs
   `page_table_marked_bit=0` and `MemoryWrite*` callbacks. The actual
   `dynarmic/backend/x64/emit_x64_memory.h` lookup checks the marked
   bit and branches to `abort`, where `emit_x64_memory.cpp.inc` calls the
   memory-write fallback. `headless/CMakeLists.txt` keeps this behavior
   when generating its optimized bit-zero `test/jnz` check for A32/A64.
   `headless/checked-fastmem.cmake` routes blocked A32 fastmem stores
   (including scalar SIMD paths) to a checked page-table lookup and then
   callbacks when the page is marked. Native A32 exclusive fastmem uses
   a separately routed page-table path; `EDEN_INLINE_EXCLUSIVES` defaults
   OFF because forced inline exclusives previously exhibited a hardware
   soft-hang. This is real generated-store **source** evidence, but not a
   native deferred-publication implementation.
5. `core/guest_memory.h`: a mutable `GuestMemory` may hold a direct
   `GetSpan()` alias. This goes through `GetPointerSilent()`, which can
   obtain the underlying pointer to a marked page. `GuestMemoryScoped`
   invalidates after in-place writes; this is not yet an ordered
   reserve/store/publish protocol, and alias lifetime must be accounted for.
6. `vendor/sources/eden/CMakeLists.txt` sets `HAS_NCE` only on
   ARM64 Linux/Android; `core/CMakeLists.txt` includes NCE only when that
   flag is set. NCE is therefore **not** an active x86-64 native producer
   under this build selection. This does not qualify NCE for ARM64 ports.

7. `headless/memory_check.cpp` already runs actual synthetic A32 and
   A64 JIT instructions. Its `Check<false>()` / `Check<true>()` paths
   assert callbacks on marked pages; `CheckFastmemA32()` covers tracked,
   unaliased, cross-page, scalar SIMD and fallback cases; and
   `StressFastmemA32()` concurrently changes page permissions and marking
   while JIT guest workers execute and checks the final backing RAM.
   `BenchFastmemA32()` already offers table-versus-checked-fastmem host
   benchmarks, but no new timing measurements were made in this audit.
   These are pre-existing test **implementations**; their presence does
   not assert that this exact commit has executed/passed them.

Source anchors (including the actual JIT emitter, A32 access-byte guard,
and pre-existing host JIT harness) are checked by
`tools/check-deferred-native-access-coverage.py`. A green **source preflight**
means its assumptions still match and the bridge is correctly blocked; it
does not prove GPU/CPU synchronization or runtime JIT correctness.

## Concrete scoped producers and first-tracking hazard

The `GuestMemoryFlags` type also does **not** enforce read-only
access at compile time: `GuestMemory<..., SafeRead>` still offers
`T* data()`, mutable `operator[]` and a mutable `std::span<T>` from
`Read()`. Therefore a search restricted to `FLAGS & Write` cannot
prove the absence of in-place modifications through nominally read-only
buffers. This is a possible API-level escape, **not** a demonstrated
write at every read-only call site. Qualify actual mutating uses before
counting CPU-producer coverage as complete.

The scoped template in `core/guest_memory.h` is not tied to one
producer domain. Actual writable GPU-side instantiations are present:

| Consumer | Scoped write flag | Ownership / cache path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `video_core/engines/engine_upload.cpp` | `SafeReadCachedWrite` | GPU upload swizzle; contiguous mapped span may be modified in place |
| `video_core/engines/maxwell_dma.cpp` | `SafeReadCachedWrite`, `UnsafeReadCachedWrite` | GPU DMA linear/tiled copies; explicit `SetAddressAndSize()` changes the eventual destination in some paths |
| `video_core/engines/sw_blitter/blitter.cpp` | `SafeReadWrite` | GPU software blit into a writable destination |
| `video_core/host1x/vic.cpp` | `SafeWrite` | GPU video processing output |

All these aliases use `Tegra::MemoryManager` through
`GpuGuestMemoryScoped` and are **GPU engine producers**, not proof of
an uncaptured CPU/JIT store. `Tegra::MemoryManager::GetSpan()`
returns its mapped backing pointer via `memory.GetSpan()`.
With a mapped span, `GuestMemoryScoped` performs a **post-write
`InvalidateRegion()`**, not an ordered CPU reserve/store/publish.
Fallback copies may instead use `WriteBlockCached()`, which writes
through to RAM and records the invalidate in `accumulator`; its
`FlushCaching()` drains the accumulator. The native bridge must
preserve GPU command order and cache visibility; it must **not**
automatically classify these GPU-engine writes as CPU transaction
producers. The inventory is not exhaustive for CPU-side writable
`GuestMemory` users; further call-site qualification is required.

The more serious native page-transition gap is independent of the
above GPU engine aliases: `RasterizerMarkRegionCached()` calls
`host_buffer->Protect()` **before** it marks the PTE. The A32
`HostMemory::Protect()` function updates the checked access map
under its own mutex, but a JIT instruction tests that map without
taking the mutex. A previously passed guard can therefore proceed
with a direct store while protection/marking is happening. This
source sequence does not contain an **in-flight JIT writer quiescence
barrier** before the page becomes GPU-visible. The pre-existing
`StressFastmemA32()` verifies eventual RAM values under flips; it
does not assert a per-write callback/notification happened before
the GPU first used a newly cached page.

Before #187 can be activated, prove a transition protocol satisfying
both invariants: (a) no untracked direct CPU write still races when a
page becomes GPU-tracked, and (b) every later tracked write is ordered
against the GPU consumer. Avoid broad per-instruction locking. A
candidate epoch/safepoint scheme must have measured cost and a
concrete memory-model proof before being implemented in native code.

## Conditional stores: an existing read fence is not a CAS fence

`core/memory.cpp::WriteExclusive<T>()` and `WriteExclusive128()`
call `HandleRasterizerWrite()` **before**
`Common::AtomicCompareAndSwap()`, whether or not the comparison
succeeds. Neither function invokes `HandleRasterizerDownload()` in
its atomic path. Separately, `video_core/gpu.cpp::OnCPURead()`
already has an actual GPU read/download synchronization sequence
(`RequestSyncOperation`, `TickGPU`, `WaitForSyncOperation`).

This does **not** demonstrate that native CAS operations currently
corrupt game data. It does establish why moving the existing eager
notification into the deferred queue would be wrong: an unsuccessful
CAS is not a modified RAM store, and a future deferred CAS must
synchronize its expected-value read against any GPU-resident data
before the atomic attempt. `CommitConditionalAfterRead()` models
this host-side but is not attached to the native CPU/JIT path.
For the eventual bridge, reserve before the read fence, wait for
predecessors only, complete the GPU device transfer, attempt CAS
exactly once, then `PublishAndWake()` on success or
`CancelAndWake()` on failure. Keep the native gate closed.

## Required transaction for an intercepted GPU-tracked store

```text
CPU/JIT hits tracked page
  -> confirm actual callback/fault routing (including exclusives)
  -> finish GPU-to-CPU device read/download fence, if required
  -> reserve ordered producer ticket before modifying backing RAM
  -> execute the host RAM store exactly once (or report CAS failure)
  -> publish after successful modification, otherwise cancel
  -> GPU consumer drains only published tickets before dependent work
  -> GPU cache invalidation and dirty collection run in original order
```

There must be no GPU-cache mutex held while reserving, waiting for a
device fence, or publishing. A reserved-but-unpublished ticket must
prevent its consumer from passing the corresponding read hazard without
deadlocking the CPU producer. A failed publication is terminal for that
title/session, not permission to replay the store or fall back to an
unordered write. Cross-page stores and A64 128-bit stores need a
transaction covering the complete affected range.

The **linearization point** for a modified RAM store is its successful
post-store publication. A false CAS/failed conditional store cancels
the ticket. Do not enqueue a cache-maintenance operation as though it
had modified RAM; classify it separately.

The current `HandleRasterizerWrite()` calls the rasterizer *before*
the underlying `memcpy`/CAS. The developer bridge currently enqueues
at that earlier point; therefore a consumer could observe a notification
before the CPU has stored the bytes. Merely switching the queue's
notification ordering does not repair missing producers.

## Qualification gates: all required, none currently met as a set

| Boundary | Minimum evidence | Current status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A32/A64 cached page through page-table JIT | Generated lookup routes marked stores to callbacks; verify current host execution results and temporal ordering | Source and pre-existing synthetic JIT test coverage; not rerun here |
| A32 checked fastmem (A64 native has no arena) | Access-byte map selects direct/fallback; test marked, vector, crossing and exclusive cases | Source and pre-existing A32 host JIT test coverage; no new execution claim |
| Dynamic page transition | Prove no untracked in-flight store can overlap first GPU-cache use; inspect ordering of access-byte protection and PTE marking | Existing A32 concurrent stress test checks backing values; no GPU coherency proof |
| Writable `GuestMemory` aliases | Distinguish GPU engine aliases from CPU-side producers; preserve post-write invalidation and FIFO visibility | GPU DMA/upload/blitter/VIC owners identified, CPU-side call sites not exhausted |
| Conditional/atomic write | GPU-device read fence, predecessor wait, CAS success/failure and exactly-once publication | Native CAS pre-notifies and has no download call in its atomic path; host protocol only |
| GPU work and dirty collection | Confirm no GPU consumer overtakes unpublished writes and that cache invalidation/dirty collection are properly ordered | Not demonstrated |
| x86-64 build NCE applicability | Conditional compilation in CMake | Excluded under current settings |
| Performance | Compare host-run JIT on tracked/untracked pages and under contention | Existing `--fastmem-bench` for table vs checked A32; no new measurements or GPU contention profile |

### Proposed implementation boundary

Keep fastmem and page-table access active for **untracked pages**. Use
the existing page-marking / protection machinery to select only
GPU-tracked pages for a prospective callback-based store transaction.
No global JIT-wide mutex, no blanket `fastmem_pointer=nullopt`, and
no all-memory callback conversion. The pinned x64 Dynarmic backend and
native-derived port do have marked-page fallback mechanisms; the open
task is verifying their interaction with a post-store GPU transaction,
not rediscovering whether marked pages can reach callbacks.

Introduce no deferred native write until the producer-side post-store
publication and consumer-side fence are part of the **same proven path**.
Mutable writable spans need an explicit separate solution: a raw pointer
cannot retroactively acquire a store ticket after users have changed its
contents.

### Measurement without another console test

Reuse `headless/memory_check.cpp` instead of creating another synthetic
JIT harness: the default test already exercises real A32/A64 marked
page-table stores plus A32 checked-fastmem and concurrent page flips.
Its `--fastmem-bench` mode reports `FASTMEM_BENCH kind=... mode=table/checked
ns_per_iteration=...`; preserve that baseline. If a future developer-only
host transaction prototype is built, add the missing *post-store*
publication/consumer visibility/fence assertions on tracked pages and
compare with existing non-deferred numbers, with p50/p95/p99 under GPU
contention. Never infer actual runtime wins from source coverage or
queue-only tests.

If the proof shows an unobservable tracked-page store, a deadlock,
out-of-order consumer, or an unbounded slowdown, stop: the bridge
cannot be activated. FC27 freezes, HUD rendering defects and stutters
remain independent open problems until game-level evidence exists.

## Current follow-up

1. Reuse the pinned x64 JIT emitter and `memory_check.cpp` as the
   actual interception baseline; do **not** disable direct memory broadly.
2. Inventory actual mutable `GuestMemory` call sites and their lifetime,
   and determine whether marked-page aliases bypass the write transaction.
3. Prove the first-tracking transition excludes in-flight direct stores;
   a successful A32 backing-value stress test alone does not establish
   GPU-visible ordering.
4. Only then prototype tracked-store post-publication plus the actual
   GPU-to-CPU device read fence, behind a host-only gate, keeping the
   native gate false.

No console build, release or new gameplay test follows from this design.

```

```md
# Eden Encore — main-only development policy

**Effective 30 October 2026:** [`niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore`](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore) is an independent GitHub repository, and **`main` is both its default branch and the only branch authorized for new development**.

This supersedes the original October 13 policy that used `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. Its obsolete branch reference has been **removed after merging its five final commits into `main`**; the commits and PR #5 remain accessible in Git history. Do **not** recreate, push to, merge, fast-forward, cherry-pick into, open new PRs against, or run new development automation on that old development branch. No parallel F07 branch or fork may become the source of truth.

## Rules for changes

1. Fetch and verify the current **`main` HEAD** before every write. Concurrent F07 fixes must not be overwritten.
2. Commit directly to `main`, preserving its existing commit history. Use a safe expected SHA or other optimistic-concurrency check when updating refs.
3. Do not force-push or rewrite `main`. Do not resurrect the old history containing the oversized `vendor/` source tree.
4. Keep the pinned `vendor` Git submodule in the original path; its repository is `niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore-vendor`. Ordinary clones must initialize submodules.
5. Test the exact commit changed. Source/host checks and CI are distinct from native PS5 compilation and from **hardware validation on firmware 13.60**.
6. Do not launch a final native PS5 release build until the F07 optimization work is signed off. A green source test or a successful screenshot does not justify a release.
7. Avoid using a secondary development branch for documentation, security, launcher, Vulkan or performance fixes. Existing secondary branches can remain for historical reference but must not receive new work.

**All automation prompts, badges, README build links and issue templates must point to `main`.** GitHub's old branch-filtered runs remain usable as historical proof, not as the current active pipeline.

## Migration checkpoints (historical)

- **13 October 2026:** the former repository `niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore` consolidated R419–R428 on its then-primary `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` branch. Older [CI evidence](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38380839924) describes the state **at that date only**.
- **30 October 2026:** the active code and branches, release tags, release assets, and pinned `vendor` were moved to independent `niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore`. The old fork was reduced to a historical redirection containing a Git submodule link to the new repository.
- **30 October 2026:** Avatar PR #1 and the main synchronization PR #4 were merged; `main` became the only active branch for subsequent work by explicit maintainer instruction.

The archived fork's stars and historic release/issue metadata remain distinct from the new repository's GitHub metadata. The Git history rewrite and mirror are documented separately in [repository history compaction](REPO_HISTORY_COMPACTION_2026-10-30.md). Historical document references to `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` or older SHAs do **not** override this policy.

## Current references

- [Official repository and README](../README.md)
- [Install and build instructions](../INSTALL.md)
- [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Accessibility](../ACCESSIBILITY.md)
- [Security](../SECURITY.md)
- [F07 source/hardware validation tracker](FC27_F07_MASTER_TRACKER.md)

### P1.3 — décodeur vidéo H.264/VP8/VP9 natif commun (06/11/2026)

Cinq sources maintenues dans `vendor/encore-active/ns2-runtime/video_decoder` :
`video_core/host1x/nx2_video_decoder.{h,cpp}`, `h264_packet.h` (GPL-3.0,
portage adapté d'Eden NX2/Lichii `nx2`) et le véritable service IPC
`core/hle/service/am/service/graphics_video_decoder_session.{h,cpp}`.
Le backend est sélectionné par `video_core`, le service par `core`, dans
le même binaire natif NS1/NS2 sans mode expérimental.

La famille de sessions GSV 902/905/906/1002 crée de vrais handles, la
sous-session 1 crée le décodeur ; 200/201/202 vérifient le KTransferMemory,
101 configure uniquement des codecs réellement ouverts H.264/VP8/VP9,
6 démarre, 3 fournit un KEvent réel, 311/314/212 gèrent les images de sortie
et leurs fences, 109/400 alimentent le décodeur, 213 retourne uniquement
des images effectivement écrites dans le NVMap du processus. Un échec de
Render/WriteBlock, une image détruite ou une fence de retour non atteinte
**ne signale aucune frame**. Il n'y a pas de branche spéciale pour un jeu.

Témoins hôte Clang/GCC UBSan O0/O2 :
`check_native_video_decoder_backend_host.py` (framing H264),
`check_native_video_decoder_ipc_host.py` (réelle méthode `Pump` extraite,
fences, écriture, échecs). Syntaxe C++ des vrais backend et service validée
sur Mac. Pas encore de preuve end-to-end HOS/codec/frame sur PS5 ; les
cas limites EOS/flush/backpressure et l'AV1 restent à qualifier/traiter. La
compilation du supervisor entier sur Mac requiert les propriétaires kernel
GPU natifs (attribut `GpuAccessible` absent du header Eden hôte).


### P1.3 — propriétaires NVDRV communs post-F07 (06/11/2026)

Deux unités C++ complètes dans `vendor/encore-active/eden-core`, sélectionnées
par `headless/CMakeLists.txt` dans le moteur commun :

- `src/core/hle/service/nvdrv/core/nvmap.cpp` — vérifie la session lors du
  pin/unmap ; refuse une session introuvable au lieu de la déréférencer.
- `src/core/hle/service/nvdrv/devices/nvmap.cpp` — conserve le rollback
  d'allocation PS5 N11 et rejette les FD absents/fermés avant `Alloc`/`Free`.
- `src/core/hle/service/nvdrv/devices/nvhost_nvdec_common.cpp` — refuse
  une adresse basse non épinglée et restaure les références NVMap déjà
  acquises lorsqu'un élément ultérieur d'un lot NVDEC échoue.
Le propriétaire `ns2-runtime/nvdrv_as` commun refuse aussi tout pin SMMU
nul ou physiquement hors plage avant `gmmu->Map`, pour les fonctions
legacy NS1 et les fonctions natives NS2. Une allocation du bas de l'espace
GPU qui échoue ne compte plus comme un pin réussi.
La récupération SMMU n'attend plus le verrou d'un autre handle en tenant
celui de la file : elle essaie les candidats disponibles sans blocage mutuel,
puis refuse l'opération si tous sont occupés. La file n'enregistre plus de
pins négatifs après un double `UnpinHandle`; `FreeHandle` refuse aussi les
comptages de doublons déjà nuls. Témoins :
`check_native_nvmap_smmu_reclaim_host.py` et
`check_native_nvmap_pin_refs_host.py`, Clang/GCC O0/O2.

Le propriétaire existant `src/core/hle/service/nvdrv/core/container.cpp`
rejette également les identifiants invalides ou les sessions inactives. Ces
sources ajoutées après la revue F07 ne modifient pas ses 337 entrées historiques.
Témoin : `tools/ns2/check_nvdrv_fd_session_owners_host.py` (Clang/GCC O0/O2) ;
compilation syntaxique hôte des trois vrais fichiers. Le propriétaire NVMap
commun récupère désormais le bon handle en cas de saturation SMMU, refuse une
queue de récupération vide et termine sans boucle infinie. Témoin réel :
`tools/ns2/check_native_nvmap_smmu_reclaim_host.py` (Clang/GCC O0/O2).
Le pointeur `Session*` reste emprunté : aucune garantie de durée de vie
concurrente ni essai console.

## Critères de tenue à jour

Chaque nouveau fichier C/C++ ou en-tête introduit dans le fork doit figurer
dans ce tableau, même s'il n'a pas encore été qualifié. Tout déplacement ou
retrait doit mettre à jour la liste et les liens du graphe.

Tous les chemins actifs sont inventoriés ; seuls les deux en-têtes de correction d'avertissements possèdent un garde dédié sans ID historique dans le graphe. La prochaine étape est de
prouver la sélection native, la parité des transformations et le comportement
console des changements pertinents. Ne pas gonfler les résultats HOST.

#### P1.3 — sortie décodée CPU/GPU (06/11/2026)

La session vidéo adapte les images RGBA/BGRA au layout block-linear lorsque
la ressource GSV est effectivement mappée au GPU (TIPC 426), via le swizzle
partagé Eden. NV12 demeure pitch-linear ; le propriétaire revalide l'état
des mappings sous verrou avant écriture. Test hôte :
`tools/ns2/check_native_video_decoder_ipc_host.py`. Aucun test PS5.

#### P1.3 — décodeurs AV1 et HEVC (06/11/2026)

Le backend maintenu de `video_core/host1x/nx2_video_decoder.cpp` utilise
FFmpeg pour sélectionner AV1 (av01/av1) et HEVC (hevc/h265/hev1/hvc1), sans
modifier l'enum NVDEC du moteur NS1. Si la bibliothèque liée ne propose pas
le codec demandé, l'initialisation échoue explicitement. Les flux HEVC
length-prefixed utilisent le convertisseur Annex-B partagé. Validation hôte :
compilation syntaxique du propriétaire et tests O0/O2 du sélecteur réel.
Aucune preuve de lecture AV1/HEVC sur PS5.

#### P1.3 — fin de flux vidéo (06/11/2026)

`native_video_eos.h` fait partie du propriétaire IPC natif. L'entrée 109/400
accepte maintenant un paquet EOS sans données compressées et appelle le drain
FFmpeg. En l'absence de nouvelle image décodée, le marqueur EOS est appliqué
à la dernière image réelle en attente, ou à la dernière image déjà écrite mais
encore dans la queue de sortie. Sans image réelle, la commande retourne une
erreur, sans simuler un framebuffer ni signaler un fence imaginaire. Test hôte
Clang/GCC O0/O2 : `tools/ns2/check_native_video_eos_host.py`.

#### P1.3 — durée de vie du work buffer du décodeur (06/11/2026)

La session `nn::codec::video` vérifie l'origine du KTransferMemory pour
l'application liée au GraphicsSupervisor, son état initialisé et la taille
alignée aux pages. Elle conserve une véritable référence kernel de COPY
pendant toute la session jusqu'à Finalize (RAII), même après la fermeture
du handle invité. Test de contrat hôte :
`tools/ns2/check_native_video_work_buffer_host.py` Clang/GCC UBSan O0/O2.

#### P1.4 — correspondance du swizzle vidéo avec le vrai moteur Eden (06/11/2026)

`tools/ns2/check_native_video_tiling_roundtrip_host.py` compile les véritables
méthodes `SwizzleTexture`, `UnswizzleTexture` et `CalculateSize` à partir de
`vendor/sources/eden/src/video_core/textures/decoders.cpp` (seul son
include transitif GPU, sans rapport avec ces méthodes, est retiré dans la
copie éphémère de test). La suite reconstruit 48 géométries, de 64×64 à
1920×1080, pour vérifier les tailles de surface et l'intégrité exacte des
pixels aller-retour. Clang/GCC O0/O2 UBSan : PASS sur Mac. Aucune preuve de
texture affichée par le pilote GPU PS5.

#### P1.3 — notification de disponibilité des entrées vidéo (06/11/2026)

Le service `nx2:vdec` possède une source C++ `native_video_ready_state.h`
maintenue dans `vendor`. Les clients auto-clear peuvent attendre de nouveau
l'événement TIPC 3 tant que la file d'entrées est disponible : CoreTiming
réémet un signal toutes les 4 ms. La notification est suspendue si la file
est pleine ou si la session est arrêtée. À la destruction, le callback
se détache avant `UnscheduleEvent`, puis le kernel event est fermé, sans
référence suspendue vers la session. Contrôles C++ réels et tests hôte
Clang/GCC O0/O2 `tools/ns2/check_native_video_ready_event_host.py`.

#### P1.3 — éveil répétable du décodeur vidéo et fermeture sûre (06/11/2026)

La session native utilise `native_video_ready_state.h`, un propriétaire de
signal prêt auto-clear partagé avec son minuteur CoreTiming. La notification
est reproduite toutes les 4 ms lorsque la session fonctionne et que la file
d'entrée a de la capacité, sans succès factice de décodage. En fermeture,
la notification est détachée sous mutex **avant** l'annulation du minuteur
et la libération de l'objet KEvent, évitant le pointeur de callback périmé.
Le vrai propriétaire C++ compile et les tests hôte
`check_native_video_ready_event_host.py` Clang/GCC UBSan O0/O2 passent.
Cela ne prouve pas la cadence de la console PS5.

#### P1.3 — initialisation native du contexte vidéo GSV (06/11/2026)

Les commandes TIPC `901` et `1001` d'initialisation du service codec
reconnaissent désormais la requête sans arguments de l'API `nn::codec::video`.
Le succès IPC est conditionné à la préparation réelle du contexte GPU et à
la présence du module NVDRV de ce processus ; mauvaises tailles, service
absent et GPU non initialisé sont refusés. Les sessions décodage 902/905/906
et 1002 restent gérées avec des objets kernel propres au processus.
Vérification de source et compilation hôte : `check-ns2-graphics-hle-host.py`.

#### P2.3 — atomiques GPU Compute avec pointeur QMD3 authentifié (06/11/2026)

Propriétaire maintenu : `vendor/encore-active/ns2-runtime/ampere/shader_recompiler/frontend/ampere/native_global_atomic_binding.h` ; dans `renderer_spirv_bridge.cpp`, le passage effectif `NativeAtomic::Rewrite(ir)` convertit les globales 32 bits à adresse de descripteur CBUF connue en véritables `StorageAtomic*32` existants. Les accès restent contraints par les vérifications SSBO/QMD3 et le contrôle de plage Vulkan. Le symbole n'est pas activé dans le pipeline NS1. Le normaliseur de pointeur prend en charge les deux mots CBUF scalaires consécutifs et les additions commutatives, sans substituer une adresse non authentifiée ; les tests vérifient aussi la correspondance du second slot SSBO dans une table NVN aplatie. Les sept variantes flottantes CAS F32/F16x2/F32x2 sont raccordées au backend SPIR-V qui effectue réellement un échange atomique sur un mot 32 bits (F32x2 passe par la représentation half2), sans prétendre à une écriture atomique de deux mots. Tests hôte : `tools/ns2/check_native_qmd_direct_cbuf_host.py`.

#### P2.3 — ABI du CAS flottant F16x2 SPIR-V (06/11/2026)

Le propriétaire natif sélectionné `vendor/encore-active/ns2-runtime/ampere/shader_recompiler/backend/spirv/spirv_emit_context.cpp` lie `f16x2_{add,min,max}_cas` avec un `memory_type = U32[1]`, tandis que `value_type = F16[2]`. Le stockage est un mot U32 avec `OpAtomicCompareExchange` de largeur 32 bits. Vérification dans `tools/ns2/check_shared_ns2_spirv_compiler_host.py` ; NS1 conserve son propriétaire original.

#### P2.3 — CAS F32x2 sur mot SSBO U32 (06/11/2026)

Les trois boucles CAS natives `f32x2_{add,min,max}_cas` dans `spirv_emit_context.cpp` lisent et écrivent un mot U32, avec OpUnpackHalf2x16/OpPackHalf2x16 pour la valeur F32x2 ; l'opération est un seul OpAtomicCompareExchange 32 bits. Qualification du propriétaire et du CMake dans `check_shared_ns2_spirv_compiler_host.py`.

#### P2.3 — qualification réelle des sept modules SPIR-V CAS (06/11/2026)

L'intégration `tools/ns2/test_ampere_real_spirv.cpp` crée sept modules Compute à travers l'émetteur SPIR-V réel. `tools/check-ns2-spirv-host.py` valide chaque sortie avec `spirv-val --target-env spv1.5` et `--target-env vulkan1.2`. Le test conserve un `OpAtomicCompareExchange` par module et ne simule pas le runtime PS5.

```

`docs/EDEN_ARCHITECTURE.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore — architecture du dépôt et contrat de source unique

**Statut : décision d'architecture / cible obligatoire, migration en cours.**
**Référence :** `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`, relevé structurel du 18 octobre 2026.
**Périmètre :** moteur natif, dépendances, JIT, CPU/HLE, mémoire, GPU, backend vidéo, build, scripts et CI. Le launcher reste un chantier fonctionnel distinct.

> **Principe : une modification de code d'une dépendance = une source maintenue dans `vendor/encore-active/` = un seul chemin réellement sélectionné par le compilateur.**
>
> Ce document définit la **cible**, pas un état déjà atteint. Ne jamais assimiler la présence d'un fichier sous `encore-active`, un test hôte vert ou un manifeste à une preuve d'exécution correcte sur console.

## 1. Architecture cible

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    UP["vendor/sources/<br/>Dépendances épinglées et immuables"]
    ACTIVE["vendor/encore-active/<br/>SOURCE UNIQUE des adaptations<br/>C/C++ / headers / backports / pilotes"]
    DATA["Données & ressources<br/>profils, traductions, shaders, assets"]
    PREP["tools/ + Makefile<br/>Vérifier, préparer, copier sans réécrire le moteur"]
    CFG["CMake<br/>Choisir les unités et options<br/>Configurer / compiler / lier"]
    PROD["Artefact natif<br/>sources et options compilées traçables"]
    VERIFY["Tests et CI<br/>parité → build natif → qualification matérielle"]
    UP --> PREP
    ACTIVE --> PREP
    PREP --> CFG
    DATA --> CFG
    CFG --> PROD
    PROD --> VERIFY
    ACTIVE -. "Comparaison avec l'original" .-> VERIFY
```

**Il existe deux catégories différentes d'entrées :**

- **Code tiers adapté :** sa version Encore maintenue est versionnée **exclusivement** sous `vendor/encore-active/`. Le code épinglé reste intact. Les outils ne fabriquent pas un deuxième corps C++.
- **Code propre à l'application, configuration et ressources :** ils peuvent résider dans `headless/`, `src/`, `data/`, `assets/` ou d'autres emplacements identifiés. Un shader, un catalogue de chaînes ou un profil généré n'est pas automatiquement un override de dépendance.

Les fichiers CMake maintenus eux-mêmes peuvent figurer dans `encore-active` lorsque ce sont des **recettes de build versionnées** : ce n'est pas une permission de réintroduire des fonctions C++ sous forme de chaînes dans CMake.

Les volumes changent à chaque migration : les chiffres courants sont dans les registres de sources et de générateurs, pour éviter de figer plusieurs totaux contradictoires dans l'architecture.

## 2. Inventaire récursif des dossiers : rôle et frontière

L'arbre Git a été interrogé pour les **racines du dépôt et leurs sous-arbres**. Cette carte couvre les familles de répertoires, y compris celles qui ne contiennent pas de code C++. Elle ne signifie pas que chaque fonction de chaque dépendance a été relue, ni que les chemins de build ont été prouvés par compilation.

| Famille | Sous-dossiers / contenu recensés | Rôle autorisé | Risque à contrôler |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/` | `workflows/`, `codeql/`, `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` | CI, analyse, automatisation de tests et packaging | Aucun workflow ne doit créer un correctif C++ hors `encore-active` |
| `assets/` | Artworks / ressources | Ressources applicatives | Aucun code moteur |
| `data/` | Dont `glyph-research/` et données des glyphes | Entrées de contenu et profils | Génération d'en-tête de **données**, pas de fonctions tiers |
| `docs/` | Architecture, audits, migration, catalogues | Contrats et preuves | Ne pas confondre inventaire et validation |
| `fixtures/` | Cas d'essai, fragments de tests | Oracles/tests | Ne doit pas remplacer le code compilé en release |
| `headless/` | `backports/`, `dynarmic/`, `prosperoeden/`, `elevation/`, sources natives, CMake, `.inc` | Application/bridge natif, launcher, sélection de build | **Dette majeure** : générations et injections de C++ |
| `sce_sys/` | Métadonnées de package | Emballage | Pas de modification du moteur |
| `src/` | Petites sources propres au port | Code natif local | Bien distinguer code original et substitution de dépendance |
| `third_party/` | Dont `fonts/` | Bibliothèques/ressources embarquées | Toute adaptation d'une source tierce doit être déclarée |
| `tools/` | `ci/`, `fixtures/`, `launcher/`, `stubs/`, `verify/`, scripts racine | Préparation, copie, génération de **ressources**, vérification | Scripts d'écriture et patches cachés dans le chemin de build |
| `vendor/sources/` | 23 arbres de dépendances épinglées, dont `eden/`, `eden-cpm/`, `ps5-mesa/`, `encore-overrides/`, OpenGL, runtime, SDK | Origines intègres, auditées par révision et empreinte | Ne jamais servir de seconde source modifiée |
| `vendor/objects/` | Objets/chunks et manifestes des dépendances | Cache/versionnement d'objets sources | Pas de correctif C++ actif caché |
| `vendor/encore-active/` | `compiler-rt/`, `eden-backports/`, `eden-build/`, `eden-core/`, `eden-gpu/`, `eden-shader/`, `eden-surface-lifecycle/`, `eden-sync/`, `eden-threading/`, `eden-vulkan/`, `ps5-mesa/` | **Source unique** des adaptations de dépendances | Chaque version doit être réellement sélectionnée, sans remplacement ultérieur |
| Racine | `Makefile`, README, licences, `UPSTREAM.json` et documentation utilisateur | Orchestration et provenance | Pas de correctif du moteur encodé dans la recette |

Les sous-dossiers de `vendor/sources/` restent du **code tiers épinglé**, non des emplacements autorisés pour de nouveaux correctifs Encore. La forêt volumineuse de `eden-cpm/boost` dépasse la limite de réponse récursive de l'API GitHub : sa présence et sa racine ont été vérifiées séparément ; **aucun contrôle exhaustif du contenu de toutes ses fonctions n'est revendiqué**. Les répertoires racine `headless/`, `tools/`, `vendor/encore-active/` et `vendor/objects/` ont été énumérés récursivement sans troncature.

### Cas particuliers à ne pas mélanger

- `vendor/sources/encore-overrides/` : **base épinglée de profils de jeux** ; malgré le terme « overrides », elle n'est pas le stockage des correctifs C++ du moteur. Les en-têtes `headless/encore_overrides_generated.h` et `headless/glyph_overrides_generated.h` en sont des sorties de **données** contrôlées, pas des réécritures C++ du CPU/GPU.
- `headless/prosperoeden/` : code du launcher, thème, UX, traduction. Ne pas déplacer aveuglément ces fichiers sous `vendor/encore-active` ni empiéter sur les travaux UI.
- `headless/backports/` : patches historiques ; ils peuvent rester des **oracles d'équivalence** hors production, mais **pas** constituer une autre implémentation livrée.
- `vendor/encore-active/eden-threading/native-hle-overrides.cmake` : sélecteur de sources maintenues et de headers copiés sans transformation textuelle de fonctions. Ce modèle est acceptable.
- Les tests hôtes qui transforment temporairement un staging (par exemple FFmpeg ou Meson) doivent être identifiés **hôte/configuration**, séparés des mutations de sources effectivement livrées.

## 3. Règles obligatoires, applicables à tout le dépôt

| Élément | Autorisé | Interdit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vendor/encore-active/**` | Vrais fichiers C/C++, en-têtes complets, backports matérialisés, CMake de build versionné, driver fork | Plusieurs implémentations actives concurrentes d'une même variante non documentée |
| `vendor/sources/**` | Sources épinglées immuables, identité SHA | Corriger directement la copie de référence versionnée |
| `headless/CMakeLists.txt`, `headless/**/*.cmake` | `target_sources`, `target_include_directories`, `target_compile_definitions`, liaison et options | `file(READ)` + `string(REPLACE)` pour réécrire des fonctions C++ destinées au binaire |
| `headless/**/*.inc` | Fragments applicatifs autonomes, ressources et entrées déclarées | Cacher un patch de dépendance injecté dans une source dérivée |
| `tools/**` | Vérifier SHA, recopier les sources maintenues, préparer SDK/cache, tester, générer des ressources | Reconstruire au build une variante C++ corrigée à partir d'un patch ou de substitutions |
| `.github/**` | Tester les invariants, construire, publier des reçus | Mutation silencieuse du code tiers avant le build |
| `docs/**` | Contrats, statut, sources, preuves, décisions et liens | Afficher « conforme » sans preuves de sélection effective |

**Une exception temporaire n'est pas une norme :** les mécanismes existants sont une **dette explicitement suivie** et ne doivent pas être copiés pour de nouveaux correctifs. Ne pas désactiver brutalement un générateur JIT/mémoire/GPU sans prouver la parité et la sélection équivalente.

### Contrat de sélection

Pour chaque fichier tiers adapté, on doit pouvoir répondre sans ambiguïté :

1. **Provenance :** quel fichier/commit original a été adapté ?
2. **Propriétaire :** quel chemin unique sous `vendor/encore-active/` maintient le correctif ?
3. **Variante :** `PS5_NATIVE`, `EDEN_DEV_PROFILE`, Vulkan/OpenGL, JIT, fastmem, option expérimentale ou release ?
4. **Compilation :** quelle cible, quel `.cpp` ou header et quelles priorités d'inclusion sont réellement actifs ?
5. **Concurrence :** la source précédente a-t-elle été retirée de la cible, sans double compilation ni masquage par un include prioritaire ?
6. **Preuve :** résultat d'un contrôle d'équivalence, d'un build natif et, quand nécessaire, d'un essai console à SHA identique ?

Les variantes volontairement distinctes doivent chacune avoir une **sélection conditionnelle explicite** et un propriétaire documenté. « Un propriétaire » n'interdit pas les variantes contrôlées : cela interdit les réécritures concurrentes et opaques.

## 4. État réel : dette connue, non résolue

**Photographie des registres, mise à jour le 19 octobre 2026 et susceptible de changer entre deux commits :**

- `vendor/encore-active/` : inventaire de sources et fragments maintenus dans [`EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md`](EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md) ; la couverture de chemins n'est pas une preuve d'exécution.
- `headless/CMakeLists.txt` : générateurs `write_derived()` restants et positions exactes dans [`EDEN_OVERRIDE_MIGRATION_INVENTORY.md`](EDEN_OVERRIDE_MIGRATION_INVENTORY.md) ; les modules indirects y sont suivis séparément.
- Modules CMake secondaires : **0 appel** supplémentaires ; le total courant (principal + modules) figure dans l'inventaire de migration. Un site ne représente pas nécessairement un fichier unique.
- Aucun module CMake actif ne modifie indirectement une variable contenant du C++ ; X05/X06 sont migrés et leurs oracles sont hors build.
- `headless/` : fragments `.inc` résiduels à classer par **consommateur effectif**, inventoriés dans [`EDEN_OVERRIDE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md`](EDEN_OVERRIDE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md) ; les patches historiques restent comptés distinctement.
- `tools/` comporte des centaines de scripts ; **les scripts de préparation/installation et leurs effets sur le staging** doivent être vérifiés, pas classés « tests uniquement » par leur répertoire.
- Les catalogues `EDEN_HEADLESS_SOURCE_CATALOG.md` et `EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md` inventorient les unités connues ; ils ne prouvent pas encore les entrées effectives du compilateur.

**Dette C++ G11/X06 migrée :** huit variantes JIT complètes sont directement sélectionnées dans `vendor/encore-active`. Les anciennes transformations G11/X06 servent seulement d'oracles dans `tools/fixtures`. Le site `write_derived` restant fabrique une ressource GLSL G23, pas du C++.

**Exemple du bon sens de migration :** `eden-threading/native-hle-overrides.cmake` choisit explicitement un vrai fichier C++ versionné et refuse l'absence de la source d'origine. Il ne compose pas le corps d'une fonction.

## 5. Procédure standard pour chaque migration

1. **Repérer tous les producteurs :** CMake principal, modules inclus, `.inc`, `tools/`, hooks de préparation, manifestes, anciennes recettes, patches historiques, dépendances et archives restaurées.
2. **Reconstituer le résultat actuel** pour la combinaison de flags concernée : fichier **réellement généré** et sélectionné, pas seulement le texte d'un patch.
3. **Matérialiser un vrai fichier maintenu** dans la famille appropriée de `vendor/encore-active/`, avec licence, provenance et changements intentionnels.
4. **Remplacer la mutation par la sélection** explicite du fichier `encore-active` ; retirer la source épinglée de la cible correspondante et traiter la priorité des headers.
5. **Prouver l'équivalence** de la version maintenue avec la version générée précédente pour les variantes pertinentes ; toute divergence doit être justifiée, testée et documentée.
6. **Faire passer les vérifications** : audits de source, compilations hôtes utiles, build natif, contrôles du package, puis tests console ciblés pour le comportement matériel/performance.
7. **Éliminer uniquement après preuve** le générateur, les fragments et le replay devenus inutiles ; préserver au besoin un oracle historique non branché sur le build.
8. **Actualiser les registres** et l'inventaire des fonctions : « migré » n'implique pas « bug corrigé » ou « FPS améliorés ».

Pour une zone risquée (JIT RW/RX, guest memory, scheduler, GPU queue, HLE/IPC), conserver le comportement et les options pendant la migration ; **ne pas mélanger refonte d'architecture et optimisation fonctionnelle**.

## 6. Contrôles CI à maintenir ou compléter

Le contrôle de conformité doit inspecter **les dossiers et sous-dossiers**, pas simplement rechercher `write_derived` dans un seul `CMakeLists.txt`.

- **Recensement récursif** des fichiers suivis : `git ls-files` / arbre Git, avec classification de chaque nouveau `.cmake`, `.inc`, `.patch`, `.diff`, `.py`, `.sh` pouvant affecter le build.
- **Graphe des écritures :** pour chaque générateur et script actif, identifier l'entrée, l'étape d'exécution, la sortie, la sélection et le propriétaire.
- **Source sélectionnée :** manifest de chemins et empreintes des sources C/C++ et headers résolus, conditions de build et cible, plutôt qu'une simple présence sur disque.
- **Non-régression :** interdire l'ajout d'une transformation de source tierce hors `encore-active` sans exception explicite de migration ; les contrôles existants de dette restent actifs.
- **Séparation des preuves :** parité de contenu, test hôte, build natif, qualification console. Aucun niveau n'implique automatiquement le suivant.
- **Préservation des droits :** licences, entêtes de copyright, `LICENSES/`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` et crédits amont, y compris si le dépôt cesse d'être un fork GitHub.

**Critère de fin de chantier :** zéro correctif C++ tiers produit ou transformé hors `vendor/encore-active/` sur **tous les chemins de build livrés**, zéro doublon de source sélectionnée, et source compilée traçable de manière reproductible. Les générateurs légitimes de données, certificats, ressources et shaders restent autorisés lorsqu'ils sont explicitement classés.

## 7. Documents de suivi (non redondants)

- [Source de vérité des overrides](EDEN_OVERRIDE_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md) : **registre des mécanismes**, modules CMake et fragments.
- [Inventaire de migration](EDEN_OVERRIDE_MIGRATION_INVENTORY.md) : **dette active, générateurs et scripts**, état par sortie.
- [Catalogue des sources maintenues](EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md) : **chemins sous `encore-active`**.
- [Catalogue headless hors `encore-active`](EDEN_HEADLESS_SOURCE_CATALOG.md) : fichiers natifs et fragments à qualifier.
- [Graphe d'audit CPU/JIT/GPU/mémoire](EDEN_CORE_AUDIT_DEPENDENCIES.md) : **fonctions, contrats, états, preuves**.

`docs/EDEN_AUDIO_PCM_OVERFLOW_GUARD_2026-10-21.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore — validation PCM sans dépassement arithmétique

**21 octobre 2026.**

Dans la source native `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/audio_core/renderer/voice/voice_info.cpp`, les tailles PCM16 et PCMFloat étaient contrôlées avec `offset * bytes_per_sample > buffer_size` avant le test explicite des offsets négatifs. Selon les promotions de types, cette opération pouvait introduire un dépassement ou une conversion signée non souhaitée avant que l'adresse invalide soit rejetée.

`PcmOffsetsWithinBuffer` valide `sample_bytes != 0`, les deux offsets signés non négatifs, puis `static_cast<u64>(offset) <= size / sample_bytes`. Cette comparaison rejette les offsets trop grands sans multiplication ni conversion précoce d'un entier négatif. Les chemins ADPCM, le gestionnaire de pools, et les mises à jour DSP restent inchangés.

Le test `tools/check-native-audio-pcm-offsets-host.py` extrait cette véritable fonction constexpr, la compile avec Clang C++20 ASan/UBSan et exerce offsets valides/invalides, échantillonnages 2 et 4 octets, `INT32_MIN`, `INT32_MAX`, stride nul et buffers de grande taille.

**Compteur : 415/491 sources prises en charge ; 14 fichiers moteur/runtime restant à examiner ; 62 fichiers interface séparés ; 76 globalement.** Aucun résultat de fluidité, audio console ou freeze n'est encore validé.

## Fermeture des chemins de performance

Le pipeline doit rester réparti entre les familles **J** (JIT/CPU),
**H** (HLE/scheduler), **M** (mémoire invitée), **V** (Vulkan),
**R** (pilote RADV), **N** (GPU/NVDRV), **S** (progrès jeu/frames),
**A** (audio), **F** (fichiers/IPC), **Q** (durée de vie/arrêt),
ainsi que construction, ressources, réseau et entêtes applicatifs.

Chaque contrat P0 encore SOURCE ou OPEN représente une qualification
en attente, pas automatiquement un défaut à corriger. Un changement
dans une fonction partagée est acceptable si :

1. Le **chemin C++ réellement sélectionné** et ses propriétaires
   sont prouvés pour le profil natif concerné.
2. Le symptôme est relié à une observation précise, et une
   hypothèse de contention, de mémoire, de JIT ou de progression
   n'est pas présentée comme une causalité prouvée.
3. Un témoin du *comportement original* et un test ciblé de la
   correction existent (ASan/UBSan et cas de défaut si utile).
4. Le contrôle hôte entier, la sécurité C/C++ et un paquet natif
   au **même SHA** sont contrôlés. Le build n'est jamais déduit
   d'une simple copie vers `encore-active`.
5. La PS5 démontre dans une scène identique la progression des
   threads/du contenu et le p50/p95/p99 en temps de frame,
   les intervalles >50/>100/>500 ms, l'absence de gel et
   l'intégrité HUD/textures. Un affichage stable à 30 FPS ne
   prouve pas que le match progresse.

L'audit de complétude automatisé **ne peut pas prouver** qu'il
n'existe aucune optimisation possible, ni que tous les codes
C++ externes hors du périmètre inventorié sont couverts.
Il garantit que **chaque contrat déjà cartographié reste traçable,
que ses inconnues sont visibles, et qu'aucune preuve source ne
peut être convertie implicitement en preuve matérielle**.

Les branches de thèmes/launcher et les fonctions de rendu UX sont
hors modifications de cette passe ; les options post-store
