`docs/EDEN_BUFFER_PAGES_WIDE_PROBE_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# CPU writes: two-word guest buffer ownership probe (22 October 2026)

## Identified inefficiency
`Eden::BufferPages::NeverRegistered` maintains a 16-GiB guest physical
registration bitmap with 4-KiB granularity. Its previous 64-KiB size
threshold caused every larger write/unmap/readback to fall through to
locking even when all the bitmap pages were definitely never owned by
a GPU buffer. Normal operation still requires conservative locking for
any previously registered page, unknown coverage, invalid spans or
queries beyond the bounded probe.

An arbitrary unaligned **256-KiB** range covers at most 65 guest pages,
intersecting at most **two** 64-bit bitmap words. The same two atomic
loads therefore safely inspect four times the old byte range. The
change does not relax the safety requirements or change registration,
cache invalidation ordering, dirty-state publication or shader/texture
invalidation.

## Qualified source and tests
- `headless/buffer_pages.h`: raise only the read-side bounded probe from
  64 KiB to 256 KiB, retaining the immutable ownership witness and
  fail-closed overflow/unknown branches.
- `tools/check-native-buffer-pages-wide-probe-host.py`: actual header
  under UBSan in `-O0`/`-O2`, across an unaligned two-word boundary,
  first/last owned pages, adjacent distinct pages, overflow and >256-KiB
  fail-closed behavior.
- `tools/check-native-batched-buffer-invalidation-host.py`: never-owned
  128-KiB batch skips the buffer lock but still invalidates shader/query;
  >256-KiB batch retains original cache invalidation.
- `tools/check-native-single-range-buffer-invalidation-host.py`:
  equivalent per-range ordering and fallback.
- `tools/check-ps5-never-owned-buffer-unmap-host.py`:
  independent unmap and query/shader invariants.
- `tools/check-ps5-buffer-readback-elision-host.py`: source-selected
  ASan/UBSan readback witness, now also part of the fast gate.
- Fast gate on this branch succeeded after test qualification;
  full preflight and native build are independently checked.

## Scope and performance limits
In 21 October FC27 diagnostics, a late five-second window had about
16,029 recorded buffer-lock contentions and 147.9 ms total waiting,
but no individual tracked lock wait exceeded 1 ms. Draw-pipeline
configuration and GPU command recording dominate other sampled costs.
Those measurements were collected with advanced diagnostics enabled,
which changes lock instrumentation. They do not prove the frequency
of CPU write operations between 64 and 256 KiB on quiet firmware.

Thus, this patch removes a provable unnecessary lock acquisition for
unowned spans in that range. **No measured gain in game fluidity or
HUD/texture correctness is claimed.** Keep the JIT shared/compile-ahead
experimental paths separate until quiescence and stale-code controls
are validated.

```

`docs/EDEN_BUFFER_REGISTRATION_MULTIPAGE_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Buffer ownership: multi-page CPU invalidation (22 October 2026)

## Root cause and impact

The native `BufferCache::IsRegionRegistered` walked caching pages only until
it found a *non-overlapping* buffer occupying the first partial page. Instead
of checking subsequent pages, it set `page` to the end of the whole query.

Example: a small buffer registered in `[0x1000,0x1400)` and another buffer
in `[0x2000,0x2800)`. A guest write to `[0x1800,0x2800)` overlaps the
second buffer, but the old implementation returned false. This can suppress
buffer dirty-state publication and leave a stale GPU buffer until later work.

The test uses the actual method body extracted from the native maintained
buffer cache, with optimized and nonoptimized host builds under UBSan.
The previous loop fails the multi-page overlap witness; the corrected loop
passes. Zero-sized queries are explicitly rejected as non-overlapping.

## Selected patch and validation

- `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`
  carries the native-specific fix selected by the PS5 CMake profile.
- The 83 shipping backport sources and their exact hash-locked manifest remain
  unchanged; the source replay still installs identical pinned inputs.
- The independent native R437 reconstruction oracles apply the narrow fix
  after the original backport and DMA-width protections.
- `tools/check-ps5-buffer-region-multipage-host.py` covers a partially
  overlapping first page, later owned pages, unowned gaps, direct overlap
  and a zero-length guest range.
- The fast host gate confirms the regression at `-O0` and `-O2`, plus
  pinned 41-unit Vulkan regeneration and ordinary JIT/GPU source contracts.

## Qualification boundary

This patch fixes an actual false-negative buffer ownership query. It does
not prove FC27's HUD, jersey textures or frame pacing are corrected. Console
testing should only happen after the remaining independently measured JIT
and cache-wait bottlenecks have an actionable fix and a green release build.
Do not enable the experimental deferred guest-write bridge or unsafe JIT
sharing as a workaround without separate quiescence and ordering evidence.

```

```md
  vérifient le correctif sous ASan/UBSan. La reconstruction du bitmap conserve
  aussi la permission de la page suivante au lieu de la relire : 1 048 577
  évaluations au lieu de 2 097 152 pour la fenêtre complète, avec une carte
  résultante identique dans le témoin hôte. Voir
  [l’analyse fastmem](EDEN_FASTMEM_WINDOW_BOUNDS_2026-10-20.md).
- `QueryCacheRuntime::SyncValues` réserve les destinations avant le mutex et
  trie des indices pour fusionner les plages en O(N log N), avec redirections
  vers les requêtes d’origine. Les boucles de copie conservent leur ordre.
  Le témoin de 1 024 plages passe de **523 776 à 1 023 comparaisons** et de
  **11 allocations sous verrou à zéro** (une allocation avant verrou).
  Une plage traversant une page ne laisse plus deux groupes qui se recouvrent.
  Voir [les hypothèses et limites](EDEN_QUERY_SYNC_ALLOCATIONS_2026-10-20.md).
- Le fast gate exécute les nouveaux témoins et les deux anciens contrôles HLE
  qui avaient divergé. Aucun push, lancement de CI, release ou changement de
  réglage expérimental n’a été effectué.

mi-temps/fin de match ou reprise effective du PC invité n’est revendiqué.

Un second défaut HLE a été reproduit : l’échec du drapeau pouvait survenir

## Lot GPU / mémoire / intégration native supplémentaire

- Le clear DMA vérifiait l’enregistrement GPU avec un nombre de mots traité
  comme des octets. La vérification utilise toute la plage en octets ; elle
  refuse aussi les fills vides ou les tailles qui seraient tronquées par
  `FindBuffer(u32)`. Le chemin CPU existant est conservé. Le témoin compile
  les vrais `DMAClear` et `IsRegionRegistered`, reproduit le chevauchement
  tardif manqué, puis vérifie les octets GPU, les opérations de cache et le
  fallback sous ASan/UBSan. La parité complète R437 est conservée avec ce delta
  explicitement décrit dans ses deux oracles.
- Le premier build complet a révélé que l’override natif de DeviceMemoryManager
  remplaçait le backport actuel par une ancienne implémentation : `id_pool`
  n’existait plus dans son en-tête. La version native reprend maintenant tout
  le backport maintenu : atomiques de tables, protections de remappage,
  bornes physiques et registre ASID protégé sans réutilisation. La comparaison
  intégrale avec cette base autorise seulement les deux retours GetSpan décrits
  ci-dessous. Aucun manifeste de dépendance épinglée n’a été réécrit.
- Les deux vrais `GetSpan` réutilisent le numéro de page physique déjà validé.
  Cela supprime une seconde lecture atomique de la première page et les
  vérifications répétées de `GetPointer`. Le témoin démontre aussi le défaut
  précédent : un remappage entre validation et seconde recherche pouvait faire
  retourner une autre adresse physique, dont toute la plage n’avait pas été
  validée. Les variantes const/mutable, trous, remappages non contigus, bords
  virtuels/physiques et tombstones ASID passent sous ASan/UBSan. Cette propriété
  ne constitue pas un instantané atomique de toutes les pages pendant un remap.
- Les accès atomiques au bool d’interruption de PhysicalCore utilisent les
  builtins du compilateur, pris en charge par le SDK PS5. L’ABI bool et l’ordre
  relaxed restent identiques pour les lecteurs et les écrivains. Les deux
  profils maintenus et le témoin concurrent passent ; `std::atomic_ref` était
  indisponible dans ce SDK. Un include local redondant du memory manager GPU,
  devenu invalide après déplacement du fichier, a aussi été supprimé.
- Le tableau d’indices de SyncValues est dimensionné une fois pour le lot,
  au lieu de croître par `push_back`. La fusion et les copies gardent les
  résultats vérifiés précédemment.

La compilation en collecte d’erreurs a permis de traiter les deux derniers
échecs ensemble, puis de reprendre sur 13 étapes plutôt que de reconstruire
les dépendances. Le premier exécutable PS5 a été lié ; un package final incluant
le dernier changement GetSpan est en cours. Les nouvelles unités (memory
manager, PhysicalCore, instanciation DeviceMemoryManager) passent les vrais
arguments Clang PS5. Le précontrôle natif inclut désormais 22 unités.

Les vérifications restent ciblées après ces modifications : pas de relance
systématique des 332 commandes déjà exécutées. Les sept contrôles concernés

GetSpan additionnels. Les compteurs 400 / 98 / 411 restent soumis aux critères
individuels du registre, et les tests PS5 restent différés à la fin.

## Complément GPU — regroupement des invalidations dirty

`GPUDirtyMemoryManager::Gather` reconstitue les plages contiguës qui avaient
été divisées en masques de 2 Kio par le producteur. Il conserve l’ordre, les
trous et les doublons ; aucune allocation, aucun tri ni verrou n’est ajouté.
Chaque appel est limité à 256 Kio, borne du probe ImagePages, pour conserver
son filtrage et borner le travail des caches par appel. Les plages commençant
à zéro restent séparées : les deux rasterizers ignorent explicitement ces
invalidations et leur fusion ne doit pas absorber une plage non nulle.

Le témoin compile les classes complètes épinglée et maintenue sous ASan/UBSan.
Pour 2 Mio contigus, il mesure **1 024 → 8 appels**, puis compare exactement
la séquence de cellules couvertes sur 8 192 écritures dispersées, avec trous,
retours en arrière, doublons et filtrage de l’adresse zéro. Les collectes
vides, les époques successives et une écriture depuis le callback sont couvertes.
L’oracle intégral et le scénario concurrent de masque déplacé sont conservés.
Les trois contrôles du complément passent dans
`results/gpu-dirty-gather-2026-10-20/`. Le fast gate et la prévalidation incluent
le nouveau témoin. Le compteur reste **398 / 96 / 409** : M09 exige encore
une preuve aux frontières réelles des caches, sans gain FPS PS5 revendiqué.

## Suite — propriété des métadonnées de transfert GPU

Trois sources sont modifiées : `vk_buffer_cache_cost.cpp`,
`vk_texture_cache_cost.cpp` et `vulkan_query_cache.cpp`. Les captures des sept
chemins de copie de buffers, copie d’images, upload normal/MSAA et download
normal/MSAA prennent la propriété des vecteurs. Les commandes gardent donc
leurs données pendant l’exécution différée sans recopier leurs allocations.
Les deux chemins multi-destination réservent leurs conteneurs avant la boucle.
La réserve initiale des résultats de samples devient
`min(num_slots_used, pending_sync.size())` : chaque requête fournit au plus
un résultat, et le nouveau plafond n’augmente jamais l’estimation précédente.
Aucun transfert, ordre de commande, barrière, tick ou attente n’est supprimé.

Le nouveau témoin compile les captures réelles, les classes et les méthodes
Record/ExecuteAll du scheduler avec Boost et les types Vulkan épinglés. Sous
ASan/UBSan, il détruit les conteneurs appelants avant de rejouer les commandes,
force la reprise après débordement, vérifie les octets et recycle les blocs.
Pour les scénarios au-delà du stockage inline, chaque capture simple passe
de **1 à 0 allocation**, et chacun des deux scénarios imbriqués de **33 à 0**.
```

```md
ces deux décomptes comme s'il s'agissait de travaux différents**.

La pastille verte signifie uniquement : **le test hôte cité a réussi
pour la propriété indiquée**. Elle ne signifie **ni validation console,
ni gain de FPS, ni disparition des freezes**. Certains tests verts
démontrent précisément qu'une approche est dangereuse.

Une analyse historique n'est pas automatiquement un correctif ni un
test complet. Ces archives sont à relire **avant** d'ouvrir un doublon.


## Status is not success in game

- **HOST**: a *specific property* was exercised by a host test. A passing
  test may deliberately prove an unsafe behavior. It does NOT certify
  end-to-end console performance, correct emulation or freeze resolution.
- **SOURCE**: located and inspected in source, but no causal or end-to-end
  proof. Do not count it as solved.
- **OPEN**: concrete source-level question not resolved yet.
- **PARKED**: intentionally stopped. Deferred native bridge #187 stays OFF.

Priority **P0** means actual frozen gameplay/HUD/long-frame causality;
**P1** means correctness and native integration; **P2** means experimental
memory bridge safety. A HOST property can still have an unmet device gate.

## Dependency order / no more circular audits

- Runtime build: B01 => Q01/Q02/Q03 => V01 => V02/V04/V05 => S01/S02
- Guest progress: B01 => J01/J02/J03/J04 => H01/H02/H03
- Deferred bridge only: D01/D02 + M01/M02/M03/M04 (**PARKED**, not a
  prerequisite to fixing normal game freezes).

**Next work in order:** H03 using already reviewed H01/H02 and the native-selected scheduler; then
H06 for the concrete wake transition; then H09 only with a controlled invalid-key witness; then V02 and V04 if there is a
presentation/HUD stall distinct from guest progress; then J01 and V05
only for remaining *unattributed* long-frame events. Do not return to
aggregate JIT/cache statistics already studied.

first, not a claim that they are semantically proved. Source paths and
function/contract tokens are checked by CI for existence only; the
**Remaining acceptance** column is what still needs proof.

## Couverture encore NON exhaustive (à inventorier, pas à déclarer OK)

Outre les **81 lignes du graphe**, le dépôt comprend d'autres composants
susceptibles d'influencer le symptôme observé, dont les interfaces HID/commandes
en jeu, l'ordonnancement des services IPC, la restitution audio et les chemins
host-syncpoint. **Ils ne sont pas tous vérifiés par le présent tableau.**

- **Entrées/HID et pause en match :** isoler les fonctions de
  `ControllerUpdate`, du routage d'entrées et de l'overlay dans les
  sources réellement sélectionnées par CMake ; l'existence d'un contrôleur
  fonctionnel ne prouve pas que le match reçoit ses événements.
- **Services IPC/HLE et synchronisation multiple :** compléter H01–H05
  avec les objets de réveil effectivement impliqués dans les états
  des threads invités ; prioritaire pour un rendu à 30 FPS avec
  simulation figée.
- **GPU IOCTL/syncpoints, audio et composition :** N01, F01, A01
  et V09 sont désormais **ouverts et non validés**. Ne les approfondir
  qu'avec une dépendance mesurable au scénario gelé.
- **Toutes les variantes upstream/vendor et modules UI :** NON
  couvertes par cet audit de stabilité native ; inventaire complet
  du dépôt ≠ assurance de correction de FC27.

**Règle de clôture :** aucune réponse ne doit présenter « 81 lignes »
comme « toutes les fonctions restantes ». L'inventaire s'étend à mesure
des véritables appels, et une tâche n'est verte que pour son critère
de validation nommé.

### Source/build status after restructuring

- **HLE portion completed:** the maintained guest threading/SVC sources and synchronization header live under `vendor/encore-active`; `native-hle-overrides.cmake` only selects/copies these full sources. Its four-mode host CMake gate succeeded. The unchanged pinned sources stay under `vendor/sources/eden` as comparison baselines.
- **Not a repository-wide conversion:** `headless/CMakeLists.txt` still hosts legacy generated/derived code for other CPU/GPU/JIT/runtime components. Do not claim all overrides have migrated or add new source transformations there. Migrate one proven compiled source at a time to `encore-active` with a strict source parity test.
- **Priority after V10:** J01: use the already-shipped `EDEN_FRAME_JIT_CORE` and dev-only `EDEN_PERF_PROGRESS`, `EDEN_PERF_DUPLICATES`, `EDEN_PERF_JITPATH` alongside `tools/analyze-fc27-stutter.py` before adding instrumentation. The October 15 trace associates several long-frame *windows* with substantial JIT work, but not an individual frame or confirmed invalidation cause. H03/H05/H06/H07 still require real guest wake-to-JIT forward progress; V05/R03 still require the actual 285-ms mutex owner or proven GPU fence wait. Preserve these OPEN gates.
- **Upstream cherry-pick gate:** no further blanket import from the reviewed heads. Only an exact native path regression and its existing trace/test justify a selective backport.
- **Latest completed core audit preflight:** [#39033188668](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/39033188668) SUCCESS on `edecacafd570dc0a658ce04cc6dfed541b4bc0aa`; it verifies the prior register/HLE/Vulkan state, **not** a new console/game result.

## Established findings — do not re-run without changed evidence

1. October 15 FC27 session uses **Vulkan**. The 285.3 ms mutex wait is
   time lost by a guest CPU callback; the mutex *owner* is unknown.
   Texture-GC evictions were zero around frames 3300-3600. An ~980 ms
   frame had much less lock contention. See S01/S03 and the linked triage.
2. Nearly perfect 30 FPS can coexist with the **guest match remaining
   frozen**. This is not evidence the guest simulation advances.
   Sampled last-SVC values are NOT actual live waiting stacks.
   See S02 and the earlier guest freeze forensic report.
3. Atomic native physical-core flag fix (8f88877): host PASS, but
   interrupt request is not JIT exit acknowledgment. DMA partial
   resume/restart is unsafe by the prior host witness.
4. Native GPU queue slot lifetime fix (3e5af13, 8ac4929): the
   specific regression first passed inside preflight 38992155660 while
   that historical workflow failed on the separate T01 generator budget.
   Both checks now pass in the complete host preflight 39017376187.
   Neither result is console proof.
5. Native post-store #187 bridge is still DISABLED. Negative
   host witnesses for FIFO, aliases or DMA are not permission to
   enable the bridge or request a console build.

### GPU map/reverse-table patch ownership (M06–M07)

Les fichiers épinglés `src/core/device_memory_manager.inc` et
`src/core/device_memory_manager.h` disposent maintenant de points de
contrôle dédiés. Leurs fonctions sont identifiées, mais le code compilé
résulte de plusieurs patches successifs : **ceci n'est pas une validation
du chemin GPU actif**. Avant tout déplacement vers `vendor/encore-active`,
vérifier l'ordre de replay, la propriété des verrous ASID, les tables de
mappage inversé, les limites physiques et les unités effectivement
sélectionnées par le build.

### Overrides à matérialisation directe — fonctions identifiées

Les deux anciennes transformations indirectes X01 (MacroJIT) et X02
(SlotVector) sont maintenant **migrées** vers les sources maintenues dans
`vendor/encore-active/eden-core`. Q05 et B03 suivent désormais les chemins
compilés ; les vérifications hôtes reconstruisent strictement les anciens
résultats sans les générer pendant CMake. La validation console reste ouverte.

This is a complementary file-level view, **not** proof that each impacted
function has been read or exercised. The existing P01–P46 replay list
tracks *patch installation*, not complete source/function coverage.
A tracked active override can already subsume a patched original; therefore
"no exact graph row" means **needs source-owner reconciliation**, not
"definitely unfixed" or "needs another patch".

the complete patch target footprint and reports target files without an
exact pinned/active path in the function register; its result is a

## How to update after each task

1. Read this register, the completed-audit index, the current branch HEAD, its linked evidence,
   then only the immediate caller/callee of the first relevant OPEN
   (or SOURCE with new evidence). Preserve concurrent work ownership.
2. Record an explicit hypothesis and a falsifiable check **before**
   changing behavior. If a previous hypothesis was disproved, do not
   reopen it without a code change or new observation.
3. After a narrow fix, update its row with the test, the *actual*
   completed CI URL/conclusion and the next still-unmet acceptance.
   A green test is not a green workflow; a green workflow is not
   a console game test.
4. When blocked or out of evidence, say so and leave the row open.
   Do not add another speculative test or pseudo-progress commit.
5. Keep source/derived file distinction. Console release/build
   only upon demonstrated benefit and authorization. No UI edits here.

The automated host register check validates paths, symbols, IDs,
dependency acyclicity and statuses, **not** behavior.
```

```md
# Eden Encore — migration coordonnée CPU/JIT G11–G12 et X06/X07

**Actualisation au 19 octobre 2026 : migration de source effectuée ; plan
ci-dessous conservé comme historique, et non comme travaux à recommencer.**
Le sélecteur actif `headless/CMakeLists.txt` utilise désormais des unités
entières et exclusives `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/arm/dynarmic/g11/`
pour A32/A64 × hôte/natif × DEV/normal (8 fichiers, 16 combinaisons
avec l'option inline OFF/ON), au lieu de construire leurs fonctions
par `write_derived`. Le contrôle `tools/check-g11-jit-profile-matrix-host.py`
rejoue la sélection et compare les variantes à l'ancien générateur.
La compilation G12 sélectionne
`vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/hle/kernel/physical_core_{dev,standard}.cpp`
par copie sans transformation C++, avec l'atomicité X07 incluse aux
sources maintenues. Les anciennes recettes X06/X07 ne sont plus incluses
en tant que générateurs de fonctions.

**La prochaine étape n'est pas une migration supplémentaire de G11/G12 :
c'est l'analyse des compilations, invalidations, prises de verrous et
attentes constatées en exécution.** Les tests hôte et la sélection CMake
ne qualifient ni les FPS ni la progression de FC27 sur console.


**État au 18 octobre 2026 :** cartographie de la prochaine frontière ; sources
G11, G12 et substitutions indirectes X06/X07 **non migrées**. G10 (interface
native A32) a été déplacée dans `encore-active` et possède son contrôle de
parité propre. Le présent périmètre n'inclut ni le launcher ni ses ressources.

## Périmètre réel et interfaces

| Site restant | Source épinglée / module | Propriétaire futur | Variantes obligatoires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G11 | `src/core/arm/dynarmic/arm_dynarmic_{32,64}.cpp` et `headless/CMakeLists.txt` | Unités complètes `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/arm/dynarmic/` | A32/A64, hôte/natif, DEV/release, exclusifs désactivés/expérimentaux |
| X06 | `headless/native_jit_memory_read_guard.cmake` | Méthodes de callback mémoire des mêmes unités G11 | Aborts/refus de lecture, page-table, callback de suivi guest, absence de lecture après refus |
| G12 | `src/core/hle/kernel/physical_core.cpp` et `headless/CMakeLists.txt` | Unité complète de `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/hle/kernel/` | Idle normal, profilage DEV, host/native, préfetch abort |
| X07 | `headless/physical_core_interrupt_atomic.cmake` | Synchronisation de `m_is_interrupted` dans l'unité G12 | `IsInterrupted`, `Idle`, `Interrupt`, `ClearInterrupt`, stores/loads atomiques, DEV |

## G11 — contrôles couplés à conserver

La boucle CMake dérive les deux wrappers de Dynarmic. Elle applique
notamment : politique de code-cache A32/A64 avec capacité initiale,
`std::countl_zero(PageTable::ATTRIBUTE_MASK)`, fastmem exclusifs
(option `EDEN_INLINE_EXCLUSIVES` **OFF** par défaut), profilage de
callbacks DEV, diagnostics des accès invités, `Eden::Watch` et
`Eden::CrashSite` pour A64, rappel de `JitStartup::ConstructWithCapacityFallback`
sur allocations contiguës échouées, et le module X06.

**Couplage non négociable :** la source complete du wrapper A32 et celle
du wrapper A64 doivent recevoir les mêmes changements de capacité et les
mêmes signatures de callback prévues pour leur ISA. Les chemins `watch`,
`crash_site` et les compteurs n'entrent pas dans le hot path normal
lorsque les diagnostics sont désactivés. Ne pas activer l'inline
exclusive pour « améliorer » les chiffres sans preuve matérielle :
l'ancien commentaire de production documente un risque de soft hang.

Les bascules DEV, native et inline-exclusives doivent passer en
**gardes C++ explicites** ; CMake sélectionne ou copie l'unité complète,
mais ne reconstruit plus de corps de fonction par `string(REPLACE)`.

## G12/X07 — atomicité et arrêt sur faute

`physical_core.cpp` garde le chemin condition-variable original en
shipping. En DEV, l'échantillonnage Idle ne prend l'horloge que lorsque
la télémétrie détaillée est active. X07 transforme **toutes** les lectures
et écritures du booléen `m_is_interrupted` avec `std::atomic_ref` ;
une seule écriture ordinaire subsistante serait une data race.

L'arrêt après `PrefetchAbort` conserve le dump borné des registres
invités, la recherche de mapping LR et `RecordGuestFault` sur la seule
voie fatale. Aucun suivi par frame ni déréférencement d'adresse invitée
non fiable ne doit être introduit.

**Migration atomique :** produire les corps complets normal/DEV et intégrer
X07 **avant** de retirer simultanément G12 et
`physical_core_interrupt_atomic.cmake`. Ne pas laisser deux mécanismes
d'atomicité concurrents actifs.

## Preuves requises avant statut HOST / retrait des compteurs

1. Comparer chaque source maintenue à la source épinglée et aux
   transformations historiques, y compris les profils DEV et natif.
   Verrouiller les ancres de fonctions et la sélection CMake.
2. Exécuter `tools/check-native-physical-core-atomic-host.py`,
   `tools/check-native-physical-core-interrupt-ack-host.py`,
   `tools/check-ps5-guest-fault-recovery.py` pour G12/X07.
3. Exécuter `tools/check-native-jit-memory-read-guard-host.py`,
   `tools/check-ps5-architecture.py`, les tests de cache JIT et
   de callback pour G11/X06 ; comparer les chemins A32/A64.
4. Exécuter l'inventaire exact des modules et générateurs par
   `tools/check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py` et les catalogues de
   sources/graphes ; supprimer X06/X07 seulement avec leurs transformations.
5. Valider par préflight hôte ; qualifier séparément la compilation native
   et la console. Un test textuel ou CMake vert ne prouve ni le timing
   guest ni l'absence de soft hang.

**Contrat de reprise :** commencer par G12/X07 (un propriétaire commun
avec mode DEV), puis traiter G11/X06 comme un ensemble A32/A64. Les
générateurs G13 et suivants restent hors de ce périmètre.
```

```md
# DMA extent correction · 19 October 2026

`AccelerateDMA::DmaBufferImageCopy` previously multiplied two u32
guest dimensions before converting the already-wrapped product to
u32 for the Vulkan buffer cache. The accelerated path now widens first
and returns `false` for unrepresentable transfers.

The complete maintained native
`vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/engines/maxwell_dma.cpp`
now handles three software fallback extents using u64 arithmetic and
u32 upper bounds. The intermediate calculation checks division before
multiplication to avoid overflow even at u64 width. Negative minimum
pitch magnitude is widened before absolute value. The outer DMA
launch still releases its guest semaphore; normal-size copies follow
the original path.

Native CMake selects this complete unit under `encore-active`; host
builds and pinned sources remain unchanged. The source-extracted
`tools/check-native-dma-extent-host.py` enforces full replay parity
and executes the real guard expressions under ASan/UBSan, covering
large/normal/zero and signed-minimum cases. No console-build or FPS
improvement is claimed from this host-only witness.
```

`docs/EDEN_FASTMEM_SIGNAL_INSTALL_2026-10-21.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore — transactional signal installation and bounded fastmem JIT ranges

On the active A32 fastmem handler in `headless/fastmem_handler.cpp`, the former boolean short-circuit could successfully replace `SIGSEGV`, fail to replace `SIGBUS`, then return `installed=false` **with one handler still installed**. A subsequent unrelated fault could reach an unqualified custom trap path. The new installer restores the prior `SIGSEGV` action if the second registration fails and aborts when that restoration itself fails, rather than continuing in an ambiguous signal state.

`ValidCodeRange` also rejects null, reserved publication-sentinel, empty and wrapping JIT code spans **before** they are published into the lock-free fault lookup. The handler's signal-time range scan, callback and guest fallback semantics are unchanged; no locks or allocations were introduced into a signal handler.

The host test `tools/check-native-fastmem-signal-install-host.py` extracts the true initializer and range helper from maintained source, compiles them with C++20 ASan/UBSan and a deterministic `sigaction` mock, and verifies complete/partial-install rollback and boundary values. Fast gate and preflight execute it.

**422/491 inventoried sources reviewed; 7 remaining engine/runtime paths, 62 launcher UI sources separate.** No assertion of improved FC27 FPS, JIT throughput or console crash behavior.

## F07 / J07 — bounded fastmem fault lookup (30 October 2026)

On the maintained native handler, `Handle` previously scanned all 64 code ranges for every unclaimed synchronous signal even when only one or two live JIT arenas had registered. The high-water mark `published_range_prefix` is raised with release CAS **only after** the callback, end address and executable begin are published. `Handle` acquires it once and scans at most that many entries; retirement never shrinks it (low-index reuse is safe). No added locks, allocations, clocks or logging in the handler; callback, forwarded signal and code registration order remain unchanged. Source-extracted C++20 ASan/UBSan test checks zero reads when empty, one-slot scans, sparse higher slots, retirement/reuse and callback return addresses under O0/O2. This reduces avoidable signal-path work, not a proven PS5 FPS/HUD improvement. F07 PRE-BUILD remains **22/29** pending CI and console measurements.

```

`docs/EDEN_FASTMEM_WINDOW_BOUNDS_2026-10-20.md`:

```md
# A32 fastmem window: overflowing page-range clipping

The broader inventory found `src/host_memory.cpp` outside the 478-row contract
graph, although CMake compiles it into `common` and existing bridge checks read
it. The graph must not be described as a complete inventory of Encore code.

Hypothesis: `Window::Pages` clips the end using `min(offset + length,
WindowBytes)`. The addition can wrap before clipping. At offset 1 and length
`SIZE_MAX`, the derived last page becomes far larger than the A32 window.
`Unmap` then iterates over page arrays using that last page; `Protect` derives
an invalid iterator. Public unmap/protect calls do not independently bound it.

Preserve the helper's existing clipping semantics by limiting the length to
`WindowBytes - offset` before addition. A source-extracted ASan/UBSan witness
must reject the original result and verify zero, invalid, ordinary, cross-page,
end-of-window and maximal-length inputs. No whole guest-address-space walk or
console run is needed to reproduce the range error.

This is a bounds correction for the optional A32 fastmem window. It does not
enable that window, alter the A64 JIT, or establish a cause of FC27 freezes.

## Refresh work hypothesis

Under the window mutex, `Refresh` evaluates `Own(page)` and `Own(page+1)`
for every map byte, repeating the same page-access lookup on consecutive
iterations. The access/alias arrays are stable during this loop and distinct
from the map being written. Carry the successor value into the next iteration.
Compare the entire output map against the previous loop across page/alias
boundaries and the final guard page, while counting helper evaluations. N map
bytes should require N+1 evaluations instead of 2N. This is a source-work
measurement, not a PS5 frame-time benchmark.

### 30 October 2026 — redundant single-page fastmem permission no-op

`src/host_memory.cpp::Window::Protect` now skips the redundant `Refresh` for a single guest page whose requested permission matches its current permission. All Map/Unmap/Protect publishers already serialize under the same mutex and refresh their own map-byte modifications, so an unchanged page cannot change its own direct-JIT guard or the preceding page's cross-boundary guard. Existing accounting remains; changed protections and multi-page ranges use the original path. The `tools/check-fastmem-window-bounds-host.py` C++20 source-extracted host ASan/UBSan fixture exercises 20,000 repeated no-op calls under -O0/-O2 plus changed, adjacent and invalid requests. No console FPS claim; F07 still **22/29**.

### 30 October 2026 — fastmem repeat Map/Unmap skip, fail-safe kernel retry

`src/host_memory.cpp::Window::Map/Unmap` bypasses redundant per-page guard refresh for an identical, **already aliased** one-page mapping, or for a one-page Unmap whose backing and permissions are already absent. Map never skips an unaliased chunk, even when metadata is identical, preserving the attempted retry after a refused fixed kernel alias. Calls still increment diagnostics counters, while changed mappings and requests spanning pages retain the original Update and guard publication. The source-extracted C++20 O0/O2 ASan/UBSan witness checks 10,000 repeat unchanged aliases, 10,000 repeat unmaps, nonaliased retries and crossing page boundaries. No PS5 frame-time claim. **F07 remains 22/29**.

### 30 October 2026 — no-op permission updates within one PS5 16 KiB granule

`Window::Protect` now bypasses the metadata fill and JIT guard rebuild for unchanged permissions over **2–4** contiguous guest 4 KiB pages *inside one 16 KiB PS5 granule*. This extends the proven single-page no-op without a full-window search or modifications to native virtual mapping. Checks are bounded to at most four existing permission bytes under the original mutex; a changed byte or any cross-granule range takes the original publication path. The source-extracted O0/O2 ASan/UBSan witness distinguishes repeated same-granule requests from cross-granule requests, plus 20,000 repeated single-page calls. No console FPS measurements. F07 **22/29**.

### 30 October 2026 — repeated Map/Unmap within a 16 KiB kernel granule

`Window::Map` compares at most four existing page records before bypassing a repeated 2–4-page mapping **only if the direct alias is already active**. A rejected fixed-map leaves `chunk_aliased` unset, preserving the next attempt's `Update` retry. `Window::Unmap` likewise skips an already-zeroed 2–4-page range within one granule, checking both the backing and access metadata. All multi-granule and changed mapping operations still issue the original updates, including adjacent JIT crossing-guard refresh. Both checks remain under the existing mutex, with no new allocations. Source-extracted `check-fastmem-window-bounds-host.py` validates cold retry, changed access, 10,000 repeated multi-page mapped/unmapped calls and cross-granule fallback under C++20 -O0/-O2 ASan/UBSan. **F07 remains 22/29**; no console FPS assertion.

### 30 October 2026 — bounded 64 KiB cross-granule map/unmap no-op

`Window::Map` now checks a maximum of 16 guest pages (64 KiB) on an otherwise identical cross-16-KiB mapping; it skips `Update` **only** when every 16-KiB granule has a previously successful active fixed alias and all host backing-page indices and permission bytes match. An unaliased chunk, changed offset/access or longer mapping always takes the original kernel retry and guard update path. `Window::Unmap` skips short cross-granule ranges only if their backing and access arrays are entirely cleared. Existing `Window::mutex` and page counters remain unchanged. Source-extracted O0/O2 ASan/UBSan tests cover 10,000 cross-granule repeats, an unaliased chunk retry, changed access, exactly 16 pages and the 17-page fallback. F07 **22/29**; console performance not measured.

### 30 October 2026 — bounded cross-granule Protect no-op completes short fastmem family

`Window::Protect` now handles unchanged requests up to 16 guest pages (64 KiB) that cross native PS5 16 KiB granule boundaries. An unchanged short span leaves the authoritative JIT map untouched, while *any* changed permission or request of 17+ pages always retains the original `std::fill` + `Refresh` path (including predecessor cross-page guards). The check is bounded to 16 existing metadata bytes under the original mutex, with no kernel calls or allocations. Source-extracted C++20 ASan/UBSan O0/O2 oracle covers changed vs repeated cross-granule updates and the 16/17 page boundary. `Map`, `Unmap`, `Protect` all now share the same bounded unchanged-request policy, while Map still requires actual live native aliases before skipping. **F07 22/29**, native FPS not measured.

```

```md
### 31 October — flexible package add-on folders

The selector now discovers NSP/NSZ/XCI/XCZ add-ons in arbitrarily named
nested wrapper directories (e.g. `custom/extensions/bonus.nsp`), not only
under literal `updates/` or `dlc/`. It never regards the selected
base package as add-on content, rejects symlinks and does not recurse
into extracted RomFS/ExeFS payloads. The detected paths are passed to
the metadata-aware native content provider. Host source regression is
tracked by `tools/check-exefs-directory-host.py`; see
`docs/FLEXIBLE_LAYOUT_INTEGRATION_SOURCE_REVIEW_2026-10-31.md`.

A mixed title folder with exactly one XCI/XCZ and other NSP/NSZ content
selects the unique card image as its base. Multiple candidate card images
or anonymous NSP-only mixtures still fail closed rather than guessing.

## Addendum 2026-11-01 — ExeFS-first identification

The loader's reviewed source is now blob `7943b817dfa8118b150c4970d6513ec179262af0`. The exact source-owner gate reconstructs the maintained file from pinned Eden, plus existing NSZ/XCZ and NAX handling, and the explicitly reviewed first-choice `AppLoader_DeconstructedRomDirectory` for a file named `main` that actually belongs to a valid ExeFS directory. Standalone NSO files continue through the generic NSO detector. This avoids treating an extracted program with `main.npdm`, `rtld` and `sdk` as an isolated `main` NSO; no claim is made that Bananza gameplay boots or that Switch 2 emulation is complete.

### Revue complémentaire du 3 novembre 2026 — ExeFS mixte

Le nouvel objet `headless/game_files.h` (`dd89d9f9c5c0cde824f41889918f665275c05bdc`) ne modifie que trois sélections d'`exefs`/`base` : reconnaissance insensible à la casse des noms de répertoires exacts (`ExeFS`, `BASE`), sans accepter des préfixes ou les répertoires de mise à jour/DLC comme titres de base. Les contrôles des segments, erreurs de système de fichiers et liens symboliques restent inchangés; `tools/check-exefs-directory-host.py` est le témoin hôte. Cet inventaire reste distinct d'une preuve de lancement PS5.

### Revue complémentaire du 3 novembre 2026 — sélection NUP strictement P5

L'objet source `headless/game_files.h` (`0432c4c2651b2af22343f1401751b3222e30cdc4`) ajoute seulement `IsNupFile()` et ses appels dans `IsGameFile`, `IsNestedGameFileSelection` et `FindNestedGamePackage`. La qualification du sélecteur n'est **pas** une preuve d'exécution d'un jeu NUP sur PS5.

### Revue du 3 novembre — sélections enregistrées d'updates/DLC

Le blob `headless/game_files.h` `d292275239472a9df01205ceabbcd96a2e6a2877` applique désormais **la même exclusion** de noms réservés aux packages rencontrés lors de la découverte et aux chemins de titre déjà enregistrés. Les stems exacts update/patch/DLC/AOC/addon et leurs variantes avec suffixe `_` ou `-` sont refusés comme *base*; les noms de conteneurs AOC/patch sont aussi écartés des racines extraites. Les packages réels sont toujours classés via leurs métadonnées par le provider AoC; aucun routage de DLC n'est supprimé. Un fichier caché `.nsp` ou `.xci` ne peut pas être sélectionné depuis un ancien cache. Les tests hôte `tools/check-exefs-directory-host.py` couvrent la découverte et une sélection persistée, sans changement du chemin NS1 normal, du lecteur NUP P5 ou de la console.
```

`docs/EDEN_GPU_EMPTY_DESCRIPTOR_PAYLOAD_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# GPU descriptor payload: empty layouts (22 October 2026)

## Scope
The active Vulkan graphics pipeline keeps an immutable `num_descriptor_entries`
count per shader pipeline. For zero-entry layouts, the descriptor queue uses
`AcquireKnownEmpty`, but the later draw configuration still evaluated a
zero-byte `memcmp` and constructed empty iterator ranges from
`entries + num_descriptor_entries`. The cached vector can be empty, making
its `data()` pointer null. Neither operation is necessary in that case.

## Change
- Only run byte-wise equality/inequality comparisons for nonempty layouts.
- Clear the cached vector instead of forming the pointer range for empty layouts.
- Retain the first-use ring allocation, frame ownership, stage descriptor
  refresh, draw submission and all nonempty descriptor comparisons.
- Keep the pinned Vulkan reconstruction generator and active graphics TU in parity.

## Verification boundary
- `tools/check-ps5-known-empty-graphics-descriptors-host.py` exercises
  source-extracted comparison and snapshot code in C++ at -O0/-O2 with UBSan.
- It tests empty cached payloads and null pointers, first-use ring generation,
  pipeline rebind, one-entry unchanged and changed descriptor data.
- The fast host gate also checks the exact regenerated active Vulkan sources.
- No console graphics performance, HUD pixels or frame pacing is inferred from
  these host checks. No JIT profile flag is toggled.

## Recheck
Native compile and complete preflight must pass for this exact code, followed by
target hardware qualification only when there is a performance/correctness
reason to run a new title test.

## Compute path follow-up

The compute pipeline had the same legacy 1024-entry guest descriptor fallback
in `Acquire(0)`, and `RasterizerVulkan::DispatchCompute` ran the queue
preflight before reading its active immutable shader descriptor count.
For a descriptor-free compute shader this could block the GPU worker for
payload space it would never consume, including while preparing a dispatch.

- Native `ComputePipeline::HasDescriptorEntries()` reports the immutable
  `num_descriptor_entries` count.
- The compute owner selects the pipeline before deciding whether a guest-queue
  preflight is necessary; on a real wait it flushes guest invalidations and
  selects the current pipeline again.
- `ComputePipeline::Configure` selects `AcquireKnownEmpty` only for exact
  zero-entry layouts. Nonempty shader payloads continue the ordinary path.
- Descriptor-buffer ring allocation, compute bindings and barriers are
  unchanged, even for zero-entry shaders.
- `tools/check-ps5-compute-empty-descriptors-host.py` checks source-selected
  behavior under native defines, both C++ optimization levels and UBSan.
- The Vulkan source generator reproduces the new compute header, pipeline
  and rasterizer changes; the core fast gate passed.

This qualifies a host-side contention elimination, not PS5 frame pacing.
The archival register still lists zero unreviewed emulator source files.

### Conditional compute TIC/TSC synchronization

A compute shader without any texture, storage image, sampled image or
texture-buffer descriptors consumes no compute TIC/TSC table entries. The
selected Vulkan compute pipeline now avoids `SynchronizeDescriptors(true)`
for those exact layouts. Nonempty layouts retain the full synchronization,
including binding serial publication. The source-selected UBSan host fixture
exercises all four descriptor families individually and a descriptor-free case.

This is a cache-lock work reduction, not an assertion about FC27 performance.
```

`docs/EDEN_GPU_GRAPHICS_RESOURCE_SLOT_BOUNDS_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Native graphics resource-slot bounds — 22 October 2026

## Observed defect

The selected `BufferCache::BindGraphicsStorageBuffer` and
`BindGraphicsTextureBuffer` performed a u32 mask shift and indexed per-stage
fixed arrays without rejecting out-of-range shader descriptor indices.
The channel reserves exactly 16 graphics storage buffers and 32 graphics
texture buffers per stage, across five stages. Both compute equivalents
already rejected oversized buffer-slot indices.

An SSBO index >=16 overwrote memory past the stage array; a TBO index
>=32 caused an undefined-width bit shift and a possible out-of-bounds
write. Either error could corrupt adjacent GPU binding state. This is a
concrete safety defect; it is not yet traced to a specific FC27 image.

## Maintained fix and regression

Check stage and descriptor-slot bounds before reading or modifying ANY
enabled/written/image masks or per-stage binding arrays. Valid indices and
the existing driver storage-binding limit behave unchanged.

`tools/check-native-graphics-buffer-slot-bounds-host.py` compiles
the real selected C++ methods at -O0/-O2 with ASan/UBSan and tests
the valid endpoints, both first and far out-of-range indices, invalid
stages and dynamic host-limit accounting.

Both independent R437 reconstruction oracles include precisely these
two native changes. The source remains solely under
`vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`.
No speculative JIT/cache-lock policy is enabled. There is no claim of
improved frame pacing or repaired FC27 jersey/HUD graphics until console
measurement.

## Constant-buffer index bounds

The same SSBO binding paths formerly trusted the embedded constant-buffer index. The
Maxwell graphics stage owns 18 CBUFs; the Kepler compute launch owns 8. Both
indices are now checked before touching any enabled/written mask, array or
compute mask shift, including a stage-slot combination that is otherwise valid.
The existing source-extracted ASan/UBSan fixture also covers the last valid and
first invalid CBUF index on both graphics and compute. No texture descriptor
ordering, fence or CPU-write semantics change.

## Disabled compute CBUF must invalidate its old binding

When a shader reuses a storage slot but disables its source constant buffer,
the existing compute bind path returned early **after** setting the slot
mask, leaving the previous dispatch's storage binding intact. This could
replay stale resource content and incorrectly mark that memory GPU-written.
The disabled path now sets `NULL_BINDING` and clears only that slot's
write flag while preserving the logical enabled position (shader descriptor
binding-index ordering must remain stable). The source-extracted fixture
exercises a valid SSBO followed by disabled-CBUF rebind at the **same** slot.
```

`docs/EDEN_GPU_INDEX_DRAW_DIRTY_SPAN_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Indexed draw command range and cache dirty flag — 22 October 2026

## Cause

The pinned `engines/draw_manager.cpp` receives dynamic index `first` /
`count` from macro and indirect draw calls, independently of the
underlying Maxwell register writes. `BufferCache::UpdateIndexBuffer` skips
rebinding when `Dirty::IndexBuffer` is false. Thus, consecutive macro
draws with different index ranges but the same register values could
reuse the preceding draw's buffer binding extent.

The old draw-manager already forced dirty for index-small and inline
index draws; `DrawIndex`, `DrawIndexedIndirect`, and indexed
`DrawEnd` returning from a macro draw omitted that transition.

## Maintained fix

- Native CMake selects the complete maintained TU at
  `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/engines/draw_manager.cpp`,
  removing the pinned `engines/draw_manager.cpp` from the video_core target.
- Those three methods now arm `Dirty::IndexBuffer` **only when first/count
  changes**. Existing dirty state is never cleared here.
- Identical ranges retain the existing no-op cache fast path. Index-small,
  inline indices, nonindexed draws, shader selection, cache locks,
  Vulkan commands, and JIT policy remain unmodified.

## Proof / qualification

`tools/check-native-index-draw-dirty-span-host.py` enforces whole-file parity
except for the three selected methods, compiles the real extracted C++
methods at O0/O2 with UBSan, and checks changed/same indexed spans,
indexed indirect draws, return to general register state, previously set
dirty flags and inline-index forced refresh.

Fast gate and full source preflight invoke this regression. A green native
PS5 build at the new commit is also required. No assertion is made
that this particular missed index update occurred in FC27, or that it
eliminates GPU contention, stutters, missing HUD or jersey textures.
```

```md
# GPU indirect draw byte-range guard — 22 October 2026

## Confirmed source issue

The maintained BufferCache::UpdateDrawIndirect in
`vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`
passed a `size_t` indirect-command length through `static_cast<u32>(size)`
twice without checking that the span was nonempty and representable.
A 4 GiB input could become a zero-byte `FindBuffer` request; an input
slightly larger could silently bind an incorrectly short command buffer.

Reject zero-length and greater-than-u32 ranges before address translation,
resetting the binding to `NULL_BINDING`. Keep valid 1..UINT32_MAX spans,
the count-buffer path, the existing address translation failure handling,
buffer caching, and the draw submission order unchanged. The pinned
upstream backport is not altered. The maintained-source replay oracles
in `tools/check-ps5-buffer-pages-r437.py` and
`tools/check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py` include this exact delta.

## Verification

`tools/check-native-indirect-draw-range-host.py` extracts the selected
C++ method and compiles it at -O0 and -O2 with UBSan. Cases include a
normal count/indirect pair, zero size, 4 GiB overflow, UINT32_MAX,
unmapped memory and SIZE_MAX. The host test is included in fast gate
and full preflight. CI and a PS5-native build must qualify this commit
separately; no gameplay, FPS or HUD correction is claimed.
```

```md
# Indirect Vulkan draw null binding guard — 22 October 2026

## Observed source path

The selected native `BufferCache::UpdateDrawIndirect` returns `NULL_BINDING`
when a guest indirect command byte span is empty, too large for u32,
or unmapped. The selected `BindHostDrawIndirectBuffers` previously
still touched/synchronized that sentinel and `RasterizerVulkan::DrawIndirect`
dereferenced the resulting sentinel buffer handle before recording
a `vkCmdDraw*Indirect` command. This could turn a rejected guest
command span into an invalid native draw.

## Correction and limits

- Skip null/zero byte bindings in the active cache sync path;
- Return a null pointer (and zero offset) from the active indirect command
  and count-buffer getters when the cache has no valid binding;
- Fail closed on either missing binding before `buffer->Handle()` and
  `scheduler.Record`. Normal valid draw submission is unchanged.
- Preserve guest cache mutex ownership, fence submission order, shader
  selection, texture invalidation, CPU/HLE scheduling and JIT parameters.

The selected source lives in `vendor/encore-active`; the pinned
backports remain untouched. Both independent R437 source reconstruction
oracles include this exact, audited transformation.

`tools/check-native-indirect-null-binding-host.py` compiles the extracted
native C++ cache getter/bind bodies at -O0 and -O2 under UBSan, verifies
zero and live bindings, and asserts that both Vulkan handle dereferences
are guarded. This is not PS5 validation, and does not prove FC27 contains
an unmapped indirect draw or that frame pacing/HUD issues are resolved.

## OpenGL consumer closure

The same selected buffer-cache getters are also consumed by both native
OpenGL rasterizer profiles. Both maintained `gl_rasterizer.cpp` and
`gl_rasterizer_dev.cpp` now reject a missing command/count binding before
`glBindBuffer` dereferences. The full-source OpenGL parity oracle and
indirect-null host guard check both paths; no release profile switch is made.
```

```md
# Graphics sampler stage-local reuse — 22 October 2026

## Measured motivation

The FC27 October 21 detailed trace logged ~1,116,606 graphics Configure calls.
The aggregated `stage_texture_handles` phase consumed ~0.94 s; that
measurement includes much more than sampler lookups, so it is not an
estimate of the benefit of this patch. Similarly, the `fill_views` phase
consumed ~0.97 s over the whole session.

## Maintained source change

Under both paired GPU cache mutexes, the selected native Vulkan graphics
pipeline read the exact same sampler handle repeatedly for consecutive
texture descriptors in the same Configure stage. Each lookup reads the
TSC table and consults sampler IDs. Reuse only the previously resolved
sampler ID when the next handle is identical. The cache is automatic
local state inside `config_stage`, recreated on every stage of every draw,
not persisted across stage/pipeline boundaries or guest invalidations.
Image view resolution, actual descriptor payload ordering, sampler
selection for different handles, and all synchronization remain intact.

An empty image-view vector skips `FillImageViews` (an empty loop).
Render-target refresh and feedback barriers still execute, and textured
draws keep full descriptor synchronization.

`tools/check-ps5-consecutive-sampler-reuse-host.py` extracts the
selected native sampler stage into C++ test fixtures and compiles/runs
O0/O2 UBSan. The oracle rebuilds the two precise native transformations
from the pinned generated source. The test checks empty, repeated,
alternating, multiple-descriptor and repeated-draw cases, plus the
separate render-target/feedback phases.

No synthetic timing is claimed as FC27 improvement. Runtime frame pacing,
HUD fidelity and memory pressure need independent PS5 proof.
```

```md
# Safe graphics uniform binding when a GPU virtual address is unmapped

## Verified failure mode

`BufferCache::BindGraphicsUniformBuffer` originally dereferenced the
`std::optional<DAddr>` returned by `gpu_memory->GpuToCpuAddress(gpu_addr)`
without checking whether the mapping existed. The result can be empty for
an unmapped GPU address, so dereferencing it is undefined behavior.
Other buffer-cache translation consumers, including compute uniform,
vertex, index, indirect and transform-feedback paths, already guard
unmapped addresses.

## Selected native fix

- For a missing GPU-to-CPU translation, retire the graphics stage's previous
  uniform binding with the existing `NULL_BINDING` sentinel and return.
- For valid translations, preserve the original binding address, size,
  buffer-id reset and downstream uniform binding sequence.
- Do not change the shader descriptor cache, buffer/texture invalidation,
  GPU work submission, or the immutable shipping backport.
- Both R437 native-source reconstruction oracles reproduce this extension.

## Source-selected regression

`tools/check-native-unmapped-uniform-buffer-host.py` compiles the actual
maintained `BindGraphicsUniformBuffer` and `DisableGraphicsUniformBuffer`
method bodies with ASan/UBSan under `-O0` and `-O2`. It verifies valid
mapping, a formerly mapped slot becoming unmapped, and subsequent remapping,
including complete retirement of stale address/size/buffer-id.

The same fast gate also verifies the zero-tick fence optimization:
`tools/check-native-zero-write-tick-fence-host.py` runs the actual
`SynchronizeBufferWrites` method under UBSan, confirming an unwritten
tick avoids the scheduler's semaphore query while all nonzero-fence
synchronization remains unchanged. Both host tests passed in the fast gate.

## Qualification boundary

A native source dereference bug is fixed; there is no recorded evidence
yet that FC27 caused this optional to be empty during its HUD/jersey
rendering. The earlier PS5 game still had observable stutter despite
stable presentation FPS. No new FC27 frame-time or graphics correctness
measurements are available. Full preflight, CodeQL C++ and the exact native
PS5 build are separately checked before asking for any console retest.
```

`docs/EDEN_GPU_WIDE_VERTEX_INDEX_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Native GPU geometry buffer bounds — 22 October 2026

## Corrected source paths

The selected, maintained guest BufferCache contained two independent
32-bit truncations while calculating GPU-virtual geometry buffer lengths:

- `UpdateVertexBuffer` cast `limit.Address()+1 - array.Address()` to
  `u32` before evaluating the extent. A valid 4 GiB range could become
  zero, suppressing the vertex binding entirely; a slightly longer
  range could become an incorrectly tiny vertex buffer.
- `UpdateIndexBuffer` independently cast the GPU range to `u32`, and
  calculated `(count + first) * FormatSizeInBytes()` in 32-bit
  arithmetic. Either overflow could cause an indexed draw to miss
  required geometry data.

Both methods now check the exclusive GPU range endpoints in `u64`,
calculate all relevant byte counts in `u64`, and clamp the result to
the `u32` interface consumed by `FindBuffer`. The vertex path still
uses the existing `MaxContinuousRange` clip for large or invalid-end
ranges and additionally retires a vertex binding if that clip returns
zero bytes.

No code changes were made to the pinned shipping backport, source shader
compiler, texture cache, guest scheduler or draw descriptor queue.
Two independent native-source replay checks reconstruct the extra
geometry bounds guards after the earlier buffer-cache transformations.

## Targeted host regression

`tools/check-native-wide-vertex-buffer-range-host.py` compiles the
real `UpdateVertexBuffer` method with UBSan at `-O0` and `-O2`.
The fixture tests an ordinary binding, exact and larger-than-4-GiB
address ranges, inverted addresses, an empty contiguous mapping,
an unmapped CPU translation, and a clean dirty flag.

`tools/check-native-wide-index-buffer-range-host.py` compiles the
real `UpdateIndexBuffer` method with UBSan at `-O0` and `-O2`.
Its draws independently set their dirty flags and exercise normal
indices, exactly-4-GiB GPU addresses, overflowed count-plus-first,
inverted and unmapped ranges, and the inline-index route.

The complete fast gate succeeded for both methods in both host
optimization modes. Full native PS5 build, exhaustive source preflight,
and security analysis are separately qualified.

## What is and is not established

These changes correct objective geometry range truncations and can
prevent a drawable vertex or index binding being accidentally dropped.
The historical game reports include missing textures and geometry
artifacts, but no telemetry establishes that one of these overflow
conditions occurred in those frames. No reduction in guest-frame
stutter or improvement in HUD/image correctness is claimed without
hardware evidence. Keep the PS5 console test deferred until the
remaining HLE/JIT/cache invalidation issues are independently qualified.
```

`docs/EDEN_GPU_ZERO_TICK_BUFFER_FENCE_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Guest buffer zero-write-tick fence elision

## Verified source invariant

The guest Vulkan BufferCache looks up resident GPU buffers in
`FindBuffer`. Under accurate-fence mode, a cache hit may call
`SynchronizeBufferWrites`. The base Buffer's `write_tick` initializes to
zero. The only GPU-write path sets that field to
`BufferCacheRuntime::CurrentTick()`. On the Vulkan scheduler,
`Wait(0)` does not perform a wait.

Before this patch, every such lookup with an untouched buffer probed
`runtime.IsFree(0)`, reading the scheduler's fence state even though no
write fence was associated with that buffer.

## Native-only change

`vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h`
now checks `buffer_tick != 0` before calling `runtime.IsFree`.
All nonzero, completed and pending write fences follow the original paths.
No GPU buffer mutation, guest write ordering, cache lock, shader invalidation,
texture invalidation, or descriptor scheduling was removed.

The shipping backport remains hash-pinned and unchanged. Two independent
source-reconstruction witnesses reproduce the native-only transformation:
`tools/check-ps5-buffer-pages-r437.py` and
`tools/check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py`.

`tools/check-native-zero-write-tick-fence-host.py` extracts the exact
maintained C++ method body and compiles it with UBSan at `-O0` and
`-O2`, verifying that:
- A zero tick causes neither a semaphore probe nor a wait.
- A nonzero completed tick still probes `IsFree`.
- A nonzero unfinished tick still calls `Wait`.
- A later zero tick remains independent of a previous wait.

The fast host gate succeeded. Source preflight, CodeQL, native PS5 build,
and gameplay performance are independent qualification stages.

## Performance / FC27 boundaries

This is a bounded reduction of unnecessary semaphore-state loads on
previously unmodified GPU buffers when the accurate-fence mode is in use.
Without a hardware counter for `getWriteTick() == 0` on actual FC27
draws, no throughput improvement is claimed. Previously captured FC27
stutters with stable 30 FPS, HUD inconsistencies and jersey texture defects
remain unresolved until an independently qualified render/guest-pacing fix
and eventual on-console verification.

```

```md
# Eden Encore — dix propriétaires du runtime natif examinés

**21 octobre 2026 · branche `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`**

Objectif : éliminer rapidement les reprises de code inutiles sur des
sous-systèmes déjà instrumentés ou optimisés. Le statut **examiné**
signifie lecture de la source actuelle et décision explicite ;
il ne signifie ni gain de FPS ni validation PS5.

| Fichier source | Fonction / zone | Constat et décision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `headless/heap_pages.cpp` | Mémoire directe et heap (`U02`) | Heap C bridge already delegates allocation, reservation and rollback to its single owned backend; initial direct-memory provenance is startup-only, no redundant per-allocation lookup found. |
| `headless/pad.cpp` | Manette et vibration (`U03`) | Controller input and rumble path has release/acquire pending hint before mutex; no hotpath locking on silent polls, preserve paired publication. |
| `headless/audio.cpp` | Audio 48 kHz (`U04`) | Audio worker is stop-aware, output is paced by 256-frame device calls, mutex protects PCM publish; do not disrupt device cadence. |
| `headless/network_audit.c` | Audit réseau local (`U05`) | Network audit disabled path returns after atomic acquire; duplicate DNS denies suppressed before file lock and writes batched, so quiet-mode bottleneck not evident. |
| `headless/network_audit_sockets.c` | Sockets instrumentées (`U06`) | POSIX socket wrappers preserve errno and call target formatting, getpeername and file audit only when diagnostics active; no unconditional socket peer query. |
| `headless/network_domain_rules.c` | Filtre de domaines (`U07`) | Guest domain policy is immutable after release-ready publication and no heap/socket work in lookup; linear scan is bounded but needs DNS workload measurements to justify indexing. |
| `headless/ps5_net_compat.c` | Compatibilité DNS PS5 (`U08`) | Native resolver and fcntl compatibility wrappers preserve special console ABI; resolver setup could be profiled but blind caching could change lifecycle and errno. |
| `headless/vulkan_surface.cpp` | Surface Vulkan PS5 (`U09`) | Vulkan surface enumerates display modes once at initialization and chooses 60/120 mode; loop and vector allocations are not a per-frame rendering bottleneck. |
| `headless/vulkan_allocator.cpp` | Traduction VMA (`U10`) | Single VMA_IMPLEMENTATION ownership TU contains no hotpath logic to optimize; verify no double implementation rather than replacing allocator source. |
| `headless/crash_report.cpp` | Rapport de crash (`U11`) | Crash reporter keeps signal path separate from helper threads, uses fixed buffer and atomics; startup/report failure handling isn't a per-frame cost, do not simplify signal safety without fault trace. |

**Décision du lot : 10 fichiers réellement lus, 0 nouveau patch C++.**
Les attentes GPU/HLE liées aux freezes FC27 ne sont pas « résolues »
par cette revue. Conserver le comportement de l'audio, des signaux de
crash et des politiques réseau est préférable à une micro-optimisation
non mesurée qui risquerait la stabilité.

Le suivi de l'optimisation de code passe de **279/491** à **289/491**
chemins examinés ou déjà corrigés, soit **202 fichiers restant à
traiter** dans cette passe. Ce chiffre est une file de tri, pas 202
correctifs prouvés nécessaires. Les preuves des contrats de test et la
compilation native sont suivies indépendamment.
```

```md
## Interfaces critiques du moteur qualifiées au niveau des chemins

Douze interfaces de `headless/` ont un propriétaire précis dans le graphe
(`U22–U33`) et un consommateur vérifié par
`tools/check-headless-critical-interface-owners.py`. Ce sont des
composants **de l'application**, non des overrides de sources vendor.
Les déplacements vers `encore-active` seraient ici une erreur de
séparation des responsabilités. Le test contrôle les inclusions directes
(JIT A32/A64, runtime, watchdog, comptabilité mémoire et diagnostics GPU)
et les gardes DEV/probe ; il ne prouve pas leur exécution console.

La majorité des chemins restants sans entrée fonctionnelle comprend des
modules de launcher, des harnais de test et des interfaces applicatives.
Ils demeurent inventoriés, mais ne sont pas déclarés comme correctifs
moteur ni comme preuves de performance.

## Priorités de qualification

La priorité technique se porte sur les unités `runtime/bridge`,
`JIT/expérimental`, les en-têtes réellement sélectionnés et les
fonctions CPU/GPU/mémoire ; les fichiers du launcher restent dans
le chantier UI indépendant. Les programmes de test ne doivent pas être
confondus avec des overrides de production. Une source réellement sélectionnée
avec un comportement corrigé doit acquérir une entrée fonctionnelle
dans `EDEN_CORE_AUDIT_DEPENDENCIES.md`, puis une preuve indépendante.
```

```md
# HID polling — stable production cadence

Source: `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/hid_core/resource_manager.cpp` (H31).

The prior 1 ms NPad scheduler period was labeled by the source as an overclock relative to 4 ms. The selected single native shipping cadence is 4 ms (250 Hz), preserving the other HID event periods, guest samples and registered controller API.
```

`docs/EDEN_HLE_CV_HANDOFF_2026-10-20.md`:

```md
# CV waiter-flag failure must precede mutex-owner handoff

## Hypothesis

The checked key-write failure added in `b8793d2` prevents a lost wait but runs
after `RemoveUserWaiterByKey` and `next_owner_thread->EndWait`. A failed flag
write then returns before the mutex value is updated. The next owner is already
detached and runnable while guest memory still names the old owner.

Extend the existing full-`Wait` lost-mapping fixture to require no ownership
handoff, no next-owner wake and no mutex write when the flag cannot be published.
The current maintained source must fail this check before moving the checked
flag publication ahead of the handoff, under the same scheduler lock. Keep the
release fence between successful flag publication and the remaining operations.

Normal waits must still hand off the mutex, publish the flag, enter the tree and
begin waiting. Invalid initial keys and failed flag publication must cancel
sleep without those ownership side effects. This is a host state-transition
proof, not guest instruction progress or an FC27 freeze diagnosis.

## Local result

The stronger full-Wait witness failed on the prior maintained source because
the next owner had already been detached/woken. Moving checked publication
before that transfer passes both the failed-write case (no handoff/wake/tree
insertion/sleep) and the normal case (handoff, wake, flag, mutex value and wait).
Initial invalid keys still fail before all these operations. The independent
helper parity oracle, full-Wait parity oracle, isolated key-write sanitizer
fixture, four-mode CMake selection and HLE overlay checks pass locally.
Remote CI and native console execution are not established by these results.

```

`docs/EDEN_HLE_IPC_DEADLINE_2026-10-19.md`:

```md
# HLE IPC — correction de délai d'attente ReplyAndReceive

Révision du 19 octobre 2026 · Branche `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.

## Défaut constaté dans les sources

Le `ReplyAndReceiveImpl` épinglé construisait l'échéance absolue en
additionnant le tick courant, un délai positif et deux ticks dans un
entier signé de 64 bits, puis vérifiait `timeout <= 0`.
Cette vérification se produit **après** l'éventuel débordement signé,
qui constitue un comportement indéfini en C++. Les chemins
`WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic`, `WaitForAddress`,
`WaitSynchronization` et `SleepThread` possédaient déjà un calcul
d'échéance saturant ; le chemin IPC manquait encore ce garde.

## Correction maintenue

- En mode normal, CMake sélectionne la traduction complète
  `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/core/hle/kernel/svc/svc_ipc_standard.cpp`,
  identique à l'unité épinglée sauf la conversion vérifiée.
- En mode de diagnostic, `svc_ipc.cpp` conserve l'attribution des
  requêtes IPC aux threads et ajoute le **même** contrôle de débordement.
- Les deux additions sont effectuées avec `__builtin_add_overflow`
  et les délais impossibles saturent à `INT64_MAX`, en conservant le
  traitement des délais nuls/négatifs et les boucles d'attente HLE.
- La source dans `vendor/sources/eden` est inchangée ; les deux
  traductions complètes appartiennent exclusivement à
  `vendor/encore-active`. Aucune édition de corps de fonction en CMake.

## Témoins et limites

`tools/verify/hle/check-native-hle-ipc-timeout-host.py` compile les
calculs extraits des vrais fichiers C++ sous UBSan. Deux configurations
de dépassement doivent échouer sur l'original ; les variantes normales
et DEV doivent les gérer sans débordement, tout en respectant les valeurs
usuelles et limites. Le contrôle `check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py`
vérifie en parallèle la parité des traductions complètes.

**Ce correctif élimine un risque démontrable de comportement indéfini
dans le noyau HLE.** Il ne démontre pas que les gels observés à 30 FPS
étaient causés par ces délais extrêmes, ni une amélioration de FPS.
Les tests hôte ne remplacent ni compilation native ni vérification
console, et aucune option de synchronisation expérimentale n'est activée.

```

```md
# Eden Encore — optimisation verrou de slab HLE et revue runtime

**21 octobre 2026.** Les 62 sources du frontend restent isolées du compteur prioritaire. `runtime_shims.cpp` est conservé du côté moteur car ses symboles C sont globaux.
```

```md
# Eden Encore — JIT RX→RW alias et revue de quatre sources
```

`docs/EDEN_JIT_BLOCK_RANGE_REBASE_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Dynarmic multi-page block-range invalidation — 22 October 2026

## Observed correctness / throughput issue

A guest A64/A32 block may span multiple 4 KiB guest-code pages. The
maintained `BlockRangeInformation::AddRange` indexed such a block in
each page bucket. The old `InvalidateRanges` only removed an invalidated
entry from buckets directly visited by the write range.

When the write intersected just the first page of a multi-page block, other
buckets retained a stale location descriptor. A later recompile of the same
guest location covering a *shorter* range could then be spuriously evicted by
a write to the old trailing page. The stale page entries could also accumulate.

## Selected native fix

- On encountering a matching entry, collect the original compiled block's
  full page span. Every invalidated location is removed from those buckets.
- Sort and deduplicate only the touched owner page indices; **do not scan**
  every JIT index bucket or erase live unrelated blocks.
- Retire empty buckets and preserve the existing per-page 4 KiB index.
- Keep A64/A32 default per-core compilation, sparse JIT allocation and
  RX/RW alias publication policy unchanged.
- Pin the maintained Dynarmic source blob to the updated code.

## Evidence / qualification

`tools/check-native-jit-block-range-rebase-host.py` compiles the actual
maintained C++ method bodies at `-O0` and `-O2` under UBSan. It covers a
two-page block, invalidation of the first page, another live block on the
same last page, shorter recompilation of the same location, and overlapping
later ranges. The prior implementation fails this source-selected witness;
the corrected version passes both optimization levels.

The fast gate has passed, including full regenerated Vulkan parity.
Separate source preflight, native build and CodeQL checks qualify the exact
HEAD independently.

Archived FC27 phase telemetry shows that in an early detailed window,
the three active guest JIT workers spent approximately 10.20 s in emit
out of 12.43 s cumulative compile time (82%, aggregated across workers).
This directs subsequent performance work toward emitter hot paths; it does
not prove frame-level causality or quantify any gain from this fix.

No console stability or stutter reduction is claimed until hardware evidence.

```

```md
# G06–G07 — frontières de migration des émetteurs mémoire Dynarmic

## But et sources d'autorité

`vendor/sources/eden/src/dynarmic/src/dynarmic/backend/x64/` restent épinglées.

l'assemblage CMake** conservées sous `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/dynarmic/scalar/`.

de leurs insertions CMake. Le futur corps maintenu de G06 doit intégrer leur

## Matrice de profils à préserver

| Dimension | Modes à vérifier |
| --- | --- |
| Architecture | A32, A64 — un même fragment G06 est inclus depuis deux TU |
| Mémoire | Direct fastmem, page-table, checked A32, fallback exception-handler |
| Exclusifs | Lecture/écriture, alignement, 8/16/32/64/128 bits |
| JIT | Standard, `EDEN_SHARED_JIT` expérimental |
| Runtime | Hôte Linux, `PS5_NATIVE` |
| Diagnostics | DEV / normal, sans imposer de mesure permanente dans le chemin shipping |

## Ordre de migration sans duplication

1. Construire les deux **fichiers complets maintenus** `emit_x64_memory.h`
   et `emit_x64_memory.cpp.inc` en conservant les séparations de variantes
   nécessaires dans le C++, pas par substitutions dans CMake. Le fragment
   `.cpp.inc` demeure un include C++ réel partagé, pas un patch CMake.
2. Contrôler chaque bloc source contre les transformations épinglées par
   les points de vérification ci-dessus ; refuser les divergences et ne
   supprimer aucun garde A32/A64 non prouvé.
3. Remplacer G06/G07 par des `configure_file(... COPYONLY)` aux mêmes
   chemins dérivés ; retirer **ensemble** les producteurs C++ de
   `scalar-memory.cmake`, `checked-fastmem.cmake` et les macros mémoire
```

`docs/EDEN_JIT_NATIVE_EMPTY_INVALIDATION_2026-10-22.md`:

```md
# Native JIT empty invalidation — 22 October 2026

## Problem

The native Dynarmic `EmitX64::InvalidateBasicBlocks` previously entered
`BlockOfCode::EnableWriting` and `DisableWriting` even when the selected
guest-code invalidation matched no compiled block. On PS5 native code areas,
changing an existing RX page to RW and back can entail costly protection
transitions. Empty invalidations require no instruction patches.

## Change

The native-only emitter now exits before changing code-write permissions
when `locations.empty()`. A nonempty set always follows the existing
`Unpatch` / descriptor-removal / RX-publication sequence. No JIT policy
switch, guest instruction translation, code sharing, compiler scheduling,
A32/A64 configuration or shader invalidation was changed.

The shipping source was kept as a minimal, exact derivation of the pinned
common emitter source. The host emitter is intentionally unchanged.

## Regression witness

`tools/check-native-jit-empty-block-invalidation-host.py` extracts the actual
maintained native C++ method body, compiles it at `-O0` and `-O2` with
UBSan, and verifies both the empty and populated invalidation paths.
`tools/check-maintained-common-emit-x64.py` reconstructs both native/host
variants, including source selection in the two CMake profiles.

The fast gate succeeded, including the C++ regression and reconstruction.
Full preflight, CodeQL and PS5 native build are separate qualifications.

## FC27 evidence and limitation

In archived detailed telemetry from 21 October 2026, some early five-second
windows show ~4.2 s of cumulative JIT compiling on three emulated guest
cores. Later five-second windows show almost no JIT activity yet many
thousands of contended cache accesses (e.g. 16,029 buffer lock contentions
and ~148 ms aggregate buffer lock waiting in one window). Therefore one
native-JIT fix cannot account for all gameplay stutter.

This prevents a demonstrable pointless JIT permission change. The frequency
of no-op invalidations and improvement on target hardware are not established
by host tests. Avoid console retests until a meaningful release candidate
covers the remaining cache/HUD and pacing hypotheses.

```

`docs/EDEN_MAXWELL_DMA_CONTIGUOUS_BATCH_2026-10-21.md`:

```md
# DMA pitch-copy coalescing (Maxwell U81)

The active `MaxwellDMA::Launch` performed a `MemoryManager::CopyBlock` and destination flush per row, even when the source and destination buffers represented two distinct, contiguous linear spans.

An entirely statically qualified fast path now uses one `CopyBlock` when source and destination pitches exactly equal row width, rows and width are nonzero, `width*rows` fits the u32 buffer address span, both u64 end addresses are representable, and the two spans **do not overlap**. Any other transfer falls back to the exact original per-line loop. The DMA semaphore release and `FlushCaching` remain unchanged.

The strict pinned-source oracle `tools/check-native-dma-extent-host.py` admits only this transformation atop already qualified pitch/extent guards. New source-extracted C++20/ASan/UBSan `tools/check-native-dma-contiguous-host.py` exercises valid contiguous and adjacent regions, overlapping and self-copies, signed pitch mismatches, empty transfers, u32 extent overflow, and GPU address overflow.

**Source coverage 417/491; 12 engine files outstanding; launcher 62 excluded.** A reduced per-line dispatch cost is expected only on qualified contiguous DMA workloads. No PS5 FPS or freeze claim.
```
