`docs/PERFORMANCE_ROADMAP.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore — CPU/HLE stability and 30 → 60 FPS research

Status: **engineering investigation only**, 8 October 2026. No shipped feature or
measured PS5 performance improvement is claimed by this document.

## The two separate results

1. **True emulation FPS**: the guest CPU, game logic, physics and render production
   advance faster. Taking a 30 FPS engine from 33.33 ms per real frame to 60 FPS
   requires a 16.67 ms total frame budget *and* correct game timing, if a legitimate
   game-specific 60 FPS modification is available. Changing the TV from 60 Hz to
   120 Hz does not achieve this.
2. **Perceived/display FPS**: the game continues to advance at 30 genuine frames/s,
   while a separate renderer interpolates an intermediate image for every pair,
   potentially presenting 60 frames/s. This does **not** update controller
   responsiveness, guest physics or animation logic twice as often.

The first is a performance/compatibility improvement; the second is image
synthesis. Neither repairs a stalled guest. Do not report synthetic output as
native game FPS.

## Priority A: locate FC27's real freeze

Evidence already observed in a previous hardware trace: the guest PC
`0x124AA117A8` remained unchanged for an extended interval despite host
present telemetry continuing. That suggests (but does not prove) a CPU/JIT,
synchronization, or HLE waiting problem rather than simple GPU overload.

- Establish a **baseline** on the current unchanged PS5 firmware 13.60 build,
  with reproducible boot/game save point and the original conservative CPU/JIT
  settings. Preserve the exact ELF/symbols for every hardware session.
- Repeat once with developer profiling to collect `EDEN_PERF_CPU_POINT`,
  `EDEN_PERF_PROGRESS`, `EDEN_DEV_HLE`, `EDEN_DEV_QUEUE`, and
  `EDEN_GAME_FRAME`/`EDEN_DEV_FRAME`. These are *different* signals; counting
  host presents cannot establish guest progress.
- Analyse text with:
  `python3 -B tools/analyze-fc27-trace.py <session-log.txt> --json`.
  Repeated guest PCs are **hypotheses**, not a diagnosis: real polling loops
  can legitimately hold their PC while other guest state progresses.
- Conduct one-variable-at-a-time A/B experiments for (a) backward/self JIT
  loop pre-emption, (b) dummy-thread wait ownership/lifetime, (c) service
  initialization blocking, and (d) I-cache coherency. Retain a fix only after
  guest-state liveness, replayed behavior, and extended idle/shutdown coverage.
- Compare host CPU consumption and per-frame GPU work before reducing rendering
  resolution. A stuck guest cannot be fixed by FSR or extra rendered frames.

Current experimental source flags are **OFF by default**:
`EDEN_EXPERIMENTAL_DUMMY_THREAD_WAITS`,
`EDEN_EXPERIMENTAL_ICACHE_COHERENCE`, and
`EDEN_EXPERIMENTAL_SM_HOST_WAIT`. They must **never be bundled together
into the baseline** without individual tests. Stable default per-core Dynarmic
JIT remains the comparison point.

## Priority B: real FPS improvements

Once repeatable baseline performance exists:

- Profile CPU/JIT compilation, HLE service latency, GPU queues, Vulkan buffer
  synchronization and game-specific graphics load. Remove actual bottlenecks
  first; tune presets only on measured hardware evidence.
- Investigate **per-game**, legally distributable community 60 FPS mods where
  the game can keep correct audio, physics, timing and input. A generic forced
  60 Hz guest clock is not safe for games built around 30 FPS.
- Test the unchanged 30 FPS original alongside each candidate. Record native
  1% low, worst-frame time, timing glitches, memory/VRAM, temperatures where
  observable, and crashes; avoid claims without matched A/B sessions.
- Keep native frame unlocks title-specific with a per-game fallback. No
  unverified 60 FPS patch is activated globally.

## Priority C: experimental optical-flow frame interpolation

**Candidate:** AMD FidelityFX FSR 3.1's Vulkan optical-flow/frame interpolation,
or a purpose-built, engine-independent optical-flow approach where guest motion
vectors/depth are unavailable. The public AMD FSR 3 frame-generation APIs are
*not* a drop-in emulator switch: they expect coherent frame inputs, correct
presentation/swapchain ownership, pacing and careful UI handling.

Reference: https://gpuopen.com/fidelityfx-super-resolution-3/
Reference: https://gpuopen.com/manuals/fidelityfx_sdk/techniques/super-resolution-interpolation/

A testable design must:

1. Capture two **completed distinct game frames** from the selected presenter.
   Do not extrapolate frames while the guest is frozen, static, or a pause menu
   is on-screen. Limit history to a bounded number of surfaces.
2. Evaluate 1080p input and stable 30 FPS output first. At 30 real frames/s,
   source-frame spacing is **33.33 ms**. True interpolation of frames A and B
   cannot calculate the midpoint until **B is complete**. Pacing A, synthetic
   midpoint and B every ~16.67 ms therefore normally needs source-frame
   buffering/delayed presentation, adding latency. Unbuffered extrapolation
   instead predicts an unknown future and can increase artifacts. Measure both
   GPU execution time **and end-to-end input latency** before considering 60
   presented FPS a user-visible improvement.
3. Keep synthesized-frame presentation independent of the guest simulation
   clock; present 30 real + 30 synthetic at 60 Hz without changing input,
   audio, save state, emulated vsync or game timing.
4. Treat menus/HUD as a **separate layer where possible**. Motion synthesis
   over FC27 player labels, UI glyphs, stadium advertising, fast balls, cross
   dissolves and replay cuts can produce strong ghosting. Enable detection,
   conservative fallback and a user-controlled OFF switch.
5. Collect real latency, drop, motion-artifact and PS5 GPU-memory measurements
   for both Vulkan and OpenGL. Any transport between OpenGL and Vulkan has
   to demonstrate no extra expensive full-frame copies or cross-API stalls.
6. Keep optical flow and frame generation entirely behind a future explicit
   **experimental per-game option**, OFF by default and disabled in Safe Launch.

### Decision criteria

A pilot is worth continuing only if 1080p 30→60 *presented* FPS actually works
on the PS5 firmware 13.60 target with predictable GPU timing, reasonable
latency and no guest crashes, artifacts or increased FC27 hangs. AMD recommends
a faster base game than 30 FPS for its general frame-generation technology;
**60 smooth synthesized FPS from 30 source FPS is a research goal, not a
promise**. The PS5 AMD RDNA2 platform does not provide NVIDIA's
`VK_NV_optical_flow` hardware extension. Do not assume newer AMD RDNA4
machine-learning frame generation is available on PS5.

### Deliberately not implemented yet

- No fake `FPS boost` toggle or shader that merely duplicates frames.
- No forced emulation clock, broken game physics, or CPU/JIT patches by default.
- No external PC-only frame generator bundled into a native PS5 application.
- No assertion that frame interpolation resolves FC27's stalled guest.

## Reproducible output and credit requirements

Any performance feature must ship with baseline-vs-candidate traces, exact
source commit, console firmware, renderer, video settings, test duration,
real/presented FPS recorded separately, and an OFF/rollback path. If AMD code
or another optical-flow library is **actually integrated later**, its author,
project maintainers and license must be added to `README.md`,
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the installed legal bundle first.

Offline trace analyzer: `tools/analyze-fc27-trace.py`.
Regression: `python3 -B tools/check-fc27-trace.py`.

## 8 October 2026 — Hardware evidence, no-build follow-up

The supplied PS5 FW 13.60 logs include an approximately 70.3-minute Vulkan
session with 29.58 average host-present FPS but 13 five-second windows under 20,
31 under 25 and 148 gaps above 100 ms; the worst single gap is 2641 ms.
Repeated 30 FPS windows do **not** prove smooth per-frame gameplay.

- Late-session `EDEN_JIT_PRESSURE` events repeatedly report roughly 1 MiB
  remaining in per-core code regions (256 MiB / 192 MiB / 192 MiB).
  The pressure recurs near some of the worst present gaps. Do not infer exact
  causality without aligned JIT clear/compile durations, guest progress and
  shader/GPU timing. Saved-block compile-ahead and shared JIT stay OFF.
- `EDEN_WORKER_TOPOLOGY ready=0 distinct_cores=1` persists on the real console,
  so the intended CPU worker pinning and secondary-CPU placement are inactive.
  Do not force logical/SMT placement without verifying the actual CPU affinity
  and topology reported by firmware; it might worsen frame pacing.
- Cache clearing was performed from Diagnostics and some sessions report zero
  preloaded shader pipelines. Repeated cache deletion is not a stutter fix;
  preserving a warm cache is the comparison baseline.
- Before experimenting with cache capacity or CPU placement, add bounded
  compile/clear-cost timing to the exact pinned Dynarmic implementation and
  driver GPU-completion timestamps where supported. The release present summary
  now additionally reports gaps >200/>500 ms and longest >=50ms streak.
- The shipping PlayStation control profile no longer switches to Switch mapping
  when sticks/triggers resemble gameplay. Keep custom mappings deterministic.
  Individual button transitions are printed only in diagnostic builds.

### Experimental technology decision (do not ship unqualified)

1. **JIT tuning**: candidate pressure-aware region sizing or code reuse; requires
   hardware memory headroom and fault-free long A/B sessions. No blanket
   cache increase or experimental shared JIT until those gates pass.
2. **Vulkan presentation timing**: inspect driver support for
   `VK_GOOGLE_display_timing` / `VK_EXT_present_timing` (or PS5-native present
   timestamps), measure real display intervals, then trial pacing with an OFF
   switch. Never invent a supported extension.
3. **FSR 3.1 frame generation**: AMD recommends 60 FPS input and warns against
   below-30 FPS; this observed 15–20 FPS tail is not a safe target.
   FSR SDK 2.3 has no Vulkan backend, and newer ML FSR-FG is not an assumed
   RDNA2 PS5 feature. Generating duplicate frames cannot recover slow guest
   CPU/JIT frames. Keep any optical-flow experiment isolated and OFF by default.
4. **Radeon GPU/texture cache and shader batching**: already in the PS5 driver.
   Bench new changes with graphics output fidelity, GPU time, worst-frame
   tail, and guest liveness, not average presented FPS alone.

Source and baseline observations only. No PS5 app build or GitHub workflow
dispatched; no measured improvement claimed.

## Opt-in source experiments (8 October 2026)

The experimental source path is implemented at
`docs/FC27_EXPERIMENTS.md` with per-title `config/experiments.json`:
expanded fixed-at-creation A64 Dynarmic caches (to evaluate pressure),
logical-CPU placement only after a failed physical topology probe, and a
passive six-bucket Vulkan presentation histogram. Stable and Safe Launch
settings are unchanged. CPU affinity is restored after a game and on errors.
No frame-generation implementation or proven FPS improvement is claimed.
```

`docs/PRETEST_AUDIT_2026-10-14.md`:

```md
# Encore — pre-test source, logs, upstream and package audit

**Audit date:** 14 October 2026. **Working branch:** `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.
The repository and the already compiled console package must be identified by
**different immutable commit SHAs** if another commit lands after packaging.

## Decision

Do **not** call the outstanding gameplay problems resolved. A native All-On build
from `b5f0301a31cef17f70a8c4e19484d2fb638daa17` (Actions
[38587429272](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38587429272))
passed its packaging and debug-symbol artifacts, but changes to the launcher
and session-log capture landed afterward. That archive is **not** a binary of
the latest development branch.

The source preflight [38587774361](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38587774361)
passed at `4e4a3cd2`; later edits require their own successful validation.
Successful packaging is not an FC27 full-match stability, HUD or mapping test.

## Supplied hardware evidence (build 2efd8b3c)

- `heap.prev(8).log`: 422 five-second graphics windows from one longer
  session. Media/selected storage service-completion counters stop progressing
  in the late tail while draw, dispatch, IPC and CPU-write totals continue to
  advance. This is **suspected application/scene progression stall**, not a
  proven deadlock or a GPU hardware halt.
- `heap(20261014-112903).log`: 207 five-second graphics windows across
  two game starts, **not** one continuous match. Its beginning has already
  lost the one-time application source-SHA marker, though the preceding
  rotated log identifies `2efd8b3c`.
- `stderr(20261014-112909).log` records a fatal unmapped guest jump in
  `MuseLogicThread_match`; its other explicit directory-open messages
  report `errno=2` for an **optional** native OpenGL cache path on return
  to the launcher, not a second fatal crash.
- The files examined contain no NUL or invalid UTF-8 replacement characters.
  This **does not** prove every final write survived a forced application
  closure, nor that a rendered scene was correct.
- `result.tsv` contains stage PASS milestones; this **does not** mean the
  game finished a match successfully.

## Diagnostic completeness and overhead

The native developer package provides opt-in **Detailed Logging**, bounded
`heap`/`stderr` first-and-tail segments, guest services/IPC (including
age of ongoing IPC >500 ms when sampled), cache waits, GPU command
progress, JIT activity, memory ownership, CPU affinity evidence, and
driver/present state. Crash-only reports contain host registers and stack
addresses; a guest invalid-branch error now retains PC/LR/SP/FP, thread
identity and the attempted execution target.

What it **cannot** currently prove automatically during a visually frozen
match: scene-content freshness/pixel hashes, a complete consistent snapshot
of every live guest thread's wait owner/backtrace, which controller preset
the game's own UI stored and selected, or shader-cache **hits** merely from
a cache-directory configuration message.

The current log pipe copies files on worker threads and buffers stdout;
forced termination can lose a small unwritten tail. Long runs retain initial
and latest bounded segments, potentially discarding intervening history.
Detailed profiling itself may introduce measurement overhead. Therefore
**maximum evidence and zero measurement overhead are incompatible**.
Never enable synchronous per-draw stack dumps on the hot path just to claim
“all logs”.

### Collect once, before any further app restart

When Detailed Logging has been enabled in the launcher, retain the complete
diagnostic directory **without renaming or omitting first/previous files**:

- `/data/prosperoeden/logs/heap.log`, `heap.first.log`, `heap.prev.log`,
  `heap.prev.first.log` (only those that exist)
- `stderr.log`, `stderr.first.log`, `stderr.prev.log`,
  `stderr.prev.first.log`, `result.tsv`, `boot-trace*.txt`
- `network-accepted.log` if present; `crash-*.txt` if a native fatal
  signal produced one; `/data/prosperoeden/user/log/eden_log.txt` if present

The new one-line `EDEN_SESSION_SOURCE source_sha=<sha>` identifies the
build at **each** game session (alongside the startup `EDEN_BUILD_SOURCE`).
The offline guest-progress analyzer now segments by session start or reset
of cumulative graphics-frame count, rather than comparing independent
games as one run. It still emits a *candidate*, never an asserted root
cause, when work counters continue and selected service calls remain flat.

Do **not** delete shaders or saves again for this comparison; the previous
test already cleared cache. Record the rough elapsed match time, what was
visible when animation froze, whether the overlay still updated, and whether
the launcher could close the guest normally. A deliberate user close will
not necessarily produce `crash-*.txt`.

## External-source coverage and explicit gaps

Original upstream master (14 October) contains #156 lazy guest-memory
allocation and incremental JIT code commitment. Encore retains its
independently adapted sparse-table/JIT and dense fallbacks; those
upstream APIs and ownership changes are **not a qualified, active port**.
This is important pending memory work, but must not be batch-merged before
a baseline because executable alias ownership, fastmem and page-backings
are native-firmware-sensitive.

Other upstream updates on 14 October include the emulator FPS overlay's
own CPU/GPU information, menu key remapping and new translations. They are
not proof of a guest-generated FC27 HUD or in-match preset fix. They are
tracked, not claimed integrated into Encore's active native image.

The independent native-graphics/Wine fork remains distinct architecture.
The console shader disk-cache credential adaptation and unpresented
swapchain ownership transfer are selectively present in Encore's *active*
Mesa/WSI source; complete scaled-WSI parity and Wine stream-gate changes
are not. Frame interpolation can generate display images but cannot repair
an application deadlock, bad texture contents or in-game controls.
See `INTEGRATION_AUDIT_CPU_GPU_JIT_2026-10-14.md` and
`UPSTREAM_GAP_REGISTER_2026-10-14.md` for source-path references.

## Cleanup and documentation

- GitHub's branches API reported a **single remote branch**,
  `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`, when audited. This is **not** a claim that a local
  Mac checkout has no uncommitted changes or that no retained CI artifact
  exists.
- Marketing READMEs (`README.md`, `docs/i18n/README.fr.md`), `SECURITY.md`,
  `MEMORY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and a populated `LICENSES/`
  are present. Their existence is verified; not every historical statement
  or third-party latest commit is proven current by the presence of the file.
- Native build and source preflight both need to succeed on the **specific
  final source SHA** chosen for the next device trial. Preserve its matching
  app ZIP and debug symbols, so a later guest fault can be symbolized.

**No claim of fully repaired gameplay:** the end-of-match progression stall,
late frames, texture/HUD freshness and guest custom mapping remain open
until a matching hardware run supports a conclusion.

## Rechecked log clocks, DNS and default FPS display (pre-test update)

**New diagnostic build only** (not the already green older native artifact):
`headless/network_audit.c` now includes `epoch` seconds, explicit UTC
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmmZ`, and `mono_ns` on **each recorded** network
API event, including a DNS denied-summary flush. Denied summaries include the
usual `bytes=0 status=0` fields plus `count=N`, so the parser can ingest
them. The timestamp of a grouped denial count is the **summary flush**
time, not invented times for its individual suppressed requests. At a cold
launch, network `session-start` carries the native SHA; for each guest
launch, the stdout `EDEN_SESSION_SOURCE` and `EDEN_TIME_ANCHOR` record
source and clock alignment, and the periodic GPU diagnostic window emits an
additional time anchor even after log-file rotation.

**Historical console capture checked:** `network-accepted(6).log` has 3,624
lines; the backwards-compatible parser recognizes 3,624/3,624, including
1,291 formerly ignored summary rows totaling 17,564 grouped requests. The
original legacy records themselves are only accurate to **whole seconds**.
The updated analyzer reports old/new timestamp coverage and uses explicit
UTC for human-readable start/end; it does not retroactively claim that
old records contain milliseconds.

**Clock limitations:** legacy `stderr`, raw Vulkan driver text and
`result.tsv` do not all include independent wall timestamps on *every*
line. They are scoped by phase/CPU-monotonic observations and the new
periodic anchor. It would be inaccurate to claim that literally every
third-party driver message receives a wall-clock timestamp. Adding
synchronous clock/format operations to every draw, IPC or stderr print
would bias the frame-latency diagnosis. Forced closure can still lose the
last unflushed pipe contents; the initial and latest bounded segments
must be collected as a complete set.

**Default visible FPS:** both normal preference models have `hud=false`,
and settings load defaults from that value when `/video/fps_overlay`
is missing. Existing explicit user settings are preserved. A new source
gate checks the default and the saved preference contract. Internal
frame-time sampling is independent of display visibility.

**What the model tests actually prove:** duplicate DNS audit rows are
bounded without changing denied/allowed network results; old and new
formats parse consistently; source-to-stream clock identity is preserved;
buffer-page witnesses avoid redundant atomic read-modify-writes after
a page bit is known set; multi-session forensic analysis does not merge
guest lifetimes. They **do not** prove lower GPU frame time, live HUD
freshness, successful in-game mapping or resolution of the end-of-match
freeze. Those are still awaiting game-level hardware comparison.
```

`docs/PROSPERO_WIN_PS5_AUDIT.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore ↔ prospero-win: PS5 runtime audit (2026-10-13, R416)

Scope: real native PS5 title on FW 13.60, FC27 (0100C49025D3E000), BOTW. This is a **cross-project technical comparison**, not a blanket Wine/DXVK transplant: Wine runs Windows PE->DXVK->Vulkan, whereas Eden translates Switch guest GPU commands->Eden Vulkan/RADV. Proven fixes in one stack may not be present in the other.

## Grounded sources
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/WINE_PS5_BUILD.md — PS5 native memory, synchronization, scheduler and Vulkan display, FW 12.02 measurements.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/cs-thread-profile.md — per-Present/driver/guest attribution and cache path/writeability checks.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/vulkan-progress-gate.md — release global Vulkan stream gate before driver waits and pipeline creation; their cold GTA IV traces contained 300–500 ms frames.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/vulkan-replay-workers.md — pool-scoped recording, resource lifetimes and ordering; document explicitly says worker runtime is not fully connected or console-qualified.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/docs/vulkan-spsc-append.md — bounded producer-owned SPSC transport, no invalid reorder; host tests ≠ console FPS.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/wine/patches/0881-ntdll-ps5-report-the-cpus-a-game-runs-on.patch — 13 allowed CPUs vs 16 online; measured excess SCHED_FIFO worker starvation.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win/blob/main/wine/patches/0882-server-ps5-round-robin-scheduling-and-priorities.patch — opt-in SCHED_RR at priority 700, *not* unconditional or native app proven.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5_Mesa/commit/a01ce0e1b49a — 2026-10-09 credential gating disk shader-cache correction.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5_Mesa/commit/9d3cd417ff488bd1a7cc68c1f1c8e1df409c2a11 — framebuffer-size-limited VideoOut WSI with correctly scaled off-size Vulkan images.
- https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5_Mesa/commit/f2ee3891be81f5f36fc1e64ada36e36033bae5e4 — unpresented swapchain can release display ownership.
- https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa — Encore's pinned 0b2d6d1a61d9bbf89cf8beb88a696144f67c61f8, with separate pinned/active overlays; newer upstream is not automatically binary compatible.
- PS5CEMU-HAR, PS5SX2, PS5LM and fail0verflow/ps5-umtxdbg for firmware CPU access and possible SMT pairs; those conventions are not firmware 13.60 physical topology proof.

## Findings and decisions

| Area | Exact cross-project finding | Encore state / decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repeated shader compilation on relaunch | Mesa `disk_cache_enabled()` rejects `!__normal_user()` before it ever honors a writable `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`. PS5 title credentials can trigger that silently. | **FIX IN R414**: a pinned, independently audited native Mesa `disk_cache_os.c` uses upstream `#if !defined(__PROSPERO__)`. Non-PS5 setuid safeguard, user cache-disable flags and disk headroom policy preserved. R414 source CI SUCCESS; **R415 native build SUCCESS** #38335095928. No FC27 warm-cache measurement yet. |
| Pipeline compilation stalls | Wine's *PE command-stream global mutex* previously held across `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines`; 300–500 ms cold frames reduced by draining and releasing gate before compile. | **NOT A DIRECT PORT**. Encore compiles pipelines with `PipelineCache`, Vulkan `Scheduler`, shader workers, and `GraphicsPipeline::ConfigureDraw`; no Wine PE gate exists. Current R403 first-use draw preservation schedules a wait on a Vulkan scheduler worker; audit that worker's `execution_mutex` scope and whether pipeline compilation/guest GPU synchronization can block its progress. Never release per-resource Vulkan/texture locks without a proof of lifetime, queue and ordering. |
| OS worker scheduling | FW12.02 Wine probe: 13 game CPU IDs `0..12`, default `SCHED_FIFO` priority ~700: a 14th busy worker of same priority waits indefinitely for CPU release; Wine patch 0882 opts into `SCHED_RR`. | **OPEN**. R410 All-On currently pins guest+GPU to `{2,4,6,8,10}`, *assuming* pairs; reserves possible SMT siblings `{3,5,7,9,11}`, and puts shader/IO on `{0,1,12}`. For 3 available secondary IDs `GetTotalPipelineWorkers()` selects **ONE** shader pipeline worker (2 service headroom); this avoids overcommit, but may underutilize shader compilation. Need actual `pthread_getschedparam` readback on **FW13.60** and explicit controlled RR A/B, not automatic global scheduling policy or an unbounded worker boost. |
| GPU wait/deadlock | Wine flush-only sentinel + release of gate before `WaitSemaphores`, queue idle, present, pipeline compile; scoped command-pool synchronization and owned parameter snapshots protect ordering. | **CONCEPTUAL TRANSFER** to Encore; R404–R407 now record DMA sync/puller semaphore currently active and independent stall watchdog/pad-input witness. Contrast `EDEN_GPU_DMA_SYNC`, `EDEN_GPU_PULLER_SEMAPHORE`, `EDEN_GPU_REPORT_STALLED` with `EDEN_GUEST_CACHE_DOMAIN` and pipeline timers on one run. Old R400c log predates new probes. Avoid removing guest semaphores or deferring Vulkan resource destruction blindly. |
| VideoOut / resolution | Console rejects direct buffers at 1280x720, 1440x960, 1440x1080 (0x80290005); newer Pereira WSI uses native 1080p or 2160p targets with aspect-correct blit for others. Swapchain-owner fix prevents a hidden, never-presented window from blocking actual output. | **MISSING IN ENCORE'S PINNED MESA WSI**; its current WSI still has fixed 3840x2160 VideoOut image buffers. BUT Encore's own PresentManager already uses `vkCmdBlitImage(... VK_FILTER_LINEAR)` from render framebuffer to target; this means small game renders do not necessarily create forbidden-sized WSI swapchains. Do not wholesale merge WSI/videoout: it changes format/layout/registration/direct-memory lifetime and could regress currently correct 4K presentation. First inspect actual swapchain `imageExtent` and dimensions. |
| Texture/HUD corruption and flicker | Wine's pixel probes verify D3D frame readback, while Mesa display blit/lifecycle fixes address final presentation not the guest texture cache or descriptor semantics. | **UNPROVEN** whether WSI contributes to FC27 texture/HUD flicker. Eden #4473/#4477 was already shipped via immutable source backports BEFORE R408 (R411 corrected double application). Prioritize guest texture invalidation, Vulkan buffer ownership, DMA transfers, transient aliasing and descriptor lifetimes. Never mistake smooth VideoOut scanout or 30 FPS presentation for correct frame contents. |
| Quality / scaling | Direct VideoOut uses restricted framebuffer sizes; Pereira's WSI scales off-size with aspect preserved, whereas Encore already applies render-target scaling/FSR and another presentation blit if dimensions differ. | Check effective *guest resolution → scaling pass → present extent → physical output* before changing sharpness. Avoid double bilinear scaling and unqualified FSR3/DLSS integration. Visual correctness requires stable terrain/HUD and actual per-pass extents, not only final 2160p buffer dimensions. |
| Direct vs flexible memory | Wine measured ~440 MiB flexible memory and ~12 GiB direct for FW12.02; its direct-memory allocator obeys 16 KiB host pages. | Encore already uses native direct memory, mspace, JIT safeguards and GPU budgets. Do not copy Wine VM/PE mapping or WoW64 low-4GiB allocator into a Switch emulator. Preserve budget and lifetime assertions. |
| Network / input | Wine's separate XInput/WSI APIs do not share Switch guest controller or HLE protocol semantics. | No automatic application of Wine XInput bindings, sync shortcuts or network overrides to Eden's per-game mappings / DNS policy. |

## Audit of current Encore code
- `headless/main.cpp`: configures `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`, disk-space-based `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_MAX_SIZE`. Those variables did **not** bypass prior `!__normal_user()` rejection.
- `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vk_pipeline_cache_cost.cpp`: `GetTotalPipelineWorkers()` takes live process/thread cpuset mask and preserves two logical slots for other background duties. Three secondary allowed CPUs means one builder in R410, not six.
- `headless/performance.cpp`: `PlaceSecondary()` currently calls `cpuset_setaffinity`, not `pthread_setschedparam`. No blanket RR policy has been shipped.
- `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vulkan_rasterizer.cpp`: `CurrentGraphicsPipeline()` occurs before paired guest buffer/texture cache lock in normal PrepareDraw; `PipelineCache` schedules shader workers. Do not claim Wine's global PE stream-gate bug exists identically here.
- `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vulkan_scheduler.cpp`: command chunks execute under `execution_mutex`, allowing queued work admission with separate `queue_mutex`; waiting inside that executor is relevant to pipeline first-use stutters. Any concurrency change requires queue/order/memory-lifetime testing.
- `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vulkan_present_manager.cpp`: direct `VK_FILTER_LINEAR` blit to swapchain when supported. Rendering at 1440p with 2160p display can therefore already scale without allocating a 1440p VideoOut swapchain.

## Evidence gate before claims or future merges
1. Qualify **R415 first**, not R413: one FC27 gaming session with existing settings, cache preserved between two starts. Inspect cache file creation and size, native `EDEN_PS5_SHADER_WORKERS` CPU mask and actual frame/wait witnesses. Do not require extra stress tests or repeated clearing of the shader cache.
2. If warm cache works but stutters persist on same scenes, categorize `gpu_dispatch_ms`, `dma_active_ms`, `puller_active_ms`, shader compile time, cache lock waits, and queue/present cadence. Correct the dominating path rather than guessing that faster output solves it.
3. Investigate on-console scheduler `pthread_getschedparam` for 5 hot + background workers **before** enabling RR. A policy/mask difference from Pereira's FW12.02 nullifies direct conclusions for FW13.60.
4. Stage only focused backports from current PS5 Mesa, with host WSI memory/release/scaling correctness tests and real PS5 compiler gate; preserve original vendored snapshots and native 4K present.
5. Keep one performance A/B variable per compiled build and do not conflate debug-log overhead with final FPS.

Status 2026-10-13: R414 source CI SUCCESS, R415 native CI SUCCESS, next PS5 hardware run unperformed. No live gameplay performance gain claimed.

## R417 follow-up — firmware scheduling evidence (source-only)

R417 captures `EDEN_PS5_THREAD_SCHED` exactly once per actual Vulkan command worker and shader graphics/compute compilation thread. It records `pthread_getschedparam` policy (FIFO/RR/OTHER), effective priority, permitted CPU affinity and both API error codes. The change is read-only: it does not modify thread priorities, CPU placement, mutex scopes, the renderer, the shader-worker count, Mesa, or VideoOut.

The tracked prepared Vulkan files and `prepare-vulkan-port.py` source generator are updated together and qualified by a host fixture. Host tests establish source/wiring behavior only, not console performance. The real FW13.60 readback remains unknown until a hardware run; R415 is still the latest tested native archive, and R417 must NOT be presented as a FPS or graphics fix. Only contemplate explicit SCHED_RR A/B once the priority/mask measurements and hot-stage timings have been reviewed.
```

```md
# R1 — Offline forensic review, 15 October 2026 (no console test)

Branch: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`. Evidence: user-provided `boot-trace(20261015-161205).txt`, `heap(20261015-161206).log`, `stderr(20261015-161213).log`, `result(1).tsv`, and prior logs. Examined build SHA: `5629395324ff65c98b50c44f35f2142a4a92654a`. This is **not** a new performance-fix claim. User has stopped console testing: do not request another run or publish another experimental build on the strength of these observations.

## Evidence, with limits

1. **Input availability, not a stopped poll worker.** In the current stderr, polls progress from 273750 to 281250 between epoch_ms 1792080623781 and 1792080654695 (about 30.9 s); `samples` rises from 730317 to 737817 while `usable` stays at 729588, `intercepted=0`, `errors=0`, and `last_read=1`. At 282500, `usable` resumes increasing. In `headless/pad.cpp::Poll`, `usable_samples` is incremented only for `ps5::pad::is_usable`; the predicate in `third_party/ps5_pad.hpp` requires `sample.connected != 0` and absence of the interception bit. Therefore the sampled controller records were non-usable, consistent with `sample.connected == 0` during that window. The heartbeat `connected=1` is **not** the sample's connected flag: it is the number/mask of opened controller slots. Do not diagnose this as a stopped thread or attribute it to a game deadlock. An OS focus/connection transition is possible but unproven.

2. **Rendering activity survives that interval.** Correlated `EDEN_TIME_ANCHOR` and `EDEN_VULKAN_FRAME` reports around epoch_ms 1792080623115–1792080658281 each report about 150 frames/5 s (30 FPS), `worst_ms` roughly 33–35 ms, and no `late50` or `gpu_full` events. The HID service command-206 cumulative count continues rising. This rules out a wholly stopped native render callback in that specific interval, but **does not prove image content changed or that the guest UI remained interactive**. GPU idle is about 3.6–3.9 s per 5 s window; this is not proof of a defective shader pipeline or an isolated GPU bottleneck.

3. **Measured launch spikes, not a sustained JIT bottleneck.** Early session reports `fps=21.562`, `worst_ms=894.738`, and `jit_ms=4243.201` in a multithreaded five-second profile. Later 30-FPS windows have near-zero JIT time, while the game can still appear frozen. A successful sparse JIT startup does not resolve the reported long-run symptoms.

4. **Memory retained, not proven leaked.** `core_destroyed` reports `live_bytes=6063474`, while native heap physical backing remains `1744830464` bytes (1664 MiB). `EDEN_HEAP_RETENTION` distinguishes 939524096 pinned and 805306368 unpinned bytes, both with `reclaim=disabled quiescence=unproven`. Do not infer that these pages are safe to unmap; see `docs/PS5_RESOURCE_RECLAIM_AND_GPU_CPU_SCALE_DESIGN.md`. A separate per-root accounting anomaly appears: `EDEN_HEAP_ROOT ... root=9 ... held_bytes=-6288 held_blocks=2`. A negative held byte count is invalid as a physical-memory measurement; audit the observational ledger and `realloc` ownership transitions before relying on root totals. Do **not** clamp this counter or reclaim based on it.

5. **CPU topology remains unverified.** `EDEN_PS5_CPU_TOPOLOGY_REJECT reason=more_than_8_physical_ids observed=13` and `EDEN_EXPERIMENT_CPU result=skipped reason=physical_topology_unverified`. The logical isolation optimization is not proved active; retaining the safety fallback is appropriate until a genuine kernel topology source validates the sibling groups.

6. **Texture/catalog path has a distinct defect.** `EDEN_CASE_RESULT` for `01007EF00011E000` is `front=1 back=1 spine=1` and the current launcher also logs texture creation; this proves resource preparation, **not** the exact final on-screen image. For `0100C49025D3E000`, the catalog lookup is `status=no-match` and `front=0 back=0 spine=0`: this is a confirmed catalog coverage gap, separate from frame stalls. Do not invent artwork associations.

7. **Cleanup did not crash in this run.** `result(1).tsv` marks `shortcut_return_to_menu`, `core_shutdown`, and `core_destroyed` as PASS. GPU unmapped counters are zero in captured summaries, though this does not rule out other texture/HUD synchronization problems.

## Engineering stop gate

- No new console request, default experimental toggles, release, runtime controller reconnect, physical unmap, JIT budget increase, or speculative frame-pacing change.
- Review-only candidates: (a) isolate actual guest image/UI progress from native present counts; (b) verify the semantics of disconnected controller samples and whether focus/system takeover explains them; (c) audit per-root memory ownership/counters without treating them as reclaim authorization; (d) correct only verified missing catalog mappings with a traceable source.
- A future gameplay patch must identify the source-level defect, include deterministic source/host regression coverage, and state which observed symptom it addresses. A green build and diagnostic-only changes are not grounds to request further console testing.

**Status:** forensic report committed to preserve evidence. No runtime patch or PS5 release, and no new console testing requested.
```

# Eden Encore — Build PS5 de test unifié, fonctions activées

**État vérifié le 10 octobre 2026 : compilation PS5 All-On réussie sur GitHub, validation réelle sur console encore en cours.**

## Règle fondamentale

- **AUCUNE option « Expérimental » à activer dans Paramètres.** Pour le profil de test PS5, les fonctions implémentées de correction/réduction mémoire JIT sparse, placement CPU logique et télémétrie frame time sont activées directement à la compilation et au lancement, sous réserve du contrôle physique d'alias mémoire.
- Le rendu RADV/Vulkan, les patches PRMT Index/Fermi2D pris en charge, les protections mémoire, la gestion des couvertures Nlib et le mapping PlayStation Auto font partie du même binaire de test.
- Si les alias RW/RX ne passent pas le probe du firmware 13.60, le JIT sparse est désactivé avec un diagnostic et le lancement se poursuit en mode dense. **Safe Launch** contourne également les fonctions de test.
- Les anciens fichiers `experiments.json` ne sont plus consultés par le profil de test et ne peuvent pas lui désactiver les fonctions à ton insu.
- Des glyphes PlayStation **dans les jeux** exigent des textures/ROMFS originales et des packs individuels réellement qualifiés : actuellement **zéro règle graphique**. Les touches DualSense correctement mappées ne sont pas l'art dans le jeu.
- Les modes GPU non encore implémentés, le frame generation IA inexistant et les chemins JIT cross-core/compile batching indépendants non qualifiés ne deviennent pas corrects par une simple case à cocher. Ils ne sont donc pas présentés comme des capacités prêtes.

## Lancement GitHub — test natif uniquement

Workflow existant : [Build and release Prospero.Eden Encore](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/workflows/build-040-zbic.yml). Sur `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`, `workflow_dispatch` accepte :

- `test_all_on = true` : construit `tools/build-package.sh dev`, avec `EDEN_DEV_PROFILE=ON`, `EDEN_SPARSE_JIT_DEV=ON`, `EDEN_DEV_VULKAN=ON`, renderer RADV et source preflights ; produit **Prospero.Eden-Encore-PS5-all-on-test** uniquement après validation du staged app.
- `test_title_id = 0100C49025D3E000` : FC27 est l'identifiant de développement/diagnostic, **pas un autoboot implicite**. Le build de test ouvre le launcher avec le DualSense réel ; lancer FC27 ou Zelda manuellement depuis la bibliothèque. Seul `dev-settings.txt autoboot=on` demande explicitement un démarrage automatique unique. Un autre identifiant Switch 1 vérifié peut servir aux diagnostics du build suivant.
- `build_only = false` : ne jamais sauter les gates pré-compilation après modifications récentes.
- `publish = false`, `resume_run_id` vide. Le flux de test refuse toute invocation sur `fix/0.40-zbic-13.60` et n'entre jamais dans `make-dist.py` ou la publication GitHub Release.

Une alternative automatique, utilisée uniquement sur la branche de développement, est un commit déclencheur portant à la fois `[full-build]` et `[test-all-on]`. Les commits normaux `[skip ci]` ne lancent aucune compilation native. Ne pousser aucun autre commit sur la branche dev **pendant ce run**, car son groupe GitHub Actions utilise `cancel-in-progress: true`.

## Contrôles ajoutés

- `tools/check-ps5-all-on-contract.py` : refuse de laisser une configuration de test basculer silencieusement vers la release ou le dense standard ; lancé dans la validation des sources avant compilation.
- `tools/ci/check-all-on-test-binary.py` : après compilation, inspecte le CMakeCache réel, le frontend.json, le binaire de PS5, l'identifiant FC27 et l'activation effective des indicateurs de compilation. Ces données ne prouvent **pas** que l'exécutable sait utiliser les mappings du firmware.
- Nlib navigation, analyse dédupliquée des logs FC27, architecture PS5, GPU, jeux de glyphes, JIT mémoire et règle de livraison sont vérifiés par les tests hôtes préparatoires.

## Diagnostics et comparaison FC27 / Zelda

Dans le **prochain** artefact PS5 de test (après compilation explicitement autorisée), les logs sur fenêtres de 5 secondes distingueront :

- `EDEN_VULKAN_FRAME` : FPS, pire frame, nombre de frames au-delà de 38/50/100/200 ms.
- `EDEN_DEV_GPU`, `EDEN_DEV_GUEST`, `EDEN_PERF_CPU_POINT` : GPU-worker, file GPU, IPC et temps des guest-cores. Ce ne sont pas des pourcentages d'utilisation réels de la puce GPU.
- `EDEN_MEMORY_LIVE` : dernière **mesure noyau confirmée** du plus grand bloc de mémoire directe libre, sans nouvelle interrogation système depuis le rapport vidéo. Zéro avant un premier probe réussi signifie « inconnu », pas « épuisé ».
- `EDEN_JIT_SPARSE_MEMORY phase=dev-profile` : réservation virtuelle JIT et pages physiques engagées, obtenues par atomiques, sans verrou du JIT sur la frame. Les étapes `core_initialized`, `core_shutdown`, `core_destroyed` conservent les états de mémoire physique détaillés.
- `EDEN_DEV_HLE` : au plus 32 commandes HLE cumulativement les plus coûteuses sur le rapport GPU. `EDEN_DEV_HLE_SUMMARY` et `EDEN_DEV_HLE_OVERFLOW` conservent la comptabilité des commandes non détaillées.

L'outil en lecture seule `tools/analyze-ps5-frame-windows.py` sait afficher ces fenêtres, la pression mémoire directe et le JIT sparse, y compris avec les anciens logs ne possédant pas les nouveaux champs. Les nouveaux préflights `tools/check-hle-counter-contention.py` et `tools/check-ps5-frame-window-analysis.py` sont configurés dans GitHub Actions mais ne constituent pas encore des validations exécutées. Pour une mesure honnête, comparer les **mêmes scènes, paramètres vidéo et durées**, séparément entre premier démarrage et relancement avec caches.

## Vérification du profiler CPU/GPU sur une session longue

- `EDEN_DEV_SNAPSHOT_COST mono_ns=… elapsed_ns=…` mesure le coût du relevé PC en développement. Il est analysé **séparément** des vrais `EDEN_VULKAN_FRAME` ; ce coût peut lui-même retarder des images, sans prouver qu'il explique à lui seul un hitch donné.
- Le mode `pc_fast=on` à ~500 Hz attend 45 secondes avant de commencer ; il est maintenant lié au cœur invité par un `std::jthread` à arrêt borné. Pour valider réellement le changement, quitter le jeu, revenir à la bibliothèque puis lancer un autre jeu dans **le même processus**, en recherchant l'absence de signaux adressés à un vieux thread.
- Les deux tampons de PC normaux enregistrent désormais en continu jusqu'à la fin du jeu, avec remplacement circulaire des anciennes entrées. `EDEN_PERF_PC_SAMPLES_LOST source=gpu|guest count=…` annonce un éventuel retard du consommateur ; il ne faut pas interpréter ces fenêtres comme exhaustives.
- Le mode spécial `EDEN_DEV_WAIT_CALLERS`, qui capture également huit pointeurs de pile **non atomiques**, reste plafonné à son ancien volume : il n'hérite pas du mécanisme circulaire GPU tant que la protection des chaînes d'appels n'est pas qualifiée.
- Les tests hôtes à lancer dans les preflights incluent `tools/check-ps5-pc-ring-host.py`, `tools/check-hle-counter-contention.py`, `tools/check-heap-growth-rollback-host.py`, `tools/check-ps5-direct-limit-host.py` et `tools/check-library-docked-snapshot-host.py`. Aucun de ces tests ne remplace une compilation SDK 13.60 ni un retour PS5 après plusieurs jeux.

## Ce qu'un run vert ne prouve pas

Il reste à installer l'artefact sur PS5 FW13.60, comparer FC27 premier/deuxième lancement sans purger les caches, contrôler l'absence de `std::bad_alloc`, les mesures de frame time et Home/Library, la bonne activation sparse (probe et commit physique), les rendus PRMT/Fermi2D et les glyphes graphiques effectivement affichés. Les issues #7 et #8 ainsi que les 26 preuves de clôture matérielle restent ouverts jusqu'à ces tests.

### Identifiants de workers réutilisés au retour du jeu

- L'enregistrement d'un worker CPU/GPU est maintenant supprimé quand **son propre thread** s'arrête. La tâche de profilage qui demande un PC ne doit donc pas retrouver un ancien `pthread_t` encore marqué vivant au démarrage du prochain titre. Cela ne remplace pas le test firmware d'une course exceptionnelle entre une demande de signal déjà en cours et la fin du thread.

```md
# R426 — PS5 artifact-first native build hardening

R422 reached `Save build caches immediately after staging` only after the expensive native PS5 compilation. That step can run for a long time because it uploads toolchain/CMake/dependency caches while the **usable PS5 ZIP and crash symbols have not yet been uploaded**. A cancelled/failed optional cache upload therefore discards an otherwise completed console build.

R426 adjusts only `.github/workflows/build-040-zbic.yml`:

1. Keep build, package metadata checks, all-on ZIP root validation, actual uploaded ZIP extraction verification, and crash symbol upload.
2. Keep the release staged app and compiled release bundle uploads.
3. **After** those essential artifacts have been uploaded, save incremental caches as a last optional step.
4. Add `continue-on-error: true` for cache persistence. A cache service outage cannot invalidate a successful PS5 image or release. Caches continue to use the previous immutable run-scoped hash key and the same file paths.

The source-only `tools/check-ci-cache.py` now enforces ordering and cache failure isolation. This does not affect PS5 runtime, shaders, actual frame duration, native compiler command lines, or the vendored hashes. It reduces lost builds and repeated physical-test delays.

R426 is intentionally staged **outside** `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` while R422 is still running to avoid another cancellation of the active native job.

```

```md
# Eden Encore — Clôture complète PS5, FC27, JIT sparse, GPU et glyphes

**État au 9 octobre 2026 : NON TERMINÉ.** Développement : \`dev/ps5-sparse-jit\`; livraison protégée : \`fix/0.40-zbic-13.60\`. Maquette violette approuvée à préserver. **Fait :** de vraies mesures de 5 s ont présenté 18–27 FPS et des frames retardées de ~100–496 ms, malgré un compteur fixe perçu de 30 FPS. Deuxième lancement avec cache similaire. Navigation maintenue vers le bas : hitches d'UI observés à 122 et 175 ms. La console ne chauffant pas beaucoup ne prouve ni sous-exploitation CPU/GPU ni absence de limites. Anciens marqueurs de topologie CPU « non confirmée » n'indiquent pas cinq workers sur un seul cœur.

**Source déjà modifiée :** décompression/réduction des couvertures Nlib sur worker, maintien de l'upload GL sur le thread principal ; contexte PlayStation Auto collant après passage en match pour empêcher D-pad, Options ou popup de renverser la disposition pendant le match. **Clôture :** démarrage/reprise répétée de FC27 sur FW13.60, première et deuxième sessions du même match, distribution des frame times (dont p95/p99), CPU/GPU/VRAM et shaders/chargements, absence de crash \`std::bad_alloc\` après plusieurs minutes et pression mémoire, vérification du défilement bibliothèque/Home, test de la manette entre match, pause, overlays et véritable menu. `docs/PS5_F07_ALIAS_COPY_COMMIT_ROLLBACK_2026-11-01.md`:
```

```md
# PS5 Vulkan alias copy — publish freshness after successful submission

## Verified source-level failure mode

`TextureCache::SynchronizeAliases`, in the maintained Vulkan `texture_cache.h`, gathers newer GPU image aliases, sorts them by `modification_tick`, and calls `CopyImage` to bring an older destination up to date. Before this change, it wrote the newest source revision to `image.modification_tick` and marked `GpuModified` **before** the copies had been recorded. `CopyImage` enters Vulkan runtime copy/emulation/reinterpret/convert paths that may throw or reject a copy.

On a failure after one earlier source copy, the destination could retain an incorrectly up-to-date revision and suppress later alias synchronization. This is a concrete stale-image retry failure mode, although the November 1 FC27 logs do not prove that this exact failure was responsible for its HUD lag.

## Corrective behavior

- **PS5 only:** keep the destination's previous revision and `GpuModified` publication until all selected alias-copy calls complete.
- The original monotonic sort and copy order are unchanged. If any copy throws, the caller still observes the same exception; a subsequent guest draw sees an older destination revision and can retry.
- **Desktop unchanged** (original eager publication retained within `#ifndef PS5_NATIVE`).
- No discarded Vulkan work, GPU wait removal, framebuffer backpressure changes, image ID reuse or NS2 runtime changes. This is not a generic way to recover from device loss and does not guarantee completion of a driver-side GPU execution after successful queueing.

## Executed-source regression

`tools/check-fc27-f04-native-dma-alias-bytes-host.py` already extracts and compiles the production `SynchronizeAliases` method alongside an actual DMA source fragment and CPU invalidation. The extension injects an exception **after the first source copy** of two sorted aliases, asserts that neither the destination tick nor its GPU-dirty flag is published prematurely, then retries successfully and compares the destination pixel bytes. It runs PS5 source at `-O0` and `-O2` under UBSan.

The generator `tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py` reproduces the exact edited vendor source via two reviewed deltas. Host validation proves a reproducible failure-before/success-after property only; console HUD content/freshness, performance and real Vulkan driver behavior still require the consolidated PS5 test.

```

`docs/PS5_F07_BOUNDED_PRESENT_LAYER_REUSE_2026-11-01.md`:

```md
# PS5 Vulkan — bounded inactive presentation-layer retention (2026-11-01)

## Source finding

In `BlitScreen::DrawToFrame` (PS5), an ordinary change in the number of Nvnflinger presentation layers already grows the `std::list<Layer>` without an idle. A **decrease** previously triggered `WaitIdle(device)`, deleted all layers and rebuilt exactly the smaller count. A subsequent increase then had to create new layer resources. This is a plausible source of intermittent stalls when a title adds/removes transient UI layers, but the FC27 November 1 logs do **not** identify a layer-count transition in either residual stutter window. **No measured FC27 FPS or HUD gain is claimed.**

`WindowAdaptPass::Draw` uses `configs.size()` as the draw count, advances `layer_it` only across those active configs and records only their descriptor sets. Therefore extra inactive `Layer` objects can remain in the list without being rendered or referenced by that frame.

## Change

- PS5 only: keep a high-water reserve of at most **8 inactive/reusable layer identities** without an idle when the active guest layer count decreases.
- The limit is on **retained owner count during a shrink**, not the number of active guest layers. If a title needs 9+ simultaneous layers, all are created and drawn. When it later shrinks, owners above 8 are retired via the original `WaitIdle` and rebuilt to the exact active count.
- Rebuild with original device/queue synchronization when swapchain image count, descriptor/layout contract or format changes, or FSR/SGSR output-sensitive window dimensions change.
- No draw skipping; no change to guest textures, CPU memory invalidation, Vulkan fences, wait ordering or NS2 GPU logic. Desktop path unchanged.
- Tradeoff: up to 8 layers and their per-swapchain resources may remain allocated while fewer are active. Capacity is reclaimed on layout rebuild/teardown, or on over-budget shrink.

## Host qualification

`tools/check-ps5-f07-present-layer-growth-host.py` extracts the **actual** native/desktop conditional decision and compiles it at O0/O2 under UBSan. The fixture covers grow → shrink → re-grow without idle, unchanged layer identity, forced contract rebuild, FSR/SGSR rectangle changes and a 9 → 8 → 2 → 8 bounded sequence. The test also checks the source of `WindowAdaptPass::Draw` consumes only the active `configs.size()` entries.

The native source generator emits the same changed decision. CI parity and full build remain necessary; **PS5 hardware verification is not inferred** from a host test. Please combine any PS5 comparison with the main release/NS2 functional testing rather than requesting another standalone FC27 install.

```

`docs/PS5_FRAME_PIPELINE_FAIRNESS_R421.md`:

```md
# R421 — PS5 cold-pipeline scheduling / frame-hitch reduction

Context: FC27 can remain near 30 FPS while suffering long individual frame stalls. The emulator's real-time frame path, texture cache ownership and presentation are not the same as average FPS; higher GPU throughput alone cannot resolve a pipeline compilation wait. No PS5 frame-time improvement is claimed without new console data.

## Identified concurrency

Under the native **EDEN_DEV_PROFILE / All-On** configuration, `fast_first_pipelines=true` builds a quickly usable, nonoptimized Vulkan graphics pipeline on the first-use `VkPipelineBuilder` worker, then schedules a full optimized rebuild on the separate `VkPipelineOptimize` worker. Before R421 these two workers could enter the same RADV driver concurrently, even when more first-use shaders were queued. `GetTotalPipelineWorkers` itself is conservatively constrained by the real kernel CPU affinity; changing its limit without verified firmware SMT topology would risk starving presentation and I/O.

R421 gives first-use graphics builds priority **without altering GPU submissions, descriptor cache locking, Vulkan object ownership, guest CPU mapping, or graphics output**:

- An atomic pending count tracks queued and running first-use graphics builds, but **only while `fast_first_pipelines` is enabled**.
- Each queued build decrements this count via `SCOPE_EXIT` on success, exception or early return; an unsuccessful queue insertion is also compensated.
- The separate `VkPipelineOptimize` callback yields in 2 ms sleeps, at most 48 ms per optimized pipeline, whenever newer graphics builds need CPU/driver time.
- This wait is **solely on the speculative background optimization thread** and **never delays frame presentation or the first-use graphics build**. After the bound expires the optimizer proceeds, avoiding indefinite starvation.
- The original `optimized_ready` publication and pipeline destructor's cancellation/finish guard remain intact. PS5 release builds default `fast_first_pipelines=false`, so there is no pending-counter work there.
- `tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py` is updated along with the active `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vk_graphics_pipeline_cost.cpp`; verify byte-for-byte equivalence via `tools/check-vendored-vulkan-fork.py`.

This is a **hypothesis-driven frame-time contention reduction**. It cannot by itself repair guest texture coherence, HUD drops, shader correctness or display refresh pacing. Confirm with first-use/present/cache profiling before attributing stutter improvements to this change. Prefer one combined hardware validation after the next All-On build, retaining the current game/shader cache for a warm-frame comparison.

## CodeQL

GitHub created `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` during the manual transition from Default Setup to Advanced. That generated file had no `config-file`, scanning the vendor test fixtures twice and making results inconsistent. R421 removes this duplicate, retaining the existing `.github/workflows/codeql-advanced.yml` with `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` and all three languages. `tools/check-codeql-security-scope.py` now prevents accidentally reintroducing it. The 14 vendor-source alerts are scope exclusions, not claims of patched upstream code.

## R422 native qualification

After R421 source regression checks passed, run one PS5 **All-On native** build with the verified R421 shader-fairness code and R417 scheduler thread probes. Package a single candidate for a combined FC27 console test; no change to release graphics presets, per-game FPS policy or cached media.

```

`docs/PS5_FRAME_PRESENT_DIAGNOSTICS_R424.md`:

```md
# R424 — Diagnose 30 FPS frame hitches by presentation phase

An FPS counter holding 30 FPS doesn't establish regular frame delivery. Previous PS5 detailed profiles accumulated `gpu_present_wait` across both `PresentManager::GetRenderFrame()` waits: (1) the producer waiting for a recycled frame in `free_queue` and (2) the GPU fence associated with that frame. A 30 FPS plateau with hitches cannot distinguish FIFO queue starvation from GPU completion latency with that one aggregate.

R424 adds two **detailed-mode only** counters, retaining the existing aggregate and respecting the original sequence:

- `gpu_present_free_wait`: `free_mutex` acquisition, `free_cv.wait` and ownership transfer from `free_queue`.
- `gpu_present_fence_wait`: blocking `frame->present_done.Wait()` after `free_mutex` has been released.
- `EDEN_PRESENT_WAIT_PHASE frame=... free_calls=... free_ns=... fence_calls=... fence_ns=...` every regular detailed GPU snapshot, reporting cumulative totals for delta analysis.

No new queue depth, fence semantics, swapchain structure, presentation policy, spin, busy-wait or sleep. The normal non-detailed path doesn't call a clock in either new `DiagnosticTimer`. The original `EDEN_DEV_GPU ... present_calls= ... present_ns=...` remains unchanged for existing parsers, as does the renderer's frame time.

For source provenance, the tracked complete `vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vulkan_present_manager.cpp` and `tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py` both contain equivalent transforms. Regression gates are `tools/check-ps5-present-phase-timing.py` and the full `tools/check-vendored-vulkan-fork.py`.

## Interpretation

Compare two consecutive five-second snapshots:

- Rising `free_ns` plus low `fence_ns`: free image scarcity / asynchronous presentation back-pressure, investigate presenter throughput and swapchain.
- Rising `fence_ns`: returned image is still used by GPU, investigate command completion/synchronization, not shader build count alone.
- Neither dominates while FC27 hitches: prioritize existing `EDEN_DEV_GPU` queue, `EDEN_GPU_DMA_SYNC`, guest cache wait, pipeline build, and game-vsync timestamps.

Diagnostic counters alone are **not a claim of performance improvement**. If R422 finishes first, keep it as the safe physical baseline; incorporate these counters only in the subsequent combined native candidate. No additional physical test required for a source-only R424 commit.

```

`docs/PS5_GLOBAL_SHADER_PREWARM_2026-11-01.md`:

```md
# PS5 Vulkan — global bounded persisted shader prewarm (2026-11-01)

## Runtime observation and goal

The FC 27 console trace on 2026-11-01 shows a strong cluster of first-use shader compilation and
long presentation intervals near match startup. The tester also reports residual micro-stutter
and occasional delayed HUD content during otherwise largely smooth gameplay. These are two
possibly distinct problems: widening startup cache restoration cannot alone prove a fix for
late-match frame pacing, texture freshness, or guest rendering progress.

## Scope of this candidate change

- Every title (NS1 and NS2) uses **the same** persisted-pipeline reader quota: up to **32**
  entries instead of 8. There are **no title-ID special cases**.
- If a title's cache has fewer than 32 valid serialized entries, the reader naturally loads
  only the available entries. This does not manufacture pipelines for unseen shaders.
- Quota cancellation affects **only the cache file reader**. Accepted shader-builder jobs
  finish before the local load state is destroyed; the worker pool stays alive for gameplay.
- Valid native handles are the only ones admitted into the prewarm maps, as before.
- The startup summary includes `limit=32` and the real queued/completed/valid/rejected counts.
- The active Vulkan vendor source and its reproducible `prepare-vulkan-port.py` generator
  must remain byte-for-byte equivalent for the quota and summary changes.
- No buffer/texture cache ownership, GPU scheduler wait, draw ordering, fence handling,
  JIT path, framebuffer lifetime, guest controls, or NS2 loader code changes.

## Trade-off and limitations

More persisted pipelines may move some cold first-use IR / SPIR-V translation **before**
the first guest frame, potentially reducing initial visible hitches. It may also extend
startup and increase temporary compilation memory/CPU use for titles with many saved entries.
No claim of improved FPS, reduced HUD latency, or guaranteed benefit on a cleared cache:
without persisted pipeline entries there is nothing to prewarm.

The current reader takes the first serialized cache entries, not a proven usage-ranked
list. Further quota increases or priority scheduling should use matching console
measurements rather than treating all stutter as shader-first-use latency.

## Validation before merge

1. Run the bounded-prewarm host tests, admission tests, persistence tests, and
   generator parity/build preflight with the pinned vendor submodule commit.
2. Keep the PR separate from ongoing NS2 GMMU/GPFIFO changes; do not merge or build
   on the other conversation's behalf.
3. On a later combined PS5 build, compare warm-cache startup duration,
   `EDEN_PS5_SHADER_PREWARM` valid/queued metrics, FC27 first-match late50/100,
   and in-match residual frame pacing. Check HUD correctness and title switching.
4. Also compare cold-cache launch (0 persisted entries) and one non-FC27 game.
5. Treat per-frame HUD freshness and buffer/texture lock attribution as **OPEN**.
   Do not remove GPU waits/fences or disable texture invalidation to hide artifacts.
```

```md
# Eden Encore R441 — Hot path audit and source-proven external paths

Source audited: dev/ps5-sparse-jit, after R440. Source-only, no PS5 native build.

## Repeated-frame and shader wait

- `vk_pipeline_cache_cost.cpp::CurrentGraphicsPipelineSlowPath` creates first-use graphics pipelines, and the PS5 `BuiltPipeline` returns an unbuilt pipeline rather than drop a draw.
- `vk_graphics_pipeline_cost.cpp::ConfigureDraw` inserts an ordered `scheduler.Record` callback waiting on `build_condvar` for the pipeline to become ready.
- `vulkan_scheduler.cpp::WorkerThread` holds `execution_mutex` while executing that callback. A cold compilation can **block the Vulkan worker** while the separate shader-building worker runs. This is analogous to Pereira's #676, but not Wine's PE stream gate; bypassing this ordering could drop HUD draws or race descriptor resources.
- `vulkan_rasterizer.cpp::PrepareDraw` takes the **buffer+texture cache lock pair** around pipeline configuration/descriptor setup. Existing source-phase probes cover pair waits, texture alias scans/copies, and descriptor work; no authoritative same-frame proof that these cause FC27's freeze.
- `vulkan_present_manager.cpp::Present` can progress in a thread independently of the game's simulation. A 30 Hz present counter may continue during a guest freeze. Avoid using presents as the simulation-progress clock for Swordpdf's frame generation.

## Already ported: do not duplicate

- Official Mihawk PS5_Mesa 120 Hz offer/configuration validation entered Encore in **R400**, despite R438's stale version comparison.
- PS5 input `headless/pad.cpp` already calls `scePadRead` with a full buffer and consumes each returned sample; drakmor's gamepad batching research confirms this design.
- Pereira's shader disk cache credentials fix entered R414, so do not reapply.
- R439 GC has an independent 8192-visit traversal bound and historical 10/20/40 eviction budgets with rollback. R441 teaches the existing offline log analyser to read `EDEN_VULKAN_GC_SCAN` without incorrectly aligning sparse samples to unrelated five-second telemetry.
- R440 ports Pereira's unpresented-swapchain takeover (host-model-tested upstream). The author did not establish PS5 native qualification for **that exact patch**, and neither have we.

## Rechecked relevant sources

- [mpereiraesaa/prospero-win](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/prospero-win): 0881/0882 CPU affinity/fairness, PR #676 Vulkan compilations outside global Wine stream lock, 0879 GUI wake-state bug.
- [mpereiraesaa/PS5_Mesa 9d3cd417](https://github.com/mpereiraesaa/PS5_Mesa/commit/9d3cd417ff488bd1a7cc68c1f1c8e1df409c2a11): off-size swapchains and refused VideoOut allocation cleanup validated through its author host model after native Wine evidence. Needs ownership adaptation: Encore's WSI always registers 3840x2160, unlike Pereira's scalable WSI.
- [Swordpdf/ps5-framegen](https://github.com/Swordpdf/ps5-framegen): reusable Vulkan optical-flow interpolation proven in PS5SX2 (ps5vk) and RPCS3-PS5 (RADV). Pacer must use guest/source ticks, not repeated presents, to avoid self-feeding; it cannot unfreeze game simulation or repair corrupt render targets.
- [drakmor/ps5-hwinfo](https://github.com/drakmor/ps5-hwinfo): CPU/GPU clock and logical-load diagnosis; payload APIs may not work from an ordinary native title.
- [EchoStretch/kstuff-lite](https://github.com/EchoStretch/kstuff-lite), [soniciso1/ps5-linux-archive](https://github.com/soniciso1/ps5-linux-archive), [ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit](https://github.com/ntfargo/Relapse-Exploit): loader/firmware/ABI evidence rather than drop-in frame timing patches.
- [ArkSama/PS5_RPCS3](https://github.com/ArkSama/PS5_RPCS3): PS3 port reference with distinct GPL license/distribution boundary; [Unlock PS5 Pro memory](https://github.com/ArkSama/Unlock-ps5-pro-memory) benefits Pro models, not Encore's base PS5.
- External Mesa [RADV docs](https://docs.mesa3d.org/drivers/radv.html) and [26.2 release notes](https://docs.mesa3d.org/relnotes/26.2.0.html): userspace SPIR-V -> NIR -> ACO, separately from PS5 native GPU winsys; cherry-pick specific proven correctness work instead of blindly rebasing a diverged Mesa fork.

## Practical order

1. Keep source/CI checks after porting, do not require another user hardware test *before* implementation.
2. Diagnose worker shader waits vs stalled guest CPU progress; preserve queued GPU draw correctness.
3. Improve texture descriptor residency/HUD alias freshness, not stale readback shortcuts.
4. Port author's image-size WSI only as one coherent ownership change.
5. Import Swordpdf framegen full sources, shaders, licenses and native presentation integration as a separate optional feature once guest-tick pacing can be trusted.
6. Bundle console testing across changes. Never equate a green host contract with verified PS5 FPS/fidelity.

## R442 — Align GPU-written texture prefetch with R439 collector (2026-10-13)

Confirmed mismatch: R439's `Cleanup` counts actual eligible evictions while `headless/vulkan_gc_downloads.inc::PrefetchDownloads` still decremented its 10/20/40 batch lookahead allowance before checking IsDecoding/CostlyLoad. Under LRU-skew, the collector could evict dirty images that were not prefetched, forcing individual GPU Finish() waits. R442 now mirrors the collector's **8192 bounded visits**, skip semantics and `gc_scan=upstream` visit-count rollback in both the generator include and checked-in active source. It does not expand the maximum of 40 prefetched downloads or the 32 MiB byte budget, change guest GPU memory ownership, or discard draws. Adds a host contract/model `tools/check-gc-prefetch-budget.py` and R439 cross-check update. Source-only; no FC27 performance claim before a native run.

## R444 — Prioritize gameplay shaders until cold compilation drains

Source inspection confirmed the secondary `VkPipelineOptimize` worker could begin `MakePipeline` as soon as a fixed 48 ms delay expired, even when `pending_first_use_graphics_builds` remained nonzero. With only 13 logical CPUs allowed, concurrent compilation can contend for both CPU and RADV cache operations exactly as first-use draws are stalled. The optional optimized pipeline is **not needed for correctness** because its fast-first pipeline is already valid. R444 holds only the background optimizer while the first-use counter is nonzero; it checks per-pipeline cancellation with a short 2 ms sleep. The existing `OptimizeState` mutex ensures title teardown aborts a waiting worker even if a first-use build remains stuck, without holding any guest/GPU locks. Source generator and checked-in Vulkan copy are identical. The host C++ gate now covers a 100 ms backlog that formerly let optimizing begin at 48 ms, cancellation during a permanent backlog, and immediate idle path. No claim of a measured FC27 FPS gain yet.

## R445 — Cross-test parity for R442 (2026-10-13)

GitHub core-preflight R443 demonstrated R439/R442's source tests and real GC admission/batching fixtures pass but the older `check-vulkan-gc-mixed-prefetch-host.py` stopped on the obsolete exact string `if (remaining == 0) return true;`. The host-side literal staging model now treats skipped decoding/costly-load images as non-evictions under the same 8192 scan ceiling as the shipping collector, and adds 180 excluded textures before five dirty GPU-written images. The updated test still compiles and runs its existing ASan/UBSan C++ staging, 32 MiB cap and one-Finish scenarios. Source-only; console result pending later combined test.

## R447 — Repair validated WSI cache admission for native build

R446 failed before compiling because the exact source SHA-256 `4175fad06454b5c14a2be8045d791deb33fc6034959a7d58b733ed27b22d23b2` from Encore's own R439 WSI was present in the cached compiler staging tree. It was no longer equal to post-R440 active WSI nor the R398 legacy fixture. The pre-R440 WSI bytes are now retained under `tools/fixtures/ps5-r439-wsi-videoout.c` and explicitly recognized **only** for the WSI translation unit. `check-vendored-radv-fork.py` replays and verifies the exact fixture → R440 canonical input; unknown inputs remain fatal. This is a CI staging fix, not a GPU-rendering change.

## R448 — FC27 per-title gameplay map separated from global PlayStation UI

The fixed-input implementation hardcoded `pad->SetMapping(mapping)` for every guest screen, so the global PlayStation navigation map and FC27's separately saved title mapping could not coexist. FC27 (ID `0100C49025D3E000`) now preserves the global menu map and retains its **explicit, saved, distinct title map** as a match profile. Press Touchpad + Square together to enter the custom map when gameplay starts; press again to return to PlayStation navigation for cinematics/dialogs. The chord is edge-latched, consumed before guest HID, and all stale guest held buttons are released before the map change. Other titles retain their fixed profile. **No reliable automatic game-scene detection exists in HID:** this does not automatically detect kickoff or pause, and no such claim is made. Source and host tests verify scope and preservation, not PS5 behavior.

## R452 — FC27 chord held-state correction

A physical Touchpad+Square press must toggle once even if Cross/Options or other buttons change during the held chord. The R448 predicate mixed “physically held” with “valid for entering mode”, causing its latch to reset if a disallowed button entered during the hold. R452 separates the physical latch (remains true until the actual chord is released) from the acceptance predicate (only the first permitted press toggles); guest chord buttons remain suppressed throughout the hold. This prevents unintended match/menu reversals. No extra guest scene inference is introduced.

## R456 — Make FC27 in-game controls effective without a launcher title override

**Corrected oversight:** R448 required `game_video.own_mapping` to be true, despite the reported configuration being edited inside FC27 rather than in Encore. The guest's internal control assignments cannot set `own_mapping`. R456 permits the title `0100C49025D3E000` to keep the global PlayStation UI profile while selecting physical Switch guest button positions in *manual match context*, with the saved Encore per-title mapping taking precedence if actually present. Other titles unchanged. The existing Touchpad+Square context toggle remains explicit; no automatic scene recognition was added. The C++ regression checks FC27 with and without a launcher override. Source-only until native validation.
```
