`docs/UPSTREAM_HOTPATH_REVIEW_2026-10-15.md`:

```md
# October 15 GPU cache/JIT upstream review — source qualification only

Scope: `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`; no new native build and no physical console test.

## Evidence from supplied Oct 15 FC27 traces

Two independent session files were analyzed separately. Their maximum *cumulative*
buffer-cache lock waits per ~5-second window were 176.2 ms and 252.2 ms.
For texture-cache mutexes the maxima were 120.9 ms and 510.1 ms.
These are sums across completed waits, not one stalled render frame and
not a causal proof of pause-menu freeze. Latest per-session results had
323 and 466 displayed frames >50ms, respectively. Do not merge session
counter resets or equate presenter FPS with guest simulation progress.

## Current upstream disposition

- ProsperoEden [#187](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/f1b83c21d157):
  high-priority, **not completely integrated**. This change includes much
  more than buffer lock elision: deferred guest writes, GPU-side replay before
  dependent commands, GPU-modified/fence exceptions, and core-scoped queues.
  Importing only the early deferred-write version would risk stale HUD/terrain
  textures. The `buffer_write_ahead.h` subcomponent is separately staged:
  it marks registered buffer pages only under an existing cache lock, stops
  at unregistered or GPU-owned pages, and is **OFF by default** (`cpu_write_ahead=0`).
  Offline sanitizer tests do not prove any speedup. The complete deferral
  semantics are not enabled or claimed.
- ProsperoEden [#188](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/b94216347b9a):
  **not integrated**. Direct JIT page table + page reuse need matching sparse
  commit order, page invalidation, new Dynarmic IR opcodes and host memory
  differential tests. Existing sparse JIT is not an equivalent implementation.
- ProsperoEden [#185](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/99e381ed29f7):
  **not integrated**. Dirty block-row texture refresh needs per-image, per-cache
  lifetime accounting and same-snapshot unswizzle verification; an earlier
  upstream variant left stale page state across title switches.
- ProsperoEden [#179](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/9c898feb254a):
  already covered by `headless/jit-compile-batch.inc` line 21.
- ProsperoEden [#183](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/a13e040cd502):
  equivalent 1.5ms guest VI composition delay already present.
- ProsperoEden [#181](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/6b4d27ff3352):
  256-entry native GPU queue already present.
- ProsperoEden [#178](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/96d8f4a8e852):
  native `video_core` ThinLTO + Zen2 already present.

## Stop conditions

No more user console trials for these source checks. Do not enable the
new write-ahead optimization on a release from host contracts alone.
Prioritize full write/read/fence ordering proof for #187, then independent
JIT memory differential verification for #188, then per-texture lifecycle
checks for #185. CI success proves source contracts, not FC27 gameplay.

## Deferred write pipeline gate (follow-up)

A standalone `headless/gpu_deferred_write_queue.h` now models per-core deferred
ranges, same-page-only merging, release/acquire handoff, GPU owner replay
without holding queue mutexes, and explicit shutdown quiescence. The
`tools/check-gpu-deferred-queue-host.py` sanitizer fixture covers four
concurrent producers (1,280 distinct writes), invalid/overflow ranges,
cross-page boundaries and a simulated GPU-modified fence case.

**This is deliberately NOT wired to OnCPUWrite, FlushCaching, or the DMA
pusher.** The test validates queue ownership mechanics but cannot prove that
real GPU cache invalidation, guest dirty range collection, guest submits and
GPU fences remain ordered. Runtime behavior therefore stays unchanged; a
console test now would provide no useful signal. The next engineering gate is
a source-level native integration whose actual guest cache and HLE ordering
passes host validation before any activation.

## GPU-dirty replay correctness gate (follow-up)

The pinned `core/gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h` uses `DEVICE_PAGEBITS-1`
(2,048-byte) transform regions and 64-byte alignment. Passing an arbitrary
queued guest write directly to `Collect` can cross one or several transform
regions and violate its bit-mask preconditions. `headless/gpu_deferred_replay.h`
slices each GPU-owned replay at the exact 2-KiB boundary while preserving
the original CPU-core index; regular guest writes must still go through
texture/shader invalidation but do not create false GPUDirty entries.
`tools/check-gpu-deferred-replay-host.py` runs sanitizer-backed boundary,
large-span, core-attribution and reentrant-drain checks.

**Not yet connected to actual GPU dispatch or caches**. A native runtime
bridge still requires source and lifecycle validation across
`HandleRasterizerWrite`, `OnCPUWrite`, `FlushCaching`, DMA and fences.
No PS5 test is warranted until that integration is qualified.

## Queue coalescing narrowed to the GPU-dirty transform

A previously staged queue could merge disjoint guest writes inside a 4-KiB
page. The actual GPU dirty collector tracks 2-KiB regions, so an overly
wide merged range could cause false GPU-owned dirty marks. Coalescing now
requires both a single 2-KiB region AND overlapping/touching spans;
disjoint spans are kept separate. The host sanitizer fixture checks both
cross-region adjacency and unwritten gaps within a region.

This conservative policy is source-only; the full #187 runtime path
remains intentionally disconnected until ordered GPU/DMA/fence replay is
verified, including on title teardown.

## Cross-core FIFO requirement and correction

The first host queue drained all core 0 writes before core 1-3 writes.
That could reorder CPU invalidations across independent core producers
and make a GPU cache snapshot inconsistent. The new session-owned FIFO
assigns one mutex-protected enqueue order across all cores and stores
the original core on each range. Replaying never holds the queue mutex;
a callback may enqueue more work for a subsequent batch. Coalescing
only applies to adjacent/overlapping ranges from the **same core**
in the **same 2-KiB dirty region**, and only when consecutive in FIFO.
The sanitizer fixture asserts cross-core [2,0,3,1] ordering and prohibits
a coalescing shortcut across intervening core writes.

This guarantees enqueue order only. It does NOT prove the memory visibility
order between guest writes and GPU command execution; native enablement
remains blocked on DMA/fence and title-lifecycle contracts.

## Native Vulkan bridge (source integration; strictly OFF)

A guarded `headless/guest_write_deferred_bridge.cmake` is included by the
native CMake port, with `EDEN_GUEST_WRITE_BRIDGE_DEV=OFF` by default. Only a
native Vulkan development profile can select the CMake path. Its derived
source translations (immutable upstream + immutable maintained Vulkan files)
pair the title-owned `Tegra::MemoryManager` queue with Vulkan
`RasterizerVulkan::OnCPUWrite`, `MemoryManager::FlushCaching`, GPU-dirty
per-core collection and command boundaries at start/end of DMA dispatch,
Maxwell DMA and Kepler compute launches. Reentrant GPU replay suppresses
its own enqueue through a thread-local scope.

**Not yet production-ready.** `cpu_write_defer` remains false with no
activation through settings. Host CI tests CMake parsing in OFF mode and
pinned-source anchors, but no native SDK build has compiled the opt-in branch.
Even a successful native compilation would not yet prove callback ordering,
GPU cache synchronization, shutdown quiescence or stable game HUD. No
console test is justified.

## Inline guest memory upload barrier

The development bridge now also derives `engine_upload_deferred.cpp`.
Its `State::ProcessData(std::span<...>)` drains the title-owned pending
guest writes before either direct linear `AccelerateInlineToMemory` or
tiled `GpuGuestMemoryScoped` upload, rather than waiting until a later
draw or dispatch. This closes one ordering hole between DMA and renderer
command boundaries. The mock native-ON CMake generator now expects **six**
derived units, while the runtime defer gate and normal build remain OFF.

## Prevent partially replayed cache invalidations

Review of pinned `HandleRasterizerWrite` and active Vulkan `OnCPUWrite`
identified a critical asymmetry: buffer cache invalidation runs before
texture cache invalidation. If the buffer phase succeeds, it is unsafe to
queue the entire write only because the subsequent texture mutex is held.
The disabled native bridge therefore **only defers before acquiring the
buffer cache mutex**, before either cache has been modified. Once that
mutex is acquired, the existing full buffer, texture and pipeline sequence
runs synchronously, including the texture mutex wait. The host generation
contract requires exactly one enqueue call in the active derived method
and forbids texture mutex `try_lock` in that path.

## Serialize GPU-dirty writes across guest and GPU producers

The pinned `Core::GPUDirtyMemoryManager::Collect` performs its
`current.exchange(new_transform)` under `guard` but the initial
`current.load` and same-region CAS occur outside the mutex.
With a GPU replay producer collecting into the same guest core concurrently,
one producer may replace a newer current transform with a stale snapshot,
silently dropping dirty blocks before `Gather`. Atomic exchange alone
does **not** solve a compare-and-swap race.

The **developer-only**, default-OFF bridge now derives
`deferred-core/core/gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h` from the pinned original,
acquiring the existing `guard` for the entire `Collect` method, while
removing the obsolete nested lock. `Gather` already takes `guard`.
No changes to `TransformAddress`, dirty bit granularity, fences, or the
normal vendor header. Both `core` and `video_core` opt-in builds must see
the same shadow header; the memory-manager replay translation unit now
includes its complete type explicitly. The host contract checks the
derived source and is extended with concurrent collection stress.

## Guest-core attribution and GPU-thread exclusion

The development bridge now derives `memory-ps5-deferred.cpp` from the
native-specific, already patched core memory translation unit. It scopes
`ScopedGuestWriteOrigin` around the **actual** `HandleRasterizerWrite ->
GPU::OnCPUWrite` call, restoring the previous TLS origin on return.
`Tegra::MemoryManager::EnqueueDeferredCPUWrite` takes that explicit guest
core instead of guessing from `GetCurrentHostThreadID`. The opt-in Vulkan
branch may only defer when the guest origin is valid, the queue gate is
enabled and the call is not itself a replay. Ordinary GPU-worker writes
have no guest origin and remain on the original synchronous path.
The developer CMake fixture checks the resulting seventh translation
unit and the exact origin guard. The shipping mode stays OFF.

## GPU write queue-pressure gate (unsafe shortcut withdrawn)

The candidate's 8,192-entry cap was withdrawn before runtime activation.
Returning false at capacity would make a *later* CPU write run the blocking
cache path ahead of older writes still queued for GPU replay. That breaks
the intended cache/fence ordering guarantee. The queue instead requires a
true GPU-drain barrier with shutdown-aware backpressure before any cap
can be introduced safely. Until then it remains OFF in all native builds.

Nested guest-core origin scope and worker TLS isolation are independently
covered by the sanitizer test of the replay header.

## Post-store FIFO cancellation model (2026-10-16)

The inactive host queue now has `Cancel(Ticket)` and `CancelAndWake(Ticket, RequestGpu)`
for a reserved write that completed without changing guest backing RAM (for
example a failed conditional store). Cancellation marks the ordered reservation
as published/no-op, rather than erasing its sequence and overtaking preceding
writes. The GPU drain advances the completed watermark past canceled entries
but never calls the cache invalidation callback for them. Canceling an
unpublished FIFO head triggers the same shutdown-joined GPU wake contract as
publishing a completed ordinary store; failed wake callbacks poison the queue.

The sanitizer host test exercises a canceled middle write, FIFO replay around
that write, a canceled head releasing a published tail, and stale/duplicate
resolution rejection. The native bridge remains OFF and
`kNativePostStorePublicationReady = false`: a failed atomic compare first
READS guest memory, so its read/download ordering must be solved as well as
post-store cancellation. All store classes, GPU cache ownership, direct
JIT/fastmem accesses, title shutdown and DMA must be qualified before
activation. This commit does not address game frame stalls or FC27 HUD.

## Cancelled-tail coalescing correctness (2026-10-16)

A cancelled pending conditional write remains in FIFO as a published no-op.
Before this follow-up, the queue\'s eager same-core coalescing could merge a
later real write into that cancelled tail. Because replay skips cancelled
entries, the merged genuine cache invalidation was silently lost. Eager
coalescing now requires `!tail.cancelled` in addition to its old same-core,
same-region and overlap checks. A sanitizer regression reproduces a failed
conditional write followed by a genuine overlapping write and verifies that
exactly the latter reaches the invalidation callback. No native/runtime bridge
is enabled, and this is not a gameplay/HUD/performance fix.

## Bounded backpressure for future post-store producers (2026-10-16)

The source-only queue now exposes `ReserveOrdered` for a new write arriving
while 8,192 older writes remain unacknowledged. A plain `Reserve` rejection
must never allow the native producer to fall through to synchronous cache
invalidation ahead of older FIFO work. `ReserveOrdered` instead captures
the accepted watermark, asks the GPU owner to drain OUTSIDE queue locks,
waits through the older watermark, and retries its reservation. Scheduling
callbacks are joined during `Close`; callback failures poison the session
and release waiting readers/producers. An unpublished FIFO head still blocks
later replay until `PublishAndWake` or `CancelAndWake` resolves it.

The host sanitizer test covers synchronous drain after saturation, a blocked
unpublished head released by publication, and a failing scheduler callback.
This interface is NOT used by the inactive CMake bridge, and the native
runtime gate stays `false`. In particular, there is still no proven GPU
command scheduler wake, read-after-write fence, atomic publication or native
teardown integration. A caller must not invoke this helper while holding a
cache mutex or on the GPU consumer thread. No claim of FC27 improvement.

## Explicit failed GPU scheduling callbacks (2026-10-16)

The host-only request/wakeup contract now accepts callbacks returning either
`void` (an exception signals failure) or `bool` (a `false` result signals
rejection). Previously a boolean rejection was ignored. That could leave a
published head with no GPU wake or cause `ReserveOrdered` to wait forever after
backpressure without any GPU job being scheduled. Both code paths now treat
`false` as a thrown scheduling error and enter their existing session-poisoning
and waiter notification paths; successful `true` and existing `void` callbacks
retain their behavior. Source guards and sanitizer host tests cover both APIs,
including cancelled writes. The native bridge and its runtime gate remain OFF.

## Post-store transaction adapter, host-only (2026-10-16)

`headless/gpu_deferred_store_publication.h` now composes the existing
`ReserveOrdered`, `PublishAndWake` and `CancelAndWake` operations around
an explicit noexcept RAM store callback. It reserves a FIFO position before
executing the operation exactly once, publishes only after a real modification,
and cancels a failed conditional write. The compiler rejects potentially
throwing store callbacks to avoid a partially modified but unpublished
reservation. If the title is closed/poisoned before reservation, no RAM operation
is attempted. A failed publication after RAM mutation is a fatal caller error;
there is no safe synchronous fallback.

The source-backed sanitizer test checks pinned ordinary/scalar/zero/CAS/cache
maintenance call-site ordering and exercises the actual host queue with a
normal RAM store, failed CAS, cross-core publication gap, saturated queue,
invalid reservation and explicit rejected scheduler wake. It proves the
standalone protocol's mechanics, **not** native GPU coherence.

`headless/guest_write_deferred_bridge.cmake` does not call this adapter.
The current native derived `HandleRasterizerWrite` bridge still eagerly
enqueues before backing RAM store and the fail-closed
`kNativePostStorePublicationReady` remains `false`. A real integration must
separately classify cache maintenance (no subsequent store), synchronize
reads/atomic RMW before the attempted write, and cover direct fastmem/JIT
stores and renderer/fence shutdown ordering. No native build, release, console
test, or claim of FC27 improvement.

## Developer source write-intent classification (2026-10-16)

The CMake-derived developer-only guest memory source now marks five
pre-store callbacks: block copy, zero block, scalar write, regular exclusive,
and 128-bit exclusive. The two cache-maintenance callbacks (StoreDataCache
and FlushDataCache) have no following RAM store and remain unmarked.
The GPU memory manager and Vulkan candidate both require the scoped
StoreFollows intent and the existing guest-core origin. The native bridge
still uses unsafe eager publication, which remains blocked by the unchanged
kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false gate. Normal builds are unchanged.
CMake source derivation tests assert all five marked and two unmarked sites;
the host sanitizer verifies nested and cross-thread TLS restoration.

## Nested cache-maintenance context isolation (2026-10-16)

Unmarked cache-maintenance callbacks could inherit `StoreFollows` from an
enclosing guest write on the same thread. The developer-only derived guest
memory source now puts an explicit `ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent` around
both `StoreDataCache` and `FlushDataCache` rasterizer callbacks. The scope
forces `NoStore` even under nested guest writes and restores the previous
intent on exit. The CMake derivation refuses changed or missing two-site
anchors; the generated-source contract verifies two tagged maintenance
callbacks without converting either into a RAM store. The host sanitizer
tests Store -> Maintenance -> Store nesting and restoration. The native
runtime bridge remains gated off and normal native sources are unchanged.

## Full store lifetime scoping in derived guest memory (2026-10-16)

A source review revealed that the previous `StoreFollows` markers for scalar
`Write`, `WriteExclusive` and `WriteExclusive128` lived only inside the
`GetPointerImpl` rasterizer callback; they ended before the subsequent
`memcpy` or atomic compare-and-swap. The tracked `WriteBlockImpl` marker
also ended before `memcpy`. This prevented any later post-store publication
hook from sharing the scoped operation identity.

The derived developer-only guest memory source now keeps markers in scope
for the complete tracked `WriteBlockImpl` callback and at function scope
for scalar/exclusive writes. The unsafe WriteBlockImpl branch performs its
original memcpy without a marker. `ZeroBlock` already covered its memset,
and cache-maintenance callbacks still force `NoStore`.
The host-generated-source contract checks the marker lifetime relative to
actual memcpy/CAS lines and confirms the five paths are still distinct.

This is **not** post-store publication: no native ticket, wake callback,
GPU-to-CPU read fence, or conditional-store outcome has been wired. The
developer-only enqueue path remains blocked by
`kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false`; shipping Vulkan sources are
unchanged. No console build, release, gameplay test or performance claim.

## Host conditional guest-write read fence (2026-10-16)

The standalone `CommitConditionalAfterRead` helper now models the missing
precondition for CAS and 128-bit exclusive stores: an explicit, **blocking**
guest CPU-read synchronization callback must report `ReadBarrierResult::Complete`
before any reservation or atomic RAM access. A rejected/incomplete read leaves
the queue unchanged and does not execute the attempt. Once synchronized,
`CommitPostStore` reserves, executes exactly one noexcept CAS attempt, then
publishes the modified range or cancels an unsuccessful comparison.

The host sanitizer now covers earlier GPU invalidations drained before a
successful CAS, failure without invalidation, and an uncompleted download
that cannot run the CAS. The test proves operation ordering in the standalone
queue and callback model, not cache-coherent native CPU reads. Native callers
would still need a real GPU-to-CPU download fence **and** arbitration against
concurrent write producers between the read and reservation, all fastmem/JIT
write paths, correct GPU scheduling, and title-lifetime joins. The developer
CMake source still does not invoke this helper and
`kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false`. No FC27 gameplay effect.

## Reserve-before-read and producer serialization model (2026-10-16)

The earlier `CommitConditionalAfterRead` synchronized CPU RAM before reserving
its FIFO ticket. Under saturation, the later reservation could drain queued GPU
invalidations after the read fence, leaving the CAS with stale data. Now an
unpublished CAS ticket is reserved first, and the blocking read callback receives
only its predecessor watermark (sequence minus one). It must never wait for the
CAS's own unpublished ticket. A failed read cancels that ticket without running
the atomic operation; a successful read proceeds to CAS and publish/cancel.

`GuestStoreOrderGate` provides one address-space-local mutex for participating
guest CPU writers, held through reservation, read synchronization, backing RAM
store, resolution and GPU wake. A threaded ASan/UBSan fixture proves a competing
producer cannot interleave with a conditional read; a full-queue fixture proves
pressure drain precedes the read, and the unpublished ticket stays excluded.
The GPU replay worker must never acquire the gate or recursively call it.
Complete native correctness additionally requires all guest/JIT/fastmem
producers and readers to participate, a true GPU-to-CPU device fence, and
safe session-lifetime joins. The developer CMake bridge does NOT use this
gate and remains disabled via `kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false`.

## Fatal GPU-to-CPU read-barrier errors (2026-10-16)

Prior to this host-only correction, an incomplete or throwing CPU read fence
was treated as a benign failed CAS comparison: the reserved ticket could be
cancelled and acknowledged while the title queue continued accepting writes.
But an uncompleted GPU download makes guest RAM coherence unknown. The
new `Queue::FailClosed()` immediately marks the session failed, notifies
blocked waiters and disallows subsequent reservations. It does not falsely
acknowledge a reserved write, replay invalidations, or schedule GPU work.
`CommitConditionalAfterRead` now uses it when the blocking read returns
`ReadBarrierResult::Failed` or throws (preserving the original exception).
A correctly completed read followed by a CAS mismatch STILL cancels normally
and does not poison the title. Host sanitizer regressions cover both fatal
read outcomes, lack of subsequent writes, failed waiter results, and a
quiescent close/reset. This changes only the inactive model, not FC27.

## Zero predecessor for the first conditional store (2026-10-16)

A first CAS reservation produces a generation-tagged predecessor watermark
of sequence zero. Ordinary `Queue::WaitUntil` correctly rejects such a ticket,
but using it as the conditional-read barrier would incorrectly reject a valid
first CAS. The host-only `Queue::WaitForPredecessors` now accepts a zero
predecessor ONLY when it belongs to the current generation with a live
reservation and a healthy, open session. It uses ordinary `WaitUntil` for
nonzero predecessors and preserves close/failure wakeup behavior. Host
sanitizer tests cover the first CAS, prior replay, stale/foreign generation,
fatal session, and reset. The caller remains responsible for scheduling GPU
replay and completing the actual GPU-to-CPU device transfer. The native
bridge stays off; no gameplay behavior changes.

## Native guest write coverage blockers — source inventory (2026-10-16)

The CI now runs `tools/check-deferred-native-access-coverage.py`.
Its `DEFERRED_NATIVE_ACCESS_COVERAGE_BLOCKED` result is explicitly a **NO-GO
check**, not a GPU functionality qualification. It pins the actual source
contracts preventing activation of PR #187:

| Path | Confirmed direct-access capability | Required before native enablement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dynarmic A64 and A32 | `config.page_table` / `absolute_offset_page_table` plus optional `config.fastmem_pointer` and fastmem exclusives; the JIT need not invoke `MemoryWrite*` for every store | Prove direct JIT store participation or a fully qualified callback/trap routing, including load and exclusive paths |
| Generic `GuestMemory` | `TrySetSpan()` exposes a direct writable span; scoped Safe/Cached destruction calls `InvalidateRegion` afterward instead of a `Memory::WriteBlock` transaction | Audit real instantiations, lifetime, direct writes, and their post-store notification ordering |
| NCE backend | A separate native execution and fault-handling mechanism exists, conditional on host platform | Determine build applicability; if used, qualify direct writes independently |
| CPU `memory.cpp` | Tracked `HandleRasterizerWrite` runs before RAM stores; conditional stores and cache-maintenance notifications have distinct outcomes | Wire `ReserveOrdered` before stores, GPU read fence before atomic access, `PublishAndWake` or `CancelAndWake` afterward |

Disabling `fastmem_pointer` alone is **not** evidence of complete coverage:
the Dynarmic page-table memory access mode remains. Forcing every JIT memory
access through callbacks would require a deliberately evaluated, probably
substantial performance compromise. A global guest producer mutex is
ineffective for JIT instructions which never acquire it, and cannot be
considered harmless in hot paths.

Keep the native gate `kNativePostStorePublicationReady=false`. The
CI contract deliberately fails if pinned source assumptions change, so
the inventory must be audited rather than silently considered qualified.
Do not ask for new console tests, rebuild a native release, or claim
the FC27 symptoms were fixed by this audit. The next meaningful task is a
concrete direct-store interception design, with a measurable host runtime
path and correct GPU-device fence semantics, not more queue-only microtests.

# R428 — selective upstream ProsperoEden v1.001.000 (d7f2764)

Upstream commit: https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/d7f2764f8ecf8bdbd979eece2b402621edceee2f (2026-10-13, 115 files changed).

## Integrated without modifying pinned source archives

1. **Boost ADL small-vector:** Eden's pinned `src/video_core/texture_cache/util.h` tests `BOOST_VERSION` without including `boost/version.hpp`. In some translation units the macro is undefined, selecting a heap-backed `std::vector` instead of `boost::container::small_vector` even with modern Boost. Generate a private `video_core` include override containing the missing include. No change to the upstream tarball. Upstream measured ~2,300 unnecessary allocations out of ~3,400 per frame in one game; **not measured on Encore yet**.
2. **ASTC array recompression:** Eden currently decodes every array layer in a mip level into one RGBA scratch buffer before BC1/BC3 recompression. Upstream demonstrated a case with 121 layers requiring ~484 MiB temporary CPU memory; split the same operation into layer-sized pieces. Preserve per-layer BC compressed output order and offsets and existing quality choice, without changing when textures are converted or switching compression modes.
3. **Logging write bursts:** The pinned Eden error backend flushes after every error (and with an explicit `Flush` or per-line logging). On PS5 a stream of guest invalid-memory reports can stall guest CPU cores due to synchronous storage IO. Generate a private `common/logging.cpp` overlay, preserving all emitted entries and explicit flush; during an error burst, flush no more often than every 100 ms unless the log limit is exceeded. **Tradeoff:** after an abrupt process termination, up to 100 ms of recent error lines may remain in the OS/file buffer. This path must be monitored in crash diagnostics.

All modifications use CMake configure-time substitutions with fail-closed pinned-source anchors. The existing source archive checks, PS5 native pipeline, launcher, profiles and per-game control mapping stay unchanged. `tools/check-upstream-texture-memory-r428.py` compiles a Boost/C++ host fixture and checks ASTC layout and the log-throttle boundary.

## Findings *not* automatically enabled

- **CPU physical core discovery by pair timing**: upstream `AdjacentCpusShareCore` is new evidence on firmware with invalid SMT CPUID. Our FW 13.60 code requires verified CPU masks; a timing-only SMT result could be affected by scheduling, frequency variation and sibling contention. Port as diagnostic before using it for affinity.
- **Guest clock adaptive slowdown (up to 15%)**: changes guest-perceived time and may reduce self-imposed 30→20 FPS switches without improving actual rendering throughput. It risks affecting game timers and determinism; requires explicit per-game A/B and must not be conflated with fewer stutters.
- **ASTC CPU asynchronous policy**: can avoid 130–290 ms first-use decode hitches but can temporarily display a missing/low-detail texture, hurting HUD/pitch fidelity. Keep existing Encore policy until qualified on FC27 and BOTW with warm/cold cache runs.
- **Yield-to-guests cache-lock arbitration**: upstream sleeps/spins up to 2 ms to hand off texture/buffer cache locks. Our guest/GPU mutex instrumentation differs and defaults to an upstream blocking path when detailed profiling is off. Merge only after deadlock and critical-section order review.
- **PS5 OpenGL SDK 1.0.2, theme Canopy, new launcher UI, runtime memory ABI**: different dependency and UI contracts; not suitable for a mechanical merge with Encore's already customized native renderer and neon-tropical interface.

## Validation gates

Core source regressions including R428 host fixture; all pinned dependency source digests unchanged; PS5 build required for actual CMake generation and linkage; only then a combined FC27/BOTW test. Neither the upstream FPS claims nor its memory measurements are presented as measured Encore results.

## CodeQL CI overload addressed in the same source-only release

After moving from GitHub default CodeQL to Advanced, `python` and `actions` analyses succeeded, but `c-cpp` `build-mode:none` was still extracting approximately **40,477 source files and 138,465 repository files**. A runner shutdown around 33 minutes into source extraction is **not** evidence of a C++ vulnerability or a passing scan.

R428 narrows **C/C++ no-build extraction** to Encore-owned `.github`, `headless`, `src`, `tools`, `third_party`, `fixtures`, plus the **active** renderer forks under `vendor/encore-active`. Pinned source archives `vendor/sources` and archived objects are preserved, but deliberately outside static analysis of maintained compilation units. This matches GitHub's officially supported `paths` setting for `build-mode:none` and makes the intended partial scope explicit; it does not claim a security audit of third-party archive contents. The R419 five unused-vendor-test-script exclusions remain documented as defense in depth. The code-scanning workflow must successfully upload C/C++ SARIF before closing the prior CI incident.

## Qualification native R432

The source-only preflight for final R428/R431 passed (GitHub Actions 38381027494). CodeQL's first restricted active-source scan passed (38380526647). Initiate one native PS5 All-On build with the integrated Boost small-vector, per-layer ASTC, and error-flush coalescing overlays, without touching the game caches or renderer profile. A successful native build establishes link/package correctness, not FC27 frame-time improvement.

# Eden Encore — audit des vendors du 12 octobre 2026

**Intégration sur une seule branche : `dev/ps5-sparse-jit`.** Les correctifs upstream ne sont pas automatiquement compatibles avec nos forks Vulkan, RADV et nos 83 backports : aucun SHA vendor n'est modifié dans cet audit.

## Sources et versions

| Composant | SHA actuellement figé dans `tools/deps.json` | `main` / `master` contrôlé | Différence Git |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Eden officiel](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror) | `5f142c7926d0` | `9580e54f2f47` | +80 commits |
| [PS5_Vulkan](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan) | `3f3ee6960701` | `252bf912a745` | +18 commits |
| [PS5_Mesa](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa) | `0b2d6d1a61d9` | `47e9eb61ee7e` | **divergent : +110/−103 commits**, 110 fichiers changés |
| [PS5 native boilerplate](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate) | `dd44bbdc7543` | `b8dc4a3fe2e0` | +43 commits |
| [Encore overrides](https://github.com/niakw/encore-overrides) | `4fdb329e732a` | `4fdb329e732a` | à jour |

ProsperoEden upstream n'est pas lui-même le pin du moteur de base : les sources compilées sont dérivées de `eden-emulator/mirror`, puis de nos modifications complètes vendorizées. Ne pas assimiler les arbres ni appliquer un `git pull` général.

## Correctifs à examiner en priorité

**P0 — Fidélité GPU, textures/HUD.** [Eden #4473/#4477](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror/commit/dbeb73ee01) sont **déjà intégrés** à Encore dans `headless/backports/eden-4473-4477.patch` et les fichiers complets de `vendor/encore-active/eden-backports` (vérifié le 12/10). Pas de nouveau port ni de correction de textures à leur attribuer. [Eden #4499](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror/commit/6352612425) **absent de notre fork avant R392** : R392 supprime strictement l'actualisation des buffers dans `FlushEndTFB()` mais la conserve dans `FlushBeginTFB()`. Vérifier le rendu sur console, sans gain FC27 présumé.

**P0 — HID/état des applets.** [Eden #4442](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror/commit/07f40d5cac) était **déjà intégré aux backports actifs** : le compteur Npad est lu dans `.state`, les notifications/focus des applets et le stub HID ont été portés. Il faut instrumenter le dernier maillon de publication Npad de notre nouveau mapping HOME/Capture R390, pas réappliquer #4442. Le freeze actif de FC27 ne lui est pas attribué.

**P1 — Saccades de collecte des textures.** [ProsperoEden 002c40c](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/002c40cb794c) précharge aussi les images mises à l'échelle avant leur éviction, avec des lots de 64 images/64 Mio plutôt que des attentes GPU par image. Notre `headless/vulkan_gc_downloads.inc` a déjà un préchargement 40 images/32 Mio, **mais exclut explicitement `image.HasScaled()`** : écart confirmé. Un port ciblé est pertinent, mais exige une vérification de la copie scaled→guest, durée de vie des staging buffers et budget RAM unifiée; ne pas élargir la limite sans qualification.

**P1 — Diagnostiquer le gel de simulation.** [ProsperoEden b59cef8](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/b59cef86fd85) mesure le délai entre réveil et reprise réelle des threads invités; [6cab789](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/6cab7898c05d) identifie le thread dans `SendSyncRequest`; [8b35097](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/8b350979303c) échantillonne ses appelants. À importer uniquement en diagnostic borné, pour distinguer boucle guest/condition variable/attente IPC sans se fonder seulement sur les FPS.

**P1 — CPU/JIT.** [ProsperoEden 376f75c](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/376f75c9dc45) préserve les accès exclusifs inlinés en mode Unsafe/Faster CPU alors que le pointeur fastmem est désactivé. Gain rapporté par upstream sur Pokémon Violet, **non transférable directement à FC27** : vérifier le mode CPU réellement utilisé et les chemins A32/A64 avant port.

**P1 — Réduire le coût de profilage.** [ProsperoEden 2e59218](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/2e59218ae21b) réserve les mesures de phases par draw aux builds de développement. À comparer aux sondes R377 et R382 déjà corrigées pour éviter d'ajouter des coûts par draw dans les builds normaux.

## Changements à ne pas importer aveuglément

- [PS5_Mesa 47e9eb6](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Mesa/commit/47e9eb61ee7e1112194557e1e047178562827bc6) et [PS5_Vulkan 252bf91](https://github.com/mihawk-99/PS5_Vulkan/commit/252bf912a745e3566a93b69b098bdc8ec4048837) rendent la détection du mode 119,88 Hz fidèle à la négociation réelle et au vblank. C'est utile pour un affichage 120 Hz compatible, **pas un déverrouillage du FPS de FC27 ni une solution automatique aux saccades à 30 FPS**. Notre PS5_Mesa diverge lourdement; pas de repin global.
- [Boilerplate b8dc4a3](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ps5-native-app-boilerplate/commit/b8dc4a3fe2e05e826b037bd68824751c7468a6d7) corrige la durée de vie du helper Lapy optionnel (SDK v0.42), hors chemin de rendu. À regarder si Eden utilise ce helper, pas comme correctif du match.
- [ProsperoEden 487fa34](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/487fa348265bf05e3eabc5f659efd3ba71787336) apporte la configuration de graine RNG par jeu et sa validation ; fonctionnelle, mais sans rapport direct avec FC27.
- [Eden c95ad02](https://github.com/eden-emulator/mirror/commit/c95ad020fb) corrige un hang de thread GPU **au shutdown/reset**. Ne pas confondre avec R384, où le GPU continue de rendre pendant la séquence répétitive.

## Contrat d'intégration

1. Rester exclusivement sur `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` ; commits atomiques, sans branche de travail.
2. Comparer chacun de ces correctifs avec le pinned `vendor/sources/eden`, les 83 fichiers backport et le fork `vendor/encore-active` effectivement compilé.
3. Ne modifier ni `tools/deps.json` ni l'archive immuable de vendor tant qu'un port ne reproduit pas ses tests source et ses signatures.
4. Ajouter tests hôte, équivalence générateur/fork et métriques de logs avant **un seul** build/test PS5 combiné.
5. Ne pas attribuer à un commit upstream la résolution des freezes, textures ou saccades sans essai console.

Cet audit ne lance pas de compilation PS5 et ne change aucun pin.

```

`docs/VENDOR_SUBMODULE_MIGRATION.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore — pinned vendor submodule

The directory `vendor/` remains at the same relative path as before, and is the **sole Git submodule**, pinned to `niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore-vendor`. MihawkGen, FSR3 Optical Flow and libwebp are now regular, unchanged upstream source trees under `vendor/sources/` (specifically `ps5-mihawkgen/`, `ps5-fsr3-optical-flow/` and `libwebp/`). **Strict policy: `vendor/sources/` contains original third-party snapshots, whereas `vendor/encore-active/` is exclusively for Encore-maintained ports, patches and runtime overrides. No unmodified upstream dependency belongs in `encore-active/`.** Their exact byte-for-byte upstream tree hashes are checked by `tools/graphics/check-internalized-ps5-deps.py`; original revision identities are recorded in `vendor/docs/PS5_INTERNAL_DEPENDENCY_ORIGINS_2026-11-10.md`. This work was deliberately performed on isolated branches to protect parallel P1/P2 development.

## Clone and checkout

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore.git
# Or, in an existing working copy:
git submodule sync --recursive
git submodule update --init --recursive vendor
git submodule status vendor
```

All build and validation workflows initialize the pinned submodule. When the gitlink changes, parent-repository Git diffs report **`vendor`**, not `vendor/encore-active/**`; workflow path filters must therefore include `vendor` and `.gitmodules`.

## Update procedure

The submodule is locked to an immutable commit. Commit vendor changes in `niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore-vendor`, then commit the updated `vendor` gitlink in Encore and rerun preflight/build checks. Active F07 edits under `vendor/encore-active/**` now require a coordinated vendor commit and parent gitlink bump. Keep the exact dependency licenses and source hashes.

## Storage limitation

This reduces the current parent working-tree content but **does not remove old vendor blobs from the parent repository's Git history**. A decrease in GitHub's reported repository storage or full-history clone size needs separate history cleanup, which must not be performed during ongoing F07 optimizations. Prefer shallow/partial clones where suitable.

The initial vendor repository import is required to pass an exact Git tree hash comparison before the parent gitlink is activated. A successful checkout and build/preflight checks are required before merging this branch.

```

`docs/VENDOR_TRANSLATIONS_UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md`:

```md
# Native build recovery, vendored sources and upstream assessment

Audit of `dev/ps5-sparse-jit` — 14 October 2026.

## Red native build: actual cause and repair

The build [38478857146/job/115576208233](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38478857146/job/115576208233) failed in the **pre-build source/host gate**, not in the compiler. Both that job and its independent Linux source preflight rejected a mismatch in exactly one tracked file:

`vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan/vulkan_swapchain.cpp`

The generator/oracle `tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py` had been updated for native bounded image acquisition, obsolete-swapchain handling and deferred suboptimal-image recreation, but the *compiled, versioned* Vulkan fork had not been updated. The failure was **correctly caught** by `tools/check-vendored-vulkan-fork.py`. The three changes were applied verbatim to the tracked active C++ source; that exact-equivalence check remains mandatory, never bypassed. A subsequent native compilation is required before declaring a usable console build. No attempt has been made to relabel this historical red job as a successful build.

## What is actually vendored — and what is not yet consolidated

`vendor/sources/` contains all currently declared production dependency snapshots from `tools/deps.json`, including source snapshots, complete native toolchain object chunks and all pinned active CPM inputs for the current platform. `vendor/objects/` preserves archives and SDK binaries. This answers **source availability**, not **build integration**. The source trees include the exact original copyright/licenses and are not modified when applying Encore-specific patches.

The five maintained native forks are in `vendor/encore-active/`: `eden-backports`, `eden-gpu`, `eden-surface-lifecycle`, `eden-vulkan`, `ps5-mesa`. The active Vulkan fork is already compiled directly: `headless/vulkan.cmake` performs `file(COPY ... vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan ...)` and the old Python port adapter runs as an **equivalence oracle only**. Its CMake integration file under `headless/` is not evidence of a missing Vulkan source snapshot.

**The consolidation is nevertheless incomplete.** As of this audit, `headless/CMakeLists.txt` still contains **87 occurrences of `write_derived(`**, **98 of `file(READ`**, and **235 of `string(REPLACE`** (counts include support code and non-source rewrites; they are *not* 235 independent fixes). Native Core/HLE, JIT/memory, parts of the guest GPU stack and selected OpenGL code still use derived/overridden sources under `headless/`. This was explicitly recognized in `vendor/README.md`; it should never have been described as a *completed* active-source migration.

`tools/check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py` now checks that every `tools/deps.json` production source is still preserved and prevents increases in the above CMake rewrite counts, while `check-vendored-vulkan-fork.py` enforces byte-for-byte generation consistency. **These are regression gates, not an artificial "vendor migration complete" certificate.** The next migration should convert the remaining derived units to complete, maintained C++ translation units under `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/` with exact-source parity tests; transition each target one by one with a native compile gate. Do not delete source provenance, licenses, or user profile/override databases in this process.

Source inventory is distinct from a *universal* air-gapped build of all optional targets: `vendor/README.md` explicitly records 22 used PS5 CPM packages out of 42 possible cross-platform package declarations. The 20 other possibilities are not proof that a current PS5 production dependency is missing.

## Translation warnings: changed, not hidden

The historical build displayed **336 individual `warning: untranslated` lines** due to per-catalog truncation, while its per-catalog totals sum to roughly **5,982 warnings** across 29 catalogs. These include genuinely untranslated terms, obsolete entries and excessively long translations; 336 was never the full missing-translation count.

- Fully maintained **fr-FR**: eight overlong UI labels shortened, three stale translations deleted, and embedded French synchronized byte-for-byte.
- **fr-CA**: preserve existing local translations, fill missing current keys with maintained French rather than English, remove 62 obsolete entries, and shorten three overlong translations. Both French locales now target **zero missing keys and zero warnings**, enforced directly by `tools/launcher/strings.py check`.
- Other 27 catalogs: remove **61 obsolete source IDs each** (1,647 entries) rather than suppressing warnings. Already translated localized entries remain untouched. Their remaining missing strings are **genuine incomplete localization work**, not build errors we may silently conceal. Never assign fake English `msgstr` values to pass a coverage metric.
- `tools/check-launcher-translation-coverage.py` is a new audited CI inventory: it fails on obsolete entries, enforces exact coverage in both French locales, and fails if any other locale loses existing coverage. The count of remaining untranslated strings is visible in CI.

## Upstream [9ce26e65](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/commit/9ce26e650e26112d958f6db4b20d93260de77825)

The commit “More free memory for demanding games (#156)” spans nine files. It implements several **different** mechanisms: page-on-demand guest memory backing, commit hooks for growing JIT code arenas, changes to x86 alias allocation, a reduced `flexibleMemorySize` request (320 MiB rather than the usual 448 MiB), and improved reporting of PS5 Pro direct-memory mode. Its objective is memory headroom/avoiding OOM rather than 30-FPS animation pacing.

**Do not cherry-pick all nine files blindly.** Encore already has separately qualified sparse JIT virtual ranges, source-derived x86 alias behavior and memory-allocation fallbacks; the upstream allocator rewrite intersects these guarantees. A 128 MiB shift from the flexible pool into direct memory may improve some content but also reduces the space available to the title/system libraries and cannot be assumed safe for the existing emulator/renderer/launcher. The upstream's “PS5 Pro” detection/reporting should not be conflated with memory available on a base console. Compare the guest-memory backing and flexible-pool requirements independently against our own allocation telemetry and existing fail-closed lifetime tests before integrating them. **Potentially worth adapting for memory pressure, not currently a justified fix for the reported stable-30-FPS judder.**

## Upstream [issue #97](https://github.com/blackbearreloaded/ProsperoEden/issues/97)

The open report describes an app freeze **after returning from console rest mode**, on **firmware 11.60** with a particular homebrew environment. It contains **no debug log or hardware trace**. That is a plausible Vulkan surface/swapchain lifecycle hazard and is relevant to a dedicated suspend/resume recovery test, but it is **not a reproduction of our firmware 13.60 game-session freeze while actively playing**. In particular, no rest/resume event was reported in the recorded FC27 28-minute GPU-stall trace. Treat these as separate failure classes until a common call site is proven; do not add generic forced restarts or timeouts to normal gameplay merely to make an unrelated suspend issue disappear.

## Validation gates

1. Re-run `tools/check-vendored-vulkan-fork.py` and `tools/check-ps5-native-acquire-failfast.py` in Linux source preflight, then compile the active fork in the native All-On build; block packaging if any check fails.
2. Run `tools/launcher/strings.py check` and `tools/check-launcher-translation-coverage.py` before source compilation. The two French locales must have no missing or obsolete translation and no overlong labels.
3. Run `tools/check-vendor-consolidation-debt.py` and existing vendor-source/binary/archive integrity checks; do not claim completion while generated source rewrites remain.
4. The original stable-30-FPS gameplay lag, title action mapping and sustained GPU freeze remain separate **open runtime defects**; successful host tests do not prove their resolution on hardware.

Validation request: re-run source preflight, warning-free maintained French checks, vendored fork exact-equivalence gate and one native All-On compile from the same head; no release/publish requested. The non-French translation coverage work and remaining derived-source migration are explicitly still open.


## Kernel header consistency follow-up (14 October 2026)

The paired native scheduler lock overlay now owns the slab header AND the
existing object-destruction guard in one maintained source. The old CMake
generated slab-header clone has been removed, preventing inconsistent header
layouts between core and the libraries that consume its public ABI. The JIT
CPU diagnostic is corrected to use the actual ArmDynarmic class member
m_system, rather than nonexistent m_parent, based on the failed native build
run 38495903010. This is source qualification until a new native build passes.
The remaining CMake rewrite count is still **not zero**.


## Locale completion (14 October 2026)

All 29 currently supported locale catalogs now contain 376 / 376 active
msgids each: **zero missing translations**, 2,775 previously empty entries
filled across 25 non-primary locales. The existing translations were not
replaced. Initial drafts for 23 languages came from machine assistance;
the remaining two Chinese variants used an original simplified translation
with the traditional variant converted by an offline OpenCC s2tw pass.
The tool checks all substitutions, forbids stale ids and verifies the
supported font glyphs where available, but **human linguistic proofreading,
truncation checks and physical system-font verification remain outstanding**.
These translations are not synthetic copies of the English msgid and must
not be represented as native-speaker certified. The new source coverage
gate fails if any supported locale loses a translation.

## Additional native CMake migration (14 October 2026)

Pinned-source-equivalent copies of the code loader and bounded error logger now live under `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src`. Their generated CMake translation units have been replaced by maintained sources, and a source-parity regression gate checks both against their exact pinned transformations. The count is now **79 write_derived**, **89 file(READ** and **227 string(REPLACE** occurrences. Migration is incomplete, and native compilation on the new commit remains to be verified.

## Maintained audio units (14 October 2026)

The pinned native audio sink-selection unit and renderer voice-flag unit are now
versioned under `vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src`. Exact source-parity
checks ensure the native sink factory and SRC bit position keep their former
behaviour. The buffer-stream generation is **not** migrated or modified.
CMake generation debt is now **77 write_derived**, **87 file(READ**, and
**225 string(REPLACE** calls. This is source-only validation pending a fresh
native compile and is not a correction of the FC27 end-match freeze.

# R09 — before/after pixels from real Vulkan GPU readback
November 7, 2026.

**These are NOT screenshots of a game, DLSS Super Resolution output,

# Eden Encore — Προσβασιμότητα · Ελληνικά

[Επισκόπηση](README.el-GR.md) · [Εγκατάσταση και ενημέρωση](INSTALL.el-GR.md) · [Ρυθμίσεις](SETTINGS.el-GR.md) · [Αντιμετώπιση προβλημάτων](TROUBLESHOOTING.el-GR.md) · [Υποστήριξη](SUPPORT.el-GR.md) · [Προσβασιμότητα](ACCESSIBILITY.el-GR.md) · [🌐](../../LANGUAGES.md)

Το μεγαλύτερο κείμενο, η υψηλή αντίθεση και η μειωμένη κίνηση ενεργοποιούνται ανεξάρτητα στις ρυθμίσεις προσβασιμότητας και είναι απενεργοποιημένα από προεπιλογή. Η πλοήγηση του μενού δεν εγγυάται προσβασιμότητα κάθε παιχνιδιού.

## Ρυθμίσεις · Touchpad

Ένα σύντομο πάτημα στο Touchpad ανοίγει τις γρήγορες ρυθμίσεις του Encore μέσα στο παιχνίδι. Το κεντρικό πλήκτρο συστήματος παραμένει δεσμευμένο για την κονσόλα. Εκεί βρίσκονται γραφικά, αντιστοίχιση πλήκτρων, FPS και διαγνωστικά. Κάποιες αλλαγές απαιτούν επανεκκίνηση του παιχνιδιού. Η γλώσσα επιλέγεται από Settings → Language. Το μενού περιλαμβάνει ακριβώς τις 31 επίσημες επιλογές γλώσσας συστήματος PS5.

`L1/R1` · `Settings → Accessibility` · `Settings → Controls`

## Ρυθμίσεις

Οι προτεινόμενες αρχικές ρυθμίσεις είναι Vulkan, έξοδος 1440p, εσωτερική ανάλυση 1.25x, FSR 1 με ευκρίνεια 50%, FXAA και 60 Hz. Η έξοδος της τηλεόρασης διαφέρει από την εσωτερική ανάλυση του παιχνιδιού. Η δημιουργία καρέ δεν επιταχύνει την ίδια την προσομοίωση.

## Υποστήριξη

Στην αναφορά σφάλματος αναφέρετε έκδοση Encore, firmware PS5, ακριβή βήματα, σχετικές ρυθμίσεις και καθαρισμένα αρχεία καταγραφής. Χρησιμοποιήστε GitHub Issues· μη δημοσιεύετε κλειδιά ή προσωπικά δεδομένα.

Μη διαγράφετε το /data/prosperoeden/: μπορεί να περιέχει αποθηκεύσεις, ρυθμίσεις και κλειδιά. Κρατήστε αντίγραφο και της εξωτερικής αποθήκευσης.

---

Η τελευταία δημόσια μεταγλώττιση PS5 έγινε στις 15 Οκτωβρίου 2026. Η έκδοση της 30ής Οκτωβρίου ήταν αντίγραφο. Το νέο προσχέδιο δεν περιέχει εκτελέσιμα αρχεία ούτε επαληθευμένη συμβατότητα δεύτερης γενιάς.

# Prospero.Eden Encore — Accessibility (English UK)

[All 31 PS5 language choices](../../LANGUAGES.md) · [English US complete reference](../../ACCESSIBILITY.md) · [PS5 language policy](../PS5_SYSTEM_LANGUAGE_POLICY.md)

The launcher documents larger text, high contrast, reduced motion and TV navigation. Move with the DualSense D-pad, choose with Cross and go back with Circle. Per-game and global controller mappings can be customised, but the PS button remains the PS5 system's reserved control.

A short touchpad click opens the native Vulkan quick overlay with graphics, button mapping, FPS, diagnostic switches and a Multiplayer shortcut. This shortcut does not embed another real-time lobby: it requires a second confirmation and then **ends the game** before opening the original room browser. The launcher provides exactly 31 PS5 language catalogues, including separate British and American English; complex-script legibility needs PS5 device validation.

[Full accessibility reference](../../ACCESSIBILITY.md) · [Overlay behaviour](../PS5_TOUCHPAD_QUICK_OVERLAY.md)

> **Safety and qualification:** The last public native PS5 build dates from 15 October 2026. Later source changes are not necessarily released or hardware-tested. Keep your original data and lawful game files. These British English guides add useful regional guidance without claiming professional human QA for all source strings.

# Eden Encore — Accesibilidad · Español (Latinoamérica)

大きい文字、高コントラスト、動きの軽減はアクセシビリティ設定で個別に有効にできます。初期状態はすべてオフです。ランチャーで操作できることは、すべてのゲームのアクセシビリティを保証しません。

## 設定 · Touchpad

ゲーム中に Touchpad を短く押すと Encore のクイック設定を開けます。中央のシステムボタンは本体専用で、このメニューには使用しません。グラフィック、ボタン割り当て、FPS、診断情報を確認できます。変更内容によってはゲームの再起動が必要です。言語は Settings → Language で選択できます。メニューにはPS5の公式システム言語31項目のみが表示されます。

`L1/R1` · `Settings → Accessibility` · `Settings → Controls`

## 設定

推奨初期設定は Vulkan、テレビ出力 1440p、ゲーム内部倍率 1.25x、空間アップスケーリング FSR 1（シャープネス 50%）、FXAA、60 Hz です。テレビへの出力解像度とゲーム内部解像度は別です。フレーム生成はゲームの処理速度そのものを上げません。

## サポート

GitHub Issues には Encore のバージョン、PS5 ファームウェア、再現手順、関連する設定、個人情報を取り除いたログを記載してください。鍵、セーブデータ、個人情報は公開しないでください。

/data/prosperoeden/ を削除しないでください。設定、セーブデータ、鍵が保存されている可能性があります。外部ストレージもバックアップしてください。

---

実際にコンパイルされた最後の公開 PS5 パッケージは 2026 年 10 月 15 日版です。10 月 30 日の公開は同じパッケージの複製です。新しいプレリリースの下書きには実行バイナリも第二世代ゲームの実機動作保証もありません。

# Eden Encore — 접근성 · 한국어

큰 글씨, 높은 대비, 움직임 줄이기 옵션은 접근성 메뉴에서 각각 켤 수 있으며 기본적으로 모두 꺼져 있습니다. 런처의 접근성이 모든 게임 내부의 접근성을 보장하지는 않습니다.

## 설정 · Touchpad

게임 중 Touchpad를 짧게 누르면 Encore 빠른 설정 메뉴가 열립니다. 중앙 시스템 버튼은 콘솔 전용입니다. 그래픽, 버튼 매핑, FPS, 진단 정보를 이 메뉴에서 확인할 수 있습니다. 일부 설정 변경은 게임을 다시 시작해야 적용됩니다. 언어는 Settings → Language에서 선택합니다. 메뉴에는 PS5 공식 시스템 언어 31개 항목만 표시됩니다.

/data/prosperoeden/ 폴더를 삭제하지 마세요. 설정, 저장 데이터, 키가 들어 있을 수 있습니다. 외부 저장소도 백업하세요.

# Eden Encore — การช่วยการเข้าถึง · ไทย

[ภาพรวม](README.th.md) · [การติดตั้งและอัปเดต](INSTALL.th.md) · [การตั้งค่า](SETTINGS.th-TH.md) · [แก้ไขปัญหา](TROUBLESHOOTING.th-TH.md) · [การสนับสนุน](SUPPORT.th-TH.md) · [การช่วยการเข้าถึง](ACCESSIBILITY.th-TH.md) · [🌐](../../LANGUAGES.md)

สามารถเปิดข้อความขนาดใหญ่ คอนทราสต์สูง และลดการเคลื่อนไหวแยกกันในเมนูการช่วยการเข้าถึง โดยค่าเริ่มต้นปิดทั้งหมด การใช้หน้าตาแอปได้ไม่ได้หมายความว่าเกมทุกเกมเข้าถึงได้

## การตั้งค่า · Touchpad

แตะ Touchpad สั้น ๆ เพื่อเปิดการตั้งค่าด่วนของ Encore ระหว่างเล่นเกม ปุ่มระบบตรงกลางสงวนไว้สำหรับคอนโซล เมนูนี้มีกราฟิก การกำหนดปุ่ม FPS และการวินิจฉัย การเปลี่ยนบางอย่างต้องเริ่มเกมใหม่ เลือกภาษาได้ใน Settings → Language เมนูมีเฉพาะ 31 ตัวเลือกภาษาระบบ PS5 อย่างเป็นทางการ

`L1/R1` · `Settings → Accessibility` · `Settings → Controls`

## การตั้งค่า

ค่าเริ่มต้นที่แนะนำคือ Vulkan, เอาต์พุตทีวี 1440p, ความละเอียดเกมภายใน 1.25x, FSR 1 แบบเชิงพื้นที่ ความคมชัด 50%, FXAA และ 60 Hz ความละเอียดทีวีกับความละเอียดที่เกมเรนเดอร์เป็นคนละค่า การสร้างเฟรมไม่ได้ทำให้การจำลองเกมเร็วขึ้น

## การสนับสนุน

ห้ามลบ /data/prosperoeden/ เพราะอาจมีเซฟ การตั้งค่า และคีย์ ควรสำรองพื้นที่จัดเก็บภายนอกด้วย

# Eden Encore — Доступність · Українська

## Налаштування · Touchpad

Коротке натискання Touchpad відкриває швидкі налаштування Encore під час гри. Центральна системна кнопка залишається за консоллю. У меню доступні графіка, призначення кнопок, FPS і діагностика. Для деяких змін потрібен перезапуск гри. Мову можна вибрати в Settings → Language. У меню є рівно 31 офіційний варіант системної мови PS5.

`L1/R1` · `Settings → Accessibility` · `Settings → Controls`

## Налаштування

Рекомендований профіль: Vulkan, виведення на телевізор 1440p, внутрішній масштаб гри 1.25x, просторовий FSR 1 із різкістю 50%, FXAA та 60 Hz. Роздільна здатність ТВ відрізняється від внутрішнього рендерингу гри. Генерація кадрів не прискорює симуляцію гри.

## Підтримка

У GitHub Issues зазначте версію Encore, прошивку PS5, послідовність дій, потрібні налаштування та очищені від приватних даних журнали. Не публікуйте ключі, збереження чи особисті відомості.

Ніколи не видаляйте /data/prosperoeden/: там можуть зберігатися ігри, налаштування та ключі. Резервуйте також зовнішнє сховище.

# Eden Encore — 无障碍 · 简体中文

放大文字、高对比度、减少动态效果可在无障碍设置中分别开启，默认全部关闭。启动器可用并不代表每款游戏内部都具备无障碍功能。

## 设置 · Touchpad

游戏中短按 Touchpad 可打开 Encore 快速设置；中央系统按钮保留给主机使用。该菜单包含图形设置、按键映射、FPS 和诊断信息。部分修改需要重启游戏。语言可在 Settings → Language 中选择。菜单仅提供 PS5 官方的 31 项系统语言选项。

`L1/R1` · `Settings → Accessibility` · `Settings → Controls`

## 设置

推荐初始配置为 Vulkan、1440p 电视输出、1.25x 游戏内部渲染倍率、空间 FSR 1（锐度 50%）、FXAA 和 60 Hz。电视输出分辨率与游戏内部渲染分辨率不同。帧生成并不会提高游戏的实际模拟速度。

## 支持

# Eden Encore — التثبيت والتحديث · العربية

[نظرة عامة](README.ar.md) · [التثبيت والتحديث](INSTALL.ar.md) · [الإعدادات](SETTINGS.ar.md) · [حل المشكلات](TROUBLESHOOTING.ar.md) · [الدعم](SUPPORT.ar.md) · [إمكانية الوصول](ACCESSIBILITY.ar.md) · [🌐](../../LANGUAGES.md)

نزّل آخر حزمة منشورة بالفعل من صفحة الإصدارات، ثم احتفظ بنسخة احتياطية من التطبيق والبيانات. في تثبيت ZIP/FTP انسخ مجلد PPSA99008 كاملاً إلى /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/. لا تخلط هذه الطريقة مع FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus، وتحقق من بصمة SHA-256 عند توفيرها.

## ZIP / FTP

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/eboot.bin
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/sce_sys/
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/ui/lang/
```

لا تحذف /data/prosperoeden/؛ فقد يحتوي إعداداتك وملفات الحفظ والمفاتيح. احتفظ بنسخة من بيانات التخزين الخارجي أيضاً.

## FFPFSC / ShadowMountPlus

نزّل آخر حزمة منشورة بالفعل من صفحة الإصدارات، ثم احتفظ بنسخة احتياطية من التطبيق والبيانات. في تثبيت ZIP/FTP انسخ مجلد PPSA99008 كاملاً إلى /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/. لا تخلط هذه الطريقة مع FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus، وتحقق من بصمة SHA-256 عند توفيرها.

[FFPFSC / ShadowMountPlus — English reference](../../INSTALL.md#method-2--ffpfsc-with-shadowmountplus)

## الإعدادات

تبدأ الإعدادات الموصى بها بمحرك Vulkan ودقة إخراج 1440p ومقياس لعب 1.25x وFSR 1 بحدة 50% وFXAA وتحديث 60 Hz. يختلف إخراج التلفاز عن دقة اللعبة الداخلية. لا تفترض أن تحسين الصورة أو توليد الإطارات يزيد سرعة محاكاة اللعبة.

## حل المشكلات

إذا لم يبدأ التطبيق، تحقق من وجود eboot.bin وsce_sys وui/lang في المجلد الصحيح. إذا اختفت الألعاب، تحقق من مجلد roms تحت جذر التخزين المحدد. إذا بقيت اللغة الإنجليزية، تحقق من ملفات الترجمة. استخدم التشغيل الآمن لإعادة ضبط إعدادات لعبة واحدة دون حذف الحفظ.

## الدعم

عند الإبلاغ عن مشكلة، أرفق رقم إصدار Encore ونسخة النظام والخطوات اللازمة لإعادة المشكلة والإعدادات والسجلات المنقحة. استخدم صفحة Issues الرسمية ولا تنشر مفاتيح أو ملفات حفظ أو بيانات شخصية.

---

آخر إصدار PS5 مُجمّع علناً يعود إلى 15 أكتوبر 2026؛ إصدار 30 أكتوبر مجرد نسخة من الحزمة نفسها. لا تتضمن المسودة الجديدة ملفات تشغيل، ولم يُتحقق بعد من ألعاب الجيل الثاني على الجهاز.

[English — complete installation and migration](../../INSTALL.md) · [R1 — October 15, 2026](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953)

/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/ui/lang/
```

Nikdy nemažte /data/prosperoeden/: může obsahovat nastavení, uložené hry a vaše klíče. Zálohujte i případné externí úložiště.

## FFPFSC / ShadowMountPlus

Stáhněte skutečně vydaný balíček ze stránky Releases a nejdříve zazálohujte aplikaci i data. Při instalaci ZIP/FTP zkopírujte celý adresář PPSA99008 do /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/. Nemíchejte ZIP/FTP s FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus a případně ověřte kontrolní součet SHA-256.

[FFPFSC / ShadowMountPlus — English reference](../../INSTALL.md#method-2--ffpfsc-with-shadowmountplus)

## Nastavení

Doporučené výchozí nastavení používá Vulkan, výstup 1440p, interní měřítko 1.25x, prostorové FSR 1 s ostrostí 50 %, FXAA a 60 Hz. Rozlišení televizního výstupu a vykreslovací rozlišení hry jsou rozdílné. Generování snímků nemění rychlost emulované hry.

## Řešení problémů

Pokud aplikace nenaběhne, ověřte eboot.bin, sce_sys a ui/lang ve správné složce. Chybějící hry hledejte v roms pod vybraným úložištěm. Pokud nabídky zůstávají anglické, zkontrolujte soubory překladů. Safe Launch obnoví nastavení problematické hry bez smazání uložených pozic.

## Podpora

Při hlášení chyby uveďte verzi Encore, firmware PS5, přesný postup, příslušná nastavení a anonymizované logy. Využijte oficiální GitHub Issues; nikdy nezveřejňujte klíče, soukromé soubory ani uložené hry.

---

Poslední veřejně sestavený balíček PS5 pochází z 15. října 2026. Vydání z 30. října je jeho kopie. Nový koncept vydání neobsahuje binární soubory ani ověřenou podporu her druhé generace na konzoli.

# Prospero.Eden Encore — Wechsel vom Originalprojekt (Deutsch)

[← Deutsch](README.de.md) · [Vollständige Installationsanleitung (Englisch)](../../INSTALL.md) · [Alle Sprachen](../../LANGUAGES.md)

## Schnellstart

1. Lade das vollständige Paket aus den Encore Releases und prüfe die Prüfsumme.
2. Sichere PPSA99008, die Daten unter /data/prosperoeden und externe Laufwerke.
3. Kopiere den gesamten Ordner PPSA99008 nach /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/; nur eboot.bin reicht nicht.
4. Starte Encore, prüfe Settings → Storage und Language und verwende nur rechtmäßig erworbene Dateien.

## Anwendung / PPSA99008

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/         # complete application
/data/prosperoeden/               # persistent user files
/data/prosperoeden/keys/          # legally obtained keys
/data/prosperoeden/firmware/      # compatible firmware files
/data/prosperoeden/roms/          # games
/data/prosperoeden/updates/       # game updates
/data/prosperoeden/config/        # settings
/data/prosperoeden/logs/          # diagnostics
```

## Wechsel vom Originalprojekt

Encore und das ursprüngliche ProsperoEden nutzen dieselbe App-ID PPSA99008 und sind keine unabhängigen Installationen. Ersetze die vollständigen Anwendungsdateien, aber behalte Spielstände, Schlüssel, Einstellungen und Spiele unter /data/prosperoeden. Sichere einen alten assets/-Ordner vor der Migration.

**Wichtig:** Lösche beim Aktualisieren niemals `/data/prosperoeden/` und formatiere keine externen Laufwerke. Erstelle zuerst ein Backup und überschreibe keine Spielstände oder Schlüssel.

## Kompatibilität und Grenzen

Nur PS5-Firmware 13.60 wurde mit Encore auf einer echten Konsole getestet. Ältere Versionen könnten funktionieren, sind aber nicht bestätigt; eine Mindestversion ist nicht bekannt. Einige Spiele ruckeln weiterhin, zeigen verzögerte HUD-Grafik, fehlerhafte Tasten oder Hänger beim Pausieren. Eine grüne CI ist kein Spieltest.

## Häufige Fragen

Bleibt das Menü englisch, wähle Settings → Language und überprüfe den gesamten Ordner ui/lang/.

Startet ein Titel nach einer Einstellungsänderung nicht mehr, nutze **Safe Launch** für diese Sitzung, ohne Spielstände zu löschen. Weitere Informationen: [ZIP/FFPFSC-Installation](../../INSTALL.md), [Fehlerbehebung](../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md), [Support](../../SUPPORT.md).

Encore verteilt keine Spiele, Schlüssel oder Firmware. Keine privaten Daten in öffentlichen Fehlerberichten teilen.

# Prospero.Eden Encore — Migrar desde el proyecto original (Español (Latinoamérica))

[← Español (Latinoamérica)](README.es-419.md) · [Instalación completa en inglés](../../INSTALL.md) · [Todos los idiomas](../../LANGUAGES.md)

## Primeros pasos

1. Descarga el paquete completo en Encore Releases y verifica su checksum.
2. Respalda la carpeta PPSA99008, los datos /data/prosperoeden y el almacenamiento externo.
3. Copia toda la carpeta PPSA99008 en /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/; no basta con copiar eboot.bin.
4. Abre Encore, revisa Settings → Storage y Language, y utiliza solo tus archivos obtenidos legalmente.

## Aplicación / PPSA99008

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/         # complete application
/data/prosperoeden/               # persistent user files
/data/prosperoeden/keys/          # legally obtained keys
/data/prosperoeden/firmware/      # compatible firmware files
/data/prosperoeden/roms/          # games
/data/prosperoeden/updates/       # game updates
/data/prosperoeden/config/        # settings
/data/prosperoeden/logs/          # diagnostics
```

## Migrar desde el proyecto original

Encore y ProsperoEden nativo comparten el ID PPSA99008: no son dos apps que se puedan instalar por separado. Reemplaza los archivos completos de la aplicación, conservando guardados, configuración, juegos y claves en /data/prosperoeden. Respalda también cualquier carpeta antigua assets/ antes de migrar.

**Importante:** Nunca borres `/data/prosperoeden/` ni formatees el almacenamiento externo para actualizar. Haz un respaldo primero y no sobrescribas partidas ni claves.

## Compatibilidad y problemas conocidos

Encore solo ha sido probado en una consola PS5 con firmware 13.60. Los anteriores podrían funcionar, pero no están confirmados ni existe una versión mínima verificada. Algunos juegos aún presentan tirones, HUD atrasado, controles incorrectos y bloqueos durante pausas. Una compilación correcta no prueba la jugabilidad.

## Preguntas frecuentes

Si el menú sigue en inglés, entra a Settings → Language y comprueba que instalaste toda la carpeta ui/lang/.

Si un juego deja de arrancar después de cambiar opciones, prueba **Safe Launch** para esa sesión sin borrar guardados. Consulta [instalación ZIP/FFPFSC](../../INSTALL.md), [solución de problemas](../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md) y [soporte](../../SUPPORT.md).

El proyecto no incluye juegos comerciales, claves ni firmware. No compartas información privada en reportes públicos.

# Instalar y actualizar Encore — Español (España)

[← README en español](README.es.md) · [Todos los idiomas](../../LANGUAGES.md) · [Instalación completa (inglés)](../../INSTALL.md)

**Firmware probado con Encore en PS5 real: únicamente 13.60.** Otras versiones podrían funcionar, pero no están verificadas y no existe un mínimo confirmado. No actualices la consola solo porque se mencione 13.60.

## Instalar en cuatro pasos

1. Descarga un paquete **completo** de [Encore Releases](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/releases) y comprueba la versión y su integridad. Una compilación CI satisfactoria no demuestra compatibilidad en PS5.
2. **Haz una copia de seguridad** de la aplicación `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/`, los datos `/data/prosperoeden/` y cualquier almacenamiento externo.
3. Para **ZIP/FTP**, copia toda la carpeta `PPSA99008/` con `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/` y `ui/lang/` en `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/`. Evita `PPSA99008/PPSA99008/`. Para **FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus**, sigue [el método específico](../../INSTALL.md#method-2--ffpfsc-with-shadowmountplus), sin mezclarlo con ZIP.
4. Abre Encore y comprueba **Settings → Storage / Language**, la biblioteca y los guardados antes de eliminar copias anteriores.

## Pasar desde ProsperoEden nativo

**ProsperoEden original y Encore comparten el ID `PPSA99008`.** Es una actualización de la aplicación existente, no otra aplicación instalada en paralelo.

- **Nunca borres `/data/prosperoeden/`**: contiene configuraciones, partidas, juegos, claves y datos persistentes.
- Si tu versión anterior tenía archivos de usuario en `PPSA99008/assets/`, **respáldalos primero** y conserva esa carpeta hasta finalizar la migración.
- Conserva la raíz de almacenamiento externo seleccionada. No sobrescribas guardados para resolver un conflicto de archivos.
- Para **Encore → Encore**, utiliza una versión oficial de **Encore Releases**, sustituye todos los archivos de aplicación y verifica los datos.
- La actualización automática **R21 está planeada, pero aún no se ha publicado**.

## Carpetas importantes

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/     # aplicación
/data/prosperoeden/           # datos persistentes
/data/prosperoeden/keys/      # claves propias
/data/prosperoeden/firmware/  # firmware compatible
/data/prosperoeden/roms/      # juegos
/data/prosperoeden/updates/   # actualizaciones de juegos
/data/prosperoeden/logs/      # diagnósticos
```

En un disco externo se utiliza la misma estructura bajo la raíz seleccionada. El programa no incluye juegos.

## Solución de problemas

- **El menú sigue en inglés**: elige Settings → Language y verifica los **31 catálogos** de `PPSA99008/ui/lang/`. El selector ofrece **exactamente las 31 opciones de idioma/región del sistema PS5** publicadas por [Sony](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/), sin idiomas adicionales.
- **Biblioteca vacía**: comprueba la raíz elegida y la carpeta `roms/`.
- **Configuración incompleta**: revisa `keys/` y `firmware/` con tus archivos adquiridos legalmente.
- **Un juego deja de funcionar después de cambiar ajustes**: prueba **Safe Launch** sin borrar los guardados.
- **Tirones, HUD atrasado o bloqueos**: siguen siendo posibles aunque los tests de código sean correctos.

[Solución de problemas (inglés)](../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md) · [Soporte](../../SUPPORT.md).

Encore no proporciona juegos, claves ni firmware propietario.

> La dernière compilation publique authentique PS5 date du 15 octobre 2026; celle publiée le 30 octobre était une copie. La nouvelle préversion en brouillon ne contient aucun binaire ni jeu de deuxième génération validé sur console.

# Prospero.Eden Encore — Migration depuis le projet d’origine (Français (Canada))

[← Français (Canada)](README.fr-CA.md) · [Guide complet en anglais](../../INSTALL.md) · [Toutes les langues](../../LANGUAGES.md)

**Dernière release PS5 réellement compilée :** [R1 du 15 octobre 2026](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953), avec l'archive FTP `Eden-Encore-56293953-FTP-PPSA99008.zip` et son `SHA256SUMS`. La version recopiée le 30 octobre n'est pas une nouvelle compilation, et les changements récents de `main` ne sont pas intégrés à ce binaire. [Audit](../../docs/RELEASE_BASELINE_WORKFLOW_AUDIT_2026-11-09.md).

## Bien démarrer

1. Téléchargez l’archive complète dans Encore Releases et vérifiez son empreinte.
2. Sauvegardez le dossier PPSA99008 existant, les données /data/prosperoeden et votre stockage externe.
3. Installez le dossier PPSA99008 complet dans /data/homebrew/PPSA99008/; ne copiez pas seulement eboot.bin.
4. Lancez Encore, vérifiez Settings → Storage et Language, puis utilisez vos propres fichiers obtenus légalement.

## Application / PPSA99008

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/         # complete application
/data/prosperoeden/               # persistent user files
/data/prosperoeden/keys/          # legally obtained keys
/data/prosperoeden/firmware/      # compatible firmware files
/data/prosperoeden/roms/          # games
/data/prosperoeden/updates/       # game updates
/data/prosperoeden/config/        # settings
/data/prosperoeden/logs/          # diagnostics
```

## Migration depuis le projet d’origine

Encore et ProsperoEden natif partagent le même identifiant PPSA99008 : ils ne s’installent pas indépendamment. Remplacez les fichiers de l’application au complet, sans supprimer les sauvegardes, préférences, jeux ou clés dans /data/prosperoeden. Sauvegardez tout ancien dossier assets/ avant la migration.

**Important :** ne jamais supprimer `/data/prosperoeden/` ni formater le stockage externe pendant une mise à jour. Sauvegarder d’abord et ne pas écraser les données existantes.

## Compatibilité et limites actuelles

Seul le micrologiciel PS5 13.60 a été testé sur une console réelle avec Encore. Les versions antérieures pourraient fonctionner, mais aucun minimum n’a été vérifié. Des saccades, retards du HUD, problèmes de commandes et blocages à la pause restent possibles. Une CI verte n’est pas un test matériel.

## Questions fréquentes

Si l’interface demeure en anglais, choisissez Settings → Language et vérifiez l’installation complète de ui/lang/.

Si un jeu ne démarre plus après un changement de réglage, essayer **Safe Launch** pour cette session, sans effacer les sauvegardes. Voir l’[installation ZIP/FFPFSC](../../INSTALL.md), le [dépannage](../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md) et le [support](../../SUPPORT.md).

Encore ne fournit aucun jeu, aucune clé et aucun micrologiciel propriétaire. Ne publiez pas de données privées dans les signalements.

# Installer et mettre à jour Encore — Français

[← README français](README.fr.md) · [Toutes les langues](../../LANGUAGES.md) · [Installation détaillée (anglais)](../../INSTALL.md)

**Firmware PS5 testé avec Encore : 13.60 uniquement.** Les versions antérieures pourraient fonctionner, mais ne sont pas validées. Aucun minimum n'est établi ; ce guide n'est pas une invitation à mettre à jour la console.

**Référence historique à télécharger :** la vraie [R1 FTP du 15 octobre 2026](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953) contient `Eden-Encore-56293953-FTP-PPSA99008.zip` et `SHA256SUMS`. L'importation de la release sur le nouveau dépôt le 30 octobre n'a **pas** recompilé l'application. Les fonctions ajoutées depuis à `main` ne sont pas dans cette archive. [Audit des builds](../../docs/RELEASE_BASELINE_WORKFLOW_AUDIT_2026-11-09.md).

## Installer en quatre étapes

1. Télécharger un paquet **complet** des [Releases Encore](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/releases), en vérifiant les informations de version et les empreintes fournies. Un build CI vert n'est pas une preuve de jouabilité.
2. **Sauvegarder** l'application actuelle `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/`, les données `/data/prosperoeden/` et la racine de stockage externe si elle existe.
3. Pour **ZIP/FTP**, copier tout le dossier `PPSA99008/`, comprenant `eboot.bin`, `sce_sys/` et `ui/lang/`, dans `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/`. Ne pas créer un double dossier `PPSA99008/PPSA99008/`. Pour **FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus**, suivre [la méthode image](../../INSTALL.md#method-2--ffpfsc-with-shadowmountplus), sans mélanger ZIP et image.
4. Démarrer Encore, contrôler **Settings → Storage / Language**, la bibliothèque et les sauvegardes avant de supprimer toute ancienne copie.

## Mise à jour depuis ProsperoEden natif

**ProsperoEden d'origine et Encore partagent le même identifiant `PPSA99008`.** On met donc à jour l'application existante, pas une deuxième application indépendante.

- **Ne pas effacer `/data/prosperoeden/`** : il contient des paramètres, sauvegardes, jeux, clés et autres données utilisateur.
- Si l'ancienne application stockait des fichiers sous `PPSA99008/assets/`, **sauvegarder ce dossier avant le remplacement** et le conserver jusqu'à la fin de la migration.
- Conserver la racine externe sélectionnée. Une copie incomplète ou un conflit de destination ne justifie jamais d'écraser les sauvegardes.
- Pour **Encore → Encore**, installer la nouvelle application complète depuis les Releases **Encore** et vérifier les données au redémarrage.
- La mise à jour automatique **R21 est prévue, mais pas encore publiée**.

## Dossiers importants

```text
/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/     # application
/data/prosperoeden/           # données persistantes
/data/prosperoeden/keys/      # vos propres clés
/data/prosperoeden/firmware/  # firmware compatible
/data/prosperoeden/roms/      # jeux
/data/prosperoeden/updates/   # mises à jour de jeux
/data/prosperoeden/logs/      # diagnostics
```

En stockage externe, la structure reste identique sous la racine choisie. Les jeux ne sont pas inclus.

## Dépannage

- **Toujours en anglais** : choisir Settings → Language et vérifier les **31 catalogues** dans `PPSA99008/ui/lang/`. Le menu propose **exactement les 31 choix officiels de langue/région système PS5**, ni plus ni moins, selon la [liste Sony](https://www.playstation.com/fr-fr/legal/language-support/).
- **Bibliothèque vide** : vérifier la racine active et le dossier `roms/`.
- **Configuration incomplète** : vérifier les dossiers `keys/` et `firmware/` avec des fichiers légalement obtenus.
- **Jeu devenu instable après modification des réglages** : essayer **Safe Launch**, sans supprimer les sauvegardes.
- **Saccades, retard HUD ou gel à la pause** : problèmes pouvant encore survenir, même si les tests hôtes sont verts.

[Dépannage complet (anglais)](../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md) · [Support](../../SUPPORT.md).

Encore ne fournit ni jeu, ni clé propriétaire, ni firmware.

## Dukungan

Saat melaporkan masalah melalui GitHub Issues, sertakan versi Encore, firmware PS5, langkah reproduksi, pengaturan terkait, serta log yang sudah disamarkan. Jangan unggah kunci, berkas simpanan, atau data pribadi.
