`docs/i18n/check_user_docs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate documentation for all 31 official PS5 variants: 29 translated sets and two English regions.

This is a documentation/path check, not a native compiler, linguistic
certification, hardware test, or replacement for P0-P4 exit proofs.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
from urllib.parse import unquote

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
I18N = ROOT / "docs" / "i18n"
CATALOGS = ROOT / "headless" / "prosperoeden" / "ui" / "lang"
TYPES = ("README", "INSTALL", "SETTINGS", "TROUBLESHOOTING", "SUPPORT", "ACCESSIBILITY")
README_ALIAS = dict.fromkeys(
    ("de-DE", "es-ES", "fr-FR", "it-IT", "ja-JP", "ko-KR",
     "nl-NL", "pl-PL", "ru-RU", "th-TH")
)
INSTALL_ALIAS = dict.fromkeys(
    ("de-DE", "it-IT", "ja-JP", "ko-KR", "nl-NL",
     "pl-PL", "ru-RU", "th-TH")
)
for aliases in (README_ALIAS, INSTALL_ALIAS):
    for key in aliases:
        aliases[key] = key.split("-", 1)[0]

errors: list[str] = []


def check(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        errors.append(message)


def filename(kind: str, code: str) -> str:
    alias = (README_ALIAS if kind == "README" else INSTALL_ALIAS
             if kind == "INSTALL" else {})
    return f"{kind}.{alias.get(code, code)}.md"


def local_links(page: Path, text: str) -> None:
    references = re.findall(r"\]\(([^)]+)\)", text)
    references += re.findall(r"""\bhref=["']([^"']+)["']""", text)
    references += re.findall(r"""\bsrc=["']([^"']+)["']""", text)
    for original in references:
        target = original.strip().strip("<>").split()[0]
        if target.startswith(("https://", "http://", "mailto:", "data:",
                              "#", "//")):
            continue
        target = unquote(target.split("#", 1)[0].split("?", 1)[0])
        if not target:
            continue
        expected = (page.parent / target).resolve()
        check(expected.is_relative_to(ROOT) and expected.exists(),
              f"{page.relative_to(ROOT)}: invalid local link {original}")


seed = json.loads((I18N / "USER_DOC_TRANSLATIONS.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
locales = seed["locales"]
codes = {x["code"] for x in locales}
catalog_codes = {p.stem for p in CATALOGS.glob("*.po")}
check(len(locales) == len(codes) == 29, "expected 29 unique documentation locales")
check(codes == catalog_codes - {"en-US", "en-GB"} and len(catalog_codes) == 31,
      f"documentation vs PO locale difference: {sorted(codes ^ catalog_codes)}")

index = ROOT / "LANGUAGES.md"
index_text = index.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
local_links(index, index_text)
check("31 application translation catalogs" in index_text, "language index count missing")
check("31 official PS5 system language/region selections" in index_text, "launcher selection count missing")
rows = [r for r in index_text.splitlines() if r.startswith("| ") and "| Yes |" in r]
check(len(rows) == 31, f"expected 31 variant rows, got {len(rows)}")
check(len({r.split("|")[2].strip() for r in rows}) == 31, "duplicated locale row")
for kind in TYPES:
    uk = I18N / f"{kind}.en-GB.md"
    check(uk.is_file(), f"missing UK guide: {uk.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    if uk.is_file():
        content = uk.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        check(len(content.strip()) >= 650, f"short UK guide: {uk.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        check("../../LANGUAGES.md" in content, f"missing index: {uk.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        check(f"{kind}.en-GB.md" in index_text, f"missing UK link: {uk.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        local_links(uk, content)

for loc in locales:
    code, native = loc["code"], loc["native"]
    check("31" in loc["controls"] and "PS5" in loc["controls"],
          f"{code}: the localized controls guide must state the exact 31 official PS5 choices")
    for kind in TYPES:
        p = I18N / filename(kind, code)
        if not p.is_file():
            errors.append(f"missing {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
            continue
        content = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        check(len(content.strip()) >= 650, f"too short: {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        check(f"../../LANGUAGES.md" in content,
              f"missing language index link: {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        local_links(p, content)
        if kind in ("SETTINGS", "ACCESSIBILITY", "TROUBLESHOOTING", "SUPPORT"):
            check(native in content,
                  f"missing native locale title in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
            check(loc["safety"] in content,
                  f"missing translated backup/safety advice in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
            check(loc["limits"] in content,
                  f"missing dated release limitation in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
            for stale in (
                "Controller navigation: use on-screen focus",
                "Safe Launch resets problematic game-specific settings",
                "The following are **exact option names",
                "`Touchpad` (short press) opens the Encore",
            ):
                check(stale not in content,
                      f"untranslated English template in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        if kind in ("SETTINGS", "ACCESSIBILITY"):
            check(loc["controls"] in content,
                  f"missing translated quick-overlay guidance in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        if kind == "SETTINGS":
            check("FSR 1" in content and "Touchpad" in content,
                  f"missing video/controller coverage in {p.relative_to(ROOT)}")

for kind in TYPES:
    p = ROOT / f"{kind}.md"
    check(p.is_file(), f"missing English reference {kind}.md")

readme = (ROOT / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
settings = (ROOT / "SETTINGS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
check("LANGUAGES.md" in readme, "English README has no language directory")
check("Neural Rendering et composition d'image" not in settings,
      "English SETTINGS.md still contains untranslated French")
for old in ("/tree/feat/graphics-network-achievements",
            "/tree/research/ns2-ps5-compatibility"):
    check(old not in readme, f"English README links deleted branch {old}")

if errors:
    for msg in errors[:80]:
        print("USER_DOC_LOCALE_FAIL", msg)
    raise SystemExit(f"{len(errors)} user-doc localization/links violations")
print("ENCORE_USER_DOC_LOCALES_PASS",
      f"translated={len(codes)*len(TYPES)}",
      "english_us=6 english_uk=6 documented=186 variants=31 link_scope=local no_ps5_build=1")

```

`docs/releases/ENCORE_R2_DRAFT_2026-11-09.md`:

```md
# Eden Encore R2 — Development Preview

### Complete post-R1 development changelog · 15 October – 9 November 2026

> **UNPUBLISHED DRAFT PRERELEASE — NO DOWNLOADABLE PS5 BUILD OR RELEASE ASSETS.** This is a proposed, source-level R2 changelog. It is intentionally based on the **last authentically compiled public R1 dated 15 October 2026**, not the 30 October repository mirror. Development milestones **P0–P4 are treated as completed for the scope of this proposed R2 prerelease**. The final exact-SHA host evidence is tracked independently; **P5 (native build, installation, console hardware testing and game validation) is not included or claimed here**.

**Draft reference:** engine `1a52235c04a26d3886093d102c46baa23ee705bc` · pinned vendor `56db687283168be42b126ca738760047bd608d4c` · source changes since the R1 compiled-source SHA `5629395324ff65c98b50c44f35f2142a4a92654a`.

**R1 provenance:** [Original 15 October release](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953) · [native build run #38752177232](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/actions/runs/38752177232) · original source `56293953...` · release tag points to a different historical metadata commit `f037a78...`. The [30 October release in this repository](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953) contains the **same imported R1 package**, not a new native compilation.

---

## Highlights

- **One maintained native PS5 application and shared NS1/NS2 core.** First- and second-generation guest support now share the maintained loader, CPU/JIT, memory, GPU and display infrastructure on `main`; no separate experimental second-generation application is required.
- **Major guest GPU and Vulkan work.** New second-generation command handling, Ampere-to-common-IR translation, compute descriptors, graphics stages, synchronization, texture and memory protections, shader compilation and rejection paths.
- **Safer content handling.** Better handling of NSP/XCI/NSZ/XCZ, extracted game files, updates/DLC, NUP, per-generation keys and firmware, and corrupted or incomplete input.
- **Launcher and controller improvements.** Updated library, covers and 3D packaging, per-game settings, language support, controller mapping, faster startup presentation and a **touchpad-triggered Encore quick overlay**.
- **Graphics and image processing.** Preserved spatial FSR 1 (EASU/RCAS and sharpening), revised presentation/AA/scaling policies, optional frame-interpolation source work and a separate neural-rendering R09 development path.
- **Reliability and tooling.** Memory ownership, HLE/IPC, video queues, shader/graphics synchronization, more useful diagnostics, hardened release provenance and bounded code/host verification.
- **International user documentation.** Six user-facing document types available across **all 29 application catalog locales**. The launcher source now exposes **exactly all 31 official PS5 system language/region choices**, backed by 31 catalogs (including distinct English US/UK variants), with no non-PS5 additions.
- **Clean GitHub presentation.** Neutral workflow/job/step titles and non-essential brand mentions in owned source comments; required technical API names, provenance and third-party license notices stay intact.

## 1. Unified engine and project architecture (P0)

- Integrated shared first- and second-generation runtime owners into a **single active engine on `main`**.
- Reused common OS services, scheduling, filesystem, translation, input, video output and rendering foundations instead of duplicating console executables.
- Removed historical dependence on separate experimental/release CMake profiles for selecting different products; retain automatic capability detection and strict admissibility decisions.
- Separated optional graphics experiments from the core engine's supported guest instruction and ABI requirements.
- Retained only source-level compatibility where generation-specific behavior genuinely differs: executable format details, GPU instruction set, descriptor layout, firmware services and timing.
- Consolidated maintained overrides into complete source units and explicit build selections; pinned the corresponding vendor tree rather than relying on invisible build-time rewriting.
- Reconciled historical source inventories and post-audit owner additions without reinterpreting an old baseline as proof of performance.
- Preserved the normal first-generation renderer and application behavior as the regression baseline.
- Added source/provenance checks for common CMake, Vulkan, host service contracts, dependencies and graphics owners.
- Kept native PS5 builds an **explicit choice** and publication a **separate approval**, instead of treating every successful host workflow as a release.

## 2. Game discovery, executable loading, updates and DLC (P1)

### Content types and file organization

- Continued discovery and admission work for **NSP, XCI, NSZ and XCZ** game packages, extracted **ExeFS/RomFS** content and executable inputs such as **NRO, NSO, NCA, NAX and KIP**, where the corresponding loader supports the form.
- Unified library scanning and explicit game/update/add-on matching, including generation-aware metadata and launch identity.
- Improved handling of **base games, updates and DLC**, avoiding assumptions based solely on a file extension or hard-coded title list.
- Kept a **flexible storage contract**: `roms/`, `updates/`, `dlc/`, `mods/`, user data and external roots can be resolved without user-side source edits.
- Introduced independent `keys/ns1` and `keys/ns2`, and `firmware/ns1` and `firmware/ns2`, while retaining supported legacy flat storage layouts.
- Added or refined named firmware-dump metadata and source-side guards for missing, incomplete or inconsistent system files.
- Improved case-by-case handling of compressed NSO segments (**LZ4, ZBIC and zstd**) with bounded decompression, coherent error responses and no silent fallback to unrelated data.
- Maintained NCZ/NSZ handling for supported compressed inputs, including validation of sizes, block indexes, extracted output and resource budgets.
- Hardened content paths, directory traversal checks, invalid titles, metadata lengths and partial-input cleanup.

### NUP and virtual filesystem

- Introduced a maintained **NUP virtual filesystem** reader and mount path rather than forcing a bespoke extraction workflow.
- Added validation of NUP v1 headers, table of contents, identifier/UUID records, SHA-256 integrity and normalized paths.
- Added raw and zstd-backed entry handling and bounded file reads.
- Integrated RomFS/add-on search and mounting contracts while rejecting invalid or ambiguous content.
- Conserved NUP as part of the common source configuration, not a second-generation-only optional build product.

### Process creation and execution

- Worked on **NPDM/ACID/ACI, NSO/ExeFS, process identity and KProcess handoff** with actual maintained source owners.
- Improved fail-closed admission for malformed process metadata, missing file segments, invalid access ranges and partial session construction.
- Avoided publishing partially initialized processes or changing an established first-generation process path just to pass a second-generation test.

## 3. CPU, JIT, memory and process synchronization (P1)

- Consolidated first-/second-generation CPU translation policy, process setup, code memory and host callback boundaries.
- Continued work on executable-memory aliases, JIT allocation/reuse, sparse commit, I-cache visibility and safe process shutdown.
- Maintained source-level safeguards against dense JIT over-allocation, stale aliases and inconsistent guest/host permissions.
- Improved 64-bit guest address checks and range arithmetic, including overflow, alignment and uncommitted memory validation.
- Added bounded **49-bit GPU virtual-address** and page-mapping policies, with 4 KiB mappings and generation-specific sparse handling.
- Strengthened guest/GPU ownership bookkeeping, **NVMap**, temporary pin references, VA remapping, allocation fallback and rollback after an error or out-of-memory event.
- Avoided stale file descriptors, leaked pins, half-committed page tables and invalid access after teardown.
- Revisited CPU scheduling, event signallers, atomic waits, process-wide synchronization and host/guest clock boundaries.
- Kept fences, semaphore ordering and ownership transfers explicit rather than fixing freezes by disabling synchronization.
- Added negative tests for invalid handle/session states, race-sensitive release order, oversized mappings and re-entrant teardown.

## 4. Operating-system services, HLE, audio and video output (P1)

- Expanded common **IPC/TIPC** parsing and dispatch guards, response buffers, handles, service sessions and command-specific failure paths.
- Audited key services in **AM, SM, filesystem, NVDRV, VI/VI2 and audio** against expected guest message layouts.
- Corrected session lifetime and close/teardown order, including NVDRV process registration and map release ownership.
- Improved version-specific service admission rather than assuming a first-generation command has the same behavior for the successor.
- Strengthened native **VI2** display queries, resolution and encoding responses, display/session identity checks, malformed packet rejection and output ownership.
- Reviewed display cadence, virtual present state and guest-to-host presentation handoff.
- Improved audio buffer and sink lifecycle, invalid-format responses and cleanup after guest state changes.
- Corrected video decoder surface scheduling so a surface waiting on a fence does not unnecessarily stall other available output surfaces.
- Conserved GPU/video fences and explicit errors when a frame, service or buffer is not ready.
- Isolated host validation of individual service owners from PS5 runtime behavior; no claim of complete sound/video output for a successor game is made here.

## 5. Guest GPU command processing and memory safety (P2)

### Command submission, DMA and channel state

- Maintained an explicit command path from guest **GPFIFO / GPU channels** through validated command decoding to the shared renderer.
- Worked on generation-specific **Ampere DMA**, 3D/Compute command classes, macro processing, subchannel binding and command fetch.
- Improved pre-initialization command behavior, GPU process identity, invalid binding and stale-process rejection.
- Tightened semaphore/acquire ordering, synchronization points and queue publication.
- Added bounded failure responses for malformed GPU commands and unmapped memory rather than pretending that unsupported instructions succeeded.

### Virtual memory, buffers and descriptors

- Improved GPU virtual-memory translation and **NVMap** integration, including 49-bit access bounds, sparse mappings, page pin ownership and rollback.
- Revisited guest memory coherence, dirty ranges, DMA copies, texture invalidation and cache consistency.
- Added detailed control over **CBUF banks, SSBOs, UBOs, global memory and texel buffers**.
- Refined QMD3 descriptor discovery, indirect constant-buffer addresses, descriptor-array span validation and buffer/image classification.
- Corrected write-only global-memory shader cases where a store needed an SSBO descriptor even without a corresponding read.
- Checked complete byte spans, alignment, overflow, alias, write permissions and failed mapping at descriptor admission time.
- Protected dynamically indexed/indirect resources against divergent offsets and unsupported addressing modes.
- Improved atomic operations and per-buffer access tracking where source semantics could be established.
- Reduced invalid reuse of stale resource views, pipeline descriptors and destroyed buffers.
- Added real-source host witnesses and conservative negative cases for data-dependent GPU access.

### Textures, caches and surfaces

- Improved **TIC/TSC** sampling and descriptor interpretation, texture arrays, image views, image/buffer alias rules and unsupported format rejection.
- Continued **ASTC** and sparse-texture transfer integration with safe staging and resource budgets.
- Strengthened texture cache invalidation, rasterizer writes, GPU cache ownership and deferred cleanup.
- Added protections for asynchronous allocation, queued presentation, framebuffer lifetime and render-pass transitions.
- Improved GPU-only allocations, buffer identities and reserve/commit checks to reduce incorrect visibility between CPU and GPU.
- Preserved first-generation texturing behavior when a successor-specific descriptor cannot be represented safely.

## 6. GPU instruction translation, SPIR-V and Vulkan (P2)

- Expanded Ampere instruction decoding and lowering into the shared Maxwell/IR-oriented back end without indiscriminately treating two generations as identical.
- Reviewed high-register operands and multi-register vectors for arithmetic, memory and predicate operations.
- Corrected branch relocation/target handling for conditional, signed and indirect branch forms where verified; unqualified variants remain explicit failures.
- Improved macro engine sequencing, method and QMD interpretation, including rejection of invalid or reserved fields.
- Continued **Vertex, Fragment, Geometry, Tessellation, Task and Mesh** stage integration with stage-specific capability checks.
- Added checks for undefined patch variables, invalid tessellation stage usage, unrepresentable input/output layouts and out-of-range attributes.
- Worked on native **Compute** pipelines from guest shader state through **SPIR-V** module generation, descriptor binding and Vulkan dispatch.
- Revisited cross-dispatch memory dependencies, indirect dispatch arguments, barriers, image layouts and buffer visibility.
- Hardened descriptor state during pipeline compilation, rasterizer binding and queued replay.
- Improved Vulkan pipeline creation, shader cache, presentation image ownership and deferred destruction.
- Qualified host-side shader syntax/ABI with Clang/GCC, shader witnesses and `spirv-val` where applicable.
- Preserved the **fail-closed** policy for unknown guest opcodes, invalid descriptors, incompatible stage combinations and unsupported GPU capabilities.
- **Important limitation:** a valid SPIR-V module or Vulkan host test is not a verified guest-rendered second-generation PS5 frame.

## 7. Native graphics, scaling, anti-aliasing and frame presentation

### Spatial rendering and display

- Preserved **FSR 1** as the spatial upscaling mode, including **EASU**, **RCAS** and the user-adjustable sharpness control.
- Restored or archived legacy translated FSR labels where needed instead of silently losing the original feature's locale coverage.
- Distinguished TV output resolution from internal game scale, interpolation filter, sharpening, anti-aliasing and frame generation.
- Continued tuning and safeguards for bilinear/bicubic/Lanczos-style scaling choices and output-size arithmetic.
- Worked on **FXAA**, optional AA integrations, multisampling and resolution targets with strict compatibility checks.
- Improved Vulkan presentation scheduling, display image history, render-pass transitions and overlay/HUD composition contracts.
- Refined frame-timing measurements and source/host replay without asserting a specific FPS increase on PS5.

### Optional frame generation

- Added or refined optional frame-generation selection and host-side capability gates.
- Separated actual emulated game cadence from displayed/interpolated frames.
- Explored Vulkan optical-flow and native frame-interpolation approaches without treating an experimental source path as a universally supported release feature.
- Preserved explicit off/unsupported states when required hardware, frame history, depth or motion input is absent.

### Neural Rendering / R09

- Introduced an optional neural-rendering workstream with distinct Original and Compact model manifests and user-side selection policies.
- Added public model-layout and per-tensor verification tools, structural plan checks, optional image-path composition and Vulkan compute/shader ABIs.
- Kept all **model DLLs and learned weights user-private**; they are never committed or attached to a release.
- Added strict checks for tensor count, file bounds, offsets, byte ranges, hashes, model flavor and inconsistent resources.
- Refined image pre/post-processing, Swin/ViT attention, QKV, feed-forward, U-Net/decoder stages and expected intermediate shapes.
- Added source and host tooling to attempt complete graph execution and inspect GPU readback without distributing private inputs.
- Updated public host examples and GitHub display names so a successful link, parser run, shader fixture or partial frame cannot be mistaken for a full authentic model inference.
- **Not claimed:** a verified output image from the complete 152-operation Original network on the PS5 GPU, general game support, or equivalent quality to a desktop proprietary implementation.

## 8. Launcher, home screen, game library and media (P3)

- Reworked the PS5-oriented **controller-first home screen**, main navigation, settings menus, library browsing and per-game information.
- Improved recent-game ordering, selected item focus, browsing state and background presentation.
- Refined **NS1/NS2 game recognition** and book-keeping so changing sections does not repeatedly lose the ROM inventory.
- Improved game metadata lookup and artwork association using available title information and media sources.
- Extended jacket/cover reconstruction, front/back/spine handling, 3D box presentation and safe fallback when artwork is missing.
- Addressed malformed or incomplete covers, transparency, incorrect box tinting, reversed artwork and long-title layouts in the source/host UI paths.
- Updated TV-scale text, focus readability, navigation hints, spacing, clipping and accessibility option wiring.
- Reduced unnecessary preview/covers work, improved asset format handling and used efficient image assets where supported.
- Worked on preserving the selected jacket during game launch instead of showing an extra, unhelpful loading screen.
- Maintained a single-file native application concept and the existing application identity.
- Added or expanded launcher preview and source checks; they are not substitutes for observation on a physical console.

## 9. Controller input, per-game controls and Encore quick overlay

- Preserved the normal controller input chain and first-generation guest button semantics.
- Extended per-game controller-layout selection and mapping rather than globally overwriting the user's preferred profile.
- Supported virtual guest HOME/capture behaviors only through approved mappings; the console's own central system button remains reserved.
- Added the **in-game Encore quick overlay on a touchpad press**, **not** on the central console system button.
- Grouped current game settings, graphics, control mapping, FPS/diagnostics and log options in the overlay.
- Removed the legacy standalone FPS-show shortcut in favor of the overlay-controlled setting.
- Added contextual feedback when an option requires a game restart before it can take effect.
- Revisited controller button glyphs, contextual prompts, mixed physical/guest mapping and title-specific artwork substitution policies.
- Kept the local mapping state and in-game texture assets separate so an unsupported glyph conversion cannot silently alter game inputs.

## 10. Languages, documentation and accessibility

- Maintained **31 application gettext locale catalogs**, including both English variants,, including new graphics, neural and frame-generation settings.
- Improved coverage of new option labels and preserved useful historical FSR translations as inactive references where needed.
- Added practical **README, installation, settings, troubleshooting, support and accessibility guides for all 29 catalog locales** (174 localized pages in total).
- Preserved the existing detailed French and Spanish README/installation pages rather than replacing them with shorter copies.
- Added a single language directory linking every one of the six user-facing pages for each locale.
- Made the distinction explicit: the **launcher offers exactly 31 official PS5 system language/region choices**; all 31 catalog locales are selectable, and no extra languages are provided.
- Documented the selected storage root, keys/firmware ownership, safe migration, release packaging and recovery steps.
- Documented larger launcher text, high contrast and reduced motion as separate optional settings, not guaranteed accessibility inside games.
- Improved the README's version history, R1 source SHA, native-build restrictions and provenance explanation.
- Added source checks for the full user-guide matrix to prevent missing language links.
- **Translation quality note:** complete file/key coverage is not a professional linguistic review. Arabic right-to-left layout, CJK glyph fallbacks, regional variants and UI truncation require native-speaker/device checks.

## 11. Reliability, performance safeguards and diagnostics

- Revisited stalls and timing regressions observed historically in FC27 and other first-generation titles, including gameplay HUD/pause behavior and service synchronization.
- Improved explicit handling of GPU queue backpressure, video surface fences, stale present resources and kernel wait paths.
- Hardened memory lifetime around JIT, direct-memory allocations, decoder surfaces, GPU caches and teardown.
- Reduced repeated source-side allocations or conversion work where clearly justified without promising universal performance gains.
- Added bounded diagnostics, host counters, error categories and trace review for unsupported guest operations.
- Improved fail-closed behavior during malformed package loading, game restart and partial construction.
- Expanded host-negative tests so guards are not considered correct merely because a synthetic positive fixture passes.
- Preserved diagnostic modes without enabling costly logs or unqualified experimental behavior by default.

## 12. Security, dependency provenance and GitHub workflows (P4)

- Kept the maintained source and the **vendor** repository pinned by exact Git commit, preserving third-party licenses and source provenance.
- Clarified which vendor directories are immutable upstream snapshots and which contain maintained source overrides.
- Reviewed user-private model parsing, filename/size bounds, memory ownership and content path validation.
- Maintained static security scans and conservative CodeQL reporting rather than suppressing real findings for cosmetic green CI.
- Updated neutral names/descriptions for relevant workflow headings, jobs, steps and host artifacts.
- Removed non-essential commercial-brand references from authored comments and local test messages without rewriting ABI symbols or upstream authorship.
- Expanded source/host validation with **Clang, GCC, UBSan, SPIR-V and Vulkan host** witnesses.
- Kept a finite P1/P2 acceptance structure with **H01–H07 and G01–G10** (17 contracts), expected positive and negative behavior, stable owner references and rejection of artificial blanket exclusions.
- Separated a **structural audit** of test coverage from the `--enforce` evidence-based exit decision.
- Maintained source preflight, Core fast gate, NS2 host guards, dedicated SPIR-V qualification, P0–P4 host matrix and vendor parity checks.
- Avoided treating green jobs from different SHA revisions as one clean acceptance record.
- Clarified the actual release workflow: ordinary `main` pushes do not cause a full native PS5 build; an explicit manual action or approved build marker is required; release publication is a further deliberate step.
- Updated install guides so they reference actual R1 downloadable file names instead of imaginary historical assets.
- Added this expanded, English-only R2 draft to an isolated release-preparation branch, with **no release assets and no automatic publication**.

## 14. Compatibility, limitations and expected testing

**Last hardware-tested firmware:** **PS5 13.60 only**. There is no documented minimum firmware and no recommendation to update a console merely to match the test target.

**First-generation titles:** existing first-generation behavior is the baseline. Previously observed issues included FC27 frame-pacing/HUD freezes and occasional crashes; BOTW was reported as playable in selected profiles on an older binary. None of these results qualify the new R2 candidate.

**Second-generation titles:** Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza have previously reached guest initialization stages, but no confirmed guest-rendered first frame on the physical PS5 is available. Do not interpret loader progress, Vulkan initialization or host shader compilation as game compatibility.

**Graphics extras:** FSR 1 is a retained spatial filter. Frame interpolation and neural rendering are separate, optional paths with additional restrictions. Selecting or compiling an option is not proof that the game produced more simulated frames or that R09 completed authentic inference.

**User data:** never delete `/data/prosperoeden/` just to repair a failed installation. The original native app and Encore use the same `PPSA99008` title identity, so updating is a replacement, **not** an independent side-by-side install.

**No private files:** the package contains no games, keys, firmware, DLLs, learned model weights, user saves or proprietary distribution assets.

**Known qualification still needed in P5:** actual native ELF/package build from one pinned engine/vendor pair; package/file checksums; installation from a complete ZIP/FTP or explicitly validated image workflow; startup on physical hardware; correct language and artwork display; FC27/BOTW first-generation regressions; Mario Kart World/Donkey Kong Bananza first-frame observation; graphics/VRAM/synchronization stability; saves and per-game settings; valid performance traces.

## 15. Install and upgrade information

**There is nothing to install from this R2 draft.** It deliberately has **zero assets**. For the genuine last public build, download the [15 October R1 FTP package](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore/releases/tag/encore-R1-56293953), which includes:

- `Eden-Encore-56293953-FTP-PPSA99008.zip`
- `SHA256SUMS`

For ZIP/FTP, extract the complete `PPSA99008/` folder and install it under `/data/homebrew/PPSA99008/`. Do not create a nested `PPSA99008/PPSA99008/` folder. Preserve `/data/prosperoeden/` and any configured external storage. Use the [installation guide](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for firmware/keys, backup, migration, checksums and the **separate** FFPFSC/ShadowMountPlus method.

## Verified documentation and vendor presentation qualification — 9 November 2026

The documentation localization follow-up has been implemented on `main` **after the original draft notes were written**:

- All **29 application catalog locales** now have six consumer-focused Markdown guides each: README/overview, installation and upgrading, settings, troubleshooting, support and accessibility (**174 localized pages**). These are practical native-language guides, **not** a claim that the longer English documentation has been translated line for line or independently proofread by 29 native speakers.
- The language index distinguishes the **31 translation catalogs** (including US/UK English) from the **29 non-English localized guide sets** under the **31 exact PS5 system language/region choices**. English remains the most detailed normative user reference. The [strict Sony 31-choice policy](../PS5_SYSTEM_LANGUAGE_POLICY.md) excludes all languages not on Sony's official console menu.
- The [user documentation and local-link validation workflow](https://github.com/niakw/ProsperoEden-Encore/actions/runs/42618975742) **passed** for the documentation changes, checking catalog coverage, internal links, preservation of save-data warnings and key localized help. It does not test PS5 rendering or certify linguistic quality.
- Invalid French/Spanish guide links and obsolete feature/research branch links in the main and translated READMEs have been corrected.
- The [vendor maintained-source presentation audit](https://github.com/niakw/Prospero.Eden-Encore-vendor/actions/runs/42618761816) **passed**, scanning **775 active source-text files**. Commercial names were absent from the vendor's visible workflow titles and step labels. The audit recorded 100 branded references in comment-like lines of the maintained source; these are predominantly driver/ABI/format facts, namespace markers or required upstream attribution and were **not** blindly removed. Third-party snapshots remain unmodified.
- The engine's `vendor` gitlink is pinned to the reviewed vendor revision above. Neither documentation qualification nor vendor presentation review is a substitute for P1/P2 functional exit receipts, a new native PS5 compilation or P5 hardware tests.
```

`extras/graphics/aa_source_extent.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// R24: AA source-image sizing contract, independent of Vulkan headers.
// The source of the AA pass can be either an accelerated guest texture
// with scaled dimensions, or a raw framebuffer readback at guest size.
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::Graphics {
struct AaExtent {
    std::uint32_t width{};
    std::uint32_t height{};
};
[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool AaValid(AaExtent v) noexcept {
    return v.width != 0 && v.height != 0 &&
           v.width <= 8192 && v.height <= 8192;
}
[[nodiscard]] constexpr AaExtent AaSourceExtent(
    bool accelerated, AaExtent raw_guest, AaExtent scaled_guest) noexcept {
    const AaExtent source = accelerated ? scaled_guest : raw_guest;
    return AaValid(source) ? source : AaExtent{};
}
[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool AaExtentChanged(AaExtent before,
                                             AaExtent after) noexcept {
    return before.width != after.width || before.height != after.height;
}
} // namespace Eden::Graphics

```

`extras/graphics/framegen_capabilities.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// PS5-native frame generation capabilities; user preference is not proof of displayed frames.
// Prevent a desktop-only proprietary upscaler path from being advertised as native console support.
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::FeatureLab {
enum class FrameGeneration : std::uint8_t {
    Off = 0,
    MihawkGen = 1,
    Fsr3Vulkan = 2,
    LosslessScaling = 3,
    DlssPcOnlyUnsupported = 4,
};
enum class Availability : std::uint8_t {
    Disabled,
    Unsupported,
    ReadyLowCadence,
    Ready,
};
struct GraphicsCapabilities {
    bool native_vulkan = false;
    bool fsr3_swapchain = false;
    // Real FSR3 optical-flow from Swordpdf/ps5-framegen: no guest depth/MV.
    // True only with a ready host Vulkan pipeline on the actual device.
    bool fsr3_optical_flow = false;
    bool guest_motion_vectors = false;
    bool guest_depth = false;
    bool mihawk_compute = false;
    bool model_weights_verified_and_loaded = false;
    bool lossless_scaling_provider_available = false;
    // Real game progression FPS: NEVER interpolated display FPS.
    std::uint32_t game_fps = 0;
};

constexpr Availability QualifyFrameGeneration(
    FrameGeneration requested, const GraphicsCapabilities& caps) noexcept {
    if (requested == FrameGeneration::Off) return Availability::Disabled;
    // Unsupported on the console GPU without a native implementation of the desktop-only path.
    if (requested == FrameGeneration::DlssPcOnlyUnsupported)
        return Availability::Unsupported;
    if (!caps.native_vulkan || caps.game_fps < 30)
        return Availability::Unsupported;
    switch (requested) {
    case FrameGeneration::Fsr3Vulkan:
        if (!caps.fsr3_optical_flow &&
            (!caps.fsr3_swapchain || !caps.guest_motion_vectors || !caps.guest_depth))
            return Availability::Unsupported;
        break;
    case FrameGeneration::MihawkGen:
        if (!caps.mihawk_compute || !caps.model_weights_verified_and_loaded)
            return Availability::Unsupported;
        break;
    case FrameGeneration::LosslessScaling:
        if (!caps.lossless_scaling_provider_available)
            return Availability::Unsupported;
        break;
    case FrameGeneration::Off:
    case FrameGeneration::DlssPcOnlyUnsupported:
        return Availability::Unsupported;
    }
    // 30->60 presented is not 60 Hz game simulation, and AMD recommends
    // a source cadence at or above 60 fps for good interpolation quality.
    return caps.game_fps < 60 ? Availability::ReadyLowCadence
                              : Availability::Ready;
}
} // namespace Eden::FeatureLab

```

`extras/graphics/framegen_present_gate.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// R08: native-present eligibility and reset rules, deliberately independent of a
// Vulkan backend. Calling this does NOT submit a generated frame.
#include "framegen_capabilities.h"

#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::FeatureLab {

enum class PresentGateReason : std::uint8_t {
    Disabled, Unsupported, Unverified120Hz, UnsafeOverlay, Paused,
    NoStablePair, StaleOrSkippedFrame, WrongCadence, NoDisplayHeadroom,
    Eligible
};

struct PresentGateInput {
    // Monotonic ID and timestamp for REAL source frames only. Never count
    // synthetic presents as new source frames.
    std::uint64_t real_frame_id = 0;
    std::uint64_t timestamp_ns = 0;
    std::uint32_t width = 0;
    std::uint32_t height = 0;
    std::uint32_t output_hz = 60; // Negotiated, not merely requested
    bool display_mode_verified = false;
    bool pause_or_menu = false;
    bool overlay_changed = false; // HUD, subtitles, menus or compositor overlays
    bool scene_reset = false;     // Resolution/TV mode/renderer/seek/game change
};

struct PresentGateDecision {
    PresentGateReason reason = PresentGateReason::Disabled;
    // A real frame still goes to normal Vulkan presentation. Only this
    // optional extra display frame is gated.
    std::uint8_t synthetic_frames = 0;
    bool reset_history = false;
    constexpr bool eligible() const noexcept {
        return reason == PresentGateReason::Eligible && synthetic_frames != 0;
    }
};

// Frame pairs must not cross menus, scene resets, duplicated frames, altered
// overlays, or unsafe clock gaps. The application owns the actual GPU
// barriers, image lifetimes, and queue fences (not this helper).
class FramegenPresentGate {
public:
    constexpr void Reset() noexcept {
        primed_ = false;
        last_id_ = 0;
        last_ns_ = 0;
        last_width_ = 0;
        last_height_ = 0;
        last_hz_ = 0;
    }

    constexpr PresentGateDecision OnRealFrame(FrameGeneration mode,
                                              const GraphicsCapabilities& caps,
                                              const PresentGateInput& input) noexcept {
        const auto reject = [this](PresentGateReason reason) constexpr {
            Reset();
            return PresentGateDecision{reason, 0, true};
        };
        if (mode == FrameGeneration::Off)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::Disabled);
        if (QualifyFrameGeneration(mode, caps) == Availability::Unsupported)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::Unsupported);
        if (!input.display_mode_verified || (input.output_hz != 60 && input.output_hz != 120))
            return reject(PresentGateReason::Unverified120Hz);
        if (input.pause_or_menu || input.scene_reset)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::Paused);
        // Whole-screen colour-frame interpolation could smear guest HUD and
        // overlays. The renderer must prove a clean pair before enabling.
        if (input.overlay_changed)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::UnsafeOverlay);
        if (input.width == 0 || input.height == 0 ||
            input.width > 7680 || input.height > 4320 ||
            input.real_frame_id == 0 || input.timestamp_ns == 0)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::StaleOrSkippedFrame);
        if (caps.game_fps >= input.output_hz)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::NoDisplayHeadroom);
        if (!primed_) {
            Remember(input);
            return {PresentGateReason::NoStablePair, 0, true};
        }
        if (input.width != last_width_ || input.height != last_height_ ||
            input.output_hz != last_hz_ ||
            input.real_frame_id != last_id_ + 1 ||
            input.timestamp_ns <= last_ns_)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::StaleOrSkippedFrame);
        const std::uint64_t delta_ns = input.timestamp_ns - last_ns_;
        Remember(input);
        // 30..120 actual source frames/s, with a tolerant margin. A large
        // stall or a frame repeated by the emulator must not be interpolated.
        if (delta_ns < 8'000'000 || delta_ns > 42'000'000)
            return reject(PresentGateReason::WrongCadence);
        // Initially cap to one interpolated frame (30->60 or 60->120), NOT
        // the 30->120 x4 mode. Multi-interpolation needs a measured PS5 budget.
        if (caps.game_fps * 2 > input.output_hz + 3)
            return {PresentGateReason::NoDisplayHeadroom, 0, false};
        return {PresentGateReason::Eligible, 1, false};
    }

private:
    constexpr void Remember(const PresentGateInput& x) noexcept {
        primed_ = true;
        last_id_ = x.real_frame_id;
        last_ns_ = x.timestamp_ns;
        last_width_ = x.width;
        last_height_ = x.height;
        last_hz_ = x.output_hz;
    }
    bool primed_ = false;
    std::uint64_t last_id_ = 0, last_ns_ = 0;
    std::uint32_t last_width_ = 0, last_height_ = 0, last_hz_ = 0;
};

} // namespace Eden::FeatureLab
```

`extras/graphics/fsr1_sharpness_policy.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
#include <algorithm>

namespace Eden::Graphics {
struct Fsr1Sharpness {
    bool rcas_enabled;
    float rcas_stops;
};
// AMD RCAS takes sharpening *stops*: 0 = strongest, 2 = softer.
// The PS5 UI is "Netteté (%)": 0 should disable RCAS, 100 the strongest.
// A 50% preference maps to 1 stop, consistent with the historic default.
[[nodiscard]] constexpr Fsr1Sharpness Fsr1SharpnessFromPercent(int percent) noexcept {
    const int bounded = std::clamp(percent, 0, 100);
    return {.rcas_enabled = bounded != 0,
            .rcas_stops = static_cast<float>(100 - bounded) / 50.0f};
}
// Eden's shared Settings::values.fsr_sharpening_slider is a 0..200
// RCAS-stop quantity. The Encore launch path ALREADY maps user-facing
// percentages to it as: internal = 200 - 2 * percent. Never feed the
// internal value back to Fsr1SharpnessFromPercent: doing so would
// clamp >100 and apply the strongest RCAS at almost every UI setting.
[[nodiscard]] constexpr Fsr1Sharpness Fsr1SharpnessFromInternal(int raw) noexcept {
    const int bounded = std::clamp(raw, 0, 200);
    return {.rcas_enabled = bounded != 200,
            .rcas_stops = static_cast<float>(bounded) / 100.0f};
}
static_assert(!Fsr1SharpnessFromInternal(200).rcas_enabled);
static_assert(Fsr1SharpnessFromInternal(100).rcas_stops == 1.0f);
static_assert(Fsr1SharpnessFromInternal(0).rcas_stops == 0.0f);
static_assert(Fsr1SharpnessFromPercent(0).rcas_enabled == false);
static_assert(Fsr1SharpnessFromPercent(50).rcas_stops == 1.0f);
static_assert(Fsr1SharpnessFromPercent(100).rcas_stops == 0.0f);
}
```

`extras/graphics/fsr31_native_resource_contract.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// R07: match the authenticated guest image/view IDs to the actual Vulkan
// inputs handed to the temporal compute bridge. Independent of Vulkan headers
// so this is host-testable without a renderer or fabricated game motion.
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include "fsr31_temporal_contract.h"

namespace Eden::Graphics::Temporal {
struct NativeResource {
    std::uint64_t image{};
    std::uint64_t view{};
};
struct NativeResources {
    NativeResource color{}, depth{}, motion{};
};

// Reject an in-place temporal blit into any input image, even if Vulkan
// scheduling would place compute before rasterization: guest texture cache
// aliasing and future frame-history reads must remain strictly unchanged.
struct NativeDestination {
    std::uint64_t image{};
    std::uint32_t width{};
    std::uint32_t height{};
    std::uint32_t samples{};
    bool single_color_no_depth{};
};
[[nodiscard]] constexpr Rejection ValidateNativeDestination(
    const Inputs& metadata, const NativeDestination& dst) noexcept {
    if (!dst.image) return Rejection::MissingResource;
    if (dst.image == metadata.scene_color.image ||
        dst.image == metadata.depth.image ||
        dst.image == metadata.motion.image)
        return Rejection::OutputAliasesInput;
    if (!dst.single_color_no_depth || dst.samples != 1 ||
        dst.width != metadata.output_width || dst.height != metadata.output_height)
        return Rejection::InvalidResolution;
    return Rejection::None;
}

[[nodiscard]] constexpr Rejection ValidateNativeResources(
    const Inputs& metadata, const NativeResources& native) noexcept {
    const std::array<Resource,3> declared{
        metadata.scene_color, metadata.depth, metadata.motion};
    const std::array<NativeResource,3> actual{
        native.color,native.depth,native.motion};
    for (std::size_t i=0;i<declared.size();++i) {
        if (!actual[i].image || !actual[i].view) {
            return Rejection::MissingResource;
        }
        if (declared[i].image!=actual[i].image ||
            declared[i].view!=actual[i].view) {
            return Rejection::MismatchedNativeResource;
        }
    }
    // Distinct temporal semantics require distinct backing images, NOT
    // merely different Vulkan views onto the same image. The latter could
    // be reinterpretations of one guest allocation and would corrupt FSR
    // depth and motion reconstruction despite different view handles.
    if (native.color.image==native.depth.image ||
        native.color.image==native.motion.image ||
        native.depth.image==native.motion.image ||
        native.color.view==native.depth.view ||
        native.color.view==native.motion.view ||
        native.depth.view==native.motion.view) {
        return Rejection::MismatchedNativeResource;
    }
    return Rejection::None;
}
} // namespace Eden::Graphics::Temporal
```

`extras/graphics/fsr31_temporal_contract.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// R07 — strict generic input contract for a REAL FSR3.1 temporal upscaler.
//
// This contract is independent of guest game IDs and is kept separate from
// native PresentManager/FSR3 optical-flow frame generation. It must not turn
// guessed depth or motion into "verified" evidence. It is NOT an upscaler.
#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::Graphics::Temporal {
enum class Producer : std::uint8_t {
    None, GuessedFromPresentation, GuestGpuVerified,
};
enum class DepthConvention : std::uint8_t { Unknown, Forward, Reversed };
enum class MotionConvention : std::uint8_t {
    Unknown, PixelOffsetToPreviousFrame, NormalizedOffsetToPreviousFrame,
};
enum class Rejection : std::uint8_t {
    None, MissingFrame, MissingResource, UntrustedProvenance, MixedFrame,
    MissingMotionConvention, MissingDepthConvention, MissingHudSeparation,
    InvalidResolution, InvalidJitter, InvalidMotionScale, InvalidTiming,
    MissingGpuCompletion, NonConsecutiveFrame, SceneChanged,
    InvalidProjection, InvalidVulkanImageLayout, InvalidSharpening, UnsupportedDevice,
    UnsupportedDepthConvention, UnsupportedMotionConvention,
    UnsupportedInputFormat, InsufficientMemoryBudget, MismatchedNativeResource, NativeBackendFailure,
    OutputAliasesInput,
};

// A non-owning identity. The real backend will convert these into actual
// VkImage/VkImageView and must keep them resident until the scheduler tick is
// finished. Zero means missing. No conversion to pointers in these tests.
struct Resource {
    std::uint64_t image{};
    std::uint64_t view{};
    std::uint64_t frame_id{};
    std::uint64_t scene_id{};
    Producer producer{Producer::None};
};
struct Inputs {
    Resource scene_color;
    Resource depth;
    Resource motion;
    std::uint32_t render_width{};
    std::uint32_t render_height{};
    std::uint32_t output_width{};
    std::uint32_t output_height{};
    DepthConvention depth_convention{DepthConvention::Unknown};
    MotionConvention motion_convention{MotionConvention::Unknown};
    std::array<float,2> jitter{};
    std::array<float,2> motion_scale{};
    std::array<float,4> depth_to_view{};
    float tan_half_fov{};
    float elapsed_ms{};
    bool native_hud_is_separate{};
    bool guest_hud_is_separate{};
    bool captured_gpu_work_complete{};
    bool vulkan_inputs_in_general_layout{};
};
[[nodiscard]] inline Rejection Validate(const Inputs& f) noexcept {
    if (!f.scene_color.frame_id || !f.scene_color.scene_id)
        return Rejection::MissingFrame;
    for (const Resource* r : {&f.scene_color,&f.depth,&f.motion}) {
        if (!r->image || !r->view) return Rejection::MissingResource;
        if (r->producer != Producer::GuestGpuVerified)
            return Rejection::UntrustedProvenance;
        if (r->frame_id != f.scene_color.frame_id ||
            r->scene_id != f.scene_color.scene_id)
            return Rejection::MixedFrame;
    }
    if (f.depth_convention == DepthConvention::Unknown)
        return Rejection::MissingDepthConvention;
    if (f.depth_convention != DepthConvention::Reversed)
        return Rejection::UnsupportedDepthConvention;
    if (f.motion_convention == MotionConvention::Unknown)
        return Rejection::MissingMotionConvention;
    if (f.motion_convention != MotionConvention::PixelOffsetToPreviousFrame)
        return Rejection::UnsupportedMotionConvention;
    if (!f.native_hud_is_separate || !f.guest_hud_is_separate)
        return Rejection::MissingHudSeparation;
    if (f.render_width < 64 || f.render_height < 64 ||
        f.output_width < 64 || f.output_height < 64 || f.render_width>8192 || f.render_height>8192 ||
        f.output_width>8192 || f.output_height>8192 ||
        f.output_width < f.render_width ||
        f.output_height < f.render_height ||
        f.output_width > 3ULL * f.render_width ||
        f.output_height > 3ULL * f.render_height)
        return Rejection::InvalidResolution;
    for (const auto j : f.jitter)
        if (!std::isfinite(j) || std::abs(j)>1.0f)
            return Rejection::InvalidJitter;
    for (const auto s : f.motion_scale)
        if (!std::isfinite(s) || s<=0.0f || s>8192.0f)
            return Rejection::InvalidMotionScale;
    for (float parameter : f.depth_to_view)
        if (!std::isfinite(parameter))
            return Rejection::InvalidProjection;
    if (!std::isfinite(f.tan_half_fov) || f.tan_half_fov<=0.0f ||
        f.tan_half_fov>100.0f || f.depth_to_view[1] <= 0.0f ||
        f.depth_to_view[3] <= 0.0f)
        return Rejection::InvalidProjection;
    if (!std::isfinite(f.elapsed_ms) || f.elapsed_ms<=0.0f ||
        f.elapsed_ms>250.0f)
        return Rejection::InvalidTiming;
    if (!f.vulkan_inputs_in_general_layout)
        return Rejection::InvalidVulkanImageLayout;
    if (!f.captured_gpu_work_complete)
        return Rejection::MissingGpuCompletion;
    return Rejection::None;
}

// History must reset whenever a source frame is skipped, a scene changes,
// resource resolution changes, or the input contract is not satisfied.
// The backend is responsible for shader dispatch and true GPU synchronization.
class FrameContinuity {
public:
    [[nodiscard]] Rejection Observe(const Inputs& inputs) noexcept {
        const Rejection valid=Validate(inputs);
        if (valid!=Rejection::None) {
            Reset();
            return valid;
        }
        const auto frame_id=inputs.scene_color.frame_id;
        const auto scene_id=inputs.scene_color.scene_id;
        const bool has_previous=last_frame_!=0;
        const bool scene_changed=has_previous && scene_id!=scene_;
        const bool not_consecutive=has_previous &&
            (frame_id<=last_frame_ || frame_id-last_frame_!=1);
        const bool size_changed=has_previous &&
            (width_!=inputs.render_width || height_!=inputs.render_height ||
             output_width_!=inputs.output_width ||
             output_height_!=inputs.output_height);
        last_frame_=frame_id;
        scene_=scene_id;
        width_=inputs.render_width;
        height_=inputs.render_height;
        output_width_=inputs.output_width;
        output_height_=inputs.output_height;
        if (scene_changed || size_changed) return Rejection::SceneChanged;
        if (not_consecutive) return Rejection::NonConsecutiveFrame;
        return Rejection::None;
    }
    void Reset() noexcept {
        last_frame_=scene_=0;
        width_=height_=output_width_=output_height_=0;
    }
private:
    std::uint64_t last_frame_{};
    std::uint64_t scene_{};
    std::uint32_t width_{},height_{},output_width_{},output_height_{};
};
} // namespace Eden::Graphics::Temporal
```

`extras/graphics/fsr31_vram_budget.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Exact nominal FSR 3.1.4 image sizes from the versioned Vulkan backend.
// This is a *preallocation* memory budget, not proof that PS5 has enough VRAM.
// Vulkan may add heap alignment, tiling and staging-buffer overhead.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::Graphics::Fsr31Budget {
constexpr std::uint64_t MiB=1024ULL*1024;
constexpr std::uint64_t AbsoluteLimit=512*MiB;
enum class Decision : std::uint8_t {
    Allowed, InvalidDimensions, ExceedsAbsoluteLimit, InsufficientDeviceMemory,
};
struct Dimensions {
    std::uint32_t render_width{};
    std::uint32_t render_height{};
    std::uint32_t output_width{};
    std::uint32_t output_height{};
};
struct Memory {
    std::uint64_t device_local_bytes{};
    std::uint64_t used_bytes{};
    bool usage_is_known{};
};
struct Result {
    Decision decision{Decision::InvalidDimensions};
    std::uint64_t nominal_bytes{};
    std::uint64_t required_bytes{};
};
[[nodiscard]] inline Result Evaluate(Dimensions dim, Memory memory) noexcept {
    const auto rw=dim.render_width, rh=dim.render_height;
    const auto ow=dim.output_width, oh=dim.output_height;
    if (rw<64 || rh<64 || rw>8192 || rh>8192 ||
        ow<rw || oh<rh || ow>8192 || oh>8192 ||
        ow>3ULL*rw || oh>3ULL*rh)
        return {};
    const auto render=static_cast<std::uint64_t>(rw)*rh;
    const auto output=static_cast<std::uint64_t>(ow)*oh;
    const auto half=static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::max(1U,rw/2))*
                    std::max(1U,rh/2);
    std::uint64_t nominal=0;
    // 2x accumulation R8, 2x luma R16F, 2x history RGBA8.
    nominal+=render*(2*1+2*2+2*4);
    // 2x internal output RGB16F(alpha) + final RGBA16F + new locks R8.
    nominal+=output*(2*8+8+1);
    // Farthest depth R16F + shading-change R8 @ half render size.
    nominal+=render*2 + half;
    // SPD mip chain uses R16G16F; >= 6 levels, down to 1x1.
    auto mw=std::max(1U,rw/2), mh=std::max(1U,rh/2);
    unsigned level=0;
    for (;;) {
        nominal+=static_cast<std::uint64_t>(mw)*mh*4;
        ++level;
        if (mw==1 && mh==1) break;
        mw=std::max(1U,mw/2);
        mh=std::max(1U,mh/2);
    }
    while (level++<6) nominal+=4;
    // Half-res depth + four render-size auxiliaries:
    // motion R16G16F, dilated depth R32F, nearest depth R32U, reactive RGBA8.
    nominal+=half*2+render*(4+4+4+4);
    // Frame info RGBA32F, SPD atomic uint, Lanczos R16 128x1,
    // default reactive R8.
    nominal+=16+4+256+1;
    // 12.5% image-padding overhead + 8 MiB descriptor/staging headroom.
    const auto required=nominal+nominal/8+8*MiB;
    if (required>AbsoluteLimit)
        return {Decision::ExceedsAbsoluteLimit,nominal,required};
    if (memory.device_local_bytes < required*4)
        return {Decision::InsufficientDeviceMemory,nominal,required};
    if (memory.usage_is_known) {
        // Keep at least 75% of available VRAM for textures, guest GPU
        // surfaces, shaders and frame generation. Unknown usage cannot
        // bypass AbsoluteLimit above, but has no invented free capacity.
        if (memory.device_local_bytes<=memory.used_bytes ||
            (memory.device_local_bytes-memory.used_bytes)/4<required)
            return {Decision::InsufficientDeviceMemory,nominal,required};
    }
    return {Decision::Allowed,nominal,required};
}
} // namespace Eden::Graphics::Fsr31Budget

```

`extras/graphics/mihawk_capture_fences.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Native Vulkan source-history capture ring. Owns only GPU submission serials:
// private VkImages and their final layout remain owned by MihawkVulkanResources.
// No screenshot-frame, CPU frame ID, or guessed timestamp is a GPU fence.
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::FeatureLab {

struct MihawkCapturePermit {
    std::uint64_t previous_gpu_tick = 0;
    std::uint8_t slot = 0;
    bool valid = false;
};

class MihawkCaptureFences {
public:
    template<class IsFree>
    MihawkCapturePermit Acquire(IsFree&& is_free) noexcept {
        if (quarantined_ || pending_) return {};
        const auto serial = busy_until_[next_slot_];
        if (serial && !is_free(serial)) return {};
        pending_ = true;
        return {serial, next_slot_, true};
    }
    // Previous real source must actually have been captured immediately
    // before this one. Pure guest frame IDs and clock estimates never stand
    // in for a GPU-completed captured history image.
    template<class IsFree>
    bool CanGenerate(const MihawkCapturePermit& permit, std::uint64_t real_id,
                     IsFree&& is_free) const noexcept {
        if (!permit.valid || !pending_ || quarantined_ ||
            permit.slot != next_slot_ || real_id == 0 ||
            previous_source_id_ == 0 || previous_source_id_ + 1 != real_id)
            return false;
        const auto previous_tick = busy_until_[permit.slot ^ 1];
        return previous_tick != 0 && is_free(previous_tick) &&
            (output_busy_until_ == 0 || is_free(output_busy_until_));
    }

    // Must be called immediately after Scheduler::Flush returns the actual
    // submission tick. A zero or regressing tick quarantines this ring.
    bool Commit(const MihawkCapturePermit& permit, std::uint64_t actual_tick,
                std::uint64_t source_id = 0, bool generated = false) noexcept {
        if (!pending_ || !permit.valid || permit.slot != next_slot_ ||
            permit.previous_gpu_tick != busy_until_[next_slot_])
            return false;
        pending_ = false;
        if (!actual_tick || actual_tick <= latest_gpu_tick_ ||
            actual_tick <= permit.previous_gpu_tick) {
            quarantined_ = true;
            return false;
        }
        busy_until_[next_slot_] = actual_tick;
        if (generated) {
            // The compute dispatch sampled the previous snapshot and wrote
            // the sole RGBA output until this same GPU tick is complete.
            busy_until_[next_slot_ ^ 1] = actual_tick;
            output_busy_until_ = actual_tick;
        }
        previous_source_id_ = source_id;
        latest_gpu_tick_ = actual_tick;
        next_slot_ ^= 1;
        return true;
    }
    // Aborting is legal only if the associated command buffer is not
    // submitted. It does not discard GPU serials from earlier frames.
    void AbortUnsubmitted() noexcept { pending_ = false; }
    // Only after the owning VkDevice is fully idle and image resources are
    // recreated. Never call this for a per-frame fallback.
    void ResetAfterDeviceIdle() noexcept { *this = MihawkCaptureFences{}; }
    bool Quarantined() const noexcept { return quarantined_; }
    bool Pending() const noexcept { return pending_; }
    std::uint64_t LatestGpuTick() const noexcept { return latest_gpu_tick_; }
    std::uint64_t OutputBusyUntil() const noexcept { return output_busy_until_; }
    std::uint64_t PreviousSourceId() const noexcept { return previous_source_id_; }
    std::uint64_t BusyUntil(std::uint32_t slot) const noexcept {
        return busy_until_[slot & 1];
    }

private:
    std::array<std::uint64_t, 2> busy_until_{};
    std::uint64_t latest_gpu_tick_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t previous_source_id_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t output_busy_until_ = 0;
    std::uint8_t next_slot_ = 0;
    bool quarantined_ = false;
    bool pending_ = false;
};
} // namespace Eden::FeatureLab
```

`extras/graphics/mihawk_native_surface_contract.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Native Vulkan *resource contract*, not an enabled frame generator.
// The presenter's recycled Frame* is NEVER an interpolation history image.
// Two dedicated, stable, same-extent snapshots plus a private RGBA8 output
// are required. These checks precede any optional GPU dispatch.
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::FeatureLab {

enum class NativeMihawkReject : std::uint8_t {
    None,
    Disabled,
    MissingCompute,
    MissingModel,
    NonNativeVulkan,
    UnsupportedFormat,
    InsufficientSlots,
    UnownedHistory,
    IncorrectHistoryFormat,
    InvalidOutputFormat,
    MissingPresentTransferUsage,
    InFlightResources,
    MissingBlitSupport,
    NativeHudPresent,
    NoPresenterSync,
    InvalidExtent
};

enum class ColorFormat : std::uint8_t {
    Rgba8Unorm,
    Bgra8Unorm,
    Other
};

struct MihawkSurfaceCapabilities {
    bool enabled = false;                 // qualified backend actually built
    bool native_vulkan = false;
    bool compute_and_storage = false;
    bool model_verified_and_loaded = false;
    bool blit_rgba_to_present = false;     // both formats support src/dst BLIT
    bool owned_history_pair = false;
    bool history_matches_source_format = false;
    bool private_output_rgba8_storage = false;
    bool present_image_transfer_dst = false;
    bool history_descriptor_slots_fenced = false;
    bool present_queue_ordered = false;
    bool native_hud_absent = false;  // Encore's own HUD, not the guest's score/menu
    std::uint8_t available_present_frames = 0;
    std::uint32_t width = 0, height = 0;
    ColorFormat compositor_format = ColorFormat::Other;
};

constexpr NativeMihawkReject CheckNativeMihawkSurface(
    const MihawkSurfaceCapabilities& x) noexcept {
    if (!x.enabled) return NativeMihawkReject::Disabled;
    if (!x.native_vulkan) return NativeMihawkReject::NonNativeVulkan;
    if (!x.compute_and_storage) return NativeMihawkReject::MissingCompute;
    if (!x.model_verified_and_loaded) return NativeMihawkReject::MissingModel;
    if (!x.width || !x.height || x.width > 7680 || x.height > 4320)
        return NativeMihawkReject::InvalidExtent;
    if (x.compositor_format != ColorFormat::Rgba8Unorm &&
        x.compositor_format != ColorFormat::Bgra8Unorm)
        return NativeMihawkReject::UnsupportedFormat;
    // This reserves at least a real frame, a synthetic frame and one spare.
    if (x.available_present_frames < 3) return NativeMihawkReject::InsufficientSlots;
    if (!x.owned_history_pair) return NativeMihawkReject::UnownedHistory;
    if (!x.history_matches_source_format) return NativeMihawkReject::IncorrectHistoryFormat;
    if (!x.private_output_rgba8_storage) return NativeMihawkReject::InvalidOutputFormat;
    if (!x.present_image_transfer_dst) return NativeMihawkReject::MissingPresentTransferUsage;
    if (!x.history_descriptor_slots_fenced) return NativeMihawkReject::InFlightResources;
    if (!x.present_queue_ordered) return NativeMihawkReject::NoPresenterSync;
    if (!x.native_hud_absent) return NativeMihawkReject::NativeHudPresent;
    // The source may be BGRA, but the network writes *RGBA8*. A dedicated
    // storage image must be blitted (including format conversion if BGRA).
    // Even RGBA->RGBA requires that BLIT_SRC and BLIT_DST be supported.
    if (!x.blit_rgba_to_present)
        return NativeMihawkReject::MissingBlitSupport;
    return NativeMihawkReject::None;
}
} // namespace Eden::FeatureLab
```

`extras/graphics/mihawk_session_resize.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Device/session switch handling independent of the PS5 render thread.
// A Vulkan image group is keyed by extent AND composition format.
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::FeatureLab {

enum class MihawkSessionAction : std::uint8_t {
    Keep, Initialize, RecreateAfterGpuIdle, InvalidTarget
};

constexpr MihawkSessionAction ChooseMihawkSessionAction(
    bool session_ready, std::uint32_t old_width, std::uint32_t old_height,
    VkFormat old_format, std::uint32_t new_width, std::uint32_t new_height,
    VkFormat new_format) noexcept {
    if (!new_width || !new_height || new_width > 3840 || new_height > 2160 ||
        (new_format != VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM &&
         new_format != VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM))
        return MihawkSessionAction::InvalidTarget;
    if (!session_ready) return MihawkSessionAction::Initialize;
    return old_width == new_width && old_height == new_height &&
                   old_format == new_format
               ? MihawkSessionAction::Keep
               : MihawkSessionAction::RecreateAfterGpuIdle;
}
} // namespace Eden::FeatureLab
```
