`headless/game_files.h`:

```h
// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright 2026 Oliv3rmoon
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// File selection for the nine extensions recognized by Encore's game picker:
// NSP/XCI, their NCZ-compressed NSZ/XCZ variants, and direct NRO/NSO/NCA/NAX/KIP.
// Direct inputs can require external program contents and are not guaranteed
// to boot. Internal .ncz, NSO LZ4 and ZBIC/zstd are not standalone games.
#pragma once
#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <charconv>
#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <system_error>
#include <vector>

namespace Eden {
inline bool EndsWithNoCase(std::string_view name, std::string_view suffix) {
    if (name.size() < suffix.size()) return false;
    name.remove_prefix(name.size() - suffix.size());
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < suffix.size(); ++i)
        if (std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(name[i])) != suffix[i]) return false;
    return true;
}
// Read as an NSP: a package of NCAs.
inline bool IsPackageFile(std::string_view name) {
    return EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nsp") || EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nsz");
}
// Read as an XCI: a game card's image.
inline bool IsCardImageFile(std::string_view name) {
    return EndsWithNoCase(name, ".xci") || EndsWithNoCase(name, ".xcz");
}
inline bool IsNupFile(std::string_view name) {
#ifdef EDEN_NUP_V1_RUNTIME
    // Only a P5-qualified runtime may offer NUP to the game picker.
    // The core's signature probe still decides whether it can be loaded.
    return EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nup");
#else
    (void)name;
    return false;
#endif
}
// Eden also has dedicated NRO, NSO, NCA, NAX and KIP loaders. These may be
// standalone homebrew, program partitions or system components, not necessarily
// complete game containers. Keep them selectable; let the native core loader
// determine whether enough content exists to boot the selection.
inline bool IsDirectLoaderFile(std::string_view name) {
    return EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nro") || EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nso") ||
           EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nca") || EndsWithNoCase(name, ".nax") ||
           EndsWithNoCase(name, ".kip");
}
inline bool IsGameFile(std::string_view name) {
    return IsPackageFile(name) || IsCardImageFile(name) ||
           IsDirectLoaderFile(name) || IsNupFile(name);
}
// Folder classification runs for every ROM scan entry. Match the fixed ASCII
// tokens directly rather than allocating and lowercasing a temporary string.
inline bool StartsWithNoCase(std::string_view name, std::string_view lowercase_prefix) {
    if (name.size() < lowercase_prefix.size()) return false;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lowercase_prefix.size(); ++i)
        if (std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(name[i])) != lowercase_prefix[i])
            return false;
    return true;
}
inline bool EqualsNoCase(std::string_view name, std::string_view lowercase) {
    return name.size() == lowercase.size() && StartsWithNoCase(name, lowercase);
}
inline bool IsAddOnContainerName(std::string_view name) {
    return EqualsNoCase(name, "updates") || EqualsNoCase(name, "update") ||
           EqualsNoCase(name, "patches") || EqualsNoCase(name, "patch") ||
           EqualsNoCase(name, "dlc") || EqualsNoCase(name, "aoc") ||
           EqualsNoCase(name, "addon") || EqualsNoCase(name, "addons") ||
           EqualsNoCase(name, "add-on") || EqualsNoCase(name, "add-ons") ||
           EqualsNoCase(name, "add_on");
}
// Apply the same update/DLC safeguard to newly discovered packages and
// previously saved selections. A stale persisted path is not proof of a base.
inline bool IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(std::string_view name) {
    if (IsAddOnContainerName(name)) return true;
    for (const char* prefix : {"update_", "update-", "patch_", "patch-",
                               "dlc_", "dlc-", "aoc_", "aoc-", "addon_", "addon-"}) {
        if (StartsWithNoCase(name, prefix)) return true;
    }
    return false;
}
// Extracted AOC stores can also sit beneath arbitrary wrapper names.
// Discover only canonical 16-digit hex AOC Title IDs; the vendor filesystem
// revalidates IDs and the actual read-only RomFS before mounting.
inline bool LooksLikeExtractedAocTitleId(std::string_view name) {
    if (name.size() != 16) return false;
    std::uint64_t id = 0;
    const auto [end, error] =
        std::from_chars(name.data(), name.data() + name.size(), id, 16);
    return error == std::errc{} && end == name.data() + name.size() &&
           (id & 0x1fffU) >= 0x1000U && (id & 0x1fffU) <= 0x17ffU;
}
inline bool IsExtractedAssetFolderName(std::string_view name) {
    return EqualsNoCase(name, "romfs") || EqualsNoCase(name, "exefs");
}

// A saved extracted title is either <title>/main (legacy), or
// <title>/[subdirectories]/exefs/main. The first component is always the
// title folder in roms/. Nested updates/DLC must never become base titles.
// No arbitrary file paths, parent traversal or symlinked entries are allowed.
inline bool IsDeconstructedGameSelection(std::string_view name) {
    constexpr std::string_view suffix{"/main"};
    if (!name.ends_with(suffix)) return false;
    name.remove_suffix(suffix.size());
    if (name.empty() || name.size() > 250) return false;
    std::size_t segments = 0;
    std::string_view last;
    while (!name.empty()) {
        const auto slash = name.find('/');
        const auto segment = name.substr(0, slash);
        if (segment.empty() || segment == "." || segment == ".." ||
            IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(segment) || (segment.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(segment, "romfs")))
            return false;
        for (unsigned char c : segment)
            if (c < 32 || c == 127 || c == '\\') return false;
        last = segment;
        ++segments;
        if (segments > 8) return false;
        if (slash == std::string_view::npos) break;
        name.remove_prefix(slash + 1);
    }
    return segments == 1 || (segments >= 2 && last.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(last, "exefs"));
}

// Symlink-free detection avoids treating arbitrary ROM directories or
// symlink targets outside the selected storage root as launchable titles.
inline bool IsDeconstructedGameDirectory(const std::filesystem::path& folder) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    std::error_code error;
    const auto directory_status = fs::symlink_status(folder, error);
    if (error || !fs::is_directory(directory_status) || fs::is_symlink(directory_status))
        return false;
    for (const char* name : {"main", "main.npdm"}) {
        error.clear();
        const auto status = fs::symlink_status(folder / name, error);
        if (error || !fs::is_regular_file(status) || fs::is_symlink(status))
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}
// Avoid following symlinks at every directory level, not just at main.npdm.
inline bool IsSafeExtractedDirectory(const std::filesystem::path& folder) {
    std::error_code error;
    const auto status = std::filesystem::symlink_status(folder, error);
    return !error && std::filesystem::is_directory(status) &&
           !std::filesystem::is_symlink(status);
}

// Returns a title-relative file path such as "main" or
// "base/exefs/main". The search is bounded, deterministic and scans only
// under the selected top-level title; it never descends into RomFS/assets,
// patches or add-on folders.
inline std::string FindDeconstructedGameMain(const std::filesystem::path& title) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title)) return {};
    // Root-level content stores are not games, even when an update happens
    // to carry its own valid ExeFS. Only <title>/base is a launchable title.
    const auto root_name = title.filename().string();
    if (IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(root_name) || (root_name.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(root_name, "romfs")))
        return {};
    if (IsDeconstructedGameDirectory(title)) return "main";
    // Canonical dumps must remain discoverable even when this title folder
    // has hundreds of unrelated assets. Probe only validated, symlink-free
    // base/ExeFS paths before the generic bounded wrapper search.
    for (const char* base_name : {"base", "Base", "BASE"}) {
        const auto base = title / base_name;
        if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(base)) continue;
        for (const char* exefs_name : {"exefs", "ExeFS", "EXEFS"}) {
            const auto executable = base / exefs_name;
            if (IsSafeExtractedDirectory(executable) &&
                IsDeconstructedGameDirectory(executable))
                return std::string(base_name) + "/" + exefs_name + "/main";
        }
    }
    std::size_t visited = 0;
    bool incomplete = false;
    std::vector<std::string> candidates;
    const auto search = [&](const auto& self, const fs::path& dir,
                            const std::string& relative, unsigned depth) -> void {
        if (incomplete) return;
        if (depth > 6 || ++visited > 128 || candidates.size() > 1) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        if (const auto leaf = dir.filename().string();
            leaf.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(leaf, "exefs") && IsDeconstructedGameDirectory(dir)) {
            candidates.push_back(relative + "/main");
            return;
        }
        std::error_code error;
        std::vector<fs::path> subdirs;
        std::size_t examined = 0;
        for (fs::directory_iterator it{dir, fs::directory_options::none, error},
                                    end;
             !error && it != end; it.increment(error)) {
            // An incomplete wrapper walk cannot prove that an ExeFS is
            // unique. A second hidden base might otherwise get ignored.
            if (++examined > 512 || subdirs.size() >= 128) {
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            const auto path = it->path();
            const auto name = path.filename().string();
            if (name.empty() || name.front() == '.' ||
                (name.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(name, "romfs")) ||
                IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(name)) continue;
            std::error_code status_error;
            const auto status = fs::symlink_status(path, status_error);
            if (status_error) {
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            if (!fs::is_symlink(status) && fs::is_directory(status))
                subdirs.push_back(path);
        }
        if (error) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        std::sort(subdirs.begin(), subdirs.end(), [](const fs::path& a, const fs::path& b) {
            const auto rank = [](const fs::path& p) {
                const auto name = p.filename().string();
                return name.size() == 4 && EndsWithNoCase(name, "base") ? 0 :
                       name.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(name, "exefs") ? 1 : 2;
            };
            if (rank(a) != rank(b)) return rank(a) < rank(b);
            return a.filename().string() < b.filename().string();
        });
        for (const auto& path : subdirs) {
            if (incomplete) return;
            const auto segment = path.filename().string();
            const auto next = relative.empty() ? segment : relative + "/" + segment;
            self(self, path, next, depth + 1);
        }
    };
    search(search, title, "", 0);
    return !incomplete && candidates.size() == 1 ? candidates.front() : std::string{};
}

inline bool IsSafeDeconstructedGamePath(const std::filesystem::path& roms_root,
                                        std::string_view selection) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!IsDeconstructedGameSelection(selection) || !IsSafeExtractedDirectory(roms_root))
        return false;
    fs::path path = roms_root;
    const fs::path relative{std::string(selection)};
    for (const auto& part : relative.parent_path()) {
        path /= part;
        if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(path)) return false;
    }
    return IsDeconstructedGameDirectory(path);
}

// Accept packaged base titles inside a title folder, while excluding extracted
// updates/DLC and unsafe path components. Content type still needs metadata.
inline bool IsNestedGameFileSelection(std::string_view selection) {
    if (selection.empty() || selection.size() > 255) return false;
    if (!IsPackageFile(selection) && !IsCardImageFile(selection) &&
        !IsNupFile(selection)) return false;
    const auto last_slash = selection.find_last_of('/');
    if (last_slash == std::string_view::npos || last_slash == 0 ||
        last_slash == selection.size() - 1) return false;
    const auto basename = selection.substr(last_slash + 1);
    const auto extension_dot = basename.find_last_of('.');
    if (basename.front() == '.' || extension_dot == std::string_view::npos ||
        IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(basename.substr(0, extension_dot)))
        return false;
    std::size_t levels = 0;
    while (!selection.empty()) {
        const auto slash = selection.find('/');
        const auto segment = selection.substr(0, slash);
        if (segment.empty() || segment == "." || segment == "..") return false;
        for (const unsigned char c : segment)
            if (c < 32 || c == 127 || c == '\\') return false;
        if (slash == std::string_view::npos) break;
        if (IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(segment) || (segment.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(segment, "romfs")))
            return false;
        if (++levels > 8) return false;
        selection.remove_prefix(slash + 1);
    }
    return levels >= 1;
}

// Look for a packaged base, allowing one or more ordinary wrapper folders.
// Prefer a uniquely named "base.*" or "game.*" package. If multiple possible
// base packages exist, do not guess or accidentally launch an update/DLC.
inline std::string FindNestedGamePackage(const std::filesystem::path& title) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title)) return {};
    const auto root_name = title.filename().string();
    if (IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(root_name) || (root_name.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(root_name, "romfs")))
        return {};
    std::vector<std::string> candidates;
    std::size_t visited = 0;
    bool incomplete = false;
    const auto scan = [&](const auto& self, const fs::path& directory,
                          const std::string& relative, unsigned depth) -> void {
        if (incomplete) return;
        // Ignoring deeper wrapper branches can select a shallow package
        // while hiding a competing base/update in the same title. A capped
        // walk is an unknown library, not proof of a unique candidate.
        if (depth > 6) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        if (++visited > 128 || candidates.size() > 64) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        std::error_code error;
        std::vector<fs::path> subdirs;
        std::size_t examined = 0;
        for (fs::directory_iterator it{directory, fs::directory_options::none, error},
                                    end;
             !error && it != end; it.increment(error)) {
            // Never select a base from a truncated, iteration-order-dependent
            // subset that may hide a competing package or an update.
            if (++examined > 512) {
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            const auto path = it->path();
            const auto name = path.filename().string();
            if (name.empty() || name.front() == '.' || IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(name) ||
                (name.size() == 5 && EndsWithNoCase(name, "romfs"))) continue;
            // One non-following stat per entry. The old directory probe and
            // subsequent file probe both called symlink_status for every NSP.
            std::error_code entry_error;
            const auto status = fs::symlink_status(path, entry_error);
            if (entry_error) {
                // A package can be removed or a ROM volume can disappear
                // between directory iteration and stat. Do not silently
                // choose another candidate from an incomplete library.
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            if (fs::is_symlink(status)) continue;
            if (fs::is_directory(status)) {
                subdirs.push_back(path);
                continue;
            }
            if (!fs::is_regular_file(status) ||
                (!IsPackageFile(name) && !IsCardImageFile(name) &&
                 !IsNupFile(name))) continue;
            if (IsReservedAddOnPackageStem(path.stem().string())) continue;
            const auto candidate = relative.empty() ? name : relative + "/" + name;
            // The validator consumes a ROM-root-relative persisted selection.
            // A package in the title folder itself is still nested from roms/.
            const auto selection = title.filename().string() + "/" + candidate;
            if (IsNestedGameFileSelection(selection)) candidates.push_back(candidate);
        }
        if (error) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        std::sort(subdirs.begin(), subdirs.end(), [](const fs::path& a, const fs::path& b) {
            const auto a_name = a.filename().string();
            const auto b_name = b.filename().string();
            if (a_name == "base" && b_name != "base") return true;
            if (b_name == "base" && a_name != "base") return false;
            return a_name < b_name;
        });
        for (const auto& path : subdirs) {
            if (incomplete) return;
            if (visited >= 128 || candidates.size() > 64) {
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            const auto name = path.filename().string();
            self(self, path, relative.empty() ? name : relative + "/" + name, depth + 1);
        }
    };
    scan(scan, title, "", 0);
    if (incomplete || candidates.empty() || candidates.size() > 64) return {};
    std::sort(candidates.begin(), candidates.end());
    std::vector<std::string> named_base;
    for (const auto& candidate : candidates) {
        std::string stem = fs::path(candidate).stem().string();
        std::transform(stem.begin(), stem.end(), stem.begin(),
                       [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
        if (stem == "base" || stem == "game") named_base.push_back(candidate);
    }
    if (named_base.size() == 1) return named_base.front();
    if (named_base.size() > 1) return {};
    if (candidates.size() == 1) return candidates.front();
    // A unique game-card image is a safer base candidate than an NSP when
    // a mixed folder also contains packaged updates and DLC. Never guess
    // between two NSPs or two card images without content metadata.
    std::string unique_card;
    for (const auto& candidate : candidates) {
        if (!IsCardImageFile(candidate)) continue;
        if (!unique_card.empty()) return {};
        unique_card = candidate;
    }
    return unique_card;
}

inline std::string FindGameFolderInput(const std::filesystem::path& title) {
    if (const auto extracted = FindDeconstructedGameMain(title); !extracted.empty())
        return extracted;
    return FindNestedGamePackage(title);
}

inline bool IsSafeNestedGameFilePath(const std::filesystem::path& roms_root,
                                    std::string_view selection) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!IsNestedGameFileSelection(selection) || !IsSafeExtractedDirectory(roms_root))
        return false;
    fs::path path = roms_root;
    const fs::path relative{std::string(selection)};
    for (const auto& part : relative.parent_path()) {
        path /= part;
        if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(path)) return false;
    }
    std::error_code error;
    const auto status = fs::symlink_status(path / relative.filename(), error);
    return !error && fs::is_regular_file(status) && !fs::is_symlink(status);
}

// Discover add-on content roots without treating each update/DLC as a game.
// These roots may contain arbitrary deeper subdirectories: the existing
// ExternalContentProvider classifies packages by Nintendo title metadata.
// Keep traversal bounded and do not inspect extracted ExeFS/RomFS payloads.
inline std::vector<std::filesystem::path> FindAddOnContentDirectories(
    const std::filesystem::path& title_root, bool* scan_complete = nullptr) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    // Distinguish a genuinely empty add-on directory from an incomplete
    // traversal. The metadata scanner must never publish a partial snapshot.
    if (scan_complete) *scan_complete = false;
    std::vector<fs::path> found;
    if (!IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title_root)) return found;
    // The base may be extracted or packaged in an arbitrary wrapper. Its
    // package must never be counted as an additional content package.
    const auto base_relative = FindGameFolderInput(title_root);
    const fs::path base_package = base_relative.empty() ? fs::path{} :
                                  title_root / fs::path(base_relative);
    // A partial directory walk must not publish only whichever DLC happened
    // to be enumerated first. Preserve a bounded scan but invalidate the
    // entire discovery result if a directory exceeds that bound.
    constexpr std::size_t MaxVisited = 256;
    constexpr std::size_t MaxEntriesPerDirectory = 512;
    constexpr std::size_t MaxRoots = 128;
    std::size_t visited = 0;
    bool incomplete = false;
    const auto scan = [&](const auto& self, const fs::path& dir, unsigned depth) -> void {
        if (incomplete) return;
        // A depth cap must never silently publish only the add-ons encountered
        // in shallower siblings: discard the whole incomplete discovery.
        if (depth > 5) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        if (++visited > MaxVisited || found.size() > MaxRoots) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        std::error_code error;
        std::vector<fs::path> subdirs;
        bool loose_add_on = false;
        std::size_t examined = 0;
        for (fs::directory_iterator it{dir, fs::directory_options::none, error},
                                    end;
             !error && it != end; it.increment(error)) {
            if (++examined > MaxEntriesPerDirectory) {
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            const auto path = it->path();
            const auto name = path.filename().string();
            if (name.empty() || name.front() == '.') continue;
            // Preserve symlink rejection without two filesystem probes
            // for each ordinary file in a wrapper or DLC directory.
            std::error_code entry_error;
            const auto status = fs::symlink_status(path, entry_error);
            if (entry_error) {
                // Even ENOENT can mean an update/DLC disappeared between
                // iterator discovery and symlink_status. Skipping the entry
                // would publish a partial catalogue from a moving library.
                incomplete = true;
                return;
            }
            if (fs::is_symlink(status)) continue;
            if (fs::is_directory(status)) {
                // Do not descend into extracted payloads or into a detected
                // add-on container: the native package provider handles the
                // latter recursively using package CNMT/Title ID metadata.
                if (IsExtractedAssetFolderName(name)) continue;
                if (IsAddOnContainerName(name) ||
                    LooksLikeExtractedAocTitleId(name)) {
                    // A full AOC Title ID is enough to locate an extracted
                    // DLC candidate even in custom/wrapper/ directories.
                    found.push_back(path);
                } else {
                    subdirs.push_back(path);
                }
                continue;
            }
            // A package with any name in any wrapper can be an update/DLC.
            // Do not rely on a "dlc" filename prefix; the native provider
            // classifies its actual content records. Ignore symlinks.
            if (fs::is_regular_file(status) &&
                (IsPackageFile(name) || IsCardImageFile(name)) &&
                path != base_package)
                loose_add_on = true;
        }
        if (error || found.size() > MaxRoots) {
            incomplete = true;
            return;
        }
        if (loose_add_on) {
            // Provider takes directories, not individual packages. This root
            // includes all local packages and their nested add-on wrappers.
            // Avoid registering descendants twice or opening extracted RomFS.
            found.push_back(dir);
            return;
        }
        std::sort(subdirs.begin(), subdirs.end());
        for (const auto& child : subdirs) {
            if (incomplete) return;
            self(self, child, depth + 1);
        }
    };
    scan(scan, title_root, 0);
    if (incomplete || found.size() > MaxRoots) return {};
    std::sort(found.begin(), found.end());
    found.erase(std::unique(found.begin(), found.end()), found.end());
    // Keep only minimal roots; a provider scans their descendants. Build a
    // separate result to avoid mutating the same vector under std::remove_if.
    std::vector<fs::path> minimal;
    for (const auto& child : found) {
        bool covered = false;
        for (const auto& parent : found) {
            if (child == parent) continue;
            const auto relative = child.lexically_relative(parent);
            if (!relative.empty() && *relative.begin() != ".." &&
                *relative.begin() != ".") {
                covered = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!covered) minimal.push_back(child);
    }
    if (scan_complete) *scan_complete = true;
    return minimal;
}
} // namespace Eden
```

`headless/game_liveness.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// Low-overhead, developer-only evidence for suspected *in-game* GPU stalls.
// Sampling is from the existing one-second boot watchdog thread, not the
// guest/JIT/GPU hot path. Never kill or restart a guest based on these hints.
// Counter absence, pause screens and deliberate suspend can look alike.
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

namespace Eden::GameLiveness {
struct Counters {
    std::uint64_t dispatches = 0;
    std::uint64_t draws = 0;
};
struct Result {
    bool suspected = false;
    std::uint64_t seconds_without_progress = 0;
    bool established_gpu_progress = false;
};
class Probe {
    Counters prior_{};
    std::uint64_t last_progress_second_ = 0;
    bool initialized_ = false;
    bool witnessed_gpu_progress_ = false;
    unsigned total_reports_ = 0;
    unsigned reports_this_stall_ = 0;
public:
    void Reset() noexcept { *this = Probe{}; }
    Result Observe(Counters now, std::uint64_t second) noexcept {
        if (!initialized_) {
            prior_ = now;
            last_progress_second_ = second;
            initialized_ = true;
            return {};
        }
        if (second < last_progress_second_) {
            // Clock reset / impossible timestamp; never signal a freeze.
            last_progress_second_ = second;
            prior_ = now;
            witnessed_gpu_progress_ = false;
            reports_this_stall_ = 0;
            return {};
        }
        if (prior_.dispatches != now.dispatches || prior_.draws != now.draws) {
            witnessed_gpu_progress_ = true;
            last_progress_second_ = second;
            prior_ = now;
            reports_this_stall_ = 0;
        }
        Result result{};
        result.established_gpu_progress = witnessed_gpu_progress_;
        if (!witnessed_gpu_progress_) return result;
        result.seconds_without_progress = second - last_progress_second_;
        // Max FOUR reports over the entire guest session. A temporary
        // pause may resume; do not flood kernel/SD logs with repeated events.
        if (total_reports_ < 4 &&
            result.seconds_without_progress >= (std::uint64_t{reports_this_stall_} + 1) * 30) {
            ++total_reports_;
            ++reports_this_stall_;
            result.suspected = true;
        }
        return result;
    }
};
} // namespace Eden::GameLiveness

```

`headless/glyph_overrides_runtime.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// In-game PlayStation button ART, not DualSense input mapping.
// Declarative per-title catalogue, just like encore-overrides. Once at
// launch, gate an installed RomFS graphic mod against the current update.
// Unsupported/unverified versions retain the game's native artwork.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include <nlohmann/json.hpp>

#include "mods.h"
#include "glyph_overrides_generated.h"
#include "glyph_sha256.h"

namespace Eden::GlyphOverrides {
inline constexpr std::string_view kModName = "Eden Encore PS Glyphs";
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxCatalogBytes = 128u * 1024u;
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxEvidenceBytes = 128u * 1024u;
inline constexpr std::uintmax_t kMaxGraphicFileBytes = 128ull * 1024 * 1024;
inline constexpr std::uintmax_t kMaxGraphicPackBytes = 512ull * 1024 * 1024;
inline constexpr bool FitsGraphicPackBudget(std::uintmax_t verified,
                                            std::uintmax_t next) noexcept {
    return verified <= kMaxGraphicPackBytes &&
           next <= kMaxGraphicFileBytes &&
           next <= kMaxGraphicPackBytes - verified;
}

enum class Style { PlayStation, Nintendo };
enum class State { Unsupported, Disabled, MissingMod, UnknownVersion, VersionMismatch,
                   EvidenceMismatch, Enabled };
inline const char* StateName(State state) noexcept {
    switch (state) {
    case State::Unsupported: return "unsupported";
    case State::Disabled: return "nintendo_selected";
    case State::MissingMod: return "mod_missing";
    case State::UnknownVersion: return "update_version_unknown";
    case State::VersionMismatch: return "update_version_mismatch";
    case State::EvidenceMismatch: return "pack_evidence_mismatch";
    case State::Enabled: return "playstation_art_active";
    }
    return "invalid";
}
struct Rule {
    std::uint64_t title = 0;
    std::string update_version;
};
struct Catalogue {
    bool valid = false;
    int revision = 0;
    std::vector<Rule> rules;
};
inline bool ParseHex(std::string_view input, std::uint64_t* value) noexcept {
    if (!value || input.size() != 16) return false;
    std::uint64_t parsed = 0;
    for (unsigned char c : input) {
        unsigned digit = 0;
        if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') digit = c - '0';
        else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') digit = c - 'a' + 10;
        else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') digit = c - 'A' + 10;
        else return false;
        parsed = (parsed << 4) | digit;
    }
    *value = parsed;
    return parsed != 0;
}
inline bool ParseCatalogue(std::string_view text, Catalogue* output) {
    if (!output || text.empty() || text.size() > kMaxCatalogBytes) return false;
    try {
        const auto root = nlohmann::json::parse(text.begin(), text.end());
        if (!root.is_object() || root.size() != 3 ||
            !root.contains("schema_version") || !root["schema_version"].is_number_integer() ||
            root["schema_version"].get<int>() != 2 ||
            !root.contains("revision") || !root["revision"].is_number_integer() ||
            root["revision"].get<int>() < 0 ||
            !root.contains("titles") || !root["titles"].is_array() ||
            root["titles"].size() > 256) return false;
        Catalogue parsed;
        parsed.revision = root["revision"].get<int>();
        for (const auto& item : root["titles"]) {
            if (!item.is_object() || item.size() != 2 ||
                !item.contains("title_id") || !item["title_id"].is_string() ||
                !item.contains("update_version") || !item["update_version"].is_string())
                return false;
            Rule rule;
            if (!ParseHex(item["title_id"].get<std::string>(), &rule.title))
                return false;
            rule.update_version = item["update_version"].get<std::string>();
            if (rule.update_version.empty() || rule.update_version.size() > 64 ||
                std::any_of(rule.update_version.begin(), rule.update_version.end(), [](unsigned char c) {
                    return c < 32 || c == 127;
                })) return false;
            // One build per title+display-version: ambiguities fail closed.
            if (std::any_of(parsed.rules.begin(), parsed.rules.end(), [&](const Rule& old) {
                    return old.title == rule.title && old.update_version == rule.update_version;
                })) return false;
            parsed.rules.push_back(std::move(rule));
        }
        parsed.valid = true;
        *output = std::move(parsed);
        return true;
    } catch (...) { return false; }
}
inline bool ReadBounded(const Mods::fs::path& file, std::size_t limit, std::string* out) {
    if (!out) return false;
    std::error_code ec;
    if (Mods::fs::is_symlink(file, ec) || ec ||
        !Mods::fs::is_regular_file(file, ec) || ec ||
        Mods::fs::file_size(file, ec) > limit || ec) return false;
    std::ifstream input(file, std::ios::binary);
    if (!input) return false;
    out->clear();
    std::array<char, 4096> buffer{};
    // A pre-open file_size check alone is not a bound. The file could grow
    // after stat() (or a replace could race the open). Never use an unbounded
    // istreambuf iterator for external JSON, even on developer builds.
    for (;;) {
        input.read(buffer.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(buffer.size()));
        const auto bytes = input.gcount();
        if (bytes < 0 || static_cast<std::size_t>(bytes) > limit - out->size()) {
            out->clear();
            return false;
        }
        if (bytes) out->append(buffer.data(), static_cast<std::size_t>(bytes));
        if (input.eof()) break;
        if (!input) {
            out->clear();
            return false;
        }
    }
    // Detect truncation/replacement while reading as well as oversize.
    const auto final_size = Mods::fs::file_size(file, ec);
    if (ec || final_size != out->size()) {
        out->clear();
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}
inline Catalogue BuiltInCatalogue() {
    Catalogue built_in;
    built_in.valid = true;
    built_in.revision = GlyphOverridesGenerated::kRevision;
    for (const auto& entry : GlyphOverridesGenerated::kRules)
        built_in.rules.push_back({entry.title, entry.update_version});
    return built_in;
}
inline Catalogue LoadCatalogue(const Mods::fs::path& path) {
    Catalogue built_in = BuiltInCatalogue();
    std::string content;
    Catalogue remote;
    // Runtime updates may add support, never silently downgrade the embedded
    // source snapshot (same model as encore-overrides video profiles).
    if (ReadBounded(path, kMaxCatalogBytes, &content) &&
        ParseCatalogue(content, &remote) &&
        remote.revision > built_in.revision) return remote;
    return built_in;
}
inline bool EvidenceMatches(const Mods::fs::path& folder, const Rule& rule) {
    std::string text;
    if (!ReadBounded(folder / "eden-glyph-pack.json", kMaxEvidenceBytes, &text))
        return false;
    try {
        const auto value = nlohmann::json::parse(text);
        if (!value.is_object() || !value.contains("schema") ||
            !value["schema"].is_number_integer() || value["schema"].get<int>() != 2 ||
            !value.contains("title_id") || !value["title_id"].is_string() ||
            !value.contains("update_version") || !value["update_version"].is_string() ||
            !value.contains("rights") || !value["rights"].is_string() ||
            value["rights"].get<std::string>().empty() ||
            !value.contains("files") || !value["files"].is_array() ||
            value["files"].empty() || value["files"].size() > 64)
            return false;
        std::uint64_t evidence_title = 0;
        if (!ParseHex(value["title_id"].get<std::string>(), &evidence_title) ||
            evidence_title != rule.title ||
            value["update_version"].get<std::string>() != rule.update_version)
            return false;
        // Installer checks ORIGINAL RomFS bytes at packaging; launch checks
        // each replacement asset byte-for-byte via SHA-256. The original
        // file currently mounted by the emulator is still a separate gate.
        // Match the 512 MiB aggregate installer cap, not only the 128 MiB
        // per-file cap: otherwise an edited 64-file manifest could force
        // gigabytes of filesystem reads and freeze the game-launch path.
        std::uintmax_t verified_bytes = 0;
        // LayeredFS path names must be unambiguous regardless of a target
        // filesystem's case sensitivity. Two manifest rows for the same
        // lowercased path (or a file also acting as a parent directory)
        // could pass individual SHA checks but resolve to different bytes
        // depending on extraction order or host OS.
        std::vector<std::string> claimed_romfs_paths;
        for (const auto& item : value["files"]) {
            if (!item.is_object() || !item.contains("romfs_path") ||
                !item["romfs_path"].is_string() ||
                !item.contains("original_sha256") || !item["original_sha256"].is_string() ||
                !item.contains("replacement_sha256") || !item["replacement_sha256"].is_string()) return false;
            // Evidence must still be a file-hash-verified pack generated by
            // the installer. Valid declarations alone do NOT attest the
            // currently decrypted original RomFS on hardware.
            const auto hash_ok = [](const std::string& hash) {
                return hash.size() == 64 && std::all_of(hash.begin(), hash.end(),
                    [](unsigned char c) {
                        return (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f') ||
                               (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F');
                    });
            };
            if (!hash_ok(item["original_sha256"].get<std::string>()) ||
                !hash_ok(item["replacement_sha256"].get<std::string>()))
                return false;
            const std::string relative = item["romfs_path"].get<std::string>();
            if (relative.empty() || relative.size() > 240 ||
                relative.front() == '/' || relative.find('\\') != std::string::npos ||
                relative.find(':') != std::string::npos) return false;
            Mods::fs::path safe;
            for (const auto& segment : Mods::fs::path(relative)) {
                if (segment == "." || segment == ".." || segment.empty()) return false;
                safe /= segment;
            }
            // Refuse aliases via doubled separators, dot segments or
            // host-dependent path normalization before checking file hashes.
            if (safe.generic_string() != relative) return false;
            const std::string folded = Mods::Lower(relative);
            for (const auto& prior : claimed_romfs_paths) {
                if (folded == prior ||
                    (folded.size() > prior.size() &&
                     folded.compare(0, prior.size(), prior) == 0 &&
                     folded[prior.size()] == '/') ||
                    (prior.size() > folded.size() &&
                     prior.compare(0, folded.size(), folded) == 0 &&
                     prior[folded.size()] == '/'))
                    return false;
            }
            claimed_romfs_paths.push_back(folded);
            // Reject symlinks in any component, not only at the leaf.
            // These graphics are injected into the guest's RomFS and must
            // not escape the installed pack or point to executable mods.
            Mods::fs::path asset = folder / "romfs";
            std::error_code ec;
            if (Mods::fs::is_symlink(asset, ec) || ec) return false;
            for (const auto& part : safe) {
                asset /= part;
                if (Mods::fs::is_symlink(asset, ec) || ec) return false;
            }
            if (!Mods::fs::is_regular_file(asset, ec) || ec) return false;
            const auto bytes = Mods::fs::file_size(asset, ec);
            if (ec || !FitsGraphicPackBudget(verified_bytes, bytes)) return false;
            verified_bytes += bytes;
            const auto actual = GlyphIntegrity::FileSha256(asset, kMaxGraphicFileBytes);
            std::string expected = item["replacement_sha256"].get<std::string>();
            std::transform(expected.begin(), expected.end(), expected.begin(),
                           [](unsigned char c) { return static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)); });
            // The previous check only ensured *presence* of artwork; an
            // altered atlas with the same filename was silently admitted.
            // Hash the replacement once during launch before loading RomFS.
            if (!actual || *actual != expected) return false;
        }
        return true;
    } catch (...) { return false; }
}
// Version discovery can decrypt/open a game container to inspect NACP.
// Never do it for games without a published rule, absent graphic mods,
// or when PlayStation art is disabled. Especially important when the
// shared catalogue is empty: no all-library metadata penalty at all.
inline bool NeedsGameVersion(const Catalogue& catalogue, std::uint64_t title,
                             Style style, const std::vector<Mods::Mod>& mods) {
    if (!catalogue.valid || style == Style::Nintendo) return false;
    const bool candidate = std::any_of(catalogue.rules.begin(), catalogue.rules.end(),
        [&](const Rule& rule) { return rule.title == title; });
    if (!candidate) return false;
    return std::any_of(mods.begin(), mods.end(), [](const Mods::Mod& mod) {
        return Mods::Lower(mod.name) == Mods::Lower(kModName) && (mod.kinds & Mods::kFiles);
    });
}
inline State Select(const Catalogue& catalogue, std::uint64_t title,
                    std::string_view running_update_version, Style style,
                    const std::string& mods_root, const std::vector<Mods::Mod>& mods) {
    if (style == Style::Nintendo) return State::Disabled;
    if (!catalogue.valid) return State::Unsupported;
    const auto it = std::find_if(catalogue.rules.begin(), catalogue.rules.end(),
                                 [&](const Rule& rule) { return rule.title == title; });
    if (it == catalogue.rules.end()) return State::Unsupported;
    // Eden mod discovery is case-insensitive for titles but not for mod
    // payload order. Two visually identical mod names differing by case
    // can be applied together, with ambiguous graphic replacement order.
    const auto matching = [](const Mods::Mod& entry) {
        return Mods::Lower(entry.name) == Mods::Lower(kModName);
    };
    const auto count = std::count_if(mods.begin(), mods.end(), matching);
    if (count == 0) return State::MissingMod;
    if (count != 1) return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    const auto mod = std::find_if(mods.begin(), mods.end(), matching);
    if (mod->name != kModName || !(mod->kinds & Mods::kFiles))
        return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    if (running_update_version.empty()) return State::UnknownVersion;
    const auto rule = std::find_if(catalogue.rules.begin(), catalogue.rules.end(),
                                   [&](const Rule& r) {
                                       return r.title == title && r.update_version == running_update_version;
                                   });
    if (rule == catalogue.rules.end()) return State::VersionMismatch;
    // The ordinary mod loader chooses the first case-insensitive title
    // directory it encounters. Two folders with the same logical Title ID
    // can change which RomFS wins between filesystem enumerations. Require
    // exactly one unambiguous physical title folder for verified artwork.
    const std::string wanted_title = Mods::Lower(Mods::TitleName(title));
    unsigned title_folders = 0;
    for (const auto& entry : Mods::ListFolder(mods_root)) {
        if (Mods::Lower(entry.path().filename().string()) != wanted_title) continue;
        std::error_code symlink_error;
        if (!Mods::IsFolder(entry) ||
            Mods::fs::is_symlink(entry.path(), symlink_error) || symlink_error ||
            ++title_folders > 1) return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    }
    if (title_folders != 1) return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    const auto root = Mods::TitleFolder(mods_root, title);
    if (root.empty()) return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    const auto title_folder = Mods::fs::path(root);
    const auto pack_folder = title_folder / std::string(kModName);
    std::error_code ec;
    if (Mods::fs::is_symlink(title_folder, ec) || ec ||
        Mods::fs::is_symlink(pack_folder, ec) || ec ||
        !EvidenceMatches(pack_folder, *rule))
        return State::EvidenceMismatch;
    return State::Enabled;
}
} // namespace Eden::GlyphOverrides
```

`headless/glyph_sha256.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// Minimal bounded SHA-256 for validating installed in-game graphic assets.
// This does NOT authenticate the guest-original artwork currently mounted by Eden.
// Host-tested known vectors; a cryptographic signature of the catalogue is
// a separate distribution/trust problem. Never execute on the frame hotpath.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <optional>
#include <string>

namespace Eden::GlyphIntegrity {
class Sha256 {
    std::array<std::uint32_t, 8> state_{
        0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a,
        0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19};
    std::array<std::uint8_t, 64> buffer_{};
    std::size_t filled_ = 0;
    std::uint64_t bytes_ = 0;

    static constexpr std::array<std::uint32_t, 64> kRound{
        0x428a2f98,0x71374491,0xb5c0fbcf,0xe9b5dba5,0x3956c25b,0x59f111f1,0x923f82a4,0xab1c5ed5,
        0xd807aa98,0x12835b01,0x243185be,0x550c7dc3,0x72be5d74,0x80deb1fe,0x9bdc06a7,0xc19bf174,
        0xe49b69c1,0xefbe4786,0x0fc19dc6,0x240ca1cc,0x2de92c6f,0x4a7484aa,0x5cb0a9dc,0x76f988da,
        0x983e5152,0xa831c66d,0xb00327c8,0xbf597fc7,0xc6e00bf3,0xd5a79147,0x06ca6351,0x14292967,
        0x27b70a85,0x2e1b2138,0x4d2c6dfc,0x53380d13,0x650a7354,0x766a0abb,0x81c2c92e,0x92722c85,
        0xa2bfe8a1,0xa81a664b,0xc24b8b70,0xc76c51a3,0xd192e819,0xd6990624,0xf40e3585,0x106aa070,
        0x19a4c116,0x1e376c08,0x2748774c,0x34b0bcb5,0x391c0cb3,0x4ed8aa4a,0x5b9cca4f,0x682e6ff3,
        0x748f82ee,0x78a5636f,0x84c87814,0x8cc70208,0x90befffa,0xa4506ceb,0xbef9a3f7,0xc67178f2};
    static constexpr std::uint32_t Rot(std::uint32_t v, unsigned count) noexcept {
        return (v >> count) | (v << (32u - count));
    }
    void Block(const std::uint8_t* input) noexcept {
        std::array<std::uint32_t, 64> words{};
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i)
            words[i] = (std::uint32_t(input[i * 4]) << 24) |
                       (std::uint32_t(input[i * 4 + 1]) << 16) |
                       (std::uint32_t(input[i * 4 + 2]) << 8) | input[i * 4 + 3];
        for (unsigned i = 16; i < 64; ++i) {
            const auto a = words[i - 15], b = words[i - 2];
            words[i] = words[i - 16] + (Rot(a, 7) ^ Rot(a, 18) ^ (a >> 3)) +
                       words[i - 7] + (Rot(b, 17) ^ Rot(b, 19) ^ (b >> 10));
        }
        auto [a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h] = state_;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; ++i) {
            const auto choose = (e & f) ^ (~e & g);
            const auto majority = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);
            const auto t1 = h + (Rot(e, 6) ^ Rot(e, 11) ^ Rot(e, 25)) + choose +
                            kRound[i] + words[i];
            const auto t2 = (Rot(a, 2) ^ Rot(a, 13) ^ Rot(a, 22)) + majority;
            h = g; g = f; f = e; e = d + t1; d = c; c = b; b = a; a = t1 + t2;
        }
        state_[0] += a; state_[1] += b; state_[2] += c; state_[3] += d;
        state_[4] += e; state_[5] += f; state_[6] += g; state_[7] += h;
    }
public:
    void Update(const void* bytes, std::size_t size) noexcept {
        const auto* source = static_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(bytes);
        bytes_ += size;
        while (size != 0) {
            const std::size_t count = std::min(size, buffer_.size() - filled_);
            std::memcpy(buffer_.data() + filled_, source, count);
            filled_ += count; source += count; size -= count;
            if (filled_ == buffer_.size()) {
                Block(buffer_.data());
                filled_ = 0;
            }
        }
    }
    std::string FinishHex() noexcept {
        const std::uint64_t bits = bytes_ * 8;
        buffer_[filled_++] = 0x80;
        if (filled_ > 56) {
            std::fill(buffer_.begin() + filled_, buffer_.end(), 0);
            Block(buffer_.data());
            filled_ = 0;
        }
        std::fill(buffer_.begin() + filled_, buffer_.begin() + 56, 0);
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
            buffer_[56 + i] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(bits >> (56 - 8 * i));
        Block(buffer_.data());
        constexpr char alphabet[] = "0123456789abcdef";
        std::string out(64, '0');
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < 8; ++i)
            for (unsigned j = 0; j < 4; ++j) {
                const auto octet = static_cast<unsigned>((state_[i] >> (24 - 8 * j)) & 0xff);
                out[i * 8 + j * 2] = alphabet[octet >> 4];
                out[i * 8 + j * 2 + 1] = alphabet[octet & 15];
            }
        return out;
    }
};

// Reads a bounded file in 32 KiB chunks, checking I/O state; no allocation
// proportional to the graphics asset. Return nullopt on missing/truncated,
// oversized, unreadable or otherwise unstable files.
inline std::optional<std::string> FileSha256(
    const std::filesystem::path& path, std::uintmax_t max_bytes = 128u * 1024u * 1024u) {
    std::error_code error;
    const auto length = std::filesystem::file_size(path, error);
    if (error || length > max_bytes) return std::nullopt;
    std::ifstream input(path, std::ios::binary);
    if (!input) return std::nullopt;
    Sha256 hash;
    std::array<char, 32768> buffer{};
    std::uintmax_t observed = 0;
    while (input) {
        input.read(buffer.data(), static_cast<std::streamsize>(buffer.size()));
        const auto got = input.gcount();
        if (got < 0 || observed + static_cast<std::uintmax_t>(got) > max_bytes) return std::nullopt;
        if (got > 0) {
            hash.Update(buffer.data(), static_cast<std::size_t>(got));
            observed += static_cast<std::uintmax_t>(got);
        }
    }
    if (!input.eof() || observed != length) return std::nullopt;
    return hash.FinishHex();
}
} // namespace Eden::GlyphIntegrity
```

`headless/glyph_version.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// A game title's base control.nacp display-version, never its NSO Build ID.
// Shared by native metadata bridge and host-only C++ source regression.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstddef>
#include <string>

namespace Eden::GlyphVersion {
template <std::size_t N>
inline std::string FromNacp(const std::array<char, N>& raw) {
    if (N == 0 || N > 64) return {};
    const auto end = std::find(raw.begin(), raw.end(), '\0');
    if (end == raw.begin()) return {};
    std::string version(raw.begin(), end);
    // Source names and catalog rules intentionally use a narrow, stable
    // ASCII subset. Unrecognized metadata must fall back to Nintendo art.
    for (unsigned char c : version)
        if (!((c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') ||
              (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '.' || c == '_' ||
              c == '+' || c == '-' || c == ' ')) return {};
    return version;
}
} // namespace Eden::GlyphVersion
```

`headless/gpu_deferred_replay.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// GPU-owned dirty guest ranges must be split on transform boundaries.
#include "gpu_deferred_write_queue.h"
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>

namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite {
// Native opt-in source derivation still calls eager Enqueue before the guest
// backing-store write. Fail closed even if cpu_write_defer is toggled at
// runtime: this must remain false until ALL producer/read/fence paths are
// integrated and qualified with post-store publication semantics.
inline constexpr bool kNativePostStorePublicationReady = false;
// The origin belongs to the guest's HandleRasterizerWrite invocation, not
// whichever host worker later drains or dispatches a GPU command. The GPU
// thread and all unrelated threads have NoGuestCore by default.
inline constexpr unsigned NoGuestCore = Queue::Cores;
inline thread_local unsigned guest_write_origin_core = NoGuestCore;
struct ScopedGuestWriteOrigin final {
    const unsigned previous;
    explicit ScopedGuestWriteOrigin(unsigned core) noexcept
        : previous{guest_write_origin_core} {
        guest_write_origin_core = core < Queue::Cores ? core : NoGuestCore;
    }
    ~ScopedGuestWriteOrigin() { guest_write_origin_core = previous; }
    ScopedGuestWriteOrigin(const ScopedGuestWriteOrigin&) = delete;
    ScopedGuestWriteOrigin& operator=(const ScopedGuestWriteOrigin&) = delete;
};

// Guest RAM writes have a follow-up store; cache-maintenance notifications
// have none. This scoped classification does NOT enable deferred execution.
enum class GuestWriteIntent { NoStore, StoreFollows };
inline thread_local GuestWriteIntent guest_write_intent = GuestWriteIntent::NoStore;
struct ScopedGuestStoreIntent final {
    const GuestWriteIntent previous{guest_write_intent};
    ScopedGuestStoreIntent() noexcept { guest_write_intent = GuestWriteIntent::StoreFollows; }
    ~ScopedGuestStoreIntent() { guest_write_intent = previous; }
    ScopedGuestStoreIntent(const ScopedGuestStoreIntent&) = delete;
    ScopedGuestStoreIntent& operator=(const ScopedGuestStoreIntent&) = delete;
};
// An explicit maintenance exclusion overrides any enclosing StoreFollows
// scope, including reentrant cache operations on the same host thread.
struct ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent final {
    const GuestWriteIntent previous{guest_write_intent};
    ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent() noexcept {
        guest_write_intent = GuestWriteIntent::NoStore;
    }
    ~ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent() { guest_write_intent = previous; }
    ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent(const ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent&) = delete;
    ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent& operator=(const ScopedGuestCacheMaintenanceIntent&) = delete;
};
// GPU-owner replay must never defer itself. No process-global session queue.
inline thread_local bool replaying_guest_write = false;
struct ScopedReplay final {
    const bool previous = replaying_guest_write;
    ScopedReplay() noexcept { replaying_guest_write = true; }
    ~ScopedReplay() { replaying_guest_write = previous; }
    ScopedReplay(const ScopedReplay&) = delete;
    ScopedReplay& operator=(const ScopedReplay&) = delete;
};
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kDirtyRegionBytes = 2048;
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kDirtyBlockBytes = 64;
struct ReplayTotals {
    std::uint64_t queued_ranges{}, deferred_gpu_owned{}, dirty_segments{};
};

// GPU owner only, outside buffer/texture cache locks and before dependent work.
// on_cpu_write must call the ORIGINAL rasterizer path with DEFER disabled;
// return true only when the cache still owns the old GPU-written contents.
// collect_dirty represents at most one 2048-byte GPUDirty transform per call.
template <class OnCpuWrite, class CollectDirty>
ReplayTotals ReplayQueued(Queue& queue, OnCpuWrite&& on_cpu_write,
                          CollectDirty&& collect_dirty) {
    ReplayTotals totals{};
    queue.Drain([&](unsigned core, std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size) {
        ++totals.queued_ranges;
        if (!on_cpu_write(address, size)) return;
        ++totals.deferred_gpu_owned;
        for (std::uint64_t cursor = address, left = size; left != 0;) {
            const auto room = kDirtyRegionBytes - (cursor % kDirtyRegionBytes);
            const auto chunk = std::min(left, room);
            collect_dirty(core, cursor, chunk);
            cursor += chunk;
            left -= chunk;
            ++totals.dirty_segments;
        }
    });
    return totals;
}
} // namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite
```
