`headless/gpu_deferred_store_publication.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Source-only post-store publication primitive. This is NOT wired into the
// shipping core or the disabled native bridge.
#include "gpu_deferred_write_queue.h"
#include <cstdint>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>

namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite {
enum class StoreOutcome { Modified, Unchanged };

// Reserve BEFORE an actual host RAM store, commit AFTER the store, or cancel
// a conditional store that made no modification. The owner callback can be
// synchronous or asynchronous; a bool false scheduler return poisons Queue.
//
// Crucial caller contracts that this helper cannot itself prove:
//  - Caller has completed any GPU->CPU read/download synchronization first.
//  - Store is noexcept and happens exactly once; no cache mutex is held.
//  - Guest producer lifetime extends through resolution (join before Close).
//  - A nullopt after a store means fatal title failure, never synchronous
//    fallback or a second store.
//  - Normal store, cache flush (no new data), CAS/LL-SC and direct JIT paths
//    must be classified independently in the source-derived native bridge.
// This header does not enable kNativePostStorePublicationReady.
template<class Store, class RequestGpu>
std::optional<StoreOutcome> CommitPostStore(
    Queue& queue, unsigned core, std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size,
    Store&& store, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
    static_assert(std::is_nothrow_invocable_r_v<StoreOutcome, Store&>,
                  "Backing RAM operation must be noexcept and return StoreOutcome");
    const auto ticket = queue.ReserveOrdered(core, address, size, request_gpu);
    if (!ticket) return std::nullopt;  // Must not execute the operation.
    const auto outcome = std::forward<Store>(store)();
    const bool accepted = outcome == StoreOutcome::Modified
        ? queue.PublishAndWake(*ticket, request_gpu)
        : queue.CancelAndWake(*ticket, request_gpu);
    if (!accepted) return std::nullopt;  // Irrecoverable: caller must stop title.
    return outcome;
}
// Reserve the guest CAS FIFO position before reading RAM. The read callback
// must fence ONLY its predecessors, never the unpublished CAS itself. Complete
// the real GPU-to-CPU transfer before reporting ReadBarrierResult::Complete.
// Guest CPU/JIT/fastmem producers must share the GuestStoreOrderGate below.
// This source-only composition intentionally does not enable the native path.
enum class ReadBarrierResult { Complete, Failed };

template<class SyncRead, class Attempt, class RequestGpu>
std::optional<StoreOutcome> CommitConditionalAfterRead(
    Queue& queue, unsigned core, std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size,
    SyncRead&& synchronize_read, Attempt&& attempt,
    RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
    static_assert(std::is_same_v<std::invoke_result_t<SyncRead&, Queue::Ticket>,
                                 ReadBarrierResult>,
                  "Read barrier must report completed prior FIFO work");
    static_assert(std::is_nothrow_invocable_r_v<StoreOutcome, Attempt&>,
                  "Atomic store attempt must be noexcept and report modification");
    // Saturation may drain older invalidations. Reserve BEFORE synchronizing
    // the CPU read so no such drain can occur after the read fence.
    const auto ticket = queue.ReserveOrdered(core, address, size, request_gpu);
    if (!ticket) return std::nullopt;
    // Never wait for our own unpublished ticket. The read callback must
    // check queue.WaitForPredecessors(predecessors), then complete the actual
    // GPU-to-CPU device fence. Ordinary WaitUntil(0) rejects a first CAS.
    const Queue::Ticket predecessors{ticket->sequence - 1, ticket->generation};
    ReadBarrierResult read_status = ReadBarrierResult::Failed;
    try {
        read_status = std::forward<SyncRead>(synchronize_read)(predecessors);
    } catch (...) {
        // A thrown read fence is a fatal title-coherence failure, not a
        // harmless failed comparison. Preserve the original exception.
        queue.FailClosed();
        throw;
    }
    if (read_status != ReadBarrierResult::Complete) {
        queue.FailClosed();
        return std::nullopt; // Caller must abort; RAM may be stale.
    }
    const auto outcome = std::forward<Attempt>(attempt)();
    const bool accepted = outcome == StoreOutcome::Modified
        ? queue.PublishAndWake(*ticket, request_gpu)
        : queue.CancelAndWake(*ticket, request_gpu);
    if (!accepted) return std::nullopt;
    return outcome;
}

// This per-title gate serializes PARTICIPATING producer transactions across
// read fences, RAM stores, FIFO resolution and scheduling callbacks. It is
// not acquired by the GPU consumer. No callback may recursively take it.
// All native CPU/JIT/fastmem paths must participate before activation.
class GuestStoreOrderGate final {
public:
    explicit GuestStoreOrderGate(Queue& queue) noexcept : queue_{queue} {}
    GuestStoreOrderGate(const GuestStoreOrderGate&) = delete;
    GuestStoreOrderGate& operator=(const GuestStoreOrderGate&) = delete;

    template<class Store, class RequestGpu>
    std::optional<StoreOutcome> Write(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address,
                                      std::uint64_t size, Store&& store,
                                      RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return CommitPostStore(queue_, core, address, size,
                               std::forward<Store>(store),
                               std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu));
    }
    template<class SyncRead, class Attempt, class RequestGpu>
    std::optional<StoreOutcome> Conditional(
        unsigned core, std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size,
        SyncRead&& synchronize_read, Attempt&& attempt, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return CommitConditionalAfterRead(queue_, core, address, size,
                                          std::forward<SyncRead>(synchronize_read),
                                          std::forward<Attempt>(attempt),
                                          std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu));
    }
private:
    Queue& queue_;
    std::mutex mutex_;
};
} // namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite

```

`headless/gpu_deferred_write_queue.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Source-only, session-owned FIFO for deferred guest cache writes.
// Completion watermarks are a host contract, NOT a GPU fence or runtime enable.
#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdint>
#include <exception>
#include <limits>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <type_traits>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite {
struct Range {
    std::uint64_t begin{}, end{}; // half-open
};
struct Write {
    unsigned core{};
    Range range{};
    // A merged FIFO entry acknowledges all consecutive enqueues through this id.
    std::uint64_t last_sequence{};
    bool published{true}; // False until producer finishes the guest RAM store.
    bool cancelled{false}; // Failed conditional store: advances FIFO without cache invalidation.
};

class Queue {
public:
    using Sequence = std::uint64_t;
    struct Ticket {
        Sequence sequence{};
        std::uint64_t generation{};
    };
    static constexpr unsigned Cores = 4;
    static constexpr std::uint64_t PageBytes = 4096;
    static constexpr std::uint64_t DirtyRegionBytes = PageBytes / 2;
    // Upper bound on accepted-but-not-acknowledged guest stores, including
    // entries in an active GPU replay snapshot. Saturation must be handled by
    // the producer with a synchronous/cache-safe fallback BEFORE its store.
    // Never silently drop a write while pretending the ticket was accepted.
    static constexpr Sequence MaxOutstandingWrites = 8192;

    // Legacy host-only immediate publication. The inactive native bridge
    // still calls this BEFORE its backing RAM store; that path is unsafe to
    // activate until it is replaced by Reserve + post-store Publish.
    std::optional<Ticket> EnqueueTracked(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address,
                                         std::uint64_t size) {
        return EnqueueImpl(core, address, size, true);
    }

    // Reserve an order position before touching guest RAM. The GPU consumer
    // cannot replay this entry until the producer has finished the actual
    // write and explicitly called Publish(ticket).
    std::optional<Ticket> Reserve(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address,
                                  std::uint64_t size) {
        return EnqueueImpl(core, address, size, false);
    }

    // Backpressure for a prospective post-store producer. A rejected Reserve
    // MUST NOT fall back to a synchronous write ahead of older FIFO entries.
    // Request GPU-owner replay outside queue locks, wait through the exact
    // older watermark, then try reserving again. Never call from the GPU
    // consumer or while holding a GPU-cache mutex. Producers must be joined
    // before title destruction; the native integration remains disabled.
    template<class RequestGpu>
    std::optional<Ticket> ReserveOrdered(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address,
                                         std::uint64_t size, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        if (core >= Cores || size == 0 ||
            size > std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max() - address)
            return std::nullopt;
        for (;;) {
            if (auto ticket = Reserve(core, address, size)) return ticket;
            Ticket barrier;
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                if (closed_ || failed_ ||
                    accepted_ == std::numeric_limits<Sequence>::max())
                    return std::nullopt;
                // The queue drained after Reserve failed; retry, not fallback.
                if (accepted_ - completed_ < MaxOutstandingWrites) continue;
                barrier = {accepted_, generation_};
                // Join scheduling callbacks at Close, just as PublishAndWake.
                ++pending_wake_callbacks_;
            }
            if (active_consumer_ == this || active_wake_callback_ == this)
                std::terminate();
            struct RestoreWake {
                const Queue*& slot;
                const Queue* previous;
                ~RestoreWake() { slot = previous; }
            } restore{active_wake_callback_, active_wake_callback_};
            active_wake_callback_ = this;
            try {
                RequestGpuOrThrow(request_gpu);
            } catch (...) {
                {
                    std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                    failed_ = true;
                    --pending_wake_callbacks_;
                }
                wake_cv_.notify_all();
                completed_cv_.notify_all();
                throw;
            }
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                --pending_wake_callbacks_;
            }
            wake_cv_.notify_all();
            // The callback may be asynchronous. WaitUntil also wakes on
            // title close/failure; no younger guest write may overtake barrier.
            if (!WaitUntil(barrier)) return std::nullopt;
        }
    }

    // Host-only legacy publication without GPU wakeup. This is NOT sufficient
    // for a native CPU reader to await the replayed write.
    bool Publish(Ticket ticket) {
        return PublishImpl(ticket).has_value();
    }

    // Resolve a failed conditional write. No-op only at the memory level:
    // the FIFO ticket stays ordered with all earlier cache invalidations.
    // Native callers must use CancelAndWake to preserve worker liveness.
    bool Cancel(Ticket ticket) {
        return PublishImpl(ticket, false, true).has_value();
    }

    // A native-ready producer needs TWO actions after its actual guest store:
    // publish the payload, then request a GPU-owner wake when the oldest FIFO
    // reservation first becomes replayable. Run the caller's scheduling
    // callback OUTSIDE mutex_ to avoid a scheduler/cache-lock inversion.
    //
    // This is a host-only scheduling contract. The disabled native bridge
    // does not invoke it or guarantee GPU-thread lifetime/fence ordering.
    template<class RequestGpu>
    bool PublishAndWake(Ticket ticket, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        return ResolveAndWake(ticket, false, std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu));
    }

    // A failed conditional write did not change backing RAM. Resolve its
    // reserved FIFO position without replaying an unnecessary invalidation.
    // Still request a GPU wake when it unblocks the next published writer.
    template<class RequestGpu>
    bool CancelAndWake(Ticket ticket, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        return ResolveAndWake(ticket, true, std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu));
    }

    // Existing opt-in native bridge uses this signature. There is deliberately
    // no automatic fallback for a rejected write: caller must not reorder work.
    bool Enqueue(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size) {
        return EnqueueTracked(core, address, size).has_value();
    }

    Sequence AcceptedSequence() const {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return accepted_;
    }
    Sequence CompletedSequence() const {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return completed_;
    }

    // True includes entries being replayed but not yet acknowledged.
    bool Pending() const {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return completed_ != accepted_;
    }

    // A callback exception permanently poisons this title's queue. Replaying
    // it again is unsafe because the callback may have made partial cache
    // changes before throwing. Only quiescent teardown can clear the poison.
    bool Failed() const {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return failed_;
    }

    // A failed GPU->CPU download compromises guest memory coherence. Unlike
    // a failed CAS comparison, do not acknowledge or replay its reservation:
    // poison the whole session and release blocked producer/reader threads.
    void FailClosed() {
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            failed_ = true;
        }
        completed_cv_.notify_all();
        wake_cv_.notify_all();
    }

    // Generation-tagged wait for either queued or reserved writes.
    // Caller MUST schedule a GPU-owner drain, without holding any GPU cache
    // lock, before waiting. The result is replay-callback completion only,
    // NOT GPU/device-fence completion or safe native CPU-read synchronization.
    // A stale ticket cannot become valid again after an idle session reset.
    bool WaitUntil(Ticket ticket) {
        std::unique_lock lock(mutex_);
        if (ticket.generation != generation_ || ticket.sequence == 0 ||
            ticket.sequence > accepted_) return false;
        completed_cv_.wait(lock, [&] {
            return completed_ >= ticket.sequence || closed_ || failed_ ||
                   generation_ != ticket.generation;
        });
        // A callback may complete while Close() is joining the GPU owner.
        // Never report a successful CPU read for a closed/poisoned title,
        // even if the sequence watermark was acknowledged before shutdown.
        return !closed_ && !failed_ && generation_ == ticket.generation &&
               completed_ >= ticket.sequence;
    }

    // A conditional RAM read must wait ONLY for the FIFO work preceding its
    // own still-unpublished ticket. Sequence zero represents no predecessors.
    // It is valid only for a live reservation in the correct session and must
    // not bypass poison or title shutdown. GPU-owner scheduling is external.
    bool WaitForPredecessors(Ticket predecessor) {
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            if (closed_ || failed_ || predecessor.generation != generation_ ||
                accepted_ == 0 || predecessor.sequence >= accepted_)
                return false;
            if (predecessor.sequence == 0) return true;
        }
        return WaitUntil(predecessor);
    }

    // Deliberately NO WaitUntil(Sequence) overload. Sequence numbers reset
    // after quiescence; only generation-tagged tickets can be waited upon.
    // A stale read ticket must never succeed against another title session.

    // GPU owner only. Capture ONE finite FIFO batch while holding the queue
    // mutex, then replay it without that mutex. New enqueues remain pending
    // until a later GPU boundary, even if they arrive during replay.
    //
    // The requested generation-tagged ticket is a MINIMUM completion target,
    // not an upper cutoff: entries accepted before the snapshot may be
    // included. A stale session's ticket cannot drain another session.
    // Only published guest payloads are eligible for replay.
    template<class Replay>
    std::uint64_t DrainThrough(Ticket target, Replay&& replay) {
        // Only one GPU owner can replay a session at a time. A second owner
        // waits for the first before it rechecks its requested watermark.
        // Recursive replay on the same thread is a caller contract violation:
        // fail fast rather than deadlock or silently skip an invalidation.
        if (active_consumer_ == this) std::terminate();
        std::unique_lock owner(consumer_mutex_);
        struct RestoreOwner {
            const Queue*& slot;
            const Queue* prior;
            ~RestoreOwner() { slot = prior; }
        } restore{active_consumer_, active_consumer_};
        active_consumer_ = this;
        std::vector<Write> work;
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            if (closed_ || failed_ || target.generation != generation_ || target.sequence == 0 ||
                target.sequence > accepted_ || completed_ >= target.sequence) return 0;
            // Reserve + Publish is ordered, but publishers can finish out of
            // order. Drain only the contiguous PUBLISHED prefix. Never
            // overtake an earlier uncommitted guest RAM write.
            std::size_t ready = 0;
            while (ready != queue_.size() && queue_[ready].published) ++ready;
            if (ready == 0) return 0;
            if (ready == queue_.size()) {
                work.swap(queue_);
            } else {
                work.assign(queue_.begin(), queue_.begin() + ready);
                queue_.erase(queue_.begin(), queue_.begin() + ready);
            }
        }
        // Under the consumer mutex no other replay can be in flight.
        // The snapshot includes ONLY the published FIFO prefix.
        std::uint64_t replayed = 0;
        try {
            for (const auto& item : work) {
                if (item.cancelled) continue;
                replay(item.core, item.range.begin, item.range.end - item.range.begin);
                ++replayed;
            }
        } catch (...) {
            // The callback may have partially modified GPU caches. Never
            // acknowledge this batch, retry it, or permit later work to
            // overtake it. Report failure to readers and propagate the error.
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                failed_ = true;
            }
            completed_cv_.notify_all();
            throw;
        }
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            completed_ = work.back().last_sequence;
            // A complete drain traditionally swapped the entire FIFO into
            // `work`, leaving queue_ with zero capacity. Repeated short
            // bursts then reallocated the FIFO on almost every GPU boundary.
            // Recycle the emptied snapshot's backing storage only when no
            // producer enqueued a new tail while replay ran. Never disturb
            // a newer unpublished reservation or its sequence ordering.
            if (queue_.empty()) {
                work.clear();
                queue_.swap(work);
            }
        }
        completed_cv_.notify_all();
        return replayed;
    }

    template<class Replay>
    std::uint64_t Drain(Replay&& replay) {
        Ticket target{};
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            target = {accepted_, generation_};
        }
        return DrainThrough(target, std::forward<Replay>(replay));
    }

    // Shutdown barrier: reject future work, release CPU waiters, then wait
    // until any in-flight GPU replay callback has returned. No GPU cache lock
    // may be held while calling Close(). Never call it recursively from replay.
    // Producers and waiters still must be joined before destroying the Queue.
    void Close() {
        if (active_consumer_ == this || active_wake_callback_ == this)
            std::terminate();
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            closed_ = true;
            close_completed_ = false;
        }
        completed_cv_.notify_all();
        // A publish may have released mutex_ and be about to invoke the GPU
        // scheduling callback. Join all such callbacks before returning:
        // otherwise the caller could free the scheduler underneath them.
        {
            std::unique_lock lock(mutex_);
            wake_cv_.wait(lock, [&] { return pending_wake_callbacks_ == 0; });
        }
        // DrainThrough holds consumer_mutex_ for the complete replay batch.
        // Lock order is consumer_mutex_ -> mutex_ on a drain; never hold
        // mutex_ while waiting for this lock.
        std::lock_guard owner(consumer_mutex_);
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
            close_completed_ = true;
        }
    }

    // Reset only AFTER Close(), joining producers/readers and releasing all
    // GPU cache locks. Serialize with the consumer as an extra safety barrier.
    // Reject open-session resets instead of silently recycling live tickets.
    // A caller must still enforce full thread quiescence before destruction.
    bool ResetAfterQuiescence() {
        if (active_consumer_ == this) return false;
        std::lock_guard owner(consumer_mutex_);
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        if (!closed_ || !close_completed_ || pending_wake_callbacks_ != 0)
            return false;
        queue_.clear();
        accepted_ = completed_ = 0;
        generation_ = FreshGeneration(); // Unique across ALL queue instances.
        failed_ = false;
        closed_ = false;
        close_completed_ = false;
        return true;
    }

private:
    // The scheduler may expose either a void callback (throw on failure) or
    // an explicit bool acceptance result. Treat false as failure: otherwise
    // a published FIFO head can strand readers or a saturated producer.
    template<class RequestGpu>
    static void RequestGpuOrThrow(RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        if constexpr (std::is_same_v<std::invoke_result_t<RequestGpu>, bool>) {
            if (!std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu)())
                throw std::runtime_error("deferred GPU wake rejected");
        } else {
            std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu)();
        }
    }

    template<class RequestGpu>
    bool ResolveAndWake(Ticket ticket, bool cancel, RequestGpu&& request_gpu) {
        const auto became_ready = PublishImpl(ticket, true, cancel);
        if (!became_ready) return false;
        if (*became_ready) {
            // A synchronous scheduling callback must never recursively close
            // this very queue: Close() waits for the callback's own counter.
            // Keep the owner marker scoped, including exception unwinding.
            struct RestoreWake {
                const Queue*& slot;
                const Queue* prior;
                ~RestoreWake() { slot = prior; }
            } restore{active_wake_callback_, active_wake_callback_};
            active_wake_callback_ = this;
            try {
                RequestGpuOrThrow(std::forward<RequestGpu>(request_gpu));
            } catch (...) {
                // A publication without a successful GPU wake cannot safely
                // satisfy its reader. Fail closed, never assume another GPU
                // command will eventually rescue this title.
                {
                    std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                    failed_ = true;
                    --pending_wake_callbacks_;
                }
                wake_cv_.notify_all();
                completed_cv_.notify_all();
                throw;
            }
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
                --pending_wake_callbacks_;
            }
            wake_cv_.notify_all();
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Returning true means a blocked/unready FIFO head became published.
    // A later ready tail does NOT schedule an unnecessary second GPU tick.
    // The wake callback itself runs after this queue lock is released.
    std::optional<bool> PublishImpl(Ticket ticket, bool arm_wake = false, bool cancel = false) {
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        if (closed_ || failed_ || ticket.generation != generation_ || ticket.sequence == 0 ||
            ticket.sequence > accepted_) return std::nullopt;
        // Strictly monotone upper sequence IDs survive tail merges and
        // published-prefix drains: binary search remains exact.
        const auto entry = std::lower_bound(
            queue_.begin(), queue_.end(), ticket.sequence,
            [](const Write& write, Sequence sequence) {
                return write.last_sequence < sequence;
            });
        if (entry == queue_.end() || entry->last_sequence != ticket.sequence ||
            entry->published) return std::nullopt;
        const bool was_ready = !queue_.empty() && queue_.front().published;
        entry->published = true;
        entry->cancelled = cancel;
        const bool became_ready = !was_ready && !queue_.empty() &&
                                  queue_.front().published;
        // Account for the notifier WHILE holding mutex_, before Close() can
        // set closed_. Close() waits for this callback before returning.
        if (arm_wake && became_ready) ++pending_wake_callbacks_;
        return became_ready;
    }

    // Tickets must identify the owning queue as well as the title session.
    // An epoch starting at 1 for every Queue would permit cross-address-space
    // confusion whenever two independent queues reached the same sequence.
    static std::uint64_t FreshGeneration() {
        auto prior = next_generation_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        do {
            if (prior == std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max())
                std::terminate(); // Never issue a duplicate epoch on wrap.
        } while (!next_generation_.compare_exchange_weak(
            prior, prior + 1, std::memory_order_relaxed));
        return prior + 1;
    }
    static inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> next_generation_{0};

    std::optional<Ticket> EnqueueImpl(unsigned core, std::uint64_t address,
                                      std::uint64_t size, bool published) {
        if (core >= Cores || size == 0 ||
            size > std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max() - address)
            return std::nullopt;
        const auto end = address + size;
        std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        if (closed_ || failed_ || accepted_ == std::numeric_limits<Sequence>::max() ||
            accepted_ - completed_ >= MaxOutstandingWrites)
            return std::nullopt;
        const Sequence sequence = accepted_ + 1;
        if (published && !queue_.empty()) {
            auto& tail = queue_.back();
            const auto& last = tail.range;
            // A cancelled conditional write is a no-op. Never fuse a later
            // real memory write into it or the replay would skip that write.
            if (tail.published && !tail.cancelled && tail.core == core &&
                (address / DirtyRegionBytes) == ((end - 1) / DirtyRegionBytes) &&
                (last.begin / DirtyRegionBytes) == ((last.end - 1) / DirtyRegionBytes) &&
                (address / DirtyRegionBytes) == (last.begin / DirtyRegionBytes) &&
                address <= last.end && last.begin <= end) {
                tail.range.begin = std::min(last.begin, address);
                tail.range.end = std::max(last.end, end);
                tail.last_sequence = sequence;
                accepted_ = sequence;
                return Ticket{sequence, generation_};
            }
        }
        queue_.push_back({core, {address, end}, sequence, published});
        accepted_ = sequence;
        return Ticket{sequence, generation_};
    }

    std::mutex consumer_mutex_; // Never held by producer or CPU waiter.
    static inline thread_local const Queue* active_consumer_{nullptr};
    static inline thread_local const Queue* active_wake_callback_{nullptr};
    mutable std::mutex mutex_;
    std::condition_variable completed_cv_;
    std::condition_variable wake_cv_;
    std::size_t pending_wake_callbacks_{};
    std::vector<Write> queue_;
    Sequence accepted_{};
    Sequence completed_{};
    std::uint64_t generation_{FreshGeneration()};
    bool closed_{};
    bool failed_{};
    bool close_completed_{};
};
} // namespace Eden::GpuDeferredWrite

```

`headless/gpu_dirty_region_split.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// The GPU dirty collector's 32-bit mask represents exactly 32 x 64-byte
// cells (2 KiB). A guest write crossing a collector boundary must be split
// BEFORE calling GPUDirtyMemoryManager::Collect(), not after.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <exception>
#include <limits>

namespace Eden::GpuDirty {
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kRegionBytes = 2048;
static_assert((kRegionBytes & (kRegionBytes - 1)) == 0, "mask region must be power of two");

template <class Collect>
void ForEachRegion(std::uint64_t address, std::uint64_t size, Collect&& collect) {
    // Fail closed rather than silently wrap a guest address or lose a range.
    if (size > std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max() - address) {
        std::terminate();
    }
    if (size == 0) return;
    // A one-region guest write needs only the first boundary comparison,
    // not a std::min plus two subsequent loop/tail condition checks.
    const auto first_span = kRegionBytes - (address & (kRegionBytes - 1));
    if (size <= first_span) {
        collect(address, size);
        return;
    }
    // At least one byte remains after this first partial/full region.
    collect(address, first_span);
    address += first_span;
    size -= first_span;
    // If bytes remain after peeling the first region, address is now
    // aligned to 2 KiB. Consume complete regions without re-masking the
    // already aligned address or re-running std::min on each region.
    while (size >= kRegionBytes) {
        collect(address, kRegionBytes);
        address += kRegionBytes;
        size -= kRegionBytes;
    }
    if (size != 0) collect(address, size);
}
} // namespace Eden::GpuDirty
```

`headless/gpu_failure.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
#include <exception>
#include <mutex>
#include <utility>

namespace Eden {
inline std::mutex gpu_failure_mutex;
// One delivery per failure for the UI observer, independent of the persistent
// fatal state consulted by worker/synchronization waiters.
inline std::exception_ptr gpu_failure;
inline std::exception_ptr gpu_failure_latched;
inline void RecordGpuFailure(std::exception_ptr error) {
    if (!error) return;
    std::lock_guard lock(gpu_failure_mutex);
    if (!gpu_failure_latched) gpu_failure_latched = error;
    if (!gpu_failure) gpu_failure = std::move(error);
}
// A UI observer may already have consumed the notification. Every outstanding
// GPU waiter must still observe the fatal cause until the title is fully gone.
inline std::exception_ptr PeekGpuFailure() {
    std::lock_guard lock(gpu_failure_mutex);
    return gpu_failure_latched;
}
inline std::exception_ptr TakeGpuFailure() {
    std::lock_guard lock(gpu_failure_mutex);
    return std::exchange(gpu_failure, {});
}
// Only at the next title's launch boundary, once prior GPU workers have joined.
inline void ResetGpuFailureForTitle() {
    std::lock_guard lock(gpu_failure_mutex);
    gpu_failure = {};
    gpu_failure_latched = {};
}
}
```

`headless/gpu_fault_rate_limit.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once
// Count every invalid GPU access; format only the first eight and powers of two.
// Unmapped read-zero/write-discard semantics remain unchanged.
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
namespace Eden::GpuFault {
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> reads{0}, writes{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> guest_map_zero{0}, guest_null_mapped{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> guest_alias_mapped{0}, guest_alias_access{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> remap_replaced{0}, remap_mismatch{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> bad_map_range{0}, bad_unmap_range{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> bad_physical{0};
inline std::atomic<std::uint64_t> remap_cache_evictions{0};
inline bool ShouldReport(std::atomic<std::uint64_t>& counter) noexcept {
    const std::uint64_t n = counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed) + 1;
    return n <= 8 || (n & (n - 1)) == 0;
}
inline void ResetTitleCounters() noexcept {
    reads.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    writes.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_map_zero.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_null_mapped.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_alias_mapped.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_alias_access.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    remap_replaced.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    remap_mismatch.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    bad_map_range.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    bad_unmap_range.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    bad_physical.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    remap_cache_evictions.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
inline bool ShouldReportRead() noexcept { return ShouldReport(reads); }
inline bool ShouldReportWrite() noexcept { return ShouldReport(writes); }
inline bool ShouldReportGuestMapZero() noexcept { return ShouldReport(guest_map_zero); }
inline bool ShouldReportGuestNullMapped() noexcept { return ShouldReport(guest_null_mapped); }
inline bool ShouldReportRemapMismatch() noexcept { return ShouldReport(remap_mismatch); }
inline bool ShouldReportBadMapRange() noexcept { return ShouldReport(bad_map_range); }
inline bool ShouldReportBadUnmapRange() noexcept { return ShouldReport(bad_unmap_range); }
inline bool ShouldReportBadPhysical() noexcept { return ShouldReport(bad_physical); }
}
```

`headless/gpu_native_probe.inc`:

```inc
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// Diagnostic-only native queue test, called with a drained GL context.
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <cstdint>
extern "C" {
int sceAgcSetSubmitMode(int);
int sceAgcSuspendPoint();
int sceAgcDriverSubmitDcb(void*);
uint32_t* sceAgcCbReleaseMem(void*,uint8_t,int16_t,uint64_t,int8_t,void*,uint32_t,
                           uint64_t,uint16_t,uint16_t,int8_t,int32_t);
int64_t sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize();
int sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory(int64_t,int64_t,size_t,size_t,int,int64_t*);
int sceKernelMapDirectMemory(void**,size_t,int,int,int64_t,size_t);
int sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory(int64_t,size_t);
int sceKernelUsleep(uint32_t);
}
namespace Eden {
namespace {
long long ProbeClock(clockid_t id) {
    timespec t{}; Check(clock_gettime(id,&t)==0,"native probe clock");
    return static_cast<long long>(t.tv_sec)*1000000000LL+t.tv_nsec;
}
void ProbeNativeQueue(unsigned memory_type) {
    struct Command {
        uint32_t *bottom,*top,*up,*down;
        uintptr_t callback; void* user; uint32_t reserved,padding;
    };
    struct Submit { void* words; uint32_t count; uint8_t flag,padding[3]; };
    static_assert(sizeof(Command)==56 && sizeof(Submit)==16);
    constexpr size_t bytes=0x4000;
    int64_t physical=-1;
    Check(sceKernelAllocateDirectMemory(0,sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize(),bytes,bytes,memory_type,&physical)==0,
          "native probe allocate");
    void* memory=nullptr;
    if (sceKernelMapDirectMemory(&memory,bytes,0x33,0,physical,bytes)!=0 || !memory) {
        sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory(physical,bytes);
        Check(false,"native probe map");
    }
    SCOPE_EXIT {
        if (munmap(memory,bytes)!=0 || sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory(physical,bytes)!=0)
            std::_Exit(1);
    };
    const auto flush=[](const void* p,size_t n) {
        for (size_t i=0;i<n;i+=64) __builtin_ia32_clflush(static_cast<const char*>(p)+i);
        __builtin_ia32_mfence();
    };
    auto* words=static_cast<uint32_t*>(memory);
    auto* head=words+1024; auto* tail=words+1040; auto* marker=words+1056;
    Check(sceAgcSuspendPoint()==0,"native probe initial period");
    Check(sceAgcSetSubmitMode(0)==0,"native probe submit mode");
    // variant: baseline, color release, L2 destination, timestamp last.
    for (const unsigned data : {0u,1u,2u,3u}) {
        for (unsigned sleep=0;sleep<2;++sleep) for (unsigned rep=0;rep<4;++rep) {
            std::memset(memory,0,bytes);
            Command cb{words,words+512,words,words+512,0,nullptr,0,0};
            Check(sceAgcCbReleaseMem(&cb,40,0x30c,0,0,head,3,0,0,0,0,0),"native head timestamp");
            if (data==1)
                Check(sceAgcCbReleaseMem(&cb,45,12,1,0,nullptr,0,0,0,1,0,0),"native color release");
            if (data!=3)
                Check(sceAgcCbReleaseMem(&cb,40,0x30c,0,0,tail,3,0,0,0,0,0),"native tail timestamp");
            Check(sceAgcCbReleaseMem(&cb,40,0x30c,data==2?1:0,0,marker,1,101,0,0,3,0),"native value release");
            if (data==3)
                Check(sceAgcCbReleaseMem(&cb,40,0x30c,0,0,tail,3,0,0,0,3,0),"native final timestamp");
            Submit submit{words,static_cast<uint32_t>(cb.up-words),0,{0,0,0}};
            flush(memory,bytes);
            const auto start=ProbeClock(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), cpu=ProbeClock(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
            if (sceAgcDriverSubmitDcb(&submit)!=0) std::_Exit(1); // Uncertain GPU ownership: no cleanup.
            const auto issued=ProbeClock(CLOCK_MONOTONIC);
            long long first=0,end=0; unsigned polls=0;
            for (;;) {
                flush(head,192);
                const auto now=ProbeClock(CLOCK_MONOTONIC);
                if (!first && *reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(head)) first=now-start;
                if (*reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(marker)==101 &&
                    *reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(tail)!=0) { end=now; break; }
                if (now-start>2000000000LL) std::_Exit(1); // Never free an unretired command buffer.
                ++polls;
                if (sleep) sceKernelUsleep(1000); else __builtin_ia32_pause();
            }
            const auto used=ProbeClock(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID)-cpu;
            const auto begin_ticks=*reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(head);
            const auto end_ticks=*reinterpret_cast<volatile uint64_t*>(tail);
            Check(first>0 && end_ticks>=begin_ticks,"native probe GPU timestamps");
            std::printf("EDEN_NATIVE_QUEUE memory_type=%u data=%u sleep=%u rep=%u submit_ns=%lld first_ns=%lld wall_ns=%lld cpu_ns=%lld gpu_ticks=%llu polls=%u marker=101\n",
                memory_type,data,sleep,rep,issued-start,first,end-start,used,
                static_cast<unsigned long long>(end_ticks-begin_ticks),polls);
            Check(sceAgcSuspendPoint()==0,"native probe final period");
        }
    }
    std::printf("EDEN_NATIVE_QUEUE_PASS cases=32 memory_type=%u matrix_submit_mode=0\n",memory_type);
}
}
}
```

`headless/gpu_probe.inc`:

```inc
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
// Compiled only into the explicitly selected graphics-only candidate.
#include "gpu_native_probe.inc"
namespace Eden {
void GraphicsWindow::RunGpuProbe() {
    Check(eglMakeCurrent(display, surface, surface, root), "probe current");
    SCOPE_EXIT { Cleanup(eglMakeCurrent(display, EGL_NO_SURFACE, EGL_NO_SURFACE,
                                      EGL_NO_CONTEXT), "probe release"); };
    const auto ns = [](clockid_t id) -> long long {
        timespec t{};
        Check(clock_gettime(id, &t) == 0, "probe clock");
        return static_cast<long long>(t.tv_sec) * 1000000000LL + t.tv_nsec;
    };
    glFinish();
    for (unsigned memory_type : {12u,0u}) ProbeNativeQueue(memory_type);
    const auto started = ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC);
    GLuint program = glCreateProgram(), vao{}, texture{}, framebuffer{}, query{};
    glGenVertexArrays(1, &vao);
    glGenTextures(1, &texture);
    glGenFramebuffers(1, &framebuffer);
    glGenQueries(1, &query);
    SCOPE_EXIT {
        glFinish(); glUseProgram(0); glBindVertexArray(0); glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0);
        glDeleteQueries(1, &query); glDeleteFramebuffers(1, &framebuffer);
        glDeleteTextures(1, &texture); glDeleteVertexArrays(1, &vao); glDeleteProgram(program);
    };
    const char* sources[]{
        "#version 330 core\nvoid main(){vec2 p=vec2((gl_VertexID<<1)&2,gl_VertexID&2);"
        "gl_Position=vec4(p*2.0-1.0,0.0,1.0);}",
        "#version 330 core\nout vec4 color;void main(){color=vec4(0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0);}"};
    for (unsigned i=0; i<2; ++i) {
        GLuint shader=glCreateShader(i ? GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER : GL_VERTEX_SHADER);
        glShaderSource(shader,1,&sources[i],nullptr); glCompileShader(shader);
        GLint ok{}; glGetShaderiv(shader,GL_COMPILE_STATUS,&ok);
        glAttachShader(program,shader); glDeleteShader(shader);
        Check(ok,"probe shader");
    }
    glLinkProgram(program);
    GLint linked{}; glGetProgramiv(program,GL_LINK_STATUS,&linked); Check(linked,"probe link");
    glUseProgram(program); glBindVertexArray(vao);
    glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST); glDisable(GL_BLEND); glDisable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST);
    glDisable(GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB);
    glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D,texture); glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER,framebuffer);
    // API-only control. With no queued draw, this is NOT a native empty GPU submission.
    for (unsigned rep=0;rep<4;++rep) {
        glFinish(); const auto t=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), c=ns(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
        GLsync fence=glFenceSync(GL_SYNC_GPU_COMMANDS_COMPLETE,0); Check(fence,"probe empty fence");
        glFlush(); const auto status=glClientWaitSync(fence,0,GL_TIMEOUT_IGNORED);
        const auto end=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), cpu=ns(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
        glDeleteSync(fence);
        Check(status==GL_ALREADY_SIGNALED || status==GL_CONDITION_SATISFIED,"probe fence completion");
        std::printf("EDEN_GPU_PROBE_CONTROL rep=%u wall_ns=%lld cpu_ns=%lld\n",rep,end-t,cpu-c);
    }
    const char* modes[]{"group","flush_each","finish_spin","query_wait","query_poll","present"};
    for (const unsigned width : {16u,1920u}) {
        const unsigned height=width==16 ? 16 : 1080;
        glTexImage2D(GL_TEXTURE_2D,0,GL_RGBA8,width,height,0,GL_RGBA,GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE,nullptr);
        glFramebufferTexture2D(GL_FRAMEBUFFER,GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0,GL_TEXTURE_2D,texture,0);
        Check(glCheckFramebufferStatus(GL_FRAMEBUFFER)==GL_FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE,"probe framebuffer");
        glViewport(0,0,width,height);
        for (unsigned mode=0;mode<6;++mode) for (const unsigned draws : {1u,16u,128u}) {
            for (unsigned rep=0;rep<4;++rep) {
                glClearColor(0,0,0,0); glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT); glFinish();
                const auto t=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), c=ns(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
                unsigned ready=0;
                for (unsigned n=0;n<draws;++n) {
                    Check(ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)-started<90000000000LL,"probe 90s deadline");
                    if (mode==3 || mode==4) glBeginQuery(GL_SAMPLES_PASSED,query);
                    glDrawArrays(GL_TRIANGLES,0,3);
                    if (mode==1) glFlush();
                    if (mode==2) {
                        GLsync fence=glFenceSync(GL_SYNC_GPU_COMMANDS_COMPLETE,0);
                        Check(fence,"probe busy fence"); glFlush();
                        const auto deadline=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)+2000000000LL;
                        for (;;) {
                            const auto status=glClientWaitSync(fence,0,0);
                            if (status==GL_ALREADY_SIGNALED || status==GL_CONDITION_SATISFIED) break;
                            if (status!=GL_TIMEOUT_EXPIRED || ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC)>=deadline) std::_Exit(1);
                            __builtin_ia32_pause();
                        }
                        glDeleteSync(fence);
                    }
                    if (mode==3 || mode==4) {
                        glEndQuery(GL_SAMPLES_PASSED);
                        GLuint result{};
                        glGetQueryObjectuiv(query,mode==3 ? GL_QUERY_RESULT : GL_QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE,&result);
                        if (mode==3) Check(result==width*height,"probe query samples");
                        else ready+=result!=0;
                    }
                }
                glFlush();
                const auto submitted=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), submitted_cpu=ns(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
                if (mode==5) Check(eglSwapBuffers(display,surface),"probe presentation");
                glFinish();
                const auto end=ns(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), cpu=ns(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID);
                Check(glGetError()==GL_NO_ERROR,"probe GL error");
                // Readback follows the timed interval and validates actual GPU output.
                unsigned char pixel[4]{};
                glReadPixels(width/2,height/2,1,1,GL_RGBA,GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE,pixel);
                Check(pixel[0]==64 && pixel[1]==128 && pixel[2]==191 && pixel[3]==255,"probe pixel");
                std::printf("EDEN_GPU_PROBE mode=%s width=%u height=%u draws=%u rep=%u "
                    "issue_ns=%lld issue_cpu_ns=%lld finish_ns=%lld finish_cpu_ns=%lld "
                    "wall_ns=%lld cpu_ns=%lld available=%u pixel=64,128,191,255\n",
                    modes[mode],width,height,draws,rep,submitted-t,submitted_cpu-c,
                    end-submitted,cpu-submitted_cpu,end-t,cpu-c,ready);
            }
            std::fflush(stdout);
        }
    }
    std::puts("EDEN_GPU_PROBE_PASS cases=36 repeats=4 warmup_rep=0");
}
}
```

```cpp
// No new clocks or HLE traversal on present. Ordinary five-second reports
// read these cumulative counters once; only the explicit native DEV interval
// witness samples them on each presentation callback (relaxed atomic loads).
// Their deltas are concurrent worker time, NOT additive wall-clock frame time.
// R404 captures the four guest JIT cores from the SAME report-boundary reads,
// avoiding false attribution of parallel compilation to one paused thread.
// Indexes 0..11 retain the R403 aggregate format for backward compatibility;
// 12..15: compile ns/core, 16..19: compile calls/core, 20..23: evacuations/core.
using FramePressureNumbers = std::array<unsigned long long, 24>;
FramePressureNumbers CaptureFramePressure() noexcept {
    using namespace Eden::Performance;
    const auto read = [](const std::atomic<unsigned long long>& value) {
        return value.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    };
    FramePressureNumbers result{read(gpu_queue_wait.nanoseconds), read(gpu_dispatch.nanoseconds),
            read(gpu_fence_drain.nanoseconds), read(gpu_present_wait.nanoseconds),
            read(gpu_queue_full.nanoseconds), read(guest_dequeue_wait.nanoseconds),
            read(guest_sync_wait.nanoseconds), read(guest_ipc_wait.nanoseconds),
            read(cache_lock_contended), read(cache_lock_blocked),
            read(cache_lock_wait_ns), 0};
    unsigned long long jit_ns = 0;
    for (unsigned core = 0; core < compilation.size(); ++core) {
        const auto ns = read(compilation[core].nanoseconds);
        jit_ns += ns;
        result[12 + core] = ns;
        result[16 + core] = read(compilation[core].calls);
        result[20 + core] = read(evacuations[core]);
    }
    result[11] = jit_ns;
    return result;
}

        std::snprintf(detail, sizeof(detail), "%s (EGL 0x%x)", operation, eglGetError());
        Report("Graphics failure", detail);
        std::fflush(stdout);
```
