```h
// Sampled only when Detailed Logging is ON, never during normal gameplay.
inline Totals gpu_present_free_wait, gpu_present_fence_wait;
// Guest threads entering the GPU caches: CPU writes to tracked pages and flush-area lookups.
inline Totals guest_cpu_write, guest_cpu_read;
// Upstream #187 write-ahead candidate: only mark subsequent registered buffer
// pages after a successful OnCPUWrite under the buffer-cache mutex. This is
// not deferred-write replay. Default OFF pending native title qualification.
inline std::atomic<unsigned> cpu_write_ahead{0};
// Bridge is source-only; no normal build or dev option enables this automatically.
inline std::atomic<bool> cpu_write_defer{false};
// Those entries take the buffer and texture cache locks, which the GPU thread holds for one draw at
// a time. Shipping builds block exactly as upstream: the earlier bounded spin reduced wake latency
// but remains a development-only experiment until it is requalified against PS5 soft hangs.
// dev-settings cache_spin=N can still opt into bounded try_lock retries for profiling.
inline std::atomic<unsigned> cache_lock_spins{0};
inline std::atomic<bool> detailed_gpu_profile{false};
inline std::atomic<unsigned long long> cache_lock_contended{0}, cache_lock_blocked{0};
// Accumulated time actually blocked on the guest cache mutex, not just
// number of failed try_lock attempts. Updated ONLY during detailed profiling.
inline std::atomic<unsigned long long> cache_lock_wait_ns{0};
// The old aggregate hides whether CPU writes block on the graphics buffer
// cache or the texture cache. Only count when detailed diagnostics are active.
struct GuestCacheDomainTotals {
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> contended{}, blocked{}, wait_ns{};
    // Exact completed waits above 1/10 ms, plus largest wait since snapshot.
    // Never touched in quiet gameplay; high-threshold diagnostics only.
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> waited_ge1ms{}, waited_ge10ms{}, max_wait_ns{};
};
inline std::array<GuestCacheDomainTotals, 2> guest_cache_domain_totals{}; // buffer, texture
template <typename Mutex>
inline void GuestCacheLock(Mutex& mutex, bool texture_domain = false) {
    // Source of thousands of contended-cache atomic writes in FC27. When
    // diagnostics are OFF use the exact upstream blocking mutex path; do not
    // try_lock first or hammer two shared accounting cache lines per miss.
    // This changes instrumentation, NOT GPU/guest lock ownership or order.
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
        mutex.lock();
        return;
    }
    if (mutex.try_lock()) return;
    auto& domain = guest_cache_domain_totals[texture_domain ? 1u : 0u];
    cache_lock_contended.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    domain.contended.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (unsigned tries = cache_lock_spins.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); tries != 0; --tries) {
        for (int pause = 0; pause < 4; ++pause) __builtin_ia32_pause();
        if (mutex.try_lock()) return;
    }
    cache_lock_blocked.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    domain.blocked.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const auto blocked_start = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
    mutex.lock();
    const auto waited = (Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS() - blocked_start).count();
    if (waited > 0) {
        cache_lock_wait_ns.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(waited),
                                     std::memory_order_relaxed);
        domain.wait_ns.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(waited),
                                 std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (waited >= 1'000'000) {
            domain.waited_ge1ms.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            if (waited >= 10'000'000)
                domain.waited_ge10ms.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            const auto elapsed = static_cast<unsigned long long>(waited);
            auto old_max = domain.max_wait_ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
            while (old_max < elapsed &&
                   !domain.max_wait_ns.compare_exchange_weak(
                       old_max, elapsed, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {}
        }
    }
}
// R310: sampled GPU-owner cache phases.  A successful FPS average does not
// explain a late frame; measure how much of each 16th draw is waiting for the
// cache pair, configuring images/buffers/descriptors, or recording commands.
// Detailed Logging ONLY. The quiet path does not touch clocks or counters.
// All phase measurements are nested inside the ORIGINAL cache locks; this
// code changes neither memory ownership nor draw/fence ordering.
enum class CachePhase : unsigned {
    PairWait, PairHeld, PipelineConfigure, TextureDescriptorSync,
    TextureFillImageViews, GraphicsBufferUpdate, DescriptorQueueAcquire,
    DynamicStates, QueryAndDraw,
    TextureCpuRefresh, TextureAliasScan, TextureAliasCopy,
    StageTextureHandles, BindTextureBuffers, BindStageDescriptors,
    StageHostBuffers, StageImageDescriptors,
    RefreshRenderTargets, CheckFeedbackLoop, CommitGraphicsDraw, DescriptorRingFinish, DescriptorRingPreflight,
    GuestWriteBufferWait, GuestWriteBufferWork, GuestWriteTextureWait,
    GuestWriteTextureWork, GuestWriteShaderInvalidate,
    GraphicsPipelineCreate, ComputePipelineCreate, GraphicsShaderEnvironment, ShaderPoolReset, ShaderCfg, ShaderIr,
    ShaderSpirv, ShaderModule, GraphicsPipelineWait, ComputePipelineWait,
    TextureUploadStaging, TextureUploadContents,
    TextureUploadBarrier,
    ComputePairWait, ComputePairHeld, ComputeConfigure,
    FrameTextureWait, FrameTextureHeld, FrameBufferWait, FrameBufferHeld,
    TextureBudgetQuery, TextureGcCollect, TextureAsyncTick, TextureRuntimeTick, Count
};
struct CachePhaseTotal {
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> samples{}, total_ns{}, max_ns{};
};
inline std::array<CachePhaseTotal, static_cast<unsigned>(CachePhase::Count)> cache_phase_totals{};
// Per-thread, first-use-only breakdown. Asynchronous Vulkan workers and
// cache-hit draws never inherit another thread's shader-miss attribution.
struct ShaderMissStageCosts {
    unsigned long long env_ns{}, pool_ns{}, cfg_ns{}, ir_ns{}, spirv_ns{}, module_ns{};
};
inline thread_local ShaderMissStageCosts* shader_miss_stage_active{};

inline thread_local bool cache_draw_sample_active = false;
inline bool ShouldSampleCacheDraw() noexcept {
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
    static thread_local unsigned sequence = 0;
    // Sampling avoids injecting high-frequency clock calls into the render path.
    return (++sequence & 15u) == 0u;
}
inline bool ShouldSampleCacheFrame() noexcept {
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
    static thread_local unsigned sequence = 0;
    // One cache-owner sample per 16 completed GPU frames, independent of
    // sampled draws or guest writes. No wall-clock probes in quiet mode.
    return (++sequence & 15u) == 0u;
}
inline bool ShouldSampleTextureHousekeeping() noexcept {
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
    static thread_local unsigned sequence = 0;
    // Sample texture housekeeping independently of the outer lock owner.
    return (++sequence & 15u) == 0u;
}
inline bool ShouldSampleGuestWrite() noexcept {
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
    static thread_local unsigned sequence = 0;
    // One in 64 guest CPU-write callbacks, independent of the GPU-owner
    // per-16 draw sequence. An entire callback shares the same sample flag.
    return (++sequence & 63u) == 0u;
}
class CachePhaseTimer {
public:
    explicit CachePhaseTimer(CachePhase phase, bool enabled = cache_draw_sample_active)
        : phase(phase), stats(enabled ? &cache_phase_totals[static_cast<unsigned>(phase)] : nullptr) {
        if (stats) started = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
    }
    CachePhaseTimer(const CachePhaseTimer&) = delete;
    CachePhaseTimer& operator=(const CachePhaseTimer&) = delete;
    void Stop() noexcept {
        if (!stats) return;
        const auto elapsed = (Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS() - started).count();
        if (elapsed > 0) {
            const auto ns = static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed);
            // No global-counter subtraction: concurrent worker phases cannot
            // inflate the phase costs of this cold shader cache key.
            if (auto* const keyed = shader_miss_stage_active) {
                switch (phase) {
                case CachePhase::GraphicsShaderEnvironment: keyed->env_ns += ns; break;
                case CachePhase::ShaderPoolReset: keyed->pool_ns += ns; break;
                case CachePhase::ShaderCfg: keyed->cfg_ns += ns; break;
                case CachePhase::ShaderIr: keyed->ir_ns += ns; break;
                case CachePhase::ShaderSpirv: keyed->spirv_ns += ns; break;
                case CachePhase::ShaderModule: keyed->module_ns += ns; break;
                default: break;
                }
            }
            stats->total_ns.fetch_add(ns, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            auto previous = stats->max_ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
            while (previous < ns &&
                   !stats->max_ns.compare_exchange_weak(
                       previous, ns, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {}
        }
        stats->samples.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        stats = nullptr;
    }
    ~CachePhaseTimer() { Stop(); }
private:
    CachePhase phase;
    CachePhaseTotal* stats{};
    std::chrono::nanoseconds started{};
};
// V01: one diagnostic-only sample per genuinely blocked Vulkan pipeline.
// This is worker wall time (mutex acquisition + condition wait), NOT shader CPU
// translation or a presentation-frame stall. No logging on hot draw callbacks.
struct PipelineWaitTrace {
    const bool enabled{detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)};
    const std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point started{
        enabled ? std::chrono::steady_clock::now() : std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{}};
    std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point lock_acquired{};
    void MarkLockAcquired() noexcept {
        if (enabled) lock_acquired = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    }
    // If publication won the race during mutex acquisition, the condition
    // wait is unnecessary, but a real lock stall must not disappear from V01.
    // Reuse the already captured timestamp; no new clock read on the hot path.
    [[nodiscard]] bool WasBlockedOnMutex() const noexcept {
        return enabled && (lock_acquired - started) >= std::chrono::milliseconds(1);
    }
    void Complete(const char* kind, std::uint64_t cache_key, bool usable) const {
        if (!enabled) return;
        const auto finished = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        const auto elapsed = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
            finished - started).count();
        // Both components use the SAME finished snapshot, so the split
        // sums back to wait_ns without double counting or overlapping CPU
        // compilation. Post-mutex includes condition wake and callback work.
        const auto mutex_ns = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(
            lock_acquired - started).count();
        // Compute the remainder in integer nanoseconds to guarantee
        // mutex_ns + post_mutex_ns == wait_ns on every steady_clock period,
        // including clocks with a tick coarser than one nanosecond.
        const auto post_mutex_ns = elapsed - mutex_ns;
        std::printf("EDEN_VULKAN_PIPELINE_WAIT kind=%s key=%016llx wait_ns=%llu usable=%u mutex_ns=%llu post_mutex_ns=%llu\n",
                    kind, static_cast<unsigned long long>(cache_key),
                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed), unsigned(usable),
                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(mutex_ns),
                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(post_mutex_ns));
    }
};
// R361: Count draws rejected before recording, including hidden HUD/pitch
// candidates. Only increment on an actual rejected draw with diagnostics on.
// In particular no atomic writes are added to the normal successful draw path.
enum class GraphicsDrawDrop : unsigned {
    NoPipeline, ConfigureRejected, BuiltPipelineFailed, DescriptorBufferFull,
    WorkerPipelineFailed, Count
};
inline std::array<std::atomic<unsigned long long>,
                  static_cast<unsigned>(GraphicsDrawDrop::Count)> graphics_draw_drop_totals{};
inline void RecordGraphicsDrawDrop(GraphicsDrawDrop reason) noexcept {
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    graphics_draw_drop_totals[static_cast<unsigned>(reason)].fetch_add(
        1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
inline void ResetCachePhases() noexcept {
    for (auto& drop : graphics_draw_drop_totals)
        drop.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (auto& s : cache_phase_totals) {
        s.samples.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        s.total_ns.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        s.max_ns.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
}

// Guest waits: nvhost_ctrl syncpoint event registration -> signal, and
// BufferQueueProducer::DequeueBuffer waiting for a free buffer slot.
inline Totals guest_sync_wait, guest_dequeue_wait;
// F05: a hung producer never returns from DequeueBuffer, so completed-call
// timers stay flat. Count *currently* blocked host dequeuers separately.
// Multi-producer safe; only an actual wait updates this count, and only
// with detailed profiling enabled. No guest scheduling or queue semantics
// change. One diagnostic count is not a per-thread/guest PC proof.
inline std::atomic<unsigned> guest_dequeue_blocked{};
class GuestDequeueBlockedScope {
public:
    GuestDequeueBlockedScope() noexcept
        : enabled(detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
        if (enabled) guest_dequeue_blocked.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
    }
    GuestDequeueBlockedScope(const GuestDequeueBlockedScope&) = delete;
    GuestDequeueBlockedScope& operator=(const GuestDequeueBlockedScope&) = delete;
    ~GuestDequeueBlockedScope() {
        if (enabled) guest_dequeue_blocked.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);
    }
private:
    bool enabled{};
};
// fsp-srv IFile/IStorage reads (guest asset streaming): time in the backend and bytes.
inline Totals guest_fs_file, guest_fs_storage;
inline std::atomic<unsigned long long> guest_fs_file_bytes{}, guest_fs_storage_bytes{};
// Guest svcSendSyncRequest latency (queueing + HLE handling), and HLE handling time per
// service command (RecordHle, reported as EDEN_DEV_HLE).
inline Totals guest_ipc_wait;
// R393: bounded attribution of synchronous guest IPC waits. Only invoked
// when detailed GPU profiling is active; no allocation, string lookup,
// blocking lock or per-request log on the hot path.
// FC27 R394 observed >63k unattributed calls in 9m32s once 128 TIDs filled.
// 1024 slots cost only ~32 KiB; fixed bounded probing avoids O(1024)
// per-call scans after high thread churn. Diagnostics only.
inline constexpr unsigned guest_ipc_thread_slots = 1024;
inline constexpr unsigned guest_ipc_max_probes = 64;
struct GuestIpcThread {
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> tid{}, calls{}, ns{}, max_ns{};
    // A completed-call profiler alone cannot see an IPC which never returns.
    // Guest-thread ownership is unique; zero means no observed in-flight call.
    std::atomic<long long> active_since_ns{};
};
inline std::array<GuestIpcThread, guest_ipc_thread_slots> guest_ipc_threads{};
inline std::array<std::atomic<unsigned long long>, 4> guest_ipc_hist{};
inline std::atomic<unsigned long long> guest_ipc_overflow_calls{};
inline GuestIpcThread* FindGuestIpcThread(unsigned long long tid) noexcept {
    if (tid == 0) return nullptr;
    unsigned slot = static_cast<unsigned>(tid % guest_ipc_thread_slots);
    for (unsigned n = 0; n < guest_ipc_max_probes; ++n) {
        auto& row = guest_ipc_threads[slot];
        auto found = row.tid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (found == 0) {
            unsigned long long expected = 0;
            found = row.tid.compare_exchange_strong(expected, tid, std::memory_order_relaxed)
                        ? tid : expected;
        }
        if (found == tid) return &row;
        slot = (slot + 1u) % guest_ipc_thread_slots;
    }
    return nullptr;
}
// Diagnostic-only caller (gated by detailed_gpu_profile). Never allocates,
// holds an emulator lock, or changes synchronous service IPC semantics.
inline GuestIpcThread* BeginGuestIpc(unsigned long long tid, long long started_ns) noexcept {
    auto* row = FindGuestIpcThread(tid);
    if (row && started_ns > 0) {
        long long empty = 0;
        row->active_since_ns.compare_exchange_strong(
            empty, started_ns, std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    return row;
}
inline void CountGuestIpc(GuestIpcThread* row, long long elapsed_ns) noexcept {
    const auto ns = static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed_ns > 0 ? elapsed_ns : 0);
    guest_ipc_wait.nanoseconds.fetch_add(ns, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_ipc_wait.calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_ipc_hist[ns < 50'000 ? 0u : ns < 500'000 ? 1u : ns < 5'000'000 ? 2u : 3u]
        .fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (row) {
        row->calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        row->ns.fetch_add(ns, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        auto previous = row->max_ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
        while (previous < ns && !row->max_ns.compare_exchange_weak(
                   previous, ns, std::memory_order_relaxed)) {}
    } else {
        guest_ipc_overflow_calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
}
// Preserve the existing standalone completed-IPC contract used by host tests.
inline void RecordGuestIpc(unsigned long long tid, long long elapsed_ns) noexcept {
    CountGuestIpc(FindGuestIpcThread(tid), elapsed_ns);
}
inline void FinishGuestIpc(GuestIpcThread* row, unsigned long long tid,
                           long long started_ns, long long elapsed_ns) noexcept {
    CountGuestIpc(row ? row : FindGuestIpcThread(tid), elapsed_ns);
    if (row && started_ns > 0) {
        // Only clear this invocation's pending timestamp. A nested/older IPC
        // cannot be mistaken for this completion.
        long long expected = started_ns;
        row->active_since_ns.compare_exchange_strong(
            expected, 0, std::memory_order_release, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
}
void RecordHle(const char* service, unsigned command, long long ns);
// kspin=N: bounded host mutex acquisition used for guest scheduler locks.
inline std::atomic<unsigned> kernel_spin_iterations{4000};
template <typename Mutex>
inline void SpinAcquire(Mutex& mutex) {
    const unsigned spins = kernel_spin_iterations.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < spins; ++i) {
        if (mutex.try_lock()) return;
        __builtin_ia32_pause();
    }
    mutex.lock();
}

inline long long NowNs() { return Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS().count(); }
// Texture cache garbage collection (tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py, vulkan_gc_downloads.inc).
// Past its "expected" memory use Eden's collector also evicts images the GPU wrote, and each of
// those is first copied back to guest memory behind a wait for the GPU. On the console a large
// open-world game sat just past that mark (4.8 GiB against 4.5 with the FSR filter's images):
// entering gameplay took ten seconds at 3-9 FPS (15 collector runs took 4.6 s of one 5 s window)
// and frames of 70-115 ms kept coming. Those images are now kept, as they are below the mark,
// until memory is really short: use reaches the "critical" mark, or the largest free block of
// direct memory (what the next allocation needs) is under kShortMemory.
// dev-settings gc_dirty=upstream restores Eden's rule.
inline std::atomic<bool> gc_keep_dirty{true};
// R439: old visits budget can be restored with dev-settings gc_scan=upstream.
inline std::atomic<bool> gc_count_visits{false};
inline std::atomic<bool> graphics_memory_short{false};
inline constexpr std::size_t kShortMemory = std::size_t{384} << 20;
// Development: the texture cache reports its memory use and marks every 300 frames.
inline std::atomic<bool> texture_budget_log{false};
// Native DEV: expensive GPU-thread/HLE/CPU-snapshot reporting is opt-in.
// The lightweight frame-pacing counters still run in quiet gameplay.
// Reset per title, rather than inheriting a prior game's diagnostic session.

// "Is memory short?", installed by the PS5 build (performance.cpp, GraphicsMemoryShort). This
// header is compiled into libraries with and without PS5_NATIVE, so the function below must read
// the same in all of them: the platform part is behind this pointer, not behind an #ifdef.
inline std::atomic<bool (*)()> graphics_memory_probe{nullptr};
// Graphics memory still free: the largest block of the direct memory pool, which is what the
// driver's next allocation can be given. Installed by the PS5 build (performance.cpp).
//
// The texture and buffer caches decide what to evict from "memory in use" against a budget. On
// the console that figure is the budget less this free block (tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py,
// Device::GetDeviceMemoryUsage), not the driver's own count, for two reasons. The CPU and the
// GPU share one pool, so what limits graphics is what is left of it, whoever took the rest; and
// the driver reports its allocations twice over (as VRAM and as visible VRAM), which made the
// caches evict at half the use they were set to. dev-settings graphics_usage=driver restores
// the driver's count.
inline std::atomic<unsigned long long (*)()> graphics_memory_free{nullptr};
inline std::atomic<bool> graphics_usage_from_pool{true};
// GPU thread only (the collector).
inline bool KeepDirtyTextures() {
    if (!gc_keep_dirty.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
    const auto probe = graphics_memory_probe.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return !probe || !probe();
}
// 1.5ms compose delay after signaling guest VSync (compose_delay_us=0 restores upstream).
inline std::atomic<int> compose_delay_us{1500};
// Development boot trace (dev-settings boot_trace=START:END, milliseconds after the settings
// are read): guest GPU submissions and GPU-thread dispatches inside it are logged one by one.
inline std::atomic<long long> boot_trace_begin{0}, boot_trace_end{0};
// dev-settings fs_callers=on: log the guest caller of each IFileSystem request (its backtrace
// walk delays that request by ~0.1 s, so it is off unless asked for).
inline std::atomic<bool> trace_fs_callers{false};
// Maxwell render-enable evaluations (Maxwell3D::ProcessQueryCondition): [0] host conditional
// rendering, [1]/[2] always/never overrides, [3 + mode * 2 + result] per render_enable mode
// (False, True, Conditional, IfEqual, IfNotEqual) and the CPU-evaluated result. With
// VK_EXT_conditional_rendering, the host path's decisions (tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py): [13] CPU
// evaluation, [14] drawn unconditionally, [15] predicate read from one value, [16] compute
// compare, [17]/[18] hcr=cpu constant predicate draw/skip, [19] hcr=exact pending-query fallback.
inline std::array<std::atomic<unsigned long long>, 20> render_conditions{};
// Guest core idle waits (PhysicalCore::Idle): calls, nanoseconds until the
// interrupt, and calls that went to sleep because nothing arrived while spinning.
struct IdleCounters {
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> calls{0}, nanoseconds{0}, sleeps{0};
};
inline std::array<IdleCounters, 4> guest_idle{};
// PAUSE iterations a guest core spins on its interrupt flag before sleeping (~20 ns each on the
// console). Guest job systems hand work between cores ~150 times a frame; sleeping on each
// handoff put the host's thread wake-up latency on the critical path. 100 us (the default) took
// a racing game's heavy phase from ~55 to ~59.6 FPS; dev-settings
// idle_spin_us=N overrides it (0 sleeps at once).
inline std::atomic<unsigned> idle_spin_iterations{25000};
// R355: 16 draws between Vulkan worker hand-offs instead of 8. FC27 measured
// ~1,000-2,000 dispatches per five-second window with an otherwise idle GPU
// owner; halving dispatch submissions keeps the same hard 512-draw flush bound.
// The guest-visible command order and all texture/buffer synchronization remain
// unchanged. 8 is still available with dev-settings dispatch_draws=8.
// This is a candidate optimization, not a measured PS5 FPS improvement.
inline std::atomic<unsigned> dispatch_mask{15};
inline void CountIdle(std::size_t core, long long nanoseconds, bool slept) {
    // A quiet release must not bounce the guest-core counter cache lines on
    // every HLE idle/wake cycle. These statistics are diagnostic only.
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ||
        core >= guest_idle.size()) return;
    guest_idle[core].calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    guest_idle[core].nanoseconds.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(nanoseconds), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (slept) guest_idle[core].sleeps.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
// Development: reads 32-bit guest words for code dumps (installed by the frontend per session).
inline bool (*guest_read32)(unsigned long long address, unsigned& value) = nullptr;
inline void CountCondition(unsigned slot) {
    // Conditional-rendering decision counts are never needed to draw a frame.
    if (!detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ||
        slot >= render_conditions.size()) return;
    render_conditions[slot].fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
inline bool BootTrace() {
    const auto end = boot_trace_end.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (end == 0) return false;
    const auto now = NowNs();
    return now >= boot_trace_begin.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) && now < end;
}
inline void AddSince(Totals& totals, long long start) {
    totals.nanoseconds.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(NowNs() - start), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    totals.calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
// A32/A64 memory accesses that left JIT code through the C++ callback (tracked,
// unmapped or misaligned pages, exclusive stores). Written only by the owning core.
struct alignas(64) JitCallbacks {
    std::atomic<unsigned long long> reads{}, writes{}, exclusive_writes{};
};
inline std::array<JitCallbacks, 4> jit_callbacks{};
inline void CountJit(std::atomic<unsigned long long>& counter) {
    // A32 memory callbacks can run extremely often. Development counters
    // must not bounce shared cache lines with Detailed Logging turned off.
    if (detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed))
        counter.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}
// GPU thread only (Vulkan frame report): cumulative GPU-thread idle/dispatch/wait
// totals with the owner's CPU clock, then a guest-core CPU snapshot.
// Once per title, after the previous GPU owner has joined. Do not report
// the preceding title's last GPU frame as a freeze in this session.
void ResetGpuReportForTitle() noexcept;
void ReportGpuThread(unsigned frame);
inline std::atomic<unsigned> capture_passes{};

class Timer {
public:
    explicit Timer(Totals& target, unsigned long long bytes = 0)
        : totals(target), requested_bytes(bytes), start(Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS()) {}
    Timer(const Timer&) = delete;
    Timer& operator=(const Timer&) = delete;
    ~Timer() {
        const auto elapsed = (Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS() - start).count();
        totals.nanoseconds.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed), std::memory_order_relaxed);
        if (requested_bytes) totals.requested_bytes.fetch_add(requested_bytes, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        totals.calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
private:
    Totals& totals;
    unsigned long long requested_bytes;
    std::chrono::nanoseconds start;
};

// GPU/guest waits can execute many thousands of times per second. A normal
// game must never sample two wall clocks or update global Totals for each
// dispatch/lock solely because the binary was compiled as EDEN_DEV_PROFILE.
// Expensive per-command timing is only active with Detailed Logging.
class DiagnosticTimer {
public:
    explicit DiagnosticTimer(Totals& target) noexcept
        : totals(detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ? &target : nullptr) {
        if (totals) start = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
    }
    DiagnosticTimer(const DiagnosticTimer&) = delete;
    DiagnosticTimer& operator=(const DiagnosticTimer&) = delete;
    ~DiagnosticTimer() {
        if (!totals) return;
        const auto elapsed = (Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS() - start).count();
        totals->nanoseconds.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed),
                                      std::memory_order_relaxed);
        totals->calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
private:
    Totals* totals{};
    std::chrono::nanoseconds start{};
};

// R406: a blocking DMA or puller semaphore may never return during a freeze.
// DiagnosticTimer only counts completed calls. Publish an active timestamp
// without a per-iteration probe, and clear it on every normal/scope exit.
// GPU-owner single-writer; five-second presenter may read concurrently.
class DiagnosticActiveTimer {
public:
    DiagnosticActiveTimer(Totals& target, std::atomic<long long>& active_slot,
                          bool waiting = true) noexcept
        : totals(waiting && detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ? &target : nullptr),
          active(totals ? &active_slot : nullptr) {
        if (totals) {
            start = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
            active->store(start.count(), std::memory_order_release);
        }
    }
    DiagnosticActiveTimer(const DiagnosticActiveTimer&) = delete;
    DiagnosticActiveTimer& operator=(const DiagnosticActiveTimer&) = delete;
    ~DiagnosticActiveTimer() {
        if (!totals) return;
        const auto end = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
        const auto delta = end - start;
        if (delta.count() > 0)
            totals->nanoseconds.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(delta.count()),
                                         std::memory_order_relaxed);
        totals->calls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        active->store(0, std::memory_order_release);
    }
private:
    Totals* totals{};
    std::atomic<long long>* active{};
    std::chrono::nanoseconds start{};
};
inline unsigned long long ActiveDiagnosticWaitNs(
        const std::atomic<long long>& active_slot) noexcept {
    const auto since = active_slot.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (since <= 0) return 0;
    const auto now = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS().count();
    return now >= since ? static_cast<unsigned long long>(now - since) : 0ULL;
}

// Guest OnCPUWrite can run tens of millions of times per match. Counting
// every one using shared atomics makes the DEVELOPMENT logger itself contend
// across guest cores. Preserve exact per-callback wall-clock measurements,
// but publish each thread's accumulated calls/elapsed only every 64 writes.
// No guest cache mutex or buffer/texture resource lifetime is changed.
class BatchedGuestWriteTimer {
public:
    BatchedGuestWriteTimer() noexcept
        : enabled(detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) {
        if (enabled) start = Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS();
    }
    BatchedGuestWriteTimer(const BatchedGuestWriteTimer&) = delete;
    BatchedGuestWriteTimer& operator=(const BatchedGuestWriteTimer&) = delete;
    ~BatchedGuestWriteTimer() {
        if (!enabled) return;
        const auto elapsed = (Common::g_wall_clock.GetTimeNS() - start).count();
        auto& batch = LocalBatch();
        batch.nanoseconds += static_cast<unsigned long long>(elapsed > 0 ? elapsed : 0);
        if (++batch.calls == 64) batch.Flush();
    }

private:
    struct Batch {
        unsigned calls{};
        unsigned long long nanoseconds{};
        ~Batch() { Flush(); }
        void Flush() noexcept {
            if (!calls) return;
            guest_cpu_write.nanoseconds.fetch_add(nanoseconds, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            guest_cpu_write.calls.fetch_add(calls, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            calls = 0;
            nanoseconds = 0;
        }
    };
    static Batch& LocalBatch() noexcept {
        static thread_local Batch batch{};
        return batch;
    }
    bool enabled{};
    std::chrono::nanoseconds start{};
};

// Opt-in API wall times: calls may overlap across threads, so do not sum them as frame time.
inline std::atomic<bool> vulkan_cost_enabled{false};
inline std::array<Totals, 24> vulkan_api;
inline std::optional<Timer> VulkanTimer(unsigned index) {
    if (vulkan_cost_enabled.load(std::memory_order_relaxed))
        return std::optional<Timer>{std::in_place, vulkan_api.at(index)};
    return std::nullopt;
}
inline void ReportVulkan() {
    if (!vulkan_cost_enabled.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    constexpr const char* names[]{"graphics_pipeline", "compute_pipeline", "submit",
                                  "fence_wait", "semaphore_wait", "device_idle",
                                  "guest_fence", "buffer_sync", "texture_sync", "present_sync",
                                  "descriptor_sync", "range_reuse", "astc_submit",
                                  "texture_gc", "texture_cpu_download", "texture_async_release",
                                  "pipeline_ready_wait", "shader_prepare", "pipeline_cache_save",
                                  "shader_pool_reset", "shader_cfg", "shader_ir",
                                  "shader_spirv", "shader_module"};
    static_assert(std::size(names) == vulkan_api.size());
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < vulkan_api.size(); ++i)
        std::printf("EDEN_VULKAN_COST api=%s calls=%llu ns=%llu\n", names[i],
                    vulkan_api[i].calls.load(std::memory_order_relaxed),
                    vulkan_api[i].nanoseconds.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
}
// Call only before guest startup and after worker shutdown, respectively.
inline void Reset() {
    for (auto& entry : compilation) {
        entry.calls = 0;
        entry.nanoseconds = 0;
        entry.requested_bytes = 0;
    }
    for (auto& count : evacuations) count = 0;
    storage.calls = 0;
    storage.nanoseconds = 0;
    storage.requested_bytes = 0;
    jit_protection.calls = 0;
    jit_protection.nanoseconds = 0;
    jit_protection.requested_bytes = 0;
}
inline void Report() {
    for (unsigned core = 0; core < compilation.size(); ++core) {
        std::printf("EDEN_PERF_JIT core=%u compilations=%llu compile_ns=%llu evacuations=%llu\n",
                    core, compilation[core].calls.load(), compilation[core].nanoseconds.load(),
                    evacuations[core].load());

    }
    std::printf("EDEN_PERF_STORAGE calls=%llu read_ns=%llu requested_bytes=%llu\n",
                storage.calls.load(), storage.nanoseconds.load(), storage.requested_bytes.load());
    std::printf("EDEN_PERF_JIT_PROTECTION calls=%llu elapsed_ns=%llu requested_bytes=%llu\n",
                jit_protection.calls.load(), jit_protection.nanoseconds.load(), jit_protection.requested_bytes.load());
}
}
```

`headless/pipeline_trace_registry.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once

// Debug-only Vulkan first-use attribution; never touched when pipeline
// tracing is disabled. Shader workers may build/use pipelines concurrently.
// The former function-static unordered_set was mutated without a mutex,
// which is undefined behavior on the multithreaded PS5 shader pool.
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <mutex>
#include <unordered_set>

namespace Eden::PipelineTrace {

class FirstUseRegistry final {
public:
    // A game can compile tens of thousands of unique pipelines. Put a firm
    // bound on long-lived diagnostic allocations and the number of log lines.
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxPipelinesPerTitle = 65536;

    // Return ordinal for a newly observed pointer, 0 for duplicates/overflow.
    // Only the set mutation happens under the lock: caller formats and logs
    // OUTSIDE it, preventing kernel I/O from blocking other shader workers.
    std::size_t Record(std::uint64_t title_epoch, const void* pipeline) {
        if (!pipeline) return 0;
        const std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        if (epoch_ != title_epoch) {
            seen_.clear();
            epoch_ = title_epoch;
        }
        if (seen_.size() >= kMaxPipelinesPerTitle)
            return 0;
        const auto [_, inserted] = seen_.insert(pipeline);
        return inserted ? seen_.size() : 0;
    }

    std::size_t CountForTest() {
        const std::lock_guard lock(mutex_);
        return seen_.size();
    }

private:
    std::mutex mutex_;
    std::unordered_set<const void*> seen_;
    std::uint64_t epoch_ = std::numeric_limits<std::uint64_t>::max();
};

// Separate graphics/compute IDs and unique lists. The atomically bumped
// gpu_time_session epoch is shared with the existing per-title Vulkan device
// lifetime and is advanced only after old game workers have joined.
inline FirstUseRegistry graphics_first_use;
inline FirstUseRegistry compute_first_use;

} // namespace Eden::PipelineTrace
```

```cpp
// Host check of the JSON settings store (settings_store.h) and its migration from the earlier
// text files. Build: c++ -std=c++20 -I<nlohmann include> preferences_check.cpp && ./a.out
#include "preferences.h"
#include <cassert>
#include <fstream>
#include <filesystem>
#include <unistd.h>

static std::string Read(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream in(path);
    return {std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in), {}};
}

int main() {
    char directory[] = "/tmp/eden-settings-XXXXXX";
    assert(mkdtemp(directory));
    const std::string file = std::string(directory) + "/prosperoeden.json";

    // Defaults with no file.
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).volume == 100);
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).backend == Eden::GraphicsBackend::Vulkan);
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).hud);

    // Preferences round trip and validation.
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences({false, 40, true, true, Eden::GraphicsBackend::OpenGL}, file));
    auto saved = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(!saved.hud && saved.volume == 40 && saved.mute && saved.detailed_logging &&
           saved.backend == Eden::GraphicsBackend::OpenGL);
    assert(!Eden::SavePreferences({true, 101, false, false}, file));
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).volume == 40);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"renderer\": \"opengl\"") != std::string::npos);

    // Language: English (US) by default, saved by code, invalid values rejected or ignored.
    assert(saved.language == 0);
    saved.language = 13;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(saved, file));
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).language == 13 && std::string(Eden::kLanguageLabels[13]) == "Japanese");
    assert(Read(file).find("\"language\": \"ja\"") != std::string::npos);
    saved.language = int(std::size(Eden::kLanguageKeys));
    assert(!Eden::SavePreferences(saved, file));
    const std::string unknown_language = std::string(directory) + "/unknown-language.json";
    std::ofstream(unknown_language) << R"({"system": {"language": "xx"}})";
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(unknown_language).language == 0);

    // Last and recent games.
    assert(Eden::SaveLastGame("Sample Quest [id].nsp", file));
    assert(Eden::LoadLastGame(file) == "Sample Quest [id].nsp");
    for (const char* invalid : {"../escape.nsp", "game.zip", "a/b.nsp"}) assert(!Eden::SaveLastGame(invalid, file));
    assert(Eden::LoadLastGame(file) == "Sample Quest [id].nsp");
    assert(Eden::SaveRecentGame("Sample Quest.nsp", file));
    assert(Eden::SaveRecentGame("Demo Racer.xci", file));
    assert(Eden::SaveRecentGame("Sample Quest.nsp", file));
    assert((Eden::LoadRecentGames(file) == std::vector<std::string>{"Sample Quest.nsp", "Demo Racer.xci"}));
    for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i) assert(Eden::SaveRecentGame("Game" + std::to_string(i) + ".nsp", file));
    assert((Eden::LoadRecentGames(file) == std::vector<std::string>{"Game4.nsp", "Game3.nsp", "Game2.nsp", "Game1.nsp"}));

    // Console mode per title.
    constexpr uint64_t racer = 0x0100000000010000, quest = 0x0100000000030000;
    assert(Eden::LoadGameDocked(racer, file) && Eden::LoadGameDocked(quest, file));
    assert(Eden::SaveGameDocked(racer, false, file));
    assert(!Eden::LoadGameDocked(racer, file) && Eden::LoadGameDocked(quest, file));
    assert(!Eden::SaveGameDocked(0, true, file));
    assert(Read(file).find("\"0100000000010000\"") != std::string::npos);

    // Resolution and upscaling filter (Settings > Video).
    auto video = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(video.resolution == 4 && video.upscaling_filter == 0 && video.anti_aliasing == 1 &&
           video.output == 1 && video.performance_profile == 1);
    video.resolution = 2;
    video.upscaling_filter = 1;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    video = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(video.resolution == 2 && video.upscaling_filter == 1 && video.volume == 40);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"resolution\": \"0.75x\"") != std::string::npos);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"upscaling_filter\": \"fsr\"") != std::string::npos);
    // The largest scale is 4x; nothing beyond the list is saved.
    video.resolution = 8;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(video, file) && Eden::LoadPreferences(file).resolution == 8);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"resolution\": \"4x\"") != std::string::npos);
    video.resolution = int(std::size(Eden::kResolutionKeys));
    assert(!Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    video.resolution = 2;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));

    // Refresh rate (Settings > Video): 60 Hz unless 120 Hz is chosen; other values are refused or
    // read as 60 Hz.
    video = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(video.refresh == 0 && Eden::kRefreshHz[video.refresh] == 60);
    video.refresh = 1;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).refresh == 1 && Eden::kRefreshHz[1] == 120);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"refresh_rate\": \"120\"") != std::string::npos);
    video.refresh = 2;
    assert(!Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    const std::string unknown_refresh = std::string(directory) + "/unknown-refresh.json";
    std::ofstream(unknown_refresh) << R"({"video": {"refresh_rate": "144"}})";
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(unknown_refresh).refresh == 0);

    // Output resolution (Settings > Video): Recommended starts at 1440p; invalid values fall back to it.
    video = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    // The earlier manual edits make this configuration Custom, but output remains the Recommended 1440p default.
    assert(video.output == 1 && Eden::kOutputWidth[video.output] == 2560 && Eden::kOutputHeight[video.output] == 1440);
    video.output = 2;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    video = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(video.output == 2 && Eden::kOutputWidth[2] == 3840 && Eden::kOutputHeight[2] == 2160 && video.refresh == 1);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"output_resolution\": \"2160p\"") != std::string::npos);
    video.output = 3;
    assert(!Eden::SavePreferences(video, file));
    const std::string unknown_output = std::string(directory) + "/unknown-output.json";
    std::ofstream(unknown_output) << R"({"video": {"output_resolution": "720p"}})";
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(unknown_output).output == 1);

    // Vibration (Settings > Controls): on unless turned off.
    auto controls = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(controls.vibration);
    controls.vibration = false;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(controls, file));
    assert(!Eden::LoadPreferences(file).vibration);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"vibration\": false") != std::string::npos);

    // The launcher's look (Settings > Accessibility): all off unless turned on.
    auto look = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(!look.large_text && !look.high_contrast && !look.reduce_motion);
    look.large_text = look.reduce_motion = true;
    assert(Eden::SavePreferences(look, file));
    look = Eden::LoadPreferences(file);
    assert(look.large_text && !look.high_contrast && look.reduce_motion && !look.vibration);
    assert(Read(file).find("\"reduce_motion\": true") != std::string::npos);

    // Renderer, resolution and filter per title (Library > Game settings); -1 = Settings default.
    auto game = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(game.renderer == -1 && game.resolution == -1 && game.upscaling_filter == -1);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {0, 4, 3}, file));
    game = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(game.renderer == 0 && game.resolution == 4 && game.upscaling_filter == 3);
    assert(!Eden::LoadGameDocked(racer, file));  // the title's console mode stays
    assert(Eden::LoadGameSettings(quest, file).renderer == -1);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {-1, 4, -1}, file));
    game = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(game.renderer == -1 && game.resolution == 4 && game.upscaling_filter == -1);
    assert(!Eden::SaveGameSettings(0, {}, file) && !Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {2, -1, -1}, file));
    // The same for the refresh rate.
    assert(game.refresh == -1);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {-1, 4, -1, 1}, file));
    game = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(game.refresh == 1 && game.resolution == 4 && Eden::LoadGameSettings(quest, file).refresh == -1);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {-1, 4, -1, -1}, file) && Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file).refresh == -1);
    assert(!Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, {-1, -1, -1, 2}, file));

    // A per-title button map without a selected layout must keep its base
    // after saving. The old writer used PlayStation while the reader assumed
    // legacy Switch, silently changing custom controls on the next launch.
    auto title_controls = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    title_controls.controller_layout = -1;
    title_controls.own_mapping = true;
    title_controls.mapping = Eden::Assign(Eden::kPlayStationMapping,
                                          Eden::game_a, Eden::pad_circle);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, title_controls, file));
    auto restored_controls = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(restored_controls.controller_layout == 0 && restored_controls.own_mapping);
    assert(restored_controls.mapping == title_controls.mapping);
    assert(Eden::ResolveSessionButtonMapping(
        0, Eden::kPlayStationMapping, restored_controls.controller_layout,
        restored_controls.own_mapping, restored_controls.mapping).buttons == title_controls.mapping);

    // Explicit Switch positioning remains unaffected by this migration.
    title_controls.controller_layout = 1;
    title_controls.mapping = Eden::Assign(Eden::kSwitchMapping,
                                          Eden::game_a, Eden::pad_cross);
    assert(Eden::SaveGameSettings(racer, title_controls, file));
    restored_controls = Eden::LoadGameSettings(racer, file);
    assert(restored_controls.controller_layout == 1 &&
           restored_controls.mapping == title_controls.mapping);

    // Game files folder.
    assert(Eden::LoadSavedAssetsDir(file).empty());
    assert(Eden::SaveAssetsDir("/mnt/ext1/eden", file));
    assert(Eden::LoadSavedAssetsDir(file) == "/mnt/ext1/eden");
    assert(!Eden::SaveAssetsDir("relative/path", file) && !Eden::SaveAssetsDir("/a/../b", file));

    // Everything saved so far survives in one document.
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).volume == 40 && Eden::LoadLastGame(file) == "Sample Quest [id].nsp");

    // A damaged file reads as defaults and is replaced by the next save.
    { std::ofstream out(file); out << "{ not json"; }
    assert(Eden::LoadPreferences(file).volume == 100 && Eden::LoadLastGame(file).empty());
    assert(Eden::SaveLastGame("Game.XCI", file) && Eden::LoadLastGame(file) == "Game.XCI");

    // Migration from the text files of earlier versions, once, leaving them in place.
    char legacy[] = "/tmp/eden-legacy-XXXXXX";
    assert(mkdtemp(legacy));
    const std::string folder = legacy, migrated = folder + "/prosperoeden.json";
    { std::ofstream(folder + "/settings.txt") << "2 0 70 0 1 0\n"; }
    { std::ofstream(folder + "/last-game.txt") << "Demo Racer [0100000000010000].nsp"; }
    { std::ofstream(folder + "/recent-games.txt") << "Demo Racer [0100000000010000].nsp\nTest Platformer.nsp\n"; }
    { std::ofstream(folder + "/assets-dir.txt") << "/mnt/ext1/eden\n"; }
    { std::ofstream(folder + "/game-0100000000030000-mode.txt") << "1 handheld\n"; }
    const auto old = Eden::LoadPreferences(migrated);
    assert(!old.hud && old.volume == 70 && !old.mute && old.detailed_logging &&
           old.backend == Eden::GraphicsBackend::OpenGL);
    assert(std::filesystem::exists(migrated));
    assert(Eden::LoadLastGame(migrated) == "Demo Racer [0100000000010000].nsp");
    assert((Eden::LoadRecentGames(migrated) == std::vector<std::string>{"Demo Racer [0100000000010000].nsp", "Test Platformer.nsp"}));
    assert(Eden::LoadSavedAssetsDir(migrated) == "/mnt/ext1/eden");
    assert(!Eden::LoadGameDocked(quest, migrated) && Eden::LoadGameDocked(racer, migrated));
    assert(std::filesystem::exists(folder + "/settings.txt"));

    std::filesystem::remove_all(directory);
    std::filesystem::remove_all(legacy);
    std::puts("settings store: all checks passed");
}
```

`headless/present_interval_witness.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>

namespace Eden::FrameDiagnostics {

// Passive interval witness: all counters are cumulative worker totals sampled
// at two *presentation* callbacks, not work attributable to a single guest frame.
// No clocks, locks, dynamic allocation, I/O, or guest memory access here.
// Instantiate only in native development builds and call only when profiling.
template <std::size_t N>
struct PresentIntervalWitness {
    using Counts = std::array<unsigned long long, N>;
    Counts previous{};
    Counts peak_delta{};
    double peak_ms{};
    unsigned peak_frame{};
    bool seeded{};
    bool captured{};

    void Reset() noexcept {
        seeded = false;
        captured = false;
        peak_ms = 0.0;
        peak_frame = 0;
    }

    void Observe(const Counts& current, double interval_ms, unsigned frame) noexcept {
        if (seeded && interval_ms >= 100.0 && (!captured || interval_ms > peak_ms)) {
            Counts difference{};
            bool monotonic = true;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
                if (current[i] < previous[i]) {
                    monotonic = false;
                    break;
                }
                difference[i] = current[i] - previous[i];
            }
            if (monotonic) {
                peak_delta = difference;
                peak_ms = interval_ms;
                peak_frame = frame;
                captured = true;
            }
        }
        previous = current;
        seeded = true;
    }

    void NextWindow() noexcept {
        captured = false;
        peak_ms = 0.0;
        peak_frame = 0;
        // Keep the previous presentation baseline across 5-s reports.
    }
};

} // namespace Eden::FrameDiagnostics

```

```cpp
bool IsFile(const std::string& path) {
    struct stat info {};
    if (lstat(path.c_str(), &info) == 0) return S_ISREG(info.st_mode);
    if (errno != EPERM && errno != EACCES) return false;
    return stat(path.c_str(), &info) == 0 && S_ISREG(info.st_mode);
}

#ifdef PS5_NATIVE
bool IsReadableAvatarFile(const std::string& path) {
    if (!IsFile(path)) return false;
    // stat() can succeed even when a sandboxed title cannot open the
    // privileged cache. Do not choose an unreadable PNG over a valid DDS.
    const int fd = ::open(path.c_str(), O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK);
    if (fd < 0) return false;
    struct stat info{};
    const bool readable = ::fstat(fd, &info) == 0 &&
                          S_ISREG(info.st_mode) && info.st_size >= 128 &&
                          info.st_size <= 4 * 1024 * 1024;
    (void)::close(fd);
    return readable;
}
// Check actual image decodability off the UI thread, not merely stat/open.
// A readable but corrupt PS5 PNG must not shadow the same user's valid DDS.
bool IsDecodableAvatarFile(const std::string& path) {
    if (!IsReadableAvatarFile(path)) return false;
    if (path.ends_with(".dds")) {
        pe::gfx::Image decoded;
        const bool valid = pe::gfx::load_avatar_dds(path, &decoded) && !decoded.empty();
        if (!valid) {
            static std::atomic_flag warned = ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT;
            if (!warned.test_and_set())
                std::fprintf(stderr, "EDEN_PROFILE_AVATAR status=dds_decode_failed\n");
        }
        return valid;
    }
    int width = 0, height = 0, channels = 0;
    const bool header_ok = stbi_info(path.c_str(), &width, &height, &channels) != 0 &&
                           width > 0 && height > 0 && width <= 1024 && height <= 1024;
    stbi_uc* rgba = header_ok ? stbi_load(path.c_str(), &width, &height, &channels, 4) : nullptr;
    const bool valid = rgba != nullptr;
    if (rgba) stbi_image_free(rgba);
    if (!valid) {
        static std::atomic_flag warned = ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT;
        if (!warned.test_and_set())
            std::fprintf(stderr, "EDEN_PROFILE_AVATAR status=png_decode_failed fallback=dds\n");
    }
    return valid;
}

#endif

// Only a deconstructed title's base content counts towards its Library size.
// Its executable 'main' is just one 20-40 MiB NSO; counting that alone makes
// a multi-gigabyte game appear as a 32 MB title. Do NOT add updates or DLC,
// follow symlinks, block on network media, or guess if traversal is incomplete.
// The entire walk runs on the cancellable Library background scan.
std::optional<std::uint64_t> ExtractedBaseBytes(const std::filesystem::path& title,
                                                const std::atomic<bool>* cancel) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    std::error_code error;
    if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title)) return std::nullopt;
    fs::recursive_directory_iterator it(title, fs::directory_options::skip_permission_denied, error);
    if (error) return std::nullopt;
    const fs::recursive_directory_iterator end;
    std::uint64_t total = 0;
    std::size_t examined = 0;
    for (; it != end; it.increment(error)) {
        if (error || ++examined > 40000 || it.depth() > 16 ||
            (cancel && cancel->load(std::memory_order_acquire)))
            return std::nullopt;
        const auto status = it->symlink_status(error);
        if (error) return std::nullopt;
        if (fs::is_symlink(status)) {
            it.disable_recursion_pending();
            continue;
        }
        if (fs::is_directory(status)) {
            if (Eden::IsAddOnContainerName(it->path().filename().string()))
                it.disable_recursion_pending();
            continue;
        }
        if (!fs::is_regular_file(status)) continue;
        const auto size = it->file_size(error);
        if (error || size > UINT64_MAX - total) return std::nullopt;
        total += static_cast<std::uint64_t>(size);
    }
    if (error) return std::nullopt;
    return total > 0 ? std::optional<std::uint64_t>{total} : std::nullopt;
}

// Local user-supplied covers are a safe offline fallback for extracted titles
// with no packaged Control NCA or Nlib match. No game-name-specific artwork.
// Read user-supplied Control NACP without NCA keys or external title databases.
// The legacy NACP language table has up to sixteen 0x300-byte records
// (0x200-byte name + 0x100-byte developer). The compressed/extended variant
// is intentionally not guessed. This is metadata-only, never guest authority.
struct ExtractedSidecarMetadata {
    std::string name;
    std::string developer;
};

bool ValidSidecarText(std::string_view value) {
    if (value.empty()) return false;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < value.size();) {
        const unsigned char c = static_cast<unsigned char>(value[i]);
        if (c < 0x20 || c == 0x7f) return false;
        if (c < 0x80) { ++i; continue; }
        const std::size_t n = c >= 0xc2 && c <= 0xdf ? 2 :
                              c >= 0xe0 && c <= 0xef ? 3 :
                              c >= 0xf0 && c <= 0xf4 ? 4 : 0;
        if (!n || n > value.size() - i) return false;
        for (std::size_t j = 1; j < n; ++j)
            if ((static_cast<unsigned char>(value[i+j]) & 0xc0u) != 0x80u) return false;
        const auto second = static_cast<unsigned char>(value[i+1]);
        if ((c == 0xe0 && second < 0xa0) || (c == 0xed && second >= 0xa0) ||
            (c == 0xf0 && second < 0x90) || (c == 0xf4 && second >= 0x90)) return false;
        i += n;
    }
    return true;
}
std::string NacpString(const char* bytes, std::size_t capacity) {
    const auto* end = static_cast<const char*>(std::memchr(bytes, '\0', capacity));
    if (!end) return {};
    const std::string value(bytes, end);
    return ValidSidecarText(value) ? value : std::string{};
}
ExtractedSidecarMetadata ExtractedLocalNacp(const std::filesystem::path& title,
                                                  int language_choice) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title)) return {};
    // Order matches the existing extracted ExeFS/main layout. Never use
    // update/DLC control data to relabel a base game.
    for (const char* relative : {"control.nacp", "base/control.nacp",
                                 "exefs/control.nacp", "base/exefs/control.nacp"}) {
        fs::path parent = title;
        bool safe = true;
        for (const auto& part : fs::path(relative).parent_path()) {
            parent /= part;
            if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(parent)) { safe = false; break; }
        }
        if (!safe) continue;
        const fs::path candidate = title / relative;
        std::error_code ec;
        const auto status = fs::symlink_status(candidate, ec);
        if (ec || !fs::is_regular_file(status) || fs::is_symlink(status)) continue;
        const auto size = fs::file_size(candidate, ec);
        if (ec || size < 0x3000 || size > 0x20000) continue;
        std::ifstream input(candidate, std::ios::binary);
        if (!input) continue;
        // Map launcher language catalog indices to the 16 uncompressed
        // NACP slots; Polish/Thai use the compressed 18-language variant and
        // correctly fall back to available uncompressed entries instead.
        constexpr std::array<int, 18> to_nacp{
            0,1,3,9,4,7,6,5,10,15,8,11,-1,2,12,14,13,-1
        };
        const int preferred = language_choice >= 0 &&
            static_cast<std::size_t>(language_choice) < to_nacp.size()
            ? to_nacp[static_cast<std::size_t>(language_choice)] : -1;
        constexpr std::array<unsigned, 16> fallback{
            0,1,3,9,2,4,5,6,7,8,10,11,12,13,14,15
        };
        // Preferred language first, then English, French and other populated
        // entries. Never silently impose French on English-speaking users.
        for (std::size_t attempt = 0; attempt < fallback.size() + 1; ++attempt) {
            const unsigned language = attempt == 0 && preferred >= 0
                ? static_cast<unsigned>(preferred)
                : fallback[attempt == 0 ? 0 : attempt - 1];
            if (language >= 16 || (attempt != 0 && preferred >= 0 &&
                                   language == static_cast<unsigned>(preferred)))
                continue;
            std::array<char, 0x300> record{};
            input.clear();
            input.seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(language * record.size()));
            if (!input.read(record.data(), record.size())) continue;
            auto name = NacpString(record.data(), 0x200);
            if (name.empty() || name == "Application") continue;
            auto developer = NacpString(record.data() + 0x200, 0x100);
            return {std::move(name), std::move(developer)};
        }
    }
    return {};
}

std::string ExtractedLocalCover(const std::filesystem::path& title) {
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(title)) return {};
    // Borrow the upstream loose-ExeFS sidecar discovery contract (Eglantine
    // 4d2cf41837): the game icon may live next to main or in base/exefs.
    // No synthetic thumbnails or fabricated rear art are needed.
    for (const char* relative : {"cover.tga", "cover.png", "cover.jpg", "cover.jpeg",
                                 "icon.tga", "icon.png", "icon.jpg",
                                 "exefs/cover.png", "exefs/cover.jpg",
                                 "exefs/icon.png", "exefs/icon.jpg",
                                 "base/cover.tga", "base/cover.png", "base/cover.jpg",
                                 "base/icon.png", "base/icon.jpg",
                                 "base/exefs/cover.png", "base/exefs/cover.jpg",
                                 "base/exefs/icon.png", "base/exefs/icon.jpg"}) {
        // symlink_status(candidate) does not detect symlinked ancestors.
        // Check each ancestor before reading a user-supplied sidecar.
        fs::path parent = title;
        bool safe = true;
        for (const auto& segment : fs::path(relative).parent_path()) {
            parent /= segment;
            if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(parent)) { safe = false; break; }
        }
        if (!safe) continue;
        const fs::path candidate = title / relative;
        std::error_code error;
        const auto status = fs::symlink_status(candidate, error);
        if (error || !fs::is_regular_file(status) || fs::is_symlink(status)) continue;
        const auto size = fs::file_size(candidate, error);
        if (!error && size >= 128 && size <= (16u << 20)) return candidate.string();
    }
    // Eglantine's loose ExeFS sidecars are often JPEG images named
    // icon_<language>.dat rather than *.jpg. The launcher decodes image
    // CONTENT with stb_image, independently of the extension. Scan only
    // known filenames at bounded depth; never follow symlinked parents.
    constexpr const char* languages[] = {
        "French", "CanadianFrench", "AmericanEnglish", "BritishEnglish",
        "Japanese", "German", "Spanish", "LatinAmericanSpanish", "Italian",
        "Dutch", "Portuguese", "Russian", "Korean", "SimplifiedChinese",
        "TraditionalChinese"
    };
    for (const char* base : {"exefs", "base/exefs", ".", "base"}) {
        const fs::path dir = title / base;
        // Check all ancestors, including base/; symlink_status(final) is not
        // sufficient because it follows symlinked intermediate directories.
        fs::path ancestor = title;
        bool safe = true;
        for (const auto& segment : fs::path(base)) {
            ancestor /= segment;
            if (!Eden::IsSafeExtractedDirectory(ancestor)) { safe = false; break; }
        }
        if (!safe) continue;
        for (const char* language : languages) {
            const fs::path candidate = dir / (std::string("icon_") + language + ".dat");
            std::error_code error;
            const auto status = fs::symlink_status(candidate, error);
            if (error || !fs::is_regular_file(status) || fs::is_symlink(status)) continue;
            const auto size = fs::file_size(candidate, error);
            if (error || size < 128 || size > (16u << 20)) continue;
            // Only JPEG/PNG sidecars. Other binary .dat resources must NOT be
            // handed to the cover decoder as images.
            std::ifstream input(candidate, std::ios::binary);
            char signature[8]{};
            input.read(signature, sizeof(signature));
            if (input.gcount() != static_cast<std::streamsize>(sizeof(signature))) continue;
            const bool jpeg = static_cast<unsigned char>(signature[0]) == 0xff &&
                              static_cast<unsigned char>(signature[1]) == 0xd8;
            const bool png = std::memcmp(signature, "\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", 8) == 0;
            if (jpeg || png) return candidate.string();
        }
    }
    return {};
}

std::uint64_t ResolveTitleId(const std::string& path, const std::string& file) {
    const std::uint64_t metadata_id = eden_game_title_id(path.c_str());
    if (metadata_id != 0) return metadata_id;
    const std::uint64_t filename_id = Eden::TitleIdFromRomFilename(file);
    if (filename_id != 0)
        std::fprintf(stderr, "EDEN_TITLE_ID_FALLBACK file=%s title_id=%016llX\n", file.c_str(),
                     static_cast<unsigned long long>(filename_id));
    return filename_id;
}

std::string NlibLanguageCode(int language) {
    language = std::clamp(language, 0, static_cast<int>(std::size(Eden::kLanguageKeys)) - 1);
    std::string key = Eden::kLanguageKeys[static_cast<std::size_t>(language)];
    const std::size_t dash = key.find('-');
    std::string base = dash == std::string::npos ? key : key.substr(0, dash);
    static constexpr const char* supported[] = {
        "en", "ja", "es", "de", "fr", "nl", "pt", "it", "zh", "ko", "ru"};
    for (const char* code : supported)
        if (base == code) return base;
    return "en";
}

    char id[17]{};
    std::snprintf(id, sizeof(id), "%016llX", static_cast<unsigned long long>(title_id));
    return Eden::CoversDir() + "/nlib-" + id + "-" + language + ".json";
}

std::string JoinJsonStrings(const nlohmann::json& value) {
    if (!value.is_array()) return {};
    std::string result;
    for (const auto& item : value) {
        if (!item.is_string()) continue;
        if (!result.empty()) result += " · ";
        result += item.get<std::string>();
    }
    return result;
}

bool AtomicWriteText(const std::string& path, const std::string& body) {
    std::error_code directory_error;
    const std::filesystem::path parent = std::filesystem::path(path).parent_path();
    if (!parent.empty()) std::filesystem::create_directories(parent, directory_error);
    if (directory_error) return false;
    const std::string staged = path + ".new";
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(staged.c_str(), "wb");
    if (!file) return false;
    const bool written = std::fwrite(body.data(), 1, body.size(), file) == body.size();
    const bool closed = std::fclose(file) == 0;
    if (!written || !closed || std::rename(staged.c_str(), path.c_str()) != 0) {
        (void)std::remove(staged.c_str());
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

std::mutex& ArtworkCodecMutex() {
    static std::mutex mutex;
    return mutex;
}

bool WriteJpegWebP(const std::string& encoded, const std::string& output,
                   bool tall_case = false) {
    // JPEG/PNG source -> WebP directly, one lossy encode at quality 80.
    // Runs only on the bounded network worker; never during GL navigation.
    if (encoded.empty() || encoded.size() > (16u << 20)) return false;
    int width = 0, height = 0, channels = 0;
    if (!stbi_info_from_memory(
            reinterpret_cast<const stbi_uc*>(encoded.data()), static_cast<int>(encoded.size()),
            &width, &height, &channels) ||
        width <= 0 || height <= 0 || width > 4096 || height > 4096 ||
        (!tall_case && height > 2160) ||
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width) * height > 3840u * 2160u)
        return false;
    // Keep expensive 1080p/box encodes serial while HTTP downloads stay
    // concurrent. This bounds peak PS5 RAM usage across background jobs.
    std::scoped_lock codec_lock(ArtworkCodecMutex());
    stbi_uc* rgba = stbi_load_from_memory(
        reinterpret_cast<const stbi_uc*>(encoded.data()), static_cast<int>(encoded.size()),
        &width, &height, &channels, 4);
    if (!rgba) return false;
    const float scale = tall_case ?
        std::min({1.0f, 1500.0f / width, 2100.0f / height}) : 1.0f;
    const int w = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(width * scale));
    const int h = std::max(1, static_cast<int>(height * scale));
    const std::uint8_t* pixels = rgba;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> resized;
    if (w != width || h != height) {
        resized.resize(static_cast<std::size_t>(w) * h * 4u);
        for (int y = 0; y < h; ++y) {
            const auto* row = rgba + static_cast<std::size_t>(y * height / h) * width * 4u;
            auto* dst = resized.data() + static_cast<std::size_t>(y) * w * 4u;
            for (int x = 0; x < w; ++x) {
                const auto* src = row + static_cast<std::size_t>(x * width / w) * 4u;
                std::memcpy(dst + static_cast<std::size_t>(x) * 4u, src, 4u);
            }
        }
        pixels = resized.data();
    }
    std::uint8_t* compressed = nullptr;
    const std::size_t length = WebPEncodeRGBA(pixels, w, h, w * 4, 80.0f, &compressed);
    stbi_image_free(rgba);
    if (!length || !compressed || length > (16u << 20)) {
        WebPFree(compressed);
        return false;
    }
    int checked_w = 0, checked_h = 0;
    const bool valid = WebPGetInfo(compressed, length, &checked_w, &checked_h) &&
                       checked_w == w && checked_h == h;
    std::FILE* file = valid ? std::fopen(output.c_str(), "wb") : nullptr;
    if (!file) { WebPFree(compressed); return false; }
    const bool written = std::fwrite(compressed, 1, length, file) == length;
    const bool closed = std::fclose(file) == 0;
    WebPFree(compressed);
    if (!written || !closed) { (void)std::remove(output.c_str()); return false; }
    return true;
}

// The old uncompressed BGRA TGA cache remains readable during WebP migration.
// A filename alone is not sufficient: incomplete/old files previously showed
// permanently empty tiles and prevented download retries. Validate the header
// and complete payload without allocating or decoding image buffers.
bool ValidNlibTga(const std::string& path) {
    struct stat info{};
    if (stat(path.c_str(), &info) != 0 || !S_ISREG(info.st_mode) ||
        info.st_size < 18) return false;
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "rb");
    if (!file) return false;
    unsigned char header[18]{};
    const bool readable = std::fread(header, 1, sizeof(header), file) == sizeof(header);
    std::fclose(file);
    if (!readable || header[1] != 0 || header[2] != 2 || header[16] != 32)
        return false;
    const unsigned width = static_cast<unsigned>(header[12]) |
                           (static_cast<unsigned>(header[13]) << 8);
    const unsigned height = static_cast<unsigned>(header[14]) |
                            (static_cast<unsigned>(header[15]) << 8);
    if (width == 0 || height == 0 || width > 4096 || height > 2160 ||
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width) * height > 3840u * 2160u)
        return false;
    const std::uint64_t bytes = 18u + header[0] +
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width) * height * 4u;
    return static_cast<std::uint64_t>(info.st_size) >= bytes;
}

bool ValidNlibWebP(const std::string& path, int* out_width = nullptr,
                   int* out_height = nullptr) {
    struct stat info{};
    if (stat(path.c_str(), &info) != 0 || !S_ISREG(info.st_mode) ||
        info.st_size < 30 || info.st_size > (16LL << 20)) return false;
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(path.c_str(), "rb");
    if (!file) return false;
    unsigned char header[256]{};
    const auto count = std::fread(header, 1,
                    std::min(sizeof(header), static_cast<std::size_t>(info.st_size)), file);
    std::fclose(file);
    if (count < 30 || std::memcmp(header, "RIFF", 4) != 0 ||
        std::memcmp(header + 8, "WEBP", 4) != 0) return false;
    const std::uint64_t declared = 8ull + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(header[4]) +
        (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(header[5]) << 8) +
        (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(header[6]) << 16) +
        (static_cast<std::uint32_t>(header[7]) << 24);
    if (declared != static_cast<std::uint64_t>(info.st_size)) return false;
    int width = 0, height = 0;
    if (!WebPGetInfo(header, count, &width, &height) ||
        width <= 0 || height <= 0 || width > 4096 || height > 4096 ||
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(width) * height > 3840u * 2160u)
        return false;
    if (out_width) *out_width = width;
    if (out_height) *out_height = height;
    return true;
}

// One-time offline migration, only for artwork known to be generated by
// Encore. A user's own retail-scans must never be silently deleted.
// No HTTP round-trip and no UI-thread I/O. A failed encode keeps legacy TGA.
bool MigrateGeneratedTga(const std::string& preferred, bool require_receipt) {
    if (!preferred.ends_with(".webp")) return false;
    const std::string legacy = preferred.substr(0, preferred.size() - 5) + ".tga";
    const std::string old_receipt = legacy + ".source";
    std::string provenance;
    if (require_receipt) {
        std::ifstream receipt(old_receipt);
        if (!receipt || !std::getline(receipt, provenance) || provenance.empty())
            return false;
    }
    if (!ValidNlibTga(legacy)) return false;

    // Restrict the migration to our own uncompressed top-left BGRA TGA
    // contract. A manually edited, RLE, indexed or inverted asset is kept.
    std::scoped_lock codec_lock(ArtworkCodecMutex());
    struct stat info{};
    if (stat(legacy.c_str(), &info) != 0 || !S_ISREG(info.st_mode) ||
        info.st_size < 18 || info.st_size > 18LL + 3840LL * 2160 * 4) return false;
    std::FILE* input = std::fopen(legacy.c_str(), "rb");
    if (!input) return false;
    std::uint8_t header[18]{};
    const bool header_ok = std::fread(header, 1, 18, input) == 18;
    const unsigned w = static_cast<unsigned>(header[12]) |
                      (static_cast<unsigned>(header[13]) << 8);
    const unsigned h = static_cast<unsigned>(header[14]) |
                      (static_cast<unsigned>(header[15]) << 8);
    const std::size_t payload = static_cast<std::size_t>(w) * h * 4u;
    const bool is_generated = header_ok && header[0] == 0 && header[1] == 0 &&
        header[2] == 2 && header[16] == 32 && header[17] == 0x28 &&
        w > 0 && h > 0 && w <= 4096 && h <= 2160 &&
        payload <= static_cast<std::size_t>(3840u) * 2160u * 4u &&
        static_cast<std::uint64_t>(info.st_size) == 18u + payload;
    if (!is_generated) { std::fclose(input); return false; }

    if (!ValidNlibWebP(preferred)) {
        std::vector<std::uint8_t> bgra(payload);
        const bool read = std::fread(bgra.data(), 1, bgra.size(), input) == bgra.size();
        std::fclose(input);
        if (!read) return false;
        std::uint8_t* encoded = nullptr;
        const std::size_t size = WebPEncodeBGRA(
            bgra.data(), static_cast<int>(w), static_cast<int>(h),
            static_cast<int>(w * 4), 80.0f, &encoded);
        if (!size || !encoded || size > (16u << 20)) {
            WebPFree(encoded);
            return false;
        }
        const std::string staged = preferred + ".new";
        std::FILE* output = std::fopen(staged.c_str(), "wb");
        bool written = output && std::fwrite(encoded, 1, size, output) == size;
        if (output) written = std::fclose(output) == 0 && written;
        WebPFree(encoded);
        if (!written || !ValidNlibWebP(staged) ||
            std::rename(staged.c_str(), preferred.c_str()) != 0) {
            (void)std::remove(staged.c_str());
            return false;
        }
    } else {
        std::fclose(input);
    }
    // Preserve edition/region receipts before releasing source bytes.
    if (require_receipt && !IsFile(preferred + ".source") &&
        !AtomicWriteText(preferred + ".source", provenance + "\n")) return true;
    if (ValidNlibWebP(preferred)) {
        (void)std::remove(legacy.c_str());
        if (require_receipt) (void)std::remove(old_receipt.c_str());
    }
    return true;
}

bool ValidCachedArtwork(const std::string& path) {
    if (path.ends_with(".webp")) return ValidNlibWebP(path);
    return ValidNlibTga(path);
}

// Keep legacy TGA usable until a validated WebP replacement arrives.
std::string AvailableArtwork(const std::string& preferred) {
    if (ValidCachedArtwork(preferred)) return preferred;
    if (preferred.ends_with(".webp")) {
        const std::string legacy = preferred.substr(0, preferred.size() - 5) + ".tga";
        if (ValidNlibTga(legacy)) return legacy;
    }
    return {};
}

std::string CachedNlibHero(std::uint64_t title_id) {
    if (title_id == 0) return {};
    const std::string path = NlibHeroPath(title_id);
    return AvailableArtwork(path);
}

int CachedNlibPlayers(std::uint64_t title_id) {
    if (title_id == 0) return 0;
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(NlibPlayersPath(title_id).c_str(), "rb");
    if (!file) return 0;
    int players = 0;
    const int read = std::fscanf(file, "%d", &players);
    (void)std::fclose(file);
    return read == 1 && players > 0 && players <= 16 ? players : 0;
}

void CacheNlibPlayers(std::uint64_t title_id, int players) {
    if (title_id == 0 || players <= 0 || players > 16) return;
    (void)mkdir(Eden::CoversDir().c_str(), 0777);
    const std::string path = NlibPlayersPath(title_id);
    const std::string staged = path + ".new";
    std::FILE* file = std::fopen(staged.c_str(), "wb");
    if (!file) return;
    const bool written = std::fprintf(file, "%d\n", players) > 0;
    const bool closed = std::fclose(file) == 0;
    if (!written || !closed || std::rename(staged.c_str(), path.c_str()) != 0)
        (void)std::remove(staged.c_str());
}

constexpr int kNlibCacheSchema = 3; // v3 persists artwork refresh epochs

struct NlibEnrichment {
    bool artwork_changed = false; // a cached image was replaced
    std::string icon;
    std::string hero;
    std::vector<std::string> screenshots;
    int max_players = 0;
    std::string name;
    std::string intro;
    std::string description;
    std::string publisher;
    std::string developer;
    std::string release_date;
    std::string categories;
};

std::string CachedNlibIcon(std::uint64_t title_id) {
    if (title_id == 0) return {};
    const std::string path = NlibIconPath(title_id);
    return AvailableArtwork(path);
}

std::vector<std::string> CachedNlibScreens(std::uint64_t title_id) {
    std::vector<std::string> screens;
    if (title_id == 0) return screens;
    for (int index = 1; index <= 3; ++index) {
        const std::string path = NlibScreenshotPath(title_id, index);
        if (auto available = AvailableArtwork(path); !available.empty()) screens.push_back(available);
    }
    return screens;
}

bool LoadNlibMetadata(std::uint64_t title_id, const std::string& language, nlohmann::json* out) {
    if (out == nullptr) return false;
    std::ifstream file(NlibMetadataPath(title_id, language), std::ios::binary);
    if (!file) return false;
    try {
        file >> *out;
        return out->is_object();
    } catch (...) {
        return false;
    }
}

void ApplyNlibMetadata(const nlohmann::json& json, NlibEnrichment* result) {
    if (result == nullptr || !json.is_object()) return;
    const auto string_value = [&](const char* key) -> std::string {
        const auto it = json.find(key);
        return it != json.end() && it->is_string() ? it->get<std::string>() : std::string{};
    };
    result->name = string_value("name");
    result->intro = string_value("intro");
    result->description = string_value("description");
    result->publisher = string_value("publisher");
    result->developer = string_value("developer");
    result->release_date = string_value("releaseDate");
    result->categories = json.contains("category") ? JoinJsonStrings(json["category"]) : std::string{};
```
