`tools/check-active-cmake-source-boundary.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Audit the active CMake module boundary; prohibit C++ source fabrication.

Pinned upstream vendor/sources CMake and historical tools/fixtures are not
build-time Encore mutation owners. Resource generation G23 is explicitly
allowed in the root; staging maintained full sources is permitted.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
root_cmake = (ROOT/"headless/CMakeLists.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
# P5: CMake defers only target wiring, never creating a subdirectory.
# The actual project(yuzu) hook registers the immutable source before DEFER.
native_inject = (ROOT/"headless/inject.cmake").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
assert native_inject.count("cmake_language(DEFER CALL add_eden_headless)") == 1
assert native_inject.count('add_subdirectory("${EDEN_WEBP_ROOT}"') == 1
assert 'add_subdirectory("${EDEN_WEBP_ROOT}"' not in root_cmake
assert 'if(NOT TARGET webp OR NOT EXISTS "${EDEN_WEBP_ROOT}/CMakeLists.txt")' in root_cmake
assert 'target_link_libraries(eden-headless PRIVATE webp)' in root_cmake
assert native_inject.index('add_subdirectory("${EDEN_WEBP_ROOT}"') > (
    native_inject.index("cmake_language(DEFER CALL add_eden_headless)"))
# The existing maintained threading module selects absolute HLE sources.
# Compare their canonical names before replacing the single Wait64 owner;
# the unnormalised PORT_ROOT spelling may include /headless/...
assert 'foreach(eden_wait64_candidate IN LISTS eden_wait64_sources)' in root_cmake
assert 'get_filename_component(eden_wait64_reviewed_real' in root_cmake
assert 'get_filename_component(eden_wait64_candidate_real' in root_cmake
assert 'if(eden_wait64_candidate_real STREQUAL eden_wait64_reviewed_real)' in root_cmake
assert root_cmake.count('message(FATAL_ERROR "Missing unified address arbiter owner:') == 1

generator_sites = re.findall(
    r'^\s*write_derived\(\s*"([^"]+)"', root_cmake, re.M)
assert generator_sites == ["${PORT_BUILD_DIR}/include/loading_scene_glsl.h"], generator_sites
assert root_cmake.count("function(write_derived path content)") == 1
assert root_cmake.count('file(WRITE "${path}.in" "${content}")') == 1
assert len(re.findall(r"^\s*string\(REPLACE", root_cmake, re.M)) == 2
assert 'write_derived("${derived}"' not in root_cmake
assert 'write_derived("${PORT_BUILD_DIR}/kernel.cpp"' not in root_cmake
assert 'write_derived("${PORT_BUILD_DIR}/gpu.cpp"' not in root_cmake

# Discover modules recursively so a newly introduced indirect CMake owner
# cannot hide outside today's documented top-level module list.
module_paths = {
    ROOT/"tools/ps5.cmake",
    *(ROOT/"headless").rglob("*.cmake"),
    *(ROOT/"vendor/encore-active").rglob("*.cmake"),
    *(ROOT/"vendor/encore-active").rglob("CMakeLists.txt"),
}
module_paths.discard(ROOT/"headless/CMakeLists.txt")

# All original upstream source CMake files live under vendor/sources/:
# they are not maintained Encore CMake mutation owners. Every active
# override under vendor/encore-active remains in module_paths and is checked.
pinned_upstream_roots = tuple(
    ROOT / "vendor/sources" / name
    for name in ("ps5-mihawkgen", "ps5-fsr3-optical-flow", "libwebp")
)
assert all(path.is_dir() and not (path / ".git").exists()
           for path in pinned_upstream_roots)
for stale in ("PS5_MihawkGen", "PS5_FSR3OpticalFlow", "libwebp"):
    assert not (ROOT / "vendor/encore-active" / stale).exists(), stale
excluded_upstream_modules = 0
assert not any(any(upstream in p.parents for upstream in pinned_upstream_roots)
               for p in module_paths)

# Exclude source-pin SDK manifests: the checked Encore CMake layer above
# is the only location allowed to mutate included dependency sources.
active_mutation = re.compile(
    r'^\s*(?:file\s*\(\s*(?:WRITE|APPEND|GENERATE)\b'
    r'|string\s*\(\s*REPLACE\b'
    r'|write_derived\s*\('
    r'|execute_process\s*\()', re.I | re.M)
# The unified NUP owner selector tokenizes two audited source-owner names, not C++
# source text. Permit that ONE exact list-parsing invocation only. Do not
# exempt the module, a generic string(REPLACE), or future source transforms.
nup_gate_path = ROOT/"headless/nup_v1_runtime.cmake"
nup_pair_split = 'string(REPLACE "|" ";" eden_nup_parts "${eden_nup_pair}")'
assert nup_gate_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").count(nup_pair_split) == 1

def permitted_source_owner_split(path: Path, source: str, match: re.Match) -> bool:
    return (path == nup_gate_path and
            source[match.start():].splitlines()[0].strip() == nup_pair_split)

# A newly introduced CMake string replacement in this very module must still
# fail, including one that creates a .cpp output or changes the selected list.
assert permitted_source_owner_split(
    nup_gate_path, nup_pair_split, active_mutation.search(nup_pair_split))
assert not permitted_source_owner_split(
    ROOT/"headless/other.cmake", nup_pair_split,
    active_mutation.search(nup_pair_split))
for negative in (
    'string(REPLACE "old" "new" cpp_text "${source}")',
    'string(REPLACE "|" ";" eden_nup_parts "${other}")',
):
    assert not permitted_source_owner_split(
        nup_gate_path, negative, active_mutation.search(negative))

checked = 0
approved_splits = 0
for path in sorted(module_paths):
    assert path.is_file(), path
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    violations = []
    for match in active_mutation.finditer(text):
        if permitted_source_owner_split(path, text, match):
            approved_splits += 1
            continue
        violations.append((text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1,
                           match.group(0).strip()))
    assert not violations, (
        f"Active CMake module must not generate or rewrite C++: "
        f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)} {violations}")
    checked += 1
assert approved_splits == 1, approved_splits

native_build = (ROOT/"tools/build-headless-native.sh").read_text()
vulkan = (ROOT/"headless/vulkan.cmake").read_text()
assert 'file(COPY "${EDEN_ACTIVE_VULKAN}/"' in vulkan
assert 'vendor/encore-active' in vulkan or 'EDEN_ACTIVE_VULKAN' in vulkan
for path, code in (("native build", native_build),
                   ("CMake root", root_cmake), ("Vulkan selector", vulkan)):
    assert "prepare-vulkan-port.py" not in code, (
        f"Historical Vulkan source transformation invoked by {path}")
assert 'shutil.copyfile(maintained, tmp)' in (
    ROOT/"tools/install-active-core-backports.py").read_text()
print(f"ENCORE_ACTIVE_CMAKE_SOURCE_BOUNDARY_PASS modules={checked} "
      f"pinned_upstream_modules={excluded_upstream_modules} "
      "cpp_generators=0 resource_generators=1 nup_source_pair_split=1")

```

`tools/check-active-source-inventory.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fail if the active C/C++ source catalogue drifts from tracked files.

This verifies file-level coverage and exact graph cross-links only.
It is not a function audit, compiler check or console-test certificate.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import re
import runpy

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
active = root / "vendor/encore-active"
document = (root / "docs/EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md").read_text()
audit = (root / "docs/EDEN_CORE_AUDIT_DEPENDENCIES.md").read_text()
begin, end = "<!-- ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG_START -->", "<!-- ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG_END -->"
assert document.count(begin) == document.count(end) == 1
section = document.split(begin, 1)[1].split(end, 1)[0]
suffixes = {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".cxx", ".h", ".hh", ".hpp", ".inc", ".inl", ".s", ".S", ".asm", ".cl"}
physical_all = sorted(
    p.relative_to(active).as_posix()
    for p in active.rglob("*")
    if p.is_file() and p.suffix in suffixes
)
# Exactly pinned third-party sources are in vendor/sources/, not in the
# maintained/active F07 production graph. Reject stale original-source trees
# in encore-active while still auditing *every* maintained override here.
pinned_upstream_source_counts = {
    "ps5-mihawkgen": 632,
    "ps5-fsr3-optical-flow": 41,
    "libwebp": 245,
}
for name, expected in pinned_upstream_source_counts.items():
    upstream = root / "vendor/sources" / name
    assert upstream.is_dir() and not (upstream / ".git").exists(), name
    actual = sum(p.is_file() and p.suffix in suffixes
                 for p in upstream.rglob("*"))
    assert actual == expected, ("Pinned upstream inventory drift", name, actual, expected)
for stale in ("PS5_MihawkGen", "PS5_FSR3OpticalFlow", "libwebp"):
    assert not (active / stale).exists(), ("Sources belong in sources/", stale)
print("ENCORE_PINNED_UPSTREAM_SOURCES_PASS",
      f"sources={sum(pinned_upstream_source_counts.values())}",
      f"trees={len(pinned_upstream_source_counts)}", "excluded_from_f07=1")
# Preserve the audited production source catalogue. The NS2 research sources
# are tracked separately and explicitly; they are not F07 shipping proofs.
research_manifest = json.loads(
    (root / "docs/NS2_RESEARCH_ADDED_SOURCE_OWNERS.json").read_text()
)
research_paths = research_manifest["paths"]
assert research_manifest["schema_version"] == 1
assert len(research_paths) == len(set(research_paths)) == 120
assert research_paths == sorted(research_paths)
retired_am = {
    "ns2-runtime/am/core/hle/service/am/service/application_proxy.cpp",
    "ns2-runtime/am/core/hle/service/am/service/application_proxy.h",
    "ns2-runtime/am/core/hle/service/am/service/graphics_scaling_parameters_functions.cpp",
    "ns2-runtime/am/core/hle/service/am/service/graphics_scaling_parameters_functions.h",
}
assert not retired_am & set(physical_all), "Retired false-success AM sources were restored"
assert not retired_am & set(research_paths), "Retired AM sources remain in research inventory"
assert set(research_paths) <= set(physical_all), (
    "Missing pinned NS2 research source owners", sorted(set(research_paths) - set(physical_all))
)
assert all(p.startswith(("ns2-", "eden-core/include/", "eden-vulkan/include/"))
           for p in research_paths), "Unreviewed NS2 source category"

# R437: the native BufferCacheBase declarations arrived after the frozen
# 337-source F07 register. Audit this exact added owner, not the F07 snapshot.
post_f07_r437_buffer_base_owners = {
    "eden-core/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_base.h",
}
assert post_f07_r437_buffer_base_owners <= set(physical_all)
assert not post_f07_r437_buffer_base_owners.intersection(research_paths)
r437_path = next(iter(post_f07_r437_buffer_base_owners))
r437_body = (active / r437_path).read_text()
pinned_base = (root / "vendor/sources/eden/src/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache_base.h").read_text()
old_mark = "    void MarkWrittenBuffer(BufferId buffer_id, DAddr device_addr, u32 size);"
new_mark = """    // R437: preserve the legacy three-argument call while exposing explicit
    // write-tick ownership to the maintained native BufferCache implementation.
    void MarkWrittenBuffer(BufferId buffer_id, DAddr device_addr, u32 size,
                           bool needs_sync = true);"""
old_wait = "    void WaitForGpuFenceIfNeeded(Buffer& buffer);"
new_wait = """    // Same fence-wait member as the maintained R437 BufferCache body.
    void SynchronizeBufferWrites(Buffer& buffer);"""
assert r437_body.count(new_mark) == r437_body.count(new_wait) == 1
assert r437_body.replace(new_mark, old_mark).replace(new_wait, old_wait) == pinned_base, (
    "Unreviewed R437 BufferCache base-source drift")

# after the immutable 193-entry historical headless source catalogue.

    p.relative_to(root).as_posix()

        post_f07_feature_headless_owners | post_f07_r09_headless_owners |
        post_f07_p5_headless_owners)

      "historical_headless_catalog_preserved=193")
headless_rows = []

    if not entry.startswith("| `headless/"):
        continue
    cells = [cell.strip() for cell in entry.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
    assert len(cells) == 4 and cells[0].startswith("`headless/"), ("malformed headless row", entry)
    headless_rows.append((cells[0].strip("`"), cells[1], cells[2], cells[3]))
assert [r[0] for r in headless_rows] == headless_actual, (
    "headless source path catalog drift", len(headless_rows), len(headless_actual))
# The vendor-active graph above intentionally stores vendor-relative keys.
# Headless paths use repository-relative keys and need an independent map.
headless_graph = {}
for entry in audit.splitlines():
    if not entry.startswith("| "):
        continue
    cells = [cell.strip() for cell in entry.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
    if len(cells) == 9 and re.fullmatch("[A-Z][0-9]{2,3}", cells[0]) and cells[3].startswith("headless/"):
        # U23 was renamed without removing its owner; its CPU6 JIT fallback
        # changed after the frozen F07 snapshot and is retested separately.
        current_path = (
            'headless/jit_memory_policy.h'
            if cells[3] == 'headless/experimental_performance.h' else cells[3]
        )
        if current_path == 'headless/jit_memory_policy.h':
            assert cells[0] == 'U23'
            assert (root/'tools/ns2/check_unified_jit_cpu6_baseline_host.py').is_file()
        headless_graph.setdefault(current_path, []).append(cells[0])
```

`tools/check-addon-snapshot-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile the actual metadata cache registry and stress parallel readers.

The fully pinned Eden NCA scanner requires the native dependency checkout,
so this is a host-source concurrency test, NOT a complete SDK build.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
source = (ROOT / "headless/metadata_bridge.cpp").read_text()
marker = "namespace {\nstruct AddOns {"
start = source.index(marker)
end = source.index("\nvoid eden_scan_addons(", start)
registry_source = source[start:end]
assert "std::mutex& ScannedAddOnsMutex()" in registry_source
assert "std::mutex& ScanAddOnsJobMutex()" in registry_source

scan = source.split("void eden_scan_addons(", 1)[1].split("\nint eden_game_glyph_display_version(", 1)[0]
glyphs = source.split("int eden_game_glyph_display_version(", 1)[1].split("\nint eden_game_language(", 1)[0]
languages = source.split("int eden_game_language(", 1)[1].split("\nint eden_game_addons(", 1)[0]
addons = source.split("int eden_game_addons(", 1)[1].split("\nnamespace {", 1)[0]
assert "const std::lock_guard scan_job_guard{ScanAddOnsJobMutex()};" in scan
assert "AddOnScanTransaction publication(scanned);" in scan
assert "publication.Commit();" in scan
assert "ScannedAddOns().clear();" not in scan
assert "ScannedAddOns().swap(candidate_);" in registry_source
assert "UpdatesScanCompleted() = true;" in registry_source
assert "~AddOnScanTransaction()" in registry_source
assert "const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};" in glyphs
assert "const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};" in languages
assert "const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};" in addons
assert glyphs.find("ScannedAddOnsMutex()") < glyphs.find("entries.find(")
assert addons.find("ScannedAddOnsMutex()") < addons.find("scanned.find(")

fixture = """
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>
""" + registry_source + """
int main() {
    std::atomic<bool> start{false};
    std::atomic<bool> stop{false};
    std::atomic<unsigned> good_reads{0};
    auto reader = [&] {
        while (!start.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) std::this_thread::yield();
        while (!stop.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};
            if (!UpdatesScanCompleted()) continue;
            const auto& entries = ScannedAddOns();
            assert(entries.size() == 1);
            const auto& state = entries.begin()->second;
            assert(state.update_present);
            assert(state.update.size() >= 2);
            assert(state.update[0] == 'v');
            ++good_reads;
        }
    };
    std::thread readers[3] = {
        std::thread(reader), std::thread(reader), std::thread(reader)
    };
    std::thread writer([&] {
        start.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        for (unsigned i = 1; i <= 3000; ++i) {
            const std::lock_guard scan_job_guard{ScanAddOnsJobMutex()};
            // Keep the last complete snapshot visible until publication.
            // Every 73rd scan simulates a failed provider read: the old
            // map remains allocated but completion is invalidated, so
            // readers never consume stale or partially prepared entries.
            std::map<std::uint64_t, AddOns> pending;
            AddOns entry{};
            entry.update_present = true;
            entry.update = "v" + std::to_string(i);
            pending.emplace(i, std::move(entry));
            {
                AddOnScanTransaction publication(pending);
                if (i % 73 != 0) {
                    publication.Commit();
                } else {
                    const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};
                    assert(ScannedAddOns().size() == 1);
                    assert(ScannedAddOns().begin()->first == i - 1);
                }
            }
            if ((i & 31) == 0) std::this_thread::yield();
        }
        stop.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    });
    writer.join();
    for (auto& thread : readers) thread.join();
    assert(good_reads.load() > 0);
    // The latest successful scan is authoritative and complete.
    const std::lock_guard lock{ScannedAddOnsMutex()};
    assert(UpdatesScanCompleted());
    assert(ScannedAddOns().size() == 1);
    assert(ScannedAddOns().begin()->first == 3000);
}
"""
compiler = next((x for x in ("clang++-18", "clang++", "g++") if shutil.which(x)), None)
if not compiler:
    raise SystemExit("C++20 compiler unavailable")
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-addon-scan-stress-") as work:
    root = Path(work)
    cpp = root / "concurrent_metadata.cpp"
    out = root / "concurrent_metadata"
    cpp.write_text(fixture)
    subprocess.run([compiler, "-std=c++20", "-O2", "-pthread", "-Wall", "-Wextra",
                    "-Werror", str(cpp), "-o", str(out)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(out)], check=True)
print("PASS real C++ update registry: lock protected readers, serial scans, snapshot publication under 3 concurrent readers")
print("NOTE native NCA provider and PS5 SDK compilation still unqualified")
```

`tools/check-audio-upmix-scratch-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Real AppendBuffer + PCM ring: stable samples, one publication, warm allocation cost."""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
source=(ROOT/'vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/audio_core/sink/sink_stream.cpp').read_text()
start=source.index('void SinkStream::AppendBuffer(')
current=source[start:source.index('\nstd::vector<s16> SinkStream::ReleaseBuffer',start)]
old='        std::vector<s16> new_samples(samples.size() / system_channels * device_channels);'
new='''        // AppendBuffer does not call back into producers. Reuse this thread's
        // expansion storage across streams while preserving one PCM publication.
        thread_local std::vector<s16> new_samples;
        new_samples.assign(samples.size() / system_channels * device_channels, 0);'''
assert current.count(new)==1
previous=current.replace(new,old)
ring=(ROOT/'vendor/sources/eden/src/common/ring_buffer.h').read_text()
push='    std::size_t Push(const void* new_slots, std::size_t slot_count) {'
assert ring.count(push)==1
ring=ring.replace(push,push+'\n        assert(::publication_phase==1); ::publication_phase=2; ++::pcm_publications;')
common=(ROOT/'vendor/sources/eden/src/audio_core/common/common.h').read_text()
channels=common[common.index('enum class Channels : u32 {'):]
channels=channels[:channels.index('};')+2]
cpp=r'''
#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <limits>
#include <new>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <thread>
#include <type_traits>
#include <vector>
using s16=std::int16_t; using s32=std::int32_t; using u32=std::uint32_t; using u64=std::uint64_t; using f32=float;
thread_local unsigned publication_phase,pcm_publications,allocations;
void* operator new(std::size_t n) {
    ++allocations;
    if(void* p=std::malloc(n)) return p;
    throw std::bad_alloc{};
}
void operator delete(void* p) noexcept { std::free(p); }
void operator delete(void* p,std::size_t) noexcept { std::free(p); }
#include "ring.h"
CHANNELS
enum class StreamType { Render,Out,In };
struct SinkBuffer { u64 frames{},frames_played{},tag{}; bool consumed{}; };
namespace Settings { thread_local f32 volume=1.f; f32 Volume(){return volume;} }
struct MetadataQueue {
    void EmplaceWait(const SinkBuffer&) { assert(publication_phase==0); publication_phase=1; }
};
struct Stream {
    StreamType type{StreamType::Render};
    u32 system_channels=1,device_channels=2;
    f32 system_volume=0.8f,device_volume=0.9f;
    MetadataQueue queue;
    Common::RingBuffer<s16,0x10000> samples_buffer;
    std::atomic<unsigned> queued_buffers{};
};
namespace Before { struct SinkStream:Stream { void AppendBuffer(SinkBuffer&,std::span<s16>); }; BEFORE }
namespace After { struct SinkStream:Stream { void AppendBuffer(SinkBuffer&,std::span<s16>); }; AFTER }
template<class S> unsigned Append(S& stream,std::vector<s16>& samples) {
    SinkBuffer buffer{samples.size()/stream.system_channels};
    publication_phase=pcm_publications=allocations=0;
    stream.AppendBuffer(buffer,samples);
    const auto result=allocations;
    assert(publication_phase==2 && pcm_publications==1);
    return result;
}
void Run(unsigned identity) {
    Settings::volume=identity?1.75f:0.7f;
    unsigned before_allocations=0,after_allocations=0;
    for(const auto& [in,out]:std::array<std::pair<u32,u32>,4>{{{1,2},{2,6},{6,2},{2,2}}}) {
        Before::SinkStream before;
        After::SinkStream after;
        before.system_channels=after.system_channels=in;
        before.device_channels=after.device_channels=out;
        // Warm the largest valid block; subsequent blocks reuse capacity.
        std::vector<s16> warm(256*in,73);
        Append(after,warm);
        (void)after.samples_buffer.Pop(256*out);
        for(unsigned iteration=0;iteration<128;++iteration) {
            const auto frames=32*(1+iteration%8);
            std::vector<s16> left(frames*in);
            for(std::size_t i=0;i<left.size();++i)
                left[i]=static_cast<s16>((i*29+iteration*97+identity*13)%65536-32768);
            auto right=left;
            const auto old_alloc=Append(before,left),new_alloc=Append(after,right);
            assert(old_alloc==(in<out?1u:0u) && new_alloc==0);
            before_allocations+=old_alloc; after_allocations+=new_alloc;
            assert(left==right);
            auto old_pcm=before.samples_buffer.Pop(frames*out);
            auto new_pcm=after.samples_buffer.Pop(frames*out);
            assert(old_pcm.size()==frames*out && old_pcm==new_pcm);
        }
        assert(before.queued_buffers==128 && after.queued_buffers==129);
    }
    // Queue overflow still rejects the entire block before any publication.
    After::SinkStream full;
    std::vector<s16> occupied(0x10000);
    publication_phase=1; full.samples_buffer.Push(occupied);
    SinkBuffer buffer{1}; std::array<s16,1> sample{2};
    publication_phase=pcm_publications=0;
    try { full.AppendBuffer(buffer,sample); assert(false); }
    catch(const std::overflow_error&) { assert(publication_phase==0 && pcm_publications==0); }
    After::SinkStream input;
    input.type=StreamType::In;
    input.AppendBuffer(buffer,sample);
    assert(publication_phase==0 && pcm_publications==0);
    std::printf("AUDIO_UPMIX_HOST_PASS producer=%u upmix_blocks_after_warmup=256 allocations=%u->%u PCM=bit_exact publication=single\n",
                identity,before_allocations,after_allocations);
}
int main() {
    std::thread first(Run,0),second(Run,1);
    first.join();second.join();
    std::puts("AUDIO_UPMIX_TLS_PASS producers=2 channel_pairs=1to2,2to6,6to2,2to2 volumes=2 ring_wrap=covered overflow=rejected");
}
'''.replace('CHANNELS',channels).replace('BEFORE',previous).replace('AFTER',current)
compiler=shutil.which('clang++-18') or shutil.which('clang++') or shutil.which('g++')
assert compiler
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='encore-audio-upmix-') as temp:
    folder=Path(temp);(folder/'ring.h').write_text(ring)
    unit,binary=folder/'main.cpp',folder/'audio';unit.write_text(cpp)
    subprocess.run([compiler,'-std=c++20','-O2','-g','-Wall','-Wextra','-Werror',
                    '-ffp-contract=off','-pthread','-fsanitize=address,undefined','-fno-sanitize-recover=all',
                    '-I'+str(folder),str(unit),'-o',str(binary)],check=True,timeout=60)
    subprocess.run([str(binary)],check=True,timeout=30)
print('AUDIO_UPMIX_HOST_ONLY native_audio_timing_and_PS5_stutters=unverified')
```

`tools/check-buffer-write-ahead-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Source-only, sanitizer-backed regressions for conservative registered-buffer write ahead.

No console binary, guest memory or graphics pipeline is touched by this test.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import tempfile

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
header = root / 'headless/buffer_write_ahead.h'
generator = (root / 'tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py').read_text()
policy = (root / 'headless/performance.h').read_text()
settings = (root / 'headless/main.cpp').read_text()
assert header.is_file()
assert 'BufferWriteAhead::MarkFollowingPages' in generator
assert 'buffer_cache.IsRegionRegistered' in generator
assert 'buffer_cache.OnCPUWrite' in generator
assert 'cpu_write_ahead' in policy and 'cpu_write_ahead' in settings
assert 'cpu_write_ahead{0}' in policy  # Unproven on the actual title: default off.

code = r'''
#include "buffer_write_ahead.h"
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <set>
#include <vector>
using Eden::BufferWriteAhead::MarkFollowingPages;
int main() {
    std::set<std::uint64_t> registered{4096,8192,12288,16384,20480,24576};
    std::set<std::uint64_t> gpu_modified{16384};
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> touched;
    auto covers = [&](std::uint64_t a, std::uint64_t n) {
        assert(n == 4096);
        return registered.contains(a);
    };
    auto write = [&](std::uint64_t a, std::uint64_t n) {
        assert(n == 4096);
        touched.push_back(a);
        return gpu_modified.contains(a);  // true: GPU owns the page, stop.
    };
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(64, 128, 0, covers, write) == 0 && touched.empty());
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(64, 128, 64, covers, write) == 3);
    assert((touched == std::vector<std::uint64_t>{4096,8192,12288,16384}));
    touched.clear();
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(64, 4096, 64, covers, write) == 2);
    assert((touched == std::vector<std::uint64_t>{8192,12288,16384}));
    touched.clear();
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(24576, 2, 64, covers, write) == 0 && touched.empty());
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(0, 0, 64, covers, write) == 0 && touched.empty());
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(UINT64_MAX-1, 20, 64, covers, write) == 0 && touched.empty());
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(UINT64_MAX-4097, 2, 64, covers, write) == 0 && touched.empty());
    registered.clear(); gpu_modified.clear();
    for(unsigned i=1;i<200;++i) registered.insert(std::uint64_t(i)*4096);
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(0, 1, 500, covers, write) == 64); // hard cap
    assert(touched.size() == 64);
    touched.clear();
    registered.erase(8192);
    assert(MarkFollowingPages(0, 1, 64, covers, write) == 1);
    assert((touched == std::vector<std::uint64_t>{4096}));
}
'''
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='encore-buffer-write-') as directory:
    cpp = Path(directory) / 'check.cpp'
    binary = Path(directory) / 'check'
    cpp.write_text(code)
    compiler = os.getenv('CXX', 'clang++')
    subprocess.run([compiler, '-std=c++20', '-O1', '-g', '-Wall', '-Wextra',
                    '-fsanitize=address,undefined', '-fno-sanitize-recover=all',
                    '-I', str(header.parent), str(cpp), '-o', str(binary)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(binary)], check=True)
print('BUFFER_WRITE_AHEAD_HOST_PASS default_off=1 page_alignment=1 stop_at_gpu_owned=1 overflow=1 cap=64')
```

`tools/check-ci-neutral-labels.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Enforce neutral, user-facing CI steps and selected core test messages.

Do not touch immutable third-party attribution, legal notices, required
source/toolchain identifiers, or artifact names consumed by automation.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
blocked = re.compile(r"\b(?:Sony|Nintendo|PlayStation|Switch[12]?|PS[345]|Xbox|Nvidia|AMD|Mesa|Microsoft)\b", re.I)
offenders = []
count = 0
for workflow in sorted((root / ".github/workflows").glob("*.yml")):
    for number, line in enumerate(workflow.read_text().splitlines(), 1):
        # Only the human-facing descriptions of steps, never IDs or filenames.
        match = re.match(r"^\s*-\s+name:\s*(.*?)\s*$", line)
        if not match:
            continue
        count += 1
        # NS2-only research CI deliberately names the guest generation and
        # target hardware so build artifacts cannot be confused with releases.
        # Shipping/production workflows keep the original strict neutral rule.
        research_workflow = workflow.name.startswith("ns2-research-") or (
            workflow.name == "ns2-native-ps5-research.yml"
        )
        if research_workflow:
            assert "research" in workflow.name
            continue
        if blocked.search(match.group(1)):
            offenders.append(f"{workflow.relative_to(root)}:{number}: {match.group(1)}")
# Core host harness diagnostics are user-visible inside the source-preflight
# job. Keep human-facing progress text neutral, but do not rewrite required
# ABI names, source paths, license notices or original upstream identities.
message_files = (
    "tools/check-ps5-direct-pool-host.py",
    "tools/check-ps5-guest-system-buttons.py",
    "tools/check-heap-growth-diagnostics-host.py",
    "tools/check-heap-growth.py",
)
messages_checked = 0
for relative in message_files:
    source = (root / relative).read_text()
    for number, line in enumerate(source.splitlines(), 1):
        if not re.match(r"^\s*(?:print|puts)\s*\(", line):
            continue
        messages_checked += 1
        if blocked.search(line):
            offenders.append(f"{relative}:{number}: {line.strip()}")
    # Historical messages with brand names may not return through future refactors.
    assert "Sony mspace unmapping" not in source
    assert "Sony PS untouched" not in source
assert messages_checked >= 4, "No core test status messages inspected"

if offenders:
    raise SystemExit("CI_STEP_NAME_BRANDING_FAIL\n" + "\n".join(offenders))
assert count >= 35, "No meaningful workflow steps scanned"
print(f"CI_MESSAGES_NEUTRAL_PASS workflow_steps={count} core_test_messages={messages_checked}")
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pin the allocator symmetry behind CodeQL C++ alerts #18-#23.

This checks source invariants of the third-party Boost 1.90.0 snapshot,
without changing its allocator implementation or suppressing active forks.
Run after git submodule update (CodeQL's checkout uses submodules: true).
"""
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
B = ROOT / "vendor/sources/eden-cpm/boost/boost-1.90.0/libs"
paths = {
    "vector": B / "container/include/boost/container/vector.hpp",
    "fca": B / "unordered/include/boost/unordered/detail/fca.hpp",
    "impl": B / "unordered/include/boost/unordered/detail/implementation.hpp",
    "foa": B / "unordered/include/boost/unordered/detail/foa/core.hpp",
}
sources = {}
for name, path in paths.items():
    if not path.is_file():
        raise SystemExit(f"Boost submodule unavailable: {path}")
    sources[name] = path.read_text()

checks = {
    "#23 vector allocator pair": (
        "vector",
        "return allocator_traits_type::allocate(this->alloc(), n);",
        "allocator_traits_type::deallocate(this->alloc(), p, n);",
        "this->deallocate(this->m_start, this->m_capacity);",
    ),
    "#22 fca exception rollback": (
        "fca",
        "buckets = boost::allocator_allocate(bucket_alloc, num_buckets);",
        "boost::allocator_deallocate(bucket_alloc, buckets, num_buckets);",
        "BOOST_CATCH(...)",
    ),
    "#20 fca bucket teardown": (
        "fca",
        "buckets = boost::allocator_allocate(bucket_alloc, num_buckets);",
        "(pb + i)->~bucket_type();",
        "boost::allocator_deallocate(bucket_alloc, buckets, num_buckets);",
    ),
    "#21 fca group teardown": (
        "fca",
        "groups = boost::allocator_allocate(group_alloc, num_groups);",
        "(pg + i)->~group();",
        "boost::allocator_deallocate(group_alloc, groups, num_groups);",
    ),
    "#19 unordered node ownership": (
        "impl",
        "node_ = node_allocator_traits::allocate(alloc_, 1);",
        "boost::unordered::detail::func::destroy(boost::to_address(node_));",
        "node_allocator_traits::deallocate(alloc_, node_, 1);",
    ),
    "#18 foa contiguous buffer": (
        "foa",
        "arrays.elements_=storage_traits::allocate(sal,buffer_size(groups_size));",
        "storage_traits::deallocate(",
        "sal,arrays.elements_,buffer_size(arrays.groups_size_mask+1)",
    ),
}
for desc, (name, *tokens) in checks.items():
    source = sources[name]
    for token in tokens:
        assert token in source, (desc, "missing allocator ownership evidence", token)

config = (ROOT / ".github/codeql/codeql-config.yml").read_text()
workflow = (ROOT / ".github/workflows/codeql-advanced.yml").read_text()
positive, excluded = config.split("paths-ignore:", 1)
for keep in ("  - headless", "  - src", "  - tools", "  - vendor/encore-active"):
    assert keep in positive, ("active first-party scope disappeared", keep)
for path in paths.values():
    relative = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
    assert f"  - '{relative}'" in excluded, ("audited file missing scoped exception", relative)
assert not any(line.strip().startswith("- ") and "vendor/encore-active" in line
               for line in excluded.splitlines()), "active renderer excluded"
assert "config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml" in workflow
assert "build-mode: none" in workflow
print("ENCORE_CODEQL_ALLOCATOR_PAIR_AUDIT_PASS: alerts #18-#23, active scope retained")
```

`tools/check-controller-semantic-mapping.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Host-compile the actual controller mapping contract, with no PS5 app build.

Protects immutable global/game-specific emulator-input semantics independently of in-game glyph artwork.
This cannot fix a game's own Nintendo prompt textures or applet UI.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
# Source contract: default PlayStation mapping must keep the previously
# qualified in-match auto selection. The 2026-10-08 regression was a single
# launch-time SetAdaptivePlayStation(false) despite a PlayStation profile.
launch = (ROOT / "headless/main.cpp").read_text()
pad_runtime = (ROOT / "headless/pad.cpp").read_text()
assert "pad->SetAdaptivePlayStation" not in launch
assert "mapping_context" not in pad_runtime
assert "adaptive_playstation" not in pad_runtime
assert '(effective_layout == 1 ? "Switch" : "PlayStation")' in launch
assert "Eden::ResolveSessionButtonMapping(" in launch
assert "Eden::ResolveGameTitleId(rom_metadata_id, selected_game)" in launch
assert "const int pad = active_mapping[game];" in pad_runtime
# Global/menu button semantics never move as a side effect of guest input.
# Explicit FC27 match-profile activation is allowed and must be consumed.
assert "gameplay_chord" not in pad_runtime
assert "EDEN_PAD_GAMEPLAY_PROFILE" not in pad_runtime
assert "pad->SetMapping(mapping);" in launch
assert "kSwitchMapping" not in pad_runtime
CXX = next((x for x in ("clang++-18", "clang++", "g++") if shutil.which(x)), None)
if not CXX:
    raise SystemExit("C++20 compiler is required for button mapping regression")

code = r"""
#include "button_mapping.h"
#include <cassert>
#include <array>
#include <string_view>
using namespace Eden;

void check_bijection(const ButtonMapping& m) {
    assert(ValidMapping(m));
    for (int game = 0; game < kGameButtons; ++game)
        assert(MappedTo(m, m[game]) == game);
}

int main() {
    static_assert(kGameButtons == 12);
    static_assert(kPadButtons == 13);
    static_assert(kPlayStationMapping[game_a] == pad_cross);
    static_assert(kPlayStationMapping[game_b] == pad_circle);
    static_assert(kPlayStationMapping[game_x] == pad_square);
    static_assert(kPlayStationMapping[game_y] == pad_triangle);
    static_assert(kSwitchMapping[game_a] == pad_circle);
    static_assert(kSwitchMapping[game_b] == pad_cross);
    static_assert(kSwitchMapping[game_x] == pad_triangle);
    static_assert(kSwitchMapping[game_y] == pad_square);
    // In-game visual packs carry guest-action art, not hardware pin positions.
    // Only a fixed Cross-confirm session admits PS action glyphs.
    const auto ps_session = ResolveSessionButtonMapping(0, kPlayStationMapping, -1, false, kPlayStationMapping);
    const auto switch_session = ResolveSessionButtonMapping(1, kSwitchMapping, -1, false, kSwitchMapping);
    const auto switch_title = ResolveSessionButtonMapping(0, kPlayStationMapping, 1, false, kSwitchMapping);
    auto custom_buttons = kPlayStationMapping;
    custom_buttons = Assign(custom_buttons, game_a, pad_circle);
    const auto custom_session = ResolveSessionButtonMapping(0, kPlayStationMapping, 0, true, custom_buttons);
    assert(CompatibleWithPlayStationActionGlyphs(ps_session));
    assert(!CompatibleWithPlayStationActionGlyphs(switch_session));
    assert(!CompatibleWithPlayStationActionGlyphs(switch_title));
    assert(!CompatibleWithPlayStationActionGlyphs(custom_session));
    assert(BaseMappingForLayout(0) == kPlayStationMapping);
    assert(BaseMappingForLayout(1) == kSwitchMapping);
    assert(!MappingIsCustom(kPlayStationMapping, 0));
    assert(!MappingIsCustom(kSwitchMapping, 1));
    assert(MappingIsCustom(kPlayStationMapping, 1));

    for (const auto& base : {kPlayStationMapping, kSwitchMapping}) {
        check_bijection(base);
        // Every valid reassignment swaps the two guest functions, without
        // accidentally aliasing another action to the same physical key.
        for (int guest = 0; guest < kGameButtons; ++guest) {
            for (int target = 0; target < kPadButtons; ++target) {
                const auto original = base;
                auto candidate = Assign(base, guest, target);
                check_bijection(candidate);
                assert(candidate[guest] == target);
                const int original_guest = MappedTo(original, target);
                if (original_guest >= 0 && original_guest != guest)
                    assert(candidate[original_guest] == original[guest]);
                for (int other = 0; other < kGameButtons; ++other)
                    if (other != guest && other != original_guest)
                        assert(candidate[other] == original[other]);
            }
        }
    }
    const auto unchanged = kDefaultMapping;
    assert(Assign(unchanged, -1, pad_cross) == unchanged);
    assert(Assign(unchanged, kGameButtons, pad_cross) == unchanged);
    assert(Assign(unchanged, game_a, -1) == unchanged);
    assert(Assign(unchanged, game_a, kPadButtons) == unchanged);
    auto duplicate = unchanged;
    duplicate[game_b] = duplicate[game_a];
    assert(!ValidMapping(duplicate));
    auto out_of_range = unchanged;
    out_of_range[game_a] = kPadButtons;
    assert(!ValidMapping(out_of_range));

    // Input mapping changes guest *actions*, never the game's artwork.
    // The semantic test does not inspect or replace texture assets.
}
"""
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-controller-semantics-") as folder:
    tmp = Path(folder)
    source, exe = tmp / "test.cpp", tmp / "test"
    source.write_text(code)
    subprocess.run([CXX, "-std=c++20", "-O2", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                    "-I", str(ROOT / "headless"), str(source), "-o", str(exe)],
                   check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(exe)], check=True)
print("PASS controller PS5/Switch mapping semantics, bijection, custom swaps, invalid inputs")
print("In-game glyph replacement and FC27 scene-specific prompts: NOT TESTED")
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Host-only fixture for exact ELF .text-size provenance, no PS5 build."""
import hashlib
import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import struct

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
source = root / "tools/ci/write-crash-provenance.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("eden_crash_provenance", source)
assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)

buf = bytearray(0x300)
buf[:6] = b"\x7fELF\x02\x01"
names = b"\0.shstrtab\0.text\0"
buf[0x100:0x100+len(names)] = names
buf[0x120:0x160] = b"\x90" * 64
struct.pack_into("<Q", buf, 0x28, 0x200)
struct.pack_into("<HHH", buf, 0x3A, 64, 3, 1)
fmt = "<IIQQQQIIQQ"
struct.pack_into(fmt, buf, 0x200 + 64, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0x100, len(names), 0, 0, 1, 0)
struct.pack_into(fmt, buf, 0x200 + 128, 11, 1, 6, 0x400000, 0x120, 64, 0, 0, 16, 0)

assert m.text_size(bytes(buf)) == 64
bad_ident = bytearray(buf)
bad_ident[5] = 2  # big-endian rejected
try:
    m.text_size(bytes(bad_ident))
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("bad ELF identity accepted")
bad_offset = bytearray(buf)
struct.pack_into("<Q", bad_offset, 0x200 + 128 + 24, len(buf) + 4096)
try:
    m.text_size(bytes(bad_offset))
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("out-of-file .text accepted")
bad_shstr = bytearray(buf)
struct.pack_into("<H", bad_shstr, 0x3E, 9)
try:
    m.text_size(bytes(bad_shstr))
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError("invalid string table index accepted")

# The authoritative symbolizer must still fail closed on mismatched ELF code
# size; the receipt alone never blesses a crash RIP against a different build.
symbolizer_path = root / "tools/symbolize-crash.py"
symbolizer = symbolizer_path.read_text()
assert "REFUSED symbolization:" in symbolizer and "!= size" in symbolizer
spec_symbols = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("eden_symbolizer", symbolizer_path)
assert spec_symbols and spec_symbols.loader
sym = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec_symbols)
spec_symbols.loader.exec_module(sym)
valid = {"schema": 1, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x40",
         "files": {"unstripped_elf": {"sha256": hashlib.sha256(buf).hexdigest()}}}
sym.verify_elf_receipt(bytes(buf), 64, valid)
for wrong in (
    {"schema": 1, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x40", "files": {"unstripped_elf": {"sha256": "0" * 64}}},
    {"schema": 1, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x41", "files": valid["files"]},
    {"schema": 0, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x40", "files": valid["files"]},
    {"schema": 1, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x40", "files": None},
    {"schema": 1, "elf_text_size_hex": "0x40", "files": {"unstripped_elf": None}},
):
    try:
        sym.verify_elf_receipt(bytes(buf), 64, wrong)
    except ValueError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("mismatched ELF receipt passed symbolizer")
workflow = (root / ".github/workflows/build-040-zbic.yml").read_text()
writer = source.read_text()
assert 'build/release/PPSA99008' in writer
assert 'build/dev/PPSA99008' not in writer
assert 'if title_id != "PPSA99008"' in writer
assert '"app_title_id": title_id' in writer
assert "tools/ci/write-crash-provenance.py" in workflow
assert "--app build/release/PPSA99008" in workflow
assert "--app-title PPSA99008" in workflow
assert "build/headless-native/crash-provenance.json" in workflow
assert "build/symbols/crash-provenance.json" in workflow
assert "EDEN_TEST_ALL_ON" not in workflow
print("PASS host-only PS5 crash provenance: ELF bounds, SHA256 receipt binding and build gate")
```

`tools/check-crash-report.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Host check of the crash report (headless/crash_report.cpp).

Builds the report's source with a small program that crashes on purpose, twice: as the host
sees it, and with the console's calls stood in (the code that ships). Each case runs in its own
process and logs folder:

  a bad write on a named thread, three calls deep   the report names the signal, the address, the
                                                    thread, what was running, and the calls
  abort, an illegal instruction, an exception       each is reported; the exception with its text
  four threads crashing at once                     one report
  a crash right after a restart                     the app closes instead of starting again,
                                                    unless a game was started since
  the system refusing the restart                   the signal takes its usual course
  memory that cannot be read                        answered, not faulted on
  what the next start does (TakeLast)               the logs move beside the report, the notice
                                                    comes once, five reports stay

and the functions are named from the report with tools/symbolize-crash.py (--show prints that
report).
"""
import datetime
import pathlib
import re
import runpy
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    # This harness intentionally builds an ELF executable with the app's linker
    # script and validates ELF section/symbol based crash reports. Mach-O cannot
    # represent that test faithfully. Keep the complete harness mandatory in
    # Linux CI; the native PS5 target compiles crash_report.cpp locally.
    print('Crash-report source scheduled for native PS5 compile (ELF runtime/symbolization harness deferred to CI)')
    raise SystemExit(0)

PROGRAM = r'''
#include "crash_report.h"
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <exception>
#include <fstream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <unistd.h>

// The app's two ways out (src/lifecycle.c on the console).
static bool refuse;
extern "C" int eden_restart_app(void) {
    if (refuse) return -1;
    (void)!write(1, "RESTART\n", 8);
    _exit(42);
}
extern "C" int eden_exit_app(void) {
    if (refuse) return -1;
    (void)!write(1, "EXIT\n", 5);
    _exit(43);
}
#ifdef PS5_NATIVE
// The console calls the report makes.
extern "C" int sceKernelDebugOutText(int, const char* text) { return static_cast<int>(write(2, text, std::strlen(text))); }
extern "C" int sceKernelUsleep(unsigned microseconds) { return usleep(microseconds); }
extern "C" std::int64_t sceKernelGetDirectMemorySize() { return std::int64_t{12} << 30; }
extern "C" std::int32_t sceKernelAvailableDirectMemorySize(std::int64_t, std::int64_t, std::size_t, std::int64_t* start,
                                                           std::size_t* size) {
    *start = 0;
    *size = std::size_t{1234} << 20;
    return 0;
}
extern "C" std::size_t eden_heap_committed(void) { return std::size_t{256} << 20; }
extern "C" std::size_t eden_heap_large_held(unsigned* blocks) {
    *blocks = 3;
    return std::size_t{96} << 20;
}
#endif

#define CHECK(condition) \
    do { \
        if (!(condition)) { \
            std::fprintf(stderr, "check failed, line %d: %s\n", __LINE__, #condition); \
            return 1; \
        } \
    } while (0)

// Three calls deep, none inlined and none a tail call: the report must find the two callers.
static volatile int sink;
static volatile std::uintptr_t bad = 16;
[[gnu::noinline]] void Innermost(volatile int* target) {
    *target = 7;
    sink = 1;
}
[[gnu::noinline]] void Middle(volatile int* target) {
    Innermost(target);
    sink = 2;
}
[[gnu::noinline]] void Outer(volatile int* target) {
    Middle(target);
    sink = 3;
}

static bool Exists(const std::string& path) {
    struct stat info {};
    return stat(path.c_str(), &info) == 0;
}
static void Put(const std::string& path, const std::string& text) { std::ofstream(path) << text; }

static int TakeLastCheck(const std::string& logs) {
    using Eden::Crash::TakeLast;
    const std::string note = logs + "/crash-note.txt", eden = logs + "/eden_log.txt";
    // Nothing left by the previous run.
    CHECK(TakeLast(logs, eden).report.empty());
    // A note that does not name a report is dropped.
    Put(note, "../../elsewhere.txt 1\n");
    CHECK(TakeLast(logs, eden).report.empty() && !Exists(note));
    // So is one whose report is not there.
    Put(note, "crash-20260101-000000.txt 1\n");
    CHECK(TakeLast(logs, eden).report.empty() && !Exists(note));
    for (int run = 1; run <= 7; ++run) {
        const std::string stem = logs + "/crash-2026010" + std::to_string(run) + "-120000";
        Put(stem + ".txt", "report\n");
        Put(logs + "/stderr.prev.log", "that run's messages\n");
        Put(logs + "/heap.prev.log", "that run's stages\n");
        Put(eden, "that run's emulator log\n");
        Put(note, stem.substr(logs.size() + 1) + ".txt " + (run % 2 ? "1" : "0") + "\n");
        const Eden::Crash::Last last = TakeLast(logs, eden);
        CHECK(last.report == stem + ".txt" && last.restarted == (run % 2 == 1));
        CHECK(!Exists(note) && !Exists(logs + "/stderr.prev.log") && !Exists(logs + "/heap.prev.log") && !Exists(eden));
        CHECK(Exists(stem + "-stderr.log") && Exists(stem + "-heap.log") && Exists(stem + "-eden_log.txt"));
        CHECK(TakeLast(logs, eden).report.empty());  // announced once
    }
    for (int run = 1; run <= 7; ++run) {
        const std::string stem = logs + "/crash-2026010" + std::to_string(run) + "-120000";
        for (const char* part : {".txt", "-stderr.log", "-heap.log", "-eden_log.txt"})
            CHECK(Exists(stem + part) == (run >= 3));  // the five newest stay
    }
    std::puts("TAKELAST_OK");
    return 0;
}

static int ReadableCheck() {
    using Eden::Crash::Readable;
    char local[64] = "here";
    CHECK(Readable(local, sizeof(local)));
    CHECK(!Readable(reinterpret_cast<const void*>(std::uintptr_t{16}), 8));
    char* region = static_cast<char*>(mmap(nullptr, 8192, PROT_NONE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0));
    CHECK(region != MAP_FAILED);
    CHECK(!Readable(region, 4096));
    CHECK(mprotect(region, 4096, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE) == 0);
    CHECK(Readable(region, 4096));
    CHECK(!Readable(region + 4000, 200));  // runs into the page that cannot be read
    CHECK(Readable(local, sizeof(local)) && Readable(region, 4096));  // and nothing is left behind
    std::puts("READABLE_OK");
    return 0;
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    const std::string mode = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "";
    const std::string logs = argc > 2 ? argv[2] : ".";
    if (mode == "takelast") return TakeLastCheck(logs);
    refuse = mode == "refused";
    // As headless/main.cpp does: the exception's text goes into the report.
    std::set_terminate([] {
        const char* detail = "no active exception";
        if (const auto current = std::current_exception()) {
            try {
                std::rethrow_exception(current);
            } catch (const std::exception& error) {
                detail = error.what();
            } catch (...) {
                detail = "non-standard exception";
            }
        }
        Eden::Crash::Fail(detail);
    });
    Eden::Crash::Install(logs, "test-version", mode == "again" || mode == "again-game");
    if (mode == "readable") return ReadableCheck();
    if (mode != "again")
        Eden::Crash::SetSession("game Test.nsp (0100000000000000), Vulkan, resolution 2x, AMD FSR", true);
    if (mode == "audio-probe")
        std::thread([] {
            Eden::Crash::NameThread("audio");
            Eden::Crash::audio_worker_thread.store(
                (std::uintptr_t)pthread_self(), std::memory_order_release);
            Eden::Crash::audio_worker_phase.store(3, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            Eden::Crash::audio_completed_blocks.store(41, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            Eden::Crash::audio_last_output_result.store(-5, std::memory_order_relaxed);
            Outer(reinterpret_cast<volatile int*>(bad));
        }).join();
    if (mode == "abort") std::abort();
    if (mode == "ill") __builtin_trap();
    if (mode == "throw")
        std::thread([] {
            Eden::Crash::NameThread("Thrower");
            throw std::runtime_error("test exception: nothing caught it");
        }).join();
    const auto crash = [] {
        Eden::Crash::NameThread("CPUCore_1");
        Outer(reinterpret_cast<volatile int*>(bad));
    };
    if (mode == "many") {
        std::vector<std::thread> threads;
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) threads.emplace_back(crash);
        for (auto& thread : threads) thread.join();
    }
    std::thread(crash).join();
    return 1;
}
'''


def build(work, name, flags):
    source = work / 'crash-check.cpp'
    source.write_text(PROGRAM)
    binary = work / name
    # PS5_NATIVE also includes performance.h, whose production wall-clock
    # header lives in the pinned core. Stub only that header in this isolated
    # host harness, as check-game-liveness.py does; never alter production timing.
    if '-DPS5_NATIVE' in flags:
        clock = work / 'common' / 'cpu_features.h'
        clock.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        clock.write_text(
            "#pragma once\n#include <chrono>\n"
            "namespace Common {\n"
            "struct HostTestClock { std::chrono::nanoseconds GetTimeNS() const { return {}; } };\n"
            "inline HostTestClock g_wall_clock{};\n"
            "}\n")
    # The app's linker script names the code's bounds; the host's linker takes it as an input.
    subprocess.run(['clang++-18', '-std=c++20', '-O2', '-g', '-pthread', '-Wall', '-Wextra', '-Werror',
                    '-Wno-unused-parameter', '-fno-rtti', '-fuse-ld=lld', *flags, '-I', str(work),
                    '-I', str(root / 'headless'),
                    str(source), str(root / 'headless/crash_report.cpp'), str(root / 'tools/unwind.ld'),
                    '-o', str(binary)], check=True)
    return binary


def functions(binary):
    """name -> (offset into the code, size) of the three functions on the crashing thread's stack."""
    text_start, _offset, _size = \
        runpy.run_path(str(root / 'tools/symbolize-crash.py'))['sections'](binary.read_bytes())['.text']
    found = {}
    listing = subprocess.run(['llvm-nm-18', '-S', '--defined-only', str(binary)], capture_output=True, text=True,
                             check=True).stdout
    for line in listing.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        for name in ('Innermost', 'Middle', 'Outer'):
            if len(parts) == 4 and re.fullmatch(rf'_Z\d+{name}PVi', parts[3]):
                found[name] = (int(parts[0], 16) - text_start, int(parts[1], 16))
    assert set(found) == {'Innermost', 'Middle', 'Outer'}, listing[:400]
    return found


def run(binary, mode, console):
    """Runs one case in a fresh logs folder; returns (exit status, stdout, stderr, reports, note)."""
    logs = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f'crash-{mode}-', dir=binary.parent))
    result = subprocess.run([str(binary), mode, str(logs)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    reports = sorted(logs.glob('crash-2*.txt'))
    note = (logs / 'crash-note.txt').read_text() if (logs / 'crash-note.txt').exists() else ''
    return result.returncode, result.stdout, result.stderr, reports, note


def offsets(text):
    return [int(value, 16) for value in re.findall(r'eboot\+0x([0-9a-f]+)', text)]


def check(binary, console):
    where = functions(binary)
    inside = lambda offset, name: where[name][0] <= offset < where[name][0] + where[name][1]

    # A bad write on a named thread, three calls deep.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'thread', console)
    assert status == 42 and out == 'RESTART\n' and len(reports) == 1, (status, out, err[-600:])
    report = reports[0].read_text()
    assert report.startswith('ProsperoEden crash report\nversion: test-version (code size 0x'), report[:200]
    stamp = re.search(r'^time: (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d), (\d+) s after the app started$', report, re.M)
    assert stamp, report
    written = datetime.datetime.strptime(stamp.group(1), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
    assert abs((datetime.datetime.now() - written).total_seconds()) < 120, stamp.group(1)   # local time
    assert reports[0].name == written.strftime('crash-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.txt'), reports[0].name
    assert re.search(r'^what: SIGSEGV \(invalid memory access\), code \d+, address 0x0000000000000010$', report, re.M)
    fault = re.search(r'^where: eboot\+0x([0-9a-f]+)$', report, re.M)
    assert fault and inside(int(fault.group(1), 16), 'Innermost'), report
    assert re.search(r'^thread: CPUCore_1 \(0x[0-9a-f]+\)$', report, re.M), report
    assert 'running: game Test.nsp (0100000000000000), Vulkan, resolution 2x, AMD FSR\n' in report
    assert re.search(r'^  rip [0-9a-f]{16}  rsp [0-9a-f]{16}  rbp [0-9a-f]{16}$', report, re.M)
    assert re.search(r'^  r14 [0-9a-f]{16}  r15 [0-9a-f]{16}  flags [0-9a-f]{16}$', report, re.M)
    calls = offsets(report.split('calls found on the stack', 1)[1])
    middle = [i for i, offset in enumerate(calls) if inside(offset, 'Middle')]
    outer = [i for i, offset in enumerate(calls) if inside(offset, 'Outer')]
    assert middle and outer and middle[0] < outer[0], (calls, where)   # the callers, innermost first
    assert not any(inside(offset, 'Innermost') for offset in calls)    # the fault itself is "where"
    assert report.endswith('then: the app starts again\n')
    assert note == reports[0].name + ' 1\n', note
    assert 'EDEN_CRASH_REPORT installed=1 signals=7 ' in err and 'EDEN_CRASH what=SIGSEGV where=eboot+0x' in err
    assert f'thread=CPUCore_1 report={reports[0]} restart=1' in err, err[-400:]
    assert ('memory: largest free block 1234 MiB of 12288 MiB, heap 256 MiB and 96 MiB in 3 large blocks\n' in report) \
        == console, report

    # The functions, named from the report.
    named = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(root / 'tools/symbolize-crash.py'), str(reports[0]), str(binary)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    assert re.search(r'^where: eboot\+0x[0-9a-f]+   Innermost\(', named, re.M), named
    assert re.search(r'^  eboot\+0x[0-9a-f]+   Middle\(', named, re.M) and \
        re.search(r'^  eboot\+0x[0-9a-f]+   Outer\(', named, re.M), named
    assert 'REFUSED symbolization' not in named
    # Never let a different build attribute a system-library RIP to a
    # coincidentally similar application function. The Oct 10 console logs
    # exposed this exact source/build mismatch.
    wrong_size, substitutions = re.subn(
        r'\(code size 0x([0-9a-f]+)\)',
        lambda m: '(code size 0x%x)' % (int(m.group(1), 16) + 1),
        report, count=1)
    assert substitutions == 1 and wrong_size != report, (
        "Crash-report negative fixture must change exactly one code-size marker")
    mismatch_report = reports[0].with_name('wrong-symbols.txt')
    mismatch_report.write_text(wrong_size)
    mismatch = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(root / 'tools/symbolize-crash.py'),
         str(mismatch_report), str(binary)],
        capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert mismatch.returncode != 0 and 'REFUSED symbolization' in mismatch.stderr
    assert 'ELF .text size' in mismatch.stderr and 'code size' in mismatch.stderr
    if '--show' in sys.argv and not console:
        print(named)
    # As a console writes it: its code cannot be read there, so every value that points into the
    # code is listed with a "?". One that is no return address (an address inside the faulting
    # function that no call precedes) is left out when the functions are named.
    tool = runpy.run_path(str(root / 'tools/symbolize-crash.py'))
    data = binary.read_bytes()
    _start, at, _size = tool['sections'](data)['.text']
    begin, length = where['Innermost']
    stray = next(offset for offset in range(begin + 1, begin + length)
                 if not tool['after_call'](data[at + offset - 8:at + offset]))
    head, listed = report.split('calls found on the stack', 1)
    first, rest = listed.split('\n', 1)
    unchecked = reports[0].with_name('unchecked.txt')
    unchecked.write_text(head + 'calls found on the stack' + first + f'\n  eboot+0x{stray:x} ?\n' +
                         ''.join(line + (' ?\n' if line.startswith('  eboot+') else '\n') for line in rest.splitlines()))
    named = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(root / 'tools/symbolize-crash.py'), str(unchecked), str(binary)],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    assert re.search(r'^  eboot\+0x[0-9a-f]+   Middle\(', named, re.M) and \
        re.search(r'^  eboot\+0x[0-9a-f]+   Outer\(', named, re.M) and ' ?' not in named, named
    assert '\n1 stack values that point into the code but do not follow a call were left out.' in named, named

    # A real crash on the audio worker must include its last lock-free phase,
    # without allocating or resolving symbols on the signal handler path.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'audio-probe', console)
    assert status == 42 and len(reports) == 1, (status, err[-300:])
    snapshot = reports[0].read_text()
    assert 'thread: audio (0x' in snapshot
    assert 'audio worker snapshot: phase=3 ' in snapshot
    assert 'blocks=41 output_result=0xfffffffb' in snapshot
    assert 'audio worker snapshot:' not in report  # non-audio threads excluded

    # Other ways to end.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'abort', console)
    assert status == 42 and len(reports) == 1 and 'what: SIGABRT (abort)' in reports[0].read_text(), (status, err[-400:])
    assert '\nthread: main (0x' in reports[0].read_text()
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'ill', console)
    assert status == 42 and len(reports) == 1 and 'what: SIGILL (illegal instruction)' in reports[0].read_text()
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'throw', console)
    report = reports[0].read_text() if reports else ''
    assert status == 42 and 'what: the app stopped itself\nreason: test exception: nothing caught it\n' in report, \
        (status, report[:400], err[-400:])
    assert '\nthread: Thrower (0x' in report and note.endswith(' 1\n')

    # Four threads at once: one report, one restart.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'many', console)
    assert status == 42 and out == 'RESTART\n' and len(reports) == 1, (status, out, len(reports))

    # Right after a restart the app closes; once a game was started it starts again.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'again', console)
    report = reports[0].read_text()
    assert status == 43 and out == 'EXIT\n' and note == reports[0].name + ' 0\n', (status, out, note)
    assert 'running: starting\n' in report and report.endswith('(it had just started again after a crash)\n')
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'again-game', console)
    assert status == 42 and note.endswith(' 1\n'), (status, note)

    # The system refuses: the report is there, and the signal ends the process as it always did.
    status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, 'refused', console)
    assert status == -11 and out == '' and len(reports) == 1, (status, out)
    assert 'EDEN_CRASH the app did not start again; the system handles the crash' in err

    for mode, answer in (('readable', 'READABLE_OK\n'), ('takelast', 'TAKELAST_OK\n')):
        status, out, err, reports, note = run(binary, mode, console)
        assert status == 0 and out == answer, (mode, status, err[-600:])


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='eden-crash-') as work:
    work = pathlib.Path(work)
    check(build(work, 'host', []), False)
    check(build(work, 'console-calls', ['-DPS5_NATIVE']), True)
print('Crash report: signal, address, thread, session, registers and calls; abort, illegal instruction and '
      'uncaught exception; one report for many threads; no restart loop; refusal falls back to the system; '
      'unreadable memory; logs kept beside five reports; functions named from the report PASS')
```

`tools/check-credit-attribution.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Keep named upstream contributors visible in both README and package legal notices."""
from pathlib import Path
import re

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
readme = (root / "README.md").read_text()
notices = (root / "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md").read_text()
credit_section = readme.split("## Credits\n", 1)[1].split("## Community\n", 1)[0]
author_section = notices.split("## Identified upstream authors, maintainers and project teams\n", 1)[1].split("## Emulator and compression\n", 1)[0]
pattern = re.compile(r"^- \[([^\]\n]+)\]\((https://github\.com/[^\s)]+)\) — \*\*Authors / maintainers: (.*?)\*\* —", re.M)
entries = pattern.findall(credit_section)
assert len(entries) >= 28, f"lost upstream author attributions: {len(entries)}"
assert len({url for _name, url, _who in entries}) == len(entries), "duplicate repository credit"
for name, url, authors in entries:
    assert authors.strip(), (name, url)
    assert f"- [{name}]({url}) — {authors}." in author_section, f"legal author credit missing: {url}"
legal_count = author_section.count("](https://github.com/")
assert legal_count == len(entries), (legal_count, len(entries))
assert "Sean T. Barrett" in author_section and "Mitsunari Shigeo" in author_section
print(f"Named project authors and maintainer attributions: {len(entries)} README / legal entries PASS")
```

```py
A PASS means the *known gaps* are still correctly blocked by the developer

def expect(text: str, anchor: str, label: str) -> None:
    assert anchor in text, f"Review {label}: missing source anchor {anchor!r}"

# Both JITs may emit guest loads/stores through a directly mapped page
# table and fastmem, bypassing DynarmicCallbacksXX::MemoryWrite*.
for name, source, signature in (
    ("a64", a64, "void ArmDynarmic64::MakeJit("),
    ("a32", a32, "void ArmDynarmic32::MakeJit("),
):
    config = source.split(signature, 1)[1].split("m_jit.emplace(config);", 1)[0]
    expect(config, "config.page_table =", name)
    expect(config, "config.absolute_offset_page_table = true;", name)
    expect(config, "config.fastmem_pointer = page_table->fastmem_arena ?", name)
    expect(config, "config.fastmem_exclusive_access = config.fastmem_pointer", name)
    expect(config, "if (!Settings::IsFastmemEnabled())", name)
    expect(config, "config.fastmem_pointer = std::nullopt;", name)
    assert "GuestStoreOrderGate" not in config, name
    assert "CommitPostStore" not in config, name
    expect(source, "m_memory.Write32(vaddr, value);", name)

# A direct guest-memory span exposes the backing data for writes. In the
# scoped Safe/Cached case, the destructor uses InvalidateRegion AFTER writes,
# rather than necessarily calling Core::Memory::WriteBlock. The template is
# generic over M; it must not be claimed to cover only CPU producer paths.
expect(guest, "m_memory->GetSpan(m_addr, this->size_bytes())", "span")
expect(guest, "m_data_span = {reinterpret_cast<T*>(ptr), this->size()};", "span")
# Read-only FLAGS do not make returned aliases immutable: data(), Read()
# and operator[] expose mutable T or span<T>. Do not infer writer coverage
# from FLAGS & GuestMemoryFlags::Write call-site searches alone.
for anchor in (
    "T* data() noexcept {",
    "T& operator[](size_t index) noexcept {",
    "std::span<T> Read(u64 addr, std::size_t size,",
):
    expect(guest, anchor, "GuestMemory mutability independent of flags")
scoped = guest.split("~GuestMemoryScoped()", 1)[1]
expect(scoped, "this->m_memory->InvalidateRegion(this->m_addr, this->size_bytes());",
       "scoped span")
expect(scoped, "this->m_memory->WriteBlock(this->m_addr, this->data(), this->size_bytes());",
       "copy fallback")
expect(memory, "u8* Memory::GetSpan(const VAddr src_addr, const std::size_t size)", "memory span")
expect(memory, "return impl->GetSpan(src_addr, size);", "memory span")
assert "GuestStoreOrderGate" not in guest
assert "CommitPostStore" not in guest

# host fastmem mapping loses write permission. This is a source-level route to
# investigate, NOT proof that every Dynarmic/JIT access or concurrent transition
# executes a callback. Ordinary untracked pages may still take direct paths.
expect(page_table, "RasterizerCachedMemory = 0b11", "tracked page type")
expect(page_table, "data_raw.fetch_or(0b111);", "atomic tracked mark")
expect(page_table, "return raw.marked && !ignore_marked ? 0", "masked direct pointer")
mark_region = memory.split("void RasterizerMarkRegionCached(", 1)[1].split("\n    /**", 1)[0]
for anchor in (
    "if (!Settings::values.use_reactive_flushing.GetValue() || !cached) {",
    "if (!cached) {",

    "entry.MarkRasterizerCached();",
):
    expect(mark_region, anchor, "tracked fastmem protection")

expect(memory, "on_rasterizer();", "CPU fallback notification")
expect(memory, "HandleRasterizerWrite(addr, sizeof(T));", "scalar tracked store")
# Importantly GetSpan uses a silent raw pointer, so marking alone does not
# close the writable GuestMemory alias loophole.
expect(memory, "GetPointerSilent(addr) : nullptr;", "silent span alias")

# The tracked-page transition protects the fastmem view first, then marks
# the PTE. The byte-map update does NOT synchronously stop JIT workers that
# already passed the guard; host mapping mutex protects the updater, not JIT.
# This inventory deliberately does not claim transition linearization.
assert mark_region.index("host_buffer->Protect(vaddr, size, perm);") < mark_region.index(
    "entry.MarkRasterizerCached();"), "Re-audit protection/mark order"
a32_protect = host_mem.split("void Protect(std::size_t offset, std::size_t length, std::uint8_t access)", 1)[1]

expect(checked_a32, "code.test(code.byte[r13 + index - checked_map_bytes], blocked_bit);", "JIT guard reads map")
# Compiler/JIT accesses that already read the old byte can still be in flight.
# No producer epoch/drain is present in this protection operation.

# producers, not direct evidence of bypassing CPU/JIT callbacks. Categorize

    "using DeviceGuestMemoryScoped =",
):

expect(gpu_dma, "Tegra::Memory::GuestMemoryFlags::UnsafeReadCachedWrite>", "GPU DMA scoped write")
expect(gpu_blitter, "Tegra::Memory::GuestMemoryFlags::SafeReadWrite>", "GPU blitter scoped write")
expect(gpu_vic, "Core::Memory::GuestMemoryFlags::SafeWrite>", "GPU video scoped write")
expect(gpu_manager, "return memory.GetSpan(*dev_addr, size);", "GPU to backing span")
expect(gpu_manager, "accumulator.Add(gpu_dest_addr, size);", "GPU deferred cache invalidation")

expect(gpu_driver, "return renderer->ReadRasterizer()->OnCPUWrite(addr, size);", "CPU write-to-rasterizer")

# CPU publication. A green source inventory remains a NO-GO verdict.

# Unlike a bare config-only inventory, the pinned x64 emitter DOES route
# marked page-table stores to callback fallback. The port's derived emitter
```

```py
"""Host gate for the inactive developer-only cache replay source bridge.

Validates pinned anchors and CMake OFF parsing, not a native compilation or
correct GPU execution; opt-in ON remains explicitly unqualified.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import hashlib
import subprocess
import tempfile

root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
bridge=root/"headless/guest_write_deferred_bridge.cmake"
code=bridge.read_text()

legacy_code=legacy_bridge.read_text()
maintained_m06 = root/"vendor/encore-active/eden-core/guest-bridge/memory_manager.cpp"
maintained_m07 = root/"vendor/encore-active/eden-core/guest-bridge/vulkan_rasterizer.cpp"

                  "\n" + maintained_m07.read_text() +
                  "\n" + maintained_m08.read_text() +
                  "\n" + maintained_m09.read_text() + "\n" +
                  maintained_m10.read_text() + "\n" + maintained_m11.read_text())

perf=(root/"headless/performance.h").read_text()

assert "guest_write_deferred_bridge.cmake" in base

# Fail-closed runtime qualification, independent of any developer toggle.
assert "inline constexpr bool kNativePostStorePublicationReady = false;" in replay
assert bridge_runtime.count("::Eden::GpuDeferredWrite::kNativePostStorePublicationReady") == 2
assert bridge_runtime.index("!::Eden::GpuDeferredWrite::kNativePostStorePublicationReady") < bridge_runtime.index("deferred_cpu_write_queue.Enqueue(core, address, size)")
assert "const bool defer_candidate =\n        ::Eden::GpuDeferredWrite::kNativePostStorePublicationReady &&" in maintained_m07.read_text()
assert bridge_runtime.count("::Eden::GpuDeferredWrite::GuestWriteIntent::StoreFollows") == 2
assert "::Eden::GpuDeferredWrite::ScopedGuestStoreIntent store_intent;" in legacy_code
assert 'string(FIND "${bridge_cpu}" "${${anchor}}" found)' in legacy_code
assert 'string(FIND "${bridge_cpu}" "${NESTED_ANCHOR}" found)' not in legacy_code
# Fail-closed documentation contract: the inactive candidate does not yet
# synchronize deferred writes before either CPU-read fast path. Pin BOTH bypass
# sites so a future change must replace this negative proof with a real ordered
# read/drain qualification before runtime activation can be contemplated.
reader=(root/"vendor/sources/eden/src/core/memory.cpp").read_text()
download=reader.split("void HandleRasterizerDownload(",1)[1].split("void HandleRasterizerWrite(",1)[0]
assert download.index("if (current_area.start_address <= address") < download.index("system.GPU().OnCPURead(address, size)")
gpu_src=(root/"vendor/sources/eden/src/video_core/gpu.cpp").read_text()

# invalidations BEFORE the backing RAM write has occurred. A replay-completion
# ticket is NOT sufficient to assert the new payload has become visible.
# Pin the real source ordering until there is an explicit post-store publication
# protocol and a native read-fence qualification.
write_block=reader.split("bool WriteBlockImpl(",1)[1].split("bool ZeroBlock(",1)[0]
tracked_store=write_block.rsplit("HandleRasterizerWrite(GetInteger(current_vaddr), copy_amount);",1)[1]
assert "std::memcpy(ptr, reinterpret_cast<u8 const*>(buffer) + offset, copy_amount);" in tracked_store

                  if item["path"] == "vulkan_rasterizer.cpp")
def m07_git_blob(text):
    data = text.encode("utf-8")
    return hashlib.sha1(b"blob " + str(len(data)).encode() + b"\0" + data).hexdigest()
# G07 is a separately reviewed post-MSAA write-commit transaction change.

g07_new_commit = "            // A VA can stay mapped while a guest remaps its physical pages.\n            // Recheck the exact pre-staging backing here, under the commit\n            // lock, not merely contiguous coverage. Matches also validates\n            // the full 49-bit span, so no second mapping walk is needed.\n            if (!staged_buffer_mappings.Matches(\n                    *resources, [this](u64 address) {\n                        return gpu_memory->GpuToCpuAddress(address);\n                    }))\n                return false;"

#include "core/gpu_dirty_memory_manager.h"
#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>
int main() {
    static constexpr unsigned Cores=4, Writes=400;
    Core::GPUDirtyMemoryManager dirty;
    std::array<std::atomic<bool>,Cores> finished{};
    std::vector<unsigned char> seen(Cores*Writes,0);
    auto receive = [&](PAddr a, std::size_t length) {
        assert(a>=2048 && a%2048==0 && length==64);
        const auto index=a/2048-1;
        assert(index<seen.size());
        ++seen[index];
    };
    std::function<void(PAddr,std::size_t)> callback=receive;
    std::vector<std::thread> writers;
    for(unsigned core=0;core<Cores;++core) writers.emplace_back([&,core] {
        for(unsigned i=0;i<Writes;++i) {
            const auto address=std::uint64_t(core*Writes+i+1)*2048;
            dirty.Collect(address,64);
            if((i%11)==0) std::this_thread::yield();
        }
        finished[core].store(true,std::memory_order_release);
    });
    while(true) {
        dirty.Gather(callback);
        bool all=true;
        for(auto& done:finished) all &= done.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if(all) break;
        std::this_thread::yield();
    }
    for(auto& w:writers) w.join();
    dirty.Gather(callback);
    for(unsigned i=0;i<seen.size();++i) assert(seen[i]!=0);

    // Same-region disjoint writes must union their 64-byte dirty masks.
    Core::GPUDirtyMemoryManager blocks;
    std::vector<std::thread> union_writers;
    for(unsigned c=0;c<4;++c) union_writers.emplace_back([&,c] {
        for(unsigned j=0;j<8;++j) blocks.Collect(0x200000+c*512+j*64,64);
    });
    for(auto& w:union_writers) w.join();
    std::vector<std::pair<PAddr,std::size_t>> combined;
    std::function<void(PAddr,std::size_t)> union_callback =
        [&](PAddr a,std::size_t n){combined.emplace_back(a,n);};
    blocks.Gather(union_callback);
    assert(combined.size()==1);
    assert(combined[0].first==0x200000 && combined[0].second==2048);
}
'''
```

```py
"""Static verification of user-supplied, licensed DualSense art integration.

SOURCE inspection only. Does not compile, launch a GUI or run on PS5.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import hashlib
```

```py
# Illustrative event count model, not an executed physical input test.
def events(values):
    previous = None
    publishes = []
    for value in values:
        if value != previous:
            publishes.append(value)
        previous = value
    return publishes
```
