`tools/check-shader-cache-pressure.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Host C++ test: preserve compiled shaders unless storage is short.

This tests the real header without invoking native PS5 filesystem calls.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
compiler = next((x for x in ("clang++-18", "clang++", "g++") if shutil.which(x)), None)
if compiler is None:
    raise SystemExit("Missing C++20 compiler for shader cache storage gate")

source = r"""
#include <cassert>
#include <chrono>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <system_error>
#include <vector>
#include "cache_budget.h"

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    assert(argc == 2);
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    const fs::path dir = argv[1];
    fs::create_directories(dir);
    std::vector<fs::directory_entry> entries;

    // Only hex .bin records matching the native compiler naming convention
    // may be removed. Non-shader files are never touched.
    for (const char* name : {"abc.bin", "1234.bin", "notes.txt"}) {
        std::ofstream out(dir / name, std::ios::binary);
        out.seekp((4 * 1024 * 1024) - 1);
        out.put('X');
        out.close();
        entries.emplace_back(dir / name);
    }
    fs::last_write_time(dir / "abc.bin",
        fs::file_time_type::clock::now() - std::chrono::hours(24));

    constexpr auto mib = std::uintmax_t{1024} * 1024;
    // Plenty of free disk => no artificial 64 MiB shader cap / pruning.
    assert(Eden::TrimShaderCache(entries, 1024 * mib, 40 * 1024 * mib) == 0);
    assert(fs::exists(dir / "abc.bin") && fs::exists(dir / "1234.bin"));

    // Full-ish disk: leave 1 GiB free on a large filesystem. Only the
    // oldest cache file should be removed to cover a 4 MiB deficit.
    assert(Eden::TrimShaderCache(entries, 1020 * mib, 40 * 1024 * mib) == 1);
    assert(!fs::exists(dir / "abc.bin"));
    assert(fs::exists(dir / "1234.bin"));
    assert(fs::exists(dir / "notes.txt"));

    // Unknown space => never delete shader caches on an untrusted estimate.
    assert(Eden::TrimShaderCache(entries, std::uintmax_t(-1), std::uintmax_t(-1)) == 0);
}
"""

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-shader-storage-") as temp:
    temp = Path(temp)
    cpp, exe = temp / "check.cpp", temp / "cache-test"
    cpp.write_text(source)
    subprocess.run([compiler, "-std=c++20", "-O2", "-Wall", "-Wextra",
                    "-Werror", "-I", str(root / "headless"),
                    str(cpp), "-o", str(exe)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(exe), str(temp / "records")], check=True)

print("PASS shader cache on-disk pressure: preserve, prune oldest, protect non-cache, fallback")
print("Native PS5 storage/syscall validation: NOT RUN")

```

`tools/check-shared-compute-storage-descriptors-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Test the real shared Vulkan Compute descriptor walker without a PS5 build."""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
VENDOR = ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-vulkan"
HEADER = VENDOR / "include/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_compute_storage_layout.h"
CPP = (VENDOR / "vk_compute_pipeline_cost.cpp").read_text()
GENERATOR = (ROOT / "tools/prepare-vulkan-port.py").read_text()
assert HEADER.exists(), "pinned vendor lacks shared Compute storage layout"
assert CPP.count("ComputeStorageLayout::ForEach(") == 3
assert "ASSERT(desc.count == 1)" not in CPP
assert "const u32 max_storage_slots = num_descriptor_entries > 32" in CPP
assert CPP.count("max_storage_slots,") == 2
assert "max_storage_slots" in GENERATOR
assert '#include "video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_compute_storage_layout.h"' in CPP
assert "ComputeStorageLayout::ForEach(" in GENERATOR
assert CPP.index("const auto valid_storage_layout =") < CPP.index("guest_descriptor_queue.Acquire(")
assert "resources.storage_buffers[index].is_written == writable" in CPP
SOURCE = r"""
#include <array>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <vector>
#include "video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_compute_storage_layout.h"
struct Desc {
    std::uint32_t cbuf_index;
    std::uint32_t cbuf_offset;
    std::uint32_t count;
    bool is_written;
};
struct Binding {
    std::uint32_t flat, bank, offset;
    bool written;
};
int main() {
    using Vulkan::ComputeStorageLayout::ForEach;
    const std::array<Desc, 2> descriptors{{
        {1, 0x10, 1, false},
        {5, 0x20, 3, true},
    }};
    std::vector<Binding> bindings;
    auto collect = [&](auto flat, auto bank, auto offset, auto written) {
        bindings.push_back({flat, bank, offset, written});
        return true;
    };
    assert(ForEach(descriptors, 4, collect));
    assert(bindings.size() == 4);
    assert(bindings[0].flat == 0 && bindings[0].bank == 1 &&
           bindings[0].offset == 0x10 && !bindings[0].written);
    assert(bindings[1].flat == 1 && bindings[1].bank == 5 &&
           bindings[1].offset == 0x20 && bindings[1].written);
    assert(bindings[2].flat == 2 && bindings[2].offset == 0x30);
    assert(bindings[3].flat == 3 && bindings[3].offset == 0x40);
    std::size_t visited{};
    assert(!ForEach(descriptors, 3, [&](auto,auto,auto,auto) {
        ++visited; return true;
    }));
    assert(visited == 1); // Caller preflights before mutating guest binding.
    const std::array<Desc,1> zero{{{0,0,0,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(zero, 32, collect));
    const std::array<Desc,1> unaligned{{{0,2,1,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(unaligned, 32, collect));
    const std::array<Desc,1> overflow{{{0,0xfffffff0u,2,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(overflow, 32, collect));
    const std::array<Desc,1> huge{{{0,0,0xffffffffu,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(huge, 32, collect));
    // Last complete 16-byte descriptor, without wrapping the CBUF offset.
    const std::array<Desc,1> boundary{{{7,0xfffffff0u,1,false}}};
    assert(ForEach(boundary, 1, [](auto f, auto b, auto o, bool w) {
        return f == 0 && b == 7 && o == 0xfffffff0u && !w;
    }));
    const std::array<Desc,1> off_by_one{{{7,0xfffffffcu,2,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(off_by_one, 2, collect));
    // The first word can fit in the 32-bit CBUF index while the rest of
    // the 16-byte SSBO descriptor overflows. Both generations must reject
    // this reflection BEFORE touching BufferCache or guest CBUF state.
    const std::array<Desc,1> partial_tail{{{7,0xfffffff4u,1,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(partial_tail, 1, collect));
    const std::array<Desc,1> last_word_only{{{7,0xfffffffcu,1,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(last_word_only, 1, collect));
    const std::array<Desc,1> tail_count_overflow{{{7,0xfffffff0u,2,false}}};
    assert(!ForEach(tail_count_overflow, 2, collect));
    // Fail-closed callbacks (e.g. mismatched QMD3 reflection or write flag).
    assert(!ForEach(descriptors, 4, [](auto f, auto, auto, auto) {
        return f < 2;
    }));
    assert(ForEach(std::array<Desc,0>{}, 0, collect));
}
"""
for tool in ("clang++", "g++"):
    compiler = shutil.which(tool)
    if not compiler:
        continue
    for optimization in ("-O0", "-O2"):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-compute-layout-") as tmp:
            source = Path(tmp) / "test.cpp"
            binary = Path(tmp) / "test"
            source.write_text(SOURCE)
            subprocess.run(
                [compiler, "-std=c++20", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                 optimization, "-I", str(VENDOR / "include"),
                 str(source), "-o", str(binary)],
                check=True, timeout=40,
            )
            subprocess.run([str(binary)], check=True, timeout=10)
        print(f"ENCORE_SHARED_COMPUTE_STORAGE_LAYOUT_PASS {tool} {optimization}")

```

`tools/check-shared-gpu-queue-lifetime-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Host-only P4.2: exercise the real shared GPU SPSC queue lifetime (NS1/NS2).

The active vendor header is compiled, not a mock queue implementation.
No PS5/native build, GPU calls, or guest code is executed.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
HEADER = ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-gpu/include/common/bounded_threadsafe_queue.h"
SOURCE = HEADER.read_text()
assert "std::array<Slot, Capacity> m_data;" in SOURCE
assert "std::destroy_at(std::addressof(m_data[pos].value));" in SOURCE
assert "std::construct_at(std::addressof(m_data[pos].value)" in SOURCE
assert "Capacity != 0" in SOURCE

TEST = r"""
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <stop_token>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include "common/bounded_threadsafe_queue.h"

struct Tracked {
    static inline int alive = 0;
    static inline int destroyed = 0;
    int id;
    std::unique_ptr<int> payload;
    Tracked() = delete; // Empty slots must never manufacture a T.
    explicit Tracked(int value) : id(value), payload(std::make_unique<int>(value)) {
        ++alive;
    }
    Tracked(const Tracked&) = delete;
    Tracked& operator=(const Tracked&) = delete;
    Tracked(Tracked&& other) noexcept
        : id(other.id), payload(std::move(other.payload)) { ++alive; }
    Tracked& operator=(Tracked&& other) noexcept {
        id = other.id;
        payload = std::move(other.payload);
        return *this;
    }
    ~Tracked() { --alive; ++destroyed; }
};

int main() {
    // A default-constructed queue must have no live elements, even for
    // a non-default-constructible command/payload type.
    {
        Common::SPSCQueue<Tracked, 4> queue;
        assert(Tracked::alive == 0);
        assert(queue.TryEmplace(17));
        assert(Tracked::alive == 1);
        Tracked output(-1);
        assert(Tracked::alive == 2);
        assert(queue.TryPop(output));
        assert(output.id == 17 && output.payload && *output.payload == 17);
        // A moved-from slot must be destroyed immediately after TryPop,
        // not when a future producer eventually reuses that location.
        assert(Tracked::alive == 1);
        assert(!queue.TryPop(output));
    }
    assert(Tracked::alive == 0);
    {
        Common::SPSCQueue<Tracked, 2> queue;
        assert(queue.TryEmplace(1));
        assert(queue.TryEmplace(2));
        assert(!queue.TryEmplace(3)); // Full: no construction or destruction.
        assert(Tracked::alive == 2);
        // Destruction without popping must retire the two queued payloads.
    }
    assert(Tracked::alive == 0);
    {
        Common::SPSCQueue<Tracked, 2> queue;
        std::stop_source cancel;
        assert(queue.EmplaceWaitWithStopToken(cancel.get_token(), 4));
        assert(queue.EmplaceWaitWithStopToken(cancel.get_token(), 5));
        cancel.request_stop();
        assert(!queue.EmplaceWaitWithStopToken(cancel.get_token(), 6));
        assert(Tracked::alive == 2);
    }
    assert(Tracked::alive == 0);
    // Capacity reuse and cursor wrap retain FIFO and independent slots.
    {
        Common::SPSCQueue<int, 2> queue;
        int observed = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < 100000; ++i) {
            assert(queue.TryEmplace(i));
            assert(queue.TryPop(observed));
            assert(observed == i);
        }
        assert(!queue.TryPop(observed));
    }
    // Exercise the actual single-producer / single-consumer publication order
    // under concurrent wraparound, including move-only GPU-style payloads.
    {
        Common::SPSCQueue<std::unique_ptr<int>, 64> queue;
        constexpr int Count = 30000;
        std::thread producer([&] {
            for (int i = 0; i < Count; ++i) {
                auto item = std::make_unique<int>(i);
                while (!queue.TryEmplace(std::move(item)))
                    std::this_thread::yield();
            }
        });
        std::thread consumer([&] {
            std::unique_ptr<int> item;
            for (int i = 0; i < Count; ++i) {
                while (!queue.TryPop(item))
                    std::this_thread::yield();
                assert(item && *item == i);
                item.reset();
            }
        });
        producer.join();
        consumer.join();
    }
    assert(Tracked::destroyed >= 6);
}
"""

compilers = list(dict.fromkeys(
    path for name in ("clang++", "g++") if (path := shutil.which(name))))
assert compilers, "host C++20 compiler required"
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="encore-gpu-queue-lifetime-") as directory:
    temp = Path(directory)
    stub = temp / "common"
    stub.mkdir()
    (stub / "polyfill_thread.h").write_text("#pragma once\n")
    source = temp / "shared-gpu-queue.cpp"
    source.write_text(TEST)
    for compiler in compilers:
        for opt in ("-O0", "-O2"):

                       "-Wextra", "-Werror", "-I", str(temp),

            ran = subprocess.run([str(binary)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
            assert ran.returncode == 0, (compiler, opt, ran.stderr[-6000:])
```

`tools/check-sparse-header.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Every compiled file must have seen the derived common/sparse_large_vector.h.

The header's inline functions decide how Eden's large tables take their memory. The port
replaces it for all targets by an include folder that comes first (headless/inject.cmake). A
source file that still saw the original would announce a table's first write with mprotect
while the others give the slot memory of its own: this reads the build's dependency records and
fails when any object depends on the original header.

  check-sparse-header.py <build folder>
"""
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

build = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
canonical = root / 'vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/common/sparse_large_vector.h'
copied = build / 'headless/sparse/common/sparse_large_vector.h'
if not copied.is_file() or copied.read_bytes() != canonical.read_bytes():
    sys.exit('sparse header check failed: native copy differs from maintained canonical header')
accepted = {canonical.resolve(), copied.resolve()}
deps = subprocess.run(['ninja', '-C', str(build), '-t', 'deps'], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
original, derived, target = [], 0, None
for line in deps.splitlines():
    if line and not line.startswith(' '):
        target = line.split(':', 1)[0]
        continue
    path = line.strip()
    if not path.endswith('common/sparse_large_vector.h'):
        continue
    header = pathlib.Path(path.replace('\\', '/'))
    if not header.is_absolute():
        header = build / header
    if header.resolve() in accepted:
        derived += 1
    else:
        original.append(f'{target}: {path}')
if original or derived == 0:
    for line in original[:20]:
        print('  saw the original header:', line)
    sys.exit(f'sparse header check failed: {len(original)} objects saw the original, {derived} the derived one')
print(f'Sparse table header: {derived} objects compiled with identical canonical/derived headers, none with the original PASS')

```

`tools/check-sparse-index-boundary.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Prevent one-past-end sparse CPU/GPU table access at the 2-MiB slot boundary.

Inspect the actual Encore-maintained header, not removed CMake injection text.
Byte-for-byte parity with pinned source transformations is checked separately.
"""
from pathlib import Path

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sparse = (root / "vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/common/sparse_large_vector.h").read_text()
upstream = (root / "vendor/sources/eden/src/common/sparse_large_vector.h").read_text()
old = 'if (index > alloc_size / sizeof(T)) {'
new = 'if (index >= alloc_size / sizeof(T)) {'
assert upstream.count(old) == 3
assert sparse.count(new) == 3
assert old not in sparse
for capacity in (1, 2, 4096, 1 << 20):
    assert all(index < capacity for index in (0, capacity - 1))
    assert all(index >= capacity for index in (capacity, capacity + 1))
for token in (
    'std::mutex sparse_mutation_mutex;',
    'std::lock_guard<std::mutex> mutation_lock{sparse_mutation_mutex};',
    'if (IsCommittedPage(index)) return;',
    'void CommitPage(std::size_t index) noexcept {',
):
    assert token in sparse, token
assert sparse.count('mutation_lock{sparse_mutation_mutex}') == 2
# An unmap that clears just one 16 KiB host page inside an owned 2 MiB
# slot must zero its bytes, not only the committed-page bitmap. Otherwise
# subsequent reuse treats stale mappings as fresh; dense fallback needs it too.
section = sparse.split('    void DecommitPage(std::size_t index) noexcept {', 1)[1].split('    void CommitPage(std::size_t index) noexcept {', 1)[0]
zero = 'std::memset(reinterpret_cast<void*>(page_address), 0, HostPageSize);'
clear = 'committed_pages[page_index >> 6].fetch_and('
decommit = 'DecommitSparsePage(vector_base + slot_offset);'
assert section.count(zero) == 1
assert section.index(zero) < section.index(clear) < section.index(decommit)
assert 'only calls here for a' in section
# Model the multi-page slot lifetime: removing A with B still live must
# make A's previously set bytes zero before an A re-commit.
pages = {0: bytearray(b'ABCD'), 1: bytearray(b'WXYZ')}
committed = {0, 1}
pages[0][:] = bytes(len(pages[0]))
committed.remove(0)
assert 1 in committed and bytes(pages[0]) == bytes(4)
committed.add(0)
assert bytes(pages[0]) == bytes(4)
native = (root / "src/memory_pages.cpp").read_text()
commit_source = native.split("void CommitSparsePage(std::uintptr_t page) noexcept {", 1)[1].split(
    "std::size_t SparseCommitSpan()", 1
)[0]
# The global owner lock must protect SparseRangeOf and the first owned[slot]
# dereference; otherwise concurrent FreeSparsePages can free the bitmap.
assert commit_source.count("const std::lock_guard lock{sparse_mutex};") == 1
assert commit_source.index("const std::lock_guard lock{sparse_mutex};") < commit_source.index("SparseRange* range = SparseRangeOf(page);")
assert commit_source.index("SparseRange* range = SparseRangeOf(page);") < commit_source.index("range->owned[slot]")
print("PASS: sparse table zero/decommit and page commit serialized per vector")
print("PASS: pinned SparseLargeVector GetAndFault/Set/IsCommittedPage stop at count")
```

`tools/check-sparse-slot-reuse-host.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Compile and execute the actual Encore-maintained sparse decommit code on a host.

One 2 MiB slot backs 128 host pages of 16 KiB each. Clearing a page with
another still mapped must erase its contents, even without releasing the slot.
This is a host memory test, NOT a PS5 gameplay or GPU qualification.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sparse = (root / "vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src/common/sparse_large_vector.h").read_text()
anchor = "    void DecommitPage(std::size_t index) noexcept {"
assert sparse.count(anchor) == 1
method = anchor + sparse.split(anchor, 1)[1].split(
    "    void CommitPage(std::size_t index) noexcept {", 1)[0]
assert method.startswith(anchor)
assert "std::memset(reinterpret_cast<void*>(page_address), 0, HostPageSize);" in method
assert "for (std::size_t word = first_page >> 6; word <= last_word; ++word)" in method
assert "u64 bits = committed_pages[word].load(std::memory_order_acquire);" in method
compiler = (shutil.which("clang++-18") or shutil.which("clang++") or
            shutil.which("g++"))
assert compiler, "A host C++20 compiler is required"

prefix = r"""
#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
#include <vector>
using u64 = std::uint64_t;
constexpr std::size_t HostPageSize = 16384;
constexpr std::size_t HostPageBits = 14;
constexpr std::uintptr_t HostPageMask = ~(std::uintptr_t(HostPageSize) - 1);
constexpr std::size_t Slot = 2 * 1024 * 1024;
static unsigned releases = 0;
static unsigned bitmap_reads = 0;
struct TrackedAtomic {
    std::atomic<u64> state{};
    u64 load(std::memory_order order) const noexcept {
        ++bitmap_reads;
        return state.load(order);
    }
    u64 fetch_or(u64 bits, std::memory_order order) noexcept {
        return state.fetch_or(bits, order);
    }
    u64 fetch_and(u64 bits, std::memory_order order) noexcept {
        return state.fetch_and(bits, order);
    }
    void store(u64 bits, std::memory_order order) noexcept {
        state.store(bits, order);
    }
};
static bool dense = false;
std::size_t SparseCommitSpan() noexcept { return Slot; }
void DecommitSparsePage(std::uintptr_t p) noexcept {
    if (dense) return;
    ++releases;
    std::memset(reinterpret_cast<void*>(p), 0, Slot);
}
struct Table {
    using T = u64;
    u64* base_ptr;
    std::size_t alloc_size;
    std::vector<TrackedAtomic> committed_pages;
    Table(void* p, std::size_t bytes = Slot)
      : base_ptr(static_cast<u64*>(p)), alloc_size(bytes),
        committed_pages(Slot / HostPageSize / 64) {
        for (auto& bit : committed_pages)
            bit.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    void mark(std::size_t host_page) {
        committed_pages[host_page >> 6].fetch_or(
            u64(1) << (host_page & 63), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
"""
suffix = r"""
};
int main() {
    auto* raw = static_cast<unsigned char*>(std::aligned_alloc(Slot, Slot));
    assert(raw);
    std::memset(raw, 0, Slot);
    constexpr auto second = HostPageSize / sizeof(u64);
    {
        Table t(raw);
        t.mark(0);
        t.mark(1);
        std::memset(raw, 0xA5, HostPageSize);
        std::memset(raw + HostPageSize, 0x5A, HostPageSize);
        t.DecommitPage(0);
        assert(releases == 0);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < HostPageSize; ++i) {
            assert(raw[i] == 0);
            assert(raw[HostPageSize + i] == 0x5A);
        }
        t.mark(0);              // reused page: no stale bytes
        t.DecommitPage(second); // page zero still retains the slot
        assert(releases == 0);
        t.DecommitPage(0);      // last mapped host page
        assert(releases == 1);
    }
    {
        // Keep the last slot page occupied. The original loop reloaded its
        // two bitmap words up to 128 times. The new scan loads at most twice.
        Table t(raw);
        constexpr auto last_page_index = Slot / HostPageSize - 1;
        t.mark(0);
        t.mark(last_page_index);
        bitmap_reads = 0;
        t.DecommitPage(0);
        assert(releases == 1 && bitmap_reads <= 2);
        bitmap_reads = 0;
        t.DecommitPage(last_page_index * (HostPageSize / sizeof(u64)));
        assert(releases == 2 && bitmap_reads <= 2);
    }
    {
        // Partial last bitmap word must mask bits outside the table.
        Table t(raw, HostPageSize + 4);
        t.mark(0);
        t.mark(1);
        bitmap_reads = 0;
        t.DecommitPage(0);
        assert(releases == 2 && bitmap_reads <= 1);
        t.DecommitPage(second);
        assert(releases == 3);
    }
    dense = true;                // fallback never releases the slot
    std::memset(raw, 0xCE, HostPageSize);
    {
        Table t(raw);
        t.mark(0);
        t.DecommitPage(0);
        assert(releases == 3);
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < HostPageSize; ++i)
            assert(raw[i] == 0);
    }
    std::free(raw);
}
"""
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-sparse-reuse-") as td:
    path = Path(td) / "sparse.cpp"
    program = Path(td) / "sparse"
    path.write_text(prefix + method + suffix)
    subprocess.run([compiler, "-std=c++20", "-O1", "-Wall", "-Wextra",
                    "-Werror", str(path), "-o", str(program)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(program)], check=True)
print("PASS: host C++ sparse table word scan, partial-slot masks and dense fallback")
```

```py
#include <algorithm>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <mutex>
using u64=std::uint64_t;
constexpr std::size_t HostPageSize=16384;
static u64 AlignUp(u64 value,std::size_t alignment) {
    return (value + alignment - 1) & ~(alignment - 1);
}
static u64 AlignDown(u64 value,std::size_t alignment) {
    return value & ~(alignment - 1);
}
struct Table {
    using T=u64;
    std::mutex sparse_mutation_mutex;
    std::size_t alloc_size;
    T* base_ptr;
    unsigned decommits=0, commits=0;

        assert(index < alloc_size/sizeof(T));
        ++commits;
    }
    void DecommitPage(std::size_t index) {
        assert(index < alloc_size/sizeof(T));
        ++decommits;
        auto* page=reinterpret_cast<unsigned char*>(base_ptr+index);
        std::memset(page,0,HostPageSize);
    }
INJECT
INJECT_COMMIT

int main() {
    constexpr std::size_t Capacity=2*HostPageSize/sizeof(u64);

    auto* bytes=static_cast<unsigned char*>(std::aligned_alloc(HostPageSize,3*HostPageSize));
    assert(bytes);

    Table t{ {},2*HostPageSize,reinterpret_cast<u64*>(bytes) };

    t.ZeroRegion(Capacity-3,Capacity-10);
    assert(t.decommits==0);
    // Clip the oversized end rather than writing into a foreign mapping.
    t.ZeroRegion(Capacity-3,Capacity+40);
    for(std::size_t i=0;i<2*HostPageSize-3*sizeof(u64);++i)
        assert(bytes[i]==0xA5);
    for(std::size_t i=2*HostPageSize-3*sizeof(u64);i<2*HostPageSize;++i)
        assert(bytes[i]==0);
    for(std::size_t i=2*HostPageSize;i<3*HostPageSize;++i)
        assert(bytes[i]==0xA5);
    // Whole committed page is reclaimed only for a completely covered page.
    t.ZeroRegion(0,HostPageSize/sizeof(u64));
    assert(t.decommits==1);
    for(std::size_t i=0;i<HostPageSize;++i) assert(bytes[i]==0);
    t.uncommitted_mode=true;
    t.CommitRegion(0,0);
    t.CommitRegion(Capacity,Capacity+100);
    t.CommitRegion(Capacity-5,Capacity-7);
    assert(t.commits==0);
    t.CommitRegion(Capacity-5,Capacity+100);
    assert(t.commits==1);
    t.CommitRegion(0,Capacity+100);
    assert(t.commits==3);
    std::free(bytes);
    std::puts("ENCORE_SPARSE_ZERO_COMMIT_BOUNDS_PASS");
}
```

```py
"""Exercise actual diagnostics, live thread clocks and unavailable-clock reporting."""
from pathlib import Path

import subprocess
import sys

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

source = cache / 'source/src'
original = (source / 'common/thread.cpp').read_text()
derived = (root / 'vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src' / 'common/thread.cpp').read_text()
include_line, derived_body = derived.split('\n', 1)
assert include_line.startswith('#include "') and include_line.endswith('"')
# Cached CI/native derivatives can remember the checkout path they were generated from.
# The contract is the injected performance header, not that stale absolute checkout prefix.
assert Path(include_line[len('#include "'):-1]).name == 'performance.h'
assert derived_body == original.replace(
    'void SetCurrentThreadName(const char* name) {',
    'void SetCurrentThreadName(const char* name) {\n    ::Eden::Performance::RegisterWorker(name);')

assert main.index('Performance::PlatformChecks()') < main.index('Common::Log::Initialize()')
# Development profiling owns periodic snapshots. Shipping blocks on the ordinary completion
# condition and carries no profiler/watchdog wakeup in the gameplay hot path.
development_wait = main.split('#ifdef EDEN_DEV_PROFILE\n                        for ', 1)[1].split('#elif defined(EDEN_DEV_ROM_ID)', 1)[0]
assert development_wait.count('Performance::Snapshot()') == 1
assert main.count('Performance::Snapshot()') == 1
shipping = main.split('// Shipping path: no periodic profiler/watchdog work while a game runs.', 1)[1].split('#endif', 1)[0]
assert 'Performance::Snapshot()' not in shipping
assert 'wait_for' not in shipping
assert 'completion->wake.wait(lock, completed);' in shipping
assert 'completion->return_to_menu' in main
if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    # The executable harness below intentionally exercises Linux/x86 host APIs
    # (CPUID/RDTSC, sched_getaffinity, clock_getcpuclockid and GNU ld --wrap).
    # On Apple Silicon, keep every source/derivative assertion above and leave
    # that Linux runtime control to CI; the native PS5 build compiles the real
    # x86_64-sie-ps5 implementation immediately after these source checks.
    print('Startup performance source/derivative contract PASS (Linux x86 runtime harness deferred to CI)')
    raise SystemExit(0)
code = r'''
#include "performance.h"
#include "fastmem.h"
#include <atomic>
#include <cassert>
#include <cerrno>
#include <semaphore>
#include <thread>
#include <time.h>
static bool fail_clock;
static bool wall_as_cpu;
extern "C" int __real_clock_gettime(clockid_t, timespec*);
extern "C" int __wrap_clock_gettime(clockid_t id, timespec* out) {
    if (fail_clock && id != CLOCK_MONOTONIC && id != CLOCK_REALTIME) {
        errno = EINVAL; return -1;
    }
    if (wall_as_cpu && id == CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID) id = CLOCK_MONOTONIC;
    return __real_clock_gettime(id, out);
}
// Link-time providers that performance.cpp reports from; not exercised here.
extern "C" void ps5_opengl_heap_snapshot(const char*, unsigned) {}
namespace Eden::Fastmem {
Stats WindowStats() noexcept { return {}; }
std::uint64_t Faults() noexcept { return 0; }
}
int main() {
    using namespace Eden::Performance;
    PlatformChecks();
    Totals timed;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < 1000; ++i) { Timer timer(timed, 16); }
    assert(timed.calls == 1000 && timed.requested_bytes == 16000 && timed.nanoseconds > 0);
    Totals slept;
    { Timer timer(slept); std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(20)); }
    assert(slept.calls == 1 && slept.nanoseconds >= 15000000 && slept.nanoseconds < 500000000);
    RegisterWorker("irrelevant");
    RegisterWorker("CPUCore_0");
    SampleCpu(0, 123, 0xabcd, 0x18, 0x3000000);
    SampleCpu(0, 999, 0xffff, 0, 1); // Same epoch must not publish a second sample.
    std::binary_semaphore ready{0}, release{0};
    std::jthread worker([&] {
        RegisterWorker("CPUCore_1");
        { Timer timer(compilation[1]);
          const auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::milliseconds(20);
          while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < end) std::atomic_signal_fence(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
        }
        SampleCpu(1, 456, 0x1234, ~0u, 0);
        ready.release(); release.acquire();
    });
    ready.acquire();
    Snapshot();
    fail_clock = true;
    SampleCpu(0, 123, 0xabce, ~0u, 0);
    Snapshot();
    fail_clock = false;
    SampleCpu(0, 123, 0xabcf, ~0u, 0);
    Snapshot();
    wall_as_cpu = true;
    PlatformChecks(); // A wall clock is not a usable owner CPU clock.
    SampleCpu(0, 123, 0xabd0, ~0u, 0);
    Snapshot();
    wall_as_cpu = false;
    fail_clock = true;
    PlatformChecks(); // An API returning unusable clocks must disable CPU metrics.
    SampleCpu(0, 123, 0xabd1, ~0u, 0);
    Snapshot();
    release.release();
    worker.join(); // No sampling after shutdown or join.
}
'''
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='eden-startup-') as directory:
    directory = Path(directory)
    (directory / 'check.cpp').write_text(code)
    executable = directory / 'check'
    subprocess.run(['clang++-18', '-std=c++20', '-O2', '-pthread', '-DARCHITECTURE_x86_64',

    assert output.count('EDEN_PERF_OWNER_CLOCK_CHECK valid=0 ') == 2

    snapshots = output.split('EDEN_PERF_SAMPLE ')[1:]
```

`tools/check-storage-contract.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile and exercise Encore's exact storage-root selection contract."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
source_text = (root / "headless/prosperoeden/eden_services.cpp").read_text()
start = source_text.index("bool EdenServices::set_files_folder(")
end = source_text.index("\nint EdenServices::filesystem_access()", start)
function = source_text[start:end]

harness = r'''
#include <cassert>
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <system_error>

namespace Eden {
static bool access = true;
static std::string saved;
bool FilesystemAccess() { return access; }
bool ValidAssetsDir(std::string_view path) {
    return !path.empty() && path != "/" && path.front() == '/' && path.back() != '/';
}
bool SaveAssetsDir(std::string_view directory) {
    saved = std::string(directory);
    return true;
}
void Report(const char*, const char*) {}
}

struct EdenServices {
    bool set_files_folder(const std::string& directory);
};

FUNCTION

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    assert(argc == 2);
    namespace fs = std::filesystem;
    const fs::path base = argv[1];
    const fs::path root = base / "external";
    fs::create_directories(root);

    // Valid external root => exactly the standard schema is prepared and one root is saved.
    assert(EdenServices{}.set_files_folder(root.string()));
    for (const char* name : {"keys", "firmware", "roms", "updates", "mods",
                             "save-import", "save-export", "ryujinx"})
        assert(fs::is_directory(root / name));
    assert(Eden::saved == root.string());

    // Root symlink => reject.
    fs::remove_all(base / "link");
    std::error_code error;
    fs::create_directory_symlink(root, base / "link", error);
    if (!error)
        assert(!EdenServices{}.set_files_folder((base / "link").string()));

    // Standard child symlink => reject instead of following it.
    fs::remove_all(root / "roms");
    fs::create_directories(base / "outside");
    error.clear();
    fs::create_directory_symlink(base / "outside", root / "roms", error);
    if (!error)
        assert(!EdenServices{}.set_files_folder(root.string()));

    // No elevated filesystem access => external/internal root selection is unavailable.
    Eden::access = false;
    assert(!EdenServices{}.set_files_folder(root.string()));
}
'''.replace("FUNCTION", function)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-storage-contract-") as tmp:
    tmp = Path(tmp)
    source = tmp / "test.cpp"
    binary = tmp / "test"
    source.write_text(harness)
    subprocess.run(["clang++-18", "-std=c++20", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                    str(source), "-o", str(binary)], check=True)
    subprocess.run([str(binary), str(tmp / "fs")], check=True)

print("Storage contract: fixed schema, symlink rejection and access gate PASS")
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Execute the real R352 native SurfaceFlinger teardown methods in a tiny C++20 host harness.

Only surrounding external classes are mocked; the actual three methods plus
FindDisplay() are compiled unmodified from our versioned translation unit.
No PS5 SDK, network, GPU hardware or permanent test files are required.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from pathlib import Path
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
import importlib.util

installer = ROOT / "tools/install-vendored-surface-lifecycle.py"
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("surface_installer", installer)
assert spec and spec.loader
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
original, active = module.check()
composer_original, composer_active = module.check_composer()
source = active.decode()
composer_source = composer_active.decode()

# The second maintained TU is part of the exact native ownership graph.
# Do not let a future staged installer silently omit its inventory contract.
catalog = (ROOT / "docs/EDEN_ACTIVE_SOURCE_CATALOG.md").read_text()
audit = (ROOT / "docs/EDEN_CORE_AUDIT_DEPENDENCIES.md").read_text()
owner = "eden-surface-lifecycle/src/core/hle/service/nvnflinger/hardware_composer.cpp"
assert f"| `{owner}` | `maintained-override` | N23 |" in catalog
assert f"| N23 | P0 | N03,N06 | vendor/encore-active/{owner} |" in audit
original_source = original.decode()


def extract(name: str, prefix: str = "void") -> str:
    marker = prefix + " SurfaceFlinger::" + name + "("
    assert source.count(marker) == 1, marker
    start = source.index(marker)
    brace = source.index("{", start)
    level = 0
    for end in range(brace, len(source)):
        if source[end] == "{":
            level += 1
        elif source[end] == "}":
            level -= 1
            if not level:
                return source[start:end + 1]
    raise ValueError("Unterminated actual SurfaceFlinger method " + name)


methods = "\n\n".join(
    (extract("FindDisplay", "Display*"),
     extract("AddDisplay"),
     extract("RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack"),
     extract("DestroyLayer"),
     extract("RemoveDisplay"),
     extract("FindLayer", "std::shared_ptr<Layer>"),
     extract("AddLayerToDisplayStack"))
)

for marker in ("WaitForComposite();", "RemoveLayerLocked(", "RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack("):
    assert marker in methods
assert methods.count("WaitForComposite();") == 2
assert "WaitForComposite();" not in original_source
assert "m_composer.RemoveLayerLocked" not in original_source.split("void SurfaceFlinger::RemoveDisplay", 1)[1].split("bool SurfaceFlinger::ComposeDisplay", 1)[0]

#include <cstdio>

#include <string>
#include <vector>
using u64 = std::uint64_t;
using s32 = std::int32_t;
namespace Nvidia { namespace Devices { struct nvdisp_disp0 {}; } }
struct Layer { s32 consumer_id; };
struct Display {
    u64 id{};
    struct { std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Layer>> layers; } stack;
};
struct MasterLayers { std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Layer>> layers; };
struct MockGpu {
    std::vector<std::string>* events{};
    void WaitForComposite() { events->push_back("wait"); }
};
struct MockNvDrv {
    MockGpu* gpu{};
    template<class T> MockGpu* GetDevice(int) { return gpu; }
};
struct MockComposer {

checks = r'''
int main() {
    {
        // A duplicate display ID must not create a hidden second stack;
        // teardown has to release exactly the stack known to FindDisplay.
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.AddDisplay(42);
        s.AddDisplay(42);
        assert(s.m_displays.size() == 1);
        auto layer = std::make_shared<Layer>(Layer{7});
        s.m_layers.layers.push_back(layer);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(42, 7);
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.size() == 1);
        s.RemoveDisplay(42);
        assert(s.m_displays.empty());
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{"wait", "release:7"}));
        s.AddDisplay(43);
        s.AddDisplay(44);
        assert(s.m_displays.size() == 2);
        assert(s.m_displays[0].id == 43 && s.m_displays[1].id == 44);
    }
    {
        // A binder can be attached to several displays, but only once per
        // display. Duplicate calls must not double-compose one BufferItem.
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{1, {}});
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{2, {}});
        auto a = std::make_shared<Layer>(Layer{7});
        auto b = std::make_shared<Layer>(Layer{9});
        s.m_layers.layers = {a, b};
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(1, 7);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(1, 7);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(1, 9);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(1, 7);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(2, 7);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(2, 7);
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(1, 99); // unknown binder, no insertion
        s.AddLayerToDisplayStack(99, 7); // unknown display, no insertion
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.size() == 2);
        assert(s.m_displays[1].stack.layers.size() == 1);
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers[0] == a);
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers[1] == b);
        assert(s.m_displays[1].stack.layers[0] == a);
        s.RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack(1, 7);
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.size() == 1);
        assert(s.m_displays[1].stack.layers.size() == 1);
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{"wait", "release:7"}));
        s.RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack(1, 7); // no second release
        assert(s.events.size() == 2);
        s.RemoveDisplay(2);

    {
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{42, {}});
        s.attach(42, 7);
        s.RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack(42, 7);
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{"wait", "release:7"}));
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.empty());
        s.RemoveLayerFromDisplayStack(42, 7); // idempotent; no needless fence waits
        assert(s.events.size() == 2);
    }
    {
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{99, {}});
        s.attach(99, 17);
        s.DestroyLayer(17); // Container::OnTerminate bypasses CloseLayerLocked
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{"wait", "release:17"}));
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.empty());
        assert(s.m_layers.layers.empty());
        s.DestroyLayer(17);
        assert(s.events.size() == 2);
    }
    {
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{13, {}});
        s.attach(13, 23);
        s.attach(13, 24);
        s.RemoveDisplay(13);
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{"wait", "release:23", "release:24"}));
        assert(s.m_displays.empty());
        s.RemoveDisplay(13);
        assert(s.events.size() == 3);

    {
        SurfaceFlinger s;
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{1, {}});
        s.m_displays.push_back(Display{2, {}});
        s.attach(1, 6);
        s.attach(2, 6);
        s.DestroyLayer(6);
        assert((s.events == std::vector<std::string>{
            "wait", "release:6", "wait", "release:6"
        }));
        assert(s.m_displays[0].stack.layers.empty());
        assert(s.m_displays[1].stack.layers.empty());
    }
    std::puts("SURFACE_LIFECYCLE_HOST_PASS actual source method bodies, acquired-slot cleanup and fence order");

    unit = stage / "test.cpp"
    binary = stage / "test"
    unit.write_text(mock + methods + checks)
    env = os.environ.copy()
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        # Older Apple linker cannot parse the SDK v27 architecture tags.
        for name in ("MacOSX15.4.sdk", "MacOSX15.sdk"):
            candidate = Path("/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs") / name
            if candidate.is_dir():
                env["SDKROOT"] = str(candidate)
                break
    subprocess.run(["c++", "-std=c++20", "-O1", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                    str(unit), "-o", str(binary)], check=True, timeout=50, env=env)
    subprocess.run([str(binary)], check=True, timeout=10)

# Exercise the precise CacheFramebufferLocked implementation that ships to
# the PS5. Reuse of a still-acquired slot is valid; a RELEASED slot must not
# appear in another layer's new composite when acquire fails.
def extract_composer(name: str) -> str:
    marker = "HardwareComposer::CacheStatus HardwareComposer::" + name + "("
    assert composer_source.count(marker) == 1
    first = composer_source.index(marker)
    opening = composer_source.index("{", first)
    depth = 0
    for end in range(opening, len(composer_source)):
        if composer_source[end] == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif composer_source[end] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return composer_source[first:end + 1]
    raise AssertionError("Unterminated HardwareComposer native implementation")

composer_method = extract_composer("CacheFramebufferLocked")
assert "if (it->second.is_acquired)" in composer_method
assert "return CacheStatus::CachedBufferReused;" in composer_method
assert "return CacheStatus::NoBufferAvailable;" in composer_method
assert "this->TryAcquireFramebufferLocked(layer, it->second)" in composer_method
compose_real = composer_source.split("u32 HardwareComposer::ComposeLocked(", 1)[1]
assert compose_real.index("if (result == CacheStatus::NoBufferAvailable)") < compose_real.index("const auto& igbp_buffer = *item.graphic_buffer;")
composer_fixture = r"""
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <map>
using ConsumerId = std::int32_t;
struct Layer {};
class HardwareComposer {
public:
    enum class CacheStatus : std::uint32_t {
        NoBufferAvailable, BufferAcquired, CachedBufferReused
    };
    struct Framebuffer {
        int item{-1};
        bool is_acquired{};
    };
    std::map<ConsumerId, Framebuffer> m_framebuffers;
    bool next_available{};
    int next_item{10};
    unsigned attempts{};
    bool TryAcquireFramebufferLocked(Layer&, Framebuffer& framebuffer) {
        ++attempts;
        if (!next_available) return false;
        framebuffer.is_acquired = true;
        framebuffer.item = next_item++;
        next_available = false;
        return true;
    }
    CacheStatus CacheFramebufferLocked(Layer&, ConsumerId);
};
""" + composer_method + r"""
int main() {
    HardwareComposer h;
    Layer layer;
    using Status = HardwareComposer::CacheStatus;
    // First acquire failure must not invent a cached frame.
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::NoBufferAvailable);
    assert(h.m_framebuffers.empty());
    h.next_available = true;
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::BufferAcquired);
    assert(h.m_framebuffers[7].item == 10 && h.m_framebuffers[7].is_acquired);
    unsigned acquired_calls = h.attempts;
    // Reusing an acquired image is valid until its release.
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::CachedBufferReused);
    assert(h.attempts == acquired_calls);
    // Releasing to the producer revokes permission to sample stale memory.
    h.m_framebuffers[7].is_acquired = false;
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::NoBufferAvailable);
    assert(h.m_framebuffers[7].item == 10 && !h.m_framebuffers[7].is_acquired);
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::NoBufferAvailable);
    // A fresh, valid producer buffer restores the regular presentation path.
    h.next_available = true;
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 7) == Status::BufferAcquired);
    assert(h.m_framebuffers[7].item == 11 && h.m_framebuffers[7].is_acquired);
    // Separate layer never inherits an old cached acquisition.
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 8) == Status::NoBufferAvailable);
    h.next_available = true;
    assert(h.CacheFramebufferLocked(layer, 8) == Status::BufferAcquired);
    assert(h.m_framebuffers[8].item == 12 && h.m_framebuffers[7].item == 11);
    std::puts("HARDWARE_COMPOSER_RELEASED_FRAME_HOST_PASS");
}
"""
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-composer-released-frame-") as tmp:
    stage = Path(tmp)
    unit = stage / "hardware_composer.cpp"
    unit.write_text(composer_fixture)
    for opt in ("-O0", "-O2"):
        exe = stage / ("hardware_composer" + opt)
        subprocess.run(["c++", "-std=c++20", opt, "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                        "-fsanitize=undefined", "-fno-sanitize-recover=all",
                        str(unit), "-o", str(exe)], check=True, timeout=45)
        subprocess.run([str(exe)], check=True, timeout=15)
        print("COMPOSER_RELEASED_FRAME_NATIVE_HOST_PASS", opt)
```

```py
"""Execute real ConvertImage layout code; decoder stubs enforce full-volume writes."""
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
def method(path):
    text = path.read_text()
    start = text.index('void ConvertImage(')
    return text[start:text.index('\nboost::container::small_vector<BufferImageCopy, 16> FullDownloadCopies', start)]

#include <algorithm>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <memory>
#include <span>
#include <vector>
#include "common/scratch_buffer.h"
using u8=std::uint8_t; using u32=std::uint32_t; using s32=std::int32_t;
#define ASSERT(x) assert(x)
enum class PixelFormat { ASTC, BC7, A8B8G8R8_UNORM };
struct Extent2D { u32 width,height; };
struct Extent3D { u32 width,height,depth; bool operator==(const Extent3D&) const=default; };
struct Offset3D { s32 x{},y{},z{}; bool operator==(const Offset3D&) const=default; };
struct Subresource { u32 base_level{},base_layer{},num_layers{}; };
struct ImageInfo { Extent3D size; PixelFormat format; };
struct BufferImageCopy {
    std::size_t buffer_offset{},buffer_size{};
    u32 buffer_row_length{},buffer_image_height{};
    Subresource image_subresource; Offset3D image_offset; Extent3D image_extent;
};
namespace Common {
template<class A,class B> auto AlignUp(A n,B a) { return (n+a-1)/a*a; }
u32 DivideUp(u32 n,u32 d) { return (n+d-1)/d; }
}
namespace Settings {
enum class AstcRecompression { Uncompressed,Bc1,Bc3 };
unsigned reads;
struct Setting {
    AstcRecompression mode;
    AstcRecompression GetValue() const { ++reads; return mode; }
};
struct Values { Setting astc_recompression; } values;
}
Extent2D DefaultBlockSize(PixelFormat) { return {4,4}; }
Extent3D AdjustMipSize(Extent3D s,s32 l) { return {std::max(1u,s.width>>l),std::max(1u,s.height>>l),std::max(1u,s.depth>>l)}; }
bool IsPixelFormatASTC(PixelFormat f) { return f==PixelFormat::ASTC; }
u32 BytesPerBlock(PixelFormat) { return 4; }
u32 ConvertedBytesPerBlock(PixelFormat) { return 4; }
void Decode(std::span<const u8> input,u32 w,u32 h,u32 layers,std::span<u8> output) {
    const auto bytes=std::size_t(w)*h*layers*4;
    assert(!input.empty() && output.size()>=bytes);
    std::fill_n(output.begin(),bytes,input.front());
}
namespace Tegra::Texture::ASTC {
void Decompress(std::span<const u8> input,u32 w,u32 h,u32 layers,u32,u32,std::span<u8> output) { Decode(input,w,h,layers,output); }
}
namespace Tegra::Texture::BCN {
void Compress(std::span<const u8> input,u32 w,u32 h,u32 layers,std::span<u8> output,u32 divisor) {
    const auto bytes=std::size_t(Common::AlignUp(w,4))*Common::AlignUp(h,4)*layers/divisor;
    assert(!input.empty() && output.size()>=bytes);
    std::fill_n(output.begin(),bytes,input.front());
}
void CompressBC1(std::span<const u8> in,u32 w,u32 h,u32 n,std::span<u8> out) { Compress(in,w,h,n,out,2); }
void CompressBC3(std::span<const u8> in,u32 w,u32 h,u32 n,std::span<u8> out) { Compress(in,w,h,n,out,1); }
}
void DecompressBCn(std::span<const u8> in,std::span<u8> out,BufferImageCopy& c,PixelFormat) {
    Decode(in,c.image_extent.width,c.image_extent.height,c.image_extent.depth*c.image_subresource.num_layers,out);
}
namespace Before { BEFORE }
namespace After { AFTER }
using Converter=void(*)(std::span<const u8>,const ImageInfo&,std::span<u8>,std::span<BufferImageCopy>);
bool Run(Converter convert,const ImageInfo& info,u32 layers,Settings::AstcRecompression mode,unsigned& reads) {
    Settings::values.astc_recompression.mode=mode;
    std::vector<u8> input,expected;
    std::vector<BufferImageCopy> copies;
    std::vector<std::size_t> expected_offsets;
    for(u32 level=0;level<3;++level) {
        auto size=AdjustMipSize(info.size,level);
        const auto input_bytes=std::size_t(Common::DivideUp(size.width,4))*Common::DivideUp(size.height,4)*16*size.depth*layers;
        copies.push_back({input.size(),input_bytes,Common::AlignUp(size.width,4),Common::AlignUp(size.height,4),{level,0,layers},{},size});
        input.insert(input.end(),input_bytes,static_cast<u8>(0x40+level));
        expected_offsets.push_back(expected.size());
        const bool compressed=info.format==PixelFormat::ASTC && mode!=Settings::AstcRecompression::Uncompressed;
        const auto bytes=compressed ? std::size_t(Common::AlignUp(size.width,4))*Common::AlignUp(size.height,4)*size.depth*layers/(mode==Settings::AstcRecompression::Bc1?2:1)
                                    : std::size_t(size.width)*size.height*size.depth*layers*4;
        expected.insert(expected.end(),bytes,static_cast<u8>(0x40+level));
    }
    std::vector<u8> output(expected.size()+32,0xcc);
    Settings::reads=0;
    convert(input,info,std::span<u8>(output).first(expected.size()),copies);
    reads=Settings::reads;
    bool good=std::equal(expected.begin(),expected.end(),output.begin());
    for(std::size_t i=0;i<copies.size();++i) good&=copies[i].buffer_offset==expected_offsets[i];
    assert(std::all_of(output.end()-32,output.end(),[](u8 b){return b==0xcc;}));
    return good;
}
int main() {
    using R=Settings::AstcRecompression;
    unsigned old_reads{},new_reads{};
    for(auto format:{PixelFormat::ASTC,PixelFormat::BC7}) {
        ImageInfo volume{{16,16,4},format};
        assert(!Run(Before::ConvertImage,volume,1,R::Uncompressed,old_reads));
        assert(Run(After::ConvertImage,volume,1,R::Uncompressed,new_reads));
        assert(old_reads==3 && new_reads==1);
        ImageInfo array{{16,16,1},format};
        assert(Run(Before::ConvertImage,array,3,R::Uncompressed,old_reads));
        assert(Run(After::ConvertImage,array,3,R::Uncompressed,new_reads));
        assert(old_reads==3 && new_reads==1);
    }
    for(auto mode:{R::Bc1,R::Bc3})
        for(u32 depth:{1u,4u})
            assert(Run(After::ConvertImage,{{16,16,depth},PixelFormat::ASTC},2,mode,new_reads));
    Settings::reads=0;
    After::ConvertImage({},{{16,16,1},PixelFormat::ASTC},{},{});
    assert(Settings::reads==0);
    std::puts("TEXTURE_VOLUME_LAYOUT_PASS old_3D_overlap_reproduced=2 current_mip_ranges_disjoint=1 arrays=preserved BC1_BC3=preserved settings_reads=3->1 empty_reads=0");
}
'''.replace('BEFORE',previous).replace('AFTER',current)
```

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
# Reports the host tools the build uses (make toolchain). See docs/BUILDING.md.
set -uo pipefail
root=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd -P)
source "$root/tools/host-env.sh"
eden_host_env "$root"
missing=0
need() {
    local label=$1; shift
    for command in "$@"; do
        if command -v "$command" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            printf '  %-28s %s\n' "$label" "$(command -v "$command")"
            return
        fi
    done
    printf '  %-28s MISSING (%s)\n' "$label" "$*"
    missing=$((missing + 1))
}
echo "Compilers and LLVM 18:"
for tool in clang-18 clang++-18 ld.lld-18 llvm-ar-18 llvm-ranlib-18 llvm-nm-18 llvm-readobj-18 llvm-strip-18; do need "$tool" "$tool"; done
echo "Build tools:"
for tool in cmake ninja ccache make nasm meson rsync git flock ar pkg-config autoconf; do need "$tool" "$tool"; done
for tool in realpath install xargs sort head; do need "$tool" "$tool"; done
need glslangValidator glslangValidator
need spirv-val spirv-val
need "bison / flex" bison
need flex flex
echo "Downloads and archives:"
for tool in curl wget unzip tar sha256sum; do need "$tool" "$tool"; done
echo "Python:"
if python3 -c 'import sys; sys.exit(sys.version_info < (3, 12))' 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '  %-28s %s\n' "python3 >= 3.12" "$(python3 --version)"
else
    printf '  %-28s MISSING\n' "python3 >= 3.12"; missing=$((missing + 1))
fi
for module in venv mako yaml packaging; do
    if python3 -c "import $module" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '  %-28s ok\n' "python3 module $module"
    else
        printf '  %-28s MISSING\n' "python3 module $module"; missing=$((missing + 1))
    fi
done
if (( missing )); then
    echo "$missing tool(s) missing (Ubuntu 24.04: see docs/BUILDING.md)."
    exit 1
fi
echo "All host tools found."
```

`tools/check-tsc-fallback.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compile the actual generated frequency-selection block against CPUID cases."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import tempfile

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
cache = Path((root / '.local/headless-cache').read_text().strip())
original = (cache / 'source/src/common/cpu_features.cpp').read_text()
derived = (root / 'vendor/encore-active/eden-core/src' / 'common/cpu_features.cpp').read_text()
expected = original.replace('        } else {\n            caps.tsc_frequency = X64::EstimateRDTSCFrequency();\n        }', '        }').replace(
    '    if (max_std_fn >= 0x16) {',
    "    if (caps.invariant_tsc && caps.tsc_frequency < 1'000'000'000ULL) {\n        caps.tsc_frequency = X64::EstimateRDTSCFrequency();\n    }\n\n    if (max_std_fn >= 0x16) {")
# N76 extends the shared CPU clock with a metadata-selected guest rate.
# Reconstruct the original native TSC owner by removing ONLY this exact
# guarded include and one guarded CNTPCT block. NS1 selector parity remains
# byte-for-byte, and unqualified changes still fail the audit.
ns2_header = '#ifdef EDEN_NS2_GUEST_COUNTER\n#include "encore/guest_counter_policy.h"\n#endif\n'
ns2_block = '''#ifdef EDEN_NS2_GUEST_COUNTER
    // Shared guest-clock policy: Nintendo's second-generation SDK converts
    // CNT ticks using 31.25 MHz. Keep the original fast path for Switch 1.
    if (Eden::GuestCounter::Rate() != Eden::GuestCounter::Switch1Hz) {
        if (!invariant)
            return static_cast<s64>(Eden::GuestCounter::NanosecondsToGuest(
                static_cast<u64>(GetUptime())));
        const u64 factor = Eden::GuestCounter::NativeFactor();
        if (factor != 0)
            return MultiplyHigh(GetUptime(), factor);
        // A missing host clock calibration must not divide by zero or
        // silently keep the wrong 19.2 MHz guest rate.
        if (rdtsc_frequency == 0)
            return 0;
        return MultiplyHigh(GetUptime(),
                            GetFixedPoint64Factor(Eden::GuestCounter::Rate(),
                                                  rdtsc_frequency));
    }
#endif
'''
assert derived.count(ns2_header) == 1, "N76 header changed"
assert derived.count(ns2_block) == 1, "N76 rate body changed"
ns1_derived = derived.replace(ns2_header, "", 1).replace(ns2_block, "", 1)
assert ns1_derived == expected and ns1_derived.count('X64::EstimateRDTSCFrequency()') == 1
selection = derived[derived.index('    if (max_std_fn >= 0x15) {'):derived.index('    if (max_std_fn >= 0x16) {')]
code = '''
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdint>
using u64 = uint64_t;
static unsigned estimates;
static u64 estimated;
namespace X64 { u64 EstimateRDTSCFrequency() { ++estimates; return estimated; } }
void __cpuid(int*, int) {} // cpu_id already holds the requested fixture.
u64 select(unsigned max_std_fn, bool invariant, int denominator, int numerator, int crystal) {
    int cpu_id[]{denominator, numerator, crystal, 0};
    struct { bool invariant_tsc; u64 tsc_frequency = 0, tsc_crystal_ratio_denominator = 0,
        tsc_crystal_ratio_numerator = 0, crystal_frequency = 0; } caps{invariant};
''' + selection + '''
    return caps.tsc_frequency;
}
int main() {
    estimated = 2'200'000'000;
    assert(select(0x10, true, 0, 0, 0) == estimated && estimates == 1);
    assert(select(0x15, true, 2, 4, 0) == estimated && estimates == 2);
    assert(select(0x15, true, 0, 0, 0) == estimated && estimates == 3);
    assert(select(0x15, true, 1, 100, 24'000'000) == 2'400'000'000 && estimates == 3);
    assert(select(0x10, false, 0, 0, 0) == 0 && estimates == 3);
    estimated = 0;
    assert(select(0x10, true, 0, 0, 0) == 0 && estimates == 4);
    estimated = 500'000'000;
    assert(select(0x10, true, 0, 0, 0) < 1'000'000'000 && estimates == 5);
}
'''
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='eden-tsc-') as directory:
    path = Path(directory)
    (path / 'check.cpp').write_text(code)
```

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Source and host contracts for the paired upstream guest scheduler locks.

The source tree is based on a pinned upstream archive: replacing only
k_thread.h, k_slab_heap.h, and k_scheduler.cpp is intentional. The paired slab override stays version-pinned (including its mutex-contained relaxed atomics); Encore uses a cross-host-worker
binary semaphore for the guest context handoff, replacing owner-bound mutex.
This is not a runtime FPS or title-deadlock qualification.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

    "k_scheduler.cpp": "git:6bf49c0165ecac602628679adbb8cee8d8407190",

              if expected_sha.startswith("git:") else hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest())
    assert digest == expected_sha.removeprefix("git:"), f"Requalify changed {name}"
    sources[name] = data.decode("utf-8")

assert "python3 -B tools/verify/hle/check-hle-cmake-select-host.py" in workflow

# Cross-host-worker release is legal for std::binary_semaphore, not std::mutex.
# Compile the actual maintained member type and release sites in a finite
# two-worker interleaving. No emulator or console is run.
fixture = r"""
#include <cassert>
#include <cstdio>
#include <semaphore>
#include <thread>
struct KThread {
    std::binary_semaphore m_context_guard{1};
};
static void retry_failed_switch(KThread* highest_priority_thread) {
    highest_priority_thread->m_context_guard.release();
}
static void unload_thread(KThread* thread) {
    thread->m_context_guard.release();
}
int main() {
    for (int trial=0; trial<256; ++trial) {
        KThread guest;
        std::binary_semaphore ready{0};
        std::thread worker_acquire([&] {
            assert(guest.m_context_guard.try_acquire());
            assert(!guest.m_context_guard.try_acquire());
            ready.release();
        });
        std::thread worker_release([&] {
            ready.acquire();
            unload_thread(&guest);
        });
        worker_acquire.join();
        worker_release.join();
        assert(guest.m_context_guard.try_acquire());
        retry_failed_switch(&guest);
        assert(guest.m_context_guard.try_acquire());
        guest.m_context_guard.release();
    }
    std::puts("PASS cross-worker context semaphore acquire/release/retry");
}
"""
assert "std::binary_semaphore m_context_guard{1};" in fixture
for literal in ("highest_priority_thread->m_context_guard.release();",
                "thread->m_context_guard.release();"):
    assert literal in scheduler and literal in fixture
compiler = next((x for x in ("clang++-18", "clang++", "g++") if shutil.which(x)), None)
assert compiler, "C++20 host compiler required"
env = os.environ.copy()
if sys.platform == "darwin" and not env.get("SDKROOT"):
    sdk = Path("/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX15.4.sdk")
    if sdk.is_dir():
        env["SDKROOT"] = str(sdk)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="encore-scheduler-handoff-") as folder:
    cpp = Path(folder) / "handoff.cpp"
    exe = Path(folder) / "handoff"
    cpp.write_text(fixture)
    subprocess.run([compiler, "-std=c++20", "-Wall", "-Wextra", "-Werror",
                    "-pthread", str(cpp), "-o", str(exe)], check=True, env=env, timeout=60)
    subprocess.run([str(exe)], check=True, env=env, timeout=15)

print("PASS maintained guest-context semaphore + requalified slab mutex atomics + CMake selection")
print("HOST ONLY: native build and guest gameplay still require qualification")
```

```py
#include <boost/container/small_vector.hpp>
#include <boost/version.hpp>
#include <cassert>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <type_traits>
#include <vector>
using u32 = std::uint32_t;
template<typename T, std::size_t N>
#if BOOST_VERSION >= 108100 || __GNUC__ > 12
boost::container::small_vector<T,N> FixSmallVectorADL(
    const boost::container::small_vector<T,N>& v) { return v; }
#else
std::vector<T> FixSmallVectorADL(
    const boost::container::small_vector<T,N>& v) { return {v.begin(),v.end()}; }
#endif
constexpr u32 DivideUp(u32 a,u32 b){return (a+b-1)/b;}
constexpr u32 AlignUp(u32 a,u32 b){return DivideUp(a,b)*b;}
int main(){
    // First error flush is immediate, next flush at 100 ms, oversized log forces a flush.
    long long last_flush=-1000;
    const auto flush_error = [&](long long now, bool oversized) {
        if(oversized || now-last_flush>=100) { last_flush=now; return true; }
        return false;
    };
    assert(flush_error(1000,false));
    assert(!flush_error(1001,false));
    assert(!flush_error(1099,false));
    assert(flush_error(1100,false));
    assert(flush_error(1110,true));
    static_assert(BOOST_VERSION >= 108100, "Modern Boost must select small_vector");
    using V=boost::container::small_vector<int,16>;
    static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(FixSmallVectorADL(V{})),V>);
    for(u32 w: {4u,5u,64u,128u,1024u})
      for(u32 h: {4u,5u,128u,1024u})
        for(u32 tw: {4u,5u,6u,8u})
          for(u32 th: {4u,5u,8u})
            for(u32 layers: {1u,2u,9u,121u}) {
              const u32 layer_input=DivideUp(w,tw)*DivideUp(h,th)*16;
              const u32 layer_pixels=w*h*4;
              const u32 layer_output=AlignUp(w,4)*AlignUp(h,4);
              assert(layer_input>0 && layer_output>0);
              // Distinct per-layer offsets are contiguous without overlap.
              for(u32 layer=0;layer<layers;layer++)
                assert(std::size_t(layer)*layer_output+layer_output <=
                       std::size_t(layers)*layer_output);
              assert(layer_pixels*layers/layers==layer_pixels);
            }
}
"""
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="eden-r428-") as directory:
    src = Path(directory) / "fixture.cpp"
    binary = Path(directory) / "fixture"
    src.write_text(cpp)
    subprocess.run([cxx, "-std=c++20", "-O2", str(src), "-o", str(binary)],
                   check=True, timeout=90)
    subprocess.run([str(binary)], check=True, timeout=90)
```

```py
"""

import hashlib

    assert manifest["name"]==item["name"]
    if "sha256" in item:
        assert manifest["sha256"]==item["sha256"],item["name"]

end=SOURCE.index("\nfor item in ITEMS:",start)
def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

    vault=Path(tmp)
    env={"V":vault,"hashlib":hashlib,"json":json,"digest":digest}
    exec(SOURCE[start:end],env)
    check=env["assert_blob"]
    folder=vault/"objects"/"fixture"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True)
    def configure(payload):
        (folder/"chunk").write_bytes(payload)
        (folder/"chunks.json").write_text(json.dumps({
            "name":"fixture","size":len(payload),
            "sha256":hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest(),
            "chunks":[{"file":"chunk","size":len(payload),
                       "sha256":hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()}]}))
    original=b"sha-locked archive"
    expected256=hashlib.sha256(original).hexdigest()
    expected512=hashlib.sha512(original).hexdigest()
    configure(original)
    check("fixture",expected256,expected512)
    for sha256,sha512 in [("0"*64,expected512),(expected256,"0"*128)]:
        try:
            check("fixture",sha256,sha512)
        except AssertionError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("incorrect independent pin accepted")
    configure(b"self-consistent but unpinned archive")
    try:
        check("fixture",expected256,expected512)
    except AssertionError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("forged vault-local manifest accepted")
    configure(original)
    (folder/"chunk").write_bytes(b"corrupt")
    try:
        check("fixture",expected256,expected512)
    except AssertionError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("corrupted chunk accepted")
print("ENCORE_VENDOR_ARCHIVE_PIN_PASS archives=6 SHA256=5 SHA512=1 forged_vault=rejected")
```

```py
# Regression oracle: the maintained diagnostic IFile TU must be exactly the

        backend->Read(reinterpret_cast<size_t*>(out_size.Get()), offset, out_buffer.data(), size));"""
fs_new = """    const auto fs_start = ::Eden::Performance::detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) ? ::Eden::Performance::NowNs() : 0;
    const Result fs_result =
        backend->Read(reinterpret_cast<size_t*>(out_size.Get()), offset, out_buffer.data(), size);
    if (fs_start) {
        ::Eden::Performance::AddSince(::Eden::Performance::guest_fs_file, fs_start);
        ::Eden::Performance::guest_fs_file_bytes.fetch_add(static_cast<unsigned long long>(*out_size.Get()), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    // Diagnostic only: avoid formatting every file read while quiet.
        LOG_WARNING(Service_FS, "EDEN_FS_FILE_READ offset={:#x} size={} read={} result={:#x} ns={}", offset, size, *out_size.Get(), fs_result.raw, ::Eden::Performance::NowNs() - fs_start);
    }
    R_RETURN(fs_result);"""

# R435/F05: the prior producer-dequeue oracle is still useful for proving
# byte-for-byte provenance of all old maintained changes, but F05 now adds a
# producer release->guest-event listener. Project ONLY that separately tested
# change away before comparing against the historical expected TU. Fingerprint
# the complete new listener/registry block, so new unchecked code cannot be
# silently absorbed into an arbitrary skipped region.
wake_begin = "// A guest waiting on BufferQueueProducer::GetNativeHandle"
wake_end = "BufferQueueProducer::BufferQueueProducer("
assert dequeue_maintained.count(wake_begin) == 1
assert dequeue_maintained.count(wake_end) == 1
wake_block = dequeue_maintained[
    dequeue_maintained.index(wake_begin):dequeue_maintained.index(wake_end)
]
wake_fingerprint = 14695981039346656037
for wake_byte in wake_block.encode("utf-8"):
    wake_fingerprint = ((wake_fingerprint ^ wake_byte) * 1099511628211) & ((1 << 64) - 1)
assert wake_fingerprint == 0x83686626E6E9D1A7, "F05 producer release wake block changed"
dequeue_legacy_projection = dequeue_maintained.replace(wake_block, "", 1)

# Revert the F05 queue-mutex/kernel-scheduler lock-order repair *before*
# projecting older maintained producer patches onto the pinned Eden source.
# Changes must be present exactly once in their own method; unreviewed
# source drift fails the audit rather than being silently normalized.
def strip_producer_unlocked_signal(method_begin: str, method_end: str,
                                   before: str, after: str) -> None:
    global dequeue_legacy_projection
    start = dequeue_legacy_projection.index(method_begin)
    end = dequeue_legacy_projection.index(method_end, start + len(method_begin))
    part = dequeue_legacy_projection[start:end]
    assert part.count(after) == 1, ("F05 producer lock-order delta drift", method_begin, after[:100])
    part = part.replace(after, before, 1)
    dequeue_legacy_projection = (
        dequeue_legacy_projection[:start] + part + dequeue_legacy_projection[end:]
    )

strip_producer_unlocked_signal("Status BufferQueueProducer::SetBufferCount(", "Status BufferQueueProducer::WaitForFreeSlotThenRelock(",

                               consumer_pinned.index(consumer_end)]
consumer_new = """Status BufferQueueConsumer::Disconnect() {
    LOG_DEBUG(Service_Nvnflinger, "called");

    std::shared_ptr<IProducerListener> producer_listener;
    {
        std::scoped_lock lock{core->mutex};
        if (core->consumer_listener == nullptr) {
            LOG_ERROR(Service_Nvnflinger, "no consumer is connected");
            return Status::BadValue;
        }

        core->is_abandoned = true;
        core->consumer_listener = nullptr;
        core->queue.clear();
        core->FreeAllBuffersLocked();
        core->SignalDequeueCondition();
        // A guest blocked on the producer's Binder native handle cannot
        // observe the host condition variable. Publish the terminal wake
        // through the same release listener used for ordinary buffer frees.
        producer_listener = std::move(core->connected_producer_listener);
    }

    // Release callbacks must never execute under core->mutex: a guest or
    // external listener can reenter the queue and otherwise deadlock.
    if (producer_listener) {
        producer_listener->OnBufferReleased();
    }
    return Status::NoError;
}
"""
# Revert only reviewed F05 additions to the pinned source, not arbitrary
# consumer text. Every replacement is unique and changes fail this audit.
assert consumer_active.count(consumer_new) == 1
consumer_legacy_projection = consumer_active.replace(consumer_new, consumer_old, 1)

# Synchronous IPC: request ID and timing are captured BEFORE the potentially
# blocking call; the exact historical body is maintained, not regenerated.
ipc_rel = "core/hle/kernel/svc/svc_ipc.cpp"
ipc_pinned = (sources / "eden/src" / ipc_rel).read_text()
ipc_maintained = (active / "eden-core/src" / ipc_rel).read_text()
ipc_old = "    R_RETURN(session->SendSyncRequest(kernel, message, buffer_size));"
ipc_new = """    const bool ipc_profile = ::Eden::Performance::detailed_gpu_profile.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const auto ipc_start = ipc_profile ? ::Eden::Performance::NowNs() : 0;
    const auto ipc_tid = ipc_profile ? GetCurrentThread(kernel).GetThreadId() : 0;
    auto* const ipc_slot = ipc_profile ? ::Eden::Performance::BeginGuestIpc(ipc_tid, ipc_start) : nullptr;
    const Result ipc_result = session->SendSyncRequest(kernel, message, buffer_size);
    if (ipc_profile) ::Eden::Performance::FinishGuestIpc(ipc_slot, ipc_tid, ipc_start, ::Eden::Performance::NowNs() - ipc_start);
    R_RETURN(ipc_result);"""
assert ipc_pinned.count(ipc_old) == 1
ipc_timeout_old = """                timeout = kernel.HardwareTimer().GetTick() + offset_tick + 2;
                if (timeout <= 0) {
                    timeout = (std::numeric_limits<s64>::max)();
                }"""
ipc_timeout_fixed = """                s64 absolute{};
                if (__builtin_add_overflow(kernel.HardwareTimer().GetTick(), offset_tick,
                                           &absolute) ||
                    __builtin_add_overflow(absolute, s64{2}, &absolute) ||
                    absolute <= 0) {
                    timeout = (std::numeric_limits<s64>::max)();
                } else {
                    timeout = absolute;
                }"""
assert ipc_pinned.count(ipc_timeout_old) == 1
ipc_index_old = """            s32 index;
            Result result = KSynchronizationObject::Wait(kernel, std::addressof(index), objs, num_objects, timeout);"""
ipc_index_fixed = """            // Wait may return cancellation/termination before setting the index.
            // Never propagate an indeterminate slot on non-timeout failures.
            s32 index{-1};
            Result result = KSynchronizationObject::Wait(kernel, std::addressof(index), objs, num_objects, timeout);"""
assert ipc_pinned.count(ipc_index_old) == 1
ipc_expected = ('#include "performance.h"\n' +
                ipc_pinned.replace(ipc_old, ipc_new).replace(ipc_timeout_old, ipc_timeout_fixed).replace(ipc_index_old, ipc_index_fixed))
assert ipc_maintained == ipc_expected, (
    "Maintained DEV IPC source diverges from pinned + profiler + deadline and slot guards")
ipc_standard = (active / "eden-core/src/core/hle/kernel/svc/svc_ipc_standard.cpp").read_text()
# Final IPC source adds one fail-closed check *only* for impossible success
# indices; DEV remains the pinned profile with its instrumented timestamps.
ipc_success_old = """            if (R_SUCCEEDED(result)) {
                KServerSession* session = objs[index]->DynamicCast<KServerSession*>();"""
ipc_success_safe = """            if (R_SUCCEEDED(result)) {
                // Even a successful wake must identify an actual queued object.
                // Fail closed rather than indexing before/after the wait buffer
                // if an unexpected native wakeup publishes an invalid slot.
                if (index < 0 || index >= num_objects || objs[index] == nullptr) {
                    *out_index = -1;
                    R_THROW(ResultOutOfRange);
                }
                KServerSession* session = objs[index]->DynamicCast<KServerSession*>();"""
assert ipc_pinned.count(ipc_success_old) == 1
ipc_standard_expected = (ipc_pinned.replace(ipc_timeout_old, ipc_timeout_fixed)
                         .replace(ipc_index_old, ipc_index_fixed)
                         .replace(ipc_success_old, ipc_success_safe))
assert ipc_standard == ipc_standard_expected, (
    "Maintained normal IPC source diverges from pinned + deadline, initialized index, guarded successful slot")

# Native CPU feature detection: move the CPUID 0x15 fallback out of its
# leaf-specific block without changing the existing host frequency heuristic.
cpu_rel = "common/cpu_features.cpp"
cpu_pinned = (sources / "eden/src" / cpu_rel).read_text()
cpu_active = (active / "eden-core/src" / cpu_rel).read_text()
cpu_fallback = """        } else {
            caps.tsc_frequency = X64::EstimateRDTSCFrequency();
        }"""
cpu_leaf16 = "    if (max_std_fn >= 0x16) {"
cpu_leaf16_new = """    if (caps.invariant_tsc && caps.tsc_frequency < 1'000'000'000ULL) {
        caps.tsc_frequency = X64::EstimateRDTSCFrequency();
    }

    if (max_std_fn >= 0x16) {"""
assert cpu_pinned.count(cpu_fallback) == cpu_pinned.count(cpu_leaf16) == 1
cpu_expected = cpu_pinned.replace(cpu_fallback, "        }").replace(cpu_leaf16, cpu_leaf16_new)
# N76/N77 adds only the audited, opt-in guest-rate block to the shared owner.
# Reverse its exact bytes for the original TSC parity check; reject drift.
ns2_cpu_header = "#ifdef EDEN_NS2_GUEST_COUNTER\n#include \"encore/guest_counter_policy.h\"\n#endif\n"
ns2_cpu_block = "#ifdef EDEN_NS2_GUEST_COUNTER\n    // Shared guest-clock policy: Nintendo's second-generation SDK converts\n    // CNT ticks using 31.25 MHz. Keep the original fast path for Switch 1.\n    if (Eden::GuestCounter::Rate() != Eden::GuestCounter::Switch1Hz) {\n        if (!invariant)\n            return static_cast<s64>(Eden::GuestCounter::NanosecondsToGuest(\n                static_cast<u64>(GetUptime())));\n        const u64 factor = Eden::GuestCounter::NativeFactor();\n        if (factor != 0)\n            return MultiplyHigh(GetUptime(), factor);\n        // A missing host clock calibration must not divide by zero or\n        // silently keep the wrong 19.2 MHz guest rate.\n        if (rdtsc_frequency == 0)\n            return 0;\n        return MultiplyHigh(GetUptime(),\n                            GetFixedPoint64Factor(Eden::GuestCounter::Rate(),\n                                                  rdtsc_frequency));\n    }\n#endif\n"
if "#ifdef EDEN_NS2_GUEST_COUNTER" in cpu_active:
    assert cpu_active.count(ns2_cpu_header) == 1, "N76 header modified or duplicated"
    assert cpu_active.count(ns2_cpu_block) == 1, "N76 timing block modified or duplicated"
    cpu_active = cpu_active.replace(ns2_cpu_header, "").replace(ns2_cpu_block, "")
assert cpu_active == cpu_expected, "TSC source differs from previous configure-time transformation"
assert c.count('list(APPEND common_sources "${EDEN_MAINTAINED_NATIVE_CPU_FEATURES}")') == 1
assert 'list(REMOVE_ITEM common_sources cpu_features.cpp)' in c
assert 'if(NOT EXISTS "${EDEN_MAINTAINED_NATIVE_CPU_FEATURES}")' in c
assert 'write_derived("${PORT_BUILD_DIR}/cpu_features.cpp"' not in c
assert 'file(READ "${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/common/cpu_features.cpp" features_source)' not in c

    ("    session.is_active = true;",
     "    process->Open(impl->host1x.System().Kernel()); // Paired with the final CloseSession after SMMU unregistration.\n    session.is_active = true;"),
    ("void Container::CloseSession(SessionId session_id) {\n    std::scoped_lock lk(impl->session_guard);",
     "void Container::CloseSession(SessionId session_id) {\n    std::unique_lock lk(impl->session_guard);"),
    ("    impl->id_pool.emplace_front(session_id.id);",
```
