`tools/ps-glyph-switch1-titledb.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Offline, conservative Nintendo Switch 1 base-title metadata resolver.

Read a locally supplied JSON export from community Switch TitleDB or a
SwitchBrew-derived list. Match existing Eden Switch-1 research names to
candidate base game Title IDs, without inventing IDs from approximate names.
Never download games, parse encrypted content, or autoactivate glyph artwork.

Supported input variants:
  * list of {title_id/id/titleId, name/title/description}
  * dict mapping 16-digit Title ID -> name or object with name
  * dict mapping NSUID -> object with id/titleId and name (regional TitleDB)

Only 0100...000 Switch 1 base-application-shaped IDs are considered.
Duplicate names resolving to distinct Title IDs remain ambiguous (null).
This is database matching only: title and update/ROMFS/correct edition still
require checking the user's own actual installed game before glyph admission.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SWITCH = ROOT / "docs/PS_GLYPH_SOURCE_INDEX.json"
SEEDS = ROOT / "docs/PS_GLYPH_SWITCH1_GAME_SEEDS.json"
MAX_DB_BYTES = 96 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_RECORDS = 250000
TITLE_ID = re.compile(r"0100[0-9A-Fa-f]{9}000\Z")
NONWORD = re.compile(r"[^\w]+", re.UNICODE)


def clean_name(name: object) -> str | None:
    if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip() or len(name) > 320:
        return None
    return NONWORD.sub(" ", name.casefold()).strip()


def is_switch1_base(value: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, str) and TITLE_ID.fullmatch(value) is not None


def entries(data: object):
    """Yield only title-name/ID candidates, never fetched game files."""
    if isinstance(data, dict):
        if isinstance(data.get("titles"), (dict, list)):
            data = data["titles"]
        else:
            data = list(data.items())
    if not isinstance(data, list) or len(data) > MAX_RECORDS:
        raise ValueError("unsupported or oversized title database")
    for record in data:
        if isinstance(record, (tuple, list)) and len(record) == 2:
            key, value = record
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                identifier = value.get("id") or value.get("titleId") or value.get("title_id") or key
                title = value.get("name") or value.get("title") or value.get("description")
            else:
                identifier = key
                title = value
        elif isinstance(record, dict):
            identifier = record.get("title_id") or record.get("titleId") or \
                         record.get("id") or record.get("tid")
            title = record.get("name") or record.get("title") or record.get("description")
        else:
            continue
        if not is_switch1_base(identifier):
            continue
        normalized = clean_name(title)
        if normalized:
            yield normalized, identifier.upper(), str(title).strip()


def read_json(file: Path, bound: int) -> tuple[object, str]:
    if not file.is_file() or file.is_symlink() or not 1 <= file.stat().st_size <= bound:
        raise ValueError("database missing, symlink or out of size bounds")
    with file.open("rb") as handle:
        raw = handle.read(bound + 1)
    if len(raw) > bound:
        raise ValueError("JSON input exceeded bound")
    return json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8")), hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def resolve(source_db: object, db_sha256: str, switch: dict,
            seeds: dict, all_base_games: bool = False) -> dict:
    known = defaultdict(set)
    display = {}
    for label, tid, exact in entries(source_db):
        known[label].add(tid)
        display.setdefault((label, tid), exact)
    title_names = {obj["title"] for obj in switch["mods"]} | {
        obj["switch_game"] for obj in seeds["games"]}
    resolved = []
    for title in sorted(title_names):
        norm = clean_name(title)
        ids = sorted(known.get(norm, ()))
        resolved.append({
            "requested_switch_game": title,
            "status": "unique_name_candidate" if len(ids) == 1 else
                      "ambiguous_multiple_title_ids" if ids else "not_found_exactly",
            "candidate_title_id": ids[0] if len(ids) == 1 else None,
            "ambiguous_ids": ids if len(ids) > 1 else [],
            "game_update_verified": False,
            "original_romfs_verified": False,
            "actual_installed_game_match_verified": False,
            "glyph_art_compatible": False,
        })
    output = {
        "schema": 1,
        "source": "external_switch1_title_metadata_read_only",
        "external_json_sha256": db_sha256,
        "research_title_count": len(resolved),
        "unique_name_candidates": sum(item["candidate_title_id"] is not None
                                      for item in resolved),
        "ambiguous_names": sum(bool(item["ambiguous_ids"]) for item in resolved),
        "researched_titles": resolved,
        "warning": "A Title ID inferred from a name in external metadata is only a candidate, never a validated user game version or glyph compatibility.",
    }
    if all_base_games:
        # Same Title ID can appear in several regional/language records.
        # Do not duplicate its backlog row or imply different regional IDs.
        title_by_id = {}
        for label, ids in sorted(known.items()):
            for tid in sorted(ids):
                title_by_id.setdefault(tid, display[(label, tid)])
        pairs = sorted(title_by_id.items())
        output["all_switch1_base_title_candidates"] = [
            {"title_id": tid, "title": name, "glyph_art_compatible": False,
             "update_and_installed_romfs_unverified": True}
            for tid, name in pairs]
    return output


def main() -> int:
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    cli.add_argument("--title-db", type=Path, required=True, help="local JSON metadata export")
    cli.add_argument("--all-base-games", action="store_true",
                     help="include full deduplicated Switch 1 base-title candidate backlog")
    cli.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="NEW JSON report path")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    try:
        if args.out and (args.out.exists() or args.out.is_symlink() or
                         not args.out.parent.is_dir() or args.out.parent.is_symlink()):
            raise ValueError("invalid/occupied output report path")
        db, sha = read_json(args.title_db, MAX_DB_BYTES)
        switch, _ = read_json(SWITCH, 512 * 1024)
        seeds, _ = read_json(SEEDS, 512 * 1024)
        report = resolve(db, sha, switch, seeds, args.all_base_games)
        rendered = json.dumps(report, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2) + "\n"
        if args.out:
            args.out.write_text(rendered, encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"SWITCH 1 TITLEDB {args.out}: {report['unique_name_candidates']} research name candidates, none autoenabled")
        else:
            print(rendered, end="")
        return 0
    except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeError) as error:
        print(f"REJECTED Switch1 TitleDB metadata: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`tools/ps-glyph-unity-inventory.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only Unity Texture2D/Sprite name, dimensions and serialized rect inventory.

Requires an explicitly supplied, local authorized Unity assets file and
optional dependency UnityPy (install separately if needed).
Nothing is extracted, patched, repacked or redistributed. Serialized Sprite
m_Rect / m_RD.textureRect may expose real engine-side UI texture coordinates,
but their origin, sprite packing/rotation, name semantics, atlas asset identity,
game build and correct Switch prompt mapping need independent verification.

Supports newer UnityPy parse_as_object()/peek_name(), and older read() where
available. This is an offline *candidate* discovery stage, NOT an emulator hook.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MAX_INPUT_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_OBJECTS = 50000
MAX_REPORTED = 12000
MAX_NAME = 256
HINTS = ("button", "buttons", "btn", "gamepad", "controller", "prompt", "key",
         "glyph", "dpad", "xbox", "playstation", "dualshock", "dualsense",
         "ps4", "ps5", "switch", "joycon", "hud", "input", "touchpad", "sprite")


def safe_string(value: object) -> str | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return None
    result = "".join(c for c in value if c.isprintable()).strip()
    return result[:MAX_NAME] if result else None


def field(obj: object, key: str):
    return obj.get(key) if isinstance(obj, dict) else getattr(obj, key, None)


def sprite_rect(obj: object) -> list[float] | None:
    """Read original serialized Unity Rectf, without converting coordinate origin."""
    if obj is None:
        return None
    values = [field(obj, key) for key in ("x", "y", "width", "height")]
    if any(type(v) not in (int, float) or not math.isfinite(v) for v in values):
        return None
    x, y, width, height = values
    if x < -1000000 or y < -1000000 or width <= 0 or height <= 0 or \
            max(width, height) > 32768:
        return None
    return [float(x), float(y), float(width), float(height)]


def get_name(obj: object) -> str | None:
    if callable(getattr(obj, "peek_name", None)):
        try:
            return safe_string(obj.peek_name())
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError, AttributeError, TypeError):
            pass
    return None


def parse_object(obj: object):
    if callable(getattr(obj, "parse_as_object", None)):
        return obj.parse_as_object()
    if callable(getattr(obj, "read", None)):
        return obj.read()
    raise ValueError("unrecognized UnityPy ObjectReader API")


def digest(file: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with file.open("rb") as stream:
        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(block)
    return h.hexdigest()


def inspect(asset: Path, source_platform: str = "unverified") -> dict:
    if (not asset.is_file() or asset.is_symlink() or
            not 1 <= asset.stat().st_size <= MAX_INPUT_BYTES):
        raise ValueError("Unity assets file missing, linked or oversized")
    if not isinstance(source_platform, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_ +./-]{1,80}", source_platform):
        raise ValueError("invalid source platform label")
    try:
        import UnityPy
    except ImportError as error:
        raise ValueError("UnityPy not installed; inspect its setup/license before installing separately") from error
    try:
        env = UnityPy.load(str(asset))
    except Exception as error:
        raise ValueError("UnityPy could not open the selected asset file") from error
    records = []
    count = 0
    truncated = False
    for obj in env.objects:
        count += 1
        if count > MAX_OBJECTS:
            raise ValueError("too many Unity serialized objects")
        try:
            kind = obj.type.name
        except (AttributeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if kind not in ("Texture2D", "Sprite"):
            continue
        name = get_name(obj)
        if name is None:
            try:
                data = parse_object(obj)
                name = safe_string(field(data, "m_Name") or field(data, "name"))
            except (ValueError, RuntimeError, TypeError, AttributeError):
                continue
        if not name:
            continue
        if len(records) >= MAX_REPORTED:
            truncated = True
            break
        likely = any(hint in name.casefold() for hint in HINTS)
        record = {
            "object_type": kind,
            "name": name,
            "path_id": getattr(obj, "path_id", None),
            "possible_ui_glyph": likely,
            "texture_dimensions": None,
            "serialized_sprite_rect": None,
            "serialized_texture_rect": None,
            "texture_pixel_data_sha256": None,
            "sprite_button_identity_verified": False,
        }
        # Reading only likely UI assets avoids parsing thousands of huge
        # unrelated objects; asset pixel decoding is never requested.
        if likely:
            try:
                data = parse_object(obj)
                if kind == "Texture2D":
                    width = field(data, "m_Width")
                    height = field(data, "m_Height")
                    if type(width) is int and type(height) is int and \
                            0 < width <= 16384 and 0 < height <= 16384:
                        record["texture_dimensions"] = [width, height]
                else:
                    record["serialized_sprite_rect"] = sprite_rect(field(data, "m_Rect"))
                    render_data = field(data, "m_RD")
                    if render_data is not None:
                        record["serialized_texture_rect"] = sprite_rect(
                            field(render_data, "textureRect") or
                            field(render_data, "m_TextureRect"))
            except (ValueError, RuntimeError, TypeError, AttributeError):
                record["parse_status"] = "metadata_unavailable"
        records.append(record)
    return {
        "schema": 1,
        "source": "unity_serialized_asset_metadata",
        "container_filename": asset.name,
        "container_sha256": digest(asset),
        "source_platform_declared": source_platform,
        "object_count_seen": count,
        "reported_texture_or_sprite_objects": len(records),
        "record_limit_reached": truncated,
        "objects": records,
        "warning": "Serialized Unity sprite rects are unverified engine metadata with platform-specific origin/packing. No image bytes decoded, no Switch layout or PS5 compatibility established.",
    }


def main() -> int:
    cli = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    cli.add_argument("--asset-file", type=Path, required=True, help="local Unity resources.assets or asset bundle")
    cli.add_argument("--platform", default="unverified", help="user-declared source platform")
    cli.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="NEW JSON report only")
    args = cli.parse_args()
    try:
        if args.out and (args.out.exists() or args.out.is_symlink() or
                         not args.out.parent.is_dir() or args.out.parent.is_symlink()):
            raise ValueError("invalid or existing report path")
        data = json.dumps(inspect(args.asset_file, args.platform), indent=2) + "\n"
        if args.out:
            args.out.write_text(data, encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"UNITY UI METADATA {args.out}: read-only")
        else:
            print(data, end="")
        return 0
    except (ValueError, OSError, OverflowError) as error:
        print(f"REJECTED Unity inventory: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

`tools/ps-glyph-unity-pair.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read-only join of separate PC and Switch Unity Texture2D/Sprite inventories.

Requires JSON outputs from ps-glyph-unity-inventory.py. Exact object-name matches
are research leads; even same dimensions are NOT pixel equivalence, binding of
a runtime sprite to a texture, or an approved modification. A Sprite's Unity
serialized textureRect can expose actual engine metadata from both platforms.
No game asset decoding, extraction, alteration or copyright redistribution.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

MAX_JSON_BYTES = 6 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_REPORT = 12000


def read(file: Path) -> dict:
    if not file.is_file() or file.is_symlink() or not 1 <= file.stat().st_size <= MAX_JSON_BYTES:
        raise ValueError("invalid Unity inventory report")
    data = json.loads(file.read_text("utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("schema") != 1 or \
            data.get("source") != "unity_serialized_asset_metadata" or \
            not isinstance(data.get("objects"), list) or len(data["objects"]) > MAX_REPORT:
        raise ValueError("not a bounded Unity sprite/texture inventory")
    sha = data.get("container_sha256")
    if not isinstance(sha, str) or len(sha) != 64 or \
            any(x not in "0123456789abcdefABCDEF" for x in sha):
        raise ValueError("missing parent assets SHA-256")
    return data


def group(records: list) -> dict[tuple[str, str], list]:
    result = defaultdict(list)
    for item in records:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ValueError("invalid Unity object record")
        name, kind = item.get("name"), item.get("object_type")
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or len(name) > 256 or \
                kind not in ("Texture2D", "Sprite"):
            raise ValueError("unsafe Unity object identity")
        result[(kind, name.casefold())].append(item)
    return result


def compare(pc: dict, switch: dict) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(pc.get("source_platform_declared"), str) or \
            pc["source_platform_declared"].lower() not in ("pc", "windows", "steam", "game pass"):
        raise ValueError("first report must explicitly declare PC source platform")
    if not isinstance(switch.get("source_platform_declared"), str) or \
            switch["source_platform_declared"].lower() not in ("switch", "nintendo switch"):
        raise ValueError("second report must explicitly declare Switch source platform")
    pc_items, sw_items = group(pc["objects"]), group(switch["objects"])
    overlapping = []
    only_pc_playstation = []
    for key in sorted(set(pc_items) | set(sw_items)):
        pc_values, nx_values = pc_items.get(key, []), sw_items.get(key, [])
        if not pc_values or not nx_values:
            if pc_values and ("ps4" in key[1] or "ps5" in key[1] or
                              "playstation" in key[1] or "dualshock" in key[1] or
                              "dualsense" in key[1]):
                only_pc_playstation.append({"name":pc_values[0]["name"], "asset_type":key[0],
                                           "switch_counterpart_found":False})
            continue
        if len(pc_values) != 1 or len(nx_values) != 1:
            overlapping.append({"object_type":key[0], "name":pc_values[0]["name"],
                                "status":"ambiguous_duplicate_object_names",
                                "binary_verified":False})
            continue
        p, n = pc_values[0], nx_values[0]
        field = ("texture_dimensions" if key[0] == "Texture2D"
                 else "serialized_texture_rect")
        value_a, value_b = p.get(field), n.get(field)
        overlapping.append({
            "object_type":key[0], "name":p["name"],
            "status":"same_object_name_only",
            "pc_asset_path_id":p.get("path_id"), "switch_asset_path_id":n.get("path_id"),
            "pc_geometry":value_a, "switch_geometry":value_b,
            "declared_geometry_equal":bool(value_a is not None and value_a == value_b),
            "pc_sprite_rect":p.get("serialized_sprite_rect"),
            "switch_sprite_rect":n.get("serialized_sprite_rect"),
            "source_or_switch_texture_pixels_compared":False,
            "sprite_semantic_identity_confirmed":False,
        })
    return {
        "schema":1,"source":"cross_platform_Unity_serialized_metadata_join",
        "pc_container_sha256":pc["container_sha256"],
        "switch_container_sha256":switch["container_sha256"],
        "shared_object_name_count":len(overlapping),
        "shared_name_candidates":overlapping,
        "pc_only_playstation_named_assets":only_pc_playstation,
        "actual_switch_ps_texture_pixels_verified":0,
        "ps5_qualified":False,
        "warning":"Unity object and rect metadata only. Real decoded pixel identity, packing, UV origin, original game update, semantic mapping and PS5 runtime remain unverified.",
    }


def main() -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--pc-report", required=True, type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--switch-report", required=True, type=Path)
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="new report, never overwrite")
    args = p.parse_args()
    try:
        if args.out and (args.out.exists() or args.out.is_symlink() or
                         not args.out.parent.is_dir() or args.out.parent.is_symlink()):
            raise ValueError("output already exists or parent unsafe")
        result = json.dumps(compare(read(args.pc_report), read(args.switch_report)),
                            indent=2, ensure_ascii=True) + "\n"
        if args.out:
            args.out.write_text(result, encoding="utf-8")
            print(f"UNITY PLATFORM PAIR {args.out} (metadata only)")
        else:
            print(result, end="")
        return 0
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"REJECTED Unity platform pair: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`tools/ps5.cmake`:

```cmake
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME FreeBSD)
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_VERSION 9)
set(CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR x86_64)
set(CMAKE_TRY_COMPILE_TARGET_TYPE STATIC_LIBRARY)
set(CMAKE_C_COMPILER clang-18)
set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER clang++-18)
```

`tools/radv-active-inputs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bind a reused native graphics archive to *all* maintained compiler inputs.

The Mesa commit SHA alone is insufficient: Encore replaces 12 native Mesa
source units after staging, while the old binary cache checked only the WSI
file. Fingerprint every maintained translation unit, then stamp only after
a successful RADV rebuild with those exact staged bytes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path
import runpy
import shutil
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ACTIVE = ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/ps5-mesa"
INSTALLER = ROOT / "tools/install-vendored-radv.py"
PATHS = tuple(runpy.run_path(str(INSTALLER))["PATHS"])
assert len(PATHS) == len(set(PATHS)) == 12


def fingerprint(base: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for relative in PATHS:
        data = (base / relative).read_bytes()
        h.update(relative.encode("utf-8"))
        h.update(b"\0")
        h.update(len(data).to_bytes(8, "big"))
        h.update(hashlib.sha256(data).digest())
    return h.hexdigest()


def matches(stamp: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        recorded = stamp.read_text().strip()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return False
    return recorded == fingerprint(ACTIVE)


def write_if_compiled(stage: Path, archive: Path, stamp: Path) -> str:
    if not archive.is_file() or archive.stat().st_size == 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Cannot stamp graphics inputs without a built driver archive")
    expected = fingerprint(ACTIVE)
    staged = fingerprint(stage)
    if staged != expected:
        raise RuntimeError("Native driver staged sources differ from the maintained source set")
    stamp.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = stamp.with_name(stamp.name + ".new")
    try:
        temporary.write_text(expected + "\n")
        os.replace(temporary, stamp)
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    assert matches(stamp)
    return expected


def self_test():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="encore-native-input-stamp-") as td:
        d = Path(td)
        stage = d / "stage"
        marker = d / "source-inputs.sha256"
        archive = d / "driver.a"
        for relative in PATHS:
            target = stage / relative
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            shutil.copyfile(ACTIVE / relative, target)
        assert fingerprint(stage) == fingerprint(ACTIVE)
        assert not matches(marker)
        try:
            write_if_compiled(stage, archive, marker)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Never stamp sources without a completed archive")
        archive.write_bytes(b"fake compiled archive for stamp contract only")
        write_if_compiled(stage, archive, marker)
        assert matches(marker)
        target = stage / PATHS[-1]
        original = target.read_bytes()
        target.write_bytes(original + b"\n/* cache drift fixture */\n")
        try:
            write_if_compiled(stage, archive, marker)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Refuse to stamp staged code that differs from active")
        target.write_bytes(original)
        assert fingerprint(stage) == fingerprint(ACTIVE)
        marker.write_text("0" * 64 + "\n")
        assert not matches(marker)
        # Each individual source mutation must invalidate the complete set.
        for relative in PATHS:
            target = stage / relative
            original = target.read_bytes()
            target.write_bytes(original + b"!")
            assert fingerprint(stage) != fingerprint(ACTIVE)
            target.write_bytes(original)
            assert fingerprint(stage) == fingerprint(ACTIVE)
    script = (ROOT / "tools/prepare-build.sh").read_text()
    build = (ROOT / "tools/build-radv-dependencies.sh").read_text()
    assert 'radv-active-inputs.py --check' in script
    assert 'radv-active-inputs.py" --stamp' in build  # absolute script path is quoted
    assert 'EDEN_ACTIVE_INPUTS_SHA256' in script and 'EDEN_ACTIVE_INPUTS_SHA256' in build
    print(f"DRIVER_SOURCE_CACHE_KEY_PASS maintained_compiler_units={len(PATHS)} stale_archive_rejected")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    actions = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    actions.add_argument("--check", type=Path, metavar="STAMP")
    actions.add_argument("--stamp", type=Path, metavar="STAGE")
    actions.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("paths", type=Path, nargs="*")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.self_test:
        self_test()
    elif args.check:
        if args.paths: parser.error("--check accepts only the stamp filename")
        if not matches(args.check):
            raise SystemExit("STALE_DRIVER_INPUTS: rebuilt source stamp is absent or mismatched")
        print(f"DRIVER_COMPILER_INPUTS_MATCH units={len(PATHS)}")
    else:
        if len(args.paths) != 2:
            parser.error("--stamp needs DRIVER_ARCHIVE and STAMP paths")
        digest = write_if_compiled(args.stamp, args.paths[0], args.paths[1])
        print(f"DRIVER_COMPILER_INPUTS_STAMPED units={len(PATHS)} sha256=" + digest)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/radv-host-memory.inc`:

```inc
bool
radv_ps5_memory_grant_gpu(void *address, uint64_t bytes)
{
   const uint32_t required = PS5_KERNEL_PROT_CPU_READ | PS5_KERNEL_PROT_CPU_WRITE |
                             PS5_KERNEL_PROT_GPU_READ | PS5_KERNEL_PROT_GPU_WRITE;
   const uintptr_t begin = (uintptr_t)address;
   if (!begin || !bytes || bytes > UINTPTR_MAX - begin)
      return false;
   const uintptr_t limit = begin + bytes;
   uintptr_t cursor = begin;
   /* VideoOut already registered these GPU-visible pages. Do not change their
    * protection again: validate the entire imported range, including subviews. */
   while (cursor < limit) {
      void *start = NULL, *end = NULL;
      uint32_t protection = 0;
      if (sceKernelQueryMemoryProtection((void *)cursor, &start, &end, &protection) != 0 ||
          (uintptr_t)start > cursor || (uintptr_t)end <= cursor ||
          (protection & required) != required)
         break;
      cursor = (uintptr_t)end;
   }
   if (cursor >= limit)
      return true;
   const int32_t result = sceKernelMprotect(address, bytes, required);
   if (result != 0)
      fprintf(stderr, "radv/ps5: host GPU protection failed address=%p bytes=%llu result=0x%08x\n",
              address, (unsigned long long)bytes, (unsigned)result);
   return result == 0;
}
```

`tools/radv-link-eden.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Source after setting root to the Eden port. Keep the qualified Eden heap;
# reuse the pinned RADV platform recipe for threads, libc, TLS and unwinding.
eden_radv_link_recipe() {
    local archive=$1
    local reference="$root/../mihawk-vulkan-review"
    local radv_sdk="$reference/.deps/native/ps5-payload-sdk"
    source "$reference/tools/radv-link.sh"
    local recipe_error="" recipe_status=0
    local recipe_error_file
    recipe_error_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/encore-radv-link.XXXXXX")
    radv_link_recipe "$reference" "$radv_sdk" "$archive" 2>"$recipe_error_file" || recipe_status=$?
    recipe_error=$(cat "$recipe_error_file")
    rm -f "$recipe_error_file"

    # Mihawk's standalone recipe gets compiler-rt builtins from the host
    # Clang resource dir. Homebrew LLVM on macOS does not ship the Linux
    # x86_64 archive. Encore already compiles compiler-rt emutls.c into
    # libcommon.a; keep every real recipe input but drop only that absent
    # host-only archive. This must run even when the upstream recipe filled
    # radv_link_inputs before returning its missing-input status.
    local filtered=()
    local recipe_input
    local skipped_host_builtins=0
    for recipe_input in "${radv_link_inputs[@]}"; do
        if [[ $recipe_input == */lib/linux/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a && ! -f $recipe_input ]]; then
            skipped_host_builtins=1
            continue
        fi
        filtered+=("$recipe_input")
    done
    radv_link_inputs=("${filtered[@]}")

    if [[ $recipe_status -ne 0 ]]; then
        if [[ $recipe_status -ne 2 || $skipped_host_builtins -ne 1 ||
              $recipe_error != missing\ */lib/linux/libclang_rt.builtins-x86_64.a ]]; then
            [[ -n $recipe_error ]] && printf '%s\n' "$recipe_error" >&2
            return "$recipe_status"
        fi
    fi
    # The Eden linker already groups all native archives. lld rejects nested
    # groups, so flatten only the recipe's group delimiters.
    local input
    local inputs=()
    for input in "${radv_link_inputs[@]}"; do
        case "$input" in --start-group|--end-group) ;; *) inputs+=("$input") ;; esac
    done
    radv_link_inputs=("${inputs[@]}")
    local flag
    local retained=()
    for flag in "${radv_link_flags[@]}"; do
        case "$flag" in
            --wrap=malloc|--wrap=calloc|--wrap=realloc|--wrap=free|\
            --wrap=posix_memalign|--wrap=aligned_alloc|--wrap=memalign|\
            --wrap=malloc_usable_size|--wrap=reallocf|--wrap=reallocarray|\
            --wrap=getline|--wrap=getdelim) ;;
            # Mihawk's standalone RADV platform binds host DNS to EAI_FAIL stubs.
            # Encore instead compiles its own sceNetResolver-backed getaddrinfo shim;
            # the SDK libc resolver import may point at an unloaded WebKit module.
            --defsym=getaddrinfo=ps5_getaddrinfo|--defsym=freeaddrinfo=ps5_freeaddrinfo|\
            --defsym=gai_strerror=ps5_gai_strerror|--defsym=gethostbyname=ps5_gethostbyname|\
            --defsym=gethostbyname_r=ps5_gethostbyname_r|--defsym=getnameinfo=ps5_getnameinfo) ;;
            *) retained+=("$flag") ;;
        esac
    done
    # The static Mesa ICD exports radv_GetInstanceProcAddr. Eden's existing
    # static loader uses the standard public name.
    radv_link_flags=("${retained[@]}" --defsym=vkGetInstanceProcAddr=radv_GetInstanceProcAddr
        --undefined=__real_fclose --undefined=__real_fflush)
}
```

`tools/radv-videoout-lifecycle.inc`:

```inc
/* Eden switches between SDL, OpenGL and Vulkan within one process. Keep the
 * output shared between live WSI owners, but release it after the last owner. */
static void
videoout_ref(void)
{
   struct wsi_videoout_output *out = &videoout_output;
   mtx_lock(&out->lock);
   while (out->closing)
      cnd_wait(&out->changed, &out->lock);
   out->owners++;
   mtx_unlock(&out->lock);
}

static void
videoout_unref(void)
{
   struct wsi_videoout_output *out = &videoout_output;
   mtx_lock(&out->lock);
   assert(out->owners > 0);
   if (--out->owners != 0) {
      mtx_unlock(&out->lock);
      return;
   }
   /* Vulkan requires swapchains to be destroyed before their device. Their
    * destruction drains in_flight, so no worker references remain here. */
   assert(out->queue_count == 0 && out->current == NULL);
   out->closing = true;
   out->stop = true;
   cnd_broadcast(&out->changed);
   const bool join = out->thread_started;
   mtx_unlock(&out->lock);
   if (join)
      thrd_join(out->thread, NULL);
   mtx_lock(&out->lock);
   out->thread_started = false;
   out->stop = false;

   /* A session at 119.88 Hz hands the output back at 59.94 Hz, as it found it. */
   if (out->handle >= 0 && out->high_frame_rate) {
      const int restored = sceVideoOutConfigureOutput(out->handle, PS5_VIDEO_OUT_MODE_RESTORE, NULL, NULL, NULL);
      fprintf(stderr, "wsi/videoout: 59.94 Hz restored: 0x%08x\n", (unsigned)restored);
   }
   const int closed = out->handle >= 0 ? sceVideoOutClose(out->handle) : 0;
   if (closed == 0) {
      /* Successful close ends display ownership, including pending flips.
       * Never release scanout memory when close fails. */
      if (out->buffers) {
         const size_t bytes = VIDEOOUT_BUFFERS * VIDEOOUT_BUFFER_BYTES;
#if defined(__PROSPERO__)
         if (sceKernelMunmap(out->buffers, bytes) == 0) {
            if (sceKernelReleaseDirectMemory(out->physical, bytes) != 0)
               fprintf(stderr, "wsi/videoout: scanout direct-memory release failed\n");
         } else {
            fprintf(stderr, "wsi/videoout: scanout unmap failed; retaining allocation\n");
         }
#else
         munmap(out->buffers, bytes);
#endif
      }
      out->buffers = NULL;
      out->physical = -1;
      out->registered = false;
      out->handle = -1;
      out->opened = false;
      out->high_frame_rate = false;
      out->modes_settled = false;
      out->high_mode_offered = false;
      out->flip_argument = 0;
      out->queue_head = 0;
      memset(out->buffer, 0, sizeof(out->buffer));
   } else {
      fprintf(stderr, "wsi/videoout: close failed: 0x%08x; retaining scanout memory\n", (unsigned)closed);
   }
   out->closing = false;
   cnd_broadcast(&out->changed);
   mtx_unlock(&out->lock);
}
```

`tools/radv_official_immutable_sampler_fix.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pinned original Mesa 26.2.0 -> Mesa 26.2.4 immutable sampler ownership.
Reference: https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/+/7b5888e8ca77cc0b407c7fb113df85764b561a86
"""
C_EDITS = [
  [
    "   const size_t size = sizeof(struct radv_descriptor_update_template) +\n                       sizeof(struct radv_descriptor_update_template_entry) * entry_count;\n",
    ""
  ],
  [
    "   struct radv_descriptor_update_template *templ;\n   uint32_t i;",
    "   struct radv_descriptor_update_template *templ;\n   uint32_t immutable_sampler_count = 0;\n   uint8_t *immutable_samplers_data;\n   uint32_t i;"
  ],
  [
    "   templ = vk_alloc2(&device->vk.alloc, pAllocator, size, 8, VK_SYSTEM_ALLOCATION_SCOPE_OBJECT);\n   if (!templ)\n      return vk_error(device, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY);\n\n   vk_object_base_init(&device->vk, &templ->base, VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_UPDATE_TEMPLATE);\n\n   templ->entry_count = entry_count;\n\n",
    ""
  ],
  [
    "      templ->bind_point = pCreateInfo->pipelineBindPoint;\n",
    ""
  ],
  [
    "      set_layout = radv_descriptor_set_layout_from_handle(pCreateInfo->descriptorSetLayout);\n   }\n\n   for (i = 0; i < entry_count; i++) {",
    "      set_layout = radv_descriptor_set_layout_from_handle(pCreateInfo->descriptorSetLayout);\n   }\n\n   /* Official Mesa 26.2.4: templates own immutable sampler descriptor bytes. */\n   if (pCreateInfo->templateType == VK_DESCRIPTOR_UPDATE_TEMPLATE_TYPE_PUSH_DESCRIPTORS_KHR) {\n      for (i = 0; i < entry_count; i++) {\n         const VkDescriptorUpdateTemplateEntry *entry = &pCreateInfo->pDescriptorUpdateEntries[i];\n         const struct radv_descriptor_set_binding_layout *binding_layout = set_layout->binding + entry->dstBinding;\n         if ((entry->descriptorType == VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER ||\n              entry->descriptorType == VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLER) &&\n             binding_layout->immutable_samplers_offset)\n            immutable_sampler_count += entry->descriptorCount;\n      }\n   }\n\n   const size_t size = sizeof(struct radv_descriptor_update_template) +\n                       sizeof(struct radv_descriptor_update_template_entry) * entry_count +\n                       (size_t)immutable_sampler_count * RADV_SAMPLER_DESC_SIZE;\n   templ = vk_alloc2(&device->vk.alloc, pAllocator, size, 8, VK_SYSTEM_ALLOCATION_SCOPE_OBJECT);\n   if (!templ)\n      return vk_error(device, VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY);\n   vk_object_base_init(&device->vk, &templ->base, VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_UPDATE_TEMPLATE);\n   templ->entry_count = entry_count;\n   templ->bind_point = pCreateInfo->pipelineBindPoint;\n   immutable_samplers_data = (uint8_t *)&templ->entry[entry_count];\n\n   for (i = 0; i < entry_count; i++) {"
  ],
  [
    "      const uint32_t *immutable_samplers = NULL;",
    "      const uint8_t *immutable_samplers = NULL;"
  ],
  [
    "               immutable_samplers = radv_immutable_samplers(set_layout, binding_layout) + entry->dstArrayElement * 4;",
    "               const uint32_t *src_samplers =\n                  radv_immutable_samplers(set_layout, binding_layout) + entry->dstArrayElement * 4;\n               memcpy(immutable_samplers_data, src_samplers, entry->descriptorCount * RADV_SAMPLER_DESC_SIZE);\n               immutable_samplers = immutable_samplers_data;\n               immutable_samplers_data += entry->descriptorCount * RADV_SAMPLER_DESC_SIZE;"
  ],
  [
    "templ->entry[i].immutable_samplers + 4 * j",
    "templ->entry[i].immutable_samplers + RADV_SAMPLER_DESC_SIZE * j",
    2
  ]
]
H_EDITS = [
  [
    "   const uint32_t *immutable_samplers;",
    "   const uint8_t *immutable_samplers;"
  ]
]

def _apply(src, edits, name):
    for old, new, *occurrences in edits:
        count = occurrences[0] if occurrences else 1
        if src.count(old) != count:
            raise RuntimeError(f"{name}: unexpected pinned input for {old[:100]!r}")
        src = src.replace(old, new)
    return src

def patch_c(src):
    return _apply(src, C_EDITS, "template.c")

def patch_h(src):
    return _apply(src, H_EDITS, "template.h")
```

`tools/radv_official_indirect_draw_fix.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mesa official 26.2.2 a2f2518a: skip zero-length indirect GPU draw packets.

Source upstream: https://github.com/mirror/mesa/commit/a2f2518a9febf1b3b791cd2df079dbd25e56939b
The pinned PS5 RADV adds one GS-compute raster caller, adapted with a count
of one for its generated indirect packet. Fail closed on source drift.
"""

def patch(source: str) -> str:
    def once(haystack: str, before: str, after: str) -> str:
        assert haystack.count(before) == 1, f"Missing/ambiguous Mesa anchor: {before[:100]}"
        return haystack.replace(before, after)

    source = once(source,
        "radv_before_draw(struct radv_cmd_buffer *cmd_buffer, const struct radv_draw_info *info, uint32_t drawCount, bool dgc)",
        "radv_before_draw(struct radv_cmd_buffer *cmd_buffer, const struct radv_draw_info *info, uint32_t drawCount,\n                 uint32_t max_indirect_draw_count, bool dgc)")
    source = once(source,
        """      if (unlikely(!info->count && !info->strmout_va))
         return false;
   }

   if (!info->indexed""",
        """      if (unlikely(!info->count && !info->strmout_va))
         return false;
   } else {
      // The AMD firmware may execute the first indirect draw even with count=0.
      // Ported from official RADV a2f2518a (2026-08-31).
      if (!max_indirect_draw_count)
         return false;
   }

   if (!info->indexed""")

    # Change exactly one call inside each complete function, avoiding broad
    # string replaces that could corrupt another draw path.
    targets = [
        ("radv_gs_compute_rasterize", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &rast, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &rast, 1, direct ? 0 : 1, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDraw", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, 0, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawMultiEXT", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, drawCount, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, drawCount, 0, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndexed", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, 0, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawMultiIndexedEXT", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, drawCount, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, drawCount, 0, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndirect2KHR", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, pInfo->drawCount, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndexedIndirect2KHR", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, pInfo->drawCount, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndirectCount2KHR", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, pInfo->maxDrawCount, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndexedIndirectCount2KHR", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, pInfo->maxDrawCount, false)"),
        ("radv_CmdExecuteGeneratedCommandsEXT", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, true)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, layout->vk.draw_count ? pGeneratedCommandsInfo->maxDrawCount : 1,\n                               true)"),
        ("radv_CmdDrawIndirectByteCount2EXT", "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)",
         "radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, 0, false)"),
    ]
    for function, old, new in targets:
        token = "\n" + function + "("
        assert source.count(token) == 1, f"Cannot locate function {function}"
        a = source.index(token)
        b = source.index("\n}\n", a) + len("\n}\n")
        original = source[a:b]
        updated = once(original, old, new)
        source = source[:a] + updated + source[b:]
    assert source.count("radv_before_draw(") == 12
    assert source.count("radv_before_draw(cmd_buffer, &info, 1, false)") == 0
    return source
```

`tools/refresh-eden-atomic-source-cache.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Refresh ONLY a fully identified stale C++20 GPU atomic Eden source cache.

The PS5 native renderer compiles C++17, but previously restored source trees
contained std::atomic_ref patch bodies and corresponding application receipts.
Do not change SDK, RADV, ccache, console files or unrelated dependency caches.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

PIN = "5f142c7926d0c7fcbbd0ce30794d72f638a43b2a"
OLD = (
    "std::atomic_ref<const u32>(page.compressed_physical_ptr).load(",
    "std::atomic_ref<u32>(page.compressed_physical_ptr).store(",
    "std::atomic_ref<const u32>(page.continuity_tracker).load(",
    "std::atomic_ref<u32>(page.continuity_tracker).store(",
    "std::atomic_ref<const VAddr>(page.cpu_backing_address).load(",
    "std::atomic_ref<VAddr>(page.cpu_backing_address).store(",
    "std::atomic_ref<const u32>(slot).load(",
    "std::atomic_ref<u32>(slot).store(",
)
NEW = (
    "__atomic_load_n(&page.compressed_physical_ptr, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)",
    "__atomic_store_n(&page.compressed_physical_ptr, value, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)",
    "__atomic_load_n(&slot, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)",
    "__atomic_store_n(&slot, value, __ATOMIC_RELEASE)",
)
RECEIPTS = (
    ".encore-backport-ps5-gpu-atomic-forward-table.sha256",
    ".encore-backport-ps5-gpu-atomic-reverse-table.sha256",
)

def refresh(scratch: Path, archive: Path, owner: Path) -> bool:
    scratch = scratch.resolve(strict=True)
    owner = owner.resolve(strict=True)
    if not scratch.name.startswith("ps5-eden-headless."):
        raise RuntimeError("Not an Encore-owned build-cache directory")
    if (scratch / "owner").read_text().strip() != str(owner):
        raise RuntimeError("Eden cache belongs to a different checkout")
    source = scratch / "source"
    if source.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Refusing symlinked Eden source cache")
    if not (source / "CMakeLists.txt").is_file():
        return False
    if (source / "GIT-COMMIT").read_text().strip() != PIN:
        raise RuntimeError("Cannot repair unknown Eden snapshot")
    header = source / "src/core/device_memory_manager.h"
    if not header.is_file() or header.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Cached GPU manager header missing or symlinked")
    content = header.read_text()
    observed = tuple(v in content for v in OLD)
    if not any(observed):
        return False  # normal pristine or already C++17 cache
    if not all(observed) or any(v in content for v in NEW):
        raise RuntimeError("GPU atomic cache is mixed/partial; refusing repair")
    if not all((source / receipt).is_file() for receipt in RECEIPTS):
        raise RuntimeError("Old GPU atomic cache lacks patch receipts")
    if not archive.is_file():
        raise RuntimeError("Pinned Eden source archive missing")
    backup = scratch / ".eden-stale-atomic-backup"
    if backup.exists() or backup.is_symlink():
        raise RuntimeError("Stale GPU cache backup exists; manual recovery required")
    # Inspect the pristine, pinned archive before replacing any live source.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".eden-fresh-atomic-", dir=scratch) as temp:
        fresh = Path(temp)
        subprocess.run(("tar", "-xzf", str(archive), "--strip-components=1",
                        "-C", str(fresh)), check=True, timeout=120)
        fresh_header = fresh / "src/core/device_memory_manager.h"
        if not (fresh / "CMakeLists.txt").is_file() or not fresh_header.is_file():
            raise RuntimeError("Pinned Eden archive missing expected files")
        pristine = fresh_header.read_text()
        if any(v in pristine for v in (*OLD, *NEW)):
            raise RuntimeError("Expected a pristine pinned Eden archive")
        # The pinned archive itself has no GIT-COMMIT receipt. Persist the
        # already-verified pin before the atomic source swap so migration
        # is idempotent even without the outer prepare-build.sh lifecycle.
        (fresh / "GIT-COMMIT").write_text(PIN + "\n")
        store = source / ".cache"
        if store.is_symlink():
            raise RuntimeError("Refusing symlinked upstream CPM store")
        if store.exists() and (fresh / ".cache").exists():
            raise RuntimeError("Pristine source archive contains unexpected .cache store")
        source.rename(backup)
        try:
            fresh.rename(source)
            if (backup / ".cache").exists():
                (backup / ".cache").rename(source / ".cache")
        except Exception:
            # Preserve the backup to diagnose interruption; never claim success.
            raise
        shutil.rmtree(backup)
    print("EDEN_ATOMIC_CACHE_REFRESH pinned source reconstructed for C++17; "
          "CPM dependencies, SDK, RADV and native caches retained", flush=True)
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 4:
        raise SystemExit("usage: refresh-eden-atomic-source-cache.py <scratch> <pinned-tar.gz> <owner>")
    try:
        refresh(Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2]), Path(sys.argv[3]))
    except (OSError, RuntimeError, subprocess.CalledProcessError,
            subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as err:
        raise SystemExit("EDEN_ATOMIC_CACHE_REFRESH_REFUSED: " + str(err)) from err

```

`tools/stage-ps5-graphics-enums.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Apply PS5-only graphics enum extensions to an owner-stamped build copy.

Never patch vendor/sources/eden: its SHA-256 is an immutable input to the
83-source backport manifest, not an editable header. Preserve upstream enum
ordinals by appending Encore-only values after stock entries. Restore the
upstream Strict GPU-fence setting/handler consistently across the native
settings enum, declaration and implementation without editing the pinned
backport originals.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PINNED_UPSTREAM_SHA256 = "f2a3ae93b4257611958fab5a0c652f89c8158d2e16da31fb196a27960cf467ba"
SHIPPING_BACKPORT_SHA256 = "d617d9bd8882d6803fe885dd15302675b211a2e71e6c6faac18e549224aa1689"
RELATIVE = Path("src/common/settings_enums.h")
REPLACEMENTS = (
    ("ENUM(ScalingFilter, NearestNeighbor, Bilinear, Bicubic, Gaussian, Lanczos, ScaleForce, Fsr, Area, ZeroTangent, BSpline, Mitchell, Spline1, Mmpx, Sgsr, SgsrEdge);", "ENUM(ScalingFilter, NearestNeighbor, Bilinear, Bicubic, Gaussian, Lanczos, ScaleForce, Fsr, Area, ZeroTangent, BSpline, Mitchell, Spline1, Mmpx, Sgsr, SgsrEdge, Anime4K3D, Anime4KSoft, Anime4KDenoise);"),
    ("ENUM(AntiAliasing, None, Fxaa, Smaa);", "ENUM(AntiAliasing, None, Fxaa, Smaa, FxaaPlus, Msaa2, Msaa4, Msaa8, Msaa16);"),
    ("ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior, Default, Immediate, Balanced, Accurate);", "ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior, Default, Immediate, Balanced, Accurate, Strict);"),
)

FENCE_HEADER = Path("src/common/settings.h")
FENCE_IMPL = Path("src/common/settings.cpp")


def exact_replace(text: str, before: str, after: str, what: str) -> str:
    if text.count(before) != 1 or after in text:
        raise RuntimeError("Unexpected reviewed PS5 fence ABI: " + what)
    return text.replace(before, after)


def extend_fence_header(text: str) -> str:
    text = exact_replace(
        text,
        "GpuFenceBehavior::Accurate,\n                                                                 \"gpu_fence_behavior\"",
        "GpuFenceBehavior::Strict,\n                                                                 \"gpu_fence_behavior\"",
        "maximum supported fence behavior",
    )
    return exact_replace(
        text,
        "bool IsGPUFenceBehaviorAccurate();\n",
        "bool IsGPUFenceBehaviorAccurate();\nbool IsGPUFenceBehaviorStrict();\n",
        "fence strict declaration",
    )


def extend_fence_implementation(text: str) -> str:
    marker = (
        "bool IsGPUFenceBehaviorAccurate() {\n"
        "    return values.gpu_fence_behavior.GetValue() == GpuFenceBehavior::Accurate;\n"
        "}\n"
    )
    return exact_replace(
        text, marker,
        marker + (
            "\nbool IsGPUFenceBehaviorStrict() {\n"
            "    return values.gpu_fence_behavior.GetValue() == GpuFenceBehavior::Strict;\n"
            "}\n"
        ), "real fence strict implementation")


def sha256(value: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()

def approved_bytes() -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
    original = ROOT / "vendor/sources/eden" / RELATIVE
    reviewed = ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-backports" / RELATIVE
    source = original.read_bytes()
    base = reviewed.read_bytes()
    if sha256(source) != PINNED_UPSTREAM_SHA256:
        raise RuntimeError("Pinned Eden enum input drift: immutable source was modified")
    if sha256(base) != SHIPPING_BACKPORT_SHA256:
        raise RuntimeError("Audited 83-source Eden backport header drift")
    return source, base

def extend_graphics_enums(base_text: str) -> str:
    result = base_text
    for before, after in REPLACEMENTS:
        if result.count(before) != 1 or after in result:
            raise RuntimeError("Unexpected reviewed graphics enum source ABI")
        result = result.replace(before, after)
    return result

def validate_owned_stage(stage: Path) -> Path:
    if stage.is_symlink() or stage.name != "source":
        raise RuntimeError("Only an owned build-cache source is writable")
    cache = stage.parent
    owner = cache / "owner"
    if (cache.is_symlink() or not cache.name.startswith("ps5-eden-headless.") or
        owner.is_symlink() or not owner.is_file() or
        owner.read_text().strip() != str(ROOT.resolve())):
        raise RuntimeError("Build-cache source is not owner-stamped for this checkout")
    if not stage.is_dir() or stage.resolve() != cache.resolve() / "source":
        raise RuntimeError("Unexpected or escaping Eden build directory")
    target = stage / RELATIVE
    if (target.is_symlink() or not target.is_file() or
        not target.resolve().is_relative_to(stage.resolve())):
        raise RuntimeError("Unsafe graphics enum destination")
    return target

def apply(stage: Path, check_only: bool = False) -> str:
    _, approved = approved_bytes()
    _ = validate_owned_stage(stage)
    targets = (
        (RELATIVE, approved, extend_graphics_enums(approved.decode("utf-8")).encode("utf-8")),
        (FENCE_HEADER,
         (ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-backports" / FENCE_HEADER).read_bytes(),
         None),
        (FENCE_IMPL,
         (ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-backports" / FENCE_IMPL).read_bytes(),
         None),
    )
    targets = list(targets)
    targets[1] = (targets[1][0], targets[1][1],
                  extend_fence_header(targets[1][1].decode("utf-8")).encode("utf-8"))
    targets[2] = (targets[2][0], targets[2][1],
                  extend_fence_implementation(targets[2][1].decode("utf-8")).encode("utf-8"))
    # Inspect every target before writing any, so an unfamiliar build-cache
    # change cannot partially install or bypass the reviewed source variant.
    pending = []
    for relative, original, expected in targets:
        dest = stage / relative
        if dest.is_symlink() or not dest.is_file() or not (
                dest.resolve().is_relative_to(stage.resolve())):
            raise RuntimeError("Unsafe PS5 fence/graphics owner: " + str(relative))
        current = dest.read_bytes()
        if current == expected:
            continue
        if current != original:
            raise RuntimeError("Unreviewed PS5 staged graphics/fence source: " + str(relative))
        pending.append((dest, original, expected))
    if not pending:
        return "already-applied"
    if check_only:
        raise RuntimeError("PS5 graphics/fence overlay not yet installed")
    for dest, original, expected in pending:
        tmp = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".encore-" + str(os.getpid()))
        if tmp.exists() or tmp.is_symlink():
            raise RuntimeError("Unexpected PS5 staged graphics temporary file")
        try:
            tmp.write_bytes(expected)
            shutil.copymode(dest, tmp)
            if dest.read_bytes() != original:
                raise RuntimeError("PS5 staged graphics source changed during installation")
            tmp.replace(dest)
        finally:
            tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    return "installed"

def self_test() -> None:
    source, approved = approved_bytes()
    extended = extend_graphics_enums(approved.decode("utf-8"))
    # Strict already exists in the PINNED upstream Eden enum. The old
    # 83-source backport omitted it, while upstream fence_manager.h still
    # calls its real predicate. Only Encore's scaling/AA extras must be
    # absent from original upstream; Strict must be present there.
    upstream_enums = source.decode("utf-8")
    assert not any(after in upstream_enums for before, after in REPLACEMENTS
                   if "GpuFenceBehavior" not in before)
    assert "ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior, Default, Immediate, Balanced, Accurate, Strict);" in upstream_enums
    assert "ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior, Default, Immediate, Balanced, Accurate);" in approved.decode("utf-8")
    assert all(extended.count(after) == 1 for _,after in REPLACEMENTS)
    assert all(extended.count(before) == 0 for before,_ in REPLACEMENTS)
    assert extended.count("ENUM(ScalingFilter,") == 1
    assert extended.count("ENUM(AntiAliasing,") == 1
    assert extended.count("ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior,") == 1
    fence_h = (ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-backports" / FENCE_HEADER).read_text()
    fence_cpp = (ROOT / "vendor/encore-active/eden-backports" / FENCE_IMPL).read_text()
    updated_h = extend_fence_header(fence_h)
    updated_cpp = extend_fence_implementation(fence_cpp)
    assert updated_h.count("bool IsGPUFenceBehaviorStrict();") == 1
    assert updated_h.count("GpuFenceBehavior::Strict,") == 1
    assert updated_cpp.count("bool IsGPUFenceBehaviorStrict() {") == 1
    assert "ENUM(GpuFenceBehavior, Default, Immediate, Balanced, Accurate, Strict);" in extended
    for source, extend in ((updated_h, extend_fence_header),
                           (updated_cpp, extend_fence_implementation)):
        try:
            extend(source)
        except RuntimeError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError("Already-patched fence owner accepted")
    assert sha256(approved) == SHIPPING_BACKPORT_SHA256
    try:
        extend_graphics_enums(extended)
    except RuntimeError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Already-patched enums accepted as a new baseline")
    print("PS5_GRAPHICS_ENUM_OVERLAY_PASS pinned=1 backport=1 abi=1 failclosed=1")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("stage", nargs="?", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.self_test:
        self_test()
    if args.stage is None and not args.self_test:
        parser.error("provide an owned build source or --self-test")
    if args.stage is not None:
        print("PS5_GRAPHICS_ENUM_OVERLAY_" + apply(args.stage, args.check).upper())

```

`tools/stage-vendored-opengl-deps.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage all mandatory PS5 OpenGL transitive dependencies from our own Git.

All Git original SHAs, PSBC source/compiler patch, Mesa 26.2 tar, and the
second native boilerplate are pinned. No upstream network access is required.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import zipfile

ROOT=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT/'tools'))
import deps


def sha(path):
 h=hashlib.sha256()
 with open(path,'rb') as stream:
  for part in iter(lambda:stream.read(1<<20),b''):h.update(part)
 return h.hexdigest()


def stage(opengl_root:Path):
 opengl_root=opengl_root.resolve()
 declared=json.loads((opengl_root/'dependencies.json').read_text())
 original=json.loads((ROOT/'vendor/sources/opengl-source/dependencies.json').read_text())
 if declared!=original:raise RuntimeError('PS5 OpenGL upstream dependency pins diverged from our complete source mirror')
 workspace=opengl_root/'third_party';workspace.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 for name,pin in declared['repositories'].items():
  if pin.get('optional'):continue
  locked=next(x for x in deps.MANIFEST['items'] if x['name']=='opengl-'+name.lower().replace('_','-'))
  if locked['commit']!=pin['revision'] or locked['url']!=pin['url']:
   raise RuntimeError(f'PS5 OpenGL dep {name} version mismatch')
  deps.fetch_git(locked)
  recovered=deps.location(locked)
  checkout=workspace/name
  if not (checkout/'.git').exists():
   if checkout.exists():raise RuntimeError(f'Unrecognized third_party source {checkout}')
   shutil.copytree(recovered,checkout,symlinks=True)
  actual=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(checkout),'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
  if actual!=locked['commit']:raise RuntimeError(f'PS5 OpenGL staged {name} SHA mismatch')
  print('OPENGL_GIT_DEP_OFFLINE',name,actual[:12],flush=True)

 # Restore and preserve the ORIGINAL Mesa release archive; the audited PS5
 # OpenGL fetcher verifies SHA and unpacks it itself, but never needs network.
 mesa=declared['mesa']
 locked=next(x for x in deps.MANIFEST['items'] if x['name']=='opengl-mesa-26-2')
 if locked['sha256']!=mesa['sha256'] or locked['url']!=mesa['url']:
  raise RuntimeError('PS5 OpenGL Mesa pin mismatch')
 deps.ensure_saved_archive(locked)
 target=workspace/f"mesa-{mesa['version']}.tar.xz"
 if not target.is_file():shutil.copy2(ROOT/locked['save'],target)
 if sha(target)!=mesa['sha256']:raise RuntimeError('Wrong vendored Mesa 26.2 archive')
 print('OPENGL_MESA_ARCHIVE_OFFLINE',target.stat().st_size,flush=True)

 boiler=declared['native_boilerplate']
 locked=next(x for x in deps.MANIFEST['items'] if x['name']=='opengl-native-boilerplate')
 if locked['commit']!=boiler['revision'] or locked['url']!=boiler['url']:
  raise RuntimeError('PS5 OpenGL native boilerplate mismatch')
 deps.fetch_git(locked)
 dest=opengl_root/'build/native-app-boilerplate'
 if not (dest/'.git').exists():
  if dest.exists():raise RuntimeError(f'Unrecognized native boilerplate folder {dest}')
  shutil.copytree(deps.location(locked),dest,symlinks=True)
 actual=subprocess.check_output(['git','-C',str(dest),'rev-parse','HEAD'],text=True).strip()
 if actual!=locked['commit']:raise RuntimeError('Wrong native boilerplate staged')
 # Upstream setup checks for the extracted bin/prospero-lld BEFORE it looks
 # for the ZIP. Extract the complete pinned SDK ourselves or it re-downloads.
 extras=next(x for x in deps.MANIFEST['items'] if x['name']=='boilerplate')['setup_prefetch']
 sdk_zip=deps.restore_chunked_object({'name':'boilerplate-setup-1'})
 zlib_tar=deps.restore_chunked_object({'name':'boilerplate-setup-0'})
 assert sdk_zip and zlib_tar
 if sha(sdk_zip)!=extras[1]['sha256'] or sha(zlib_tar)!=extras[0]['sha256']:
  raise RuntimeError('Mismatch in pinned OpenGL bootstrap prefetch')
 native=dest/'.deps/native';native.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 sdk=native/'ps5-payload-sdk'
 if not (sdk/'bin/prospero-lld').is_file():
  with zipfile.ZipFile(sdk_zip) as archive:
   for entry in archive.infolist():
    path=Path(entry.filename)
    if path.is_absolute() or '..' in path.parts:
     raise RuntimeError('Unsafe vendored PayloadSDK ZIP member')
   archive.extractall(native)
   for entry in archive.infolist():
    bits=(entry.external_attr>>16)&0o777
    if bits and not entry.is_dir():os.chmod(native/entry.filename,bits)
 archive=native/'zlib/zlib-1.3.2.tar.gz'
 archive.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
 if not archive.exists():shutil.copy2(zlib_tar,archive)
 if sha(archive)!=extras[0]['sha256']:
  raise RuntimeError('Wrong vendored zlib 1.3.2')
 if not (sdk/'bin/prospero-lld').is_file():raise RuntimeError('PS5 SDK missing after vendored extraction')
 print('OPENGL_NATIVE_TEMPLATE_OFFLINE',actual[:12],'SDK and zlib verified',flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':
 if len(sys.argv)!=2:raise SystemExit('usage: stage-vendored-opengl-deps.py PS5_OPENGL_SOURCE_ROOT')
 stage(Path(sys.argv[1]))
```

`tools/symbolize-crash.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later
"""Names the functions in a ProsperoEden crash report (headless/crash_report.h).

  symbolize-crash.py REPORT ELF [CRASH_PROVENANCE_JSON]

REPORT is logs/crash-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.txt from a console. ELF is the unstripped executable of the
build that wrote it: build/headless-native/llvm-pie.elf right after a build, and for a release
the copy `make release` keeps (build/symbols/Prospero.Eden-Encore-R1.elf). Every "eboot+0x..." in the
report is an offset into that file's code; the report is printed again with the function, file
and line after each one.

The addresses under "calls found on the stack" are where calls return to, so the function named
is the caller. The list comes from scanning the stack: the console cannot read its own code, so
it lists every value that points into the code with a "?". Those are checked here against the
ELF, and the ones that do not follow a call instruction are left out. A function that returned
earlier can still show up in the list.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys


def sections(data):
    """name -> (address, file offset, size) of an ELF64 file's sections."""
    assert data[:4] == b'\x7fELF' and data[4] == 2, 'not a 64-bit ELF file'
    shoff, = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, 0x28)
    shentsize, shnum, shstrndx = struct.unpack_from('<HHH', data, 0x3A)
    headers = [struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQIIQQ', data, shoff + i * shentsize) for i in range(shnum)]
    names_at = headers[shstrndx][4]
    found = {}
    for name, _kind, _flags, address, offset, size, *_ in headers:
        end = data.index(b'\0', names_at + name)
        found[data[names_at + name:end].decode()] = (address, offset, size)
    return found


def after_call(code):
    """Whether the eight bytes that end at an address end with a call (as crash_report.cpp checks)."""
    if len(code) != 8:
        return False
    if code[3] == 0xE8:  # call rel32
        return True
    for length in (2, 3, 4, 6, 7):  # a call through a register or memory: FF /2
        at = code[8 - length:]
        if at[0] == 0xFF and at[1] & 0x38 == 0x10:
            return True
        if length >= 3 and at[0] & 0xF0 == 0x40 and at[1] == 0xFF and at[2] & 0x38 == 0x10:
            return True
    return False


def tool(*names):
    for name in names:
        if shutil.which(name):
            return name
    sys.exit('not found: ' + ' or '.join(names))


def verify_elf_receipt(data: bytes, section_size: int, receipt: dict) -> None:
    """Reject a symbol file detached from the same-run CI symbol artifact.

    The signed PS5 SELF remains separately fingerprinted; the receipt alone
    does not prove that an old console crash belongs to this binary.
    """
    if not isinstance(receipt, dict):
        raise ValueError("malformed crash-provenance receipt")
    files = receipt.get("files")
    record = files.get("unstripped_elf") if isinstance(files, dict) else None
    if (not isinstance(record, dict) or receipt.get("schema") != 1 or
            receipt.get("elf_text_size_hex") != f"0x{section_size:x}" or
            record.get("sha256") != hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()):
        raise ValueError("ELF hash or .text size does not match crash-provenance receipt")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) not in (3, 4):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    report = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    elf = sys.argv[2]
    with open(elf, 'rb') as file:
        data = file.read()
    start, at, size = sections(data)['.text']
    if len(sys.argv) == 4:
        try:
            with open(sys.argv[3], encoding='utf-8') as file:
                verify_elf_receipt(data, size, json.load(file))
        except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError, TypeError) as error:
            sys.exit(f'REFUSED symbolization: {error}')
    said = re.search(r'\(code size 0x([0-9a-f]+)\)', report)
    if not said:
        sys.exit('not a ProsperoEden crash report: ' + sys.argv[1])
    if int(said.group(1), 16) != size:
        sys.exit(f'REFUSED symbolization: crash code size 0x{said.group(1)} != '
                 f'ELF .text size 0x{size:x}. Supply the exact ELF from the same build; '
                 'stack candidates from a different build are misleading.')
    lines = report.splitlines()
    in_calls = False
    dropped = 0
    kept = []      # (line, addresses to name)
    for line in lines:
        offsets = [int(value, 16) for value in re.findall(r'eboot\+0x([0-9a-f]+)', line)]
        call = in_calls and line.startswith('  ') and len(offsets) == 1
        if line.startswith('calls found on the stack'):
            in_calls = True
        if call and line.endswith(' ?'):
            if not (8 <= offsets[0] <= size and after_call(data[at + offsets[0] - 8:at + offsets[0]])):
                dropped += 1
                continue
            line = line[:-2]
        # A return address names the instruction after the call: one byte back is inside the call.
        kept.append((line, [start + offset - (1 if call else 0) for offset in offsets]))
    wanted = [address for _line, addresses in kept for address in addresses]
    names = []
    if wanted:
        symbolizer = tool('llvm-symbolizer-18', 'llvm-symbolizer')
        output = subprocess.run([symbolizer, '-e', elf, '-f', '-C', '-i', '-p', *[hex(a) for a in wanted]],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
        names = [block.strip().replace('\n', ' ') for block in output.strip().split('\n\n')]
        if len(names) != len(wanted):  # no blank lines between answers: one answer per line
            names = [line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.startswith(' ')]
        assert len(names) == len(wanted), 'unexpected answer from ' + symbolizer
    for line, addresses in kept:
        found = [names.pop(0) for _address in addresses]
        print(line + ('   ' + ' | '.join(found) if found else ''))
    if dropped:
        print(f'\n{dropped} stack values that point into the code but do not follow a call were left out.')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

`tools/sync-encore-overrides.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, json, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

PROFILE_IDS = ("minimum", "recommended", "high", "ultra")
RENDERER = {"opengl": 0, "vulkan": 1}
OUTPUT = {"1080p": 0, "1440p": 1, "2160p": 2}
RESOLUTION = {0.25: 0, 0.5: 1, 0.75: 2, 1.0: 3, 1.25: 4, 1.5: 5, 2.0: 6, 3.0: 7, 4.0: 8}
FILTER = {"bilinear": 0, "fsr": 1, "bicubic": 2, "nearest": 3}
AA = {"none": 0, "fxaa": 1, "smaa": 2}
REFRESH = {60: 0, 120: 1}

def profile(settings: dict) -> tuple[int,int,int,int,int,int,int,bool]:
    return (
        RENDERER[settings["renderer"]],
        OUTPUT[settings["tv_output"]],
        RESOLUTION[float(settings["game_resolution"])],
        FILTER[settings["upscaling_filter"]],
        int(settings["fsr_sharpness"]),
        AA[settings["anti_aliasing"]],
        REFRESH[int(settings["refresh_rate_hz"])],
        settings.get("console_mode", "docked") != "handheld",
    )

def cpp_profile(p: tuple[int,int,int,int,int,int,int,bool]) -> str:
    return "{" + ", ".join(map(str, p[:-1])) + ", " + ("true" if p[-1] else "false") + "}"

def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--source", type=Path, required=True, help="checkout of niakw/encore-overrides")
    ap.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("headless/encore_overrides_generated.h"))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    source = args.source.resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((source / "manifest.json").read_text())
    # This shipping policy changes recommended FSR1 and adds NS2 per-title tiers.
    # Retire any cached remote manifest from the previous revision 6 build.
    database_revision = max(7, int(manifest.get("database_revision", 0)))
    general = {pid: json.loads((source / "general" / f"{pid}.json").read_text())["settings"] for pid in PROFILE_IDS}
    general_cpp = [profile(general[pid]) for pid in PROFILE_IDS]
    controls = json.loads((source / "general" / "controls.json").read_text())
    detection = controls["detection"]
    gameplay = detection["gameplay"]
    ui = detection["ui"]
    control_cpp = (
        f'{float(gameplay["stick_threshold"]):.2f}f',
        int(gameplay["trigger_threshold_raw"]),
        int(gameplay["evidence_enter"]),
        int(gameplay["evidence_per_active_poll"]),
        f'{float(ui["quiet_stick_threshold"]):.2f}f',
        int(ui["quiet_polls_before_dpad"]),
        int(ui["menu_evidence_enter"]),
        int(ui["options_touchpad_weight"]),
        int(ui["dpad_weight"]),
        bool(detection.get("hysteresis", True)),
    )
    specifics: list[tuple[int,str,list[tuple[int,int,int,int,int,int,int,bool]]]] = []
    for path in sorted((source / "games").glob("*.json")):
        data = json.loads(path.read_text())
        profiles = data.get("profiles", {})
        if not all(pid in profiles and "settings" in profiles[pid] for pid in PROFILE_IDS):
            continue
        values = [profile(profiles[pid]["settings"]) for pid in PROFILE_IDS]
        # Compare the *effective compiled video tuple*, not raw JSON. Optional
        # texture_anisotropy is handled by the native sampler tier resolver;
        # raw dict comparisons would treat 8,992 unchanged NS1 baselines as
        # game-specific simply because they inherit that optional setting.
        # All native NS2 games explicitly keep their independently tuned tier.
        if data.get("source_console") == "Nintendo Switch 2" or any(
            values[i] != general_cpp[i] for i in range(len(PROFILE_IDS))
        ):
            specifics.append((int(data["title_id"], 16), data.get("name", path.stem), values))
    # The full third-party catalogue is checked in as a normal vendored tree,
    # without a nested .git. Running `git rev-parse HEAD` there returns the
    # *parent Encore commit*, silently fabricating the catalogue revision.
    # Prefer the pinned immutable upstream commit from the vendor receipt.
    receipt = source / "VENDOR-ORIGIN.json"
    if receipt.is_file():
        origin = json.loads(receipt.read_text())
        if origin.get("name") != "encore-overrides" or origin.get("url") != "https://github.com/niakw/encore-overrides.git":
            raise ValueError("wrong pinned Encore Overrides origin")
        revision = origin.get("commit", "")
        if len(revision) != 40 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in revision):
            raise ValueError("invalid vendored Encore Overrides SHA")
    else:
        revision = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(source), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
    lines = [
        "// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later",
        "// Generated by tools/sync-encore-overrides.py; do not edit by hand.",
        f"// Source: niakw/encore-overrides@{revision}",
        "#pragma once",
        "#include <array>",
        "#include <cstdint>",
        "namespace Eden::EncoreOverrides {",
        "struct AutoControlProfile { float gameplay_stick_threshold; int trigger_threshold_raw; unsigned gameplay_evidence_enter; unsigned gameplay_evidence_per_active_poll; float quiet_stick_threshold; unsigned quiet_polls_before_dpad; unsigned menu_evidence_enter; unsigned options_touchpad_weight; unsigned dpad_weight; bool hysteresis; };",
        "struct VideoProfile { int renderer; int output; int resolution; int filter; int fsr_sharpness; int anti_aliasing; int refresh; bool docked; };",
        "inline constexpr int kAuthoredProfileCount = 4;",
        "inline constexpr int kCustomProfile = 4;",
        f'inline constexpr const char* kSourceRevision = "{revision}";',
        f"inline constexpr int kDatabaseRevision = {database_revision};",
        "inline constexpr AutoControlProfile kPlayStationAutoControls{"
            + ", ".join(map(str, control_cpp[:-1]))
            + ", " + ("true" if control_cpp[-1] else "false") + "};",
        "inline constexpr std::array<VideoProfile, kAuthoredProfileCount> kGeneralProfiles = {{",
    ]
    for p in general_cpp:
        lines.append(f"    {cpp_profile(p)},")
    lines += ["}};", "struct TitleProfiles { std::uint64_t title_id; std::array<VideoProfile, kAuthoredProfileCount> profiles; };",
              f"inline constexpr std::array<TitleProfiles, {len(specifics)}> kTitleProfiles = {{{{"]
    for title, name, values in specifics:
        safe = name.replace("*/", "* /")
        lines.append(f"    // {safe}")
        lines.append(f"    {{0x{title:016X}ULL, {{{{")
        for p in values:
            lines.append(f"        {cpp_profile(p)},")
        lines.append("    }}},")
    lines += [
        "}};",
        "inline constexpr int ClampTier(int tier) { return tier < 0 ? 0 : tier >= kAuthoredProfileCount ? kAuthoredProfileCount - 1 : tier; }",
        "inline constexpr const VideoProfile& GeneralProfile(int tier) { return kGeneralProfiles[static_cast<std::size_t>(ClampTier(tier))]; }",
        "inline constexpr const VideoProfile& ProfileForTitle(std::uint64_t title_id, int tier) {",
        "    for (const auto& entry : kTitleProfiles) if (entry.title_id == title_id) return entry.profiles[static_cast<std::size_t>(ClampTier(tier))];",
        "    return GeneralProfile(tier);",
        "}",
        "inline constexpr bool HasSpecificProfile(std::uint64_t title_id) {",
        "    for (const auto& entry : kTitleProfiles) if (entry.title_id == title_id) return true;",
        "    return false;",
        "}",
        "} // namespace Eden::EncoreOverrides",
        "",
    ]
    args.output.write_text("\n".join(lines))
    print(f"generated {args.output}: revision={database_revision} general={len(general_cpp)} specific={len(specifics)} source={revision}")
    # The default Encore snapshot sync now also captures curated visual
    # button-art rules. Custom --output fixture runs remain untouched.
    if args.output == Path("headless/encore_overrides_generated.h") and (
        source / "glyphs" / "manifest.json").is_file():
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B",
                        str(Path(__file__).with_name("sync-glyph-overrides.py")),
                        "--source", str(source)], check=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
